assertion in `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` passed while the field emptied itself.

issues.name: 🎫 Picker — a chosen option should leave the list, not sit in it wearing a tick
issues.description:
> 140 issue return selects on type, for multiselect but return does not
> select on arrow, maybe prezing enter twice is the ideal pattern also for
> both item selected needs better desing and and numbering it shoudl remove
> the selected items fro the list rather than chekcing them

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against Feature #140 (the picker token box) as shipped in f215334.

## The report

> it should remove the selected items from the list rather than checking them

Today a multiselect picker keeps every option in the dropdown and marks the chosen ones with a `✓` (`public/app.js`: the `chip-pop-check` span). Kyle wants a chosen option to **leave the list** — it is already visible as a chip in the box above, so listing it again says the same thing twice and pushes the options you can still pick further down.

## What to settle before building

- **Removing it changes what Enter-on-a-selected-row means.** Toggling off currently happens by picking the ticked row again; if the row is gone, un-picking is only ⌫ on the chip. That may be the right trade — the chips are right there — but it should be a decision, not a side effect.
- **The list will reflow under the cursor** as options leave it. Whatever is armed has to stay armed, or arming has to move somewhere predictable, or every pick will select the wrong next thing.
- Single select and workflow are unaffected: they hold one chip and close on the pick.

## Where the work lives

- `public/app.js` — the `draw()` inside `searchPicker` that emits `chip-pop-check`.
- `public/picker-core.js` — `visible()` is the honest place to filter, so the grammar and the DOM cannot disagree about what is in the list.


## Fixed 2026-08-26 (change 67, commit 7a1cfe8)

`core.visible()` is where it landed — the place this ticket named. A multi
picker's list is now `rankOptions(...)` minus everything staged in the box; a
single picker keeps its current value listed and ticked, because a pick there
overwrites rather than accumulates.

**The two things this ticket said to settle first, settled:**

| Question | Decision (Kyle, 2026-08-26) |
| --- | --- |
| What Enter-on-a-chosen-row means once the row is gone | Nothing — it cannot be armed. ⌫ on the chip is the only un-pick. The chips sit in the box and ← → already walk them. |
| Where arming goes as the list reflows | Nowhere: a pick disarms the list (`active: -1`). Predictable, and it makes the Enter after a pick the save — the two-Enter grammar [[Issue#63]] asked about, for one keystroke. |

This also **was** [[Issue#63]]: with chosen rows in the list, `↓` from a fresh
box usually armed something already chosen, and Enter took it back out. That
report and this one are one defect.

The `✓` is gone from multi rows (nothing left to tick) and stays on the single
picker's current value. An emptied list now reads "Everything is chosen"
rather than "No matches", which was a lie in the one case that matters.

**Guarded by** `test/picker-browser.test.mjs` (real key presses, Chromium) and
the grammar cases in `test/picker-core.test.mjs`.

issues.name: 🎫 Field headers do not say which table a lookup, rollup or relation reaches
issues.description:
> for design system · chips — d39937b, 9020a77, "Colour means one thing again"
> determine how we will show in field headders what table a lookup or rollup
> value is from, same for relations, maybe

— Kyle, 2026-08-25. Raised against the three-tier chip system: the chips settled what a *value* looks like, and this is the matching question one level up, at the **column header**.

## What a header says today

`fieldNameLabel()` in `public/app.js` renders the field's name plus a superscript glyph for the computed types — `ƒ` formula, `Σ` rollup, `↗` lookup — with a `title` tooltip reading "lookup — computed from other values, not editable". A relation column gets no mark at all.

So a header tells you **that** a value came from somewhere else. It never tells you **where from**, and the answer is only reachable by opening the field tray.

## The information is already in the schema

Nothing needs computing or storing — every one of these fields already names its route:

| Field type | What the schema carries | Reads as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relation | `targetDb` (`Product/Task`), `targetDbId`, `many`, `inverseField` | → Product/Task |
| lookup | `via` (the relation it travels) | ↗ via Project |
| rollup | `via`, `targetField`, `aggregate` | Σ sum of Estimate via Tasks |
| formula | its script | ƒ |

A lookup's `via` names a relation, and that relation names its `targetDb` — so the full path (this table → relation → that table → that field) is derivable in one hop from what is already loaded in `state.schema`.

## What to decide

- **How much fits in a header.** A column header is narrow and already carries the name, the sort caret, the ⋮ and the resize grip. "Σ sum of Estimate via Tasks" will not fit beside "Total Estimate" at any realistic width.
- **Where the rest goes.** Candidates: a second muted line under the name in the header; the existing superscript glyph made hoverable with a real popover instead of a `title`; a chip in the header borrowing the **pointer** tier, since a route to another table is exactly "clicking goes somewhere"; or the field tray only, with the header just marking that a route exists.
- **Whether the target should be clickable.** If a header names Product/Task, clicking it plausibly opens that table. That would make the header the third surface that navigates by reference, after the `#id` link and the relation chip — consistent with the universal reference rule (`ae6b203`), which says every entity answers to its id and permalink.
- **Whether relations get a mark at all.** They are editable, so the computed glyph vocabulary does not fit them. They may want their own, or nothing but the target name.

## Constraint from the chip work

Whatever this becomes must not spend colour. `d39937b` settled that colour means "the value was chosen from a set", and a pointer tier is deliberately neutral — *"the moment a pointer carries a hue it reads as a value, and the row loses the one thing colour was meant to say."* A header route is a pointer, so it is an outline and a mark, never a tint.

## Where the work lives

- `public/app.js` — `fieldNameLabel()`, `computedMark()`, and the `th.col-head` build inside `renderTable`.
- `public/style.css` — `.col-head`, `.field-mark`, and the `.k-rel` pointer tier if a header chip is the answer.
- Worth a specimen page first, the way the chip tiers themselves were settled — this is a design decision with four plausible answers, not a fix.

Checked 2026-09-28: fieldNameLabel (public/app.js:2278) still marks only formula, rollup and lookup, with a superscript glyph and a generic tooltip, and a relation header carries no mark. The field tray now names a rollup's and a lookup's recipe (Issue #387, 9ef6068), so the route is one click away, but the header still does not say where a value comes from.

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution
- Fixed looks like: hovering or focusing a lookup, rollup or relation header's mark shows where the value comes from ("Σ avg of Skill via Peers → Showcase/People"), and the relation header gets its own pointer mark.
- Root cause: `fieldNameLabel` (`public/app.js:2277`) knows only `COMPUTED_NAME_MARKS` (`:2269`, formula, rollup, lookup) and a generic `title`; relations return the bare name. Proposed from the code.
- The change: build the route string with the tray's own recipe logic (`relLabel`, `public/app.js:8544`, and `computedShowsAs`, `:8272`, from Issue #387) and show it in `showPopover` (`:1646`) on the mark, replacing the `title`. Add a relation mark from the same set.

## Approach
- Test first: a browser case (new `test/header-route-browser.test.mjs`) that hovers a lookup's and a relation's header mark and asserts the popover names the relation and the target table, light and dark.
- Steps: extract the recipe string helper from the tray code, call it in `fieldNameLabel`, style the relation mark in `public/style.css` beside `.field-mark` (`:1497`).
- Size: M.
- Risks: a header label never truncates and adding text must not widen other columns (weave-grid-field-width-rules); a pointer never carries a hue (weave-chip-three-tiers).
- **Decision needed:** where the route shows. Options: (a) popover on the mark; (b) a second muted line in the header; (c) a pointer chip in the header. Recommend (a): it adds no width or height to the header.

issues.name: 🎫 The clipped-cell expansion restyles what it shows — same font, better design
issues.description:
> overflow expand on hover could be better designed and keep the same font

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against the Ledger grid's clipped-cell expansion (`a2cca58`).

## The font part is a real bug, and the cause is known

The expansion is a **copy**: `showCellPop()` in `public/app.js` clones the cell's children into a `.cell-pop` hanging off `.table-wrap`, so the live cell keeps its box and no column moves. Correct mechanically — but the clone lands **outside** the cell it came from, so every selector scoped to that cell stops matching it.

Concretely, the leading column is set heavier by:

```css
.wv-grid td.name-cell .inline-edit { font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; }
```

The clone is `.cell-pop .inline-edit`, not `td.name-cell .inline-edit`, so a clipped name renders at the grid's default size in the popover and at 15px/600 in the row. The value visibly changes size at the moment you hover it to read it — which is the one moment it should not move.

`.cell-pop` also actively restyles the copy:

```css
.cell-pop .inline-edit { border-color: transparent; background: none; width: auto; }
.cell-pop .ms-box > .btn, .cell-pop .chip .x, .cell-pop .k .x, .cell-pop .date-pick-btn { display: none; }
```

Hiding the × and the + button is right — the copy is for reading, not editing. Resetting the input's box is not, or not this bluntly.

## Two ways out, and they differ in kind

1. **Copy the computed type onto the popover.** `showCellPop()` already has the source `td`; reading `font-family / font-size / font-weight / letter-spacing` off it and setting them on `.cell-pop` makes the copy match whatever the cell was, including any future per-column rule. This is what `cellFitProbe()` already does for the column-fit measurement — the same problem, already solved once in this file.
2. **Mirror the scoping in CSS.** Re-declare `.cell-pop.from-name-cell .inline-edit` and friends. Cheaper today, wrong tomorrow: every new cell-scoped rule has to remember to add its twin.

Option 1 is the one that cannot drift.

## The design part is still open

Kyle's "could be better designed" is not specified beyond that. Worth deciding on a specimen rather than in prose:

- It is a **read** surface, so it should probably not look like an editable cell at all — no input box, no transparent-bordered control, just the value set the way the cell sets it.
- Where it anchors. It currently pins to the cell's top-left and grows right and down, which can put it over the very column you were comparing against.
- Whether it should carry the field's name, since a floating box of text has no header once it leaves the row.
- Whether chips inside it wrap (they do now, `max-width: 380px`) or the popover simply widens.
- Whether it needs a delay before opening. It fires on `mouseover` today, so crossing a row of clipped cells flashes several in sequence.

## Where the work lives

- `public/app.js` — `showCellPop()`, and `cellFitProbe()` beside it as the precedent for copying computed type.
- `public/style.css` — `.cell-pop`, `.cell-pop-layer`.
- `test/ledger-grid.test.mjs` — already pins that the expansion is an overlay copy and that nothing rewrites the cell box; a font-fidelity case belongs next to those.


---

## The font half shipped, 2026-08-26 (commit `05e09d0`, Gerrit change 71)

Option 1 — copy the computed type onto the popover — is what landed, for the
reason this issue gave: it cannot drift. `copyCellType()` reads
`fontFamily / fontSize / fontWeight / fontStyle / letterSpacing / lineHeight /
color / textAlign` off the source cell AND off every element inside it, then
writes them onto the matching clone. Same technique `cellFitProbe()` already
used for the column-fit measurement.

The anchor question got answered at the same time, because Kyle filed it as a
bug (Issue #93, fault 1): the popover pinned its border box to the cell's, and
the two boxes disagree — the cell pads 9px/4px, the popover 8px/10px over a
1px border, and a cell centres its line in a row taller than one line. The
value opened 8px right and 22px high of where it already sat. `contentRect()`
now measures both after layout and the popover moves so its CONTENT lands on
the cell's content. A clipped name reads at 15px/600 in both places, in place.

Gate: `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` — *a clipped cell expands where its value
already sits* and *a clipped name keeps its type in the expansion*.

## Still open

The rest of the design section is untouched and still wants a specimen: whether
a read surface should stop looking like an editable cell at all, whether the
box carries the field's name, whether chips inside it wrap or the popover
widens, and whether hover needs a delay before it opens (crossing a row of
clipped cells still flashes several in sequence).



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T22:19:34.259Z · fixed · Gerrit 273 → cbec692

**Tests added:**
- test/grid-chrome.test.mjs (a pointer passing through a clipped cell opens nothing)

**Live verification:** Issue table on :4400 (47c98bf, carries 273): four clipped names crossed at 40ms each opened nothing; a pointer resting on one opened the expansion after ~180ms. The open design questions, decided: it stays a read surface with no input-box chrome (border transparent, background none — already so, kept); no field-name caption — the expansion sits on its own cell, under its own column header; chips wrap inside the 380px box rather than the box widening across neighbouring columns; hover waits 180ms. Reopen with a specimen if any of those four should go the other way.

issues.name: 🎫 Outline rail — the label flyout wants design, and a click should pin it
issues.description:
> the outline pop up could be better desinged maybe clicking opens it mor
> epermanently. also select shoudlnint snap and resent the scroll but smoothly
> animate to the section without resetting other nested window scroll, this may
> also be a global generatl problem, if so ticket the isue i weave separately

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against the outline dash rail (`a4a864a`).

Split in two: this issue is the rail's own design, and the scrolling half is **Issue #69**, because it turned out not to be about the rail at all.

## The flyout

Hovering the rail opens the headings as labels — `display: none` until `.doc-rail:hover`, so the resting rail stays a minimap and a dash keeps the tick's own width. It works, and it is the crudest possible version of working:

- **It is hover-only.** There is no way to keep it open, so reading a long outline means holding the pointer inside a 22px gutter the whole time. Kyle: *"maybe clicking opens it more permanently."* A click that pins the panel — and a second click, Esc, or a click outside that unpins it — is the obvious shape. Note the dash's click is already taken by "jump to this section", so pinning needs its own target: the rail's background, a caret at the top of the track, or click-the-rail vs click-a-dash.
- **The panel is the track itself**, grown a background and a border on hover. That is why it can only ever be as tall as the track and why it opens flush against the gutter. A pinned panel probably wants to be its own surface with its own width.
- **It flashes.** Crossing the gutter on the way somewhere else opens the whole outline. A pinned mode makes an open delay reasonable for the hover mode.
- **Long documents.** The track caps at `calc(100vh - 120px)` and scrolls itself; with labels showing, rows go from ~11px to ~21px, so the panel scrolls much sooner than the minimap does. Pinned, it should probably size to its content rather than to the minimap's cap.

## Where the work lives

- `public/app.js` — `attachDashRail()`, `refreshDashRail()`.
- `public/style.css` — `.doc-rail`, `.doc-rail-track`, `.doc-rail-label`.
- `test/doc-rail.test.mjs` + the browser cases in `test/editor-phase4-browser.test.mjs` already pin hover-reveal and the sticky track; a pinned state belongs beside them.

issues.name: 🎫 Programmatic scrolling jumps, and scrolls every ancestor with it
issues.description:
> the outline pop up could be better desinged maybe clicking opens it mor
> epermanently. also select shoudlnint snap and resent the scroll but smoothly
> animate to the section without resetting other nested window scroll, this may
> also be a global generatl problem, if so ticket the isue i weave separately

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against the outline dash rail (`a4a864a`).

Filed separately on Kyle's own instinct — *"this may also be a global general problem, if so ticket the issue in weave separately"*. It is. The rail's half of the report is **Issue #68**.

## The general problem

Every programmatic scroll in the app goes through `Element.scrollIntoView()`, and that method's defined behaviour is to scroll **every scrollable ancestor** of the target, not just the one you meant. Inside weave a document sits in a scrolling body, often inside a peek panel, sometimes inside an expanded document frame — so bringing one heading into view can reset scroll positions the reader never asked about. That is exactly what Kyle saw.

Second half: all of them jump. None animates, and none consults `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Every site, today

| Where | Call | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.js` — the dash rail | `heads[i].scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` | jump to a heading |
| `app.js` — the editor hint list | `.vditor-hint--current?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` | keep the armed slash-menu row visible |
| `app.js` — `setSel()` in the search palette | `rowEls[sel].scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` | keep the selected result visible |

`block: 'nearest'` limits how far each ancestor moves. It does not limit **which** ancestors move.

There is already an ad-hoc patch for the same underlying problem elsewhere: `keepScroll()` saves `window.scrollX/Y` plus the grid scroller's `scrollLeft` and restores them after a redraw. It exists because redraws lose scroll position — and it only knows about two scrollers, which is the same gap one level along.

## Worth noting: the instant jump was a deliberate call, now overruled

The rail's source carries the reasoning:

> Instant, not smooth: a backgrounded tab never runs the animation frames a smooth scroll rides on, and the jump is the point anyway.

The first clause is still true and is the argument for honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` and for not depending on animation frames to *land* the scroll. The second clause was a judgement about what a reader wants, and Kyle has now said otherwise.

## The shape of the fix

One helper, and every call site through it:

- takes a **target** and the **container** it should scroll — resolved explicitly, never left to the ancestor walk;
- animates by default, instantly under `prefers-reduced-motion` or when the document is hidden;
- moves nothing else, so a peek panel, an expanded document and the window keep their positions;
- lands on the final position even if the animation never runs.

`scrollTo({ behavior: 'smooth' })` on a chosen element gets most of this for free — the work is in picking the container and in refusing to touch the others. `keepScroll()` should end up on the same helper rather than keeping its own list.

## Where the work lives

- `public/app.js` — the three call sites above, `keepScroll()`, and wherever the helper lands.
- A pure "which container, and what offset" function belongs in `public/editor-lib.js` beside `currentSection()`, so it is testable without a DOM.

## Replay

Re-run these against this instance, in order. Times are seconds before the
reporter clicked Report, so the last steps are the ones that hurt.

1. `-38.1s` navigated to `#/`
2. `-35.0s` clicked a.nav-db "Issue"
3. `-35.0s` navigated to `#/table/b3ca39b7-1d71-48d1-b212-0531732c9265`
4. `-30.3s` clicked button.k-doc "Open Description (md)"

## Trace

4 actions, 0 errors, 0 requests (0 failed).
Field values are never captured — the recorder keeps control names only,
and secrets are stripped before the report leaves the page.

```json
[
 {
  "kind": "nav",
  "to": "#/",
  "t": 1787763487656
 },
 {
  "kind": "click",
  "target": "a.nav-db \"Issue\"",
  "t": 1787763490767
 },
 {
  "kind": "nav",
  "to": "#/table/b3ca39b7-1d71-48d1-b212-0531732c9265",
  "t": 1787763490779
 },
 {
  "kind": "click",
  "target": "button.k-doc \"Open Description (md)\"",
  "t": 1787763495421
 }
]
```


## Fixed 2026-08-26

**Measured, in the theme Kyle was in.** The code slab in the app is
`--tblr-bg-surface-dark` — `rgb(17, 24, 39)` — in **both** themes, settled that
way by [[Issue#36]] so a code block reads the same at rest and under the caret.
The highlight.js palette, though, followed the page: `github` in light,
`github-dark` in dark. So in light theme a palette drawn for a white page
landed on a near-black slab:

| Token | Colour | On the slab | AA (4.5:1) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.hljs-title.function_` | `#6f42c1` | **2.72:1** | fails |
| `.hljs-keyword` | `#d73a49` | **3.86:1** | fails |

That is the whole report: the tokens were built for a ground they never
landed on.

**The rule now: a palette answers to the surface under it, not to the theme
around it.**

- The editor loads `github-dark` in both themes, because its slab is dark in
  both. Worst token measured live afterwards: **7.04:1** (`.hljs-keyword`,
  `#ff7b72`).
- The standalone document page (`/e/:id/doc.html`) keeps a slab that follows
  the theme, so it keeps a palette that follows it too — but the slab is now
  the ground each palette was drawn for: `#ffffff` in light, `#0d1117` in dark.
  On the old `--soft` grey the github keyword measured 4.27:1, under AA by a
  hair. Its border is what keeps the block a block when the slab matches the
  page.

**Guarded by** two cases in `test/editor-phase4-browser.test.mjs` that compute
WCAG contrast for every token span against the background actually painted
under it, in both themes / both colour schemes. A stylesheet can load and
still lose to another one, so the gate reads colours, not `<link>` tags.

Before and after are attached, same block, same light theme.


## Corrected 2026-08-26 (commit 1595935) — the slab was the wrong half to hold still

Kyle, on the fix above: *"dark code block background in light mode dont make
sense."* He is right. That fix kept the dark slab of [[Issue#36]] in both
themes and moved the palette to match it; the slab should have moved.

**Both halves follow the page now.**

| Theme | Slab | Palette | Ink | Worst token, measured live |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| light | `#ffffff` | github | body colour | **4.57:1** (`.hljs-keyword`) |
| dark | `#0d1117` | github-dark | Kami cream | **13.84:1** |

What survives from the first fix is the reason the slab is those exact
colours: each one is the ground its palette was drawn for. A tinted surface
put the github keyword red at 4.27:1, under AA by a hair — so `--soft` and
`--tblr-bg-surface-dark` are both out of this job, in the editor and on the
document page alike. Sitting that close to the page, the block earns its
border in both themes rather than only in dark.

`--wv-code-bg` in `public/style.css` and the `hljs:` line in `vditorTheme()`
are two halves of one decision, and each comment points at the other.

The gate now asserts Kyle's rule as well as the contrast one: the slab is light
in a light theme and dark in a dark theme, and every token on it clears 4.5:1
either way. Both themes attached, as shipped.

issues.name: A text cell dresses markdown, so a column of literal syntax cannot be read
issues.description: # What happened The Showcase's new `Formatting` table has a `Syntax` column whose whole job is to show the literal markdown for each construct. A text cell renders inline markdown (`span.text-dressed`), so the value `> · *** · backslash` painted as `> · * · backslash`, and `**…** · *…*` painted as a bold ellipsis and an italic one. The stored values were correct throughout; only the reading was wrong. ## Why it matters Dressing a text cell is a good default — a bolded word in a note should read bolded. There is currently no way to say "this cell is literal", so any column holding syntax, a regex, a glob, a format string, or a path with asterisks reads wrong, and the writer has no affordance to fix it. ## Worked around Every `Syntax` value now sits in a code span, which the dressing renders as literal monospace. That is the right answer for this table and no answer at all for a cell that should never have been dressed. ## Shape worth considering A `literal` flag on a text field's config — or a `kind`, the way a document field already carries one — so a column opts out of dressing without every value carrying backticks. Raised 2026-08-26 while writing the Handbook's document-formatting pages. 🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T22:19:34.259Z · fixed · Gerrit 273 → cbec692 **Tests added:** - test/text-literal.test.mjs - test/text-literal-browser.test.mjs **Live verification:** Scratch copy of the weave workspace on the merged code: a text field with config { "literal": true } shows `**…** · *…* · `code`` as typed in its box; the same value in a plain text column is still dressed. The Showcase Formatting table's Syntax column can now drop its backtick workaround: `weave field update "Showcase/Formatting" Syntax --config '{"literal":true}'` (left as is — those values are content).

issues.name: Unify and size the icon vocabulary across field and selection surfaces
issues.description:
**Reported by Kyle, 2026-08-26:** "weave field and selection icons should be expanded, unified and normalized for size"

Two disjoint icon vocabularies live in the app, and neither one has a size scale. A field's icon comes from a 101-name flat SVG set; a select option's icon comes from fourteen typographic marks hard-coded in a different file. Put the two next to each other and they do not line up.

## What each surface draws from today

| Surface | Source | Vocabulary | Rendered size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Space / table icon | `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js` via `iconly:<name>` | 101 flat SVGs | `.wv-icon` inline-flex, svg at natural size, `vertical-align: -2px` |
| Select option / workflow state | `STATE_ICONS` in `public/field-dialog-core.js:118` | 14 unicode marks — `○ ◔ ◑ ◕ ● ✓ ✕ ⏸ ⚑ ★ ! ? →` | `.opt-icon` 24×24 box, `font-size: 13px` |
| Slash menu | per-item `icon` in `public/app.js:3135+`, some iconly | mixed marks + SVG | `.slash-icon` 20px box, `font-size: 12px`, svg 15×15 |
| Bug reporter | iconly | 4 names | `.bug-fab-icon` 16px, `.bug-cat-icon` 12px |
| Workspace rail | letter, image, or iconly | mixed | `.ws-icon` 36px, weave mark 46px |

## Why it reads wrong

A unicode mark carries its own advance width and its own optical size, so `✓` and `●` in one select never occupy the same box, and neither matches an SVG beside them. Every surface then patches its own alignment — `vertical-align: -2px` here, a 24px box with 13px type there — which is five local fixes standing in for one scale.

Selecting an icon is also two different experiences: a table gets a searchable 101-icon picker, a select option gets a fourteen-button strip.

## Shape of the fix

1. **Expand.** Let a select option and a workflow state take any `iconly:<name>`, the same as a table. Keep the typographic marks that carry meaning a glyph cannot (`○ ◔ ◑ ◕ ●` as progress) as a named group inside the one catalogue.
2. **Unify.** One picker component, one catalogue, one `iconEl()` path. `STATE_ICONS` stops being a second vocabulary and becomes a group in the first.
3. **Normalize.** A size scale as CSS custom properties — `--wv-icon-sm` / `-md` / `-lg` — set on the box, with the glyph and the SVG both filling it. No per-surface `vertical-align` patches.

## Tests to add

- The option picker offers the same catalogue as the table picker.
- A glyph option and an SVG option render to the same computed box in both themes.
- An existing `STATE_ICONS` mark still renders after the migration (old rows keep working).



## Evidence

`2026-08-26-field-types-entity-page.png` (attached) — one entity page carrying five icon vocabularies at five sizes: the `⌗` mark on a field definition, the `✱` on a key, `↗` on a lookup, `Σ` on a rollup, `ƒ` on a formula, an avatar on a relation, and coloured pills with no icon at all on select and workflow. Captured with Playwright at 1280×1400 @2x against `:4466`.



## Fixed — change 77, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

`iconChoices` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` is the one catalogue: the thirteen marks first, then the 101 flat names. Both a table's icon and a select option's now open the same searchable picker over it, and every paint site resolves through `iconEl`, so an option or a workflow state can wear a flat icon and draw it. A text-only context drops the `iconly:` prefix rather than spelling it.

Sizes come from `--wv-icon-sm` / `-md` / `-lg` on `:root` — 12 / 16 / 20px — applied to `.wv-icon`, `.slash-icon`, `.bug-fab-icon` and `.bug-cat-icon` in place of five surfaces each carrying their own number.

Guarded by `test/icon-vocabulary-browser.test.mjs` (4 cases, real browser) and three cases in `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`. The size test walks every icon on a page and fails any that draws outside the scale.

The workspace rail (36px, and 46 for the weave mark) is deliberately outside the scale: it is a tile, not an inline icon.



## Normalised — change 80, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

**Kyle, 2026-08-26:** "all should be flat same coloring and similar size now bug quater done and 3/4 done are too small… reflresh is also too small."

The size scale could not reach those. A mark was the Unicode character rendered at the font size, and a font gives every character its own advance and its own optical size — `◔` and `◕` drew small beside a tick, `⟳` smaller still, inside boxes that were already the right size.

`public/mark-icons.js` draws all twenty on the same `0 0 24 24` canvas as the vendored flat set, at one weight: ring 2.5, stroke 2.6, `currentColor`. Beside an Iconly glyph they now read as one family.

**The key is the character.** A state that stored `'✓'` in June resolves through the drawn set and simply starts drawing. Nothing migrated, no value changed shape.

`iconEl` resolves a mark the way it already resolved `iconly:<name>`, so one change carries the chips, the picker list and the field dialog. The chrome controls Kyle grouped with them draw from the same set: refresh, expand, copy, back, close, the year arrows in the date popover, and the theme circles — which turned out to be the progress family already.

**Letters stay letters.** `ƒ` is a function, `Σ` is a sum, `B` is bold, `¶` is a paragraph. Drawing those as pictures would say less than the letterform does, so they are deliberately absent from the set.

Two marks were caught drawing small by the new gate and redrawn: the cross now spans 5.5–18.5, the pause bars 4.1–19.9.

### Tests
`test/mark-icons.test.mjs` — every pickable mark has a shape, the key is the stored character, one stroke weight across the set, letters excluded. Two browser cases measure the **painted** extent of every mark (bbox plus half the stroke) and fail any that overflows the canvas or spans less than 15 of 24 — which is exactly the defect Kyle reported, a shape drawing small inside a correct box.

Verified live on `:4466`: every icon on an entity page draws at 16px, and the table icon picker lists 114 vector rows across both dialects.



## Closed 2026-08-31 — 82f8e10, 83cf448, ed47705

Expanded, unified, normalised, then trimmed:

* **One catalogue.** `iconChoices` serves every gate — space, table, select option, workflow state. No marks-versus-flat-set split: both sort into eleven groups in `ICON_CATEGORIES`, marks leading their own because they say a state where the flat icons name a thing.
* **Drawn, not typed.** 25 marks as flat vectors on the Iconly canvas at one weight (ring 2.5, stroke 2.6). The key is still the character, so nothing migrated.
* **One size scale.** `--wv-icon-sm/md/lg` = 12/16/20px. Five vendored icons drew short of the canvas and are scaled about the centre; a test fails any icon under 17 of 24.
* **Trimmed.** 23 near-duplicates left the offer, 16 of them arrows. Hidden from the picker, never from the data.
* **Money filled in.** Eight drawn icons — dollar, euro, card, coins, invoice, bank, trend, percent — in the same `iconly:` namespace, the vendored set resolving first.
* **A grid, not a list.** No name beside any icon, no numbered quick-select, category headings the only labels, search taking a name or a category, `No icon` as the first cell.
* **A dead reference stops printing itself.** `iconly:<unknown>` was drawing weave's own storage format into the icon slot; it draws a ghost ring with the name in the tooltip.

_Closed 2026-08-31._

_Running on `:4400`; the change is Verified in the review queue and waiting on Code-Review +2, with nine changes ahead of it._

issues.description:
**Reported by Kyle, 2026-08-26:** "formatting showcase could all be done in one entity's description"

`Showcase/Formatting` spends twelve rows demonstrating what one document can hold. Row 12, "One page using all of it", already carries the whole demonstration in a single description — the other eleven are that page cut into pieces and given a table to live in.

## The twelve rows today

| 1 | Headings and folds | Structure | 623 chars |
| 2 | Lists and task lists | Block | 315 |
| 3 | Quote, divider, line break | Block | 414 |

| 12 | One page using all of it | Structure | 583 |

Roughly 5,800 characters total, and a reader has to open twelve records to see a renderer that a single scroll would prove.

## Shape of the fix

Fold every construct into one description, ordered the way the handbook introduces them, each section still written in the construct it names. The `Construct` and `Syntax` columns survive as a markdown table inside that same document, which is itself another thing the page demonstrates.

## Decide before doing

- Keep `Showcase/Formatting` as a one-row table, or retire the table and move the page into `Handbook/Guide` or `Wiki/Article`?
- Anything currently linking to a specific row needs its link repointed.

## Tests to update

`test/handbook.test.mjs` asserts against the seeded showcase rows; the seed in `src/weaver-seed.js` writes them. Both move together with the content.



## Fixed — change 77, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

`Showcase/Formatting` is one row: **Every construct on one page** (#13). Every sample body moved over verbatim behind a divider — a section that demonstrates a construct still demonstrates it — with a lead-in and the Syntax column surviving as a table inside the page it describes.

The table was kept rather than retired, so links to `Showcase/Formatting` still resolve. The eleven rows it replaced are in the trash, not deleted.

One sentence was edited: 'This page has six, so the rail is there' became 'This section alone has six', because the count stopped being true on a combined page.

`src/handbook.js` builds the page from `FORMATTING_SAMPLES`, so the samples remain the editable source. Guarded by two new cases in `test/handbook.test.mjs`: every sample body is present, and re-applying updates the page instead of seeding twelve beside it.

issues.name: Clearing a field definition takes one click and cannot be taken back
issues.description:
**Reported by Kyle, 2026-08-26:** "i deleted a definition by mistake to see what the X did, this doesnt make sense"

Kyle clicked the `×` beside the `Definition` value on `Showcase/Field Types` #1 "Sensor board" to find out what it did. It destroyed the definition on the spot — no confirm, no toast, no visible undo. The row went from `number · currency EUR, 2 decimals` to `—`.

A `field` value is not an ordinary cell. It IS a field definition — type plus config — and it is the one value on the page a single click can erase beyond guessing. Attachments have the same `×` and lose a file that still exists in blob storage; a field definition has no copy anywhere.

## Root cause

`public/app.js:1387`

```js
box.append(el('button', {
  class: 'btn btn-sm btn-ghost-secondary tiny', title: 'Clear the definition',
  onclick: () => patch(null),
}, '×'));
```

`patch(null)` fires straight from the click handler. The chip beside it opens a modal to *edit* the definition; the button next to that modal-opening chip deletes it with no dialog at all. Two adjacent controls, opposite levels of ceremony.

The title, "Clear the definition", reads like clearing a text box. Nothing tells the reader that the type and its config go with it.

## Recovery on this row

Restored from `src/weaver-seed.js:89` — `{ type: 'number', config: { format: 'currency', unit: 'EUR', decimals: 2 } }` — by `PATCH /api/entities/98f4111d-1d4d-4c96-95ce-25b5c21e8288`. The value came back only because this row is seeded. A definition Kyle had authored himself would be gone.

`POST /api/undo` exists in `src/routes.js:343` and the UI never mentions it at the moment of loss.

## Shape of the fix

1. **Confirm before erasing a definition.** Name what disappears — "Clear the `number · currency EUR` definition?" — not a bare yes/no.
2. **Offer the way back.** A toast carrying an Undo action wired to `POST /api/undo`, so the modal stays out of the way for the reversible cases.
3. **Rank the two controls.** A destructive `×` should not sit at the same weight as the chip that opens the editor. Demote it, move it into the edit modal as "Clear definition", or both.
4. Check every other `×` that calls `patch(null)` or removes an item — attachments (`public/app.js:1409`), relation chips (`:1309`, `:846`) — against the same test: does a single click destroy something with no copy elsewhere?

## Tests to add

- Clicking `×` on a `field` value opens a confirm and leaves the definition intact when dismissed.
- After a confirmed clear, undo restores the exact `{type, config}`.



## Evidence

`2026-08-26-field-types-entity-page.png` (attached) — the entity page after the definition was restored, showing the `×` that sits beside `Definition` and `Nested definition`. Kyle's original screenshot was pasted in chat and never saved to disk; this is a reproduction capture taken with Playwright at 1280×1400 @2x against `:4466`, same page, same row.



## Fixed — change 77, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

The bare `×` is gone. Clearing now lives inside the definition editor, beside the definition it would take, behind `holdToConfirm` — the house gesture, the same one the trash row uses. Releasing early cancels.

What it takes, it offers straight back: a toast carrying an Undo that restores the exact `{type, config}`, not a walk back through the global undo stack.

The offer can also name what went. `#displayValue`'s `field` case said 'number' for the definition Kyle lost; it now says `number · currency EUR`, and carries the costume for dates, documents and nested definitions too.

Guarded by `test/field-definition-browser.test.mjs` (3 cases, real browser): no bare cross on the row, a cancelled hold changes nothing, a completed hold clears and the undo restores.

**On step 4 of the plan above** — the other crosses were checked and left alone. A relation `×` unlinks a record that still exists and re-links in one click. An attachment `×` removes an id from the column while the blob stays in storage. Neither destroys a value with no copy anywhere, which was what made this one different.



_Closed 2026-08-31. Clearing lives in the definition editor behind holdToConfirm and offers the exact `{type, config}` back._

issues.name: A daterange value renders as [object Object]
issues.description:
**Found alongside Issue #90, 2026-08-26.** Kyle's screenshot of `Showcase/Field Types` #1 "Sensor board" shows the `Window` field, type `daterange`, rendered as:

```
Window    [object Object]
```

Every other value on that page renders — `Due` as `2026-09-15`, `Start` as `8/1/2026`, `Published` as `Aug 20, 2026 14:3…`. The date range alone leaks its object.

## Root cause

`#displayValue` in `src/engine.js:2587` carries a case for `select`, `multiselect`, `workflow`, `field`, `key`, `attachments`, `date`, `number`, `formula`, and `relation`. It has no case for `daterange`, so the stored `{ start, end }` falls through to the default return and the browser stringifies it.

The normaliser at `src/engine.js:2296` stores the range correctly. Only the read side is missing.

## Shape of the fix

Add a `daterange` case that formats both ends through the same path `date` already uses — `field.config.format` and `field.config.time` applied to `start` and `end`, joined with an en dash. `2026-08-01 – 2026-09-15` under the default format, `Aug 1 – Sep 15, 2026` when a format is set.

The date case at `src/engine.js:2612` is the code to reuse rather than reimplement; both ends should agree on format, and a range inside one year should not print the year twice.

## Tests to add

- A `daterange` value renders as text in `fields`, never as an object.
- The range honours the field's `format` and `time` config, matching what a `date` field does with the same config.
- A cross-year range prints both years.



## Evidence

`2026-08-26-field-types-entity-page.png` (attached) — `Window    [object Object]` sits between `Published` and `Done`. Reproduction capture with Playwright at 1280×1400 @2x against `:4466`; Kyle's original chat screenshot shows the identical row.



## Fixed — changes 77 and 78, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

`#displayValue` has a `daterange` case. Both ends wear the same costume, mirrored in `public/date-core.js` as `formatDateRange` and contract-tested against the engine the way single dates already were. A long range inside one year says the year once — 'Aug 1 – Sep 15, 2026'; across years it says both.

The field's `format` and `time` reach a daterange now as they do a date: through `normalizeSelfContainedConfig`, through `updateField`, and out to the client in the schema payload.

The row also stopped being a text box that could only produce a value the server must refuse. A range edits as two date controls sharing a dash, and commits only when both ends read as dates.

**A second leak, one panel down.** The activity feed did `String(v)` on the stored value, so the history painted '[object Object]' too. Fixed in change 78: an object with a start or an end reads through the range costume, any other object gives its name or its JSON.

Guarded by `test/daterange-browser.test.mjs` (4 cases, real browser) and six in `test/date-core.test.mjs`. Verified live: the entity page now carries zero occurrences of the string.



_Closed 2026-08-31. `daterange` has a display case and a two-control editor; the activity feed no longer leaks the object either._

_Running on `:4400`; the change is Verified in the review queue and waiting on Code-Review +2, with nine changes ahead of it._

## What it actually was — four faults, 2026-08-26

Kyle named them after the trace was filed:

> the peak expand overflowwed cells on hover was wrong and not in line with
> exisitng entry posiiton, also both comfortbale and compact cell size expanded
> too much with new empty doc placeholder. also the relation icon in thelated
> entities did not open the entity as expected and x is not necessary in table
> view relations, only in the edit menue

| # | Fault | Cause | Measured before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The clipped-cell expansion opens beside the value, not over it | `showCellPop()` pinned the popover's BORDER box to the cell's. The cell pads 9px/4px, the popover 8px/10px over a 1px border, and a cell centres its line in a row taller than one line | content 8px right / 22px high → **0 / 0** |
| 2 | An empty document chip inflates every row | Tabler ships a global `.empty` (`display:flex; flex-direction:column; height:100%; padding:1rem`) and `docChips()` wrote that exact class name onto the chip | comfortable 85px, compact 71px → **45 / 35**; the chip itself 66px → **24** |
| 3 | The ↗ on a relation chip does not open the record | The mark was `.k-rel::after` — a pseudo-element of the CHIP, outside its `<a>`. The one pixel advertising navigation was the one pixel that did nothing | dead → the whole chip is the link |
| 4 | `×` on every relation chip in a grid | Unlinking is an edit and a grid is a record | gone from compact surfaces; the entity page keeps its × |

Fault 1 also carried the font half of Issue #67 — the clone lands outside the
`<td>`, so `td.name-cell .inline-edit` (15px/600) stops matching it and a
clipped name changed size at the moment you hovered it to read it. Both are
fixed the same way: computed type is copied onto every clone, and the popover
is moved so its content lands on the cell's content.

## Where it landed

`public/app.js` — `showCellPop()` + `copyCellType()` + `contentRect()`, the
relation branch of `editorFor()`, `docChips()`, the attachments chip.
`public/style.css` — `.k-rel > a::after`, `.k-rel > a`, `.k-doc.is-empty`.

Gate: `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs`, eight cases through a real browser — each
fault is a measurement the source can lie about. Full suite green (945 tests).

Commit `05e09d0`, Gerrit change **71**, Verified +1. Waiting on Code-Review +2:
changes 64–71 submit as one stack.

## Fixed 2026-09-02 (Gerrit change 169)

The lost note's three subjects, plus a fourth found reproducing the replay:
- **Clipped-cell expansion** now copies the cell's own typography (font family/size/weight/style, letter-spacing, line-height, color, text-align) — the pop shows MORE of the value, never a restyled version (also resolves the overlap with [[Issue#67]]).

issues.name: Every toast was invisible — Tabler switched them off
issues.description:
**Found while fixing Issue #90, 2026-08-26.** Every toast weave has ever raised was invisible.

Tabler ships `.toast:not(.show){display:none}` — Bootstrap's toast, which waits for JavaScript to reveal it. Weave hand-rolls its own toast in `public/app.js:75` and gave it the same class name, so the framework switched off every message the app produced: `Saved`, an error's real reason, a validation failure. The code ran, the element landed in the DOM, and nothing appeared.

Nothing in the source looked wrong, which is why the browser had to make the claim. A CSS read of `public/style.css` shows a fully styled toast: fixed, bottom right, `z-index: 2000`. The rule that switches it off lives in a vendored file nobody was reading.

This is the second collision of its kind in a day — `.empty` on a chip inherited Tabler's full-height flex column and took a comfortable row from 43px to 85. A bare, common class name is the pattern to watch.

## The fix

`.toast` → `.wv-toast`, `.toast-action` → `.wv-toast-action`, in `public/app.js` and `public/style.css`.

Toasts also stacked on one another at the same fixed corner, which no one could see while they were invisible. They now sit in a `#wv-toasts` layer, newest at the bottom, `column-reverse` with an 8px gap.

## Tests that now guard it

`test/toast-browser.test.mjs` — a raised toast occupies the screen, an action inside one can be clicked, and two toasts do not overlap. Asserted through a real browser, because reading the CSS is exactly what missed this.

## Worth a sweep

Every bare class name weave defines that Bootstrap or Tabler also defines. `.toast` and `.empty` were found by accident, one day apart.



## Fixed — change 77, Verified, awaiting Code-Review +2

`.toast` → `.wv-toast`, `.toast-action` → `.wv-toast-action`, off the Tabler global entirely.

Toasts also stack now, in a `#wv-toasts` layer, newest at the bottom with an 8px gap. They had been landing on one another at the same fixed corner, which nobody could see while they were invisible.

Guarded by `test/toast-browser.test.mjs` — a raised toast occupies the screen, an action inside one can be clicked, two toasts do not overlap. Asserted through a browser, because reading the CSS is exactly what missed this.



_Closed 2026-08-31. `.wv-toast`, off the Tabler global, stacking in a layer._

_Running on `:4400`; the change is Verified in the review queue and waiting on Code-Review +2, with nine changes ahead of it._



---
**v0.5 triage (2026-09-02):** Verified fixed: toasts renamed wv-toast to escape Tabler's .toast display:none (app.js:75, style.css:837).

issues.name: The Quality mirror is 28 test files behind
issues.description:
**Found while mirroring the four suites added for Issues #87, #90, #91 and #94, 2026-08-26.**

`Quality/Suite` claims to mirror the test suites. It holds 48 files; `test/` holds 76. Twenty-eight suites have never been mirrored, and one case row was still carrying a name a test was renamed away from.

The mandate in `weave/CLAUDE.md` is explicit — "when test suites change, update `Quality/Suite` + `Quality/Case` rows (suite per test file, case per test, rollup counts must match `node --test` reality)". The mirror drifts because nothing checks it.

## Unmirrored as of today

```
accounts-audit        attachments-field     bug-panel-browser     bug-report
chip-system           code-detect           doc-chips             doc-rail
editor-highlight      editor-math           editor-refs           field-type
graph-parse           handbook              heading-folds         inline-text-cell
key-field             ledger-grid           number-format         relmap-layout
saved-views           schema-apply          service               system-fields
worker
```

The four browser suites added today — `daterange`, `field-definition`, `toast`, `icon-vocabulary` — are mirrored, with the skip stubs left out so the rollups match what `node --test` actually runs.

## Shape of the fix

A test that reads `test/` and asserts the mirror agrees: one Suite row per file, one Case row per `test(` call, no rows for cases that no longer exist, and a `Case Count` rollup equal to the count on disk. A skip stub — the `test('x (browser)', { skip })` a browser suite falls back to — is not a case and must not be counted.

Once the check exists, backfill the twenty-five above in one pass, then the mirror stays honest because a drifting mirror fails the suite.

The seed's `suiteData` in `src/weaver-seed.js` still lists nine suites by hand. It should read the directory rather than name files.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-08T04:36:24Z · started · session wf-0907-2105

---

**Fixed 2026-09-08 — commit 8431aec, Gerrit 297.**

The backfill and the generator landed earlier in 8ef6210 (src/quality-mirror.js scans test/, syncQualityMirror reconciles a workspace to the scan, the seed no longer hand-lists suites, test/quality-mirror.test.mjs gates it). What was left was this Issue's "one Suite row per file" clause: the live mirror held **182 rows for 180 files**, because test/applet.test.mjs and test/structure-trash.test.mjs each carried two.

**Cause — not a rename.** syncQualityMirror keyed the workspace's existing rows into a Map by File, so a second row carrying the same File overwrote the first. The loser was then invisible to both passes: never renamed, never reconciled against the scan, and never pruned, because the prune loop walked the same collapsed Map. It outlived every reconcile. (The Structure trash pair shared an identical Name, so display-name drift was not the trigger — plain duplicate-File tolerance was.)

**Fix.** Rows are grouped by File instead of overwritten. The oldest row wins, keeping the id anything already linking to that suite points at, and every twin joins the same doomed list as a suite whose file left the tree. weave quality check therefore reports the drift it used to skip.

**Verification.** Against a copy of the live workspace, quality check went from removedSuites 0 (old code, blind to the twins) to removedSuites 2 / removedCases 49 / renamedSuites 1, and a sync then left 180 rows for 180 distinct File values. Full suite on merged main: 1952 tests, fail 0, skipped 0. The live mirror on :4400 collapsed on its own through the watcher's post-landing sync — no row was hand-deleted — and now reads 180 Suite rows for the 180 *.test.mjs files in git ls-tree 8431aec test, with no file unmirrored and no row stale.

## Update 2026-09-26: live chips on the entity page (Issue #379, f294dd4)

The entity page's live `[[…]]` chips changed in three ways, which cover part of this row:

- A chip shows the target record's name. `[[Task#1]]` used to read "# Task#1 - Design onboarding wizard", clipped to "# Task#1 -"; it now reads "# Design onboarding wizard", and the `Task#1 - Name` form shows on hover. The resolver sends the name as `data-name`; exports keep the longer label.
- The tint and the soft ring sit on the label, so the chip ends where the name ends. The anchor underneath is an opaque cover over the literal: `[[Project#2|Hermes Docs]]` went from 174px of tint to 93px.
- The cover is 2px taller than the text box, so bracket tails no longer peek out below the chip.

Still open here: the chip can only take the literal's width, because the overlay cannot move the text around it. A bare `[[Task#1]]` ellipsizes a long name, and an aliased reference leaves a blank gap where its literal was longer than the name. The full fix is a rendered reading state for documents, where chips flow as inline elements.


Still real, 2026-09-28. Measured on :4400 on Issue #65's page, Chromium and WebKit: the hand-typed [[Issue#64]] and [[Issue#165]] chips are held to their literals' widths, 81 px and 90 px, and each record name ellipsizes after a few characters. That is the literal-width limit the 2026-09-26 note names; the rendered reading state is still the fix.

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution
- Fixed looks like: a reference in a document reads as a whole chip with the record's full name, as a Notion mention does, and never ellipsizes inside the width of its `[[…]]` source.
- Root cause: `refreshRefChips` (`public/app.js:10292`) paints each chip as an overlay sized to the literal's client rect (`:10351`, `width:${r.width}px`), because Vditor owns the IR DOM and Lute cannot be taught chips. Reproduced today: 81 px and 90 px chips on Issue #65's page, names cut off.
- The change depends on the decision below.

## Approach
- Test first: in `test/entity-hierarchy-browser.test.mjs`, a bare `[[Task#1]]` whose name is longer than its literal reads whole (label scrollWidth equals clientWidth), light and dark.
- Size: L for (a), S for (b).
- Risks: Kyle ruled the rendered document is the editing surface with no edit mode or save button (weave-document-editor-is-the-renderer); option (a) must not bring back a visible toggle.
- **Decision needed:** Options: (a) a rendered reading state that swaps to the live editor on the first click or focus, with no button, so chips flow inline; (b) keep the overlay and have the `#` picker and a save-time pass write every reference as `[[Table#n|Name]]`, so the literal is about as wide as the name; (c) accept the limit. Recommend (b) first: small and inside the ruling; (a) is the full answer if Kyle accepts a focus swap.

## Fixed 2026-09-05 (commit aebe974, Gerrit 235)

The drag floor was the engine's bare 60px, so a header could be dragged narrower than its own label. The floor is now the label's measured width (icon + text + sort arrow) plus the header's padding — the right pad is where the ⋮ sits — and never below 60px; the rule is `WeaveColumnResize.floor` in `public/column-resize.js`. Tests: `test/column-resize.test.mjs` (pure floor cases) and `test/column-fit.test.mjs` (a −400px drag stops at the label, unclipped, and the stored width respects the same floor). Handbook grid guide names the label floor.

issues.name: Keyboard ↑↓ could not reach Delete field in the column menu
issues.description:
**Found while redesigning the column ⋮ menu, 2026-08-27. Fixed in the same change.**

`showPopover` builds its arrow-key walk from the rows it can see:

```js
const opts = [...pop.querySelectorAll('.chip-pop-row')];
```

Every row in the field menu was a `.chip-pop-row` except one. The delete row came from `holdToConfirm`, which rendered a Tabler `.dropdown-item`:

```js
const btn = el('button', { class: 'dropdown-item text-danger hold-btn', type: 'button' }, fill, text);
```

So ↑↓ walked Edit → Insert → Sort ascending → Sort descending → Clear sort and stopped. **A keyboard-only user could open the menu and never arrive at Delete field.** Tab closed the popover rather than moving on to it, and Escape handed focus back to the ⋮ — there was no key sequence that reached the row at all.

It looked like a styling mismatch (different padding, different radius, a label starting at its own left edge) and it was that too, which is how it survived: the visual defect was the only symptom anyone reported.

## Fix

`holdToConfirm` takes a `rowClass`, defaulting to `'dropdown-item'` so the other four call sites are untouched; the field menu passes `'chip-pop-row wv-menu-row wv-menu-danger'`. Same row, same walk.

## Gate

`test/field-menu-browser.test.mjs` → *"the arrow walk reaches the delete row"* — presses ArrowDown eight times from a freshly-opened menu and asserts the focused element's text matches `Delete field`, naming every row it visited when it does not. Fails against the pre-change `public/`.

issues.name: A deleted description comes back on the next open
issues.description:
Deleting a table's `Description` document field appeared to work and did not stick. `#migrate` runs on every constructor, found the table had zero document fields, and re-minted `Description` — so the field returned on the next server start, CLI invocation or import.

The migration could not tell "never had one" from "deliberately deleted", because it inferred the answer from the fields rather than being told. `deleteField` now sets `db.descriptionFieldId = null`, and that null is the tombstone `#ensureDescriptionField` reads.

Gate: `test/description-field.test.mjs` — "a deleted description stays deleted across a reload" and "the tombstone survives export and import".

issues.name: A renamed Issue description throws the bug report away
issues.description:
`POST /api/bug-report` filed the report as `docs: { Description: report.markdown }`. Rename the Issue table's description to anything else and `#resolveDocField` throws `'Description' is not a document field of 'Issue'` — and the handler does not catch, so the whole report was lost over a label edit, on the one workspace where renaming things is the point.

The handler resolves through `descriptionField(issues)` instead, and a table with no description at all files the row without a document rather than 400ing.

Gate: `test/bug-report.test.mjs` — "a report still files when the Issue description has been renamed".

issues.name: A schema round-trip duplicates a renamed description and revives a deleted one
issues.description:
`applySchema`'s create path skipped any descriptor named `Name` or `Description` on the assumption `createTable` had already made them. Two failures followed, both verified:

- a table whose description had been renamed to `Notes` came back as **Name + Notes + a spurious second Description**;
- a table whose description had been **deleted** came back with one anyway, because the schema had no way to say "none".

`describeSchema` now emits `role: "description"`, and applying it renames the minted field rather than guessing at the name — deleting it when no descriptor claims the role. A schema document written before roles still works: a document field literally named `Description` is adopted, not duplicated.

Gate: `test/schema-roundtrip.test.mjs` — four cases, including the pre-role back-compat one.

issues.name: Applet bug reports were filed nowhere, and said they were filed
issues.description:
Found by Kyle from the phone, 2026-08-28: *"bug from the rest rite not captured"*.

The applet's bug sheet posted `{title, description, symptoms, context}` at `POST /api/bug-report`, which reads `{categories, note, events, client}`. `renderBugReport` is the validator too, so every report threw before anything was written — **400, every time**.

The second half was worse. The sheet used a bare `fetch` and never looked at the status, so it said **"Reported"** regardless. A week of reports would have gone into the void with a green toast over it.

## Fixed

The four real category ids (`slow`, `broken-ui`, `wrong-data`, `error`) from `src/bugreport.js`, the contract's own field names, `res.ok` checked before claiming anything, and the issue number shown back to the reporter. Two tests pin it: one on the payload shape, one that files a report the way the applet files it and finds the Issue.

issues.name: timingSafeEqual disagrees with itself on workerd when handed pooled Buffers
issues.description:
The hosted applet refused the right passcode. Both sides measured eight bytes — verified live with a length-only probe — and `timingSafeEqual` still returned false.

`Buffer.from(string)` pools its memory: a short Buffer is a window onto a shared 8KB arena, not a tight array. workerd's `timingSafeEqual` compares the backing store rather than the view, so two identical passcodes disagree on Cloudflare while agreeing on node.

## Fixed

`TextEncoder().encode()` hands back an exactly-sized array, and the comparison tells the truth. Worth remembering anywhere a secret is compared in code that has to run on both adapters.

issues.name: The vendored decklet engine fails the Worker upload, for every route
issues.description:
`wrangler deploy` refused the whole script:

```
Uncaught TypeError: The "path" argument must be of type string or an instance of URL. Received undefined
  at fileURLToPath (node-internal:internal_url:155:15)
  at src/vendor/decklet/create.mjs:20:27
```

`create.mjs` resolves its own directory from `import.meta.url` at module scope, which is undefined inside a bundled Worker. `src/routes.js` imported it eagerly, so a feature nobody was calling took down every route on the hosted instance — and is the likely reason Feature #84 never got past an empty deploy.

## Fixed

`src/deck.js` is now loaded on demand inside the two deck routes. Decks stay node-only either way (the engine reads its templates off disk), but nothing else pays for that.

issues.name: Import drops a plain number field
issues.description:
Found while seeding the hosted instance from `uno.db`, 2026-08-28.

`GET /api/export` → `POST /api/import` round-trips 12 tables and 119 entities, but `Product/Task.Estimate` — a plain `number` field — is missing on the far side. So are `Project Budget` (lookup) and `Size` (formula), which may well be deliberate for derived fields; **Estimate is not derived and should have survived.**

Local:

```
Name, Description, Estimate, Due, Priority, Tags, State, Project, Spec, Project Budget, Size, Assignee, test, daste
```

Hosted after import:

```
Name, Description, Due, Priority, Tags, State, Project, Spec, Assignee, test, daste
```

Not blocking the applet, which is field-driven and simply shows what the table has. It does mean **import is not yet a faithful move**, which matters for anyone using it to migrate a workspace.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T10:33:01.779Z · started · session 0907-0302

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07 · **fixed** · merged `8cab0d9` (Gerrit change 243)

**Root cause.** Not the JSON in or the JSON out — `exportJSON`/`importJSON` round-trip `db.fields` faithfully on every store (node file, in-memory, CFStore) and over HTTP; that was checked against this commit and against the 2026-08-28 tree, and neither drops a field. What every surface actually *lists* is `db.fieldOrder`: the grid, `describeSchema()` and so `GET /api/schema`, the CSV header, and the phone applet all walk the order and never `db.fields`. A field the order has forgotten is present in the workspace and invisible everywhere — which is exactly the report: same 12 tables, same entity count, three columns gone. `importJSON` copied the incoming order across verbatim, so a hole in it survived the move.

**Fix.** `#migrate()` — which runs on every open and on every import — now reconciles a table's order with its fields: an id naming no field is dropped, a field the order forgot is appended, and the repair is saved once instead of re-derived on each open. Registry tables are reconciled too; they list columns like any other table. `updateTable` already refuses a partial order, so this only ever repairs state that arrived from outside.

**Derived fields were never excluded.** `Project Budget` (lookup) and `Size` (formula) went missing by the same mechanism as `Estimate` and come back with it — nothing in import filters derived fields, so no decision about them was needed.

**Verification.** Repro built as a damaged export (Task's order missing Estimate / Project Budget / Size, the fields still in place). Before the fix the far side listed `Name, Description, Due, Project, Chip, Card`; after it lists all nine with `Estimate` reading 5 and 13 and `Project Budget` reading 100. Re-run against the live app on :4400 after the landing (`/api/health` sha `8cab0d9`, startedAt 10:57:52Z, submit 10:56:43Z) — no longer reproduces. Screenshots attached: `before-light.png`, `after-light.png`, `live-4400-after.png`. Both themes checked; the grid chrome is unchanged apart from the columns returning.

**Tests.** `test/import-faithful.test.mjs` — an untouched export imports column for column; a forgotten field returns to the grid, `describeSchema` and the CSV header carrying its value; a dangling order id is dropped without moving anything else; a damaged `.db` heals when it is opened and stays healed; a deleted column is not resurrected; a trashed table keeps its columns. Full suite 1763 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.

issues.name: Expanding a markdown document full-screen throws

issues.name: ⌘K search ignored publicId — #143 never ranked the entity numbered 143
issues.description:
search() scored only the entity name (+10) and doc/comment text (+5); the needle was never compared against publicId. A query like #143 (or 143, or task #143) only surfaced entities whose text happened to contain the digits — the entity actually numbered 143 scored 0 and was dropped.

Fix (commit 9982a6d): parse the needle for an id form — #143, bare 143, or a table-scoped task #143 — and give an exact publicId hit score 20, above the name match, with the optional table prefix matched against the table name or its qualified name. universalSearch inherits it, so the ⌘K palette puts numbered entities on top.

Tests: test/docs-and-search.test.mjs — search ranks an exact publicId match above text matches; universalSearch puts a #id entity hit on top. Full suite 1162 pass.

issues.name: Stale server process serves new app.js against an old engine — creates fail until restart
issues.description:
2026-08-28: the :4400 server booted 07:54, commit 3f3075d (table view config fields) landed 07:57. Static assets (app.js, style.css) are read from disk per request, but src/* is loaded at boot — so the browser ran new client code against the pre-commit engine and + New / shift-enter row creation failed silently. A second boot attempt died on EADDRINUSE while the stale process held the port. Fix shape: (a) run under weave service install so launchd owns the process, (b) a version stamp in /api/health that app.js compares to its own and banners a mismatch, (c) ship-cycle hook restarting :4400 after any weave commit. At minimum (b) makes the failure loud instead of silent.

issues.name: Entity field reorder: highlighted row read as a swap, columns reshuffled on every move
issues.description:
**Reported by Kyle, 2026-08-28.** On the entity page, dragging a value field highlighted the whole target row — it read as a swap — and because `.entity-values` was a row-major CSS grid, a field's column was emergent from its index: one reorder reshuffled every later field across columns.

**Fix (d834dbf):**
- `.entity-values` is now CSS multicol (`column-count` 1/2/3 under the same container-query ladder) — column-major flow, so a reorder that stays inside a column leaves the other columns alone; only the boundary row can change columns.
- The drop cue is one horizontal line above or below the row under the pointer (`drop-before`/`drop-after` on the rows' existing 2px transparent borders), picked by pointer height against the row's midpoint. The same midpoint decides the landing side, replacing the DOM-order `compareDocumentPosition` direction for field drops.
- The container catches drops in the gap under a column's last row, so the bottom of a column is reachable.
- Dead `fieldrow[data-wide]` span rule removed (never set from JS).

**Evidence:** `test/entity-value-grid-browser.test.mjs` 11/11 (new: column-major reading order, midpoint cue sides + dragend sweep, within-column stability); `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` contract updated. Verified live on :4400 — 3-column flow, bottom-edge blue line on the drop-after row, cue swept on dragend.

issues.name: Applet mark smears on iOS — WebKit renders SVG masks in with ragged edges
issues.description: Reported by Kyle from the phone 2026-08-28 ("the logo is broken"). The rope mark was referenced as . WebKit rasterizes an SVG luminance mask inside an with ragged, feathered edges — the under-gaps render as dark smears. Chrome renders the same file clean, which is why it never showed on desktop. Fix (627bb57 + cb32d67): the applet header, the gate, and the desktop rail inline the mark via markParts() with namespaced mask ids (mL/mD, gL/gD, hL/hD). Mark geometry moved to src/mark.js (dependency-free) so the worker bundles it; brand/build-logos.mjs re-exports with byte-identical output. Verified in Playwright WebKit: gate and header render clean; deployed to weave-uno worker version 0de2eb0a.

issues.name: Applet keyboard dead after a resume — iOS keeps focus but drops the keyboard
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle from the phone 2026-08-28 ("auto cursor new task entry keyboard functionality is broken"). On backgrounding, iOS drops the keyboard but leaves the compose field focused; the first tap after a resume lands on an already-focused input and raises nothing (the exact poison the applet documents for load-time focus). The one-shot armFirstTouch grab had also already been consumed.

Fix (627bb57): visibilitychange blurs the input on hide so the next tap is a fresh focus, and re-arms the first-touch grab on show (armFirstTouch made re-armable via grabArmed, no listener stacking). Covered by test "a resume gets a fresh first tap"; suite 1185/1185.

Its cause was a rollup or lookup whose target field had been deleted — #resolve read `targetDb.fields[...]` on a dangling id — which crashed every read that reached the row. ae1f150 fixed that as Issue #206 and made deleteField refuse while a reader exists. uno's Project table still carries the scar in its description: a "Total Estimate" rollup over Task estimates, with no Estimate field left on Task. Probed today against the live table: a bare query, every workflow/rollup/relation filter shape the grid can send, and a missing-field path all answer 200 or a readable 400/404 — never a 500. No speculative engine change was invented for a crash that is already gone.

**What was fixed here:** the endless skeleton, which was a defect of its own and survived on every route. showDatabase's rejection had no catch above it, and paintSkeleton had already replaced #main, so the page held the skeleton of a table that was never going to arrive. issues.name: Cannot remove a workspace once created
issues.description:
**Pain point.** A workspace, once created, cannot be deleted from the UI or API — there is no workspace delete route (confirmed by the 2026-08-30 regression-gate review: space and table delete exist, workspace delete does not).

**Expected.** A workspace can be removed with confirmation, its .db file moved to a recoverable trash location rather than hard-deleted.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #5)

issues.name: Default config in a new workspace does not make sense
issues.description:
**Pain point.** The starter content seeded into a brand-new workspace is confusing as a first-run experience — the default space/table/field set does not read as a sensible blank slate.

**Expected.** A new workspace opens with a minimal, self-explaining starter, not scaffolding the user has to delete.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #6)

issues.name: Empty-schema banner 'This table has no fields beyond…' is not needed
issues.description:
**Pain point.** A table with only built-in fields shows the banner "This table has no fields beyond…" — noise that reads as breakage rather than help.

**Expected.** Drop the banner; the grid and the field-add affordance already communicate the state.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #7)

issues.name: Shift+Enter to create another record — cursor/focus is dropped
issues.description:
**Pain point.** Using Shift+Enter to save-and-create-another record, the cursor/focus is dropped instead of landing in the new row, breaking rapid entry.

**Expected.** Shift+Enter commits the row and immediately focuses the next new record's first editable cell.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #8; title truncated in the photo at 'cursor dr…')

**2026-09-05.** The v0.4.4 fix never held: it widened the Shift+Enter guard but leaned on a focus selector (`td:nth-child(2) input`) that Feature #132 had already broken. Re-fixed with a browser test in caeb09d under [[Issue#195]].

issues.name: Workspace space does not show in the top-level workspace nav
issues.description:
**Pain point.** The Workspace (meta) space does not appear in the core / top-level workspace navigation, so its tables are unreachable from the rail.

**Expected.** Every space of the current workspace, including the meta Workspace space, is listed in the top-level nav.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #9; title truncated in the photo)

issues.name: Converting a number field to percent should multiply display by 100
issues.description:
**Pain point.** Switching a number field's format to percent renders the stored value with a % sign but does not scale it — 0.325 should read 32.5%. Today the conversion gives the wrong reading.

**Expected.** Percent follows the spreadsheet convention: stored fraction × 100 for display, ÷100 on input, so the displayed number matches what the user means.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #10; title truncated in the photo)

issues.name: Formula builder chips do not inject field names with proper syntax
issues.description:
**Pain point.** Clicking a field chip in the formula builder inserts the field name without the syntax the parser needs (names with spaces need quoting/bracketing), so the inserted token immediately fails to parse.

**Expected.** A chip inserts the exact token the formula language accepts for that field name, spaces and all.

Transcribed 2026-08-31 from a photo of Kyle's work-machine weave instance (v0.4.3, workspace 93339371-8e8b-4446-9440-fd4cf8d050e2), where it was filed via the in-app reporter. Wording reconstructed from the photo. (original #11; title truncated in the photo)

issues.name: Vditor CSS overrides the lab toolbar glyphs (fill:currentColor, stroke-width:0)
issues.description:
Found while swapping the toolbar to the Toolbar Lab icon set (Feature #154, commit 6ec383c): the stroke-drawn glyphs rendered as solid blobs, and after a first fix, as nothing at all.

**Cause:** Vditor's stylesheet paints toolbar svgs with `fill: currentColor` and `stroke-width: 0` (index.css:418/663) — CSS beats the svg presentation attributes (`fill="none" stroke-width="2"`) the lab glyphs carry.

**Fix (commit 425a670):** the scoped rule `.doc-editor .vditor-toolbar svg` sets `fill: none; stroke-width: 2px;`. Elements that declare their own fill attribute (the quote glyph, the bullet-list dots) keep it — attributes beat inheritance, just not element-targeted CSS.

Verified live: computed fill none / stroke-width 2px, glyphs render as drawn in the mockup.

issues.name: Doc downloads ⋮ menu clips off the right edge
issues.description:
The document section's ⋮ downloads menu opens past the right edge of the page and gets clipped — the reader sees a sliver of "…ownloa" labels and cannot read or reach the items (Kyle's screenshot, 2026-09-01, entity view).

## Reproduction (measured live, v0.4.4, viewport 1280px)

1. Open any entity with a document section (e.g. Showcase/Documents #1).
2. Click the section head's ⋮ (downloads).
3. The menu's box: `left: 1219.8, right: 1397.8` — a 178px menu with ~60px on screen; the rest paints off-viewport. In narrower panes (the side peek) it clips against the panel edge instead.

## Root cause

`dotsMenu(items, { align })` in `public/app.js` (~line 1373) decides direction **statically per call site**: only callers that pass `align: 'right'` get the `dl-menu-right` flip. The doc-section downloads menu (`const dl = dotsMenu(…)`, ~line 4915) never passes it, and nothing measures the viewport on open — so any ⋮ near the right edge overflows. The bug is structural: a hard-coded alignment can never be right on both edges.

## Fix shape

On open (inside the dots button's onclick, after `classList.remove('hidden')`), measure `menu.getBoundingClientRect().right` against `document.documentElement.clientWidth` and toggle `dl-menu-right` when it would overflow — one measurement, no new config, and the static `align` option becomes a default rather than a promise. Same guard benefits every dotsMenu call site (entity ⋯, view menus, table menus).
