## Fix (2026-09-07, gerrit change 271, commit d63d931)

Every plain editor already committed through its native `change` on blur, so a click elsewhere saved. A hash change, the back button, a dock swap, a reload or leaving the site removed the focused input with no blur and the keystrokes were lost: in Safari on every one of those paths, in Chromium on the unload pair.

- `commitActiveEdit()` blurs the active input/textarea/select before the page rebuilds: a `hashchange` listener ahead of `route`, `dockClose`/`dockEntity`, and `beforeunload` + `pagehide`.
- `api()` sends `keepalive` while the page unloads so the browser finishes the write.
- The Saved toast on field and description saves is gone. Failures still toast.

Test: `test/field-autosave-browser.test.mjs`, six cases, run in Chromium and WebKit.

issues.name: Hard-deleting a table orphaned the paired inverse relation field's registry row
issues.description: deleteTable({hard:true}) removed the paired inverse relation field from the target table via #removeFieldRaw but never dropped that field's Fields registry row, leaving an orphan row for a column that no longer exists. Found by the promote rehearsal battery (src/rehearse.js) on its first run, before it ever reached production data. Fixed in the same change (Gerrit 135): the paired removal now calls #dropFieldRow(inverseFieldId). Regression: fields-registry.test.mjs 'a hard-deleted table takes the paired inverse field row with it too'.

issues.name: Column drag lands the wrong column: the # cell moves, and a second drag snaps to the wrong side
issues.description:
Two defects in the grid's header drag-to-reorder, both caught by the new real-browser suite test/table-reorder-browser.test.mjs (Playwright drives Chromium's own HTML5 drag pipeline — the earlier simulated DragEvent checks could not see either).

**1. Off-by-one in the in-place move.** `reorderField` relocated `cells[1 + idx]`, but every grid row carries TWO anchored cells before the first field (the selection box, then the # link) since the sel-cell landed 2026-08-24. So a drag moved the column one to the LEFT of the one grabbed — dragging Price moved Batch — and the # cell drifted out of its anchor slot. Fix: `cells[2 + idx]`, with a comment naming the two anchored cells.

**2. Stale closure on the second drag.** The drop handler judged the insert side with `cols.indexOf(from) < i`, both captured at draw time. The in-place move deliberately skips the redraw, so after one drag every header's `cols`/`i` were stale and the next drag snapped to the wrong side of its target. Fix: the drop handler re-reads the live order (`visibleCols(db)`) at drop time.

**Guarantees now under test (4 cases, real drags):** the # column is anchored — index 1 in the header and in every body row, before and after any drag; its header takes no drag and a drop on it goes nowhere; a dragged field snaps to the expected spot in the pre-reload DOM, the reloaded DOM, and the persisted fieldOrder; every body row's cell order matches the header after each move; two consecutive drags stay honest.

issues.name: Collapsible chip previews unstyled in-app; overlay labels polluted by hidden segments
issues.description:
Found by Kyle on the entity page right after e30a65d deployed: chip previews looked broken inside the app.

**Symptoms.** In-app surfaces that render /api/markdown HTML (doc previews, handbook, applets) showed the collapsed field segments permanently and unstyled — the collapse CSS had landed only in the standalone doc page's own style block (src/markdown.js), never in public/style.css. Separately, the editor overlay (resolveRefs) built its chip label from a.textContent, which now included the hidden segment text, e.g. "Guide#4 — Agent access (MCP)AudienceAgentOrder4". The caret also had no in-app click handler.

**Not a bug alongside it:** [[Guide#5]] rendering as a dashed broken chip on Guide#8 is correct — no Guide#5 exists in that workspace; the doc's reference is stale.

issues.name: Formulas received a date field's display string, not its stored value — day() on a day-only field returned NaN
issues.description:
Found while implementing date grain & costume (Feature: date grain & costume, 2026-09-02). Fixed in the same change (Gerrit 144, commit `427b317`).

**What was wrong.** A formula referencing a date field received the field's *display* string, not its stored value — `readEntity` handed formulas `#displayValue(...)` for everything except numbers. With the four original styles this went unnoticed because `Date.parse` happens to read `Aug 21, 2026`. It broke the moment a value could not be parsed back: a day-only field displays `15`, and `day([Rent day])` returned `NaN`.

**The Handbook already promised the opposite** (date page, *In formulas*): "Comparison, sorting and date math all run on the stored ISO value."

**Fix.** Formulas now receive a date field's stored value, exactly as they receive a number's raw value (`src/engine.js`, the `formula` case in `#resolve`). `year()` / `month()` / `day()` in `src/formula.js` read the parts a partial value holds via `weaveDateGrain.partsOf` and fall back to `Date` for anything else `Date.parse` understands.

**Regression test.** `test/date-grain.test.mjs` — "formulas read the parts a partial value actually holds" (`year('2026-08')`, `month('--08-15')`, `day('---15')`).

**Behaviour change to know about.** A text-concatenation formula over a *costumed* date (e.g. `"Due " & Due` on a `long` field) now yields the ISO value rather than `Aug 21, 2026`. That is the documented contract; nothing in the repo relied on the old behaviour.

## Fixed 2026-09-05 (commit aebe974, Gerrit 235)

A stored width is written as width + min-width + max-width on the header AND every cell (the floor that keeps a column open in a wide grid, from Issue #43 / Kyle 2026-08-24). The drag only set `th.style.width`, which those min/max pins overrode — so nothing moved during the drag and the column jumped to the new width only when release wrote all three. Every move now paints header and cells through the same `paintColumnWidth` the commit uses, with one rounding (`WeaveColumnResize.width`), so the painted width is exactly the stored width and release repaints nothing. Tests: `test/column-fit.test.mjs` (from a stored 150px, mid-drag the header and its cells sit at 150+80, release settles within 1px and the schema holds the painted integer); `test/column-resize.test.mjs` (one rounding).

issues.name: Report button and bug dialog drew the Lucide bug filled solid
issues.description:
## Report

Kyle, 2026-09-02: "bug dialog is missing correct icons", then "why is this bug icon different?" — the report button drew a solid grey bug while the sidebar's Issue table drew an outlined one, and the dialog's four category tiles were dark blobs.

## Root cause

The Iconly set was filled glyphs, so its hosts carried `fill: currentColor` — `.bug-fab-icon svg`, `.bug-cat-icon svg`, `.slash-icon svg` (and the applet's report button). A Lucide shape sets `fill="none"` and strokes in currentColor; a CSS fill outranks the attribute and paints the stroke's interior solid. The slash menu additionally still read the deleted Iconly set and fell back to typed glyphs.

## Fix

Gerrit 181 (84f3e62): the fill rules go; a Lucide shape carries its own fill and stroke, a drawn mark its own fill. The applet's traced ant retires for the same vendored bug. `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` now asserts no CSS fill on any icon host; `test/toolbar-browser.test.mjs` holds the toolbar strokes (2, 1.4 for the dense glyphs) over Vditor's own `stroke-width: 0`.

issues.name: Looks broken: chips in the state and select pickers draw as bare tinted text — the k base class was missing
issues.description:
## Report

**Looks broken** (layout, chips, or text overlap, clip, or render wrong). Reported by Kyle in chat, 2026-09-02, with a screenshot of the Status picker on the Issue table.

> chips look wrong in the selector

## What was wrong

The workflow picker handed its rows and its staged chip a state class **without the `k` base**: `k-state cat-done hue-green` instead of `k k-state cat-done hue-green`. The `.k-state` rule carries the tint and the text colour; `.k` carries the padding, the 4px radius, the 11.5px size and the inline-flex box. So every state in the list, and the staged value in the box, drew as tinted text at 14px with no padding and square corners — while the cell beside the picker drew the same state as a proper chip.

Root cause: `stateChipClass(f, name, bare = true)` was a leftover from the chip-tier rename (d39937b, 2026-08-24). Before that rename the picker prefixed `k` itself; after it, the picker paints the class it is handed, whole. Select options had no class at all in the list (slate for every option), and multiselect options and staged chips lost their option hue the same way.

## The fix

- `stateChipClass` loses its `bare` flag; the workflow picker gets the whole class.
- Select options carry `k k-select hue-*` in the list; multiselect options and staged chips carry `k k-multi hue-*`. The clear row stays a `—` chip, since the empty cell is one.
- Gate: `test/picker-browser.test.mjs` reads the classes, padding, radius and hue of every chip in the box and the rows for a workflow, a select and a multiselect field.

Issue #65 part 1 (the staged chip's *design*) stays open. This was the chip drawing wrong, not a design call.

## Before / after

Attached: `picker-before.png` (live :4400 before the fix), `picker-after.png` and `picker-after-multi.png` (working tree).



## Fixed — 2026-09-02 (Gerrit 184, commit 9a83a3b)

Merged to main; the main watcher deploys :4400 within ~2 minutes of landing.

## What changed (2026-09-04)

The 403 is the grunion-ai push credential, and it is still missing — the same refusal recurred at [[Issue#180]], [[Issue#186]], [[Issue#187]] and [[Issue#215]]. What `0d1c452` (harness, `scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs`) fixed is the blast radius: a refused mirror files its Issue and the run carries on to the :4400 deploy. Before that commit one 403 aborted the rest of the step, which is how [[Issue#173]] came to be filed against a server that was healthy.

issues.name: :4400 is not serving gerrit/main @ 6c2d8376
issues.description:
:4400 is held by pid 17847, not launchd's 75543 — a hand-started server; kill it and kickstart

Landed: 6c2d8376a307c4f8135c486f268c5e371095f12d

Filed by the main watcher after the deploy step.

## Root cause — a false positive (2026-09-04)

The probe was `lsof -ti TCP:4400`, which matches CLIENT sockets as well as the listener. Pid 17847 was the Claude desktop app's network-service helper holding an open connection to the port, and it sorted ahead of the real listener in lsof's output. launchd's server (pid 75543) owned the socket and was serving the whole time, so the watcher refused a deploy that had nothing wrong with it — and told a reader to kill a healthy process.

## Fix

`6063799` in the harness repo (`scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs`): the probe is now `/usr/sbin/lsof -ti TCP:4400 -sTCP:LISTEN`, so only the process that owns the socket can answer for it. The path is absolute because the launchd job's PATH carries no `/usr/sbin`.

The deploy this issue was filed against did land: `~/.weave-serve` was fast-forwarded to 6c2d8376 by hand and :4400 restarted, verified by the new `definitionFromFieldView` reaching the served `field-dialog-core.js`.

issues.name: Entity page ignores the System toggles — Created/Modified At/By never render
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04, on Development/Feature #2 in the weave workspace: every row in the eye popover was on — Name, Description, Status, Milestone, and all five System rows (Created At, Modified At, Created By, Modified By, Activity) — yet the Fields block showed only Status and Milestone.

**Cause.** `renderEntityView` builds its value rows from `db.fields` filtered by `hiddenFields` and never reads `db.systemFields`. The grid honours the list (SYSTEM_COLS, Feature #65); the page does not.

**Fix.** After the value fields, one read-only `.fieldrow.fieldrow-system` per name in `db.systemFields` (Activity excepted — on the page it is the side column, see the companion issue on the Activity button). Same SYSTEM_COLS formatter as the grid, so a timestamp reads the same in both surfaces.

issues.name: Entity name is clipped on the entity page instead of wrapping
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04, Development/Feature #5: the title read "Automations incl. outgoing webhooks; CSV import/export; file attac" — cut at the input edge. His rule: the full name always displays, wrapping to a new line and pushing the body down if it must.

**Cause.** The title is an `<input class="name-edit">`, capped at `max-width: 640px`; an input is one line by construction.

**Fix.** The title becomes a one-row `<textarea class="name-edit">` that sizes to its content (`field-sizing: content`, with a scrollHeight fallback for engines without it), full width, no resize handle. Enter commits (blur), never inserts a newline. Related: Issue #99 (the grid name cell on expand).

issues.name: The ⛶ expand on a document section is unnecessary
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04: "small expand buttons in description fields are not necessary." The document IS the page body; a second, full-height copy of it adds a mode without adding room.

**Fix.** Remove the ⛶ anchor from `.doc-section-head` (the deck section keeps its own expand — a framed deck is a different thing). The `{ node }` branch of `expandDocument` goes with it, which also closes Issue #111 (the throw on that path).

issues.name: Entity page: the Activity button duplicates the Activity system toggle
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04: "once visibility is fixed the dedicated activity button is not needed on entity view."

Today the side column (comments, activity, references) opens from a separate Activity button remembered per browser in localStorage (`wv-entity-side`). The eye popover already carries an Activity row under System, so the page has two switches for one column and they disagree.

**Fix.** The side column opens when `Activity` is in the table's `systemFields` — the same toggle that adds the ⚡ count column to the grid — and the button goes. One switch, stored on the table like every other visibility choice (no per-browser preference, per the no-user-settings rule).

issues.name: A refused keystore reveal answered 400 instead of 403: statusFor had no entry for forbidden
issues.description:
Found by the 2026-09-04 reusability survey; fixed in Gerrit 194.

**Symptom.** `POST /api/keys/<name>/reveal` (and the share / unshare routes) answered **400 Bad Request** when the engine refused the caller, telling them to fix the request when the answer was "not yours".

**Cause.** The engine throws `WeaveError(…, 'forbidden')` from the keystore's owner checks (engine.js ~1777, 1799, 1813), but `statusFor()` in routes.js mapped only not-found, conflict, invalid and ambiguous and fell through to 400. Nothing pinned the HTTP status: credential-reveal.test asserted `e.code === 'forbidden'` at the engine only. server.js carried a second, never-called copy of the same map; worker.js already imported the one in routes.js.

**Fix.** `forbidden → 403` in the one map; the dead server.js copy deleted. Pinned code by code in server.test (`statusFor`) and over HTTP in credential-reveal.test (sajit's admin token asks for kyle's key → 403, `code: 'forbidden'`).

issues.name: deleteField, deleteComment, deleteAutomation and deleteFile returned nothing: the CLI printed "undefined", MCP sent a text item with no text
issues.description:
Found by the 2026-09-04 reusability survey; fixed in Gerrit 195.

**Symptom.** `weave field delete …` printed the word `undefined`. Over MCP, `weave_delete_field`, `weave_delete_comment` and `weave_automations {action:'delete'}` answered with a content item `{"type":"text"}` that had no `text` key at all, a malformed item. `weave_files {action:'delete'}` the same.

**Cause.** `deleteField`, `deleteComment`, `deleteAutomation` and `deleteFile` returned nothing. HTTP wraps its own `{ ok: true }` so it never noticed; the CLI's `out()` and MCP's `textResult()` pass the engine's return straight through, and `JSON.stringify(undefined)` is `undefined` (which, as an object property, is dropped). Six broken call sites, one root cause: no rule said a mutation must answer.

**Fix.** Each returns `{ id, deleted }` in the shape `deleteView`, `deleteKey` and `deleteAccount` already used, with `deleted: false` when there was nothing to remove rather than a silent success. Pinned at the engine, over MCP's wire shape and through the CLI binary in `test/mutation-results.test.mjs`.

issues.name: teardownDocEditors left docCodeAuto passes alive after the page was gone
issues.description:
Found by the 2026-09-04 reusability survey; fixed in Gerrit 197.

**Symptom.** Code-auto-highlight passes (`docCodeAuto`) outlived the page they were attached to: after leaving an entity page their timers could still fire until the next refresh tripped the detach guard.

**Cause.** Four decoration registries feed `scheduleDecorFor` and `releaseDockPanel` (`refChipLayers`, `docRails`, `docFolds`, `docCodeAuto`), but `teardownDocEditors` cleared only the first three. The test (`editor-refs.test.mjs`) asserted only that `refChipLayers` was mentioned in the teardown, which is how a fourth registry slipped past it.

**Fix.** `teardownDocEditors` clears `docCodeAuto` too. The test now lifts the registry list `scheduleDecorFor` iterates and requires a `.clear()` for each name, so the next registry cannot be forgotten in one place while remembered in another. Wave 2 of the reuse pass proposes one registry so the enumeration disappears altogether.

issues.name: registry.report / rebuild had no HTTP route, and the agent-surface gate never checked HTTP
issues.description:
Found by the 2026-09-04 reusability survey; fixed in Gerrit 200.

**Symptom.** `registry.report` and `registry.rebuild` were reachable from MCP (`weave_registry`) and the CLI (`weave registry`) and had no HTTP route at all; `test/agent-surface.test.mjs` proved every capability reachable from two doors and never opened routes.js. A second drift in the same family: the CLI's key-subcommand error text and MCP's key-action error text are two hand-typed lists.

**Fix.** `GET /api/registry` (report) and `POST /api/registry/rebuild` exist; rebuild is structure, so the role gate treats it as a schema write (a writer token reads the report and gets 403 on rebuild, pinned in accounts-audit.test). SURFACE in agent-surface.test now carries an http column spelled the way routes.js spells its routes, and a test looks each one up; its first run failed on exactly the missing pair. A second test pins the one sanctioned difference between the key lists: MCP has no `reveal` (Feature #143), otherwise they must agree. AGENTS.md names all three doors.

issues.name: Whiteboard button unreachable since the relation-map rewrite (f4bbf56): renderMermaidIn has no caller
issues.description:
Found by the 2026-09-04 reusability survey. **Open, needs a decision.**

**Symptom.** The "open as a whiteboard" button (Feature #46) no longer appears anywhere. `renderMermaidIn()` (app.js ~1066) is the only code that draws it, and nothing has called `renderMermaidIn()` since f4bbf56 (2026-08-24, "one relation map, drawn at the workspace and at a space") removed its last call site. `openWhiteboard()` (~1025, cytoscape) is therefore unreachable from the UI as well. Mermaid fences in documents still render, because Vditor renders them itself (server.js aliases Vditor's mermaid path onto the vendored build).

**Why it was not simply deleted.** `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` ("docs go fullscreen and diagrams become whiteboards") pins `openWhiteboard` and `pre.dataset.mmd` as existing, and the boot comment at app.js ~7135 still describes the render-once diagrams as live. Deleting the two functions would pass by editing the test, but that retires a shipped feature by accident.

**Decision for Kyle.** Either (a) restore the button on Vditor-rendered diagrams (a small hook after Vditor's mermaid render, reusing `renderMermaidIn`'s tools span), or (b) retire the whiteboard: delete `renderMermaidIn`, `openWhiteboard`, the cytoscape vendor file, `graph-parse.js`, their tests, and mark Feature #46 accordingly.


Resolved, 2026-09-28. renderMermaidIn has a caller again: change 7561519 (Issues #188 and #189, v0.4.9) draws a diagram-kind document field through it, and that draws the whiteboard button. Checked today on :4400 on Showcase/Documents #5: the Diagram section carries "Open as a whiteboard" in Chromium and WebKit, and a click opens the cytoscape whiteboard with the graph drawn. A mermaid fence inside a markdown document still renders through Vditor with no button; if that should change it is a new request. Found on the way and filed as Issue #471: the whiteboard prints a mermaid \n as literal text. Closed in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

issues.name: Workspaces cannot be deleted from the UI
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 (stream of consciousness while using :4400).

**Symptom.** The hub UI (workspace switcher / workspace rail) offers **+ New workspace** but no way to delete a workspace. The server already exposes `DELETE /api/workspaces/:name` (soft delete with `POST /api/workspaces/:name/restore`; `hub.remove` absent → 400 "This deployment cannot delete workspaces").

**Expected.** A delete affordance on the workspace surface (rail chip menu or the workspace page), confirming by name, calling the existing DELETE route, with the restore path reachable (includeDeleted listing). Hide or disable it when the deployment reports it cannot delete.

**Where.** `public/app.js` workspace rail + hub view; `src/routes.js` lines ~310-330 already carry the API.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.

🛠 Fixed in 3349d47 (Gerrit change 214, 2026-09-05): right-click a rail chip → Delete workspace…, confirmed by typing the name; trash chip below the rail restores; `deletable` on GET /api/workspaces hides it on the default, weave, and hubs that cannot delete. Tests: workspace-trash +2, workspace-delete-browser (new), handbook guide.

issues.name: + New workspace icon is off-center in its button
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 (stream of consciousness while using :4400).

**Symptom.** In the workspace rail, the **add workspace** button draws its icon off-center — the glyph is not centered within the button box.

**Expected.** Icon optically centered in the button in both themes, matching the other rail chips (rope logo, workspace chips, theme toggle).

**Where.** `public/app.js` / `public/*.css` workspace rail add button (Lucide icon, Feature #167).

**Verify.** Playwright screenshot of the rail in light and dark; bounding-box check that the svg centre equals the button centre within 1px.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.



**Fixed 2026-09-05** in d4df1a1 (Gerrit 212, merge 42f0b9b): `.ws-icon.ws-new .wv-icon { margin-right: 0 }` drops the label gap that pushed the glyph 2.5px left. Test `test/ws-rail-browser.test.mjs` asserts the svg and button centres agree within 1px in light and dark.

issues.name: Icon animations all fire at once on refresh/login instead of on hover/click
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 (stream of consciousness while using :4400).

**Symptom.** After a page refresh or login, every Lucide moving icon on screen animates simultaneously. The ruling for Feature #167 is one run per trigger, never loops — and the trigger is meant to be **hover or click on that icon**, not page load.

**Expected.** No animation on mount. An icon animates once when hovered or clicked (its own trigger only), then rests until the next trigger.

**Where.** `public/icons*.js` / the generated Lucide moving-icon set and the CSS that starts the keyframes (Feature #167, Feature #124 chrome). Check whether the animation class is applied at render rather than on `:hover`/`pointerdown`.

**Verify.** Playwright: load a table page, sample computed `animation-name`/`animation-play-state` on all icons at t=0 and t=500ms — none running; hover one icon — only that icon runs, once. Both themes.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.



**Fixed 2026-09-05** in 407fd9a (Gerrit 213): the load-window mount queue and the picker in-view observer are gone; an icon plays once on its own hover (mouseover) or press (pointerdown), then rests. Handbook Icon library > Motion rewritten; load-wave and picker-scroll gifs removed. Tests: `test/icon-vocabulary-browser.test.mjs` (both themes: no motion at t=0/500ms, hover plays only that icon then rests, press plays, reload draws still) and `test/inline-icons.test.mjs`.

issues.name: Collapsible chip: retract caret points down; it should face the text
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 (stream of consciousness while using :4400).

**Symptom.** On a collapsible chip preview (Feature #163 / #175), the **expand** caret is right. The **retract** caret, shown once the chip is open, points down. It should face the text it collapses back into (pointing toward the chip label), so expand and retract read as one control folding in and out.

**Expected.** Retract caret oriented toward the text (left-facing when the preview sits to the right of the label; mirror if layout differs), same size and hit area as the expand caret.

**Where.** Chip preview renderer in `public/app.js` (chip system: value / pointer / computed tiers; see Feature #163 and #175) and the chip CSS.

**Verify.** Playwright: open a chip, read the caret svg transform / class, assert orientation; both themes.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.



## Fixed 2026-09-05
Landed in 3b7a98f (Gerrit change 211, merged). `.mention-wrap.open .mention-caret` turns 180° instead of 90° in both stylesheets (public/style.css and the src/markdown.js page CSS), so the open caret faces the label; same button, same hit box. Tests: view-fields-ui stylesheet gate + test/chip-browser.test.mjs (computed matrix 0° → 180° → 0°, unchanged box, light and dark). Gate 1585/1585, skipped 0.

issues.name: Default chip view renders too small
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 (stream of consciousness while using :4400): "Default chip view is likely too small."

**Symptom.** The default `Chip` view (system view field minted on every table, Feature #175) draws smaller than comfortable — label text and hit area read undersized next to surrounding body text and cell content.

**Expected.** Chip label at body text size (or one step below at most), padding that gives a comfortable hit target (≥ 24px tall), consistent across table cells, documents ([[…]] references), relation pickers and the rail. Decide the size once in the chip tokens, not per surface. Keep the 4px radius and the no-fill-behind-a-pointer rule.

**Where.** Chip tokens/CSS in `public/` and the chip renderer in `public/app.js`; Handbook page on chips if one exists.

**Verify.** Playwright: measure rendered chip height/font-size on a table page, a document with a reference, and a relation cell; assert the shared token; both themes; screenshots before/after attached to this Issue.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.



## Fixed 2026-09-05
Landed in c73edff (Gerrit change 216, merged). The chip size is two tokens on `:root` — `--wv-chip-font: 13px` (one step below the 14px body) and `--wv-chip-line: 22px` (24px hit target with the 1px padding) — read by `.k` (every tier), the `.chip` alias and `.filter-chip`. 4px radius and the no-fill pointer rule untouched. Tests: chip-system token gate; test/chip-browser.test.mjs measures a state cell, a select cell, a relation cell and the Appears-as chip in both themes (token font, ≥ 24px, 4px, no fill). Gate 1588/1588, skipped 0. Screenshots before/after (table + entity page, light + dark) attached to this row.

issues.name: New record (click or Shift+Enter) does not drop the cursor into the Name cell
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 on :4400 (v0.4.5): "creating a new record via click or shift+enter should automatically drop our cursor in the name box."

**Symptom.** Both creation paths — clicking **+ New record** at the foot of a table and **Shift+Enter** from a row — create the row but leave focus wherever it was. The user has to click into the Name cell before typing.

**Context.** Issue #125 covered the Shift+Enter half and is marked Fixed; either it regressed or the click path was never covered and the Shift+Enter fix does not reach the current table renderer. Treat as a regression: write the failing test first for BOTH paths.

**Expected.** After either action the new row exists, its Name cell is in edit mode with the caret inside and the row scrolled into view; typing immediately fills Name; Enter commits; Shift+Enter commits and repeats. Same on the table page, the space page tables, and the entity-view relation tables where + New record appears.

**Where.** `public/app.js` new-record handlers (table foot button + keydown Shift+Enter); the cell edit-mode entry.

**Verify.** Playwright: click + New record → `document.activeElement` is the Name editor of the new row; Shift+Enter in a row → same for the following row; both themes. Re-open #125 or link this row to it.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.

---
**2026-09-05 — fixed in caeb09d** (Gerrit change 217, merged 8964fa9). Root cause: `inlineAdd` focused `td:nth-child(2) input`, which was the Name cell until the selection column (Feature #132, b8f0a39, 2026-08-24) landed in front of it; since then nth-child(2) is the #id link, no input, and the `?.focus()` was a silent no-op. The #125 fix (3984031) only widened the Shift+Enter guard so the key fired from inside a cell editor; it leaned on that dead aim and shipped without a browser test, so it never held — #125 was fixed on paper only. Also fixed on the way: the registry grids' + New button (space page, home) called whatever `state.inlineAdd` the last-visited table left behind, creating a blank row THERE; the relation grid's + New never focused. Now one `focusNewRow(eid)` lands the caret for all three surfaces, by row id, with an instant scroll into view; #134's `newRow` verb commits the open cell before creating. Test: `test/new-record-focus-browser.test.mjs` (both themes, Shift+Enter twice over, space page, relation grid). Supersedes the fix recorded on [[Issue#125]].

issues.name: Legacy "<Space> / <Table> — fields" schema page is still reachable; the field tray replaced it
issues.description:
Kyle 2026-09-05, screenshot of `/w/weave/` showing **Workspace / Spaces — fields**: a plain table of FIELD / TYPE / DETAILS with Delete links and `+ Field` / `+ Relation` buttons; asked "what is this page and why is it needed?"

**What it is.** `openSchemaEditor(db)` in `public/app.js` (~line 6267) — the v0.3.0 schema editor page, one table per screen. Feature #109 (field tray: header click edits, in-place type migrations) superseded it. Today its only callers are itself (after add/delete) — no menu or route deliberately opens it, so whatever surfaced it is a leftover entry point (find it: search for any hash/route/menu that resolves to `openSchemaEditor`, likely the Workspace system space page).

**Why it is not needed.** Everything it offers exists in the field tray and the column ⋮ menu (Feature #144): add field, add relation, retype, delete, reorder, with the Handbook page per type. Two schema surfaces with different affordances (this one has no undo, no reorder, no type detail) is a defect.

**Expected.** Remove `openSchemaEditor` and any path into it; the system Workspace tables (Spaces / Tables / Fields / Workflows) open in the same table view + field tray as every other table. Add a test that no code path renders the `— fields` heading.

**Side note.** A `Test range` daterange field was added to the system `Workspace/Spaces` table on 2026-09-05 (id 5b91c50b…), presumably while testing dateranges (see the daterange Issue filed the same day). Delete it once that Issue has what it needs.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.

**Fixed 2026-09-05** in `4d8e74b` (Gerrit change 232, merged as `49dab34`). Root cause: `addFieldDialog`'s after-hook fell back to `openSchemaEditor` whenever the add did not start on a `#/table` route — every registry grid (Spaces on the workspace home, Tables on a space page) is exactly that, which is how the `Test range` field surfaced the page. `openSchemaEditor`, `addRelationDialog` (only it reached it) and `.schema-table` are deleted; an off-table add now redraws the route it started on. Test: `test/schema-page-gone-browser.test.mjs` (source gate + home/space/table browser cases). The stray `Test range` field (5b91c50b…) was deleted from `Workspace/Spaces` on :4400 after Issue #197 landed.

issues.name: Date range: start and end must be picked in ONE dialog; default range in the config tray needs the same dialog
issues.description:

issues.name: grid-tab-focus-browser: 'a redraw triggered by an edit leaves focus on the row' flakes ~1 in 6 runs
issues.description:
Found 2026-09-05 while gating Gerrit 213 (Issue #192): `test/grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs` failed once in the review worktree and then passed on re-run with no code change. Reproduced on gerrit/main 42f0b9b (no icon change present): 1 failure in 6 runs.

**Failure.** The first assertion, `Tab moves along the row`, sees `{ eid: null, field: null, tag: 'BODY' }` instead of `{ eid: <second row>, field: 'Tail', tag: 'INPUT' }` — the PATCH-driven redraw replaced the `<tbody>` before the Tab landed, so focus fell to body before the test read it.

**Shape of a fix.** The test clicks, types `!`, presses Tab and reads focus immediately; the redraw races that read. Either wait for the mark on the old tbody to vanish before asserting (the test already sets `dataset.mark` for the second assertion), or make the grid restore focus to the tabbed cell after the redraw regardless of order, which is what the second assertion already claims it does.

Verified -1 on a green change is the cost: the gate had to be re-run.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T23:30:36.388Z · started · session wf-0907-1520



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T23:57:45.706Z · fixed · Gerrit 292 → 2656de3

**Tests added:**
- test/grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs: `the cursor comes back however long the redraw takes` — the redraw's own query is held open for 5.5 s, longer than the 5 s cap the suite's waits used to carry, so the case is red on a budget and green on a signal
- test/grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs: `settledFocus` reports the cell it settled on from inside the same evaluate that waited for it, and `cursorInGrid` gives Tab its own wait that does not also wait on the redraw; the three 5 s caps and the "mark gone plus two animation frames" read are gone

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha 2656de3 startedAt 2026-09-07T23:55:40Z (submit was 23:54:03Z), diskSha equal and stale false. Repro re-run on the landed checkout `~/.weave-serve` at 2656de3: 8/8 green. Before landing: 10/10 green under 24 spinners on 10 cores, and the full suite `# tests 1940 # pass 1940 # fail 0 # skipped 0`.

**What the flake actually was, traced rather than assumed.** The suite settled and then read focus in a **second** round trip, and the redraw lands between the two. A per-frame trace of the gesture (`focus-frame-trace.txt`, produced by `probe-199.mjs`, both attached) shows the same dip on every run:

    83ms   TD/Tail  marked    Tab has moved the resting cursor along the row
    100ms  BODY     redrawn   the <tbody> is replaced; focus falls to <body>
    116ms  TD/Tail  redrawn   restoreGridFocus puts the cursor back

Sixteen milliseconds wide on an idle machine, and nothing bounds it on a loaded gate. A read arriving inside that window sees `{ eid: null, field: null, tag: 'BODY' }` on a grid that is behaving perfectly — the exact value in this report.

**The reported form was already unreachable.** This Issue was filed against gerrit/main 42f0b9b (09-05 09:04), where the first assertion read focus with no wait at all. Feature #134 landed five minutes later (b5e9054, 09:09) and rewrote the suite around a `settledOn` helper — the Issue's own first suggestion, arrived at independently. 18 runs on `e817047` were green, 10 of them under 24 spinners on 10 cores. So the flake in its reported form was gone before this attempt started, and closing here on that alone would have left the window and the budgets in place.

**What was left to fix, and was.** Two things the report's second suggestion points at:

1. **The settle-and-read gap.** A wait and a separate read are two round trips with a frame between them, and that frame is where the redraw lands. `settledFocus` now returns the cell from inside the wait, so nothing can move focus between the two.
2. **Three hand-written 5 s caps.** Under the full gate this suite has taken **52 s** (`review-logs/227-1`) and **27 s** (`282-1`) while every wait inside it was capped at 5 s. That is exactly the cost this Issue names — a Verified −1 on a green change, paid for by the clock. The caps are gone; the waits fall back on Playwright's 30 s default, which was checked to be what actually fires.

The "mark gone plus two animation frames" read went with them: two frames is a sleep, and the last step of this round trip is the cursor coming back, not the rebuild landing (Issue #216's lesson, applied to a second suite).

**The suite is not vacuous.** A wait that returns what it waited for can assert nothing, so `settledFocus` waits for "the rebuild landed and the cursor is back in *a* cell" and lets *which cell* stay the assertion. Proved by sabotage: `restoreGridFocus` made to return early fails the suite at Playwright's 30 s default with a TimeoutError rather than hanging or passing (`sabotage-restore-broken.txt`, attached).

**Left alone deliberately.** Tab out of a *resting* cell still reads focus with no wait, and now carries a comment saying why: it writes nothing, so no redraw is in flight and focus has already moved when the key returns. A wait there would hide a cursor that never moved behind a wait that never ends.

issues.name: Embedded relation table draws Chip/Card columns as [object Object] and ignores the field visibility toggle
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-05 on :4400 (c73edff) with a screenshot: an embedded relation table (header link `Development/Issue →`, per-row × to unlink — the relation table inside an entity view, e.g. Release.Fixes) shows exactly two columns, **CHIP** and **CARD**, and every cell reads `[object Object]`.

**Two defects.**
1. **Visibility not maintained.** `Chip` and `Card` are system `view` fields that every table hides by default (`hiddenFields: [Chip, Card]`, Feature #175) and the user's visibility toggle on the table should carry into every surface that renders that table's rows. The embedded relation table ignores `hiddenFields` (and the per-table column config on the Tables row) and shows the two hidden view fields while hiding the visible ones (Name, Status, Severity…).
2. **Raw object rendered.** The `view` field value is the render object (`{shape, id, publicId, url, name, link, state, description, fields}`) and the embedded table stringifies it instead of passing it to the chip/card renderer, so the cell reads `[object Object]`. Same class as Issue #91 (daterange rendered as [object Object]): a field type without a cell renderer falls through to String().

**Expected.** The embedded relation table uses the same column set, order and visibility as the target table's own view (hidden fields hidden, visible fields visible, toggle changes propagate on next render). Every field type has a cell renderer in every table surface; a `view` value renders as the chip or card it describes. A generic guard: any cell whose value is a non-null object without a renderer draws a visible "unrendered <type>" marker in dev and a test fails — never `[object Object]`.

**Where.** Embedded relation table renderer in `public/app.js` (entity view relation section); the shared cell renderer switch; `hiddenFields` handling.

**Verify.** Playwright: open Release #5 → Fixes table shows Name/Status/Severity, not Chip/Card; toggle Chip visible on the Issue table → it appears in the embedded table as a rendered chip; grep the rendered DOM of every table surface for `[object Object]` = 0. Both themes.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests.

---
**Fixed 2026-09-05 in 3e64089** (Gerrit change 221, merged as f7970fb). Root cause, two parts: `relatedGrid` took `target.fields` whole and never read the table's `hiddenFields`, so Chip/Card (hidden by default) showed in every embedded grid; and the generic cell fallback in `editorFor` built a text input with `value: rawVal`, so any object without a renderer stringified to `[object Object]`. Fix: the embedded grid filters through `visibleCols(target)` (same order, same hidden set, toggle carries on next render); the fallback refuses objects and draws a dashed `unrendered <type>` marker. Tests: `test/related-grid-browser.test.mjs` (5 browser cases, both themes, incl. a `[object Object]` sweep over table views, entity pages and the Activity table) + a `visibleCols(target)` gate in `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`. Gate 1638/1638, `# skipped 0`.

issues.name: Rollup over a deleted target field crashes every read of the row
issues.description:
**Symptom.** A `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max`/`join` rollup whose `targetField` was deleted makes `#resolve` throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` (engine.js:3811) whenever the row — or any row whose chip view reaches it — is read. In the `uno` workspace, `Person.Open Load` (sum over Assigned Tasks → a deleted `Estimate` field) took down `POST /api/tables/Task/query`, `export.csv`, the phone applet's `/w/uno/t/data` (500 since at least 2026-09-04, `weave-uno-pull` failing every 5 min), and every Task row assigned to a Person.

**Expected.** A rollup whose target field no longer exists resolves to `null` (count still works), the same way a deleted relation target is skipped. Deleting a field that a rollup/lookup targets should also either refuse or null out the dependant's `targetField`.

**Where.** `src/engine.js` `#resolve` — `lookup` and `rollup` branches dereference `targetDb.fields[config.targetField]` without a guard; `deleteField` leaves dependants pointing at the gone id.

**Verify.** Test: create Task.Estimate(number), Person.Load = rollup sum over Assigned Tasks.Estimate, delete Estimate, then `query('Task')` and `readEntity(person)` return 200 with `Load: null`. Same for lookup. `weave registry` reports no drift.

**Workaround applied 2026-09-06 in uno:** deleted the two dangling rollups (`Person.Open Load`, `Project.Total Estimate`) and re-added `Open Load` as `count`.

Bare anchors are excluded on purpose — `.nav-space` and `.nav-db` are an icon beside a bare text label, which `:only-child` (elements only) would still match and strip. The sweep also caught `.dots-btn` (rail chip menus) and `.icon-btn` (Set icon, 2px low at 18px; now flex-centred). `test/icon-center-browser.test.mjs` sweeps every lone icon on the workspace home and a table page, light and dark, asserting |dx|,|dy| ≤ 1px and that no matched button carries a bare text label. issues.name: Appears-as strip ignores the eye: Chip and Card switched off still draw on the entity page
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-07 (uno › Agent › Sessions #1, v0.4.8): with Chip and Card both OFF in the entity page's eye, the Appears-as strip still draws both. His words: "chip and card visibility toggled off but are still showing. this should fail a test."

**Cause.** `appearsAsPanel` read `viewFieldOf(db, 'chip'|'card')` and never consulted `db.hiddenFields`, so the one hidden set that rules the grid and the field rows stopped at the strip.

**Fix.** The strip reads the same hidden set: a view switched off leaves the strip, both off and the strip is not drawn. Note the default: a new table hides both views from the grid (engine `#ensureViewFields`), so the strip is now off on a fresh table until Chip or Card is switched on in the eye.

**Test.** `test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs` drives the page's own eye (toggle → PATCH → redraw) and asserts the strip's chip/card slots; red without the fix (2 of 3), green with it. `view-fields-ui.test.mjs` gate updated from 'hidden or not' to 'each view the eye leaves on'; `chip-browser.test.mjs` seed switches the views on.

issues.name: A url cell drew a text box: clicking placed a caret and nothing opened
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-09-07: *"in weave we need to change how URLs are clicked to open in new tab."*

A `url` field drew the same text box as a `text` field. Clicking placed a caret; nothing opened. Visiting the site meant click, ⌘A, ⌘C, new tab, ⌘V, Return. The Handbook page for `url` already promised *"a string the grid renders as a link, opening in a new tab"*, so the cell contradicted its own documentation.

## Cause

`editorFor` (public/app.js) had no `url` branch: the type fell through to the generic `<input>` at the bottom of the function. The only url-specific code in the client was `type="url"` on the bulk-set popover.

## Fix

The #97 costume, applied to a url. `dressedUrl()` draws a real `<a class="url-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">` at rest (host, then the rest, one link colour end to end), with a pencil that shows on hover and focus. The pencil, a double-click on the span, or Return on the focused cell (the keymap now reaches `.url-edit`) swap the existing input in; blur swaps the link back. Only an `http(s)://` value draws as a link — `urlParts()` in editor-lib.js returns null for anything else (a bare word, `javascript:`, `mailto:`, an empty value), which keeps the plain text box, so a stored string can never run in the reader's tab. The entity page draws the same node through the same `editorFor` call.

Design review with the four options considered (link at rest, box + arrow button, modifier-click only, site chip) was mocked up live before the pick; Kyle chose the link at rest, then asked for one hyperlink colour instead of a muted path.

## Tests

- `test/url-cell.test.mjs` — `urlParts()` splits http(s) and refuses everything else; the anchor carries `target` and `rel`; the keymap reaches the pencil; the style and Handbook line exist.
- `test/url-cell-browser.test.mjs` — a real browser: the cell rests as a link (empty and non-http values as the text box); a click opens a new tab with `window.opener === null` and the grid stays put; the pencil swaps the input in and blur saves; double-click and Return open the editor; the entity page draws the same link.

Full suite on the patchset: 1812 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.

## Handbook

The `url` page now names the click rule and the edit gestures, and says only http(s) values draw as links.

issues.name: A link in a description or document navigated the weave tab away
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-09-07, right after the url-cell change (#213): *"links need to open in a new tab by default."*

A markdown link in a table or space description, or in a document, navigated the weave tab away. The reader lost the page they were on and came back through the browser's history.

## Cause

`renderInline` in src/markdown.js wrote a bare `<a href>` for `[text](url)`; nothing client-side retargeted it. The url cell (#213), the deck link, the credential link and file links each set `target="_blank"` by hand, so the rule existed four times and nowhere.

## Fix

Two halves of one rule.

- **Server render** — `linkTarget()` in src/markdown.js gives an `http(s)://` link `target="_blank" rel="noopener"`, so descriptions, documents and exported pages carry it. A route (`#/entity/…`), a workspace path (`/e/…`) or a fragment stays in place.
- **Client** — one capture-phase click listener in public/app.js (`externalLinksOpenInTabs`) retargets any other anchor whose origin is not weave's the moment it is clicked. Every surface that draws a link obeys the rule without remembering to; an anchor that already chose its target keeps it. Vditor's own link handling (`isOpen`, a new tab) is untouched.

## Tests

- `test/markdown.test.mjs` — the external link carries `target` + `rel`.
- `test/external-links-browser.test.mjs` — the server marks far links and leaves routes, paths and fragments alone; a description link opens a new tab with `window.opener === null` and the table stays open; a client-drawn anchor is retargeted on click and a route never is.

issues.name: appears-hidden browser suite times out under the full gate (flake, 2 of 4 runs)
issues.description:
## Symptom

`test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs` → *"Card switched off too: no strip at all — and switching Chip back on brings it back"* timed out (`page.waitForFunction: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` in `flip`, line 46) on two of four Gerrit gate runs today (260 patchset 2 first run, 266 first run), each time under the full suite; the suite alone passes every time (3/3), and both re-runs of the gate were green with `# skipped 0`.

## Where

The gate log: `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/260-2.log` and `266-1.log`, test 22. The flip helper waits for the strip to disappear after the eye toggles Card off; under load the redraw that removes it lands after the 30 s budget, or the click lands before the previous redraw finished.

## Shape of a fix

Wait on the PATCH round trip (the tbody mark pattern in grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs) before flipping the second view, rather than on the strip's absence alone; or raise the budget for that one wait. Filed by the shipping agent for Issues #213/#214 so the flake stops costing a ten-minute re-gate.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T22:20:39.735Z · started · session wf-0907-1520



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-07T23:29:01.447Z · fixed · Gerrit 291 → 630a571

**Tests added:**
- test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs: flip() waits for the switch row to read the new aria-checked state — the last step of the PATCH → redraw → popover-rebuild round trip — and asserts the flip reached the table; the 2s hidden-set poll and the 400ms sleep are gone
- test/entity-eye-sync-browser.test.mjs: flipAmount() waits on that same signal with the default budget; the 5s cap that voted change 282 Verified −1 (the round trip took 8.7s on the gate) is gone

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha e817047 startedAt 2026-09-07T23:27:49Z (submit was 23:19:02Z), 630a571 an ancestor of the serving checkout and the 5s cap gone from ~/.weave-serve. Repro re-run on the landed main: appears-hidden 3/3 green, entity-eye-sync 3/3 green. Before landing: appears-hidden 6/6 green idle and 5/5 green under 2× CPU oversubscription (round trip stretched to seconds), full suite # tests 1912 # pass 1912 # fail 0 # skipped 0.

**Why it timed out, established deterministically rather than assumed.** A flip is three steps: the switch PATCHes the table, the page redraws from the fresh schema, and only then does `save` teach the popover's rows the new truth (`public/app.js`, the `const pop = document.querySelector('.chip-pop')` tail). The helper waited for the popover to close and then slept 400ms — but it started that sleep as soon as the PATCH landed on the **server**, so the sleep had to cover the client's `loadSchema` + redraw + popover rebuild. Measured on an idle machine that tail is ~20ms; nothing bounds it on a gate that boots ten browsers at once, and this suite is test 22 of ~1900.

When the rebuild lands inside the **next** flip's click, `pop.replaceChildren` detaches the row the mousedown just focused. The mouseup lands on the replacement, so no `click` event fires at all and the switch never toggles, and focus falls to `<body>` — where Escape cannot reach the popover, whose keydown listener is its own. The popover stays open and the wait burns its full 30s. Reproduced twice: once by replacing the popover's rows between `mouse.down()` and `mouse.up()` (focus lands on BODY, Escape swallowed, `.chip-pop` still present), and once end to end by holding the button down across a slowed `GET /api/schema` so the previous flip's own `save` tail landed inside the gesture (the click was swallowed: the engine's hidden set never gained the field). Both scripts are attached.

Raising the budget was rejected on that evidence: the wait was racing the redraw, not running short of time. The fix is a signal instead of a budget.

**Filed along the way:** the swallowed click is a real defect for a reader who flicks two switches quickly, not only for a test — see [[Issue#240]]. It was left out of this change to keep the fix atomic.

**Note on Gerrit numbering:** change 282 carried patchset 1 and took a Verified −1 for the entity-eye-sync 5s cap; amending its message regenerated the Change-Id, so the fix landed as change 291 and 282 was abandoned as superseded.

issues.name: A claude:// or mailto: value in a url column stayed a text box after #213
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-09-07, after #213 and #214 deployed: *"why dont i see this live in my local weave now."*

The uno Sessions table's `Session` column holds 452 `claude://resume?session=…` values and still drew a text box. The uno Task table's `Fibery` column (https) drew 47 links, so the deploy was live; the scheme rule was the gap.

## Cause

`urlParts()` (#213) accepted only `http:` and `https:`, on the theory that anything else could execute in the reader's tab. That was too narrow: the dangerous set is the schemes a browser runs, not every scheme that is not http.

## Fix

`urlParts()` refuses only `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:` and `file:` (case-insensitively), and marks http(s) as `external`. `dressedUrl` sets `target="_blank" rel="noopener"` for external links only: a custom scheme launches its handler and the page stays, so a new tab would just be a blank one. For a custom scheme the heavier "host" span is everything up to the query (`claude://resume`), the rest is the query.

## Tests

- `test/url-cell.test.mjs` — `claude://`, `mailto:`, `ftp:` are links with `external: false`; the run-able schemes stay the box, whatever the case; the anchor takes a target only when external.
- `test/url-cell-browser.test.mjs` — a `claude://` value renders as a link with no target; a click opens no tab and the grid stays.

## Handbook

The `url` page names the rule: any scheme links, custom schemes open in place, http(s) opens a new tab, the five run-able schemes rest as a text box.

issues.name: A rollup over a currency (or any costumed) column shows a bare number
issues.description:
**Symptom:** `Line total` (sum rollup over an EUR column) read `350`, not `€350`; an avg over `Cost (USD)` read `4.666666666666667`.

**Cause:** `#displayValue` had no `rollup` case — the resolved figure passed through undressed. The target column's number costume (format, currency, decimals, unit, separator) was never consulted.

**Fix:** `#displayValue` dresses a numeric rollup result in the target column's costume; date `min`/`max` results dress as dates; counts stay counts; a non-integer mean or deviation over a column without `decimals` shows two. Covered by `test/space-rollups.test.mjs` ("wears the target column's costume", "relation rollup of a currency column").

issues.name: applySchema skips the Workspace/Spaces registry, so a field on a space's row never round-trips
issues.description:
**Symptom:** `describeSchema()` emitted the space rollups on `Workspace/Spaces`; `applySchema()` into a fresh workspace silently dropped them (`wanted = doc.filter((sp) => !sp.system)`), so a schema document was not the workspace it described.

**Fix:** a post-pass in `applySchema` applies `rollup` fields carrying `viaTable` onto the Spaces registry after every user table exists — create when missing, delete-and-recreate when the descriptor differs (computed config has no update verb), delete when omitted (behind `allowDestructive`). Covered by "the schema names the table a space rollup reads, and a round trip keeps it".

issues.name: Rollup `join` ignores its documented `separator`
issues.description:
**Symptom:** the handbook says "`join` accepts a `separator`; the default is `, `", but the resolver hard-coded `', '` and `addField` never stored the key.

**Fix:** `addField` keeps `config.separator`; the resolver passes it to `src/stats.js`. Covered by `test/stats.test.mjs` ("join concatenates display values with the separator").

issues.name: The field dialog cannot author a space rollup (`via`) — only the Σ footer picker and the API can
issues.description:
**Symptom:** on the Spaces registry grid, `+ field → rollup` offers the Spaces table's relations (`Tables`, `Workflows`) — there is no way to say "over the whole Sessions table". The footer picker (click a footer cell) creates the same field with one switch, and `weave_add_field` / `weave field add` take `config.via`, so nothing is gated; the dialog is just the odd surface out. A `where` clause can only be written through the API today.

**Expected:** the rollup section of the dialog, when the host table is `Workspace/Spaces`, offers "Over a table" (a picker over the user tables) beside "Through a relation", plus an optional filter editor reusing the grid's filter chips.

**Where:** `public/app.js` fieldDialog, the `lookup || rollup` branch; `public/field-dialog-core.js` parseDefinition already validates `via`.

issues.name: Escape after flipping an eye switch does nothing when the flip's redraw lands first
issues.description:
**Symptom:** in the field-visibility eye, click a row's switch then press Escape: on a slow machine (or under the full test suite, where `test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs` timed out twice in a row) the popover stays open. The same class as the "flaky under the full suite" family ([[Issue#44]]), but this one has a cause.

**Cause:** the flip writes the table, then rebuilds the popover's rows in place (`pop.replaceChildren(...buildRows(fresh))`). The pressed row is a new node, so focus falls to `body`; the popover's keydown handler only hears keys while focus is inside it, so an Escape that lands after the rebuild goes nowhere.

**Fix:** after the rebuild, focus moves to the row with the same label (the Σ footer picker, added in the same change, does the same). Landed in Gerrit 270 with Feature #187.

issues.name: Select and multi-select chips in the field tray do not save on click-off
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-09-07, after Issue #135 landed: click-off autosave works for text fields (the field name, plain inputs) but a single-select or multi-select chip picked in the field config tray does not stick when he clicks off — Return or an explicit action is still needed, or the pick is lost.

## Expected

Every field commits when the pointer leaves it (Issue #135 rule): a select or multi-select choice in the tray writes on the pick, or at the latest when the popover closes on click-off / Escape / nav away.

## Where

Field config tray (the dock / entity tray), select + multi-select editors. Compare the same editors in the grid, where the pick writes on click.

## Verify

Browser test: open an entity in the dock, pick an option in a select and add one in a multi-select, click elsewhere (no Return), read the entity back from the engine — both values stored. Run in WebKit as well as Chromium.

## Fix (2026-09-07, gerrit change 274, commit 961be15)

Mechanism: a select writes on the pick, and always did. A multi-select stages its picks in the popover and wrote them only on a click-off — Escape dismissed the popover with the picks still in it, and a hash change, a scripted dock swap, a reload or a closing tab removed it the same way. `commitActiveEdit()` (#135) blurs `input, textarea, select`; a chip popover is none of those, so #135's fix never reached it. Reproduced in Chromium and WebKit.

- `searchPicker`: Escape on a multi picker commits instead of discarding.
- The open multi popover carries its commit (`pop.commit`) and `commitActiveEdit()` takes it, so hashchange, dockClose/dockEntity, beforeunload and pagehide all write the staged picks (keepalive on the unload pair).
- A multi picker closed with nothing changed writes nothing.

Test: `test/chip-autosave-browser.test.mjs` (dock, entity page, grid; Chromium + WebKit). Gate Verified +1, full suite 1872/1872.

issues.name: An edited value lags before it shows, so the edit looks like it did not stick
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-09-07: after a field edit the page keeps showing the old value for long enough that the edit looks lost. The write goes through (a reload shows it) but the repaint waits on the round trip.

## Likely cause

`editorFor` → `patch()` → `api(PATCH)` then `saved()` does a second `GET /entities/:id` before `onSaved(fresh)` repaints, and the page/grid refresh re-queries the table. Two to three serial requests before the cell reflects what was typed; on the tray the whole entity re-renders.

## Expected

The cell shows the typed value immediately (the input already holds it); the round trip only reconciles. A failed write reverts and toasts. No visible gap between commit and repaint.

## Verify

Browser test with a slowed PATCH (server option or route delay): after blur the cell shows the new value before the response returns; after the response it still shows it; on a 4xx it reverts.

## Fix (2026-09-07, gerrit change 274, commit 961be15)

Select, multi-select and workflow chips now paint the picked value on the control the moment it commits (`editorFor`'s `patch(value, paint)`); the PATCH → GET → re-render round trip only reconciles, and a refused write paints the stored value back before it toasts. Text inputs already showed their own value. No state-management change: one `paint` closure per chip editor.

Test: `test/chip-autosave-browser.test.mjs` — a slowed PATCH (Playwright `page.route`) proves the chip reads the pick before the response returns, still reads it after, and reverts on a 400; in the dock and in the grid, Chromium + WebKit. Gate Verified +1, full suite 1872/1872.

issues.name: Refresh loses the docked entity: the page comes back to the bare table
issues.description:
**Symptom.** With a row open in the dock beside its table, a browser refresh (or opening the same URL in a new tab) lands on the bare table. The dock is gone and the row's light is out. Kyle, 2026-09-07: "refresh brings me back to the table even when I have the tray or entity open."

**Cause.** The dock is presentation, not a history entry (Issue #198): `dockEntity` never wrote anything to the URL, so the hash stayed `#/table/<id>` and `renderRoute` on reload had nothing to re-dock. The expanded pose (`#/entity/<id>`) already survived a refresh; only the docked pose was lost.

**Expected.** The docked entity rides the table hash as `#/table/<db>?e=<id>`, written with `history.replaceState` so Back still never sees a dock entry. A reload, a new tab or a pasted link re-docks that row after the table renders. The user's own close (✕, Esc, the entity's close) strips `?e=`; a route change leaves the URL alone. A `?e=` for a row that no longer exists renders the bare table and drops the query.

**Where.** `public/app.js`: `dockEntity`, new `dockSyncUrl` / `dockDismiss` / `redock`, the `#/table` branch of `renderRoute`.

**Verify.** `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs`: "docking writes ?e=<id> onto the table hash and a reload brings the dock back", "closing the dock strips ?e=…", "a ?e= for a row that no longer exists renders the bare table". Hash expectations in `entity-pose-browser` and `entity-dock-default-browser` updated to the new shape.

issues.name: Esc on a nested dock throws: dockApplyPose and dockSyncUrl were called but never defined
issues.description:
**Symptom.** With the dock two levels deep (a relation chip followed inside the dock), pressing Esc pops one level in the surface core and then throws `ReferenceError: dockApplyPose is not defined`; the dock never redraws.

**Cause.** Commit 4b988d3 (two poses, one renderer) left the Esc handler calling `dockApplyPose()` and `dockSyncUrl()`, neither of which existed anywhere in `public/app.js`. Found while fixing the refresh loss (the sibling Issue); the missing `dockSyncUrl` is now the function that writes `?e=<id>` onto the table hash.

**Expected.** Esc pops the chain one level, re-syncs the hash to the new top entity, and redraws. The dead `dockApplyPose` call is removed — pose is two mounts of one renderer, there is nothing to apply.

**Where.** `public/app.js`, the document `keydown` Escape handler beside `DOCK_ESC_OWNERS`.

**Verify.** The dock browser suites run green; `dockSyncUrl` is defined and covered by the reload tests in `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs`.

issues.name: Nine watcher ops rows claim they were fixed in v0.4.5
issues.description:
**Found 2026-09-07** while writing up the Release table (Feature #190).

Issues #162, #166, #167, #169, #171, #172, #180, #186 and #187 are the rows the main watcher files about its own mirror and deploy loop ("gerrit/main @ … did not reach GitHub"). **Why it matters.** `Development/Release` is now the record of what each release contains, and the manifest ships it to every instance. A release that claims nine fixes it did not make is the one kind of error this table exists to prevent.

**Fix shape.** Unlink the nine from v0.4.5 (`POST /api/entities/<release>/unlink` with field `Fixes`), leaving the rows closed. v0.4.5's real contents are Issues #134, #83 and #133 plus Features #175 and #190. issues.name: Export leaks account token hashes and share tokens to a reader; import is not schema-gated
issues.description:
Found 2026-09-07 while surveying the auth surface for [[Feature#194]] (shares).

## What happens

`GET /api/export` returns `state.meta` wholesale (`src/engine.js:4486`). That includes account `tokenHash` values and view `shareToken` values in plaintext. A **reader** token is enough to fetch it, so the lowest privilege rung walks away with every share link in the workspace and the hash of every account key.

Separately, `POST /api/import` is not in the `schemaWrite` list, so a **writer** token can replace the entire workspace — a role that is explicitly barred from changing one field can swap the whole schema and every row.

## Why it matters

[[Feature#14]] sells three rungs: reader reads, writer writes data but never schema. Both holes make a rung a fiction. The export hole also undermines share links before they exist: [[Feature#194]] stores share tokens in plaintext by design, on the understanding that export redacts them.

## Fix shape

* Redact on the way out: strip `accounts[].tokenHash` and every share/view token from the export payload. Anything reconstructible on import stays; secrets do not travel.
* Move `POST /api/import` into `schemaWrite` so it needs an admin token.
* Test both in `test/accounts-audit.test.mjs`: a reader export contains no `wv_`, `wvv_` or `wvs_` string and no `tokenHash` key; a writer import returns 403.

Landing this with [[Feature#194]] is fine — that feature's test list already carries the export-redaction assertion. Filed separately because the two API holes are live today and stand on their own.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:29:33Z

## Fixed 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd)

**What was already fixed.** Both holes named above closed on 2026-09-12 in commit 05283ec (Feature #222 phase 0). The export strips account `tokenHash` values, view share tokens, sessions and invites on every surface (HTTP, `weave export`, the MCP `weave_export_json` tool), and `POST /api/import` is a schema write that needs an admin token. Tests `Issue #230 (a)` and `Issue #230 (b)` in `test/auth-wall.test.mjs` guard them.

**Recheck on gerrit/main f34f90c.** A scratch workspace held an admin, a writer and a reader account, a shared view, an open invite, a browser session, a passkey and a stored credential value. Every GET route in `src/routes.js`, the table query, an entity read, a doc read and the MCP export, workspace, accounts and schema tools were fetched with each rung's token and scanned for every raw token, every token hash, the share token, the invite, the session and the credential value, and for any `tokenHash` or `shareToken` key or `wv_`, `wvv_` or `wvs_` token. Nothing leaked. The one hash any route returns is the caller's own session id on `GET /api/auth/me`, which is the handle the revoke call takes and belongs to that caller, so it is not a leak. A writer import and a reader import both answered 403.

**What was still broken.** The round trip. `importJSON` (`src/engine.js`) replaced the whole state, so an admin who exported a workspace and imported the dump back into the same workspace wiped every token hash, share token, session and invite the export had stripped. The next call from that admin came back 401, every share link stopped resolving and every browser was signed out.

**The fix (Gerrit change 472, fe8389b).** Import keeps what the dump leaves out. `#keepSecrets` runs after the state is replaced: it matches accounts and views by id and restores each token hash and share token the dump omits, and it keeps the sessions and invites of the accounts the dump still names. How each case behaves:

* Same workspace, dump unchanged: every account token, share link, session and invite keeps working. A second round trip changes nothing.
* The dump carries its own `tokenHash` or `shareToken`: the dump's value wins over the stored one.
* The dump drops an account or a view: its token, invites, sessions and share link go with it.
* A dump imported into another workspace: no ids match, nothing is kept, and the accounts arrive with no working token and the views unshared, as before.

**Tests.** `test/auth-wall.test.mjs` gains `Issue #230 (c)`: the admin export carries no `wv_`, `wvv_` or `wvs_` token and no `tokenHash` or `shareToken` key; after an admin import the admin's next call answers 200, all three tokens verify, the share link opens its view, a session and an invite still work, twice over; a dropped account and a dropped view lose theirs; a dump's own hash replaces the stored one. Written first and seen red (the admin's call after import answered 401), then green. Gate: 2957 tests, 0 skipped, Verified +1 on patchset 1. The changelog entry is `changelog.d/import-keeps-secrets-230.md`; `Fixed in` waits for the batch release.

**Deploy.** `:4400` `/api/health` reports sha fe8389b. The live `weave` export carries no `tokenHash` or `shareToken` key and no token-shaped string. The words appear only as prose in five Feature and Issue documents. The scratch repro on the deployed `~/.weave-serve` code gives the same result as the test.

issues.name: Dead Cloudflare Workers adapter still constrains live code
issues.description:
Found 2026-09-07 in a ponytail survey of the codebase (bubble-chart bloat pass).

## What happens

The Cloudflare Workers deploy path still ships: `src/store-cf.js` (170 lines), `src/worker.js` (104 lines) and `wrangler.toml`. Hosting reversed to Fly.io on 2026-08-24 because Workers cannot run `node:sqlite`, so none of it is reachable, and nothing runs it.

## Why it matters

The dead runtime bends live code. `src/mcp.js` and `src/pdf.js` both carry lazy-load contortions with comments explaining that a module-top file read crashes the workerd bundle at cold start. `src/applet.js` is generated inside the dispatcher partly because the Cloudflare `[assets]` binding would serve `public/` before the Worker ran. Every future contributor reads those comments as a live constraint on a runtime that was abandoned.

## Fix shape

Delete `src/store-cf.js`, `src/worker.js` and `wrangler.toml` (keep `wrangler.toml.example` if it documents anything worth keeping), then unwind the workerd guards in `mcp.js` and `pdf.js` and simplify the applet's comment to name the real reason it is generated in the dispatcher. Roughly 300 lines gone and a constraint lifted off four files.

Leave one `ponytail:` upgrade-path comment in `src/routes.js` noting that the dispatcher was once dual-runtime and what it would take to be so again, in case BYOC ever wants it.

Sequencing: [[Feature#194]] touches the same dispatcher, so do this first and let the share resolver land on the simpler pipeline.

issues.name: Formula builder saved unparseable expressions, and said nothing until every cell read #ERR
issues.description:
**Pain point.** The formula builder accepted an expression the parser cannot read. Typing `if(upper(` and pressing Create returned 201, and the first sign of trouble was `#ERR: Unexpected end of formula` filling the column in every row. Nothing in the dialog validated the script, at any point, on either surface.

**Also wrong in the same dialog.**

- A function chip inserted `upper(` and left the caret after the dangling paren, so the next chip landed outside the call.
- The field being edited offered its own chip, and a formula that reads itself never converges.
- The only account of what a function takes was a `title` tooltip, invisible on touch.

**Expected.** The dialog says the expression is wrong while it is being written, and a save that cannot compute is refused rather than stored.

**Fixed** in v0.4.5. `check()` in `src/formula.js` validates syntax, function names and field references without a row; `addField` / `updateField` refuse an expression that fails it, including one naming its own field. The dialog runs the same check as you type and prints either the parse error or the value the expression computes on a real row. Chips insert `name()` with the caret between the parens, and the edited field is off its own chip list.

Reported by Kyle, 2026-09-01. Evidence in `test/formula-check.test.mjs` (19 tests).

issues.name: Summation rollup row: add a visibility toggle and pin it under the field headers
issues.description:
**Symptom.** The Σ footer (space rollups painted in `tfoot`, Feature #187) sits at the end of the table and cannot be hidden. On long tables it scrolls out of sight; on tables that do not want it, it takes space with nothing to show.

**Expected.** (1) The summation row has a visibility toggle (on the Σ picker / table header, remembered on the Tables row like filters and sort). (2) When shown, the row sits directly under the field headers, before the first entity row, so it stays visible while the body scrolls.

**Where.** Grid view of any table with `via` rollups on its Spaces row; e.g. uno › Agent › Sessions.

**Verify.** Open a table with rollups: toggle off → no Σ row anywhere; toggle on → Σ row is the first row under the header, stays put on scroll, footer `tfoot` no longer paints it. Toggle state survives reload and is stored on the table config, not localStorage. Existing footer-picker click-to-add still works from the pinned row.

Reported by Kyle 2026-09-07.

- Fixed looks like: a Σ stat switch flips and the footer shows the stat's label at once, with the value filling in when it arrives, the way the eye's switches feel.
- Root cause, measured today on a scratch copy of uno: the switch's `onclick` in `footerPicker` (`public/app.js:9050`) awaits the field POST or DELETE, then a full-table `GET /stats` (`load`, `:9043`), then repaints the rows and the footer and calls `loadSchema()`. Each flip takes 208 to 356 ms before anything moves.
- The change: flip the switch's `aria-checked` and add or remove the stat's `.foot-stat` span (value "…") before the write, then run the write, the stats read and `fillFooter` (`:9013`) as now; on an error, revert both and toast. Queue writes the way the eye does (Issue #243, `bb1fc69`) so fast flips land in order.
