- Test first: in `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs`, hold the fields POST with `page.route` and assert the switch reads on and the footer cell shows the stat label before the POST resolves; a second case fails the POST and asserts both revert.
- Steps: `public/app.js` only, inside `footerPicker`.
- Size: S.
- Risks: footer values are space rollups (weave-footer-values-are-space-rollups), so the optimistic span must be replaced by the real rollup's value, never kept. The popover's `relearnRows` rebuild must keep focus on the pressed row (Issue #240).

2026-10-05: Fixed by 4ef394e (merge 3e50db1), Gerrit 648, fork session 2026-10-05. Landed from the 09-26 orphan dafdf26, re-derived on main 568792b. A Σ switch now flips on the click, its write queues on the eye's write queue, and only its column is read back (GET /api/tables/:ref/stats?field=F, also weave_stats field and weave stats --field). Reproduced first: the five new cases in footer-rollups-browser and space-rollups failed on unchanged main and pass with the change.

issues.name: Grid: the sticky header never held on the table page — .table-wrap and th.col-head swallowed it
issues.description:
## Found while shipping Feature #196 (2026-09-07)

`.wv-grid thead th { position: sticky; top: 0 }` has been in `public/style.css` since the Tabler restyle, but on the table page the header scrolled away with the rows. Measured in Playwright on a 200-row table at 1280×720: after `scrollTo(0, 2000)` the first `th.col-head` sat at `top = -1836px`.

Two causes, both CSS:

1. `.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto }` makes the wrap a scroll container, and a sticky cell sticks to the NEAREST scroll container — a box exactly as tall as the table, so nothing ever stuck to the window. (`#dock` is the same shape: the wrap inside it, not the dock, was the sticky's box.)
2. `.wv-grid th.col-head { position: relative }` (the anchor for the field menu and resize grip) out-specifies the thead rule, so even with (1) fixed only the `#` and select-box headers stuck while the field headers scrolled away.

## Fix (lands with Feature #196)

- `.table-wrap { overflow-x: clip }` by default; `.wv-wide` (set by a ResizeObserver in buildGrid when `scrollWidth > clientWidth`) restores `overflow-x: auto`, so a grid wider than its card keeps its sideways scroll.
- `th.col-head { position: sticky }` — sticky is positioned too, so the menu and grip still anchor to it.

Covered by `test/sticky-add-row-browser.test.mjs` (header top ≥ 0 after a 2000px scroll; the wide table still scrolls sideways).

issues.name: dateadd() on an empty date returns the epoch shifted, not null
issues.description:
`dateadd(date, n, unit)` on an empty date returned the epoch shifted by n — `dateadd([Close Date], 1, "days")` on a row with no Close Date read `1970-01-02` — because `new Date(null)` is the epoch, not an invalid date. `datediff`, `year`, `month` and `day` already return null for an empty input; `dateadd` was the one date function that manufactured a value.

Found by the formula scan (Feature: scan preview, direction B): the scan counts rows that compute to null, and the seeded row with no Close Date counted as computed.

Fix: an empty or null date returns null before the Date constructor sees it. Gate: `test/formula.test.mjs` ("dateadd on an empty date is null, not the epoch").

issues.name: Browser suites flake under the full parallel gate: relation-map ⌘-click, stale chip dark theme, Roll up… parent
issues.description:
**Pain point.** While landing Feature #202 (Gerrit change 281, 2026-09-07) the full `node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'` run with Playwright linked failed one to two browser cases per run, a different case each time, and every one of them passed when its file ran alone (8/8 stable):

- `row-selection-browser`: *Roll up… creates one parent in the relation's table and links the selection to it*
- `slash-commands`: *a wheel over the slash menu never scrolls the page out from under it* (already Issue #44) — `.vditor-hint` button resolved but never visible within 30s
- `relation-map`: *a relation-map node: ⌘-click opens the table in a tab*
- `stale-build-browser`: *the stale instance chip is tinted and legible in the dark theme*

The gate voted Verified −1 on patchset 2 for the slash-menu case and +1 on patchset 3; the persisted gate log for patchset 3 still ends `# pass 1910 / # fail 2` (the two cases above), so a later append to the same log or a race in the verdict is also worth a look.

**Problem.** Sixty-odd browser suites launch their own Chromium in parallel; visibility waits time out under load, so a green change can be voted red and a red one can look like a flake. Related: #44, #199, #216.

**Solution shape.** Either cap `node --test` concurrency for the `*-browser` suites in the gate (a `--test-concurrency` for that glob), or give the gate one automatic retry of only the files that failed and vote on the retry — with the first run's failures still posted as a breadcrumb so a real regression is never hidden.

issues.name: A late eye-popover rebuild swallows the click that is in progress
issues.description:
## Symptom

Flick two switches in the eye popover quickly and the second one does nothing: the switch does not move, the field does not hide or show, and the popover is left with focus on `<body>`, so Escape no longer closes it. Nothing on screen says the gesture was dropped.

## Where

`public/app.js`, the tail of `save()` in `fieldVisibilityPopover` — the block that keeps the popover in place and rebuilds its rows:

```js
const pop = document.querySelector('.chip-pop');
if (pop) {
  const scroll = pop.scrollTop;
  const wasFocused = document.activeElement?.closest?.('.eye-row')?.querySelector('.eye-label')?.textContent ?? null;
  pop.replaceChildren(...buildRows(fresh));
  ...
}
```

A flip is asynchronous: PATCH, `loadSchema()`, the page redraw, and only then this rebuild. On an idle machine the whole tail runs ~20ms after the PATCH lands; under load it is unbounded. If it lands between a reader's mousedown and mouseup, `replaceChildren` detaches the row the mousedown focused. The mouseup then lands on the replacement, and a mousedown and a mouseup on different nodes fire **no `click` event at all** — so the row's handler never runs and the flip is lost. Focus falls to `<body>` at the same time, and the popover's Escape listener is its own (`showPopover` binds keydown on the popover), so Escape stops reaching it.

Kyle's 2026-09-02 ruling is that the popover stays put — "same node, same position, same scroll — only its rows learn the new truth". Replacing the row nodes is a coarse reading of that: the rows do not *learn*, they are swapped for new ones, which is what orphans the gesture.

## Evidence

Reproduced deterministically while fixing [[Issue#216]] (the same rebuild strands the browser suite's popover, and that fix landed as Gerrit 291 / `630a571`). Two scripts are attached to Issue #216:

- `race.mjs` — mousedown on a row, rebuild the popover's children, mouseup: `active: BODY`, `inPop: false`, `.chip-pop` still present after Escape.
- `race3.mjs` — the same thing end to end, with the app's own `save()` tail landing inside the gesture across a slowed `GET /api/schema`: the engine's hidden set never gains the field, so the click really was swallowed.

## Shape of a fix

Teach the live rows instead of swapping them. When `buildRows(fresh)` yields the same labels in the same order — which is every flip, since the eye's own switches never add or remove a row — copy the new `aria-checked` and the `.switch` `on` class onto the existing nodes and leave them attached; fall back to `replaceChildren` only when the row set itself changed. The row handlers close over the `hidden`/`sysOn` sets captured by `buildRows`, so either the handlers have to be re-bound or `row`'s `run` has to read the live table at click time; the second is the smaller idea and removes a stale-closure hazard as well.

Gate it with a browser case that holds the button down across the rebuild and asserts the field still toggles and Escape still closes the popover.

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-08T04:30:00Z · fixed · Gerrit 294 → ed4f910

**Tests added:**
- test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs: a gesture held across a rebuild slowed by a delayed GET /api/schema still lands (timed out at 30s before)
- test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs: 13 of 13 stamped rows survive a flip (0 of 13 before); ArrowDown still walks them; a second flip adds to the hidden set
- test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs: a changed row set still rebuilds, with focus following

- test/ui-contract.test.mjs: asserts the teach path, the relearnRows fallback and the three live-table reads instead of replaceChildren

issues.name: “+ New” silently does nothing on Workspace system tables (Spaces, Tables, Fields, Workflows): the create POST 400s “Name is required”
issues.description:
## Report (Kyle, UAT in the `test` workspace, 2026-09-07)

> in uat was not able to use this button to add new rows in any of the table in this space but was able to in the leads table within the same workspace

“This space” = the Workspace system space (Spaces / Tables / Fields / Workflows). Leads (Marketing space) works.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-09-07 on :4400 at dfc8f9f)

Open `/w/test/#/table/<Spaces table id>`, click `+ New space`. Row count stays the same, focus stays on `<body>`, no toast. Network: `POST /w/test/api/tables/<Spaces>/entities → 400`. Same for Tables, Fields, Workflows.

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/test/api/tables/<id>/entities -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
{"error": "Name is required", "code": "invalid"}      # all four system tables
$ … Leads … -d '{}'  → 201, publicId 12                     # regular table accepts a blank row
```

Root cause: the grid's `onAdd` posts a blank row and then focuses the Name cell (Issues #125, #195). The engine's system-table create paths (`createSpace`/`createTable`/… — `src/engine.js` `Space name is required`, `Table name is required`, …) refuse an empty Name, and the grid swallows the 400 (no toast, no console error).

## Expected

1. `+ New <term>` works on every table the grid can show, system tables included. Either the system rows accept a placeholder name that the caret then replaces (e.g. `Untitled space`, renamed on first commit — the row IS the space, so the name must exist), or the foot opens an inline Name editor first and creates on commit for tables whose create requires a name.
2. A failed create is never silent: the grid surfaces the engine error (toast / inline) and the button is not left looking dead.
3. Shift+Enter from a row (the other create path) behaves the same way.

## Where

`public/app.js` `onAdd` (~5189 and ~7342), `src/engine.js` create paths for system tables, `src/routes.js` entities POST.

## Verify

Playwright: in a scratch workspace open Workspace/Spaces, click `+ New space`, assert a new row appears with the caret in its Name cell, type a name, assert the space exists in the sidebar; repeat for Tables/Fields/Workflows; assert a forced 400 produces a visible error. Regular table path (Leads) unchanged.

## Fixed (agent, 2026-09-07) — commit 9036c63, Gerrit change 295 (PS3, Verified+1: 1952 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped; merged; :4400 redeployed 21:33 PDT)

- `public/app.js` — the table page's `inlineAdd` now seeds a **Spaces** row with `New space`, selected whole so the first keystroke replaces it (the same door the home page used); on **Tables** it opens a name + space dialog (space picked in the picker dialect, system space excluded); on **Fields** it asks which table and hands over to that table's field dialog; **Workflows** post an ordinary blank row. Every path is wrapped: a refused create lands in an error toast. Saving a registry row reloads the schema, so a renamed space shows in the sidebar at once. Shift+Enter shares `inlineAdd`, so it takes the same door.
- `src/engine.js` — `#interceptCreate` intercepts only the three registries; a Workflows row is ordinary data and accepts a blank name like any table (Spaces still refuses one: the row IS the space).
- `src/handbook.js` — the registry paragraph names the foot's behaviour.
- Tests: `test/system-table-new-row-browser.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases — each registry from the foot, Shift+Enter, a forced 400 → toast, the regular table unchanged) and a blank-Workflows-row case in `test/workflows-table.test.mjs`.

## Report (Kyle, UAT in the `test` workspace, 2026-09-07, after Feature #196 shipped)

issues.name: Two overlapping eye flips: the second PATCH overwrites the first
issues.description:
## Symptom

Two eye flips that overlap lose the first one. Both switches move on screen, but the table ends up carrying only the second flip's hidden set.

## Where

`public/app.js`, `fieldVisibilityPopover`. Each row's handler reads the table at click time (`liveTable()`, Issue #240) and PATCHes the whole `hiddenFields` array. Reading live is the right half; writing a whole array is the racy half. Two handlers that both run before either PATCH lands read the same pre-flip set, so the second PATCH overwrites the first field's change instead of adding to it.

Idle, a flip's round trip is ~20ms and two human gestures are further apart than that, so this needs load: Issue #216 measured the same tail at 8.7s on a loaded gate, long enough for two ordinary flips to overlap.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `:4400` (serving `ed4f910`) while verifying Issue #240, on `Quality/Case` starting from `hiddenFields: ["Chip","Card"]`. Two clicks dispatched in one tick — `f('Status').click(); f('Suite').click();` — left the table at `["Chip","Card","Suite"]`. Status was lost.

Predates Issue #240: the handlers used to close over the set captured when the row was built, which is the same pre-flip set, so the same last write won.

## Shape of a fix

Send the delta instead of the whole array — one field name and a direction — and let the engine apply it to whatever the set currently is; or serialise the flips on the client, queueing the next PATCH behind the one in flight. The first is smaller and survives two tabs; the second needs no engine change.

Gate it with a browser case that holds `PATCH /api/tables/:id` open across a second flip and asserts both fields end up hidden.

issues.name: A manifest correction never reaches an instance that already applied the wrong one
issues.description:
**Found 2026-09-08** while fixing Issue #229, which corrected the v0.4.5 Release row's `Fixes` on the canonical workspace and re-exported `docs/development.json`.

## Symptom

`syncDevelopment` (`src/weaver-seed.js`) applies a manifest additively. Rows are created or updated by name, and a release's relations are linked:

```
if (fixes.length) w.link(id, 'Fixes', fixes);
if (ships.length) w.link(id, 'Ships', ships);
```

Nothing unlinks. An instance that applied the 2026-09-05 manifest holds nine watcher rows under v0.4.5's `Fixes`, and the corrected manifest cannot take them back — the new manifest simply names fewer targets, and `link` adds. The same holds for any relation a release loses.

A fresh instance reads the corrected manifest and is right. Only an instance that synced between the mistake and the correction carries the false claim, and it carries it forever.

## Why it matters

The Development manifest is how a release's contents reach every instance. A wrong claim that ships is recoverable only if the correction ships too.

## Shape of a fix

Reconcile a release's `Fixes` and `Ships` to what the manifest names, rather than adding to them — the release row is manifest-owned in a way an Issue row is not, since an instance has no reason to link its own rows into an upstream release. Locally filed Issue and Feature rows must stay untouched, which is the additive rule's real purpose (`test/development-sync.test.mjs`, 'rows the manifest does not name are left alone').

Gate it with a case that syncs a manifest linking two issues to a release, then syncs one that names only one of them, and asserts the release ends with one fix.

Severity Low: it is one stale relation on one downstream row, and no instance but this one is known to have synced the bad manifest.

---

🌙 attempt 1 · 2026-09-08 00:25 PDT · fixed · Gerrit 304 → 2db00c4

`syncDevelopment` reconciles a release's `Fixes` and `Ships` to exactly what the manifest names instead of adding to them: what is missing is linked, what the manifest no longer names is unlinked (through the engine's own `link`/`unlink`, so undo, the activity log and the `Fixed in` inverse all follow). Issue and Feature rows stay additive, which is what protects a locally filed row through an update. The exporter omits an empty relation, so an absent `fixes`/`ships` key reads as empty and clears the relation.

**Tests added** (`test/development-sync.test.mjs`):
- a corrected manifest takes back a release claim the wrong one made
- a release the corrected manifest empties keeps no fixes and no ships
- reconciling a release leaves locally filed Issue and Feature rows alone

Full suite on the patchset: 1967 pass, fail 0, skipped 0.

**Live verification:** `GET /api/health` reads sha `2db00c4`, startedAt `2026-09-08T07:25:01.770Z` (later than the 07:23:24 submit). The repro is the real one: a fresh workspace fed the 2026-09-05 manifest, then the corrected one. Against the pre-fix code it holds 13 fixes with 9 watcher rows among them and the correction changes nothing; against the code `:4400` serves (`~/.weave-serve` @ `2db00c4`) it lands on the 4 fixes the manifest names, 0 watcher rows. `:4400`'s own v0.4.5 row still reads those same 4 — the canonical workspace was already correct and the deploy's boot sync left it that way. Script and transcript attached (`repro-244.mjs`, `repro-244.txt`).

**Found along the way:** applying the shipped manifest to a *fresh* seed throws `'v0.4' is not an option of 'Milestone'` before it ever reaches the release block — `bin/weave.js` swallows it in a bare `catch`, so a new install silently applies half a manifest and retries every boot. Filed separately.

*(Housekeeping: this Description was briefly blanked at 07:25 by a fixer PUT that sent the wrong body key — `content` instead of `doc`, which the route reads as an empty write. Restored verbatim from `docs/development.json` @ 2db00c4, which carries this row's text as exported.)*

issues.name: A fresh install applies half its manifest: an unknown Milestone throws and boot swallows it
issues.description:
**Found 2026-09-08** while fixing Issue #244, building a repro that seeded a fresh workspace and applied the shipped manifest to it.

## Symptom

```
$ node -e "seedWeaver(new Weave()) -> syncDevelopment(w, docs/development.json)"
WeaveError: 'v0.4' is not an option of 'Milestone'
    at #validateValue (src/engine.js:3676)
    at #applyValues (src/engine.js:3571)
    at Weave.updateEntity (src/engine.js:3539)
    at apply (src/weaver-seed.js:375)
    at syncDevelopment (src/weaver-seed.js:380)
```

The seed's `Development/Feature` table defines a Milestone select whose options do not cover every milestone the canonical workspace uses. `syncDevelopment` writes `Milestone` straight through `updateEntity`, which validates against those options and throws on the first row carrying one the seed never heard of.

`bin/weave.js` wraps the whole sync in a bare `catch { /* no manifest in this build */ }`, so nothing is printed and serving continues.

## Why it matters

The throw lands mid-pass, and the pass is not transactional:

- Issue rows are applied (`apply` runs first), Feature rows are applied only up to the first unknown milestone, and the release block never runs at all — so a fresh install gets no `Development/Release` rows and no release contents.
- `w.state.meta.developmentSync` is written after the release block, so the stamp is never set: every boot repeats the same half-pass and the same silent throw.
- The comment on the catch says "no manifest in this build", which is the one thing that is not happening.

Reproduced on v0.4.10 (`2db00c4`) against the shipped `docs/development.json`. The canonical workspace is unaffected — it already carries every option — so this only bites a genuinely new install, which is exactly the case the manifest exists for.

## Shape of a fix

Make the manifest able to carry a select option the seed does not have: either widen the option set from the manifest's own values before applying (a select's options are engine-editable), or fall back to skipping the one field rather than the whole pass. Either way the boot catch should say what it swallowed instead of guessing at the reason, and the stamp question needs an answer — a pass that half-applied should not stamp itself done.

Gate it with a case that applies the shipped `docs/development.json` to a freshly seeded workspace and asserts it applies whole: no throw, and the Release rows land.

- Steps: `public/style.css` only for the height.
- Size: S.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:35:00Z

## Reproduced (2026-09-28, harness session 1b4685bd)

Scratch server on gerrit/main f34f90c (v0.4.51), Playwright WebKit with the iPhone 13 profile and Chromium with the Pixel 7 profile (touch, mobile viewport), for the Description and for a second markdown document field named Brief.

- **Rendered editing and no Save button: already true.** Both fields mount Vditor in instant-rendering mode (`.vditor-ir` is the only visible surface) and the page has no Save button.
- **Backgrounding loses the text: 4 of 4 lost.** Type, then `visibilitychange` to hidden and `pagehide`, then the tab is frozen or discarded: nothing was ever written, in both browsers and both fields.
- **Every other leaving path wrote late.** Tap outside, Back, closing the entity panel and a composed word all saved, but only about 1.4s after the last keystroke, from a timer; no write left the page at the moment of leaving. A reload straight after typing lost the text.

Root cause: Vditor hands its text to weave 800ms after the last keystroke (its `undoDelay`), and `scheduleDocSave` writes it 600ms later. `flushDocSaves` (public/app.js) wrote only what was already queued, so inside that window it had nothing to write, and it ran on `beforeunload` and route changes only. iOS Safari rarely fires `beforeunload`; a phone leaves through `visibilitychange` and `pagehide`, and nothing listened to either.

Related: Feature #217 (autosave everywhere) plans one save queue with a pending glyph for every surface; this fix covers document fields only and does not build the glyph.

## Fixed (2026-09-28)

Landed as 374d4f0 (Gerrit change 478, patch set 4), live on `:4400` (`/api/health` sha 374d4f0, behind false).

- `mountDocEditor` keeps the text it last handed over and a `pull()` that reads the editing surface at once and hands it on if it moved. The baseline is the surface as Vditor built it, so an untouched document never saves itself. A value mid-command (a reference, block or raw-HTML marker) is left alone.
- `flushDocSaves()` pulls every live editor before it writes, and now runs on `pagehide` and when the tab is hidden, as well as on `beforeunload` and route changes. A tap outside the editor (`focusout`) pulls and flushes too.
- `api()` sends writes from a hidden tab with `keepalive`, like an unloading page, so the save survives a frozen tab. A body of 60,000 bytes or more goes as a plain fetch, because the browser refuses a larger keepalive body. Before this change a long document's leaving save failed outright.
- Rendered editing and no Save button were already true on a phone; the suite now pins both.

Guarding tests: `test/doc-autosave-phone-browser.test.mjs`, 20 cases at 390x844 with touch, for the Description and a second markdown field. On f34f90c, 14 of the first 16 cases failed. All 20 pass on the change in Chromium and in WebKit, and the Gerrit gate on patch set 4 voted Verified+1 on the full suite.

Live check on `:4400` after the deploy (every write intercepted in the browser, so nothing was stored): this row's Description in WebKit with the iPhone 13 profile and in Chromium with the Pixel 7 profile. Both are edited in the rendered view with no Save button, and the PUT carrying the typed word left the page 31 ms (WebKit) and 29 ms (Chromium) after the tab was hidden.

`Fixed in` is left for the batch release.

issues.name: Workspace space menu offers Delete on the system space; refusal toast reads like a naming clash
issues.description:
## Symptom

On the system **Workspace** space page (any workspace, seen in `uno`), the ⋮ Space actions menu offers **Delete space + 4 tables**. Holding it fires `DELETE /api/spaces/<id>`; the engine refuses with `Space 'Workspace' is part of the system registry`, surfaced as a red toast. Kyle read the toast as a name conflict between the system space and the Spaces registry table.

## Expected

- The destructive item never renders on a system space. The sidebar already hides per-table menus for system tables (`public/app.js` ~L931, `if (!db.system)`); the space page's `dotsMenu` in `showSpace` (~L5895) has no `space.system` check.
- If the DELETE still reaches the engine (API/MCP callers), the message should say *why*: `Space 'Workspace' is the workspace's own system space and cannot be deleted` rather than the registry phrasing that reads like a clash.

## Where

- `public/app.js` `showSpace` → `dotsMenu([... { hold: 'Delete space…' }])` — add `space.system ? null : {...}`.
- `src/engine.js` `deleteSpace` (~L1109), `moveTable` (~L1326) — reword the WeaveError for the `workspace` system space.
- Engine behaviour is by design (Issue #126: the Workspace space gets a Spaces row; deletion refused downstream). Do not make the space deletable.

## Verify

1. Open `#/space/<workspace-space-id>` → ⋮ menu shows only the four Export items, no Delete.
2. `curl -X DELETE /api/spaces/<id>` → 400 with the reworded message.
3. Any user space → Delete still present and still works.
4. Playwright + unit suites green; Handbook unchanged (no new field type).

Named casualties include `c-json-editor.html` and `IMG_0781.jpeg`, so these are real uploads rather than fixtures. `files/` holds 258 blobs against 296 live references.

Weave already degrades gracefully — Quality cases #2495 and #2500 cover export and cell rendering when a blob is gone — so nothing crashes. That is what makes this an Issue rather than a bug report: the bytes went missing quietly, across some unknown window, and no surface counts them. Open one of those rows and you see a named file that will not download.

**Not yet known:** when they went, and to what. Candidates worth eliminating in order — a data-dir move or restore that copied `*.db` without `files/`; a workspace import carrying references without blobs; a delete path that drops bytes while the reference survives.

**Reproduce the count:**

```bash
node ~/bin/weave-backup
# attachments 299 referenced, 59 with no bytes at source
```

The backup is unaffected and copies 258/258 of what exists. It reports this as a source condition instead of failing, because a backup cannot copy bytes that are not there.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:30:41Z

## Investigation, 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd)

**Summary.** The bytes were never deleted. All 59 blobs sit in the old repo-root data directory, `~/Documents/harness.nosync/weave/files/`, and every one matches its reference by id and by recorded size. They were left behind on 2026-08-28, when the databases moved to `~/.weave` and `files/` did not move with them. The count has not changed since 2026-09-08, so nothing is still losing files. Recovery is one no-clobber copy, which waits for Kyle's go-ahead (below).

### 1. Today's count

I ran the audit read-only: every `~/.weave/*.db` opened with `node:sqlite` `readOnly: true`, the `files[]` ledger of each entity compared with `ls ~/.weave/files`, and nothing written outside the scratchpad. The `.db` mtimes were identical before and after the run. `~/bin/weave-backup` has no dry-run mode, so I did not use it.

| Workspace | Referenced | Present | Missing | Missing on live rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| weave.db | 527 | 473 | 54 | 54 |
| uno.db | 400 | 395 | 5 | 2 |
| the other six workspaces | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **927** | **868** | **59** | **56** |

`~/.weave/files/` holds 886 blobs today, against 258 on 2026-09-08.

**The count has not grown.** I ran the same audit over every nightly snapshot in `~/Documents/Weave Backups/db/`, checking each against the append-only mirror. All 21 snapshots, from 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-28, show the same 59 ids missing (54 in weave.db, 5 in uno.db), while references grew from 299 to 927. No reference added since 2026-08-28 has lost its bytes.

### 2. The list

The attached `issue-250-missing-attachments-2026-09-28.csv` has one line per missing reference: workspace, file id, file name, mime, recorded size, upload time, table, public id, entity id, row name, live or trashed.

- Upload times run from **2026-08-16 19:28Z to 2026-08-28 01:46Z**. No missing file was uploaded after that.
- weave.db, 54: screenshots on Development/Issue #9, #11 to #15, #30, #54, #55, #72 to #77, #81, #87, #90, #91 and Development/Feature #41, #62, #108, #144.
- uno.db, 5: `c-json-editor.html` on Decks/Attached Deck #1, `IMG_0781.jpeg` on Product/Task #7, and three `thumbnail.jpg` files on Library/Saves #1 to #3. The three Saves rows are in the trash.
- The ten files on Feature #41 (`field-config-opt-A.png` and the rest) were recorded as 6 bytes when they were uploaded. They hold 6 bytes of noise, not images. They were broken when uploaded, and restoring them brings back that noise.

### 3. Location of the bytes

| Location | Missing ids found (id and size match) |
| --- | --- |
| `~/Documents/harness.nosync/weave/files/` (old repo-root data dir) | **59 of 59** |
| `~/Documents/Weave Backups/files/` (nightly mirror) | 0 |
| `~/Documents/Weave Backups/db/*` | databases only, no blobs |
| `~/.weave-serve`, `~/.weave-passkey-test`, worktrees under `harness.nosync` and `external/weave-worktrees` | no `files/` directory |
| `~/.Trash` | one unrelated folder (`verify-out-1790543174`) |

The old directory holds exactly these 59 files and nothing else. `file(1)` agrees with each recorded mime: 44 PNG, 4 JPEG, 1 HTML, plus the ten 6-byte files. Its blobs were written from 2026-08-16 12:28 to 2026-08-27 18:46 PDT, and the directory has not changed since.

**Risk until this is resolved.** That directory is gitignored (`.gitignore:9 files/`) in the shared weave checkout and is not in any backup. It is the only copy. A `git clean -fdx` in that checkout would destroy all 59 files for good.

**Recovery commands. Do not run these until Kyle agrees.** They only add files to `~/.weave/files`, never overwrite, and leave the source in place. The server checks for a blob on every request, so no restart is needed.

```bash
SRC=~/Documents/harness.nosync/weave/files
# 1. Dry run: expect exactly 59 lines, all new files (">f+++++++++")
rsync -a --ignore-existing --dry-run --itemize-changes "$SRC/" ~/.weave/files/ | tee /tmp/r250.txt | wc -l
grep -vc '^>f+++++++++' /tmp/r250.txt   # expect 0
# 2. Copy
rsync -a --ignore-existing "$SRC/" ~/.weave/files/
# 3. Verify byte for byte (expect no output)
for id in $(ls "$SRC"); do cmp -s "$SRC/$id" ~/.weave/files/$id || echo "MISMATCH $id"; done
# 4. Verify through the app (expect 200 and 200)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/weave/api/files/10db6944-ef87-4361-a3f6-5d607752b7f0
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/uno/api/files/afdce335-3f80-4613-84f0-f69f03012d7b
# 5. The next nightly (or `node ~/bin/weave-backup`) should print "0 with no bytes at source"
```

If Kyle would rather drop the ten 6-byte files on Feature #41 than restore them, exclude them from step 2 with `--exclude-from` and a list of their ids from the CSV (every row with size 6).

### 4. Root cause

**Candidate 1, a data-dir move that copied the databases without `files/`: confirmed.** The engine keeps blobs in `dirname(store.path)/files` (`src/engine.js:6838`). Until 2026-08-28 the server ran against databases in the repo root, so uploads went to `harness.nosync/weave/files/`. On 2026-08-28 (memory note "weave data dir is ~/.weave") the databases were checkpointed and copied into `~/.weave/`, and the repo-root copies were moved to `harness.nosync/backups/weave-dbs-2026-08-28/` (07:52 to 08:00 PDT). `files/` was not copied. The dates split cleanly. All 59 references uploaded before the move are missing and sit in the old directory, while the 868 uploaded after it all have their bytes. The newest blob in the old directory is from 2026-08-27 18:46 PDT; the oldest in `~/.weave/files` is from 2026-08-31 19:36 PDT.

A scratch test reproduces it: a workspace with two attached files, its `.db` copied into another directory with `VACUUM INTO`, then opened there, has 2 references and 0 blobs.

**Candidate 2, an import that carries references without blobs: not the cause here, but the path exists.** The CLI and HTTP export and import round trip keeps the bytes (Issue #121, `test/file-blobs.test.mjs`). The MCP export omits blobs by default, and importing that dump with `importJSON` leaves every reference with nothing behind it and says nothing. Filed as **Issue #462**. None of the 59 came this way, because all 59 are in the old directory.

**Candidate 3, a delete or trash path that removes bytes while a reference survives: eliminated.** No code in `src/`, `bin/` or `scripts/` ever deletes a blob. `deleteFile` (`src/engine.js:6931`) drops the reference and leaves the bytes. A hard delete of a row (`:5311`), a table or a space drops the row and leaves the bytes. Workspace delete (`src/server.js:247`) moves only the `.db` into `trash/`. Moving a row to another table skips its files and soft-deletes the original, which keeps them. Scratch tests against `f34f90c`, one per path, found no dangling reference after any of them: file delete, soft delete then restore, undo, hard delete of a row, a table and a space, table trash then restore, duplicate table then delete on the copy, move to another table, CLI/HTTP export then import, and file delete plus hard delete over HTTP on a scratch server (`serve --port 0`). 10 pass, 0 fail.

**No live code path loses bytes, so there is no fix to land.** The loss was a one-time operational step. The lesson belongs in the data-dir note: moving a weave instance means moving `files/` with the databases. `weave backup` and `weave restore` (Feature #209) now do both together.

### 5. The attachment on the live app

- **Attachments field (1 of 56, Decks/Attached Deck #1, `c-json-editor.html`).** The field shows the name in a dimmed chip followed by `(missing)`, with a tooltip saying the stored file is gone and only its name is left. There is no link, and the × is still there to remove it. This is the Issue #121 treatment.
- **Ledger only (55 of 56, for example Development/Issue #9 and uno Product/Task #7).** The entity page shows no file at all. The only trace is the activity line "attached chip-picker-after-fix.png". `GET /api/files/<id>` returns 404 `{"error":"File blob missing"}`, and `readEntity` flags the file `missing: true`, but no surface draws it. Present ledger files are just as invisible (Issue #313 has one), so this gap is not specific to lost bytes. Filed as **Issue #463**.

### Decision for Kyle

59 of 59 files can be restored from the old repo-root directory with the commands above. The cleanup of any dead reference that remains is still open. Options:

1. **Restore all 59**, which the evidence supports: no reference stays dead. The ten 6-byte files on Feature #41 come back as the noise they were uploaded as.
2. **Restore 49 and remove the ten 6-byte references** from Feature #41 with `deleteFile`.
3. **Restore nothing and remove all 59 references.** The bytes are still on disk, so this gives up data that can be recovered.

Presentation of a missing file, for any future loss. The field chip already has one treatment, and the ledger has none (Issue #463):

- a. Keep the Issue #121 chip (dimmed name, `(missing)`, ×) and give ledger files a Files card that uses the same chip.
- b. Add a count to the workspace health or admin surface ("N files have no bytes"), so a loss is no longer silent. Today only the nightly backup log reports it.
- c. Offer a "re-upload" action on a missing chip that keeps the file id, so references elsewhere, such as document links, still work.

Status stays In Progress until Kyle decides.

## Restored, 2026-09-28 (on Kyle's decision)

On Kyle's decision to keep every attachment reference and restore all 59 files, I copied the 59 blobs from `~/Documents/harness.nosync/weave/files/` into `~/.weave/files/` on 2026-09-28 at about 20:05Z. No reference was removed or edited. That includes the ten 6-byte files on Feature #41, which came back as uploaded.

**Before the copy.** The source held 59 files, and they were exactly the 59 ids in the attached CSV. None of the 59 names existed in `~/.weave/files/`. The dry run (`rsync -a -O --ignore-existing --dry-run --itemize-changes`) listed 59 new files and nothing else.

**The copy.** `rsync -a -O --ignore-existing` exited 0 and transferred 59 files. `-O` leaves the destination directory's own mtime alone. The source was only read: its sha256 list is identical before and after, and it still holds 59 files.

**Verification.**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Size against source | 59 of 59 match |
| sha256 against source | 59 of 59 match |
| Size against the size recorded on the reference | 59 of 59 match |
| `~/.weave/files` count | 888 before, 947 after |
| Read-only audit, weave.db | 529 referenced, 529 present, 0 missing |
| Read-only audit, uno.db | 400 referenced, 400 present, 0 missing |
| `GET /w/weave/api/files/10db6944…` (`chip-picker-after-fix.png`, Development/Issue #9) | 200, image/png, 45,475 bytes, PNG header |
| `GET /w/uno/api/files/afdce335…` (`IMG_0781.jpeg`, Product/Task #7) | 200, image/jpeg, 2,341,353 bytes |
| Decks/Attached Deck #1 on the live page | the chip is a link again, without the missing treatment; its download returns 200, text/html, 22,961 bytes |

**No restart.** The server checks for a blob on every request, so the files were served at once. The :4400 listener is still PID 63426, started 08:42 today.

**Tonight's backup.** `~/bin/weave-backup` runs at 04:00 and mirrors `~/.weave/files/` into `~/Documents/Weave Backups/files/` with `rsync -a`, append-only (line 175). Tonight's run will add the 59 files to the mirror, which today holds 880. After that the old repo-root directory is no longer the only other copy.

The job has a separate problem, now Issue #465. It has exited 1 every night since about 2026-09-13, because iCloud made `RESTORE.md` dataless and the write at line 186 fails. That write comes after the snapshot and the `files/` rsync, so the mirror still gets the 59 files, but the job's own report, including the orphan count, never prints. Check `~/Documents/Weave Backups/files/` after 04:00 to confirm.

Issues #462 and #463 stay open as their own rows. The old directory is left as it was.

issues.name: State field should start with default states
issues.description:
## Symptom

Adding a **State** (workflow) field starts with an empty state list. The tray refuses to save — "Workflow field needs at least one state" — so every new state field makes you invent and type a status vocabulary before you can create the column. The CLI is the same: `weave field add T Status workflow` throws unless `--config` carries a `states` array.

## What Kyle wants

A new state field arrives with sensible out-of-the-box states already filled in, and those are editable in the field config like anything else.

## Shape

- Seed the default from the four state categories the engine already knows (`STATE_CATEGORIES` in `src/engine.js:171`): **Not started · In progress · Done · Canceled**, with `Not started` as the default state.
- Seed at the point of blankness, not by weakening validation: the tray's `blankState()` for `workflow` (`public/field-dialog-core.js:305`) should hand back the four states pre-filled, and `normalizeSelfContainedConfig` (`src/engine.js:~460`) should apply the same default when `config.states` is absent.
- Keep the throw for an *explicitly empty* array — a field the user deliberately emptied is still invalid.
- Editing is unchanged: rename, reorder, recolor, add, delete in the field config tray.

## Gates

- Engine test: `field add … workflow` with no config yields the four default states, `Not started` default:true.
- Engine test: `--config '{"states":[]}'` still throws.
- Field-dialog test: opening the tray on type=workflow shows four rows, saving without edits succeeds.
- Handbook page for the state field type documents the defaults (Handbook is gated).

issues.name: # column should freeze to the left edge and never reorder
issues.description:
## Symptom

On a wide table the grid scrolls sideways (`.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto }`, `public/style.css:277`) and the **#** column scrolls away with everything else. Scroll right to read a far column and the row loses its identity — you cannot see which row you are on, and the `#12 ↗` permalink is off-screen.

The `#` header is sticky on `top` only (`public/style.css:283`), never on `left`. `th.pid-head` / `td.pid-cell` (`:288`) set width and alignment and nothing else.

## What Kyle wants

The `#` column is anchored and frozen to the left-hand edge, and it can never be reordered.

## Shape

**Freeze.** `position: sticky; left: 0` on `th.pid-head` and `td.pid-cell`, with an opaque background (a sticky cell over scrolling content must paint) and a right-edge shadow or border so the frozen column reads as a seam rather than as overlap.

- The selection checkbox column (`th.sel-head` / `td.sel-cell`, `:293`) sits LEFT of `#`, so it freezes too or the pair separates on scroll. Freeze both and give `#` a `left` offset equal to the checkbox column's width.
- z-index is load-bearing here: the header is already `z-index: 2` sticky-top, the Σ foot row `z-index: 1` (`:1940`). A left-frozen header cell needs to beat both the body cells beside it and the foot, so the corner cells (`thead th.pid-head`, `tr.wv-foot td` first cells) need a higher z than the plain sticky-top headers.
- The add-entity row (`tr.add-entity-row td`, `:491`) is sticky-bottom and spans — check it does not tear.
- Light and dark both: the frozen background is a token, never a literal.

**No reorder.** `#` is a hardcoded `th` outside the `cols.map` (`public/app.js:3691`), so today's drag path already cannot move it — but nothing asserts that. Lock it with a test rather than leaving it true by accident: a header drag whose target is the `#` column is a no-op, and no field can be ordered ahead of it.

## Gates

- Browser test: on a grid wider than its wrap, scroll the wrap right and assert `td.pid-cell` stays at the wrap's left edge and stays visible; assert the checkbox cell stays with it.
- Browser test: header drag onto `#` leaves the field order unchanged.
- Visual: the frozen column paints opaque over scrolled content in both themes (no bleed-through).
- Related grids and the stats grid use the same `pid-head` classes (`public/style.css:1091`, `public/app.js:2976`, `:7979`) — they must not regress.

issues.name: A version bump reaches users only if it is published as a release
issues.description:
**Symptom.** An install ran 0.4.4 (2026-08-31) while main was 0.4.15, 224 commits ahead, and every version check called it current. Releasing weave is a `Development/Release` row plus a package.json bump landed through Gerrit — no git tag, no GitHub Release. Tags stopped at v0.4.4 on 2026-09-02, so `gh release list`, the repo's Releases sidebar and `git describe` all named a build eleven versions old as the newest one. A user cannot notice a gap upstream never publishes.

**Expected.** Every landed version bump is a `v<version>` tag on the commit that introduced it and a GitHub Release carrying that version's CHANGELOG section, published the day it lands.

**Where.** Fixed outside this repo, in the main watcher: `harness/scripts/weave-release-tags.mjs` publishes what the landed range owes, called from `weave-review-poll.mjs` right after the green gerrit/main -> GitHub mirror. Release notes stay mandatory: a version with no `## v<version>` CHANGELOG section is skipped and files an Issue rather than shipping an empty release. v0.4.5 through v0.4.15 were backfilled 2026-09-09.

**Left open here.** Two things belong in weave itself: DEVELOPMENT.md's Releasing section still lists four steps and never mentions the tag, and a running instance still cannot tell its user a newer release exists — `/api/health` reports its own version and commit, and nothing compares that to the newest published tag.

**Verify.** `gh release list -R grunion-ai/weave` names the package.json version as Latest; `node scripts/weave-release-tags.mjs --dry-run` on a current main prints `nothing owed`. Gate: `harness/scripts/weave-release-tags.test.mjs`.



---

**Observation, 2026-09-10 01:10 PDT (overnight fixer, not an attempt on this Issue).** v0.4.16 merged as `6ea8aa4` and `:4400` serves it, but no `v0.4.16` tag and no GitHub Release were published. The cause is not in this repo and not in the tag script: `scripts/weave-release-tags.mjs` and its call site landed on harness `main` as `6d3dd9f`, while the checkout launchd actually runs the watcher from — `/Users/kyle/Documents/harness.nosync`, per `ai.grunion.weave-review.plist` — is sitting on branch `claude/email-post-address` with uncommitted work from another session. `grep -n release-tags scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs` on that working tree returns nothing, and `/tmp/weave-review-poll.log` for the `6ea8aa49` landing shows the mirror, the pack and the quality sync with no tag step between them.

So the fix for this Issue is correct and merged upstream, and it is simply not the code that ran tonight. Nothing was changed here to compensate. Two things follow, neither decided here: the watcher wants to run from a fixed ref rather than from whatever branch that tree happens to be on, and a landed bump that never got its tag needs to be caught rather than noticed by hand — `weave-release-tags.mjs --dry-run` on a current main would have printed what was owed.

Backfill owed once the tree is back on `main`: `v0.4.16` on `6ea8aa4`.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:31:02.622Z

---

**Close-out, 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd, high-severity batch).** Parts 1 and 2 are done. The only thing left on this Issue is Kyle's decision on an in-app update check (part 3).

**Part 1, tags and Releases: complete, nothing owed.** Every version from v0.4.16 to v0.4.51 that has a `## v<version>` section in CHANGELOG.md has a tag on GitHub (`git ls-remote --tags origin`) and a GitHub Release, and v0.4.51 is marked Latest. `node scripts/weave-release-tags.mjs --dry-run` from `~/.harness-serve` (harness 1ae6cdd) against gerrit/main f34f90c prints `release tags: nothing owed` and `0 published, 0 skipped`. The tagger reads GitHub's tags (`git ls-remote`) and Releases (`gh release view`), never local tags. The gaps in the release list never landed as a version. The package.json history on gerrit/main goes straight from 0.4.32 to 0.4.34 (`c2ac845`), from 0.4.40 to 0.4.42 (`1ed7e7b`), from 0.4.43 to 0.4.45 (merge `644269b`) and from 0.4.45 to 0.4.50 (`248dd00`). No commit on any ref names v0.4.33, v0.4.41 or v0.4.44. v0.4.46 to v0.4.49 are the subjects of Gerrit changes 433, 443, 444 and 445, all still open, so no Release is owed. Those four changes need new version numbers above 0.4.51 before they land.

**Part 2, DEVELOPMENT.md: complete.** The Releasing section has described the `v<version>` tag and the GitHub Release as step 6 since `2464495` (2026-09-26), and `test/development-sync.test.mjs` holds it and CLAUDE.md rule 5 to that. One stale detail remained: the section said the watcher runs from `~/Documents/harness.nosync` and publishes only while that checkout is on main, and it told readers to re-run the tagger there. launchd now runs both watcher jobs from `~/.harness-serve`. Gerrit change 474 (commit 2c0f139, pushed 2026-09-28, in review) points the section at `~/.harness-serve`, says the tagger checks GitHub, and adds an assertion to `test/development-sync.test.mjs` (red before the doc edit, 25 of 25 green after). Its changelog fragment is `changelog.d/release-docs-watcher-checkout-253.md`; there is no version bump.

**Part 3, the running instance: what it checks today.**
- `latestSha` is the output of `git ls-remote <first remote> main`, run from the server's own checkout (`src/server.js`, `refreshLatest`). The first remote is the first line of `git remote`, which git sorts alphabetically. On `~/.weave-serve` that is `gerrit`, so the live app compares against Gerrit's main. On a plain clone from GitHub it is `origin`, so the app already makes a network call to GitHub: one `git ls-remote` at most every 5 minutes, only when `/api/health` is requested, with a 4 second timeout, silent when offline.
- `behind` is `latest !== head`: main's sha differs from the boot HEAD. It compares commits on main, never tags or Releases. It is true whenever the two differ, including a checkout that is ahead of main or pinned to a release tag (filed as Issue #459).
- The UI does show it. With `behind` true and `stale` false, the instance chip in the sidebar turns amber, shows both shas, and a toast fires once per page load telling the user to run `weave service promote` (`public/app.js`, the nav health chip). That command defaults to `--remote gerrit` and fails on a plain clone with `git fetch gerrit main failed` (reproduced in a fresh clone of grunion-ai/weave at f34f90c, filed as Issue #458).
- An outside user on a plain clone learns only that GitHub's main has moved, on every commit, not that a newer release exists. An install without `.git` (the source zip on a GitHub Release page) has no HEAD, so `buildInfo()` returns null and it learns nothing at all. Nothing in the running app reads tags or Releases.

**Part 3, what an update check would take (not built, Kyle's decision).**
- One request: `GET https://api.github.com/repos/grunion-ai/weave/releases/latest`, reading `tag_name` and `html_url`, and comparing it to the running `package.json` version by semver. Unauthenticated, the API allows 60 requests an hour per IP; sending the stored `ETag` as `If-None-Match` turns a repeat into a 304 that does not count. A cheaper variant needs no API at all: add `git ls-remote --tags <remote> 'v*'` to the call a clone already makes, which works only for installs with `.git`.
- Frequency: once at boot and then once every 24 hours, cached on disk so restarts do not repeat it, with the existing 4 second timeout and silence when offline. Only `bin/weave.js serve` would run it, as with build info today, so tests and embedded servers never call out.
- Where it shows: two new `/api/health` fields, `latestRelease` and `updateAvailable`. The sidebar instance chip would read "v0.4.51 · v0.4.52 available" and link to the Release page, with one toast per new version (remembered per browser) whose remedy fits the install: `git pull` and restart for a clone, the Release page for a zip.
- Off switch: `WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK=0` in the environment or `--no-update-check` on `serve`, and a workspace setting if Kyle wants it in the UI. The request sends the instance IP and a User-Agent, nothing about the workspace.
- The open question: should a running weave call GitHub at all, and if so is the check on by default (opt-out) or off by default (opt-in)? Note that a plain clone already calls GitHub through the `git ls-remote` above, so the question is partly decided already.

**Decision and build, 2026-09-28.** Kyle decided on 2026-09-28 that the running app makes the update check, on by default with an off switch. Built in commit 62975e2 (Change-Id Ib791fe48), waiting to be pushed for review while the machine load stays near 200:
- `src/update-check.js`: one unauthenticated GET to `api.github.com/repos/grunion-ai/weave/releases/latest` at most once a day, 4 second timeout, answer and last-try time cached in `update-check.json` beside the workspace so a restart inside the day asks nothing. Offline, rate limited, timed out or malformed, it stays silent and the previous answer stands.
- `WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK=off` makes no request, following the existing WEAVE_* environment settings; documented in the Handbook's Environment reference guide, the Dockerfile and compose.yaml.
- `/api/health` gains `latestRelease`, `releaseCheckedAt` and `releaseBehind`; `sha`, `latestSha`, `behind` and `stale` keep their meaning. Works without a checkout, so a source zip also hears about a release.
- The sidebar instance chip uses the existing is-behind style and reads v<version> available, with a toast once per release per browser. Checked in both themes on a scratch server seeded with a cached 0.4.99 answer (no request made).
- Tests: `test/update-check.test.mjs` (14 pass, fetch injected, never GitHub); the tests that spawn serve or the container switch the check off. Targeted suites: 138 of 139 pass; the one failure is the Docker G3 container gate, whose health probe timed out at 90 seconds under load 200 (a scratch serve of the same commit booted and answered).
- Change 474 (DEVELOPMENT.md) got Verified -1 from the gate's 3600 second wall-clock cap at load 200; no test failed on its merits. It is re-pushed with the feature once load drops.

**Fixed, 2026-09-28.** Kyle decided on 2026-09-28 that the running app checks GitHub for a newer release; this closes the last open part of the Issue.
- Gerrit change 476, merged as a2b95b2: `src/update-check.js`, `/api/health` fields `latestRelease`, `releaseCheckedAt`, `releaseBehind`, the amber instance chip, and the `WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK=off` switch documented in the Environment reference guide, the Dockerfile and compose.yaml. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/newer-release-check-253.md`; no version bump, so Fixed in is set when the next release folds it.
- Gerrit change 474, merged in 942168b: DEVELOPMENT.md's Releasing section names `~/.harness-serve` as the tagger's checkout.
- Tests guarding it: `test/update-check.test.mjs` (14 cases, injected fetch: switched off makes no request, at most once a day across a restart, newer release marks behind, equal or older does not, every failure changes nothing, a hung request times out without blocking) and two assertions in `test/development-sync.test.mjs`. Final gate on 476 patch set 2: 2998 pass, 0 fail. Earlier gates were red only on load-sensitive browser cases (Issues #454, #466); Isolation runs on 2026-09-28 at load 11 to 26, each file alone three times on gerrit/main 942168b and three times on 942168b plus change 476: entity-block-grip-browser 3 of 3 cases green in all six runs, table-views-browser 16 of 16 in all six, grid-range-browser 21 of 21 in all six. None is red on main or on 476 alone; they go red only inside the full-suite gate.
- Live on :4400 at a2b95b2 (started 2026-09-29T00:52:41Z): `/api/health` reports `latestRelease` 0.4.51, `releaseCheckedAt` 2026-09-29T00:52:46Z, `releaseBehind` false, and `~/.weave/update-check.json` holds that one answer. The amber chip and toast were checked in light and dark on a scratch server seeded with a cached 0.4.99 answer.
- New Issues filed on the way: #458 (the behind toast tells every install to run weave service promote, which fails without a gerrit remote), #459 (behind is true whenever HEAD differs from main), #466 (a flaky browser case).

issues.name: Sorting: system fields cannot sort, and the labels are type-blind
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-09: "weave system fields also need sorting, sort should just be by ascending descending. but also largest smallest most recent to oldest or alphabetical."

## Two defects

**1. System fields have no sort path.** `Created At`, `Modified At`, `Created By`, `Modified By` toggle on in the eye and draw as read-only rows in the entity panel (Issue #174) — they never get a grid header, so there is no ⋮ menu and no way to sort by them. A direct `PATCH /tables/:id { sort: [{field:'Created At'}] }` is refused too: the validation in `updateTable` calls `getField()`, which throws on a system name. The engine itself already resolves them — `resolveField` and `#pathValue` both special-case `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `publicId`. The `#` public-id column has no sort affordance either.

**2. Sort labels are type-blind.** `fieldMenuButton` offers "Sort ascending" / "Sort descending" for every field. Ascending means A→Z on text, smallest-first on a number, oldest-first on a date — three different mental models under one word. The direction stored stays `asc`/`desc`; only the wording should change per type.

## Direction stays two-valued

`asc` / `desc` remains the stored truth (engine `sort: [{field, dir}]`, mirrored to the Tables registry `Sort` text). This is a labelling and reach problem, not a new sort model.

## Design options

Three mockups and a recommendation: see the design artifact handed to Kyle on 2026-09-09.

issues.name: Handbook rows in the live workspace never pick up a landed edit to src/handbook.js
issues.description:
## Symptom

`applyHandbook` (`src/handbook.js`) upserts every `Handbook/Guide` and `Handbook/Fields` row by name, doc included — but it only runs from `seedWeaver`, and `bin/weave.js serve` calls that **only when no `weave.db` exists beside the data file** (`bin/weave.js:196-207`). An existing docs workspace therefore never re-applies it.

So a change that edits the Handbook in `src/handbook.js`, lands it through Gerrit and deploys it leaves `:4400` showing the *old* page. The committed source is right, `test/handbook.test.mjs` gates it, and the reader sees neither.

Found while landing Issue #252 on 2026-09-10. The **Making a workspace your own** guide on `:4400` was missing the whole "Ranges, fill and paste" section that landed with Feature #220, plus the `bulk set` / `changed` sentence — the live row had been stale since that landing. I brought that one row up to date by hand (`PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc` with the generated markdown; the diff had no local-only content in it) — which is exactly the manual step this Issue is asking to remove.

## Shape

The Quality mirror already solves this shape: it is generated, never hand-edited, and `weave quality sync` re-applies it — the main watcher runs that after every landing (`harness/scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs:95`). The Handbook wants the same deal:

- a `weave handbook sync --data <weave.db>` verb that calls `applyHandbook` on an existing workspace, plus a `handbook check` that reports drift the way `quality check` does;
- the main watcher runs it beside `quality sync` after each landing;
- or, if re-applying on every boot is cheap enough, hash the generated content on `meta` the way `syncDevelopment` does and apply it when the hash moves — one write per build, not one per boot.

Either way the upsert must stay name-matched and additive, so a locally written Guide row is left alone.

## Gates

- A workspace seeded from an older build, then synced, carries the current Handbook text for every guide and field page.
- A guide row a person wrote themselves is untouched by the sync.
- `handbook check` reports drift, and reports none straight after a sync.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-11T08:56:05.873Z · started · session wf-0911-0117

## Resolution

Landed as Gerrit change 329, merged `349adba` (2026-09-11). `serve` now re-applies the generated Handbook/Guide + Handbook/Fields pages on the first boot of each build whose pages changed: `syncHandbook` stamps a hash of the generated pages on meta (`handbookSync`) and runs the name-matched, additive `applyHandbook` only when it moves. It never deletes a row and never touches a guide it does not generate. On demand: `weave handbook sync --data <weave.db>`; `weave handbook check --data <weave.db>` reports missing/stale pages (exit 1 on drift). Sync writes are attributed to actor `handbook-sync`. The harness main watcher needs no change, because the deploy restart carries the sync.

Gate: `test/handbook-sync.test.mjs` (10 cases, including serve boot end-to-end on a stale weave.db).

Verified live: the first :4400 boot of 349adba logged `Handbook sync: 0 created, 2 updated` (field pages `workflow` and `rollup` were stale; the source only added text and the live rows had no local-only content). All 25 generated pages now match src/handbook.js.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-11T09:24:45.442Z · fixed · Gerrit 329 → 349adba

**Tests added:**
- test/handbook-sync.test.mjs: 10 cases — an older-build workspace syncs to current text for every guide and field page; a hand-written guide is untouched; handbook check reports drift before and none after; ids kept; second boot of the same build is a no-op; CLI sync/check; serve boot end-to-end on a stale weave.db

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha 349adba startedAt 2026-09-11T09:22:18Z (after submit); /tmp/weave-serve.log on that boot: Handbook sync: 0 created, 2 updated (workflow, rollup field pages were stale); 25/25 generated pages on :4400 match src/handbook.js over HTTP. Gate 2111 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped.

issues.name: Slow: opening the Case table freezes the browser for 17–52 s (2,062 rows, 10 MB, no limit, no virtualization)
issues.description:
## Measured
- `POST /api/tables/<Case>/query` with an empty body returns **10,224,700 bytes** for 2,060 rows in 291 ms. The UI then rendered a **single 16,692 ms long task** (Playwright, 1440×900) and a **52,220 ms** one in the desktop-app browser pane. The tab is unresponsive the whole time.
- After paint: **2,062 `<tr>`** and **58,706 DOM nodes**. No windowing, no `limit` sent (`public/app.js:3104`), the loop at `public/app.js:3643` draws every row.
- Of the 10 MB, **4,656 KB is the `Suite` relation** re-embedded as a full summary on every row; `Chip`/`Card` view fields add 392 KB; the Description field is 4 KB total. Every row also carries `raw`, `doc`, `docs`, `comments`, `activity`, `files`.
- `GET /api/tables/<Case>/trash` is fetched on every table open too: **1,577 KB** for the Case table.
- The engine never touches SQL for a table query: `src/engine.js:3626` filters every entity in the workspace in JS, then `readEntity` per row resolves every relation (`src/engine.js:4645-4655`).

Issues #211 ("trouble loading this page") and #234 ("very slow") are almost certainly this.

## What good looks like
Airtable, Notion and Linear page or virtualize rows (~50–200 rows in the DOM), request only the columns the view shows, and resolve relations to a chip summary (id + name), never the full related row. A first paint under 1 s on 2,000 rows is the bar.

## Fix shape
1. Client sends `limit`/`offset` (the API already accepts both, `src/engine.js:4711`) and pages on scroll, or windows the rows.
2. `readEntity` in list context returns relation chips (id, name, icon) instead of the related row's full summary.
3. Drop the trash fetch from the table-open path; load it when the trash panel opens.

---
Filed by the 2026-09-12 CX/UX audit (Claude session, weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a, measured against :4400 in Chromium 1440×900 unless stated).

## Split (2026-09-12, Kyle)
This row is now the umbrella; the work is tracked in:
- #270 Slow: the trash list is fetched on every table open; load it on demand
- #271 Slow: grids draw every row; preview 300 rows and add "Show more"
- #272 Slow: table queries return every field and every related row in full; let the client ask for specific fields and chip-level relations

The 58,706-node figure: every rendered row is roughly 28 DOM nodes (a `<tr>`, ~9 `<td>`s, and inside each cell the chip/link/icon spans). 2,062 rows × 28 ≈ 58k nodes that the browser has to create, lay out and paint before it can respond to input, which is what the 17–52 s freeze is. Notion/Airtable keep ~2–5k nodes on screen by drawing only the visible window.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:30:15Z

## Re-measured on v0.4.51 (2026-09-28, harness session 1b4685bd)

The bar is met. The Case table has grown to **2,793 rows** (174 more in the trash), and it now paints its first rows in about a third of a second in both engines with no long task.

Probe: Playwright 1.62.1 against `:4400` at f34f90c, viewport 1440x900, read-only. "Cold" loads the app straight onto `#/table/<Case>`; "warm" is a hash navigation from Home, which is what a sidebar click does. First paint is the time from the navigation to the first `tr.entity-row` plus two animation frames.

| | Chromium cold | Chromium warm | WebKit cold | WebKit warm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First paint of rows | 335 ms | 115 ms | 371 ms | 155 ms |
| Longest main-thread task | none over 50 ms | none over 50 ms | none (largest frame gap 84 ms) | none (largest frame gap 92 ms) |
| Query payload | 235,130 bytes | 235,130 bytes | 235,130 bytes | 235,130 bytes |
| `<tr>` in the grid | 39 | 39 | 39 | 39 |
| DOM nodes | 2,286 | 2,286 | 2,286 | 2,286 |

Against the v0.4.17 figures: the payload fell from 10,224,700 bytes to 235,130 (the open asks for one page of 200, the four visible fields, and relations as chips), the 16,692 ms task is gone, and the grid holds 39 rows and 2,286 nodes instead of 2,062 and 58,706. No trash request runs on open. For reference, an unbounded `POST /query {}` on the same table now returns 13,642,882 bytes, so the saving comes from the client asking for less, as planned.

Scrolling the whole table (30 wheel steps of 3,000 px to the bottom, pages fetched on the way) produced one 74 ms long task in Chromium and none in WebKit, with the grid staying at 35 rows and about 2,230 nodes.

WebKit exposes no Long Tasks API, so its row reports the largest gap between animation frames instead.

## Fixed by the three children
- #270, trash list loaded on demand: a624eed, v0.4.21.
- #271, windowed rows and paged data: f211afd, v0.4.19.
- #272, requested fields and chip-level relations: 483514a, v0.4.45.

Status set to Fixed, Fixed in v0.4.45 (the last of the three to ship).

issues.name: Slow: every cell commit refetches the whole table and rebuilds the grid
issues.description:
## Measured
One Name commit on the Issue table (Tab out of the inline editor) fires, in order:
```
PATCH /api/entities/<id>
GET   /api/entities/<id>
POST  /api/tables/<Issue>/query     ← the whole table again
POST  /api/markdown
```
`public/app.js:3210-3218` (`onSaved`) refetches the full table and `drawDatabase` opens with `main.replaceChildren()` (`app.js:3116`). `rememberGridFocus`/`restoreGridFocus` exist only because the node the user was in is destroyed. The same pattern is in `relatedGrid` (`app.js:8171`) and the registry grids (`app.js:6310`, `app.js:8527`).

On the Case table this means every commit costs the 17–52 s freeze from the Case-table issue. On a 30-row table it is a visible flash and a lost scroll position.

## What good looks like
Notion, Airtable and Linear patch the one cell in place from the PATCH response, and only re-sort/re-filter if the edited field is in the active sort or filter.

## Fix shape
`onSaved` takes the PATCH response (it already contains the fresh row), replaces that row's cells, and re-runs sort/filter locally. Fall back to a refetch only when the edited field is a formula/rollup dependency.

---
Filed by the 2026-09-12 CX/UX audit (Claude session, weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a, measured against :4400 in Chromium 1440×900 unless stated).
## Refined fix shape (Kyle, 2026-09-12: "limit the fire to just the impacted data, not the full table query")

Yes. The server already knows the blast radius: every mutation records the entity ids it touched in `#dirty` (`src/engine.js:705`, `:1059`), and computed fields (formula / lookup / rollup) recompute on read (`src/engine.js:4234`), so nothing else in the table is stale after a PATCH except rows whose lookups or rollups reach the edited row through a relation.

1. **PATCH returns the impacted set.** `PATCH /api/entities/:id` responds with `{ entity, affected: [ids] }` where `affected` = the ids marked dirty by this save ∪ rows in the same table linked to the edited row by an inverse relation (they may show it through a lookup/rollup). Same-row-only edits (text, number, select, date) yield `affected: [id]`.
2. **Client patches in place.** `onSaved` (`public/app.js:3210`) takes `affected`, re-reads only those rows (`POST /tables/:id/query` with `where: [["id","in",affected]]`, or the PATCH body when it is just the one row) and swaps their `<tr>` cells. No `replaceChildren()`, no `rememberGridFocus`/`restoreGridFocus` dance, scroll stays put.
3. **Sort/filter membership is the one client-side check.** If the edited field is in the active sort or filter, re-sort/re-filter the already-loaded rows locally; the row moves or drops without a network call. Only a registry table (`db.system`, Issue #241) still reloads the schema.
4. **Full refetch survives as the fallback** for the cases the client cannot reason about: a formula on the *same* table that references another table's aggregate, or a server response without `affected` (old server).

Test shape: a Name edit on a 2,000-row table issues exactly one PATCH and one row read, the row count of `<tr>` is unchanged, `document.activeElement` is still the edited cell's neighbour after Tab, and `scrollTop` is unchanged. A Suite-name edit re-reads the linked Case rows and nothing else.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-16T07:04:25.619Z · started · session 9ad4b992

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-16T07:48:17.068847Z · FIXED · session 9ad4b992 · merged d250748 · Verified +1 (review-logs/354-1)

**What landed.** The server says what a write touched: `PATCH /api/entities/:ref` now answers with the fresh row plus `affected` — the ids this write marked dirty (`Weave#touching` collects them alongside `#dirty`, which every save clears) union the rows the edited one is linked to, since a lookup or rollup there shows its value and recomputes on read. The body is still `readEntity`, so an older client and the CLI/MCP paths read it exactly as before.

The grid swaps those rows' cells where they stand. `renderTable` grows `wvPatchRows`: the rows of `affected` this grid is holding are re-read in ONE query (`["id","in",[…]]`), and each row's `<tr>` and `<td>`s are KEPT — only the cells whose value moved are redrawn. Since the cell is the focus stop (Feature #134), a cell that is not repainted cannot lose focus, so scroll, selection, range and any open editor are never touched. The `GET /api/entities/:id` after the PATCH is gone.

The full re-read survives as the fallback for what the client cannot reason about: a registry row (Issue #241), an edit to the column the table is sorted by or filtered on (the row moves or leaves), a bulk write or an undo, and any response without `affected` — a state change, a link, an older server.

**Measured on :4400 after the deploy**, Development/Issue (277 rows), Chromium 1440×900, one Name commit with Tab:

```
before:  PATCH /api/entities/<id>
         GET   /api/entities/<id>
         POST  /api/tables/<Issue>/query      <- the whole table
         POST  /api/markdown
after:   PATCH /w/weave/api/entities/<id>     <- and nothing else, 334 ms
```

Rows drawn 47 → 47, `scrollTop` unchanged, focus on the Description cell of the same row, the value shown. The row was restored to its original name afterwards.

**Tests.** `test/cell-commit-patch.test.mjs` pins the server contract (a same-row edit on an unlinked row names one row; a linked row names its far side; a name edit names the rows whose lookups reach it and nothing else; a relation edit names both sides; the read is one `["id","in"]` query returning recomputed lookups). `test/cell-commit-patch-browser.test.mjs` pins the DOM half (one PATCH and zero table queries well down a 500-row table, row count and `scrollTop` unchanged, focus where Tab put it, a lookup row repainted from one read whose where-clause names exactly the two rows, the sorted-column fallback still firing, a sort after a commit still showing the committed value). Nine cases in `grid-keymap-browser`, `grid-tab-focus-browser` and `toggle-browser` waited on "the marked `<tbody>` has been replaced", which no longer happens on every path; they now wait on the write coming back, registered before the gesture. Gate: 2306 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, browser suites ran.

**Found on the way, filed separately:** Issue #291 — clicking a cell in a side-scrolling grid jumps the table back to the top. Reproduced on the LANDED v0.4.21 before this change, so it is older and independent.

Scope held: Issue #256 (virtualization) and #269 (resize debounce / filter chips) were not touched.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-16T07:48:17.068Z · fixed · Gerrit 354 → d250748

**Tests added:**
- test/cell-commit-patch.test.mjs: PATCH /api/entities/:ref returns { entity, affected } and affected covers dirty ids plus linked rows
- test/cell-commit-patch-browser.test.mjs: a Name commit keeps the <tr> and repaints only changed cells; no table re-query

**Live verification:** Gerrit 354 MERGED (submitted 07:44:55Z); GET /api/health sha d250748 startedAt 2026-09-16T07:46:29Z; repro re-run on :4400 (Development/Issue, 277 rows, 1440x900): one PATCH and nothing else, 334 ms, rows drawn 47->47, scrollTop unchanged, focus on the next cell. Evidence attached to this Issue.

(The line above restates the same outcome in the parsable format; the uppercase FIXED line the worker wrote does not match the routine parser.)

issues.name: Slow: no gzip or ETag, 23 render-blocking scripts, 2.1 MB cold load, schema fetched 2–3× per route
issues.description:
## Measured
- Cold load of `/`: **44 resources, 2,097,790 bytes** over the wire. `tabler.min.css` 524 KB, `app.js` 475 KB, Vditor `index.min.js` 296 KB, `style.css` 157 KB, `lucide-moving.js` 64 KB.
- `curl -sI -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, br' /app.js` → no `Content-Encoding`, no `ETag`, `Cache-Control: no-cache` (`src/server.js:269`). The only compression in `src/` is the PDF deflate.
- `public/index.html:51-74`: 23 classic `<script>` tags, zero `defer`/`async`.
- `/api/schema` (96 KB) was requested **twice on boot and three times** when opening the Case table; `loadSchema` is a serial chain (`app.js:574`, `:582`, `:586`) before routing starts.

On localhost this is 88 ms. On the planned Cloudflare-hosted instance (Feature #84) or any remote/mobile use it is the difference between a 1 s and a 6 s open.

## Fix shape
1. gzip/brotli static and JSON responses (`zlib.createGzip`, or precompress at build).
2. Content-hashed asset URLs with `Cache-Control: immutable`; keep `no-cache` only on `index.html`.
3. `defer` every script; concatenate the 20 `*-core.js` modules.
4. Cache the schema in memory for the route; fetch `/schema`, `/workspace`, `/workspaces` concurrently.

---
Filed by the 2026-09-12 CX/UX audit (Claude session, weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a, measured against :4400 in Chromium 1440×900 unless stated).



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-18T07:03:29.250Z · started · session wf-0918-0002

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-18T07:22:26.626Z · fixed · Gerrit 366 → e020da6

**Tests added:**
- test/compression.test.mjs (new, 7 cases): app.js gzipped and byte-identical once inflated; identity without Accept-Encoding and on q=0; /api/schema gzipped with route headers intact; PNG and tiny answers left alone; weak ETag + If-None-Match 304 in both encodings; the Accept-Encoding parser; the gzip cache keyed by path
- test/schema-fetch-browser.test.mjs (new, 3 cases): one schema read on boot with the relation map drawn; none on a space page or #/map; a member workspace's schema, root registry and /workspace in flight together
- test/fetch-failures-browser.test.mjs: the registry case follows the read into readRegistry()

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha e020da6 startedAt 2026-09-18T07:21:02Z (submit 07:19:13Z). Repro on :4400: app.js 533,704 B identity → 170,981 B with Accept-Encoding: gzip (Content-Encoding: gzip, Vary: Accept-Encoding, ETag W/"…", If-None-Match → 304); /api/schema 98,125 → 19,236; tabler.min.css 536,141 → 68,867; style.css 164,576 → 42,096. Cold load of / in Chromium 2,187,417 B / 46 resources (before, same data) → 506,860 B / 45. /api/schema reads: cold / 2 → 1, space page 1 → 0, #/map 1 → 0, opening the Case table 0 → 0; uno cold load 3 → 2 (its own + the root registry). Both themes screenshotted, no page errors.

**Scope:** fix-shape items 1 (gzip + ETag) and 4 (schema read once, boot reads concurrent) shipped here. Items 2 (content-hashed asset URLs, immutable caching) and 3 (defer every script, concatenate the *-core.js modules) change the asset pipeline and load order; they are split into [[Issue#313]] (Development/Issue #313).

issues.name: Wrong data: trashing rows from the selection bar has no confirmation and the toast has no Undo; ⌘Z is unbound
issues.description:
## Reproduced
1. Tick a row in the Issue table. The floating bar appears (`1 bug · ✎ · ⇄ · ⧉ · ⋯ · 🗑`).
2. Click 🗑. The row is gone immediately and the toast reads **"Moved to trash 1 bug"** with no Undo button. Focus drops to `<body>`.
3. Press ⌘Z. Nothing. `grep "key === 'z'"` across `public/*.js` finds no binding, although `POST /api/undo` works (`src/routes.js:446`).

The audit trashed Issue #65 this way by accident and restored it through the API.

Three competing destructive patterns exist side by side: hold-to-confirm (`app.js:1348`, tables/fields/spaces), instant-with-undo-toast (row delete from the context menu, `app.js:7621`), and type-the-name modal (workspace, `app.js:9007`). The selection-bar path is a fourth: instant, no undo.

## What good looks like
