## Observed
In the Issue grid every workflow and select value is the same flat grey pill: `Open` / `In Progress` / `Fixed` and `Low` / `Medium` / `High` are visually identical. The eye cannot scan the table for what needs attention. The filter strip above the grid has the same problem: "Open" and "In Progress" are both active but drawn in two different active styles.

## What good looks like
Linear, Notion and Fibery give workflow categories a fixed semantic colour (not-started = grey, in-progress = blue, done = green) and let selects carry a per-option colour. Colour is separate from the accent and works in both themes.

## Fix shape
Derive a chip tint from `workflow.category` by default, add an optional colour per select option in the field dialog, and use one active style in the filter strip.

---
Filed by the 2026-09-12 CX/UX audit (Claude session, weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a, measured against :4400 in Chromium 1440×900 unless stated).
## Correction (2026-09-12, after Kyle asked "don't we have a chip colouring option built in?")

We do. The finding above overstated it.

- **Select / multiselect options already carry a hue** from the ten-hue ramp (`src/engine.js:186`, `public/chip-core.js`), set per option in the field dialog (`app.js:5133`). On this table every Severity and Symptom option is stored as `hue: "slate"`, the default, which is why Low / Medium / High all read grey. That is table configuration, not a missing feature.
- **Workflow states are tinted by category** (`chip-core.js:47-49`: not-started → slate, in-progress → blue, done → green; `app.js:1066`). "Open" is grey by design because it is not-started; the filtered view hid the blue In Progress and green Fixed chips.
- **The filter strip is consistent**: `.filter-chip.cat-<category>.on` (`app.js:3078`) tints an active chip by its state's category, so Open (outlined) and In Progress (filled blue) differ because their categories differ.

What remains of #264, if anything: the *default* hue for a new select option is slate, so a fresh table reads monochrome until someone opts in. Peer tools auto-assign a distinct hue per option on creation. That is a defaults question for Kyle, not a defect; otherwise close this row.

issues.name: Slow: grids draw every row; window the rows with a look-ahead buffer and page the data
issues.description:
## Measured
The Case table renders all 2,062 rows on open (`public/app.js:3643` loops `sorted` with no cap; no `limit` is sent, `app.js:3104`). That produces 58,706 DOM nodes and a single 16.7–52.2 s main-thread task. The API already accepts `limit`/`offset` (`src/engine.js:4711`, `src/routes.js:631`).

## Fix shape
1. The grid requests `{ limit: 300, offset: 0 }` and draws those rows.
2. A **Show more** row at the bottom (where "+ New record" sits) loads the next 300 and appends them; the footer reads "300 of 2,062".
3. Sort and filter stay server-side so page 1 is the right 300; the Σ rollup footer keeps reading the Space rollups, not the page.
4. Selection (⌘A) selects the loaded rows and says so; a "select all 2,062" affordance can come later.

## Verify
Case table opens with 300 `<tr>`, long task under 1 s; Show more appends 300 more without re-drawing the first page; the cell-commit path (#257) patches in place and never resets the page count.

---
Split out of #256 on 2026-09-12 at Kyle's direction (weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a).

## Node composition (measured 2026-09-12, Case table, 1440×900)
- 59,312 nodes total: 58,346 inside the 2,087 rows (98%), 966 in chrome. Only 15 rows are on screen.
- One row = 28 nodes: select cell 3, # cell 2, Name 2, Description 3, Status 2, **Suite relation chip 15** (button ×3, span ×8, a, input). Tag totals: span 27,057 · td 12,517 · button 6,251 · a 4,164 · input 4,158 · label 2,086.
- The chip carries its hover controls as real buttons in every row at rest; lightening it (Feature #185, chip anatomy round 2) would take a row from 28 to ~17 nodes. Windowing the rows is the bigger lever: 300 rows ≈ 8,400 nodes, true virtualization ≈ 1,400.

## Decision (2026-09-12, Kyle): windowed render with a look-ahead buffer, not a 300-row preview
Render only the rows in view plus a buffer, and keep the buffer ahead of the scroll direction so the next rows are already drawn before they scroll in.

**Render window.** Rows [firstVisible − B, lastVisible + B·k] are real `<tr>`s; everything else is two spacer rows whose heights are rowHeight × count, so the native scrollbar and scroll position stay honest. B = one viewport of rows (min 20); k = 2 in the direction of travel, 1 behind. Row height is measured from the first painted row per density (Comfortable/Compact). Re-window on scroll via requestAnimationFrame; never on every scroll event.

**Data pages.** Fetch `{ limit: 200, offset }` (already supported by the API) in sort/filter order; prefetch the next page when the window's leading edge is within one page of the loaded end. Total comes from the first response so the spacer math and the "N of total" footer are right from the first paint.

**Keeps working.** Selection ranges and ⌘A (over loaded rows, footer says so), grid keymap (moving focus into an unrendered row scrolls it into the window first), rememberGridFocus/restoreGridFocus, "+ New record" row, Σ footer (space rollups, unchanged), column resize, deep link `?e=` opening the tray, the cell-commit path (#257 must re-window at the same scroll position, never reset to top).

**Tests.** Pure window math in its own module (`public/grid-window.js`: scrollTop, viewportH, rowH, total, buffer, direction → {start, end, topPad, bottomPad, prefetchOffset}) under node --test; a browser case on the Case table: < 200 `<tr>` after open, longest task < 1 s, scroll to the end renders the last row, End key in the grid lands on the last row.

Pass criteria: Case table (2,087 rows) opens with fewer than 200 rows in the DOM and no long task over 1 s; scrolling at speed never shows a blank band.

## Fixed (2026-09-12)
Landed as Gerrit change 342, commit f211afd on main ("Grids window their rows and page their data (Issue #271)"), deployed to :4400 at 21:07:59 PDT.

**Measured on :4400, Case table, Chromium 1440×900, same script before and after** (`<tr>` count, DOM nodes, longest `longtask`, time to first row):

| | Before (b6170d9) | After (f211afd) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rows drawn | 2,185 `<tr>` | 40 `<tr>` |
| DOM nodes | 62,094 | 2,090 |
| Longest task | 38,369 ms (3 long tasks) | none over 50 ms |
| Open to first row | 40.7 s | 1.7 s |
| Foot | — | "200 of 2,207 loaded" |

**What landed.** `public/grid-window.js` is the pure window: one viewport of rows (min 20) as the buffer, doubled ahead of the scroll direction, single behind; two spacer rows carry the rest at row height so the scrollbar and scroll position stay honest; `pagesFor`/`scrollTopFor` beside it. `renderTable` draws only the window, builds each row once per draw and keeps it, re-windows once per frame on scroll (rAF), measures against whichever box scrolls (wrap or page), and remembers the measured row height per table and density for a redraw's first paint. `showDatabase` asks for the first 200 in the table's own sort (server-side); `gridPager` holds the table as one sparse array, fetches the pages under the window plus the one past its leading edge, and a placeholder row holds the place until a page lands. Selection/⌘A/header box work over the loaded rows; the keymap counts the whole table and scrolls a row in before the cursor lands (End/Home added); + New scrolls the new row into the window; the cell-commit path re-reads the pages under the window and redraws at the same scroll (keepScroll now restores instantly — Tabler's smooth `:root` animated the restore and the first repaint cancelled it — and resolves after its restore). Handbook: a "big table" section and the two keys.

**Tests.** `test/grid-window.test.mjs` (13 unit cases) and `test/grid-window-browser.test.mjs` (9 cases on a 1,200-row Case-shaped table: < 200 `<tr>`, no long task over 1 s, no blank band after a fast scroll, last row by scroll and by End, ⌘A over loaded rows, mid-table commit holds scroll and focus, + New scrolls the new row in, short table drawn whole, page vs wrap scroller). Gate: 2,264 tests, 0 skipped, Verified +1; the browser suite needed the runner's one retry in the gate's first run (the case is not named in the gate log) — watch for a repeat.

**Left out, on purpose.** Patching the one cell in place instead of re-reading the window's pages is Issue #257. `total` drifting between two page reads (a row created or trashed by someone else) shifts positions until the next refresh and is not reconciled. The eye's "show deleted" still fetches the whole table (still windowed). A row that leaves the window while its editor is open is removed, and that blur is its commit.

Filed by the Claude session that landed change 342 (weave v0.4.18 @ f211afd).

issues.name: Slow: table queries return every field and every related row in full; let the client ask for specific fields and chip-level relations
issues.description:
## Measured
`POST /api/tables/Case/query {}` returns **10,224,700 bytes** for 2,060 rows. Composition:
- `Suite` relation: **4,656 KB** (each row embeds the full summary of its related Suite row, so the same ~40 suites are serialised ~2,000 times)
- `Chip` + `Card` view fields: 392 KB
- `Name`: 126 KB, `Status`: 18 KB, `Description`: 4 KB
- plus `raw`, `doc`, `docs`, `comments`, `activity`, `files`, `createdBy`, `modifiedBy` on every row

`readEntity` (`src/engine.js:4645-4655`) resolves every field and, for relations, `resolved.map((rid) => this.#summary(rid))`. The grid only needs what its visible columns show.

## Fix shape
1. Query body accepts `select: ["Name","Status","Suite"]` (default: the table's visible columns); unlisted fields are omitted.
2. Relations in list context return a chip: `{ id, publicId, name, icon }`. The full summary stays available on `GET /api/entities/<id>` and in the entity view.
3. `doc`, `comments`, `activity`, `files` are omitted from list responses unless selected.
4. Same `select` on the CLI and MCP query verbs so agents can ask narrow questions (`weave query Case --select Name,Status`).

## Verify
Case query with the default select under 500 KB; with `select:["Name"]` under 150 KB. The grid, chips and Σ footer render identically. `test/agent-surface` gate updated for the new query option.

issues.name: Wrong data: an open tab keeps a stale schema after a field-config change made elsewhere until a hard reload
issues.description:
## Reproduced (2026-09-12, Issue table, Severity field)
1. Tab A open on the Issue grid.
2. `PATCH /api/tables/Issue/fields/<Severity>` sets Medium → amber, High → red. `GET /api/schema` returns the new hues immediately.
3. In Tab A, navigate between tables (hash routing, no reload): Severity chips still render `hue-slate`. `state.schema` was loaded once at boot (`public/app.js:9415` `loadSchema().then(renderRoute)`) and is only refreshed on the tab's own structural edits (`loadSchema()` after a system-row save, `app.js:3214`).
4. `location.reload()` → chips render amber/red.

The same staleness applies to any schema change made by the CLI, the MCP surface, an automation, or a second browser tab: renamed fields, new options, new tables, changed workflows. Data rows refetch on every navigation, so the grid can show fresh values against a stale field definition (an option name the tab has never heard of renders as an uncoloured chip; a renamed field keeps its old header).

## What good looks like
Notion, Fibery and Airtable push schema changes to open tabs (websocket) or at minimum re-validate the schema on each route change with an ETag/version so the round-trip is a 304 when nothing moved.

## Fix shape
1. The server already tracks `PRAGMA data_version` per request (`src/store.js:285-291`); expose a cheap `schemaVersion` (bumped on any structural write) on `GET /api/workspace` and in every query response header.
2. `route()` compares the version it last loaded against the one that came back with the row query; on mismatch it reloads the schema before drawing. Zero extra round-trips in the common case.
3. Later: an SSE/websocket `schema-changed` event so an open tab redraws without navigating (pairs with Feature #174 table activity).

---
Filed 2026-09-12 from the CX/UX audit follow-up (weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a) while setting the Severity hues that closed #264.

issues.name: Slash-menu wheel test flakes on its own (fails 2 of 3 runs alone on main)
issues.description:
`test/slash-commands.test.mjs` — "a wheel over the slash menu never scrolls the page out from under it" (the Issue #137 case) fails on its own, not only under the full suite: on an untouched `gerrit/main` at f21c671, `node --test test/slash-commands.test.mjs` alone went fail / fail / pass over three runs; on the phase-2 passkey worktree (change 334, no editor changes) fail / pass / pass. The runner's retry-once (Issue #44) covers a single miss, and change 334's gate lost both runs (Verified −1 on patchset 2, log `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/334-2.log`), so the flake now costs a re-gate on unrelated changes.

Not a fixture-starvation case: the file is alone. The assertion at `test/slash-commands.test.mjs:418` waits on the menu after a wheel; the likely shape is a wheel dispatched before Vditor's menu has its `max-height`/`overscroll-behavior` applied, or `waitForTimeout(100)` racing the menu paint. Fix shape: wait on the menu's computed style or a scroll event on the menu itself before wheeling, and assert the page's `scrollY` after a settled frame.

Filed from the Feature #222 phase 2 landing (2026-09-12).

issues.name: Wrong data: opening a relation replaces the left panel with the other table, cutting the breadcrumb trail
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-09-12 on :4400 (v0.4.17, f21c671): "opening a weave relation today opens the paneled entity as expected but also redirects the left panel to a new table, this should not be the case, this is discontinuous breadcrumbs."

**Symptom.** From table A with a row docked, click a relation chip pointing at a row in table B. The dock opens the B row (good), but the left panel is torn down and replaced with table B, and a `#/table/B` history entry is pushed. The reader loses the place they were reading, the grid they had filtered, and the breadcrumb no longer reads as a path taken: it restarts at B instead of continuing A › row › B row.

**Reproduced in code, not only by eye.** `public/app.js` `openEntity()` (line ~200):

```
if (!(state.route?.page === 'db' && state.route.dbId === db.id)) {
  teardownDocEditors();
  dockClose();
  history.pushState(null, '', `#/table/${db.id}`);
  await withPageLoader(() => showDatabase(db.id));
}
await dockEntity(db, id);
```

The guard compares the entity's table to the page's table and, on any mismatch, navigates the page. The comment above it records the earlier reading of the 2026-09-02 ruling ("a reader elsewhere travels to the entity's table first"). Kyle has now overruled that reading for relation hops: the dock is presentation and follows the click; the page is the reader's place and stays put. `dockEntity(db, id)` compounds it: `dock.db.id === db.id ? S.open(dock.state, frame) : S.open(S.init(...), frame)` re-initialises the chain on any cross-table hop, so the dock's own trail is also cut.

**What good looks like.** Fibery: clicking a relation in the open entity panel pushes the related entity onto the same panel, with a back arrow and a crumb trail inside the panel; the underlying view never changes. Notion: a linked page opens in the side peek over whatever the reader was on. In weave's own terms this is `public/breadcrumbs.js` `pushTrail`: "arriving at an entity by a relation link from another entity keeps that entity (and its table, where it differs) in the crumb, so a hop People › Ada Chen › Field Types › Sensor board reads as one path."

**Fix shape.**
- `openEntity`: only navigate the page when there is no table page under the reader at all (home, space, activity, ⌘K from a non-table page). When `state.route.page === 'db'`, dock the entity beside the CURRENT table whatever its own table is. Do not push history.
- `dockEntity`: stop keying the chain on `dock.db.id`; the frame already carries `tableId`/`tableName`, so a cross-table frame extends the existing chain. `drawDock` renders fields from the frame's table, not the dock's.
- Dock crumbs: run the chain through `entityCrumbs` so a cross-table hop shows the table crumb where it changes (the existing rule), and the dock's back arrow walks the chain.
- `dockSyncUrl`: `?e=<id>` on the current table hash still works for a foreign row; `redock` on reload must fetch the row's own table for rendering rather than assuming the page table.
- The expand arrow (`dockExpand`) still lands on `#/entity/<id>`; that is the one place the page legitimately changes.
- Leave the "entity lives in no table" fallback (`if (!db)`) as is.

**Verify.** `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs` (Playwright): from table A with row a1 docked, click a relation chip to b1 in table B → `#main` still shows table A's grid, hash is `#/table/A?e=b1`, `history.length` unchanged, dock shows b1 with crumbs A › a1 › B › b1 and a working back arrow to a1; reload re-docks b1 beside table A; expand goes to `#/entity/b1`. Unit: `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` for the chain→crumb mapping. Update `entity-dock-default-browser` expectations where they assert the old table switch. Handbook entity-view page: state that the dock follows the click and the page stays.

**Execution rule.** Fix lands only through a background agent in an isolated worktree, through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`), with tests. Supersedes the "travels to the entity's table first" reading recorded on Issue #198.

Filed by the harness session (worktree weave-relation-panel-redirect-a41503), 2026-09-12, against weave v0.4.17 at f21c671.

## Fixed 2026-09-12 in 1fd9975 (Gerrit change 338, merged as 89820bc)

🌙 attempt 1 · 2026-09-12T16:35Z · fixed · Gerrit 338 → 1fd9975 (merge 89820bc)

**What changed.** `openEntity` docks beside the table under the reader whatever table the row lives in, pushes no history, and travels only when there is no table page at all (home, a space, activity, ⌘K from there). `dockEntity` keys the pane on its anchor (the table beside the dock), not the entity's table; a hop from inside the dock drills the chain and a frame already on the chain cuts back to it. The dock's crumb is the chain run through `weaveBreadcrumbs.dockCrumbs` (the `entityCrumbs` rule minus the workspace › space head), so the table crumb appears where it changes — `Release › v0.4.4 › Issue › #122` — and a back arrow (or Esc) walks it one frame. `redock` renders a foreign `?e=<id>` row from its own table on reload. Expand still lands on `#/entity/<id>`; the `if (!db)` fallback is untouched. Handbook grid guide updated; CHANGELOG Unreleased bullet in the same commit.

**Tests added:**
- `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs`: a relation hop from the dock keeps the table under it and pushes no history; the dock crumb reads as one path across the tables and the back arrow walks it; a reload re-docks the foreign row beside the same table; expanding a foreign docked row lands on its own `#/entity` page
- `test/entity-dock-default-browser.test.mjs`: expectations moved to the page-stays rule (both themes); a ⌘K hit from a page with no table under it still travels
- `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs`: `dockCrumbs` chain → crumb mapping
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`: the new `dockEntity` / `openEntity` shape

**Gate.** Local `npm test`: 2157 tests, pass 2156 + 1 retried green (entity-block-grip-browser, unrelated flake), fail 0, skipped 0. Gerrit Verified +1 on ps2 (row-selection-browser retried green), Code-Review +2 self-review, submitted MERGED.

**Live verification** on :4400 at 89820bc (process started 2026-09-12T16:37:07Z, after the 16:35Z submit): from `Development/Release` with v0.4.4 docked, clicking the `Fixes` chip to Issue #122 kept the Release grid in `#main`, hash `#/table/<Release>?e=<#122>`, history.length unchanged, dock crumb `Release › v0.4.4 › Issue`, back arrow present, root row still lit; back returned to v0.4.4 with crumb `Release`; a reload re-docked. Screenshot attached (`live276-hop.png`).

No version bump and no Release row: a landing needs neither (DEVELOPMENT.md, Releasing); `Fixed in` fills when the next release is cut.

Fixed by the harness session (worktree weave-relation-panel-redirect-a41503 → scratchpad worktree issue-276), 2026-09-12.

issues.name: Phase 2 landed Finder duplicates of three test files (" 2.mjs"), so those suites run twice per gate
issues.description:
## Pain Point

Commit 309d0ca (passkeys, Feature #222 part 2) added `test/auth-passkey-browser.test 2.mjs`, `test/auth-session.test 2.mjs`, `test/webauthn.test 2.mjs` and `test/lib/authenticator 2.mjs` beside the real files — the ` 2` suffix is what Finder/iCloud appends to a duplicate. `scripts/test.mjs` walks every `*.test.mjs`, so the passkey browser suite and the session suite now run twice per `npm test` and per Gerrit gate, doubling their Chromium load; the two copies also import `../lib/authenticator.mjs` vs the ` 2` copy inconsistently as the files drift.

## Reproduce

```bash
git ls-files test | grep ' 2\.mjs'
```

## Fix

Delete the four ` 2.mjs` files (diff them against the originals first — keep whichever is newer if they differ) and add `* 2.*` to `.gitignore` so a Finder duplicate can never be committed again. Found while gating change 335 (backup, Feature #222 phase 3).



🌙 overnight-fixer · 2026-09-14T10:05:00Z · record correction · already fixed by Gerrit commit 2155cf3 on 2026-09-12

**Not a new ship.** This Issue was already resolved in main before tonight; only the row was stale.

- Commit `2155cf3` — "Remove Finder duplicate files and guard against them (Issue #277)" — deleted all six `* 2.*` copies (src/auth-page 2.js, src/webauthn 2.js, test/auth-passkey-browser.test 2.mjs, test/auth-session.test 2.mjs, test/lib/authenticator 2.mjs, test/webauthn.test 2.mjs).
- The guard shipped as a test, not a .gitignore rule: `test/no-finder-duplicates.test.mjs` fails the suite if any tracked path matches `/ \d+\.[a-z]+$/`.
- Verified against the SHA :4400 serves (6ccb90b, which carries 2155cf3): `git ls-tree -r --name-only gerrit/main test | grep ' 2'` returns nothing.

Status moved to Fixed by the overnight fixer, 2026-09-14.

issues.name: Wrong data: date and number columns sort by their display string, so Sep 9 rows sit above Sep 12
issues.description:
**Reproduced** on uno `Agent/Sessions` (720 rows, table sort = Created desc, Created is a `date` field with format `long`). The grid shows #559 "weave multi-cell selection and fill" (Sep 9, 2026 9:51 AM) at the top, above rows created Sep 12 (e.g. "session-log — 07:30 fire", raw Created 2026-09-12T07:32:33). Every Sep 12 row sits below every Sep 9 row, so the table reads as "not updated" even though the hourly writer landed rows at 07:34 today.

**Cause** — `public/app.js:3695-3698` (b6170d9): the draw comparator reads `a.fields[sortKey]`, which is the *formatted display string* ("Sep 9, 2026 9:51 AM"), and falls to `String(fieldValueCell(av)).localeCompare(...)` for anything non-numeric. "Sep 9" > "Sep 12" lexically. The same defect hits any date format, and any number field the server formats into a string (Active (min) arrives as "18 min", Cache Read as "15,829,984", Cost as "$17.25" — all string-compared).

**Good looks like** — Airtable/Fibery/Notion sort a date column by its instant regardless of display format; the display string never enters the comparator.

**Fix shape** — sort on `item.raw[sortKey]` (ISO for dates, numbers for numbers); fall back to the display string only for text/select types. One test: a table with rows created Sep 9 and Sep 12, date format long, sort desc → Sep 12 first. Related, not the same: #254 (system fields cannot sort), #217 (created date cut off).

Filed by the harness diagnose session, 2026-09-12 14:05 PDT, weave b6170d9 (~/.weave-serve).

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-20T20:37:10.242Z · started · session wf-0920-1331



---

## Fixed 2026-09-20 — change 370, merged 41a941c

**What landed.** Every activity entry now carries `seq`, a monotonic counter over the workspace kept on `meta.activitySeq` and minted at the single stamping site (`#logActivity`). `seq` is the order and `ts` is the display: `activityFeed`, `GET /api/activity`, `GET /api/activity/<id>`, `weave_activity` and `weave activity` all sort on seq descending, and the Activity table still shows the localised time with the ISO on hover. The two sites that pushed straight onto `e.activity` — `deleted` in `deleteEntity` and `restored` in `restoreEntity` — go through `#logActivity` now, which is what gives them a seq, plus an actor they never had and the ACTIVITY_CAP trim they skipped. A folded document session keeps the seq it started with, since it is one event.

**The tie-break it replaced was wrong twice.** `rows.sort((x, y) => (x.ts === y.ts ? y.id.localeCompare(x.id) : ...))` ranked same-millisecond events across entities by entity uuid, which is arbitrary, and within one entity it compared the index as a string, so `:9` read as newer than `:10`.

**Measured on the live weave workspace.** The backfill numbered 10,531 stored entries. 6,681 of them share a timestamp with another entry, in 2,926 groups. Exactly two rows changed position, and they are the pair the bug predicts: the Documents record (`4a4c66df-f67c-4443-8b71-0eb846128ede`) rendered its feed as `12, 11, 9, 10, 8, …` before and `12, 11, 10, 9, 8, …` after. Screenshots attached: `documents-feed-before-4400-light.png` (the old order on :4400), `documents-feed-merged-4400-light.png` and `documents-feed-merged-4400-dark.png` (the merged code on :4400, both themes).

**Backfill.** A workspace written before `seq` existed is numbered once on open, oldest first, with each entity's stored order preserved: the key each entity's stream sorts on only ever rises, so a clock that stepped backwards in old data cannot lift an entry above the one it was appended after. The counter's own presence is the one-time flag. `activitySeq` is excluded from the schema fingerprint for the same reason `publicIdCounter` is — a row write must not cost every open tab a schema refetch (Issue #274).

**Tests.** `test/activity-seq.test.mjs` (9 cases: the counter and its uniqueness, the feed's order against adversarial uuids, `:10` over `:9`, a clock stepping backwards, deleted/restored stamping, the fold keeping its seq, the one-time backfill and its idempotence, the schema fingerprint, and route/MCP/CLI parity including durability across a `.db` reopen) and `test/activity-seq-browser.test.mjs` (the Activity table reads newest-first in both themes). Full suite 2367 tests, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Gerrit change 370 Verified +1, self-reviewed +2, submitted; `:4400` serves 41a941c, started 21:00:06Z after the submit.

**Docs.** `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` and the `ONTOLOGY` registry in `src/engine.js` say what an entry carries; Handbook Guide #6 (Ontology: entity types and field types) updated to match.

### Follow-up the same night — change 371, merged 40c386e

The first change gated the numbering pass on `meta.activitySeq == null`, which made it one-time. Weave lets a CLI and a second server share one `.db`, so a process still on pre-seq code can append an unnumbered entry to a workspace whose counter is already set, and no later pass would come back for it. That happened within the hour: the main watcher filed Issue #329 at 21:00:06.178Z from a checkout it had not yet ff-pulled, leaving row `9edcd04a-3927-4c6e-ac46-9b8f1b74e2b4:0` unnumbered — one row out of 10,570, and enough to make the feed's comparator return NaN.

Every open now numbers whatever it finds unnumbered, continuing from the counter and never moving a number already handed out, so the legacy workspace and the single straggler are one case. The comparator is total as well: an entry with no number sorts highest, which is what it is, and a running server holds that window until its next open.

Verified on the live workspace after the restart: 10,577 entries, 0 missing a seq, all unique and strictly descending, seq 1 to 10,577, and the straggler repaired to seq 10570. Two more tests in `test/activity-seq.test.mjs` (the repair on open, and the feed order while the hole is still there). issues.name: Wrong data: a daterange column sorts by its painted range, so Oct 1 sits above Sep 9
issues.description:
**Sibling of #279, deliberately left out of its fix.** #279 made sorting undress the two types whose painted form does not order the way the value does: a number stays a number, a date stays its stored instant. `daterange` was left on its display string, and has the identical defect.

**Reproduced** (engine, no UI needed) on weave at f211afd:

```js
const t = w.createTable({ space: 'S', name: 'T' });
w.addField(t, { name: 'Win', type: 'daterange', config: { format: 'long' } });
w.createEntity(t, { name: 'sep', values: { Win: { start: '2026-09-09', end: '2026-09-12' } } });
w.createEntity(t, { name: 'oct', values: { Win: { start: '2026-10-01', end: '2026-10-03' } } });
w.query(t, { sort: [{ field: 'Win' }] });   // -> oct, sep
```

Ascending reads `oct, sep`. The comparator is handed `"Sep 9 \u2013 Sep 12, 2026"` and `"Oct 1 \u2013 Oct 3, 2026"`, and `"O" < "S"`.

**Why #279 stopped short** — a daterange's raw value is an object, `{ start, end }`, not a scalar. `String({start,end})` is `"[object Object]"`, which would make every row compare equal and turn the sort into a no-op: worse than the lexical order it has today. Ordering it needs a product call #279 had no mandate to make: **a range sorts by its start, then by its end** is the obvious answer (it is what a calendar does), but someone has to say so, and an open-ended range (`end` null) needs a rule too.

**Fix shape** — in `src/engine.js`, `#pathValue`'s `undressed` branch already exists (added by #279); extend it so a `daterange` returns a comparable scalar built from `start` then `end` rather than the object. `public/app.js`'s local comparator (the grids that hold every row) mirrors the same rule off `item.raw`. One test each, beside `test/sort-values.test.mjs` and `test/sort-values-browser.test.mjs`, which is where the date and number cases live.

Filed by the overnight fixer while landing #279, 2026-09-13, weave f211afd.

**The rule, said out loud:** a range sorts by its start, then by its end — what a calendar does. `weaveDateGrain.rangeKey` builds that key (the stored ends joined in order) and both comparators read the one function: the engine's `#pathValue` under `undressed` (so `weave query --sort`, `POST /api/tables/:ref/query` and `weave_query` move together) and `public/app.js` for the grids that hold every row. An open end is refused at the door, so only `importJSON` can write one; it sorts after a closed range that opens on the same day, because an open range extends furthest. The `daterange` Handbook guide now says so in its Gotchas.

issues.name: Enter in a long document parks the page at its end, and the next keystroke animates back — closing the slash menu
issues.description:
Found while making the Issue #137 wheel case deterministic (Issue #275). The test race had a product mechanism under it, and the mechanism is still there.

In an 80-paragraph Description document, with the caret in the FIRST paragraph: press End, press Enter. The window scroll jumps to the end of the document (`scrollY` 0 → 2701 on a 1280×700 viewport, 3440px of document) in two instant steps, with no `scrollIntoView`, `scrollTo`, `scrollBy` or `scrollTop` write from app.js or from Vditor — instrumenting all four on `Element.prototype` and `window` logged nothing. The next keystroke then animates the page back to the caret over roughly 900ms, an easing curve of ~40 scroll events.

Vditor hides its hint menu on ANY scroll: a `window` listener and one on the editor element, both calling its `hide(['hint'])`. So when that next keystroke is `/`, the menu opens and the animation's first scroll event shuts it — 21 rows in the DOM at `display: none`. That is the user-facing half of Issue #137 ("it disappears when trying to scroll") that survived the wheel fix: the wheel no longer chains to the page, but any scroll still closes the menu, and here the editor starts one by itself.

Reproduced at an 8× CDP CPU throttle (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`) on 4 runs in 5, and seen three times in Gerrit change 334's gate (`~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/334-2.log`). At full speed the animation is short enough that the menu usually survives, which is why this reads as a flake rather than as a bug.

Two things to decide, neither taken in #275 because that change was test-only:
1. Why Enter parks the page at the end of the document at all. It is not weave calling a scroll API; the candidates left are Vditor's IR re-render replacing the DOM under the browser's scroll anchoring, or Chromium's caret scroll in a contenteditable that was just rebuilt.
2. Whether the menu should ignore a scroll it did not come from. A short grace after the menu opens, or owning the close ourselves instead of letting Vditor's two listeners do it, would both keep Issue #137's contract while surviving an animation already in flight.

Repro (needs the gate's Playwright install symlinked as `node_modules`): seed a Description of `'# Top\n\n' + 'filler line\n\n'.repeat(80) + 'end\n'`, open the entity page at 1280×700, throttle the CPU 8×, click the first `p`, End, Enter, type `/`, and watch `scrollY` and the hint's `style.display`.

**2026-09-28, still real, and worse than filed.** In a scratch server on gerrit/main 1079b88 with this row's fixture at 1280x700 and no CPU throttle, Enter moved scrollY from 0 to 2818 (the document's end) in seven smooth steps, the `/` then animated it back to 187 over about 50 scroll events, and the slash menu was not visible in 3 runs of 3. Checked in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- Fixed: Enter in a long document leaves the page where it is, and the slash menu typed next stays open until the reader closes it. Notion and Linear scroll on Enter only when the caret would leave the viewport.
- Root cause, partly found: Vditor's `setRangeByWbr` (vendor `index.min.js`, offset 77007) places the caret, a childList mutation then adds a node to `pre.vditor-reset`, and the scroll starts right after; no weave `focus()` call runs. Tabler's `:root { scroll-behavior: smooth }` turns both jumps into animations. Where inside Vditor the end-of-document reveal comes from is not pinned.
- Change: after Vditor handles Enter, when scrollY moved by more than a viewport and the caret sits where it was, put scrollY back with `behavior: 'instant'`. Own the menu's close in the hint observer (`public/app.js:9754-9790`): ignore a scroll with no wheel, touch or key from the reader in the second after the menu opens.

## Approach

- Test first: `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`, "Enter in an 80-paragraph document keeps the page still, and the next / opens a menu that stays", without the scrollStopped and centring workaround.
- Steps: add the case, add the Enter restore, own the hint close, run the file alone ten times at 1x and 8x throttle.
- Size: M.
- Risks: Issue #137's wheel contract (a wheel over the menu stops at its edge) and Issue #455's slash-line change share this editor path.

issues.name: Looks broken: clicking a cell in a side-scrolling grid jumps the table back to the top
issues.description:
## Measured

On the weave workspace's `Development/Issue` table (277 rows) at 1440x900 in Chromium, where the grid is wider than its card so the `.table-wrap` is the scroller (`wv-grid-scroll`):

```
scroll the wrap to row ~40        -> wrap.scrollTop = 1667
click a cell's <input>            -> wrap.scrollTop = 0
```

The whole table jumps back to the top the instant a cell is clicked, before any network call. Reproduced against the LANDED server on :4400 (v0.4.21 @ ce0d0c7) and against a scratch server on the same commit, so it is not a working-tree effect. It does not reproduce when the PAGE is the scroller (a grid that fits its card) - only when `.table-wrap` carries `wv-grid-scroll`.

The likely path: focusing the control inside the cell runs the browser's own scroll-into-view against the nearest scroll container, and the windowed body (Issue #271) has only a spacer standing where the row above it should be, so "into view" resolves to the top.

## What good looks like

Notion, Airtable and Linear leave the viewport exactly where it is when you click a cell. Clicking is how you start an edit; it is never a navigation.

## Fix shape

`activateCell` / the editor's focus call should use `focus({ preventScroll: true })` and let the grid place the window itself (`wvScrollToRow` already exists and knows the row's index). Test shape: in `wv-grid-scroll` mode, scroll the wrap well down, click a visible cell's control, and assert `wrap.scrollTop` is unchanged and the clicked cell still holds focus.

Filed 2026-09-16 by the overnight fixer while verifying Issue #257 (in-place cell commits) against :4400 and a scratch server on 4490. #257 removed the commit's redraw; this jump is a separate, older path and survives it.

issues.name: Error: the Gerrit review poller died silently and blocked every landing for 4.5 hours
issues.description:
## What happened

Change 354 (Issue #257) pushed to `refs/for/main` at 2026-09-16 00:35 PDT and no Verified vote ever arrived. The launchd poller that DEVELOPMENT.md rule 3 and rule 7 rest on — `ai.grunion.weave-review`, running `harness/scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs` every 120 s — had been dead since 2026-09-15 20:13, four and a half hours, and said nothing anywhere a session would look.

```
launchctl print gui/501/ai.grunion.weave-review
  state = spawn scheduled
  runs = 4330
  last exit code = 78: EX_CONFIG
```

78 is launchd failing to exec the program. The plist runs `/Users/kyle/.local/bin/node`, a symlink to `/Users/kyle/.hermes/node/bin/node`, and `~/.hermes` no longer exists. `ai.grunion.weave` — the :4400 service itself — has the same ProgramArguments, so it was living on borrowed time: its process had started before the install vanished, and the first restart would have ended it. Restarting it as part of this change's deploy is what surfaced that.

The failure is silent by construction. `/tmp/weave-review-poll.log` still ends with a run of "nothing pending" from before the break, so a session that tails it reads a healthy poller. Nothing checks the log's mtime, nothing checks the job's exit code, and the poller is the only thing that would have filed an Issue about the poller.

## Blast radius while it was down

- No patchset got a Verified vote, so no change could land through the documented path.
- `gerrit/main` was never mirrored to GitHub (rule 7), so the public repo sat at ce0d0c7 while Gerrit moved on.
- `~/.weave-serve` was never fast-forwarded and :4400 was never kickstarted, so every landing after 20:13 would have been invisible on the live app with `stale: false` still reported.

## What good looks like

A watchdog that only reports when it is alive is not a watchdog. `ai.grunion.weave-fixer-watchdog` exists for the fixer; the review poller and the main watcher have nothing above them.

## Fix shape

1. Stop depending on one dangling symlink. The plists should run an absolute node that is managed (the nvm path, or a small `~/bin/node-stable` shim that resolves at run time), and `scripts/portable-check.mjs` should assert every launchd `ProgramArguments[0]` in the MANIFEST resolves to an executable — a dangling interpreter is exactly the drift that file exists to catch.
2. Give the poller a liveness signal with teeth: write a heartbeat file each fire and have a second job (or `/api/health`) report when it is older than ~10 minutes. A `staleWatcher` chip beside the existing behind/stale chips would put it where a session already looks.
3. Make the session's own landing check it. A fixer or shipping agent that pushes to `refs/for/main` should read the poller's last exit code and heartbeat before it starts waiting 15 minutes for a vote that cannot come.

## Recovery applied 2026-09-16 00:45 PDT

`~/.local/bin/node` was repointed at `/Users/kyle/.nvm/versions/node/v24.12.0/bin/node`; `ai.grunion.weave` and `ai.grunion.weave-review` both came back (exit 0, ":4400" serving d250748), and change 354 was gated by hand with `scripts/weave-review.sh 354` (2306 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped) before its +2 and submit. The GitHub mirror was pushed by hand to d250748. Several other `~/.local/bin` entries still point into the missing `~/.hermes` — `npm`, `agent-browser`, `mcporter` — and are outside weave.

Filed 2026-09-16 by the overnight fixer while landing Issue #257.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:32:32Z

## Fixed (2026-09-28, harness session 1b4685bd)

Already in place before this session: ~/.local/bin/node points at the nvm node (repaired 2026-09-16), and since harness PR #258 the plist runs ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-review-serve.mjs.

Added by harness PR #297 (https://github.com/grunion-ai/harness/pull/297, squash 780f485):
- scripts/portable-check.mjs now reports a loaded LaunchAgent whose ProgramArguments[0] does not resolve to an executable as drift, naming the path.
- Each watcher job writes ~/.gerrit/weave/heartbeat-<mode> when a cycle finishes. Before its own poll, each job checks its peer (review checks deploy, deploy checks review) and files one weave Issue per missed heartbeat when the peer has not finished a cycle in ten minutes and launchd does not show it running.
- `node ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-watcher-health.mjs` prints both jobs (last cycle age, running or idle, last exit code) and exits 1 when one is stale. A session can run it before waiting on a Verified vote (fix shape point 3).
- Tests: scripts/weave-watcher-health.test.mjs (7) and two new cases in scripts/portable.test.mjs, red first, then green. 25 pass, 0 fail in ~/.harness-serve at 780f485.
- Live: the deploy job wrote heartbeat-deploy at 19:38Z on its first cycle at 780f485. The review job was mid-gate on change 473, and the CLI reported it running and not stale.

Not covered: the two jobs share one node and one script, so a dead interpreter stops both and neither files. The portable-check assertion covers that case only when someone runs it. The /api/health staleWatcher chip is filed as Issue #460. Found on the way: ai.grunion.weave-fixer-watchdog runs a script that is not on harness main and exits 1 on every fire, filed as Issue #461.

issues.name: Looks broken: the workspace page titles the tab with the workspace name twice
issues.description:
## Reproduced (2026-09-17, weave v0.4.23 @ fdad622)

1. Open the workspace home (`#/`) in any workspace.
2. `document.title` reads `Weave Workspace · Weave Workspace`.

`showHome()` calls `syncDocTitle(null)` first, so the title is briefly the workspace name alone, and then paints `viewHeader({ title: ws.name })`, whose `syncDocTitle(title)` puts the workspace name back as the page name. `weaveBreadcrumbs.docTitle(name, wsName)` joins the two with a middle dot, so both halves are the same word.

Its own contract says otherwise (`public/breadcrumbs.js:57-60`, Issue #267): "The workspace page is the workspace name alone". `test/doc-title-browser.test.mjs:63` asserts exactly that and passed only because it polls with a 5 s `waitForFunction` and caught the transient between the two calls, before the header repainted.

## What good looks like

Notion and Fibery title a workspace's own page with the workspace name once. A tab reading `X · X` says nothing the first word did not, and it is the widest title in the strip.

## Fix shape

`docTitle` collapses the pair when the page name IS the workspace name. One line, and it makes the assertion in the browser suite land on a resting state instead of a transient.

---
Found 2026-09-17 by the overnight fixer while landing Issue #274: chaining route renders changed when the transient ended, and the doc-title case went red on a change that never touched titles. Fixed in the same commit as #274.

🌙 2026-09-17T23:40Z · fixed · Gerrit 360 → 3fe857d, in the same commit as Issue #274. weaveBreadcrumbs.docTitle now returns the workspace name once when the page name is the workspace name, so the workspace page's title rests where its contract said it did. Gate: test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs (+1). The doc-title browser case now lands on a resting state rather than the transient between showHome's syncDocTitle(null) and the header's repaint.

issues.name: Slow: 24 render-blocking scripts and no immutable asset caching, so every warm load revalidates 32 assets
issues.description:
## Measured
Copied from Issue #258 (2026-09-12 CX/UX audit, weave v0.4.17 @ 7d9886a, measured against :4400 in Chromium 1440×900):
- Cold load of `/`: **44 resources, 2,097,790 bytes** over the wire. `tabler.min.css` 524 KB, `app.js` 475 KB, Vditor `index.min.js` 296 KB, `style.css` 157 KB, `lucide-moving.js` 64 KB.
- `Cache-Control: no-cache` on every static (`src/server.js` serveStatic): every load revalidates every asset, one round-trip each, even when nothing changed.
- `public/index.html:51-74`: 23 classic `<script>` tags, zero `defer`/`async`.

Re-measured 2026-09-18 on v0.4.24 @ 2fea3bc plus Gerrit change 366 (Issue #258's gzip + ETag), scratch server on a copy of the live data:
- `public/index.html:51-75` now carries **24 classic `<script>` tags** (plus one inline module for lean-qr), still zero `defer`/`async`; 9 of them are `*-core.js` modules.
- With gzip in place the cold load of `/` is 44 resources, **505,208 bytes** (was 2,187,417 before change 366). The byte count is no longer the problem; the request count and the parse-blocking order are. Each of the 24 scripts blocks parsing in turn. Measured on :4400 at e020da6 after the deploy: a warm reload of `/` still makes **32 static requests, 24 of them answered 304** (8 answered 200), 44,218 bytes.

On localhost this is milliseconds. On the planned Cloudflare-hosted instance (Feature #84) or any remote or mobile use, 32 revalidation round-trips at 50-150 ms RTT, behind 24 parse-blocking scripts, dominate the open.

## What good looks like
Peer tools (Linear, Notion, Fibery) ship content-hashed bundles with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`: a warm load makes zero asset requests, and only the HTML document revalidates.

## Fix shape
Split from Issue #258 (its fix-shape items 2 and 3), because both change the asset pipeline and the load order, and weave has no build step by house rule:
1. Content-hashed asset URLs with `Cache-Control: immutable`; keep `no-cache` only on `index.html`. With no build step, the server can rewrite `index.html`'s `src`/`href` to `/app.js?v=<sha1 of content>` at serve time (hash cached per mtime) and send `immutable` only when the `v` query matches the current hash.
2. `defer` every classic script (order is preserved among deferred scripts), after checking nothing reads the DOM or a global at parse time before `DOMContentLoaded`; then consider concatenating the `*-core.js` modules at serve time into one response.
Both need a browser test for boot order and a check against the Cloudflare Worker adapter's asset path (Issue #231).

---

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-22T02:31:41.579Z · fixed · Gerrit 373 → 7111c31

**Tests added:**
- test/asset-cache.test.mjs: every served shell asset carries its content hash (lean-qr module import included)
- test/asset-cache.test.mjs: immutable only at the current hash; unversioned and stale asks revalidate
- test/asset-cache.test.mjs: the shell's ETag follows its served bytes, no Last-Modified, If-Modified-Since ignored
- test/asset-cache.test.mjs: versions follow a content change; missing files and page links left alone
- test/asset-cache.test.mjs: every classic boot script deferred; public/index.html keeps plain URLs for the Worker Assets binding
- test/asset-cache-browser.test.mjs: the deferred boot renders with every boot global in place and no page error
- test/asset-cache-browser.test.mjs: a warm load of / sends only the document to the server

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha 7111c31 startedAt 02:30:46Z (submit 02:29:00Z). Repro on :4400 in Chromium 1440x900, warm load of /: before, 24 parser-blocking scripts and 24 of 33 static responses answered 304 (31 on the wire); after, 0 blocking scripts, 0 answered 304, every shell asset from cache, 0 page errors. / is no-cache with ETag W/"160a518dbf05d58c"; /app.js?v=c21becc48369 is public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Two assets still revalidate: brand/weave-loader-{light,dark}.svg, fetched by app.js at runtime (300 bytes each), outside the shell. Document editor boots as before (4 editors on a Guide row, same as the old build). Screenshots attached (after, both themes). **Not shipped.** Nothing landed on main from this attempt.

**Hypothesis:** Confirmed on :4400 v0.4.25: showPopover installs a capture-phase outside-click listener that treats the trigger as outside, so a second click on the eye closes the popover and the eye handler immediately opens a new one. After a flip the eye is redrawn as a new node, so trigger identity alone cannot recognise it. Fix shape: showPopover takes an `owns` option (fieldVisibilityPopover passes any `.eye-btn`); a click inside the trigger closes the popover and stops the event; a popover already closed by Escape or a pick only unhooks its listener.

**Tried:**
- Reproduced live on :4400: after the second eye click one popover is open and it is a new node.
- Wrote the fix in public/app.js plus test/popover-toggle-browser.test.mjs (4 browser cases) and a CHANGELOG Unreleased bullet.
- Scratch server :4490 on a copy of weave.db, driven in the Browser pane: toggle closes and reopens, flip then new eye closes, outside click closes, Escape then eye reopens, on the table and entity pages in light and dark.

**Root cause.** Which box scrolls. `fitGridScroller` (Issue #233) gives a grid wider than its card a vertical scroller of its own, so the page never moves and the header only looks pinned; a grid that fits clips (`.wv-fit`), the page is the scroller, and `.view-header` had no sticky rule anywhere, so it left with the page. Measured on this very table at the 2187 x 1359 the report was filed from: after `scrollTo(0, 2500)` the header sat at -2468..-2260.

**Fix.** `#main > .view-header` is sticky at the top of the panel, so both modes read the same. The 16px under it became padding rather than margin, because rows read straight through a transparent band. `z-index: 6` clears every sticky layer the grid has (Issue #252 tops out at 5) and ties with the cell expansion and the field menu, which are later in the document and still open over it. `viewHeader` measures the header into `--wv-view-h` on the root; a `.wv-fit` wrap adds it to the `top` of the field headers and the Σ row, every other wrap keeps its own top edge, and the same reading is `scroll-padding-top` and feeds the grid's window arithmetic, which read the page's top edge as 0. A header that would take half the window does not pin at all — a 200px window, or a description expanded to thirty lines, would hold nothing but header and put its own Show less control out of reach.

**Tests added:** `test/sticky-view-header-browser.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases): the page scrolling under a held header with crumb, title, description and toolbar all on screen; the field headers and the Σ row flush under it; a wrap-scrolling grid unchanged; an opaque band matching the panel in both themes; the dock's header static and never taking the page header's reading; a header too tall for the window standing down and pinning again when folded; a window shrunk to 200px and given back. Four cases fail on the parent for the right reason (header top -1968). `test/sticky-add-row-browser.test.mjs`, `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs`, `test/grid-window-browser.test.mjs` and `test/grid-density-browser.test.mjs` now read the body's top edge off a stuck field header rather than the `<thead>`'s layout box.

**Verification.** Full suite 2514 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Scratch server on a copy of the live `weave.db`, Chromium and WebKit, both themes, at 2187 x 1359: header held at 0..224 with the field headers at 224..260. Confirmed again on the deployed build after the merge (`:4400` at 098e16c, started 2026-09-25T19:56:03Z): header 0..224, field headers 224..260, light and dark, 0 console errors.

**Not reproduced.** The 60 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` lines in the Trace did not appear on either build, in Chromium or WebKit, before or after this change. Nothing was changed for them.

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-09-23T08:13:48.003Z · fixed · Gerrit 379 → 0cd1a78

**Tests added:**
- test/grid-bottom-bounce-browser.test.mjs (3 new cases: the last row of a page-scrolled grid fires no scroll of its own over two idle seconds; + New there lands the caret in the Name cell and leaves the page still; a density flip re-measures the row the spacer stands in for)

**Live verification:** Live on :4400 at sha 0cd1a78 (started 08:11:21Z, after the 08:09:45Z submit), Chromium and WebKit, both themes, standing at the last row of Development/Issue (the reported page) and of Quality/Case (2,325 rows, no filter): scrolls the page made by itself over two idle seconds 0, positions in the cycle 1, ResizeObserver errors 0, and the + New foot passes its actionability checks in all eight runs. Before, on a copy of the live weave.db at gerrit/main e98cf3c and the same viewport, the same click was abandoned after six seconds of an unstable button.

**What each half did.** Both came from one mechanism, so both are answered by one change.

*"clicking new breaks scroll."* The spacers standing in for the rows a grid does not draw are sized at ONE measured row height, and that height was re-read from whichever row happened to head the window, on every pass. weave's rows are not all the same height (this grid measures 46.5, 47 and 48), and the spacer above a window 250 rows down stands in for 250 of them, so a pixel of variance became hundreds of pixels of page height. At the last row, where the scroll is already at its maximum, the box clamped to the new height, the clamp resized the wrap, and the ResizeObserver watching the wrap measured again: a three-position cycle about thirty times a second with no hand on the wheel. The replay log on this report carries the other half of that signature, 60 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors in the 1.9 seconds before Report was clicked. The height is now measured once per table, density and width and then kept.

*"the new row should become an entry with the cursor in the name field."* It already did, when it could: the row takes the caret through `focusNewRow` (Issues #125, #195). What stopped it here was the same cycle, one step earlier: the + New button never held still long enough to be clicked, so nothing was created. With the page at rest the click lands and the caret goes into the new row's Name cell, verified in Chromium and WebKit in both themes.

**Not fixed here, and not a defect with one right answer.** On a table whose filter excludes the new row's default state (this table's filter reads `{"Status": ["Fixed"]}`), the row is created on the server but is nowhere in the grid's filtered order, so nothing is drawn and nothing is said. What + New should do then is Kyle's call: Issue #341 sets out four options. Also found and filed: Issue #342, a density flip sends the reader back to the top of the table, which predates this change.

**Not in scope, and untouched:** Issue #246 ("+ New record" row floats above the divider), and Issue #317's direction rule, whose own case is green on this change. #317 fixed the wheel-push bounce in a wrap-scrolled grid; the cycle here ran in a page-scrolled one, with no hand on the wheel, and #317's one-row hysteresis could not absorb it because the corrections were six rows wide.

**Evidence attached:** eight screenshots, before and after, in both themes, at the last row and after the + New click.

issues.name: Error: the gate's Playwright cannot launch any browser, so every browser suite fails before its first case
issues.description:
## What was measured

The shared Playwright install the Gerrit gate links into every worktree (`~/.gerrit/weave/pw/node_modules`, playwright 1.62.1, unchanged since 2026-09-02) pins these browser builds in `playwright-core/browsers.json`: `chromium` 1234, `chromium-headless-shell` 1234, `webkit` 2336. The cache `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/` was rewritten at 2026-09-18 16:55:05 PDT, and it now holds chromium 1200/1243, chromium_headless_shell 1200/1217/1243 and webkit 2227/2359. None of the pinned builds is there.

The result: every `*-browser.test.mjs` file, plus `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`, throws in `test/lib/browser.mjs:41` before its first case runs:

```
browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /Users/kyle/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell
```

`WEAVE_BROWSER=webkit` fails the same way on webkit 2336. The failure is a throw, not a skip, so `launch()` never reaches its skip branch. The last green gate log is `review-logs/367-1.log` (2026-09-18 00:26, 2358 pass), which predates the cache rewrite. Any patchset reviewed after 16:55 on 2026-09-18 should vote −1 no matter what it contains.

Also broken on this machine: `~/.local/bin/agent-browser` is a symlink to `/Users/kyle/.hermes/node/bin/agent-browser`, and that directory no longer exists, so the scratch-verification step of the weave fixer routine cannot run either.

## What good looks like

A peer tool's test harness keeps its browser binaries matched to its driver: Playwright's own `npx playwright install` runs as a postinstall step, or CI caches the build that `browsers.json` names. A cache change made elsewhere on the machine cannot remove the gate's browser.

## Fix shape

1. Kyle (the step downloads from the Playwright CDN): `cd ~/.gerrit/weave/pw && npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell webkit`, then re-run the gate on any open change.
2. Pin the gate's browsers so another install cannot garbage-collect them: set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=~/.gerrit/weave/pw/browsers` in `weave-review.sh` and in the browser test lib's documented local run, then install into that path once.
3. Have `weave-review.sh` check that the executable exists before the suite runs, and name a missing browser as an environment failure in its vote message, so an agent does not read it as a red change.
4. Re-point or reinstall `agent-browser` (the `~/.hermes/node` prefix is gone).

Found while fixing Issue #320: the red test for that fix could not launch a browser.

Filed by the overnight weave fixer (run wf-0919-0003, Issue #320 subagent), 2026-09-19, weave v0.4.25 at 2cabe6d.



---

## Root cause and repair, 2026-09-20 (overnight fixer run wf-0920-0955)

**Why the builds went.** Playwright keeps a registry of installations at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/.links`, one file per install that claims browsers, written by `npx playwright install`. Its collector deletes any build no registered install claims. Before this run the registry held three entries and the gate was not among them:

```
585f0965…  ~/Documents/harness.nosync/external/plumbline-worktrees/fix-165-route/platform/node_modules/playwright-core
78673f4c…  /private/tmp/pl-210-1/platform/node_modules/playwright-core
8f2a64d9…  ~/node_modules/playwright-core
```

Two of those paths no longer exist, a removed plumbline worktree and a temp directory, so the collector pruned them, found nothing claiming chromium 1234, chromium-headless-shell 1234 or webkit 2336, and deleted all three. The `/private/tmp/pl-210-1` entry is dated 2026-09-19 08:05, so the install that ran the collection was a plumbline one. The gate's install at `~/.gerrit/weave/pw` was set up on 2026-09-02 in a way that never registered it, which is what left its builds unclaimed for sixteen days.

**Reproduced first.** On untouched `gerrit/main` (2cabe6d), in a fresh worktree with the gate's `node_modules` symlinked in:

```
✖ test/activity-cap-browser.test.mjs (243.457916ms)
  Error: browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at
  .../chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell
    at launch (test/lib/browser.mjs:41:34)
```

**Item 1 is done.** `npx playwright install` inside `~/.gerrit/weave/pw` registered the gate at `.links/fae23e26…` on its first attempt, so the collector will spare these builds from now on. Its own download could not resolve `cdn.playwright.dev` from this session, so the three pinned builds came down with curl from the URLs `playwright install --dry-run` prints and were unpacked into the cache. Both engines now launch at the pinned revisions (`chromium 151.0.7922.34`, `webkit 26.5`), and the suite above passes 3 of 3 in both themes with 0 skipped.

**Items 2 and 3 are done**, on harness `main` at `eb1bdec`, [PR #201](https://github.com/grunion-ai/harness/pull/201). `scripts/weave-review.sh` now reads the pinned revisions from `playwright-core/browsers.json` and checks each build's `INSTALLATION_COMPLETE` marker before it runs anything. A missing build still votes Verified -1, since a change nobody can verify must not land and `weave-review-poll.mjs` would re-review a change that carries no vote forever, but the message opens on `REJECTED by the ENVIRONMENT check, not by this change`, names the missing builds and carries the repair command. The check and the registry entry each get a case in `scripts/weave-gerrit.test.mjs`. The pin of item 2 is the registry entry rather than `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, which would cost a second copy of every build for the same protection.

The poller runs from `~/Documents/harness.nosync`, which is still at `b6c5391`, so the new check reaches it when that checkout next syncs. It is dormant either way while the builds are present.

**Item 4 is still open.** `~/.local/bin/agent-browser` still points into `~/.hermes/node/bin`, and that directory is gone. No replacement is installed and `agent-browser` is on no PATH, so the fixer routine's scratch-server verification step has no driver. This Issue stays open for that.

---

## Item 4 closed: agent-browser reinstalled, 2026-09-28

Kyle approved reinstalling `agent-browser` from npm on 2026-09-28.

**Installed.** `agent-browser` 0.38.1 from the npm registry, installed with the nvm node's own npm (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.12.0/bin/npm install -g agent-browser@0.38.1`). Before installing, the package metadata was checked against the skill file: repository `github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser`, license Apache-2.0, published by `vercel-release-bot`. The skill names 0.27.0 only as the version at adoption and pins nothing, so the latest release went in. Nothing else was installed. No other copy of `agent-browser` existed on the machine.

**Link.** `~/.local/bin/agent-browser` now points to `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.12.0/bin/agent-browser`, which npm links to `lib/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64`. The link was replaced in one step with `ln -sfn`. The old target under `~/.hermes/node/bin` did not exist.

**Browser.** No browser download was needed. `agent-browser` launched the Chrome for Testing build already in `~/.agent-browser/browsers/chrome-151.0.7922.47`.

**Playwright cache untouched.** `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/` was listed before and after the install and the two listings are identical. The gate's pinned builds (`chromium` 1234, `chromium-headless-shell` 1234, `webkit` 2336, read from `~/.gerrit/weave/pw/node_modules/playwright-core/browsers.json`) are present with their `INSTALLATION_COMPLETE` markers, and the gate's registry entry `.links/fae23e26…` is still there. Those three build directories are symlinks to `chromium-1243`, `chromium_headless_shell-1243` and `webkit-2359`, created on 2026-09-27 by an earlier session; this run did not change them.

**Verification.**

- `agent-browser --version` in a fresh login shell prints `agent-browser 0.38.1`, resolved from `~/.local/bin/agent-browser`.
- End to end: `agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/weave/` loaded the page titled "Weave", `snapshot -i` returned the accessibility tree (workspace navigation, search, "Report a problem" and the rest, with refs), and `close` shut the browser.
- `node scripts/agent-browser-skill.test.mjs` from `~/.harness-serve` (harness `ebdb29b`) passes: "all assertions passed", exit 0. That gate was red on harness main before this repair.

**Left alone.** Other dangling links in `~/.local/bin` were not touched: `mcporter` and `npx` (both into the missing `~/.hermes/node/bin`), and `buzz`, `canopy` and `tailscale` (into apps no longer in `/Applications`). `scripts/agent-reach-skill.test.mjs` stays red until `mcporter` is reinstalled.

All four items of this Issue are now done.

**2026-09-28, still real in shape, much faster than filed.** On a scratch server over a copy of uno (gerrit/main 1079b88), hiding and showing Last Modified and Created from the Sessions Fields popover redraws in 282 to 390 ms: PATCH the view, then GET /api/schema, then POST the table query, one after another. The report's 1.5 to 3.8 s calls came from a loaded host, where every call in its trace took seconds. Issue #235 reports the same gripe. Checked in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- Fixed: a hidden field leaves the grid on the same frame, and a shown field appears after one read of its own column. Airtable and Notion hide a column at once and never refetch the table for it.
- Root cause: every flip runs `write` (`public/app.js:4592-4611`), which awaits `gridConfigWrite` (`public/app.js:3788-3794`: PATCH, then `loadSchema()`), then redraws the whole table through `showDatabase` inside `keepScroll` (4606). A hide needs no data. A show needs only the new column, because the table query asks for the columns it draws (Issue #272, 483514a); that is my reading of "fields containing data".
- Change: apply the flip to the drawn grid first, keep the PATCH queued behind `eyeWrites` in the background, skip `loadSchema()` when the PATCH answer carries the view, and fetch only the shown column for the loaded rows.

## Approach

- Test first: `test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs`, "a hide removes the column within one frame and sends no /api/schema or query request; a show sends one query".
- Steps: local apply in `write`, trim `gridConfigWrite` for view patches, one-column fetch for a show.
- Size: M.
- Risks: Issue #243 (queued flips must both land), Issue #433 (the grid dims while held), and Kyle's width rule: hide and show never change another field's width.

issues.name: + New on a filtered table makes a row the grid cannot show
issues.description:
## Report

Found while fixing Issue #324 (overnight fixer, session wf-0923-0004, 2026-09-23). Filed as its own row because the answer is a product decision, not a defect with one right fix.

## What happens

The table page queries with the table's active filter (`filterWhere` in `public/app.js`, through the engine's where-language, never client-side). The grid's paged order is that filtered order. `state.inlineAdd` creates the row, re-reads, then asks `pager.indexOf(created.id)` where it landed.

A new row is born with the workflow's default state. When the table's filter excludes that state, the row is nowhere in the paged order, `indexOf` returns `-1`, and the grid neither scrolls to it nor paints it nor puts the caret in it. Nothing is said out loud. The row exists on the server and the reader has no sign of it.

## Reproduced

On a copy of the live `weave.db`, Development/Issue, whose filter reads `{"Status": ["Fixed"]}`, at 2187 x 1359 in Chromium and WebKit, both themes:

| | Filter on | Filter cleared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Row created on the server | yes | yes |
| `pager.indexOf` | `-1` | its index |
| Row drawn | no | yes |
| Caret | stays on `<body>` | the new row's Name cell |

## The decision

What should + New do when the table's own filter hides the row it just made? The options are not equivalent, and each gives up something settled elsewhere:

1. Say it out loud: create the row and toast that the filter hides it. Costs a line of copy; keeps the filter's meaning.
2. Show the row anyway until the next re-read. Gives up "the grid never filters client-side".
3. Seed the row so it matches the filter. Writes data the reader did not ask for.
4. Clear the filter on create. Takes the reader's view away from them.

The scroll half of #324 is fixed and landed separately; this half was left for Kyle.

## Fixed (2026-09-23)

Fixed in v0.4.35, commit e45dd2d, Gerrit change 385, with Feature #229 (table views). `+ New` on a filtered grid now seeds the new row with the filter's first state when the filter does not hold the workflow's default (a toggle takes its on label when the filter holds only that), so the grid shows the row it made. Gate: `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs`, case "+ New on a filtered view makes a row the grid can show (Issue #341)".

Fixed by the Feature #229 session, weave v0.4.35 (e45dd2d).

issues.name: A density flip sends the reader back to the top of the table
issues.description:
## Report

Found while fixing Issue #324 (overnight fixer, session wf-0923-0004, 2026-09-23). Predates that change: reproduced on `gerrit/main` at `e98cf3c` and on the fix branch alike.

## What happens

Flipping the grid's density control (Comfortable / Compact) part way down a long table puts the reader back at row 0.

Measured on a 600-row grid at 2187 x 1359 in Chromium, standing at `scrollY` 10,800 with row 191 at the top of the window:

| | Before the flip | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scrollY` | 10,800 | 0 |
| First drawn row | 191 | 0 |
| Page height | 28,988px | 19,836px |

Compact rows are shorter, so the page is shorter, but the flip does not carry the reader's place across. Density is a way of READING the table (Kyle, 2026-08-24), so it should leave the reader where they were reading.

issues.name: Looks broken: hovering a clipped cell covers the value, so click-to-edit happens under the popover
issues.description:
## Reproduced

Hover a clipped cell (Name, Description, any `td.clipped`) on a table grid. After `CELL_POP_DELAY` (180 ms) `showCellPop()` (`public/app.js:2207`) draws a copy of the value in `.cell-pop-layer`, pinned by `left`/`top` to the cell's own rect and then nudged so the copied content sits exactly on the live content (`public/app.js:2250-2258`, the 2026-08-26 "opens OVER the value" rule). The pop stays up while the pointer rests on the cell.

The pop is `pointer-events: none` (`public/style.css:502-507`), so the click itself reaches the cell. The live value underneath is hidden anyway: once the inline editor opens, the caret, the selection and the text you type all sit under a static copy that still shows the old value. Kyle's report #327 (2026-09-20, v0.4.25, Safari 18.5): "overflowed test overlap conflicts with click and edit functionality". Kyle, 2026-09-23: "it blocks click and edit, should show above the row/cell instead".

## Good looks like

Airtable and Notion expand a truncated cell only on an explicit gesture, and a hover preview never covers the text you are about to edit. Linear shows a truncated title as a tooltip above the row. The live cell stays visible and editable the whole time.

## Fix shape

* Anchor the pop ABOVE the cell: its bottom edge 4 px above the cell's top edge, left edge aligned to the cell's content left. Flip BELOW the row when the space above inside `.table-wrap`'s visible area is shorter than the pop.
* Hide the pop on `mousedown`/`focusin` inside the grid and while any inline editor is open, so editing never runs under a copy.
* Keep the cell's typography on the copy (Issues #67, #93) and the 180 ms rest delay.
* Supersedes the 2026-08-26 over-the-value alignment; update the comment to say so.
* Browser test: pop rect's bottom <= cell rect's top (or top >= row bottom when flipped), and no pop after clicking into the cell.

Supersedes the vague report #327.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.29, commit 0be87e5).

---

## Fixed in v0.4.30 (commit `2a473f0`, Gerrit 381, 2026-09-23)

`showCellPop()` keeps the copy's content on the cell's content left edge (`contentRect()`), min-width at the cell's width and the 380 px measure, and now sets the pop's bottom edge 4 px (`CELL_POP_GAP`) above the cell's top. When the room above inside `.table-wrap`'s visible area (or the viewport) is shorter than the pop, it flips to 4 px below the row. `mousedown` (capture) and `focusin` inside the grid take it down, and `cellIsEditing()` keeps it closed over a cell whose own control has focus. Typography copy (#67, #93), the input-to-text swap (#157), the 180 ms delay, the layer (no column moves) and `DOCK_ESC_OWNERS` are unchanged. The 2026-08-26 comment now records the new rule.

**Tests added:** `test/cell-pop-above-browser.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases: above the cell within 8 px on the value's left edge in both themes; first row flips below the row, inside the grid; real mousedown hides it and a pointer resting on the cell being edited opens none; focusin into another cell hides it). `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs`: the over-the-value case rewritten to the new rule. Gate: 2389 tests, 0 fail, 0 skipped (Verified +1, review log 381-2).

**Live verification:** :4400 restarted at 2026-09-23T23:30:38Z on 2a473f0 (merged 23:28:59Z). Issue table, row #4 (clipped Name), 1280x860, both data-bs-theme values: pop bottom 4 px above the cell top, content left offset 0 px; click put focus in the cell's live `inline-edit` input with 0 `.cell-pop` present, and a pointer moved within the cell afterwards opened none. Screenshots attached: hover-above-{light,dark}.png, click-edit-{light,dark}.png.

Fixed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.30, commit 2a473f0).

issues.name: Error: row-selection browser case "Set a field… on a number" flakes under the full gate and needs the retry
issues.description:
## Observed

`test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs:293` (`Set a field… on a number takes a typed value and applies it on Return`) failed its first run and passed on the retry in three Gerrit gate logs: `338-2`, `376-1` and `382-1` (`~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/`). Each time the assertion at line 307 read `0 !== 1`: after Return closed the puck (`.sel-puck` gone), none of the Estimate inputs read `42` yet. The same file also needed the retry in `365-1` and `377-1`, for other cases.

Change 382 (Feature #228, table search) never touches the puck or bulk set. The case passed in the same change's local full run (2399/2399) and on the retry.

## Likely shape

The puck leaves once the bulk write is sent. The grid repaints the written rows after the response. The test reads the cells between those two moments, and under a loaded gate that gap is long enough to lose.

## What good looks like

The case waits on the value it asserts, e.g. `waitForFunction` until one Estimate input reads `42`, or on the bulk `PATCH` response, before counting. It should never need the retry.

## Fix shape

Replace the one-shot `evaluateAll` read with a wait on the painted value. Then check the sibling puck cases (`Link to…`, the modifier-click case) for the same read-before-repaint pattern.

Filed by Opus 5.5 (Feature #228 shipping session), 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.31 @ a8e56cf.

issues.name: Looks broken: a rating on a chip or card prints as a number, not icons
issues.description:
## Measured

In v0.4.34 (c2ac845), a rating field named on a table's Chip or Card config reaches the browser with its `rating` segment data (`renderView` sets `seg.rating = { value, max, icon }`), and `segmentValueEl` in `public/app.js` draws icons when it sees `seg.rating`. The chip and the card read their segments through `viewSegments` in `public/view-core.js`, which rebuilt each field segment as `{ kind, label, value }` plus only the number display's `meter` (Feature #230). The `rating` key was dropped there, so a rating on a chip or a card printed its bare number ("3") instead of three filled icons. The Feature #231 browser suite covered the grid cell, the rollup and the dialog, and no case opened a chip.

## What good looks like

A chip's or a card's rating segment draws the same read-only icons the grid's rollup cell draws, with "3 of 5" as its accessible name.

## Fix shape

`viewSegments` passes every drawing key through (`meter`, `rating`, and the sparkline's `spark` from Feature #232). A browser case opens a relation chip onto a row whose Chip names the rating and asserts the icons.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.34, commit c2ac845), found while building Feature #232; fixed in the same change.

## Fixed (2026-09-23)

Fixed in v0.4.36, commit 558550f (Gerrit change 386). `viewSegments` passes `meter`, `rating` and `spark` through; `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` opens a relation chip and asserts the icons and "3 of 5" (failed before the fix, passes after).

issues.name: Wrong data: renaming a field drops the table's saved filter and sort on it
issues.description:
## What was measured

Before v0.4.35 a table stored its state filter and its sort by field NAME (`db.filters = {State: [...]}`, `db.sort = [{field: "State"}]`), and `updateField` renamed only the hidden-field list (src/engine.js, updateField, the `hiddenFields` map). Renaming a filtered or sorted column left both keys pointing at a name the table no longer had. The grid then dropped them without a word: `filterWhere()` skips a filter whose field it cannot find, and `gridSort()` keeps only sorts on fields that still exist (public/app.js). The Tables row kept showing the stale text in Filter and Sort.

Reproduce on v0.4.34: `updateTable("Task", {filters: {State: ["Open"]}})`, then `updateField("Task", "State", {name: "Stage"})`. The grid shows every row, and the Tables row still reads `State: Open`.

## What good looks like

Airtable and Attio carry a view's filter and sort through a field rename, because they hold the field by identity.

## Fix

Fixed in v0.4.35 with Feature #229. Views hold fields by id; `updateField` moves each view's filter key and sort entry to the new name, and `deleteField` drops a filter or sort on a removed field. Gate: `test/table-views.test.mjs`, case "a new field shows in every view; a dropped field leaves them; a rename keeps visibility, filter and sort".

Filed by the Feature #229 session, 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.35 (e45dd2d).
