issues.description:
## Observed

Gerrit gate log `388-1` (`~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/388-1.log`) closed with:

```
# RETRIED and green: 2 file(s) failed the first run and passed the second — test/doc-kinds-browser.test.mjs test/doc-rail-browser.test.mjs
```

Change 388 is a test-only change to `test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs` (Issue #349). It touches nothing either doc suite reads, and the same tree ran the full suite locally at 2506 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped without a retry.

## Why it is worth a row

CLAUDE.md: a suite that keeps needing the second chance gets an Issue, not a shrug. Issue #349 has just shown what this shape usually is — a case that reads the DOM in the gap between an action being sent and the grid repainting after the response, which a loaded gate opens wide enough to lose. Neither doc suite has been read for that pattern.

## Fix shape

Read both files for one-shot reads taken straight after an action: `evaluateAll`, `allTextContents`, `textContent` and `count()` with no `waitForFunction` on the value being asserted. #349's fix is the pattern to copy — wait on the painted value, and stall the re-read behind the write in the test itself so the gap is deterministic rather than a coin flip. Evidence for a fix here is repetition (five or more consecutive raw runs plus runs under CPU pressure), not a single green run.

Filed by the overnight fixer (session wf-0924-0002) while landing Issue #349, 2026-09-24, weave v0.4.36 @ 2df5991.

## 2026-09-28, after Issues #454 and #466 (harness session 1b4685bd)

Gerrit change 483 (5df7e50, deployed) runs the browser suites in their own lane at half the cores, after the rest of the suite, and adds `styleOf`, `settled`, `eventually` and `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE` to `test/lib/browser.mjs` (see #454). In ten full suites in a row with it, at outside load 9.5 to 27.5, plus two more beside main, no case in the whole suite failed and nothing was retried.

The doc-rail half is fixed: "a burst of resize events reschedules the rails once per frame" counted every 250 ms timer on the page, and code colouring polls on that same debounce until highlight.js has loaded. It now counts only the rails' own. doc-kinds-browser was not read, so this row stays open for it.

issues.name: Error: the GitHub mirror is six landings behind gerrit/main while :4400 is current
issues.description:
## Observed

`git ls-remote origin main` on the weave checkout reads `a8e56cf` (v0.4.31, 2026-09-23) while `gerrit/main` is `2df5991`. Six landings have not reached GitHub:

```
$ git rev-list --count a8e56cf..gerrit/main
6
```

`:4400` is current — health reports `sha 2df5991`, `startedAt 2026-09-24T08:11:10Z`, `stale false` — so the deploy half of the main watcher is working and only the mirror push is behind. This is the recurrence of the shape Issues #162 and #166 already caught, with the deploy leg healthy this time.

## Why it matters

DEVELOPMENT.md rule 7: the main watcher pushes every green `gerrit/main` tip to GitHub fast-forward only, and a refused push means someone pushed GitHub directly. Six commits of drift is either a refused push nobody read or a watcher leg that stopped without saying so. The repo's public face is six landings stale either way, and the reconcile in "GitHub mirror" gets harder the longer it sits.

## Fix shape

Read the main watcher's log for the push leg (`harness/scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs`), find whether the push is failing or never attempted, and say which. If the push was refused, reconcile the way DEVELOPMENT.md prescribes: merge GitHub main into gerrit/main in a temp worktree and push both, never force. Then add the check that would have said this out loud, the way the deploy leg already files an Issue when :4400 is not launchd's pid started after the landing.

Filed by the overnight fixer (session wf-0924-0002) while landing Issue #349, 2026-09-24, weave v0.4.36 @ 2df5991.

**2026-09-28, Resolved.** Harness PR #257 (f52a2cf) makes the main watcher take `GH_TOKEN` from the grunion-ai account at start, which ended the 403 that stalled the mirror push; the backfill and root cause went to Issue #376. issues.name: Looks broken: Showcase has no bar, ring, heat, rating or sparkline columns
issues.description:
## What was measured

On :4400 (v0.4.38, commit 4257a73), Showcase › Field Types ("Every field type, in several configurations") shows none of the three displays shipped on 2026-09-23: no number field wears `display: bar | ring | heat` (Feature #230), there is no `rating` field at all (Feature #231), and no formula returns a list or wears `display: sparkline` (Feature #232). `GET /w/weave/api/schema` lists 31 data fields on Field Types, all from the 2026-08-23 seed.

Cause: `seedFieldShowcase` in `src/weaver-seed.js` returns early when the Showcase space exists (`if (w.listSpaces().some((sp) => sp.name === 'Showcase')) return w;`), and nothing else touches the Showcase after the first seed. The v0.4.34 change added a `Fit` rating to the seed, but only a brand-new docs workspace ever gets it. The seed gate (`test/seed.test.mjs`) also did not require the displays, so a display could ship with no Showcase column.

## What good looks like

The Handbook sync (Issue #255) already solves the same shape for the Handbook pages: boot re-applies generated content once per build, keyed on a hash, additive and name-matched. A product's showcase grid should demonstrate every display the engine can draw, the way Airtable's and Notion's template galleries show every field type configured.

## Fix shape

Move the new columns into a data list (`SHOWCASE_ADDITIONS`) that the fresh seed and an existing workspace both go through; add missing fields after their anchor, fill only empty cells on the seeded rows, never rename or remove. Boot runs `syncShowcase` on the docs workspace once per build. The seed gate derives the display and sparkline-style lists from `NUMBER_DISPLAYS` and `SPARKLINE_STYLES` in `src/engine.js`, so a future display without a Showcase column fails the build.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.38, commit 4257a73).

## Fixed (2026-09-25)

Fixed in v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2, Gerrit change 392 (tests 2522/2522 on the gate). Boot on :4400 at 2026-09-26T03:32:01Z logged "Showcase sync: 19 fields added"; verified in Chromium, light and dark: 6 bars, 3 rings, 3 heat cells, 12 editable rating groups, the Peer skill rollup as stars, 6 line, 3 column and 3 win/loss sparklines, and a click on the 2nd heart of Sensor board / Love wrote 2 through the API, restored to 6. Found along the way: Issue #377 (a to-many lookup of a rating prints numbers).

issues.name: Looks broken: the entity dock scrolls sideways when the description holds a wide table
issues.description:
Reproduced 2026-09-25 on :4400 (v0.4.38, commit 4257a73), uno workspace, Buyer/Shopping List #1 "Libernovo maxis" opened in the entity dock.

What happens: the whole dock body scrolls sideways. Paragraphs run off the right edge (unwrapped at the dock width) and a horizontal scrollbar sits at the bottom of the panel. Measured with the dock at its 360 px minimum: #dock clientWidth 360, scrollWidth 1917; each description paragraph laid out 1871 px wide.

Cause: public/style.css:1573 `#dock .dock-entity .entity-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }` overrides the base rule at style.css:906 (`minmax(0, 1fr)`). A bare `1fr` track has an `auto` minimum, and `.entity-body` has `min-width: auto`, so the track grows to the min-content width of the widest child. The buyer research tables hold full product URLs as unbroken text (min-content 1123 to 1701 px), which drags the grid, the section body and every paragraph to that width. The full #/entity page does not break because it keeps `minmax(0, 1fr)`: there each table scrolls inside its own 626 px box. The same bare `1fr` sits in the 900 px media query at style.css:909 for `.entity-grid.side-open`.

Probe: injecting `#dock .dock-entity .entity-grid { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }` drops scrollWidth to 384, paragraphs wrap at 286 px, and each table scrolls in its own box (clientWidth 286, overflow-x auto). The remaining 24 px comes from the Event Date / Last Researched row at 360 px: the date input plus picker button run 32 to 52 px past the padding.

Good looks like: Notion and Linear side peeks wrap body text to the panel and let a wide table or code block scroll inside itself; the panel never scrolls sideways.

Fix shape: change style.css:1573 and :909 to `minmax(0, 1fr)`; let the date field shrink (min-width 0 on the input, or wrap the row) at dock minimum width; add a browser test that opens an entity with a wide markdown table in the dock and asserts #dock scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1 at 360 px and at a wide split.

Filed by harness session 2026-09-25 (Claude Opus 5.5), weave v0.4.38, commit 4257a73.

Fixed 2026-09-25 in commit 0e81750 (Gerrit change 411, merged; deployed to :4400 at 04:11Z, sha 0e81750). The dock entity grid and the 900 px side-open query now use minmax(0, 1fr). The date box fit (Issue #159) moved from an inline min-width to a --date-fit variable folded into width: max(floor, fit), so the stylesheet min-width: 0 can shrink it in a narrow column. Re-measured on :4400, Libernovo maxis docked at 360 px: #dock scrollWidth 360 at clientWidth 360 (was 1917), light and dark. At the 360 px floor an ordinal date truncates inside its own box instead of pushing the panel. Test: test/entity-dock-overflow-browser.test.mjs (360 px minimum and even split). Filed by harness session 2026-09-25 (Claude Opus 5.5).

issues.name: Looks broken: space ⋮ menu lists every table's CSV export instead of space actions
issues.description:
## Report

Kyle, 2026-09-26: "these are the wrong space level menu options."

On a space page, the ⋮ "Space actions" menu lists one `Export <Table>.csv` row for every table in the space, then `Delete space + N tables`. On the weave workspace's Showcase space that is 18 export rows (People, Field Types, Formatting, Documents, Icons, Projects, Meetings, Docs, Notes, Tasks, Comments, Expenses, Contracts, Deploys, Approvals, Line Items, Tags, Activity) before the delete. The rows act on tables, not on the space, and each table's own ⋮ already carries Export CSV.

## Decision (Kyle)

Drop the per-table exports. The space menu keeps only `Delete space` / `Delete space + N tables` (hold to confirm, as today). No other verbs are added.

## Fix shape

- `public/app.js`, `showSpace`: remove the `space.tables.map(... Export ${d.name}.csv ...)` spread and the divider after it; update the comment above the call.
- System spaces (`space.system`, for example the Workspace space; Issue #248) have no Delete, so the menu would be empty. Render no ⋮ at all there (`actions: []`); never an empty menu.
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`: drop the per-table Export assertion from 'table and space menus carry CSV export and delete'; add one asserting the space menu holds no per-table export.
- `test/system-space-menu-browser.test.mjs`: the system space shows no ⋮; the user space has no `Export …csv` items and still shows Delete space + N tables.
- Feature row and Handbook guides that describe the old space menu get updated on :4400, then `docs/development.json` is re-exported.

## Good looks like

Showcase shows ⋮ with only `Delete space + 18 tables`, in both themes. The Workspace system space shows no ⋮.

## Fixed 2026-09-26 (Gerrit change 393, commit `a35f67f`)

`showSpace` now passes `actions: space.system ? [] : [dotsMenu([hold-to-delete])]`: the per-table `Export <Table>.csv` rows and the divider after them are gone. Tests: `ui-contract` asserts the space menu holds no per-table export; `system-space-menu-browser` asserts no ⋮ on the system space and only the hold-to-delete on a user space, in both themes.

Verified live on :4400 (serving `0e81750`, launchd pid 67431, started 04:11:03Z after the 03:54Z submit), dark and light: Showcase shows one ⋮ holding only `Delete space + 18 tables`, no divider; the Workspace system space renders no ⋮ and no menu panel. Local run of the seven affected files at `a35f67f`: 191 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.

A duplicate of this fix (`fa46525`, GitHub PR grunion-ai/weave#6, written in a cloud session three minutes after 393 landed) was closed unmerged.

Filed by Claude Code session 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.39, commit `a35f67f`.

issues.name: Looks broken: a lookup of a rating over a to-many relation prints numbers, not icons
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

On :4400 (v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2), Showcase › Field Types, the lookup `Peer skills` reads the `Skill` rating (max 5, star) on People through `Peers`, a many-to-many relation. The grid prints the values as text ("2, 4", "5", "5, 2, 4") instead of drawing rating icons. The rollup beside it (`Peer skill`, avg of the same rating) draws stars correctly. Screenshot attached (showcase-computed-light.png).

Cause: `public/app.js:2854-2856` draws a computed cell as a rating only when `typeof item.raw[f.name] === "number"`. A lookup over a to-many relation returns a list (`[2, 4]`), so it falls through to the text value. The engine side is right: `#ratingOf` in `src/engine.js` (around line 5733) gives the lookup field its `rating` scale regardless of cardinality, and `describeSchema` carries it.

Feature #231 says "A lookup of a rating draws icons", with no cardinality limit, so a to-many lookup is inside the promise.

## What good looks like

Airtable draws a lookup of a rating field as one row of icons per linked record. The same here: one read-only `ratingEl` per value, separated the way a list lookup separates chips, each with its own "n of max" label; a blank value keeps its slot as an unrated group.

## Fix shape

In the computed-cell branch, when `f.rating` is set and the raw value is an array, render `ratingEl` per entry (null as unrated). Same for the chip and card segments if they share the gate. Browser test: a to-many lookup of a rating draws one icon group per related row, in both themes.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2), found while verifying the Showcase update for Issue #371.

**2026-09-28, still real.** On :4400 (v0.4.52) Showcase > Field Types still prints Peer skills as "2, 4", "5" and "5, 2, 4" in a 136px column, while the Peer skill rollup beside it draws its icons. The gate has moved to `public/app.js:3239` (`typeof item?.raw?.[f.name] === 'number'`), and the sample preview at `public/app.js:8302` carries the same gate. Change 473 (v0.4.52) rebuilt the rollup and lookup tray and left the cell as it was. Checked in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

issues.name: Looks broken: text, borders and focus rings fail WCAG AA contrast, grid inputs have no names, and there is no skip link
issues.description:
Finding F2 from the 2026-09-26 design pass on weave v0.4.31 (a8e56cf). Measured with axe-core 4.10.2 plus a contrast walker, both themes.

## Labels and landmarks

- Issue table: 40 critical `label` violations. Grid `td .inline-edit` inputs (tabindex -1, no accessible name), `.fieldrow` number inputs, `textarea.name-edit`.
- Map: the read-only `input.view-title` fails `label`; `.view-title` fails `label-title-only`.
- `span[aria-label="Copy"]` fails `aria-prohibited-attr`.
- `#hub-foot` sits outside every landmark (`region`) on every view.

## Contrast, light theme

| Element | Colors | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.nav-space` | #7e8394 on #f3f1ec | 3.35:1 |
| `th.col-head .col-label`, `th.pid-head`, `.nav-stats`, `#nav-collapse`, "+ New space" | #6b7280 on #f3f1ec | 4.28:1 |
| search label | | 3.61:1 |

| in-progress chip #9eb1ff on #3e4c66 | 4.22:1 | |

Form-control borders: 1.23:1 light, 1.31:1 dark. Input and checkbox outlines nearly vanish.

## Focus

- Per theme, 7 of 60 tab stops change by less than 3:1 on focus. Toolbar `.table-search-btn`, `.eye-btn`, `.pose-btn` and Close reach 2.16:1 light, 1.45:1 dark. `input.view-title` 1.23:1, `textarea.name-edit` 1.08:1.

## Targets under 24px

## Fix shape

- `--wv-canvas-muted` about #5f6474 (4.5:1 or better on #f3f1ec).
- Dark `--tblr-primary` and `--tblr-link-color` near #6ea8ff.

issues.name: Looks broken: the entity page repeats its title in the document, misaligns section carets, lets rollups run off the page and shows mention refs instead of names
issues.description:
Finding F6 from the 2026-09-26 design pass on weave v0.4.31 (a8e56cf). Reproduced 2026-09-25 on v0.4.39 (gerrit/main 6a2ced2) with the demo seed (`scripts/seed.mjs`), Chromium at 1440 x 900, light theme. Screenshots attached.

## What was measured

1. **Duplicate title.** Task #1 "Design onboarding wizard": the page title is `textarea.name-edit` at 20px/700 (`public/style.css:863-869`, `.entity-head`). The Description document opens with an H1 carrying the same text at 26.25px with a rule beneath, so the document heading out-shouts the page title. Same on Project "Apollo Launch".
2. **Misaligned carets.** The FIELDS caret (`button.doc-caret`) sits at x=371; the DESCRIPTION and SPEC carets sit at x=389. 18px apart.
3. **Rollup overflow.** Apollo Launch "Task List" (rollup, join of task names) prints on one line and runs past the panel: `documentElement.scrollWidth` 1576 in a 1440 viewport. The "rollup" tag is clipped at the right edge.
4. **Mentions.** Apollo's `[[Task#1]]` renders as a 63px chip reading "# Task#1 -" (the ref, not the record name). Task #1's `[[Project#2|Hermes Docs]]` chip measures 174px for a roughly 75px label: the live-chip overlay (`style.css:1017-1056`) paints tinted space past the label.

## What good looks like

Notion and Linear show one record title; a document H1 that repeats it is suppressed, and document headings sit below the page title in the hierarchy. Section toggles share one left edge. Long relation or rollup lists wrap within the cell or collapse to "+N"; the page never scrolls sideways. A mention reads as the target's current name, and its chip hugs the label.

## Fix shape

- Hide a first-block H1 whose text matches the record name (trimmed, case-insensitive) in the rendered view; keep it in the markdown.
- Type scale (decided 2026-09-26: 11/12/13/14/16/18/20/24): page title 24, document H1 20, H2 18, H3 16 bold, document text 16. Entity page and document headings only.
- One x for every section caret.
- Rollup lists wrap within the cell; `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`.
- Mentions render the target's name; the overlay is sized to the label.

Related: #97 (md references should look more like rich chips), #372 (entity dock scrolls sideways on a wide table; separate cause at style.css:1573).

Filed by the F6 fix session, 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2.


## Fixed

Landed through Gerrit change 414 as f294dd4 on 2026-09-26 (after v0.4.42); deployed to :4400 at 08:39Z.

- A first H1 matching the record name (trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, case-insensitive; `WeaveEditorLib.isTitleEcho`) gets the class `wv-title-echo` from the fold pass and is hidden. The markdown keeps it. It is never folded or mapped, it shows again if a block is written above it, a rename re-runs the check, and a document holding only that heading keeps it visible.
- Scale: page title 24, document H1 20, H2 18, H3 16 bold, H4 16, H5 and H6 14, document text 16.
- The document section head steps out of the 18px text indent: every block caret sits at x=371 on the demo page.
- Computed values in the field block wrap inside their cell: Apollo Launch now measures scrollWidth 1440 in a 1440 viewport.
- Live mention chips read the target's name (`data-name` from the resolver; the `Task#1 - Name` label stays as the tooltip). The anchor is an opaque cover over the literal, and the tint and ring sit on the label: the Hermes Docs tint went from 174px to 93px. Trade-off: a hand-typed bare `[[Task#1]]` only has its literal's width, so a long name ellipsizes; references picked from the `#` search carry the name and fit.

Tests: `test/title-echo.test.mjs` (the rule) and `test/entity-hierarchy-browser.test.mjs` (one visible title, a non-matching H1 stays at 20px, rollup scrollWidth <= clientWidth in light and dark, one caret x, mention name and tint width). All ten new cases fail on 6a2ced2 and pass on f294dd4. Handbook: two paragraphs (chip label, hidden title heading).

Run alone today on gerrit/main 1079b88, `test/entity-hierarchy-browser.test.mjs` passes all six cases: the echoed H1 is hidden, a different H1 stays at 20px, the rollup wraps with no sideways scroll in light and dark, every block caret sits on one x, and a mention reads its record name with the tint ending at the label. issues.name: Looks broken: 18 declared font sizes, five below 11px, and Inter is declared but never loaded
issues.description:
## Measured
- `style.css` declares 18 px sizes: 8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20. It also has 8 em sizes.
- Examples: avatar initials at 8.5px, the system badge at 9.5px uppercase, type-tile labels at 10.5px.
- There is no `@font-face`, and `document.fonts` loads 0 faces, yet `style.css:93` and `:205` ask for Inter. On :4400 the body resolves to `"Inter Var", Inter, -apple-system, …` with `document.fonts.size` = 0 and no `@font-face` in `style.css`, so every machine without Inter installed renders the system stack.
- The file also has 21 z-index values and 31 colour literals that bypass tokens.

## What good looks like
Linear and Notion run on a short type scale of six to eight steps, with nothing under 11px, and ship their UI font with the app. A new component picks a step from the scale instead of a new number.

## Fix shape
Migrate to the decided scale (Kyle, 2026-09-26), with an 11px floor. This is the complete set:

| px | Role |
|---|---|
| 11 | meta |
| 12 | secondary |
| 13 | grid, unchanged |
| 14 | body |
| 16 | document text and dialog headings |
| 18 | doc H2 |
| 20 | doc H1 |
| 24 | page title |

Bring the vendored vditor heading sizes onto the same scale, and either vendor Inter into `public/vendor/` or declare a deliberate system stack.

Line references are at a8e56cf. Rechecked on :4400 (v0.4.39 @ 6a2ced2) on 2026-09-25: still present. The attached screenshots come from that recheck, Chromium 1440x900.

---
Filed by the 2026-09-26 design pass (Claude cloud session, weave v0.4.31 @ a8e56cf, scratch server, Chromium 1440x900 and 390x844)

**2026-09-28, still real.** `public/style.css` on gerrit/main 1079b88 declares 19 px sizes (8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 and 24), with 32 declarations below 11px. There is still no `@font-face`, and `'Inter'` is still asked for at lines 137 and 307. Checked in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-07T12:30:05Z · session fix-1102-1oyz · from #556, #680, #686

**Repro:** Still real on gerrit/main 3ca61e2, and the counts have moved since the 09-28 recheck. public/style.css declares 19 distinct px font sizes (8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24) across 246 declarations, 32 of them below 11px, plus 13 em declarations. No @font-face anywhere. Live on :4400 at 1440x900: document.fonts.size is 0, body resolves to 'Inter Var', Inter, -apple-system, … at 14px, and sub-11px text on screen is the system badge (.k.k-sys) at 9.5px plus runs at 10px, 10.5px and 10.7143px, the last from the vendored vditor sheet, not style.css. One thing to know before reviewing this on Kyle's Mac: document.fonts.check('700 18px Inter') answers TRUE there because Inter is installed on the machine, so the wordmark and view title look right locally and only differ on a machine without it. The z-index and colour counts in the row have drifted the other way: 29 distinct z-index values (was 21) and 67 distinct colour literals (was 31).

**Code:**
- public/style.css:80 .ws-wordmark and :174 .view-title are the only two rules asking for 'Inter' by name (the row's 137 and 307 were a8e56cf line numbers)
- public/vendor/fonts/ already holds DejaVuSans.ttf with its licence beside it, used by src/pdf.js and the vendored public/vendor/vditor/dist/index.css. So vendoring a UI font has a precedent in the tree, directory and licence habit included
- The off-scale declarations, counted: 12.5px 23, 11.5px 18, 10.5px 15, 10px 12, 13.5px 4, 15px 4, 19px 3, 9px 2, 9.5px 2, 17px 2, 8.5px 1. That is 86 of the 246 px declarations; the other 160 already sit on Kyle's eight steps

**Fix shape:** The row is one sweep holding three changes that do not need each other, and splitting them is what gets any of it landed. (1) The font: either an @font-face for Inter out of public/vendor/fonts, beside DejaVuSans, or strike 'Inter' from those two rules and declare the system stack deliberately. Two rules, no visual change on a machine with Inter installed, and it is the only part that is a decision rather than a migration. (2) The 11px floor: 32 declarations, and only four sizes on screen, so this is the smallest change with a visible result. The vditor 10.7143px comes from the vendored sheet and needs its own override rather than an edit to vendored code. (3) The eight-step scale: 86 declarations to move, plus the 13 em declarations, which is where a guard test earns its place.

**Test to write first:**
- A guard over public/style.css that fails on any font-size px value outside Kyle's eight steps (11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24), with the vendored sheets excluded by path. Write it with the current 86 off-scale declarations listed as the allowed set, shrink the list per change, and the last change deletes the list. That is the only way a sweep this size does not come back
- A rendered floor case in a browser test: no element with text computes a font-size under 11px, which the vendored vditor sheet currently breaks at 10.7143px
- If the font goes the @font-face way: document.fonts.size is greater than 0 on load, asserted in a browser test, because that is exactly what a machine without Inter installed would otherwise answer 0 for

issues.name: Looks broken: a new workspace opens on the registry grid, not an empty state
issues.description:
## Measured

Design pass 2026-09-26 on weave v0.4.31 (a8e56cf), finding F4; reproduced on gerrit/main 6a2ced2 (v0.4.39) against a fresh data dir.

- `weave serve --data <fresh>/main.db`: the root workspace holds 6 tables, all in the system **Workspace** space (Spaces, Tables, Fields, Views, Workflows, Workspaces), and 168 registry records. `/api/workspaces` reports `tables: 6` for it.
- `showHome` (public/app.js:9814) shows "Welcome to Weave. Create a space and a table to get started." only when `allTables()` is empty (app.js:9849). `allTables()` includes the system tables, so the welcome never renders on the root. The first screen is the Spaces registry grid (every workspace's spaces side by side) with a small "+ New space" link.
- `showSpace` (app.js:7433) opens every space on the Tables registry grid: FIELD ORDER, HIDDEN FIELDS, FILTER, SORT, HIDE ROLLUPS columns.
- A member workspace made from the hub has no Workspace space since Feature #219, so its welcome does render; the first-run install (the root) is the case that fails.

A first-timer's first screen is database internals.

## What good looks like

Airtable, Notion and Fibery open an empty workspace on one primary "create" action plus a few starting templates, with the structure editor one click away.

## Fix shape

1. Count user tables only: exclude system spaces and tables through the engine's `system` flag, not names.
2. No user tables: home shows an empty state with one primary **New table** action, three starting templates (Tasks with a workflow, a small CRM, Docs) built from the existing create calls, and one line on what a space and a table are.
3. The registry grids on home and space pages move behind a collapsed **Schema** disclosure, one click away.
4. The relation map stays on home once tables exist.

Screenshots attached: the fresh root home and the Workspace space page, light and dark.

Filed by the F4 empty-state session, 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.39 (6a2ced2).

## Fixed 2026-09-26 (4a652ce, Gerrit change 416)

- **User tables only.** `engine.userTables()` and `WeaveStarters.userTables(schema)` (new `public/starter-core.js`) count tables by the `system` flag, never a name. The hub list and the Cloudflare worker report that count as `tables`, so a fresh root reads 0.
- **Empty state.** A workspace with no tables of its own opens on one line about spaces and tables, a primary **New table** button (it names a first space "General" when there is none), and three templates: Tasks (To do / Doing / Done workflow, Due, Priority), CRM (Companies and Contacts, linked), Docs (Tags, Draft / Published). Templates walk the existing REST create calls and open their first table; a double click builds once.
- **Schema fold.** The Spaces grid on home and the Tables grid on a space page sit under a collapsed **Schema** disclosure, drawn on first open; open or shut is remembered per browser (`weave-schema-open`). A space page lists its tables with record counts and **+ New table**.
- **Relation map** stays on home once tables exist.
- New workspaces start with an empty description; the empty state does the job Issue #123's default text did.
- Handbook: "Making a workspace your own" gains "The home page and a space page".

Tests: `starter-core.test.mjs` (11), `first-run-browser.test.mjs` (8, both themes), hub counts in `workspaces.test.mjs`. Gate on the landed tree: 2630 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Live on :4400 at 4a652ce.

Filed and fixed by the F4 empty-state session, 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.43.

issues.name: Looks broken: a rollup's settings tray shows nothing it does, not even that it draws stars
issues.description:
## Reproduced

Showcase › Field Types, view Rich fields. Column Peer skill (a rollup, avg of People › Skill over Peers) draws 3 of 5 stars in every cell. Open ⋮ › Edit field. The tray holds Name, Description and two lines: "rollup field — the type is fixed" and "Computed config is not editable — delete and recreate to repoint it". It never says which relation it follows, which field it reads, which aggregate it runs, or why the result wears stars (the display comes from the target rating field, a decision recorded on Feature #230). A reader cannot tell what the column computes or how to change its look.

## Good looks like

Airtable's rollup and Notion's rollup settings show the relation, the target field and the aggregate as three pickers, with a live preview of the result, and a Format section beneath. Every setting the cell shows is readable, and editable where it can be.

## Fix shape

* Show the recipe as three read-only (or editable, if the engine allows repointing) rows: Relation `Peers` → Field `Skill` → Aggregate `avg`, with the row's current result.
* Show the display it inherits: "Shows as the rating on People › Skill: 5 stars" with a link to that field; for a numeric rollup over a number, the number costume controls (Feature #230) apply here too.
* Same treatment for lookups (see Issue #377, a lookup of a rating prints numbers).
* Replace "delete and recreate to repoint it" with the real edit, or say why it cannot change.
* Browser test: the rollup tray names relation, field, aggregate and display.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2). Reported by Kyle: "I don't understand the config for this rollup or formula driven rating; config tray looks wrong."

## Screenshot

![Looks broken: a rollup's settings tray shows nothing it does, not even that it draws stars](/w/weave/api/files/a94d2f52-8120-49e9-89a5-2a96afe7a1ee)

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:30:56Z

## Fixed (2026-09-28): the tray names the recipe and where the look comes from

Landed through Gerrit change 473, commit 9ef6068 (merged as d1274b1 on gerrit/main), deployed to :4400 (`/api/health` sha d1274b1). No version bump; the batch release carries it. Scope was the read-only tray only: Kyle decided on 2026-09-28 that making the recipe editable is deferred to Feature #241.

What the tray of a lookup or a rollup shows now, verified live on Showcase › Field Types, view Rich fields, column Peer skill, in both themes:

* **Relation** `Peers → Showcase/People`, **Field** `Skill · rating`, **Aggregate** `avg`, as read-only inputs in the same slots the pickers take when a rollup is created (`throughRelation(fixed)` in `public/app.js`), styled like the read-only plural in the Name tray. A space rollup shows Table, Field and Aggregate. A count shows no Field.
* The dead-end sentence is now "The recipe is set when the rollup is created and cannot be changed here."
* **Result**: the value on the first row that has one, drawn as the cell draws it (Sensor board: three of five stars). Ported from the unlanded change 443.
* **Shows as**: "Drawn as the rating on People › Skill: 5 stars.", then "A rollup takes its look from the field it reads, so change it on Skill." with an **Open Skill settings** link that opens that field's tray. A number display reads "Drawn as a bar from People › Score, on the column max."; a count reads "A count, in plain figures."; anything else names the field it reads.
* The lookup Peer skills (view Standard) gets Relation, Field, Result and Shows as. Its Result prints `2, 4`, the same as its cell, which is Issue #377 and stays its own row.

Tests: `test/rollup-tray-browser.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases): the rollup's rows, result, display and link in light and dark; the lookup's rows and display in light and dark; a count, a bar rollup and a plain number rollup, with a rename saved through the tray. The full gate passed on patchset 3 (2961 of 2963, with `table-views-browser` red once and green on the retry; the two earlier -1 votes were load flakes, recorded on Issue #290). The Handbook lookup and rollup pages describe the tray.

The `Fixed in` link to v0.4.47 was removed: the v0.4.47 Release row names this Issue, but that fix (change 443) never landed.

Screenshots attached: issue-387-after-Peer-skill-light.png, issue-387-after-Peer-skill-dark.png, issue-387-after-Peer-skills-light.png.

issues.name: Looks broken: the loading rope freezes whenever the page is busy
issues.description:
## Measured
At 4x CPU the rope was on screen from 1605 ms to 7602 ms. Inside that window the main thread ran six long tasks (53, 67, 57, 99, 107, 116 ms) and rAF frame gaps reached 199 ms. The rope stops for each one, then jumps.

Probe: Playwright Chromium 151, 1440x900, http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/weave/, rAF gap log, longtask observer, MutationObserver on #page-loader, CPU throttle 1x and 4x. Host load average was 71 during the runs.

## Cause
public/brand/weave-loader-*.svg animates stroke-dashoffset with SMIL. Chrome and Safari tick SMIL and dash offsets on the main thread, so boot's JSON parse and route render stall it.

## Good looks like
Loaders in Linear, Figma and the OS spinners run on the compositor and keep moving through main-thread work.

## Fix shape
Keep the static mark (same rope(), same masks) and reveal it with two feathered cover elements that animate transform only, keyTimes 0/.45/.62/1 with the same spline. The rope is monotonic in x, so a left-to-right wipe traces the same draw. A Chrome trace of the mockup reports compositeFailed: 0 for both covers. Gate: a browser test that forces a 250 ms long task and asserts the cover transform changes across video frames inside it.

Filed by the loader review session, 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.39, serve checkout 6a2ced2. Review report: ~/Documents/queue/2026-09-25-weave-loader-review-report.html.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:30:14Z

## Reproduced on gerrit/main f34f90c (v0.4.51), 2026-09-28
Probe: Playwright Chromium headless shell, 1440x900, CPU 4x, loader shown on :4400/w/weave/, phase pinned to the draw-in, a forced 250 ms long task, Page.startScreencast. The compositor delivered 3 frames in the first 69 ms of the task and none until 263 ms: the rope froze. A control page with a plain CSS transform animation delivered a frame every 16 ms through the same kind of task.

## Fix (committed, waiting to land)
Commit 62c0ec0, Change-Id Id397c2c73be12d133155938c992d94bc7a77a701, parked on GitHub branch park/i390-rope-compositor. Not yet pushed to Gerrit: machine load stayed between 150 and 450 for 90 minutes, and the batch rule holds pushes while load is above 30.
- brand/build-logos.mjs: loaderStill() is loaderDraw's paths and masks with no dash and no SMIL (a test pins the two together). loaderWipe() and loaderWipeCss() generate keyframes from the rope's geometry and the old timeline (2000 ms, key times 0/.45/.62/1, spline .45 0 .25 1), so the revealed span follows the dash's span at every phase.
- public/app.js: initPageLoader inlines weave-loader-still-{theme}.svg inside .rope-wipe > .rope-wipe-in. The window slides by transform and its content slides back, so the mark stays put. setCurrentTime is gone: un-hiding the host restarts the CSS animation.
- public/style.css carries loaderWipeCss() verbatim between markers. The unused SMIL copies leave public/brand; the brand SMIL files and README GIFs stay.

## Evidence
After the fix, same probe on a scratch server: 13 frames inside the 250 ms task, all distinct, one every 16 ms. Frame-by-frame against the SMIL rope at 40 phases (96px, 2x): rest frames match exactly in WebKit (0 px) and differ by 83 px in Chromium, where its own SMIL dash stops short of the end cap. Worst moving frame 0.9% of the box. The one visible difference is the moving end: a vertical cut where the dash had a round cap (the review's stated risk), most visible early in the draw-in and late in the unweave. Attached: issue-390-before-after.png.

## Tests
- test/page-loader-browser.test.mjs (new): both themes animate transform only with no SMIL and no dash; a forced 250 ms long task must yield at least 5 distinct compositor frames (red before the fix with 0, green after).
- test/page-loader.test.mjs: the still equals loaderDraw minus dash and SMIL; the wipe matches the dash span at 401 phases; style.css carries the generated CSS; no setCurrentTime.
- Full suite: 2960 pass, 2 fail at load 131. Both failures are outside the loader: deploy-artifacts G3 passed on retry, and table-views-browser Issue #341 passed alone on this branch (16/16) and failed alone on base gerrit/main (15/1) under the same load.
- WebKit: the loader and grid-loader suites pass under WEAVE_BROWSER=webkit. Playwright's WebKit video recorder stalls during a long task even for a plain transform control, so the Safari compositor check could not be automated here.

## Gate run 1 on Gerrit change 482 (patch set 1, e16e5bf), 2026-09-28
Verified -1 from the full suite (3036 pass, 5 fail; the lifecycle pack was green). None of the red cases touch the loader: doc-autosave-phone-browser (Description writes on tap outside and on panel close), entity-block-grip-browser (Issue #210 block anchor), grid-layout-browser (drop across the frozen seam), table-toolbar-browser (hidden field position). Each file passed alone three times on this patch set at load 13 to 25: doc-autosave-phone-browser 20/20 three times, entity-block-grip-browser 3/3 three times, grid-layout-browser 15/15 three times, table-toolbar-browser 7/7 three times. These are the known full-suite timing flakes (Issues #454, #466).

## Look settled by Kyle, 2026-09-28, and the rebuild
Kyle sent the first version back: the moving end must read as the old round cap, and the unweave must end on the two end dots. The compositor mechanism stays. Rebuilt: each end of the old dash is an anchor with three windows onto a copy of its strand, moving by translate and rotate only: a far-side window up to a vertical line kept clear of the strand beyond that end, a square cut at the end's point bounded 3.5 units either side, and a round cap disc. Each copy counter-moves, so the strand stays put. The unweave follows Chromium's dash, whose arc length runs 1.3% long, so it ends on the end dots; at rest one window shows the whole strand. The loader is one generated fragment, public/brand/weave-loader-rope.html, holding both themes and the CSS. Nothing animates stroke-dashoffset, clip-path, mask-position or layout.

Nine-phase strip (u = .10 .20 .30 .40 .50 .70 .80 .90 .925), old SMIL against new, pixels that differ of 36,864 at 2x, fuzz 10%. Attached: issue-390-look-settled.png.
- Chromium light: 66 103 131 109 87 78 89 72 74. Chromium dark: 60 91 121 107 83 69 81 65 67. Largest 0.36% of the box.
- WebKit light: 32 66 79 68 0 29 142 438 334. WebKit dark: 28 64 78 64 0 19 134 437 334. The rest frame is exact (0 px). At .90 and .925 WebKit differs because WebKit's own SMIL dash runs about 1% short and has already dropped the end dots there; the two engines' old ropes disagree with each other at the tail, and the new rope follows Chromium's, as Kyle asked.
- Chromium rest frame 87 px: Chromium's own SMIL dash stops short of the end cap (83 px against the bare still mark).

Frame delivery, forced 250 ms long task, CPU 4x, Chromium screencast, scratch server on this change: 13 of 13 frames inside the task distinct, three runs.

Safari: Playwright's WebKit video recorder stalls during a long task even for a plain CSS transform control, and sampling the animation clock from requestAnimationFrame across a 250 ms block is inconclusive: the new rope's clock advanced 250 ms across the block, and so did the old SMIL rope's (252 ms), which is the one that freezes on screen. Both are timeline clocks, so this measure cannot show which thread paints. No automated check here shows the rope moving through a long task in Safari.

## Gate run 2 on change 482 (patch set 2, dd1c252), rebased onto 92e78a2
Verified -1. Red: bulk-settle, doc-rail, entity-block-grip (Issue #210 anchor), hold-release, table-views (Issue #341), table-toolbar popover flip, editor slash headings, and this change's own frame test ("the rope froze: 4 frames (4 distinct) inside a 250 ms task", then 4 inside a 366 ms task on the retry). The rope kept moving; the loaded machine starved the compositor below the test's five-frame floor. The other files are outside the loader and passed alone after the run: bulk-settle 1/1, doc-rail 2/2, hold-release 4/4, table-views 16/16, table-toolbar 7/7, entity-block-grip 3/3 twice after one 2/3.

Per the batch rule (two gate runs at most), this change is stopped, not landed. The fix for the test is made and not yet gated: it now asks for at least two distinct frames and no gap longer than 60% of the task, which the old rope fails (longest gap 181 ms of 250, 72%) and the new rope passes (three local runs). Commit 863bfcc, Change-Id Id397c2c73be12d133155938c992d94bc7a77a701, on GitHub branch park/i390-rope-compositor-v2; Gerrit change 482 still holds patch set 2 without it.

## Third gate cleared; frame test reworked (patch set 3, e050e7f, on fa176b9)
The five-frame floor went red in gate run 2 under load, and the first rework (at least 2 distinct frames, no gap over 60% of the task) was not honest: the old SMIL rope passed it. Its last frames arrive stamped up to about 130 ms into the task, because the screencast sends one frame per ack and a slow PNG encode queues frames painted before the task began. The test now follows 5df7e50's convention (it waits on what it asserts, with no fixed sleeps), takes small JPEG frames, pins the rope to its draw-in, and asks for a changed frame in the last 40% of the forced 250 ms task, where no queued frame can land.
- Old SMIL rope (gerrit/main fa176b9), six runs, three at CPU 1x and three with WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE=4: red 6 of 6. 0 frames in the last 40%; last frame at +136, +135, +122, +104, +119, +118 ms, so its longest gap inside the task is the tail, 114 to 147 ms.
- New rope (this change), same six runs: green 6 of 6. 6 changed frames in the last 40% every run, last frame at +232 to +239 ms, longest gap 28 to 34 ms.
- Loader suites alone: Chromium 54 pass; WebKit 11 pass, 1 skipped (the CDP screencast case).

## Safari
Nothing automated could show the rope moving in Safari while the main thread is busy. Playwright's WebKit video recorder stalls during a long task even for a plain CSS transform control, and sampling the animation clock from requestAnimationFrame cannot tell the two ropes apart (both clocks advance by the block's length). Kyle should look at it in Safari once it is live.

## Gate run 3 on change 482 (patch set 3, e050e7f), after the flake fix
Verified -1, and the change is stopped here without landing, as agreed for this run. The files still red after the runner's retry are outside the loader: doc-autosave-phone-browser (Description and Brief write on panel close, a 400 ms waitForRequest) and grid-density-browser (a density flip keeps the reader's row). Each passed alone three times right after (20/20 and 12/12, three runs each); recorded on Issue #454, since this red came after that fix landed.
This change's own frame test went red in the first pass on a 30 s timeout in its wait for the loader's animations to be running (page-loader-browser.test.mjs line 72), then passed on the retry with 6 frames in the task, 4 changed in its last 40%, last at +187 ms. Alone it passed three more times.
Change 482 holds patch set 3 with Code-Review +2 and Verified -1. Landing it needs a person to decide on a fourth gate (or clearing the vote). Worktree .wt/i390-rope stays at e050e7f; branches park/i390-rope-compositor and park/i390-rope-compositor-v2 stay on GitHub.

issues.name: Looks broken: a fresh load shows no loader for its first second or more
issues.description:
## Measured
4x CPU: first paint 976 ms, #page-loader filled 1128 ms, rope shown 1605 ms. 1x: first paint 172 ms, rope shown 1075 ms. The shell sits bare in between.

## Cause

issues.name: Slow: a finished page waits up to 2 s behind the loader, then pops off an empty frame
issues.description:
## Measured
Mockup replaying the withPageLoader logic, 20 random finish phases: tax (hide minus done) max 1934 ms, mean 1120 ms. A 520 ms load stays covered for about 2.5 s.

## Cause
The whole-cycle rule rounds the hide up to the cycle end (LOADER_CYCLE_MS - elapsed % LOADER_CYCLE_MS). At cycle end the rope is fully unwoven, so the last frame is an empty wash, and hidden = true removes it with no fade.

## Good looks like
The loader resolves on the brand mark and gets out of the way within half a second.

## Fix shape
On finish, fast-forward at 3x to the next woven pose (keyTime .45 to .62), hold 120 ms, fade 160 ms. Set fractional iterations so the animation ends on the pose even if the main thread is busy. Same 20-phase mockup run: max 861 ms, mean 512 ms, every exit on the woven mark. Keeps the intent of the whole-cycle rule: never caught half-woven.

issues.name: Slow: home boot holds the loader 6 to 9 s behind a serial /api/schema call
issues.description:
## Measured
Network trace of /w/weave/ boot: GET /w/weave/api/schema 2990 ms, then workspaces?deleted=1 3662 ms, POST /api/markdown 3644 ms, table query 3465 ms, all queued after schema; loader hidden at about 9.2 s. curl alone: /w/weave/api/schema 1.36 s, the other calls under 20 ms. Host load average was 71, so treat absolute times as upper bounds; the serial shape holds regardless.

Makes precise the vague open row #211 ("trouble loading this apge").

## Good looks like
Boot fires independent reads in parallel and schema answers in tens of milliseconds.

## Fix shape
Profile /api/schema on the weave workspace, cache or slim it, and start the workspace, workspaces and health reads alongside it rather than after.

Filed by the loader review session, 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.39, serve checkout 6a2ced2. Review report: ~/Documents/queue/2026-09-25-weave-loader-review-report.html.

**2026-09-28, still real in shape.** Three boots of /w/weave/ on :4400 today with the host quiet finished every API call by 190 to 300 ms and never showed the loader; an hour earlier, under a load average near 50, /api/schema took 0.9 to 1.9 s and the loader held until 2.6 s. The serial shape holds either way. Before picking this up, read "Landing order for the loader rows" on Issue #391. Checked in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- Fixed: a boot sends its independent reads together and builds each schema once, so on a remote host the home page is one round trip behind the HTML.
- Measured today (resource timing, three runs): the first wave at about 80 ms is `/api/schema` from `readRegistry` (`public/app.js:868-875`), `/workspace` (886), the workspace `/schema` (889) and `/workspaces` from `buildWsRail` (12714). The second wave waits for `loadSchema().then(renderRoute)` (13311): `/health` from `renderNav` (1335), the home's `/workspace` and `/workspaces`, and `/workspaces?deleted=1`, which also waits on the rail's own read (12771). On the weave root the registry read and the schema read return the same 115,612 bytes, so the server builds that schema twice.
- Change: skip `readRegistry()` when the loaded workspace is the root; start `/health` (the `state.healthP` promise already dedupes it) and `/workspaces?deleted=1` at boot beside `loadSchema`; share one `/workspaces` promise between the rail and the home.

## Approach

- Test first: a browser case beside `test/page-loader.test.mjs`: boot /w/weave/ and assert one schema request, and that /health and /workspaces?deleted=1 start before the schema read ends.
- Steps: the root check in `loadSchema`, the early reads before line 13311, the shared promise in `buildWsRail` and the home.
- Size: M.
- Risks: member workspaces still need the registry (Feature #219); Issue #258 made the three reads parallel and its test must stay green.

issues.name: Wrong data: a rating default sent with a new max is clamped to the old max
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

`updateField` handled the `default` lane before the rating's `max`/`icon` lane (`src/engine.js`, the `if ('default' in patch.config)` block ran ahead of `if (field.type === 'rating' && ('max' in patch.config ...))`). The field dialog sends both in one patch. So a 5-point rating raised to 7 with a default of 6 in the same save stored a default of 5: `#validateDefault` rounded and clamped 6 against the old max of 5, and the new max landed after.

```js
const { w, t } = ws({ default: 4 });            // max 5
w.updateField(t, 'Fit', { config: { max: 12, default: 11 } });
w.getField(t, 'Fit').config.default;             // 5 before the fix, 11 after
```

Lowering the max also left a standing default above the new ceiling in the config (the write path clamped it per row, so rows were right; the schema and the dialog showed the stale number).

## What good looks like

Airtable and Notion apply a field's scale and its default together: a default is always a legal value of the scale on screen.

## Fix

The rating lane moves ahead of the default lane, so a default sent with a new max is judged against that max, and a lowered max clamps a standing default in the config. Gate: `test/rating-field.test.mjs`, "a default rides with the max: raised together it keeps, lowered it clamps down (Feature #234)".

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, found while building Feature #234 on weave v0.4.39, commit a35f67f).

Fixed in v0.4.43 (commit 689c2b1, Gerrit change 413), with Feature #234.

issues.name: Looks broken: the mention caret in a relation chip is an 11px target nested inside the chip link

Found while landing Issue #378 (the accessibility baseline), 2026-09-25.

## Measured

`button.mention-caret` draws 11.3x13.8 px inside a relation chip. It sits inside the chip's own link (`.k-rel > a`), between the label and the ↗ that the link paints as `::after`. So the caret now grows to 24px in height only. It stays 11px wide, under WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24 by 24, or 24px of clear spacing), because every pixel beside it belongs to the link.

A nested control gets its own box beside the link rather than inside it. GitHub's issue-reference hovercards and Linear's relation chips both keep the disclosure as a separate target outside the chip's link area.

- Move the caret out of the `<a>`: the chip becomes `[link: label ↗] [caret]`, each its own target.
- Give the caret a 24px box with the bordered glyph drawn inside it, then drop the height-only `::after` override in `style.css`.

issues.name: Slow: npm test hangs forever when a serve-boot test times out under load
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

`test/showcase-sync.test.mjs` ("serve brings an existing docs workspace's Showcase up to the current build on boot") and `test/handbook-sync.test.mjs` spawn `node bin/weave.js serve --port 0` and wait 20 s for `Weave running`. When the wait times out, the promise rejects but nothing kills the child. Its stdout and stderr pipes stay open, so the `node --test` file process never exits, and `npm test` sits there with no output.

Measured 2026-09-25 in a worktree at load average 78 (several gates running at once): `npm test` stopped printing at TAP line 1220 and stayed silent for 28 minutes. `pgrep -P` on the suite found two idle `weave.js serve --port 0 --data /var/folders/.../weave-handbook-sync-*/boot-*/ws.db` and `.../weave-showcase-sync-*/boot-*/ws.db` children, 0% CPU, elapsed 27:03 and 15:33. Killing the two serve pids let the suite continue.

## What good looks like

A test that spawns a server owns its lifetime: on timeout or failure it kills the child (`child.kill('SIGKILL')` in the reject path, or a `t.after` hook), so a slow boot costs one red case and the `scripts/test.mjs` retry, never a silent hang.

## Fix shape

In both suites: kill the child in the timeout branch and in a `finally`/`t.after`; consider a shared `spawnServe()` helper in `test/lib/` that does both, and raise the 20 s budget under load the way the browser suites did (Issue #44).

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, found while gating Feature #234 on weave v0.4.39, commit a35f67f).

## Fixed, 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd, high-severity batch)

Landed as Gerrit change 437, patch set 5 (fa176b9), the change written on 2026-09-26 and left unlanded when its session stopped. It was rebased onto current main, with a merge of main's `WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK: 'off'` spawn environment in both suites, and given the fragment `changelog.d/serve-fixture-reap-398.md`. Change-Id kept.

**Fix.** `test/lib/serve-fixture.mjs` exports `bootAndStop(child)`, which both `test/handbook-sync.test.mjs` and `test/showcase-sync.test.mjs` now use. It stops the server on every outcome (boot, timeout, early exit, spawn error), escalates a SIGTERM the server ignores to SIGKILL after one second, and waits for the child to close before the test ends, so a slow boot costs one red case and never a silent hang.

**Tests.** `test/serve-fixture.test.mjs`: a timeout reaps the child before rejecting, a server that ignores SIGTERM is killed, an early exit reports its output, a spawn error rejects at once. serve-fixture, handbook-sync, showcase-sync and changelog-fragments: 26 pass, 0 fail. Gate: review-logs/437-5.log, Verified +1 on the stack with change 483.

Deployed: :4400 reports sha fa176b9.

issues.name: Looks broken: a dragged column snaps back to its old place on the next sort, and rows scrolled in later draw the old cell order
issues.description:
## What was found

Found by reading `renderTable` in `public/app.js` (weave v0.4.39 @ 6a2ced2) while building Feature #233. The grid computed its columns once, `const cols = visibleCols(db)`, and built the header (`draw()`), the Σ row and every body row (`buildRow`) from that list. A header drag moved the cells in place and spliced `db.fields` (`reorderField`), and the view saved the new order, but `cols` kept the old one. So:

1. Sorting from a header's ⋮ menu calls `draw()`, which rebuilt the header and rows from the old `cols`: the moved column jumped back to where it was while the view held the new order. A reload then showed the new order again.
2. With the row window (Issue #271), a row built for the first time after the move (scrolled into view) carried its cells in the old order under a header in the new order, so a value sat under the wrong label until the next redraw.

## What good looks like

Airtable, Notion and Linear keep a moved column where it was dropped through every redraw, and every row agrees with the header.

## Fix shape

`cols` is reassigned when a column moves in place, and the move reorders the cells of every row built during the draw, including rows the window has taken off screen (`built`). Regression test: `test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs`, "after a drag, a sort redraw keeps the new order in the header and every row". Fixed in the Feature #233 change.

---
Filed by the Feature #233 build session (Claude, 2026-09-25), against weave v0.4.39 @ 6a2ced2.

issues.name: Looks broken: a fast view-tab drag does nothing
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

On live :4400 (v0.4.40, 0670c68), Issue table, strip `Default | zz drag test`. A mouse drag of `zz drag test` onto `Default` left the order unchanged. Pointer trace captured on the page:

```
pointerdown  on "zz drag test"  x=458
pointermove  on "Default"       x=402
pointermove  on "Default"       x=346
pointerup    on "Default"       x=346
```

The first move after the press already lands past the dragged tab's left edge (412). `viewStrip` in public/app.js only listens for `pointermove` on the dragged tab and takes pointer capture on the first move it sees there, so a move that starts outside the tab never reaches it and the drag never lifts. The Browser pane's drag sends moves this coarse, and a fast real mouse flick can too. The shipped browser case used `mouse.move(..., { steps: 12 })`, which always crosses the tab first, so it passed.

## What good looks like

Airtable and Attio pick the tab up on press and follow the pointer wherever the first move lands.

## Fix shape

Take pointer capture at `pointerdown` for a mouse, so every later move and the release go to the pressed tab. Add a browser case that drags in one jump (`mouse.move` with the default single step).

Filed by the Feature #229 drag-order session, 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.40 (0670c68), during live verification.

## Fixed (2026-09-26)

Landed as b6599a9, Gerrit change 415; deployed to :4400 in 1ed7e7b (v0.4.42), started 2026-09-26T08:08:02Z by launchd (pid 79923) after the 07:38:44Z landing. A mouse is captured at pointerdown. Verified on live: the same one-jump drag of a test view onto Default reordered the Issue strip, saved it (`GET /api/tables/Issue/views` answered `zz drag test, Default`), and the bare table route then opened the dragged view with its Fixed filter lit. The test view was deleted afterwards. Gate: `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs` gained a one-jump drag case, red before the fix and green after in Chromium and WebKit.

issues.name: Looks broken: a grid only just wider than its card jumps back to the top when scrolled to its end
issues.description:
## Observed

A grid that is only just wider than its card loses a scroll to its end: the wrap scrolls (scrollTop 56016 of 56471 right after `scrollTo`), and within 1.5 s it is back at 0 with rows 0 to 49 drawn. No script writes `scrollTop` after the scroll (traced by wrapping the `scrollTop` setter and `scrollTo`/`scrollBy`/`scrollIntoView`), and the wrap's `class` and `style` do not change (MutationObserver). The content is collapsing under the scroll position, so the browser clamps it.

Reproduced with the `test/grid-window-browser.test.mjs` seed (1,200 Case rows, a select and a relation column):

| Build | Viewport | Card width | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gerrit/main 0670c68 | 700×700 | ~320 px | pass (grid clearly wider than card) |
| gerrit/main 0670c68 | 1016×700 | ~628 px | grid fits; page mode (test asserts `wrap`) |
| gerrit/main 0670c68 | 964×700 | ~584 px | **fail**: `tr[data-eid=<last row>]` never draws after scroll to end |
| phone-drawer change | 700×700 | ~584 px | **fail**, same timeout |

The phone drawer change (Issues #262, #326) took the sidebar out of the flow below 900 px, so at 700 px the card grew to the width where this edge lives. That change moved the suite's narrow case to 390 px to keep testing the wrap; this row is the edge itself.

Possibly the same root as #291 (a click in a side-scrolling grid jumps the table to the top): both reset a wrap scroller to 0 without a script write.

## What good looks like

A scroll to the end of a wrap-scrolled grid stays at the end and draws the last rows, at every card width where the grid overflows by any amount.

## Fix shape

1. Add a case to `grid-window-browser.test.mjs` at 964×700 (card ~584 px) that scrolls the wrap to its end and waits for the last row.
2. Trace `paint()` in the row window (`public/app.js`, `const paint = (w) =>`): it removes leaving rows before `setPad` sizes the spacers, so if anything reads layout in between, `scrollHeight` collapses and the browser clamps `scrollTop`. Size the spacers first, then remove rows.
3. Check `geometry()` for a card width where `wv-grid-scroll` and the fit check disagree by a pixel.

---
Filed by the phone-drawer session (Claude, weave v0.4.40 @ 0670c68), 2026-09-25.

**2026-09-28, Obsolete.** The failing geometry came from the auto table layout of v0.4.40; Feature #233 (1ed7e7b, v0.4.42) replaced it with a fixed default width per type, and the row-window suite itself moved its default viewport to 1600px because of it. With this row's own seed (1,200 Case rows, a select and a relation) on gerrit/main 1079b88 in a scratch server, a scroll of the wrap to its end drew the last row and held the scroll at its maximum at every width where the grid overflows its card by 2 to 11px (1325 to 1334px wide), and at 964 and 1100px. The suspected order in `paint()` (rows removed at `public/app.js:6026` before `setPad` at 6029) is unchanged, so if the jump comes back, start there. Closed in the 2026-09-28 prune, harness session 1b4685bd.

issues.name: Looks broken: a rating column narrower than its icons clips the last ones
issues.description:
## What was measured

On :4400, v0.4.43 (commit 689c2b1), Showcase › Field Types at a 1500x900 window, the rating columns open at the default auto width, about 104px, whatever the max. Measured on the first row with `td.getBoundingClientRect().width` against `.wv-rating` `scrollWidth`:

| Field | Max | Column | Icons need | Clipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fit | 5 | 104px | 94px | no |
| Effort | 3 | 104px | 56px | no |
| Love | 7 | 104px | 132px | yes |
| Brightness | 12 | 110px | 227px | yes |

The last hearts and suns are cut at the cell edge, so a 7 of 7 and a 5 of 7 can read the same, and the right-most icons cannot be clicked. Feature #234 (v0.4.43) lifted the max from 10 to 100, so every rating past about 5 icons now opens clipped. Screenshot attached (234-scratch-grid-light.png).

## What good looks like

Airtable and Notion size a rating column to its icons on first draw; a narrower column the reader chose shows a compact `n/max` rather than cutting icons.

## Fix shape

Give the auto-fit (public/column-resize.js, the Feature #233 fit) a rating measure: `max` icons at the cell's icon size plus padding, capped by the auto-fit ceiling. Past the ceiling, or when a person narrows the column, draw the compact `n / max` text with the filled icon, and keep the full row in the hover. Test in `test/rating-browser.test.mjs`: a max-12 column opens unclipped, and a narrowed one shows the compact form.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-26, found while verifying Feature #234 on weave v0.4.43, commit 689c2b1).

![Showcase Field Types: the Love and Brightness columns cut their last icons](/w/weave/api/files/8c5a0d6e-d8f5-497a-80e8-88a9e0ef9b9f)

issues.name: Wrong data: the review gate votes Verified on a patch set it did not run
issues.description:
## Reproduced

Gerrit change 419 (Issue #388), 2026-09-26. Patch set 2 was uploaded at 09:34:37Z and the review poller started its run on it. Patch set 3 was uploaded at 09:39:08Z, while that run was still going. At 09:40:48Z the poller posted **Verified+1 on patch set 3**, carrying the tail of the run it had done over patch set 2's tree. The log it wrote is `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/419-2.log` and its second line names what it tested:

```
merge gate: verifying merged with main @ 483514a5c50941e55568ea2ce1650ba4756f7738
```

There is no `419-3.log`. The two patch sets differ: patch set 3 adds the guard in `public/app.js` that leaves the number Sample empty until the column answers, and one CHANGELOG clause. Patch set 2's tree fails `test/number-display-browser.test.mjs` locally (the case reads the Sample before the stats request lands and sees the example figures); the gate's run of that same tree passed it, because the timing differs under the gate's load. So the vote said green about a tree it did not run, and the tree it did run was one whose behaviour the vote's own log cannot speak for.

The shipping agent caught this and said so in its +2 message, then submitted on its own full-suite run of patch set 3 (2763 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped). Nothing wrong landed. The next change in this position may not be read as carefully: a red patch set 2 and a green patch set 3 uploaded a minute apart would land a -1 on good code, and a green patch set 2 with a broken patch set 3 would land a +1 on broken code.

## Good looks like

A Verified vote names the revision it ran. Gerrit's review endpoint takes the revision id, so the poller can vote on the sha it checked out rather than on `current`; a patch set uploaded mid-run gets its own run.

## Fix shape

* The poller records the revision sha when it starts a run and posts to `/a/changes/<n>/revisions/<sha>/review` instead of `/revisions/current/review`.
* When the change's current revision has moved on since the run started, queue the new patch set rather than letting the stale vote stand as the answer for it.
* Name the run's log after the patch set it ran, which `419-2.log` already does, so the log and the vote cannot point at different patch sets.
* Test: a run whose patch set is superseded mid-flight votes on the sha it ran and leaves the newer patch set unvoted.

Filed by Claude (overnight weave fixer, Issue #388 attempt 1, 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.43, commit 5f4a419). The poller is `scripts/weave-review-serve.mjs` and `scripts/weave-review.sh` in the harness repo, running from `~/.harness-serve`.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:32:32Z

## Fixed (verified 2026-09-28, harness session 1b4685bd)

Already fixed on harness main by PR #270 (2026-09-26, "weave-review: vote on the tested patchset, cap the suite"), after PR #266 pinned each run's fetch to a private ref and checked the SHA. No new change was made here.

- scripts/weave-review.sh reads the current revision once, before any test runs, and pins its SHA, ref and patch set number. It checks the worktree HEAD equals that SHA, and every vote posts to /a/changes/<n>/revisions/<patchset>/review, never revisions/current. Gerrit resolves a patch set number to exactly one revision, and each vote message starts "tested patchset N @ <sha>".
- When the change moved on mid-run, the vote stays on the tested patch set and says "patchset N is no longer current (current is M): this vote records the run on patchset N and does not count toward submit". --submit refuses in that case. The watcher re-lists Gerrit after every gate, so the newer patch set gets its own run.
- Tests: scripts/weave-review.test.mjs, "a patchset superseded mid-run keeps the vote and says it no longer counts" (one POST, to revisions/1, while Gerrit reports patch set 2) and "no vote is ever posted to revisions/current". 6 pass, 0 fail in ~/.harness-serve at 780f485.
- Live evidence, Gerrit change 440 on 2026-09-26: patch set 4 arrived while patch set 3 was gating. The Verified-1 at 20:41Z landed on patch set 3 with the not-current note (review-logs/440-3.log), and patch set 4 got its own run and vote at 21:10Z.

issues.name: Slow: parallel gates have no cap, so load reaches 135 on 10 cores and the p90 gate takes 42 minutes
issues.description:
Measured: the last 120 gate logs in ~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs run a median 4 minutes, p90 42 minutes, max 203 minutes (change 414 patch set 1 took 165). The machine has 10 cores. On the night of 2026-09-25 the load average sat between 89 and 135 with 75 `node --test` processes, because every session and the watcher start `npm test` whenever they like. Timing suites then fail on good changes (see #364, #403) and a serve-boot test hangs (#398), so a red gate costs a rerun.

Gerrit tallied 170 Verified+1 and 28 Verified-1 votes for 48 changes merged since 2026-09-19: about four full gate runs per landed change.

Good looks like a merge queue with one worker per runner (GitHub merge queue, Zuul, Bors): changes wait in line, and each gate runs on an idle machine in its idle time.

Fix shape: take a lock at the top of scripts/weave-review.sh (mkdir lock dir with the PID inside, stale after 30 minutes) so one gate runs at a time and the rest queue; the watcher gates only a patch set that already carries Code-Review+2, and on a stack only the tip.

Filed by the 2026-09-26 deploy-speed review session (harness, weave gerrit/main 5f4a419).

## Status 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd)

It differs from the mkdir shape on purpose: the kernel releases the lock when the holder and its test children exit, so there is no 30-minute stale rule, and a live gate is never stolen. A waiting gate waits and does not vote. The watcher log confirms it runs live: "gate policy: 12 open, targets none (Code-Review+2 stack tips with no Verified vote)".

Left In Progress because the second half changes the landing workflow and was held for Kyle's decision. It is already live. If Kyle approves it, this row can close as Fixed. If not, the change to undo is harness PR #274.

issues.name: Slow: CHANGELOG.md sits in 37 of 48 changes, so Gerrit refuses to auto-rebase and every landing forces a manual rebase and a fresh gate
issues.description:
Measured: 37 of the 48 commits on gerrit/main since 2026-09-19 touch CHANGELOG.md. The weave project refuses Gerrit's automatic rebase when two changes touch the same file (path conflict), so each landing sends every open change back to its session for a hand rebase and a new gate run. GitHub PR #5 needed six rebases over about six hours before it landed as changes 394 to 409.

Good looks like changelog fragments (towncrier, changesets, GitLab's changelogs/unreleased): each change adds its own small file and the release step folds them into CHANGELOG.md, so two changes never edit the same file.

Fix shape: each change writes changelog.d/<Change-Id>.md; the release tagger (weave-release-tags) concatenates the fragments under the new version heading and deletes them in the release commit. A test refuses a change that edits CHANGELOG.md directly outside a release commit.

Filed by the 2026-09-26 deploy-speed review session (harness, weave gerrit/main 5f4a419).

**Fixed 2026-09-26** in Gerrit change 428 (http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/428, commit b071b74, merged as 6008701 on gerrit/main). Each change now writes changelog.d/<short-slug>-<Issue or Feature number>.md and never edits CHANGELOG.md; the release commit runs `node scripts/changelog-fold.mjs`, which moves every fragment (and any `## Unreleased` bullets) under `## v<version>` and deletes the fragments, idempotently. The seven `## Unreleased` bullets moved into fragments in the same change. CLAUDE.md rule 5, a CLAUDE.md house rule and DEVELOPMENT.md "Releasing" say so; the harness tagger needed no change (it reads `## v<version>` sections only). Gate: test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs (7 cases, including a guard that fails a commit adding CHANGELOG.md lines without a package.json version bump). Full gate 2790/2790 pass. issues.name: Looks broken: entity header and document section headers scroll away
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** On an entity page, scrolling a long Description document moves the entity header (title, breadcrumbs, actions) out of view, and the document's own section head (drag handle, caret, DESCRIPTION label, history and copy icons, ⋯ menu; see attached screenshot) scrolls away with its body. Once the reader is a screen into the document, the page no longer says which entity or which section it is showing, and history, copy and the section menu are out of reach.

Code today (`public/style.css`, weave 483514a): `#main > .view-header` is sticky at line 270, but the entity page header is not caught by that selector; `.doc-section-head` (line 1396) has no `position: sticky`. `.doc-rail-track` (line 1350) already sticks at `top: 88px`, so the offset convention exists.

**Good looks like.** Notion and Fibery pin the page title bar, and Fibery pins each rich-text field's header while its body is in view. Linear pins the issue header. The section head hands off to the next section's head as it reaches the top.

**Fix shape.** (1) Entity header: `position: sticky; top: 0` with surface background and z-index above grid heads; publish its height as `--wv-entity-head-h`. (2) `.doc-section-head`: `position: sticky; top: var(--wv-entity-head-h)` inside its `.doc-section`, so it releases when its section ends; opaque background and a hairline only while stuck. (3) Check the dock and the doc rail do not collide; check a collapsed section and nested grids. Browser test: scroll a long Description, assert both heads keep their `getBoundingClientRect().top`.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-09-26 from Kyle's report, weave 0.4.43, serve commit 5f4a419.

## Fixed (2026-09-26)

Landed as 227f778, Gerrit change 423, on weave 0.4.43 (Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md). Deployed to :4400: `/api/health` reports sha 227f778, startedAt 2026-09-26T15:47:05Z, after the 15:45Z submit.

Cause: the full entity page already pinned its header (`#main > .view-header`, Issue #321). The dock, the pose a table row opens into, set `#dock .dock-entity .view-header` to `position: static`, so there the title, breadcrumbs and actions scrolled away. No `.doc-section-head` was sticky anywhere.

Fix: the docked header is sticky at the pane's top edge, and `publishViewHeaderHeight()` writes its height to `--wv-view-h` on `#dock` (the page's reading on the root is unchanged). `.doc-section-head` is sticky at `--wv-view-h` inside its own section on an opaque surface band, z-index 5 (over the heading carets, under the header), so it leaves when the document ends and the next head takes its place. The dash rail pins under the header instead of at a fixed 88px.

Verified on live: Handbook > Fields > document, scrolled to 700 and 1000, entity header top 0 and Description head top 98 at both positions. Gate: `test/sticky-entity-heads-browser.test.mjs` (8 cases, page and dock), red before the fix; full suite 2771 pass, 0 fail.

A container appears once in quick-find: Linear and Notion list a project or database as one result, never also as a row of a system table.

## Fix shape
Skip every registry row whose table is a container registry (workspaces, spaces, tables, views) inside universalSearch, before the limit is applied. Field registry rows have no container hit and stay searchable. Test: `test/search-hierarchy.test.mjs`, "a registry row never shadows its own space or table hit".

issues.name: Wrong data: a new row gets a status even when its field declares no default
issues.description:
## Reproduced

The engine forces a default onto every workflow field: `src/engine.js` ~4114 sets `states[0].default = true` when none is marked, and type conversion (~4553, ~4580) falls back to the default state for an empty value. A new row therefore always carries the first state, and the field dialog notes "the first state is the default — no radio" (~7083).

Kyle, 2026-09-26: "select fields that don't have a blank or default value should not create a value: null (empty) unless otherwise specified".

## What good looks like

A new row's select, multi-select and workflow value is null unless the field declares a default. "Nobody chose" stays distinguishable from "chose the first option", matching the slate-means-unset rule in the chip tiers.

## Fix shape

Engine: drop the implicit states[0] default; keep an explicit default when one is set; conversion of an empty value yields null. Migrate nothing silently: fields whose default was only implied keep behaving as today unless a workspace-level migration is agreed, so test both a field with an explicit default and one without. Contract test in engine suite plus one API create test.
