issues.name: Looks broken: a select chip wider than its column cuts its label mid-letter, with no ellipsis
issues.description:
## Measured
uno › Travel › Points Balances, Program column (select). The chip's text runs past the chip's own fill and the cell cuts it mid-glyph: "Chase Ultimate Re", "Amex Membership", "United MileagePlu". Kyle's screenshot (Safari) is attached.

`td.clientWidth` against the chip `button.k.k-select.chip-trigger`:

| Value | Cell | Chip box | Chip text needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amex Membership Rewards | 124px | 116px | 180px |
| Chase Ultimate Rewards | 124px | 116px | 158px |
| United MileagePlus | 124px | 116px | 126px |
| Alaska Mileage Plan | 124px | 116px | 135px |

Cause:
- `.k` is `display: inline-flex` (`public/style.css:720`), so its label is an anonymous flex item.
- `.wv-grid .k { max-width: 100%; }` (`public/style.css:530`) caps the chip box but leaves `overflow: visible`, so the text spills past the fill.
- `.wv-grid td` sets `text-overflow: ellipsis` (`public/style.css:377`), but ellipsis only applies to a block container's own inline text, never to text inside an inline-flex child. The td clips the spill with no ellipsis.
- The chip's `title` is the field name ("Program"), so hover does not reveal the full value either.

## What good looks like
Airtable and Notion end a long select chip with an ellipsis inside the chip's fill, keep the fill's right padding, and show the full value on hover.

## Fix shape
1. Put the chip's label in a span and give it the relation chip's rule: `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` (the `.k-rel > a > .k-label` rule at `public/style.css:801` already does this for relation chips).
2. Give `.wv-grid .k` `overflow: hidden` so nothing paints past the fill.
3. Set the chip's `title` to the value when the label is truncated.
4. Browser case: a select value longer than its column shows `…` inside the chip, and the label's `scrollWidth > clientWidth` with `text-overflow: ellipsis`. Cover state, multi-select and key chips too, since they share `.k`.

Related: #217 (date cut off with room to spare), #261 (Name column too narrow), #404 (rating icons clipped).

---
Filed by Claude session 2026-09-26 from Kyle's screenshot, weave v0.4.43 @ 227f778 (~/.weave-serve), measured on :4400 in the browser pane, uno › Travel › Points Balances.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (Gerrit salvage of the 09-26 changes), 2026-09-29T04:29:25Z

## Fixed (2026-09-28): landed in the Gerrit salvage of the 09-26 changes

Gerrit change 432, commit d78432e on gerrit/main. Select, state, multi-select and key chips wrap their text in a `.k-label` span that ends in an ellipsis inside the fill; value chips clip at their fill; a cut label marks its cell for the hover expansion and carries the whole value as its title.

During the salvage the rebase also gave the select chip's repaint the label span (a picked value had lost its ellipsis), and relation chips were left out of the clip, because clipping them cut off the mention caret's 24px hit area (Issue #397), which the gate caught in `test/a11y-browser.test.mjs`.

Tests: `test/chip-ellipsis-browser.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases, both themes): 5 of 5 fail on main, 5 of 5 pass; `a11y-browser` "small controls offer a 24px hit area" passes.

Live check: grid chips on the Issue table render `.k > .k-label` with `text-overflow: ellipsis`.

The stack gate is /Users/kyle/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/445-6.log (every case in this change's tree passed; the one red was in cell-color-browser, a file of the still-open change 433).

3. Browser case: a long Source value ends in an ellipsis at rest; an empty date cell shows no placeholder until focused.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T19:30:15Z

## Investigated (2026-09-28, harness session 1b4685bd)

**Where the time went: the server's queue, not the bulk write.** Every request in the report's trace took seconds, including handlers that do almost nothing: `/api/health` 3,323 ms, `/api/workspace` 3,462 ms, `/api/schema` 4 to 20 s, and a field PATCH 26,473 ms. A three-second `/api/health` means requests were waiting behind other work on a starved process. The machine ran load averages of 70 to 135 that day while many sessions gated weave at once. The trace also holds no `POST /api/bulk`. The recorder logs every write when it completes, and its 60-event buffer keeps the newest events, so neither of Kyle's two attempts (87 s and 23 s before he clicked Report) had come back when he filed.

**The bulk path is fast in both versions.** I built a scratch workspace in uno's shape: Product/Task field for field, 104 rows, the Standard view's six columns and its State = Open filter, and about 2,300 rows across 17 tables. On a scratch server I ran Set a field, State, Done on eight selected rows, timed inside the page from the click until the eight rows had left the grid and the toast was up:

| Build | Chromium | Chromium, record docked | WebKit | WebKit, record docked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.4.43 (689c2b1) | 44 ms | 79 ms | 162 ms | settled; the in-page clock missed it (371 ms wall, harness overhead included) |
| v0.4.51 (f34f90c) | 85 ms | 44 ms | 67 ms | 174 ms |

Each run made exactly two requests: one `POST /api/bulk` (7 to 113 ms) and one page re-read. There was no schema reload and no per-row write. On a copy of uno's own database, the engine ran `bulk(8 ids, set State)` in 18 ms and the Open-filtered re-read in 2 ms. The live `:4400` now answers uno's schema in 26 ms and the Task page query in 3 ms, at a machine load of about 32.

**Guard landed.** `test/bulk-settle-browser.test.mjs` fixes the client side of this gesture at one bulk write, one re-read, no schema reload, no per-row PATCH, and settled within 600 ms of the click. It fails when the bulk is replaced by a per-row PATCH loop and passes on main in Chromium and WebKit. Gerrit change 475.

**Looks broken and Error.** The report cannot identify either one. The trace records 0 errors and has no screenshot, and the recorder never keeps field values. The closest real finding is new Issue #464: opening a table in WebKit raises "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications." as a window error, and the bug recorder files it. That is not what Kyle saw, because his trace would have kept that error.

**Not fixed here:** the load itself. The weave server shares the machine with the gates. A saturated machine makes every request wait in that queue, the bulk included.

## Landed (2026-09-28)
Gerrit change 475, sha 017f21c on gerrit/main, deployed to `:4400` (health reports 017f21c). The change adds a test and a release-notes fragment (`changelog.d/bulk-settle-426.md`) and no product code, because the gesture was already fast. Patch set 3 went Verified+1 on the full suite with browser suites. Patch set 2 went Verified-1 at load 235 on unrelated browser suites; the new test passed in that run too.

Verified against the deployed checkout on a scratch server: Chromium settled in 91 ms (bulk 70 ms), WebKit in 75 ms (bulk 37 ms), with two requests each: one bulk write and one page re-read.

Status set to Fixed, on the grounds that the bulk path meets the budget and a guard now holds it there. The server starvation behind the original wait is the machine's load and is not a weave code defect. Follow-up: Issue #464 (WebKit ResizeObserver error in bug traces).

issues.description:
Reproduced in the workflow field editor (state options list). Each state row shows a colour swatch that is disabled. Hovering it shows the tooltip "Colour comes from the not-started category". Open, In progress and Review all take the fixed hue of their category, and nothing lets you pick another.

Source: public/app.js:7125-7133. The swatch renders as `opt-color locked`, `disabled: true`, hue from `chipCore.categoryHue(cat)`. The comment there states the intent: a state's colour belongs to its category so status means the same thing in every table.

Kyle's call: the category hue stays the default, but the colour must be changeable per state. Two states in the same category (for example Review and In progress) currently look identical.

Good looks like: Linear, Jira and Fibery all seed a state's colour from its category and let you override it from the same swatch picker that single-select options use.

Fix shape: store an optional `color` on the state; render the swatch as the normal option colour picker; fall back to `categoryHue(cat)` when `color` is unset; offer a "Reset to category colour" entry in the picker. Chips, board columns and the state preview read `s.color ?? categoryHue(cat)`. Check that PUT /api/schema keeps the new key (Issue #59 was option colours being dropped on save).

Filed by harness session 1b824985 on 2026-09-26, weave 0.4.43, commit 227f778 (~/.weave-serve). Logged only; no fix started, per Kyle.



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-06T20:02:51.660Z · session 1202-5753 · from #552, #431

**Repro:** Confirmed on :4400 at 144b79d. Open any table's add-field tray and pick workflow: the four state rows each draw a swatch that is disabled, so clicking it does nothing. Two states in the same category are still indistinguishable. Separately, and contrary to what the fix shape assumes is missing, the colour picker this row wants already exists and works: on a select field, clicking an option's swatch opens the ten-hue grid, hosted in a .chip-pop, with the current hue carrying sel. So the picker is not the work; unlocking the state swatch and persisting the choice is.

**Code:**
- public/app.js:6212-6216 — stateListEditor builds the swatch as opt-color locked with disabled: true and hue from chipCore.categoryHue(cat). This is the button to unlock.
- public/app.js:6040 huePopover(anchor, current, onPick), already called at public/app.js:6121 as the onclick on a select option's swatch. Reuse that call shape; it needs a tenth entry or a separate control for "Reset to category colour", since the grid's slate swatch means the slate hue, not "inherit".
- src/engine.js:457-459 — THE BLOCKER, and the Issue #59 failure mode this row warns about. normalizeSelfContainedConfig rebuilds every state as a fresh object with exactly { id, name, category, default, icon? }. A color key on an incoming state is silently dropped on every save, so the UI would appear to work and lose the colour on reload. Fix here first.
- src/engine.js:273-280 normaliseOption is the pattern to copy: it keeps hue and color on a select option and derives color from HUE_HEX[hue].
- src/engine.js:6946 re-emits states as { id, name, category, default, icon? } for the schema output, so it needs the key too, as does src/applet.js:82 which projects only { id, name, category }.
- Six call sites compute a state chip's colour independently as hue-${chipCore.categoryHue(cat)}: public/app.js:1166, 2271, 6067 (statePreview), 6147, 9847, 10170. Every one of them has to read s.color ?? categoryHue(cat), or the tray will disagree with the grid, the board and the entity page.
- src/handbook.js:356 documents states as [{ name, category, default, icon }] and src/handbook.js:1106 says outright that a state's category colours its chip. Both are wrong once this lands and must be edited in the same change.

**Fix shape:** The row's shape stands, but the order matters: extend the engine normalizer and the schema emitters to carry an optional color first, with a round-trip test, then unlock the swatch and wire the existing huePopover, then move all six chip call sites onto s.color ?? categoryHue(cat), then the Handbook. This is a schema-shape change across the engine, the UI and the docs, not a tray tweak, which is why this run left it rather than start it inside its budget.

**Test to write first:**
- An engine test that a workflow state's color survives createField, a PUT /api/schema round trip, a field rename and an export/import, which is the Issue #59 guard and is red today because engine.js:459 drops the key.
- A browser case over both themes: pick a colour on one state, assert the row swatch, the state preview, the grid chip and the board column header all take it, and that a second state in the same category keeps the category hue.
- A browser case that "Reset to category colour" clears the stored color and returns the chip to categoryHue(cat), and that the reset is one undoable step through the field config Undo the tray routes through (Issues #428, #467).

issues.name: Wrong data: field config changes save with no Undo toast and leave no Activity entry to roll back from
issues.description:
Any change to a field's configuration (options, state list, colours, type, formula, format, width, definition) saves silently. No toast confirms it, no Undo is offered, and the change is not recorded in Activity. A mistaken edit to a shared field has no way back except rebuilding it by hand.

Measured: the only field-config action with an Undo today is clearing a field definition (public/app.js:3226-3231, `toast(..., { label: 'Undo', run: () => patch(def) })`). Activity (src/engine.js:415-418) is per-entity and its kinds are created, field-updated, state-changed, relation-updated, doc-updated, doc-appended, comment-added, file-attached, automation-ran and undo. There is no kind for a schema or field-config change.

Kyle's requirement: every field config update, once it completes, (1) shows a toast with Undo and (2) is registered in the Activity table so it can be rolled back later, not only inside the toast's lifetime.

Good looks like: Airtable and Notion record field edits in the base or page history with a restore action; Linear shows an Undo toast for every settings change.

Fix shape: one write path for field config that captures the before and after definition. On success it appends an Activity entry (new kind, e.g. `field-config-updated`, holding table, field, before, after, seq) and shows `toast('<Field> updated', false, { label: 'Undo', run: () => apply(before) })`. The Undo itself writes an `undo` Activity entry. An Activity row for a config change offers "Roll back", which applies `before` after checking the field has not changed since (seq). Related: #259 (row trash had no Undo), #59 (schema PUT dropping option colours).

Filed by harness session 1b824985 on 2026-09-26, weave 0.4.43, commit 227f778 (~/.weave-serve). Logged only; no fix started, per Kyle.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28T20:04:32Z

## Fixed 2026-09-28: Gerrit change 477, merged c249bc0

**What landed.** `updateField` is the one write path for a field's configuration, and every door goes through it: the field tray, `PATCH /api/tables/:t/fields/:f`, the `Definition` on a `Workspace/Fields` row, `applySchema`, the CLI and MCP. A change it makes appends a `field-config-updated` entry to the workspace's audit log (the existing archive of structural work, no new table) holding the table, the field, the definition before and after, the keys that changed and an activity `seq`. `activityFeed` and `getActivity` read those entries back as the table's own Activity rows, id `<tableId>:f<n>`, so they show in the Activity table with the table as their record and survive a restart. The fields of a table that `applySchema` creates are not recorded; a system table is not recorded.

Saving in the field tray shows the existing toast, `<Field> updated`, with Undo. An entry's own page in Activity shows the two definitions and a Roll back button. Undo and Roll back are the same verb, `rollbackFieldConfig`: it applies the definition before through the same path and writes an `undo` entry naming the entry it reversed (which can itself be rolled back). It refuses when a later entry exists for the field or the definition no longer matches the entry's after, and the page and the toast say why instead of applying. The Definition modal on a registry row gets an Undo toast too. New doors: `POST /api/tables/:t/fields/:f/rollback {activity}` (under `/fields`, so it takes the rung the schema write takes: a writer token gets 403), `weave_rollback_field`, `weave field rollback <table> <field> --activity <id>`. The PATCH answer carries the entry id as `activity`. Handbook guide "Making a workspace your own" has a new section, "Taking a field change back"; AGENTS.md documents the history and the doors.

**What Undo and Roll back restore.**
- Options, option colours, states, formula, number and date format, default, description, rating scale, toggle labels and the field's name: the definition, in full. Stored values are not touched by these changes, so nothing else needs restoring.
- Removing a select option or a workflow state: the rows that held it keep its id, so restoring the definition brings their values back as well. Measured in the test "removing an option and rolling it back brings the stored values back".
- A type change: the migration converts every stored value to the new type and keeps no copy of the old ones. The entry records the definition before and after and is marked `lossy`, but it offers no Undo and no Roll back; the toast says "Its values were converted, so this change has no Undo" and links to the entry. Restoring the values would need a per-row snapshot at migration time, which is a product decision (see below).
- Column width: not recorded and not toasted. In the grid a width is a view setting saved under the autosave ruling (Feature #233); only a registry grid, which has no views, still writes it onto the field.

**Open questions for Kyle.**
1. Should a type change snapshot the stored values of every row so its Undo can restore them? That makes it undoable but stores one value per row per type change.
2. Width is left out as a view setting. Confirm that resizing a column (including on a registry grid) should stay silent.

**Tests.** `test/field-config-activity.test.mjs` (15: the entry and its seq, no-op and width, rename and description, roll back and its undo entry, stale by a later entry, stale by a silent write, lossy type change, option values coming back, formula/workflow/number, registry door, applySchema, system table, reopen, HTTP door with the writer 403 and the 409, MCP and CLI) and `test/field-config-undo-browser.test.mjs` (6, light and dark: toast with Undo and Undo restores, Activity entry offers Roll back and it rolls back, a stale roll back refuses and keeps the newer change). Both red before the change (13 of 15 and 6 of 6), green after. Gate: Verified +1 on patchset 3 (review log 477-3.log), submitted. Deployed: `:4400` `/api/health` reports sha c249bc0.


## Kyle's rulings on the open questions, recorded 2026-09-29T02:42:58Z

1. **Column resize stays silent.** Confirmed as built: resizing a column records no field-config history and shows no toast, because a width is a view setting. This covers the registry grids that have no views as well. No code change.
2. **A type change must be undoable, values included.** Kyle asked for a per-row snapshot so that Undo and Roll back restore the definition and every stored value. That work is its own Issue row (filed next, referencing this one); this row stays Fixed as shipped in v0.4.52.

issues.name: Looks broken: a column dragged back across the frozen seam keeps auto-scrolling after the pointer leaves the edge band
issues.description:
## Measured
`test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs` "drop across the seam freezes; drop back across unfreezes; widths hold both ways" is timing-dependent. On untouched gerrit/main 227f778 it went red 1 of 4 standalone runs (`node --test --test-name-pattern="drop across the seam" test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs`); on change 431 (Name default 260, Issues #261/#414) red 2 of 5. The failing assertion is the unfreeze drop's order: `['Name','Description','Owner','Status']` where the case wants `['Name','Description','Status','Owner']`.

Instrumented run on main (1100x900 viewport, Owner frozen first, Status scrolled to centre, drag from Owner to Status.right - 10 in 8 steps):

- before the drag: wrap 344..1064, scrollLeft 479, Owner 441..621 (the seam, so the left auto-scroll band is x 621..669), Status 642..766, target x 756;
- one pointer step lands at about x 647, inside the band;
- read with the pointer resting at x 756, outside the band: scrollLeft 407, Status 714..838, insertion line at 713, so the drop lands before Status.

The grid scrolled 72px (about nine 8px ticks) and kept going after the pointer left the 48px band. `columnDrag`'s `tick` (public/app.js, the `EDGE = 48` block) recomputes `lo` from `boxes()[fz - 1].right` every frame; if the grabbed frozen column stops being sticky while it is held, `lo` moves right with every scroll step and the band follows the pointer. That is a hypothesis from the numbers, not yet confirmed.

## What good looks like
A column drag auto-scrolls only while the pointer sits in the edge band and stops the frame it leaves, so the drop lands where the line was when the pointer arrived.

## Fix shape
1. Read the seam once at drag start, or from the frozen zone's stored width rather than the grabbed header's live box.
2. In the case, take the target after the drag reaches it, or step the pointer so no intermediate step lands in the band.

---
Filed by the Issue #414 session (Claude, 2026-09-26), while gating Gerrit change 431 on gerrit/main 227f778.

## Fixed, 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd, high-severity batch): the case, not the product

Landed in Gerrit change 483 (5df7e50); deployed, :4400 reports sha fa176b9.

**The product stops scrolling when the pointer leaves the band.** Probe on fa176b9, the same grid (1100 px wide, Owner frozen, Status scrolled to the centre), pointer held on Owner: moved into the band at seam + 20 px and held 300 ms, scrollLeft went 519 to 329; moved out to seam + 200 px, scrollLeft stayed 329 at 50 ms and still 329 one second later. Owner's right edge stayed at 621 throughout, so `lo` in `columnDrag`'s `tick` does not move. Same result with `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE=4`. The hypothesis above is not what happens.

**What made the case red.** Two things, both in the test. The drag path crosses the left auto-scroll band on its way to Status, and the grid scrolls for as long as the pointer dwells there, which is longer on a loaded machine, so a target read before the drag is stale when the pointer lands. And every drop plays a 180 ms slide of every cell (`flip`), which the helper's fixed 200 ms wait did not cover under load: in the gate and under `taskpolicy -b`, a frozen Owner measured 19 to 447 px off its pin.

**Fix.** `drag()` in `test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs` waits for the grid's animations to finish after the drop, and the unfreeze drag re-aims at Status once the pointer has arrived. Red 2 of 2 alone under `taskpolicy -b` before, green 2 of 2 after; green in ten of ten full suites and two back-to-back runs.

issues.name: Slow: filter and search leave the table looking finished while it reloads, inviting double clicks
issues.description:
Reproduced on table views. A filter chip lights up the moment you click it, but the grid keeps showing the old rows until the refetch lands. The search box behaves the same way. With no sign that work is in flight, you cannot tell whether the selected filters have loaded, and you click again. That second click toggles the filter back off.

Measured: the filter waits FILTER_DEBOUNCE 250 ms (public/app.js:3901), then setTableFilters plus onChange refetch (app.js:3910-3920). Search waits TABLE_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE 150 ms (app.js:3962), then setTableSearch. A filtered query on Issue (413 rows) took 0.40, 0.65 and 0.52 s over curl on 2026-09-26, before render. The weave rope loader (withPageLoader, app.js:11475, shown after LOADER_SHOW_AFTER_MS 500 ms) runs only on route changes (app.js:427, 624, 11641), never on an in-table refetch.

Kyle's requirement: while a filter, search or visibility change is loading, show the weave loading animation over the table, so you know the new selection is loading rather than done, and so you do not double click when a refetch runs slower than expected.

Good looks like: Linear and Airtable dim the grid and show a progress indicator in place until the new rows land; the old rows never pass for the result.

Fix shape: a table-scoped loader, reusing the rope and its 500 ms threshold, that covers the grid area (not the filter strip) from the chip click or keystroke until the redraw completes. Dim the stale rows under it (aria-busy on the grid). Keep chips clickable, but coalesce clicks made during a flush into the next one so a second click is never lost or doubled. Related open loader rows: #390 (rope freezes when the page is busy), #394 (reduced motion and screen readers). Related speed row: #269 (fixed: chip clicks refetch the whole table).

Filed by harness session 1b824985 on 2026-09-26, weave 0.4.43, commit 227f778 (~/.weave-serve). Logged only; no fix started, per Kyle.

**Fixed 2026-09-27 in v0.4.50 (commit 248dd00, Gerrit http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/461).** `gridHold()` holds the grid of the table on screen until the change's rows are drawn. While anything holds it, the grid body (`#main > .table-wrap`, never the toolbar) is dimmed to 50% and carries `aria-busy="true"` at once. Past `LOADER_SHOW_AFTER_MS` (500 ms) the weave rope, cloned from `#page-loader`, sits over the part of the grid in view and finishes its cycle, as the page loader does. Holds are taken at the chip click and the keystroke (before the 250 ms and 150 ms debounces), at each field flip, at Reset view, and around every same-table refetch in `showDatabase`. A filter burst keeps its hold until the last flush on the chain has drawn, so a chip clicked during a slow re-read is kept rather than lost.

Measured by `test/table-patch-browser.test.mjs` (new), query held 1200 ms: at 120 ms the grid is `aria-busy` and dimmed, the header is not, and no rope shows; at 620 ms the grid rope shows and the page rope stays down; a second chip clicked during the held read lands, and the table saves `{ Status: ['Done', 'Doing'] }` with only Done and Doing rows drawn. A fast search never shows the rope and leaves nothing busy. Before the fix the slow case failed at its first assertion: nothing marked the grid busy.

Verification: Gerrit 461 Verified +1 (2877 tests, 0 skipped), merged; :4400 serves sha 248dd00, v0.4.50, startedAt 2026-09-27T21:22:43Z. Probe numbers attached as issue-444-probe-before-after.txt. Related, still open: #390 (rope freezes on a busy main thread) and #394 (reduced motion and screen readers).

Filed by the Issue #444/#433 fix session (Claude Code, harness), 2026-09-27, weave v0.4.50, commit 248dd00.

issues.name: Slow: concurrent review gates overload the Mac and stall Weave CI
issues.description:
Measured 2026-09-26 12:24 PDT: load averages 96.90 / 93.40 / 88.65; 84 Chromium processes; several overlapping full suites; one orphan full suite running nearly 14 hours. Shared checkout scripts/weave-review.sh was stale: it lacked the lock, exact revision voting and suite cap already landed on harness main. Agents invoked this old path while launchd invoked ~/.harness-serve. Existing mkdir lock could also evict a live holder after one hour.

issues.name: A table query by qualified name 404s: %2F is percent-decoded before routing, so /api/tables/Product%2FTask/query never matches
issues.description:
## Reproduced

On :4400 at 2026-09-27T15:12Z, against the uno workspace:

```
POST /w/uno/api/tables/Product%2FTask/query   {"limit":1}
  → 404 {"error":"No route: POST /api/tables/Product/Task/query"}

POST /w/uno/api/tables/Task/query             {"limit":1}
  → 200 {"total":104, ...}

POST /w/uno/api/tables/Product.Task/query     {"limit":1}
  → 404 {"error":"Table 'Product.Task' not found","code":"not-found"}
```

The error text echoes the path with a literal slash, so the percent-encoded `%2F` is decoded into a path separator before the route matcher runs. The segment count then changes and no route matches. Only the bare table name works.

`GET /w/uno/api/tables` lists each table with both a `name` (`Task`) and a `qualified` (`Product/Task`). A caller that reads the listing and passes the `qualified` value back, correctly percent-encoded, gets a 404 for a table that exists.

## Who this broke

The daily-brief routine read uno `Product/Task` this way and its run at 2026-09-27T13:32Z logged the source as red with "fetch failed". Uno product tasks were missing from the brief Kyle received (thread 1a0e31130d27dc64). The routine had no way to tell a decoding defect from a table that is gone.

## What good looks like

A qualified name is the identifier the API hands out, so the API should accept it back. Either the route decodes the segment after matching, or the listing stops offering `qualified` as an addressable id.

## Fix shape

1. Match the route on the raw, still-encoded path segment, then decode that one segment as a table key.
2. Resolve a table key against both `name` and `qualified`.
3. A table key that resolves to nothing returns the existing `not-found` body, never `No route`, so a caller can tell a bad name from a bad URL.

---

issues.name: Looks broken: rows stretch past their density height (45 to 70px at Comfortable)
issues.description:
Measured 2026-09-27 on the :4400 server (weave main 483514a), every table in the weave workspace, rows painted in the viewport, spacer rows excluded.

| Table | Comfortable | Compact | Tallest cell content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guide, Issue, Feature and 20 others | 47 | 33 | .doc-preview, 28px |
| Views, Fields (system) | 45 | 31 | .sel-hit checkbox, 26px |
| Tables, Spaces (system) | 45 to 49 in one grid | 31 to 35 | .text-dressed block, 30px (4px padding around a 20px line) |
| Icons | 70 | 56 | a compact .wv-card inside a computed cell, 47px |

Row height is the tallest cell plus two --wv-row-pad plus a 1px rule, so any renderer taller than 20px sets the row. The grid windows its rows from ONE measured height per table and density (Issue #324), so a grid that mixes 45 and 49 places its window from the wrong height, and the density flip anchor (Issue #342, #413) inherits the error. grid-chrome gates the 48/34 caps against seeded rows that never hold a card, a block text value or a doc preview, so it passes.

Peer tools: Airtable row height is a fixed track per setting (short, medium, tall, extra tall); a cell never grows its row, long text truncates or clamps to the lines the setting allows, and the full value opens in an expanded cell.

Fix shape: the row height becomes a declared token per density, never a measured one. Every cell renders into one clip box of that height; each field type has a row form per density (one line, or two at the tallest setting); overflow keeps the existing clipped marker and cell pop. Windowing reads the token. A browser gate seeds one field of every type with worst-case values and asserts every row equals the token at each density. Design: the density mockups artifact from this session.

issues.name: Looks broken: every toolbar change tears down and redraws the whole page, so the table flickers
issues.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-27: "You can see flickering table when changes are made. This must be diagnosed and fixed everywhere, for search and all other changes."

Root cause from code: search, filter, view, density, field visibility and field order all end in `showDatabase` → `drawDatabase` (public/app.js:4467 on cb73586), which starts with `main.replaceChildren()` and rebuilds the breadcrumb, title, description, toolbar, header row and every visible row from scratch. Between the clear and the rebuild the browser can paint an empty or partial frame; icons re-run their entry motion; the open popover is torn down and re-anchored; the search box is recreated and has its caret restored by hand (app.js:4469-4471, 4553-4557). A one-row visibility toggle costs the same as a route change.

Kyle's recording shows the flash on search and on field changes. It also shows Issue rows at 65 to 74px while density reads Comfortable, which is Issue #440.

Good looks like: Airtable and Linear keep the chrome mounted and patch only the grid body; a filter change swaps rows in place, a hidden field removes one column, and the toolbar never repaints.

Fix shape: split the table page into chrome (breadcrumb, title, description, toolbar) that is drawn once per route, and a grid body that is patched. Each control declares what it touches: search, filter and view swap rows; visibility and order patch columns; density changes one token. Measure before and after with a PerformanceObserver long-task log and a MutationObserver count of replaced nodes on the toolbar (target zero). A browser case records frames during a search and fails if any frame paints an empty #main.

Pending state is Issue #433: the impacted region only (grid body, not the toolbar) dims and marks aria-busy at once, and the weave loader shows over it only past the 500 ms threshold.

Filed by the 2026-09-27 toolbar review session (Claude Code, harness), against weave v0.4.45, served commit cb73586. Source: Kyle's 9:10 AM feedback on Feature #237 plus his screen recording.

**Fixed 2026-09-27 in v0.4.50 (commit 248dd00, Gerrit http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/461).** Root cause confirmed and sharpened: every control ended in `drawDatabase`'s `main.replaceChildren()`. The visible flash came from the description, which re-rendered off `/markdown` and sat blank for that round trip, so the grid jumped up and back. A view switch also went through the route skeleton, and the sidebar was rebuilt on every redraw.

Fix: `tableChrome()` builds the breadcrumb, title, description and toolbar once per table. `drawDatabase` swaps only the grid body under it, in one task, and rebuilds the chrome only when the table's name, icon, description, space or row term changes or the reader arrives from another page. Controls read the view through a live ref; view and density labels and the filter count update in place. `renderRoute` skips the skeleton for another view of the table on screen, and `showDatabase` leaves the sidebar alone on a same-table redraw. Density still patches its token without a redraw.

Measured by `test/table-patch-browser.test.mjs` (new), 60-row table with a description, `/markdown` held 120 ms:

| Action | Bad frames before → after | Header nodes removed before → after | Tracked controls replaced before → after | Grid jumps before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Search | 8 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| Filter chip | 8 → 0 | 83 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| View switch | 7 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| Reset view | 8 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| Density | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Field hide | 8 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| Field reorder | 16 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| Add field | 8 → 0 | 82 → 0 | 8 → 0 | 1 → 0 |

The search input keeps its node, focus and caret; the open Filters and Fields popovers keep their nodes. Left open: after a view-config write, `loadSchema` still redraws the sidebar (48 to 96 nav nodes per action), outside the table viewport. Visibility and order swap the whole grid body in one task rather than patching single columns; no frame shows it.

## Good looks like

A browser case waits on the condition it asserts (waitForFunction on the computed style or the class), never on a fixed timeout, so a busy machine only makes it slower.

## Fix shape

## Update 2026-09-27, gate PS3 (load 5.3)

Each gate run turns a different set of timing-sensitive cases red, which is the load signature, not a regression. The rails case counts 250 ms timers across two animation frames; under load a second frame boundary lets a second reschedule in. The seam drop case reads the header's pinned offset right after the drop.



## Update 2026-09-28, change 471 PS1 (load 4.0)

Gerrit change 471 (Issue #455, the slash menu; it touches public/app.js in the document editor, public/editor-lib.js and src/handbook.js, nothing in the grid) drew Verified-1 on patchset 1 at f34f90c: "the block anchor is the row grip" (entity-block-grip-browser, red twice: "a keyboard focus lights the grip") and grid-layout-browser, red twice on two different cases ("drop across the seam freezes": "the frozen header is pinned beside #", then "system columns reorder, freeze and step like fields": "and back past the last field"). Change 479 is the v0.4.52 release commit: package.json, CHANGELOG.md, the changelog.d fragments, docs/development.json and the architecture map, with no code change. The gate reuses `479-1.log` for a re-gate, so that file now holds the second run, not the first.

Raised to High on 2026-09-28 on Kyle's decision. On that day this flake voted Verified -1 on good patch sets of Gerrit changes 473, 475, 476, 478 and 479; each file passed three runs of three alone, on main and on the change. Raised by harness session 1b4685bd.

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-29T02:45:48Z

## Fixed, 2026-09-28 (harness session 1b4685bd, high-severity batch)

Landed as Gerrit change 483 (5df7e50), stacked under change 437 (fa176b9, Issue #398). One gate, `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/437-5.log`, Verified +1. Deployed: :4400 `/api/health` reports sha fa176b9. No version bump; the note is `changelog.d/gate-browser-lane-454.md`.

**Root cause: the suite starved itself.** Measured on gerrit/main 1079b88 with an outside load of 3: `node --test` ran nine files at once (cores minus one), 130 of the 301 test files drive a Chromium, and at the peak the run held 33 Chromium processes and 11 Node processes and drove the load average to 27 on its own. That run went red on "+ New on a filtered view" before the retry, so the reds were not other sessions' load: they came from the suite. The cases that went red all read a value a fixed sleep after an action (a CSS fade, a transition, a scroll handler, a write), and nine browsers at once stretched those sleeps past what they covered.

**Fix, part 1: a browser lane.** `scripts/test.mjs` runs the files that do not drive a browser first, at node's default, then the browser suites in their own lane at half the cores (5 on this machine). Both lanes always run and each has its own retry. A caller's own `--test-concurrency` wins.

**Fix, part 2: the cases wait for what they assert.** `test/lib/browser.mjs` gains `styleOf` (waits for a computed style), `settled` (waits for a subtree's animations to finish) and `eventually` (polls a Node-side read), plus `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE=4`, which slows every page fourfold through CDP and reproduces a gate-only red on a quiet machine.

| Case | Cause | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |

| table-views "every row: a drag handle…" | row buttons fade, read at once after focus | `styleOf` |

| doc-rail "a burst of resize events…" | four layers share the 250 ms debounce; code colouring polls on it until highlight.js loads | counts the rails' own timers |
| chip "the retract caret faces the text…" | read 250 ms after the click | `settled` |
| entity-eye-sync "a flip updates the popover in place" | pop-in animation measured, 69 vs 65 | `settled` |
| hold-release "a hold carried to the end fires the delete" and the early releases | hold timed by sleeps in Node | timed on the fill's transition, sweep at quarter speed for an early release, delete read back |
| field-menu "the hold still gates the delete" | same | same |
| table-toolbar hidden-field move and grip drag | engine read before the write landed | `eventually` |
| frozen-id-column "the seam appears only once…" | read 80 ms after scrolling | waits for the colour |
| bulk-settle 600 ms budget | none in the test; the budget held in every run with the lane | unchanged |

Tests for the runner: `test/test-runner.test.mjs` gains the lane split, the lane cap, both lanes running past a red, and the Issue #435 discovery guard.
**Evidence: ten full suites in a row, 2026-09-28 20:52 to 21:38 PDT.** `npm test` exactly as the gate runs it (non-TTY, tap), in a worktree at 7773846, which is change 483 on gerrit/main 92e78a2 and differs from the landed 5df7e50 only in one test comment and the changelog wording. Outside load at each start 9.5 to 27.5 (one-minute average), peak during the runs 20 to 38. Result: 10 of 10 green, 0 failed cases, 0 retries. Wall time 276 to 297 s: the unit lane 37 to 40 s, the browser lane 237 to 255 s. Peak under the run: 22 to 24 Chromium processes, 13 to 15 Node processes.

**Before and after, back to back, 21:38 to 21:57.** gerrit/main 92e78a2 against 92e78a2 plus 483 and 437 (fa176b9), alternating, outside load 12 to 17 at each start:

| Run | Outside load at start | Wall | Peak Chromium processes | Red before the retry |

| fix | 12.4 | 281 s | 22 | none |

**Cost.** The gate is about 54 s longer at this load, 227 s to 281 s (+24%), because the browser lane runs five files at a time instead of nine and the unit lane no longer overlaps it. The first measurement of main at an outside load of 3 took 254 s including a 20 s retry of the same case. A false -1 costs a new patch set and a whole second gate of about 230 s, so the lanes pay for themselves once one gate in four would have voted -1 falsely; on 2026-09-28 change 476 alone took five.

**Not covered.** The gate that landed this change retried two other files, `doc-autosave-phone-browser` (a 400 ms request budget) and `field-definition-browser` (a hold timed by sleeps). Both are filed: Issues #476 and #475.

issues.name: Looks broken: a slash command on a line with text inserts a placeholder block and leaves the text unformatted
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

Kyle, 2026-09-28: type a line of text in a document, then run a slash command on that line (Heading, Task list). The existing text is pushed aside and stays as body text. The command's block appears with its placeholder, and the line Kyle wrote is not reformatted.

Code trace at v0.4.51 (commit 1607208), `public/app.js`:

- `slashItems()` (line 9395) gives every block command a fixed string: `# Heading` (9403, 9407), `- List item` (9409), `1. List item` (9410), `- [ ] To do` (9411), `> Quote` (9412), `Text` (9406).
- `slashHint()` (line 9540) hands that string to Vditor as the hint `value`. Vditor inserts it at the caret in place of `/query`. Nothing reads the text already on the line.
- Format commands already take the writer's text: `wrap()` (9396) uses the remembered selection. Block commands have no equivalent.

So `Buy milk /task` ends as the text `Buy milk` plus a new `- [ ] To do` item, where the writer wanted `- [ ] Buy milk`.

## What good looks like

Notion, Fibery and Linear treat a block command on a line with text as "turn this line into": the text stays and the block type changes. `Buy milk` + `/task` gives `- [ ] Buy milk`. `## Plan` + `/task` gives `- [ ] Plan`. `- [ ] Plan` + `/h2` gives `## Plan`. The placeholder appears only on an empty line.

## Fix shape

1. Line-prefix commands (Text, Heading 1 to 6, Bulleted list, Numbered list, Task list, Quote) convert the current line when it has text besides the `/query`. Strip the line's existing block marker (`#` run, `-`, `1.`, `- [ ]`, `- [x]`, `>`), keep inline marks, apply the new marker. Text converts back to a plain paragraph.
2. An empty line keeps today's behaviour: marker plus placeholder.
3. Insert-only blocks (Code block, Mermaid, Table, Divider, Image, Raw HTML, references) stay inserts.
4. The marker path already exists: `DEFERRED_INSERTS` and `REF_MARKER_RE` are swapped in the editor's `input` handler (line 9780). A block marker can ride the same path, with the line rewrite done on the markdown and the caret restored to the end of the converted line.
5. Red cases first in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`: paragraph to task, heading to task, task to heading, paragraph to quote, empty line still gets the placeholder, text before and after the caret both survive, list indent survives.

Filed by the harness session weave-commands-existing-text-da4bd5 on 2026-09-28, weave v0.4.51, commit 1607208.



## Fixed 2026-09-28

Gerrit change 471 (http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/471), commit f34f90c on gerrit/main, landed 2026-09-28 15:42 UTC. Text, Heading 1 to 6, Bulleted list, Numbered list, Task list and Quote convert the line they are typed on; an empty line keeps its prefix and placeholder; every other block still inserts. The conversion runs from a MutationObserver as the marker lands, so the marker is never painted and never reaches the undo stack. Tests: test/slash-convert-line.test.mjs (18 cases) and 14 browser cases in test/slash-commands.test.mjs; gate 2956 of 2956. Verified on :4400 at f34f90c (started 2026-09-28T15:42:37Z) on a scratch row in the test workspace, 9 of 9 checks. Version is still 0.4.51: the fix ships with the next release, so Fixed in is empty until that Release row exists. Seen along the way: Issues #456 and #457.

issues.name: Looks broken: a Raw HTML or reference command shows its marker for 800 ms, and the first undo brings the marker back
issues.description:
## What was reproduced Type `First words`, Enter, `/raw html`, Enter, at v0.4.51 (commit 1607208). - The editing surface reads `First words⁣raw-html⁣` straight after Enter: the two U+2063 characters are invisible, the word `raw-html` between them is not. The marker left the document 821 ms later. - After the block settled (`First words\n\n
html
`), one undo gave `First words\n\n⁣raw-html⁣`, and 1.5 s later the document was `
html
` again. The second undo went back to `First words`. - `/entity`, `/link table` and `/space` ride the same path, so the picker opens about 800 ms after Enter and the first undo after a pick restores `ref:entity` and reopens the picker. Cause, in `public/app.js` and the vendored Vditor: - `DEFERRED_INSERTS` and `REF_MARKER_RE` are swapped in the editor's `input` handler. - Vditor's IR mode calls `options.input` from a `setTimeout` of `options.undoDelay` (800 ms, the default; weave does not set it), and the same timer callback then calls `undo.addToUndoStack`. The swap is queued as a microtask, so the undo stack records the surface while the marker is still in it. ## What good looks like The block appears when Enter is pressed, the picker opens when Enter is pressed, and undo goes from the inserted block to the text before the command. ## Fix shape Issue #455 (Gerrit change 471) added `watchBlockMarkers()`: a MutationObserver on the editing surface that converts a block marker in the same task it lands, before Vditor's timer, so the marker is never painted and never reaches the undo stack (`test/slash-commands.test.mjs`, case "convert: undo goes back to what was typed, never to the marker"). Move the Raw HTML swap and the reference hand-off onto that observer and keep the `input` handler checks as the net under it. Red cases first: the surface text straight after Enter holds no `raw-html`, and `vditor.undo.ir.lastText` never holds U+2063. --- Filed by the harness session weave-commands-existing-text-da4bd5 on 2026-09-28 while fixing Issue #455 (Gerrit change 471), weave v0.4.51, commit 1607208. Measured in Playwright against a scratch instance of that commit. 🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-06T12:55:51.539Z · started · session 0402-de57 🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-06T13:26:30.679Z · fixed · Gerrit 668 → 374b661 **Tests added:** - test/slash-commands.test.mjs: raw html: the marker is never painted, and the first undo goes back to the text before the command - test/slash-commands.test.mjs: a reference command opens its picker on the keypress, and the undo after a pick never brings the marker back - test/slash-convert-line.test.mjs: the observer sees every command marker and nothing waits for a later turn - test/ui-contract.test.mjs: a command that Vditor cannot insert finishes itself, now in the task the marker lands in **Live verification:** GET /api/health on :4400 reads sha 374b661, startedAt 13:25:41Z, after the 13:25:21Z submit. Repro re-run live in both themes on throwaway rows (since deleted): 150ms after Enter the surface reads 'First words
html
' with no raw-html marker, and one undo gives 'First words'. Gerrit 667 carried the same work and earned Verified -1 on a source-shape contract in test/ui-contract.test.mjs that still asked for a microtask; it is abandoned and 668 is what landed.

issues.name: Error: slash-commands case "a table reference is picked from search" reads doc.html before the save lands, red in WebKit
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

`WEAVE_BROWSER=webkit node --test test/slash-commands.test.mjs` with the fourteen cases Issue #455 adds (Gerrit change 471): the case "a table reference is picked from search and resolves to a live chip" failed in 3 of 3 full-file runs with `the reference must render as a live table chip`. The same case alone passed 3 of 3, and the full file at commit 1607208 in WebKit passed 30 of 30 twice. Chromium, which is what the gate runs for this suite, passed 44 of 44.

The stored markdown at the moment of the failure was correct: `[[table:Scratch/Note]]` in the editor and in `/e/<id>/doc.md`.

Cause, in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`:

```js
for (let i = 0; i < 40 && !html.includes('mention'); i++) {
  await page.waitForTimeout(50);
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__weaveFlushDocSaves?.());
  html = await (await fetch(`${base}/e/${id}/doc.html`)).text();
}
```

`doc.html` carries `a.mention { … }` in its own stylesheet, so `html.includes('mention')` is true on the first read and the loop never waits. `flushDocSaves()` starts the PUT and returns nothing to await, so the GET races the PUT. With the condition changed to `html.includes('class="mention')` the loop waited one more pass and the file was 42 of 42 in WebKit.

The entity case above it has the same loop condition.

## What good looks like

A wait that ends on the thing the assertion reads, so the case cannot pass or fail on the order two requests reach the server.

## Fix shape

Wait on `class="mention` in both cases, or have `flushDocSaves()` return `Promise.all` of its writes and await it in the test. No product change.

---
Filed by the harness session weave-commands-existing-text-da4bd5 on 2026-09-28 while fixing Issue #455 (Gerrit change 471), weave v0.4.51, commit 1607208. Measured in Playwright against a scratch instance of that commit.

issues.name: The behind toast tells every install to run weave service promote, which fails without a gerrit remote
issues.description:
**Symptom.** When `/api/health` reports `behind: true`, the instance chip turns amber and a toast names both shas and tells the user to run `weave service promote` (`public/app.js`, the `h.behind` branch of the nav health chip). `weave service promote` defaults to `--remote gerrit` and `--serve-dir ~/.weave-serve` (`bin/weave.js`, the `promote` subcommand). A plain clone from GitHub has only `origin`, so the advice fails on its first step.

**Reproduced 2026-09-28** in a fresh `git clone https://github.com/grunion-ai/weave.git` at f34f90c: `node bin/weave.js service promote --serve-dir <scratch> --port 4999` exits 1 with `weave: error: git fetch gerrit main failed: fatal: 'gerrit' does not appear to be a git repository`.

**Expected.** The remedy the toast names works on the install that shows it: either promote falls back to the remote `buildInfo` compared against (the first `git remote`), or the toast names the command that fits a plain clone (`git pull` then restart).

Found while closing out Issue #253 (harness session 1b4685bd).

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- When fixed, the update notice names a command that works on the install showing it. An install that promotes from Gerrit (it has a `gerrit` remote, as `~/.weave-serve` does) is told `weave service promote` when main moves. A plain GitHub clone hears only about a newer release (Issue #253, v0.4.52), and that toast says "git pull, then restart weave".
- Root cause: `public/app.js:1383-1387` hard-codes `weave service promote`, and promote defaults to `--remote gerrit` (`bin/weave.js:493`).
- Change: `buildInfo()` (`src/server.js:66`) adds `updateVia: 'promote'` when `git remote` lists `gerrit`, and `'pull'` otherwise. The client raises the sha toast only when `updateVia === 'promote'`. On a clone, the chip title still notes the sha, and the toast comes only from `releaseBehind`.
- Proposed from the code. The failing promote is this row's own reproduction from earlier today.

## Approach

- Failing tests first. In `test/stale-build.test.mjs`: remotes [origin] give `updateVia: 'pull'`, and [gerrit, origin] give `'promote'`. In a browser case: a health stub with `behind: true, updateVia: 'pull'` shows no promote toast.
- Files: src/server.js, public/app.js, the tests. Size: M. Land together with #459, which reads the same payload.
- **Decision needed:** should a plain clone hear about unreleased commits on main? (a) No, releases only. (b) Yes, and the toast says git pull. (c) Promote falls back to `origin`. Recommend (a): main moves daily, and a clone should update to releases.

issues.name: Health reports behind when the checkout is ahead of main or on another branch
issues.description:
**Symptom.** `describeBuild` in `src/server.js` sets `behind: latest !== head`, where `latest` is the sha `git ls-remote <first remote> main` returns and `head` is the boot HEAD. Any checkout whose HEAD differs from main reads as behind: a dev worktree one commit ahead of main, a feature branch, or an install pinned to a release tag while main carries unreleased commits after it. Each one gets the amber chip and the "behind main" toast.

**Expected.** The comment above `describeBuild` says "behind = the checkout is older than main". The flag should say that: true only when main's sha is not an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <latest> HEAD` fails) and HEAD is an ancestor of main, or it should be renamed to what it measures (`differs`).

Found while closing out Issue #253 (harness session 1b4685bd).

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- When fixed, `behind` is true only when main has commits this checkout lacks. A checkout at main or ahead of it is not behind. A feature branch that lacks main's latest commit still is.
- Root cause: `describeBuild` (`src/server.js:53-60`) sets `behind: latest !== head`, which tests for any difference. The comment above it says "behind = the checkout is older than main".
- Change: in `refreshLatest()` (`src/server.js:36`), once `ls-remote` returns `latest`, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <latest> HEAD` with the same async `execFile` call and store the result as `BUILD.contains`. A sha missing from the local object store fails the check, which correctly means HEAD lacks it. `describeBuild` then sets `behind: !contains`. `latestSha` stays as it is.
- Proposed from the code. Not reproduced on a scratch server today.

## Approach

- Failing tests first, in `test/stale-build.test.mjs`. Pure `describeBuild` cases: latest equal to head is not behind, latest an ancestor of head is not behind, and latest not contained is behind. Add one case in a temp git repo with a commit past its remote's main.
- Files: src/server.js, test/stale-build.test.mjs. Size: S.
- Risk: the ancestor check must stay off the `/api/health` request path, so it runs inside the existing `execFile` callback. Land with #458, which decides what the flag tells each install.

issues.name: Gap: /api/health has no staleWatcher chip for the Gerrit watcher heartbeats
issues.description:
Follow-up to Issue #292, fix shape point 2.

Since harness PR "weave watchers: heartbeat, peer check" (branch claude/weave-high-criticality-issues-488c59), each harness watcher job writes a heartbeat when a cycle finishes: ~/.gerrit/weave/heartbeat-verify (ai.grunion.weave-review) and ~/.gerrit/weave/heartbeat-deploy (ai.grunion.weave-deploy). Each job files a weave Issue when its peer goes silent for ten minutes, and `node ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-watcher-health.mjs` prints both and exits 1 when one is stale.

The two jobs share one node binary and one script, so a dead interpreter (the #292 case) stops both and neither files. The :4400 server is the one long-lived process that outlives such a failure, and /api/health is where sessions already look (stale, behind). A staleWatcher field there would close the gap.

Open question for Kyle: weave's product code would read a harness path. Options: (a) an env var such as WEAVE_WATCHER_HEARTBEATS set in the ai.grunion.weave plist, field absent when unset; (b) a default of ~/.gerrit/weave/heartbeat-*; (c) leave it in the harness and add the CLI check to DEVELOPMENT.md's landing steps (fix shape point 3). A job that launchd shows running is mid-cycle and not stale (a gate holds one verify fire for up to an hour or more).

Filed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-28.

issues.name: Wrong data: importing an MCP export leaves every attachment as a reference with no bytes, and nothing says so
issues.description:
## Reproduced
On a scratch data directory (weave v0.4.51, `f34f90c`):

1. Seed a workspace with one row and two attached files.
2. Export it with the MCP tool's default call, `dispatchTool(w, 'weave_export_json', {})`. That call omits `fileBlobs` by design (Issue #121: the MCP export is a reader, not a backup).
3. Import the dump into a fresh file-backed workspace with `importJSON` (the same code `weave_import_json` and `POST /api/import` call).

The import succeeds and both rows name their files, but `files/` is empty: 2 references, 0 blobs. Nothing in the import result, the log or the UI counts them. The rows then look exactly like the 59 casualties in Issue #250.

The CLI and HTTP exports carry the bytes, so their round trip is clean (`test/file-blobs.test.mjs`). The gap is only the reader-shaped dump going back in.

## Where
- `src/engine.js:7137` `exportJSON({ blobs })`, default `true`, but `src/mcp.js` passes `blobs: false` unless asked.
- `src/engine.js:7171` `importJSON` lands whatever `fileBlobs` the dump carries and never compares the file ledger against what landed.

## Options (a product call, not picked here)
1. `importJSON` returns and logs a count of references with no bytes, and the UI shows it after an import.
2. `importJSON` refuses a dump that names files and carries none of them, unless the caller passes an explicit flag.
3. The MCP export marks the dump (`blobs: 'omitted'`) so the import can tell a reader dump from a backup.

---
Found while investigating Issue #250 (harness session 1b4685bd, 2026-09-28, weave v0.4.51 @ f34f90c).

Fixed by Gerrit change 584, commit 964a821 (merged to main as 21b7903), 2026-10-03. Option 1 taken: `importJSON` returns `{ files, missing, warning? }`, counted after the blobs land, so a reader dump imported back where its bytes sit reports nothing; `weave_import_json`, `POST /api/import` and `weave import` all return it. Handbook attachments gotcha and the tool description say so. Tests: four new cases in `test/file-blobs.test.mjs` (MCP dump into a fresh dir lists the missing file; a dump with bytes and a same-workspace reimport report none; the HTTP route and the CLI carry the report), all red before the fix. Gate: Verified +1 on the first run (unit lane 2537/2537, browser lane 1071 pass, 1 skip). Fixed in is set when the batch release is cut.

issues.name: Error: opening a table in WebKit raises a ResizeObserver loop error that the bug recorder files as an error
issues.description:
## Measured
Opening a table in WebKit raises a window `error` event, "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.", and the bug recorder keeps it as an `error` in the trace. Any report filed from Safari afterwards counts an error the reader did nothing to cause, and the Error box looks justified when it is not.

Reproduced on `:4400` at v0.4.51 (f34f90c), read-only: Playwright 1.62.1 WebKit, 1440x900, open `uno` Task (`#/table/6f1c0a34-e906-4aef-bd30-7aeb41ab9ac6`). About 870 ms after navigation:

```json
{"pageerror":"ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.",
 "windowErrors":["ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications."],
 "bugTrace":[{"kind":"error","message":"ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.","line":0}]}
```

It also fires on a scratch server with a uno-shaped Task table, at v0.4.43 and v0.4.51, with and without a docked entity. Chromium raises nothing on the same pages.

## Where to look
Two observers in `public/app.js`: `new ResizeObserver(publishViewHeaderHeight)` near line 1135 and `fitWatch` near line 5140. A callback that changes the size of what it observes (or of an ancestor) in the same frame makes WebKit report the loop. Deferring the write to the next animation frame, or ignoring this one message in the recorder's `error` listener, are the two usual answers; which one is right depends on which observer fires it.

## Found by
Harness session 1b4685bd while working Issue #426 (Kyle's report ticked Error; its own trace showed 0 errors, so this is not what he saw at v0.4.43, but it is what a Safari report would show now).

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- When fixed, opening a table in Safari raises no window error, so a report filed from Safari lists only errors the reader caused.
- Root cause, found today: the `fitWatch` observer in `renderTable` (`public/app.js:5164-5184`). Its callback toggles `wv-fit`, `wv-overflow-x` and `wv-grid-scroll` on the wrap it observes, and `wv-grid-scroll` resizes that wrap inside the callback. On :4400 in WebKit, a wrapped `ResizeObserver` logged the error right after a `fitWatch` callback on `card table-wrap wv-overflow-x wv-grid-scroll`. `stickViewHeader` (`app.js:1142`) already skips rewriting an unchanged value.
- Change: run the `fitWatch` body inside `requestAnimationFrame`, collapsing repeat callbacks into one frame.
- Tried today on a scratch server, then reverted. Before the change, 2 of 2 WebKit loads of uno Task raised the error. After, 0 of 3 did. `test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs` (15/15) and `test/grid-hairline-header-browser.test.mjs` (14/14) pass alone with the change.

## Approach

- Failing test first, a WebKit case in a new `test/resize-loop-browser.test.mjs`: open a table wider than its card and assert no `pageerror` and no recorded bug-trace error after 1.5 s.
- Files: public/app.js, the test. Size: S.
- Risks: a one-frame lag before the fit classes apply could flash the sticky header or the trailing "+" fade (Feature #240). Re-check Issue #402, which touches the same wrap.

With the stickViewHeader observer skipped the error still fired on 3 of 3 loads; with the fitWatch observer skipped it fired on 0 of 3. The enrichment named the right one. issues.name: Error: the nightly weave backup exits 1 because iCloud made RESTORE.md dataless
issues.description:
## Reproduced
`launchctl print gui/501/ai.grunion.weave-backup` reports `last exit code = 1`. The job log (`/tmp/weave-backup.log`, overwritten each run) for the 2026-09-28 04:00 run ends in:

```
Error: Unknown system error -11, open '/Users/kyle/Documents/Weave Backups/RESTORE.md'
    at run (file:///Users/kyle/bin/weave-backup:186:6)
```

`ls -lO` shows `RESTORE.md` as `compressed,dataless` with an mtime of 2026-09-12 04:00. iCloud evicted the file, and `writeFileSync` over a dataless file fails with errno -11 (the same class of failure as the memory note on Google Drive dataless files). RESTORE.md has not been rewritten since 2026-09-12, so the job has most likely exited 1 every night since 2026-09-13.

## Impact
The failing write is at line 186, after the `VACUUM INTO` snapshots (line 168) and the `files/` rsync (line 175), so the nightly snapshots and the blob mirror still land. Three steps never run: the RESTORE.md refresh, the 30-day prune (line 191) and the final report, including the orphan count Issue #250 depends on. Nothing alerts on the exit code, so the job has been red for about two weeks without anyone seeing it.

## Where
`~/bin/weave-backup` (copy of harness `scripts/weave-backup.mjs`), line 186, `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DEST, 'RESTORE.md'), ...)`.

## Options
1. Write RESTORE.md to a temp name and rename it over the old one, so the write never opens the dataless file.
2. `brctl download` or a read of the file before writing, with a try/catch that reports and continues.
3. Alert on a non-zero exit (the job currently only writes to /tmp).

---
Found while restoring Issue #250 (harness session 1b4685bd, 2026-09-28).

Enriched 2026-09-28 by harness session 1b4685bd, against weave v0.4.52 (1079b88).

## Proposed solution

- When fixed, the job exits 0 nightly, and a failed night surfaces the next morning without anyone reading /tmp.
- Confirmed today: the failing line is still `~/bin/weave-backup:186` (identical to `~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-backup.mjs`). Snapshots get offloaded too: `db/2026-09-09/keystore.json` is dataless. A correction to Impact: the oldest snapshot is from 2026-09-08, so no snapshot has passed 30 days and the skipped prune has cost nothing yet. It will from 2026-10-08.
- Change 1: never open an existing file under the iCloud folder for writing. Write the guide as a new file in each night's snapshot (`db/<day>/RESTORE.md`), and replace the root copy by writing a temp file and calling `fs.renameSync`, which swaps the directory entry without reading the evicted file.
- Change 2: on success, call `beat('backup')` from `weave-watcher-health.mjs`, whose heartbeats sit outside iCloud, and let `verdict()` mark it stale after 26 hours. On a throw or `ok: false`, file one weave Issue through the same POST that `peerAlarm()` uses.

## Approach

- Failing test first, in `scripts/weave-backup.test.mjs`: with RESTORE.md chmod 000, `run()` still completes and prunes. In the watcher-health tests, a 27-hour-old backup beat reads as stale.
- Files: the two scripts and their tests, then copy the backup script to `~/bin` (the drift test holds the two copies equal). Harness PR. Size: M.
- Risk: renaming over a dataless file comes from the code and was not tried; chmod 000 only approximates errno -11.

**Repro:** Still red nine days on, checked 2026-10-07 12:30Z. launchctl print gui/501/ai.grunion.weave-backup reports last exit code = 1 and runs = 8; /tmp/weave-backup.log still ends in errno -11 on open of RESTORE.md; ls -lO shows RESTORE.md still compressed,dataless with its mtime stuck at 2026-09-12 04:00. The snapshots do still land: Weave Backups/db holds 2026-09-08 through 2026-10-07, today included. ai.grunion.weave-backup is the only backup agent loaded.

**Code:**
- ~/bin/weave-backup:186, `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DEST, 'RESTORE.md'), restoreDoc(...))`. This is byte-identical to the harness copy at ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-backup.mjs, which has a test file beside it (scripts/weave-backup.test.mjs, 17 cases), so the fix is a harness change plus portable-sync, never a weave Gerrit change. issues.name: Wrong data: a field type change has no Undo, and the values it converts cannot be brought back
issues.description:
Changing a field's type converts every stored value, and nothing keeps the values from before. Since Issue #428 (v0.4.52) the change is an Activity entry, but its toast says "Its values were converted, so this change has no Undo" and its Activity page offers no Roll back. A mistaken type change on a shared field loses every row's value for good.

**Measured on gerrit/main 1079b88 (v0.4.52).** `#migrateFieldType` (src/engine.js) coerces each row's value in place. `#rollbackCheck` refuses any entry marked `lossy` with "A roll back would restore the definition but not the values, so it is not offered." The field tray's toast for a type change has an Activity link and no Undo.

**Kyle's ruling (2026-09-28).** A type change must be undoable, values included:
- The write path stores each row's value from before the conversion with the `field-config-updated` entry, only for rows that held a value, once per type change. Undo in the toast and Roll back in Activity restore the definition and every stored value.
- Roll back keeps its staleness rule. A row whose value was edited after the type change is left as it is; unchanged rows are restored; the toast and the `undo` entry say how many of each.
- A row created after the type change has no snapshot and is converted with the engine's existing conversion for that direction, and counted.
- Growth is bounded, following the existing storage policy or, if none fits, keeping the snapshot for the newest type change per field.
- The type-change toast offers Undo like every other config change. Only a dropped snapshot still says its values cannot come back.
- Same permission rung as a schema write. Snapshots follow the export rules for rows, and Issue #230's rule holds for credential fields.

Related: #428 (field config Undo and Activity), #230 (secrets in export).

Claimed by harness session 1b4685bd (high-severity batch), 2026-09-29T02:43:10Z


## Fixed 2026-09-28: Gerrit change 480, merged 92e78a2

**What landed.** A type change now keeps each row's value from before the conversion, and the value the conversion made, for rows that held a value, with its `field-config-updated` entry in the audit log. Undo in the toast and Roll back in Activity restore the definition and the values:
- a row unchanged since the change gets its value from before (number to text and back gives 12.5, not a reparse; select to text and back gives the option ids and colours);
- a row edited since keeps its edit, converted back to the old type, and is not overwritten;
- a row made since has no snapshot and is converted by the engine's existing conversion for that direction.
The answer, the `undo` entry and the toast count them as restored, left and converted, for example "Grade rolled back: 1 value back, 1 edited since, kept, 1 newer row converted". The undo keeps its own snapshot, so rolling it back redoes the change with values. The staleness rules are unchanged. The type-change toast now reads "<Field> is now <type>" with Undo.

**Growth bound.** The audit log has no size policy. The capped stores cap a count per subject (200 revisions a document, 500 Activity entries an entity, 200 undo steps), and a snapshot is a whole column, so none fits. A field keeps the snapshot of its newest type change only. An older entry keeps its two definitions, drops its values in place, and its page says plainly that the values are no longer kept; its roll back is refused.

**Export and permissions.** A snapshot never leaves the engine: the Activity feed, `getActivity`, `weave_audit` and `GET /api/audit` show it as its row count only, including to a reader, and `exportJSON` does not carry the audit log. A credential field's snapshot holds the secret's name, never a secret (Issue #230 holds). Roll back keeps the schema write's rung: a writer token gets 403.

**Tests.** `test/field-type-snapshot.test.mjs` (11: number and back, select and back, edited row left and counted, newer row converted, stale refusal, dropped snapshot, redo, reopen, no leak through feed, audit or export, credential names, MCP counts; 10 of 11 red before) and six new cases in `test/field-config-undo-browser.test.mjs`, light and dark (tray Undo brings the numbers back, Roll back counts edited and newer rows, a dropped snapshot says so; all six red on the old UI). The #428 test that pinned the refusal now pins the roll back. Gate: Verified +1 on the first run, submitted. Deployed: `:4400` `/api/health` reports sha 92e78a2. The Handbook section "Taking a field change back", AGENTS.md and the `weave_rollback_field` description say the same.

issues.name: Gate re-run overwrites the earlier review log of the same patch set
issues.description:
## Reproduced

The Verified gate (harness `scripts/weave-review.sh`) wrote its log to `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/<change>-<patchset>.log`. A second gate run of the same patch set, after its Verified vote was cleared, wrote the same file and destroyed the first run's log. On 2026-09-28 this lost the red run of Gerrit change 479 patch set 1, and change 476 patch set 2 was gated six times and kept one log. Those red runs were the evidence for the flaky-test rows #454 and #466.

Reproduced against the fake Gerrit fixture in `scripts/weave-review.test.mjs`: two red runs of change 7 patch set 1 left one `7-1.log`, holding only the second run.

## Fix

harness PR #305, merged as d32bfcd. The first run of a patch set keeps `<change>-<patchset>.log`. A re-run claims `<change>-<patchset>.<n>.log` with n counting from 2, using a noclobber create so two runs never share a file. Every vote message now ends with a `full log:` line naming its own run's file, green and environment votes included, and the fixer routine reads the log the vote names.

## Guard

The test "a re-run of one patchset keeps the first log byte-identical and writes its own" in `scripts/weave-review.test.mjs` runs the gate twice on one patch set and checks that the first log is unchanged, that `7-1.2.log` exists, and that each vote names its own log. It failed before the fix and passes after, 7 of 7 in the file.

issues.name: Error: the Railway build refuses the Dockerfile because of its VOLUME line
issues.description:
## Reproduced
Railway project `giving-inspiration`, service `weave`, source `grunion-ai/weave` main at `1079b88` (v0.4.52). Deployment `8f68c223-10e8-41da-9af9-844333dac04c`, created 2026-09-29T02:49:25Z, status FAILED. The build log has three lines:

```
unpacking archive
scheduling build on Metal builder "builder-chxkkb"
dockerfile invalid: docker VOLUME at Line 29 is not supported, use Railway Volumes
```

`Dockerfile:29` is `VOLUME /data`. Railway rejects any Dockerfile that carries a `VOLUME` instruction, so the image never builds and the Handbook guide "Deploy: Railway" fails at step 1 for every operator who follows it. `test/deploy-artifacts.test.mjs:50` pins the line (`assert.match(DOCKERFILE, /^VOLUME (\/data|\["\/data"\])$/m)`), so the gate holds the defect in place.

## What good looks like
The same Dockerfile builds on Railway, Fly.io, Render and plain Docker. Each platform mounts `/data` itself: `railway.json` has `requiredMountPath: /data`, `fly.toml` has its own mount, and `compose.yaml` mounts the named volume `weave-data:/data`. None of them needs the `VOLUME` instruction.

## Fix shape
1. Remove `VOLUME /data` from `Dockerfile`; keep `RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node:node /data` so a named volume still inherits writable ownership. A comment says Railway refuses the instruction and each manifest mounts `/data`.
2. Flip the assertion in `test/deploy-artifacts.test.mjs` to refuse a `VOLUME` instruction, red first.
3. Add a line to the Handbook guide "Deploy: Railway" only if it names the instruction.
4. A `changelog.d/` fragment.

issues.name: Error: in WebKit the Formatting showcase page throws an unhandled rejection from Vditor's math render
issues.description:
## Reproduced
Open Showcase/Formatting #13 ("Every construct on one page", entity a8d94784-db2e-478e-a04c-6c8d0312ed0a) as an entity page on :4400 in Playwright WebKit at 2022x1210. Every load, twice in a row, raises one page error:

```
Unhandled Promise Rejection: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'e.parentElement.classList')
    at /vendor/vditor/dist/index.min.js:1:50157
```

Chromium loads the same page with no error.

## Where
The failing code is Vditor's math renderer: after KaTeX and mhchem load it walks the math nodes it collected and reads `e.parentElement.classList` on each. A node that left the document while the scripts loaded (the IR surface rebuilt, or weave's own decoration pass replaced it) has no parent, and the whole forEach rejects. The document itself still renders.

## Fix shape
Guard the math pass on weave's side: re-query the math nodes after the render settles, or catch the rejection around Vditor's math render so a detached node is skipped. The bug recorder files such a rejection as an Error, so it also pollutes reports from this page.

issues.name: Error: a fresh hosted instance is open to anyone until an operator with a shell turns the wall on
issues.description:
## Reproduced
A first boot on Railway starts with `requireAuth` off and no accounts. The moment the service has a public domain, an anonymous caller can `POST /api/accounts` and become admin, and can `PATCH /api/workspace`. The Handbook guide "Deploy: Railway" puts the door at step 6, after the custom domain at step 4, and both commands it names (`weave workspace require-auth`, `weave account invite`) need a shell on the service.

On Railway a project token has no shell: `railway ssh` answers "Unauthorized" and `railway volume files` answers "SSH authentication failed". This session closed the gap by deleting the domain before the first boot, then creating it and locking both workspaces over HTTPS 846 ms after the domain was created (one `POST /api/accounts` and one `PATCH /api/workspace` per workspace). The audit log showed no foreign entry.

Two more facts the guide leaves out:
- The wall is per workspace. `/data/workspace.db` and the docs workspace `/data/weave.db` each hold their own `requireAuth` and their own accounts. Turning it on for one leaves the other open. `grep` finds no sentence in `src/handbook.js` that says so.
- An admin token cannot mint a passkey invite over HTTP. The invite exists only in the CLI, so an operator without a shell cannot register a passkey.

## What good looks like
A hosted instance never serves one anonymous request as admin. The operator sets one variable before the first deploy and the instance boots closed.

## Fix shape
1. An environment switch read at boot (for example `WEAVE_REQUIRE_AUTH=1`) that turns the wall on for every workspace in the data directory, the docs workspace included.
2. A bootstrap path for the first admin that needs no shell: a one-time setup secret from the environment that the first `POST /api/accounts` must present.
3. The guide moves the door ahead of the domain and says the wall is per workspace.
4. Decide whether an admin token may mint an invite over HTTP.

---

issues.name: Error: Railway ignores the deploy section of railway.json, so the health check never ran
issues.description:
## Measured
`railway.json` sets `healthcheckPath: /api/health`, `healthcheckTimeout: 120`, `restartPolicyMaxRetries: 10` and `requiredMountPath: /data`. The service manifest Railway recorded for deployments `8f68c223` and `9ea80ac7` reads `healthcheckPath: null`, `healthcheckTimeout: null`, `requiredMountPath: null`. The Railway CLI 5.57.2 prints on every call: "Config as Code (railway.json / railway.toml) is deprecated. Prefer Infrastructure as Code (.railway/railway.ts) ... Existing files keep working until 2026-12-01."

## What good looks like
A deploy is live only once `/api/health` answers 2xx, which is what the guide "Deploy: Railway" step 5 promises.

## Fix shape

2. Migrate to `.railway/railway.ts` before 2026-12-01 (`railway config migrate`).
3. Until then the guide tells the operator to set the health check path in the dashboard.
