🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-08T04:12:13.703Z · session fix-2002-a7e1 · from #623

**Repro:** Not reproduced: the Railway side is out of reach from this host (no Railway credentials in the fixer session), so nothing was measured against the service. One premise of the row was tested and fails. The row offers "a schema change" as the first thing to check; the live schema rules it out. https://railway.com/railway.schema.json redirects to https://backboard.railway.app/railway.schema.json, and its deploy object names every key railway.json sets: startCommand, healthcheckPath, healthcheckTimeout, restartPolicyType, restartPolicyMaxRetries, numReplicas and requiredMountPath, plus cronSchedule, drainingSeconds, ipv6EgressEnabled, limitOverride, multiRegionConfig, overlapSeconds, preDeployCommand, preDeployTimeoutSeconds, region, registryCredentials, runtime and sleepApplication. The top level holds $schema, build, deploy and environments only. So railway.json as written validates, and the deploy section was dropped for a reason other than an unknown or renamed key.

**Code:**
- railway.json:7-15 is the deploy section the service manifest recorded as null.
- railway.json:2 pins $schema to https://railway.com/railway.schema.json, the redirect, not the backboard URL the content actually lives at.
- DEVELOPMENT.md rule 8 says the hosted instance is not redeployed after a landing: https://weave.grunion.ai runs `node bin/weave.js supervise` with WEAVE_AUTO_UPDATE=1 and swaps workers on a v-tag. A Railway redeploy is reserved for a Node, Dockerfile or src/supervisor.js change. So the health check matters on exactly those redeploys, and the row is about that path.
- src/server.js hostAllowed() answers /api/health for any Host (Issue, change 500, commit 037db6f), so Railway probing with Host: healthcheck.railway.app would work once the path is set.

**Fix shape:** Two checks remain, and both need Railway access this session did not have. First, whether the service reads the file at all: a service with a rootDirectory set looks for railway.json under that directory, and a service whose config source was switched in the dashboard ignores the file outright. Read the service manifest with the field that names its config source and root directory before changing the file. Second, the deprecation: the CLI already warns that config-as-code works until 2026-12-01, so the migration to .railway/railway.ts (`railway config migrate`) has a deadline whatever the cause turns out to be. Until one of those lands, the guide step that promises a 2xx /api/health gate should tell the operator to set the health check path in the dashboard, because today it promises something no deploy enforces.

**Test to write first:**
- test/railway-config.test.mjs: railway.json parses, its deploy section names healthcheckPath /api/health and a timeout, and every key it uses appears in a checked-in copy of the Railway schema. That is the part this repo can gate on its own; whether Railway honoured it cannot be asserted from a test and belongs in the deploy guide as a verification step.

issues.name: Slow: the review watcher gates one change per cycle because its re-list of Gerrit throws after each gate
issues.description:
## Reproduced

The review watcher (`scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs` in the harness repo, running from `~/.harness-serve` at d32bfcd) gates one change, then re-lists Gerrit before it picks the next. On 2026-09-28 that re-list failed after nearly every gate. `/tmp/weave-review-poll.log` holds 48 lines reading `gerrit re-list failed: HTTP fetch failed; no further gates this run`. The word after "HTTP" is the message of a thrown error, so the request never got an answer: `fetch()` threw. Each failure ends the cycle, and the next gate waits for the next launchd fire 120 seconds later.

With one gate slot and up to eight changes queued, every landing on 2026-09-28 paid this wait on top of its own gate.

## Likely cause

The first list call in the same cycle succeeds, so the address and the credential are right. The re-list runs the instant a full suite ends, while the machine is still busy. Node's `fetch()` gives each resolved address 250 ms to connect (`net.getDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout()`), and `localhost` resolves to both ::1 and 127.0.0.1. A slow accept from Gerrit's JVM right after a gate would fail both attempts. This matches the failure recorded for the plumbline watch on 2026-09-20. It is a hypothesis: the log keeps only the error's message, so the cause code is not recorded.

## Good looks like

A merge queue keeps draining after a transient read error. It retries the read, and it logs the cause.

## Fix shape

* Log `e.cause?.code` beside the message, so the next failure names itself.
* Retry the re-list three times with a short backoff before ending the cycle.
* Point the watcher at `127.0.0.1` in place of `localhost`, or raise the connect attempt timeout with `net.setDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout()`.
* Test in `scripts/weave-gerrit.test.mjs`: a re-list that throws once and then answers still gates the second target.

Filed by harness session 1b4685bd on 2026-09-28, from the salvage of Gerrit changes 424 to 445. Harness main d32bfcd, weave main d78432e.

Eight commits reached GitHub main between 2026-09-29T04:27Z and 13:08Z (`3f2a8cc` through `63daaf9`). Railway created no deployment for any of them. issues.name: Error: an imported file id holding ../ wrote and read files outside the data directory
issues.description:
**What was wrong.** `#blobPath` (src/engine.js:7059-7061 at 63daaf9) joined a file id onto the workspace's `files/` directory without checking it, and `importJSON` (src/engine.js:7418) adopted whatever file ids, logo id and `fileBlobs` keys a dump carried. An id holding `../` therefore resolved outside `files/`: on import `#landBlobs` (src/engine.js:7387-7393) wrote the dump's bytes to that path, and afterwards `exportJSON` (src/engine.js:7372-7376), `readFile` (the `GET /api/files/:id` route and the `weave_files` tool) and `getWorkspaceLogo` (`GET /api/workspace/logo`) read any file the process could reach and returned it.

**The fix.** `#blobPath` accepts only ids with the uuid shape that `uuid()` (crypto.randomUUID) mints and throws otherwise, and as a second guard checks that the joined path sits directly inside `files/`. Every blob read and write goes through it, so export, the file read route, the logo route and `weave_files` share the one guard. `importJSON` checks every `fileBlobs` key, every entity file id and `meta.logo.id` before it replaces any state, so a refused import leaves the workspace as it was. The Cloudflare store (src/store-cf.js) has no filesystem; its blobs stay inline in state and pass through the same id check.

**Test.** `test/security/blob-ids.test.mjs`: a `fileBlobs` key, an entity file id and a logo id that leave `files/` are each refused with the workspace unchanged and nothing written outside; a hostile id already in state cannot be read through `readFile`, `getWorkspaceLogo` or `exportJSON`; an in-memory workspace refuses the same ids; files and logos the engine mints still round-trip.

Fixed by change 495, commit 76cc7fd, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: any workspace with no accounts listed, revealed, overwrote and deleted every key in the shared keystore
issues.description:
## What was wrong

One keystore file serves every workspace of a weave process, but access to it was decided from the accounts of the workspace named in the URL. The `/api/keys` gate (src/routes.js:603-615) applied only when that workspace had accounts, and the engine's reveal check `#mayReveal` (src/engine.js:2914) returned true for everything when it had none. A caller could list, reveal, overwrite and delete every key through any account-less workspace, for example the `weave` docs workspace or a freshly created one.

## Fix

- `/api/keys` is decided against the hub root's accounts, whichever workspace the URL names. Once the root has an account, managing keys needs an authenticated admin on the root; a root caller on a key's access list may reveal it; the key's owner (verified on the root) may rotate or delete it.
- `#mayReveal` reads the hub root's accounts (`registryHost`), so a member engine with no accounts opens nothing.
- An instance with no accounts anywhere keeps working as before.

## Guard

`test/security/keystore-root-gate.test.mjs` (6 cases: no accounts open; anonymous refused through an account-less member; root reader and writer refused except their own key and access-list reveal; member-only admin refused; root admin allowed at the root and through a member with a root session; engine reveal check on a member).

Fixed by change 497, commit 96c13ce, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: an open or writer-accessible workspace could create, delete and search every workspace on the hub
issues.description:
## What was wrong

Routes that act on the whole hub were authorized against the workspace named in the URL: the workspace list, create, restore and delete (src/routes.js:559-579), and search with `all=1` (src/routes.js:1055-1068). An anonymous caller on an unwalled workspace, or a writer on any workspace, could list every workspace, soft- or hard-delete members, create new unwalled workspaces, and read names and snippets from walled workspaces through `search?all=1`. The bug reporter (src/routes.js:705) also let an anonymous caller write into the `weave` docs workspace even when that workspace was walled.

## Fix

- Create, restore and delete need an admin on the hub root once the root holds an account (the same `mayAdminister` gate as accounts and keys).
- `GET /api/workspaces` and `GET /api/search?all=1` carry only the workspaces whose own wall the caller would pass: wall off, or a token or session that verifies there (a root session opens a member, as at the wall).
- The bug reporter keeps its documented intake: any writer files into the `weave` docs workspace; an anonymous caller files there only when it could pass that workspace's wall.
- An instance with no accounts works as before.

## Guard

`test/security/hub-routes-root-gate.test.mjs` (7 cases: no accounts open; anonymous lifecycle refused with the files intact; list and search leave out a walled workspace; root reader and writer refused; member-only admin sees its own workspace but no lifecycle; root admin allowed at the root and through a member with a root session; bug report writer intake kept, anonymous refused when weave is walled, nothing written elsewhere).

Fixed by change 508, commit 92d4b77, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: an anonymous POST /api/mcp created admin accounts, set keys and replaced the workspace after accounts existed
issues.description:
## What was wrong

The REST accounts and keys routes close to non-admins once a workspace holds an account (src/routes.js:591-606), but `POST /api/mcp` exposed the same operations as tools (`weave_accounts`, `weave_keys`, `weave_import_json`, src/mcp.js:593-639) behind only the writer cap, which does not run for a caller with no role. On a workspace with the wall off, an anonymous caller could create an admin account and receive its token, change keys, or replace the whole workspace including its accounts.

## Fix

- One gate, `mayAdminister(on, role)` in src/mcp.js: anyone until `on` holds an account, an admin of `on` after. The REST accounts, keys and import routes and the MCP dispatcher all call it.
- The HTTP door passes the caller's verified role (and its role on the hub root) into the dispatcher. `weave_accounts` and `weave_import_json` are decided by the workspace's accounts, `weave_keys` by the hub root's.
- `POST /api/import` takes the same gate, since an import replaces the accounts.
- The stdio MCP server passes no caller: it is the local operator who started `weave mcp`, the CLI's trust, and it can still bootstrap the first account (stated in a code comment).

## Guard

`test/security/mcp-admin-gate.test.mjs` (7 cases: no accounts open; anonymous refused with accounts present, including REST import; reader and writer refused; member-only admin keeps its own accounts but not keys; root admin allowed; stdio creates an account; REST and MCP share one function).

Fixed by change 507, commit 3e4150b, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: an uploaded HTML or SVG attachment opened as a page and ran its script
issues.description:
**What was wrong.** `GET /api/files/:id` (`src/routes.js`, formerly lines 1011-1017) and the task applet's `GET /t/file/:id` (`src/applet.js`, formerly around line 246) sent a stored file with the content type its uploader supplied (`attachFile` in `src/engine.js` keeps it verbatim) and `Content-Disposition: inline`, with no `X-Content-Type-Options`. A writer, an MCP agent or an applet user could upload an `.html` or `.svg` file; anyone who opened its link (the grid's attachment anchor opens it in a new tab) had it rendered as a page on the workspace origin, where its script ran with the viewer's session and could call any API they could.

**Fix.** A new `fileHeaders(meta, bytes)` in `src/engine.js` (line 110) decides how every file is served, and both routes use it. Only inert types the app shows in place are served inline: PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP when their leading bytes prove the claimed type, `application/pdf` (the document viewer iframe) and `text/plain`. Every other file, HTML and SVG included, and any image whose bytes do not match its claim, is sent as `application/octet-stream` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` and an RFC 5987 filename. Every file response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`; a PDF was checked by hand to still render in Chromium under that policy. `WEAVE_INLINE_FILE_TYPES` (comma-separated, documented in the CLI help) adds types served in place, still sandboxed. Uploading into a document now embeds only raster images and PDFs; an HTML or SVG file inserts a link instead of an iframe or image.

**Test.** `test/security/served-files.test.mjs`; the html case in `test/toolbar-browser.test.mjs` now expects a link.

Fixed by change 496, commit 85aef98, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: a request with a malformed percent-escape in the path ended the server process
issues.description:
What was wrong: src/server.js:429 (at 63daaf9) called decodeURIComponent on the request path inside the async HTTP listener with nothing around it. A request such as GET /%E0%A4%A threw a URIError, the rejection went unhandled, and node ended the process, taking every workspace offline.

Fix: the listener body in src/server.js is wrapped in try/catch. A path that will not decode answers 400 {"code":"invalid"}; any other throw answers 500 {"code":"internal"} with the detail written to the log only; a throw after headers were sent destroys the socket. The next request is served either way.

Test: test/security/malformed-path.test.mjs (runs the server in a child process; malformed escapes answer 400, a thrown error answers 500 without leaking its message, and the server keeps serving).

Fixed by change 498, commit 3ee38babd7fc6a3af50189ca4edec7e6ab7c34e1, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: a ref of __proto__ or constructor changed Object.prototype for every workspace
issues.description:
**What was wrong.** The engine's lookups indexed plain objects by the ref the caller sent: `findSpace` (src/engine.js:1448 at 63daaf9), `findTable` (:1572), `getView` (:1947), `findField` (:4174), `getEntity` (:5014), `findEntity` (:5028), the account lookups (:3035, :3063), the automation verbs (:6783, :6795) and the keystore verbs (:2847-2959). The refs `__proto__` and `constructor` resolved to `Object.prototype` or `Object` instead of "not found", and the write verb after the lookup set properties on them: `updateSpace('__proto__', {name})` made `({}).name` return the new name process-wide, `shareView('__proto__')` put a share token on every object (a different workspace's `viewByShareToken` then matched it), and `grantKey('__proto__', ...)` set `owner` on every object. Nothing stopped a space, table, field, view, account or key being named one of these, and an import could carry a collection keyed by one.

**The fix.** One helper, `own(collection, ref)`, returns a value only when the collection holds the ref as its own property (`Object.hasOwn`). Every lookup that indexes a collection by a caller ref uses it: spaces, tables, fields, entities, dashboard views, automations, accounts, keystore entries, and the cross-workspace table and field finders. `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` are refused when a space, table, field (including a relation's inverse), dashboard view, table view, account or key is created or renamed, and `importJSON` refuses a dump whose spaces, tables, fields, entities, automations, views or accounts are keyed by one, before it changes anything.

**Test.** `test/security/proto-refs.test.mjs` calls 54 write verbs with each of the three refs and asserts `Object.prototype`, `Object` and `Function.prototype` are unchanged after every call; it also asserts the refs resolve to not found, the names are refused where things are named, and a reserved-keyed import is refused with the workspace unchanged.

Fixed by change 503, commit 9c33bc5, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: a page on any website could create, edit or delete rows with a cross-site POST
issues.description:
What was wrong: the node listener (src/server.js:425-434 at 63daaf9) and the dispatcher (src/routes.js:443) served POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE whatever site sent them, and readBody (src/server.js:134) parsed any body as JSON whatever its Content-Type. A text/plain POST needs no CORS preflight, so any page the owner visited could change a loopback instance.

Fix: src/server.js crossSiteWrite() refuses a write with 403 {"code":"forbidden"} when its Origin is neither the request's own origin (Host plus https when WEAVE_TRUST_PROXY and X-Forwarded-Proto say so), nor WEAVE_ORIGIN, nor http://localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] on the server's port, or when it carries Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site. A request with no Origin (curl, the CLI, agents) is served as before. With an Origin present, readBody refuses a body whose Content-Type is not application/json (400). The WebAuthn routes keep their own origin check.

Test: test/security/cross-site-writes.test.mjs.

Fixed by change 501, commit c22d3d407ce54b50ecd12aa8f7c715003787dc55, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: the server answered any Host header, so a DNS-rebound page could reach a loopback instance
issues.description:
What was wrong: the node listener (src/server.js:425-434 at 63daaf9) served every Host header, and originFor (src/routes.js:88-97) built the loopback origin from it. A page on an attacker's name that re-resolves to 127.0.0.1 was same-origin with the instance and could read and write it.

Fix: src/server.js hostAllowed() answers loopback names (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], any port), the host of WEAVE_ORIGIN, and the names in the new comma-separated WEAVE_ALLOWED_HOSTS; any other Host gets 421 {"code":"misdirected"}. /api/health answers any Host so platform probes (Railway sends Host: healthcheck.railway.app) keep working. startServer bound off loopback with neither variable set keeps answering any Host and prints one warning line, so existing containers stay up on upgrade. The CLI help documents WEAVE_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

Test: test/security/host-allowlist.test.mjs.

Fixed by change 500, commit 037db6fa90a792d71e971e91239e6a59310a9fac, 2026-09-29

issues.name: Error: a writer token could change the schema through relations, bulk edits and CSV import
issues.description:
## What was wrong

The writer role is promised no schema changes, but three routes skipped the check:

- `POST /api/tables/:t/relations` (src/routes.js:868) added a field on the table and an inverse on the target, and was not in the `schemaWrite` list.
- `POST /api/bulk` (src/routes.js:671) takes row ids in the body, so the system-table check the entity doors run (`sysTouch`, src/routes.js:302) never saw them. A `set` on a Fields, Tables, Spaces or Views row renamed or redefined structure; a `rollup` could create a row in a system table.
- `POST /api/tables/:t/import.csv` (src/routes.js:913) created rows without the `sysTouch` check, so a CSV aimed at Spaces or Tables created structure.

## Fix

issues.name: Error: a javascript: link in a document ran script when clicked
issues.description:
**What was wrong.** The markdown renderer in `src/markdown.js` (inline image and link branches of `renderInline`, formerly lines 127-143) wrote a link or image target straight into `href` or `src` after HTML-escaping it, without checking its scheme. A document containing `[click](javascript:...)` or `![x](data:text/html,...)` produced a live anchor or image in `doc.html`, the entity export and every `/api/markdown` render the app inserts, so one click ran script on the workspace origin in the viewer's session. The Handbook's promise that `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:` and `file:` are neutralised held only for URL-typed cells.

**Fix.** A new `safeUrl()` in `src/markdown.js` gates every URL the renderer writes: inline links, images and entity reference chips. A target is kept when it has no scheme (relative path, query, in-page or in-app `#` anchor) or its scheme is `http`, `https` or `mailto`; image sources may also be `data:image/png`, `jpeg`, `gif` or `webp`. Before reading the scheme it decodes HTML entities (numeric and named, repeatedly), strips C0/C1 control characters and whitespace, and folds case. A rejected link renders its text with no anchor, a rejected image its alt text, a rejected chip the broken chip. The renderer has no reference-link or autolink syntax; `src/mark.js` emits no URLs and `src/pdf.js` reduces links to text. Raw HTML blocks are unchanged (tracked separately).

**Test.** `test/security/markdown-schemes.test.mjs`.

issues.name: Error: a workspace logo was stored and served with whatever content type its uploader named

issues.name: Error: CI actions could be replaced upstream, and the workflow token was not limited to read
issues.description:
What was wrong: .github/workflows/test.yml referenced actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 by movable tag and had no permissions block, so a moved tag ran new code in CI and the job token carried the repository default scope. There was no security workflow.

The fix: each action is pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment (checkout v4.4.0, setup-node v4.4.0), test.yml gains a top-level permissions: contents: read, persist-credentials: false on checkout, and a concurrency group. New .github/workflows/security.yml runs on push to main, on pull requests and weekly, with contents: read, installs gitleaks, actionlint and hadolint at pinned versions with sha256 checks and semgrep and zizmor at pinned versions, and runs node scripts/security-scan.mjs --require-all. actionlint and zizmor (including the auditor persona) report nothing on both files. Scheduled workflows depend on GitHub keeping them enabled, which it stops doing after 60 days without repository activity.

Test: test/security/workflows.test.mjs (SHA pins with version comments, read-only permissions, security.yml triggers).

issues.name: Error: no record of which vendored library versions ship, and no scanner could see them
issues.description:
What was wrong: the third-party code under public/vendor/ and src/vendor/ (mermaid with its bundled DOMPurify, Vditor with KaTeX and highlight.js, Tabler, cytoscape, lean-qr, the Lucide icons, DejaVu, decklet) had no manifest. Manifest-based scanners such as retire.js could not see it, a changed or swapped file passed every test, and nothing recorded which version of each library shipped.

The fix: security/vendor.lock.json lists every one of the 222 vendored files with its library, npm name, version and sha256 (DOMPurify 3.4.12 is its own entry with bundledIn: mermaid). scripts/vendor-advisories.mjs sends each npm name and version to the OSV API and exits non-zero when an advisory applies; it uses the network, so it runs in CI and by hand, not in npm test. node scripts/vendor-lock.mjs --update rehashes after a deliberate upgrade.

The same row covers the rest of the scan kit (no row of its own), landed as change 506, commit 9988de6: scripts/security-scan.mjs runs gitleaks over history (security/gitleaks.toml allowlists three known false positives), semgrep with security/semgrep/weave.yml against security/semgrep/baseline.json so only new results fail, zizmor, actionlint, hadolint (security/hadolint.yaml) and the vendor lookup, one pass/fail/skipped line each.

Tests: test/security/vendor-lock.test.mjs (hash, unlisted-file and missing-file checks), test/security/security-scan.test.mjs (baseline comparison, summary, PATH detection, semgrep fixtures).

issues.name: Error: the sign-in page on a second hostname offers a passkey that can never work
issues.description:
## Reproduced
The instance has `WEAVE_ORIGIN=https://weave.grunion.ai` and is also reachable at the Railway-generated name `weave-production-a5bd.up.railway.app`. On the second name `/auth` draws the same sign-in page, and `POST /api/auth/login/options` answers `rpId: "weave.grunion.ai"`. The browser then refuses before any prompt:

```
SecurityError: The relying party ID is not a registrable domain suffix of, nor equal to the current domain. Subsequently, an attempt to fetch the .well-known/webauthn resource of the claimed RP ID failed.
```

Kyle reported the same failure from his device as "The requested RPID did not match the origin or related origins." The page gives no hint that the address is the cause.

## What good looks like
A request that arrives on a host other than the one in `WEAVE_ORIGIN` is sent to the same path on `WEAVE_ORIGIN` (a 308 for pages), so a person always signs in on the name the passkey is bound to. API calls with a Bearer token keep working on either name.

## Fix shape
1. In the page route, when `WEAVE_ORIGIN` is set and the request host differs, redirect pages to `WEAVE_ORIGIN` plus the path.
2. The sign-in page catches `SecurityError` and says which address to open.
3. The guide "Door B: passkeys" says to remove the platform's generated domain once the custom domain works.

---

issues.name: Error: every push to main takes the hosted instance down for minutes
issues.description:
## Measured
The Railway service deploys on every push to GitHub main, which is what the guide "Deploy: Railway" step 1 sets up. A volume attaches to one container, so Railway stops the running container before it starts the new one. On 2026-09-29 the deploy of `b83f657` (deployment `e306d522`) went:

- 16:34:28 UTC deployment created, image pushed 16:47:29
- 16:54:27 new container started, "Weave running" at 16:54:28
- 16:56:49 health check passed
- 16:55:36 to 16:59:29 every request to `/api/health` answered `502 Application failed to respond` after 15 s
- 17:00:07 first 200

That is at least four minutes of 502 for one landing. Main took four deployments between 13:13 and 16:34 UTC that day.

## What good looks like
The hosted instance is replaced a few times a week, at a moment the operator picks, and a landing on main changes nothing in production.

## Fix shape
1. The guide tells the operator to deploy from release tags or a `production` branch, never from main, and says why: one volume means stop, then start.
2. `railway.json` (or its successor) sets no watch on main.
3. Find why the edge answered 502 for three minutes after the health check passed.

issues.name: Looks broken: the slash menu opens under the Description header and the record title, hiding its rows
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** Scratch server on weave main b83f657, seeded demo workspace, Chromium and WebKit at 1280 x 800. Open Task #2 "Billing API migration" as a page, put one line of text in its Description, move the caret to the empty line after it and type "/". The menu opens upward, from y 75 to y 475 (WebKit: 85 to 485). Two sticky bands draw over it:
- The DESCRIPTION section header (y 404 to 432) cuts through the menu and hides the Image row between "Line break" and "Raw HTML".
- The record header with the title covers the menu's top: document.elementFromPoint at the menu's first 30 px returns TEXTAREA.name-edit and DIV.view-header, not the menu, so the rows above "Heading 1–6" cannot be seen or clicked.

**Where.** Vditor's .vditor-hint sits at z-index 4 (public/vendor/vditor/dist/index.css:776). The document section head is sticky at z-index 5 (public/style.css:1614-1615, added for Issue #411 so it clears the heading carets), and the entity header is sticky at z-index 6 (public/style.css:295, and 1976 for the dock). The menu is the only one of the three that should win, and it is the lowest.

**What good looks like.** Notion's and Linear's slash menus float above every sticky header and flip or clamp so all of their rows stay inside the visible document area.

**Fix shape.** Raise .vditor-hint above the entity header (z-index 7 or higher, in weave's own style.css, not the vendored file), and clamp its top to the bottom of the pinned header (--wv-view-h) so an upward menu shrinks and scrolls rather than sliding under it. A browser case: open the menu on the last line under a section head, and elementFromPoint at the menu's top and middle rows returns a node inside the menu, in both engines.

issues.name: Wrong data: an option colour sent as "magenta" is saved as slate with no error
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** Scratch server on weave main b83f657. `POST /api/tables/Task/fields` with a select field whose options are `{"name":"Design","color":"magenta"}`, `{"name":"Backend","hue":"magenta"}`, `{"name":"Docs","color":"#d6409f"}` and `{"name":"Infra","hue":"pink"}` answers 201. Design and Backend are stored as `hue: "slate", color: ""`; Docs and Infra are stored as pink. A made-up name (`"color":"banana"`) is also stored as slate with a 201. The caller is told nothing, and the field tray shows Design and Backend as grey chips (attached).

**Where.** The closed palette is intended. The defect is that weave publishes one set of names and accepts another, and swaps an unknown one for slate in silence:
- src/vocabulary.js:40-49 (`OPTION_COLORS`, served as `optionColors`) and src/handbook.js:322 and :1132 name the eighth colour "magenta" and list eight colours.
- src/engine.js:353-360 (`HUE_HEX`, `hueOf`) names the same hex "pink", knows ten hues (teal and orange are missing from the vocabulary and the handbook), and falls back to slate for any name it does not know.

**What good looks like.** Notion's API answers 400 validation_error for a select colour outside its list, and names the accepted values. Airtable's field editor offers only the colours its API accepts, under the same names.

**Fix shape.** Generate the vocabulary and the handbook list from `HUE_HEX` so the names cannot drift, and accept "magenta" as an alias of pink so existing callers keep working. Any other unknown hue or colour answers 400 naming the accepted values, on every door (field POST and PATCH, PUT /api/schema, MCP, CLI). Tests: magenta round-trips as pink, banana answers 400, and the vocabulary's names equal `Object.keys(HUE_HEX)`.

Filed by harness session 1b4685bd on 2026-09-29, found while capturing release notes media, weave main b83f657.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-02T07:51:42.536Z · started · session kind-hopper-b5bb3d

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-02T08:46:13.830Z · fixed · Gerrit 527 → e85ada8

**Fix.** One ramp, one reader. `public/chip-core.js` owns the ten hues, the two names weave published for them (`magenta` for pink, `neutral` for slate) and `hueName()`, which resolves a ramp name, an alias or a hex and answers undefined for anything else. `src/vocabulary.js` generates `OPTION_COLORS` from that ramp and publishes each hue's aliases, so the served names are the accepted names: `/api/vocabulary` now lists ten entries, pink carries `aliases: ["magenta"]` and slate carries `aliases: ["neutral"]`. The field dialog's own copy of the old eight hexes, which nothing rendered and which held the vocabulary at eight, is gone.

**Reads are forgiving, writes are strict.** A colour a caller just named is refused with a 400 that quotes it and lists the ten hues: `addField`, a select or multiselect options patch, a type change that carries its own options, `applySchema` for a colour the document names, and a `field` definition value. The HTTP routes, the MCP tools and the CLI all go through those engine verbs. A colour already on disk still resolves, or rests on slate: `importJSON` writes state verbatim, `describeSchema` reads an unknown hex as slate, the Fields registry's mirror of a field definition is exempt, and an option handed back wearing the colour it already had is not treated as a new assertion. That last carve-out is load-bearing: `src/weaver-seed.js` and `src/handbook.js` widen a select by re-sending the options they found, so without it a workspace holding a pre-ramp hex would have started refusing its own docs sync.

**Handbook.** The select page and the guide "Making a workspace your own" both published eight values and the name `magenta`, which is half the defect. Both now carry the ten ramp hues, the alias rule and the refusal. Rows #8 and #10 on :4400 read the new text.

**Along the way.** weave's own Automations table seeded `Health` with `color: 'yellow'`, `'green'` and `'red'` through the hex-only reader, so all three options stored slate and the column read grey. They are ramp hues now (`green`, `amber`, `red`). Only a workspace that does not yet have the field is affected: `#ensureMetaTables` adds and never rewrites.

**Tests added:**
- `test/option-colour.test.mjs` (new, 17 cases): the alias round-trip (`color: "magenta"`, `hue: "magenta"`, the hex and `hue: "pink"` all land on pink), teal and orange as storable hues, slate for an empty colour and for `neutral`, a refusal on each door with the field untouched afterwards, the route's 400 and the vocabulary route's names, MCP parity through `dispatchTool`, and the four forgiving paths (import, describeSchema, a widen that re-sends stored options, a describeSchema round-trip through applySchema).
- `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`: the palette is pinned to the ramp and to the published aliases, not to the dialog's dead list.
- `test/chip-system.test.mjs`, `test/development-sync.test.mjs`: re-pinned to the ramp; the widening case now paints a real hue, because an invented one is refused at that door.

**Verification.** The suite ran red first against gerrit/main at 6480f82 (11 of 14 cases failing then; the three forgiving-read cases passed on both, as they should). Full suite in the worktree: 3238 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. The Gerrit gate ran the same on patch set 1 and voted Verified +1. On :4400 at e85ada8, this Issue's exact POST answers 201 with all four options at `hue: "pink", color: "#d6409f"`, the banana option answers 400 on both POST and PATCH, and the scratch space used for the check was deleted.

issues.name: Wrong data: saving a document rewrites every task item to two spaces after the box and an upper-case [X]
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** Scratch server on weave main b83f657, Chromium and WebKit at 1280 x 800.
1. `PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc` stores "Launch checklist\n\n- [ ] Draft the quickstart\n- [x] Pick the sample app\n" on a Task's Description.
2. Open the record, click at the end of the first line and type " for v1". Nothing else is touched.
3. `GET /e/<id>/doc.md` now returns "Launch checklist for v1\n\n- [ ]  Draft the quickstart\n- [X]  Pick the sample app\n" (attached). Both task items gained a second space after the box, and the ticked box became an upper-case X.

The slash command writes the same shape: on an empty line /task leaves "- [ ]  To do", and typing "- [ ] Buy milk" by hand is saved as "- [ ]  Buy milk". `setValue('- [ ] Buy milk')` followed by `getValue()` returns the two-space form, so the rewrite is Vditor's (Lute's) markdown output, and weave saves what the editor returns.

**Why it matters.** The Handbook promises that "the box is `[ ]` or `[x]` in the stored text, so an agent can tick one with a string edit" (src/handbook.js:2097). After any human edit, an agent looking for "- [x] " or "- [ ] Draft" no longer matches, and every task line shows as changed in the document's revision history although nobody touched it. The slash test's task case (test/slash-commands.test.mjs, `/^- \[ \] /m`) passes on two spaces, so nothing guards the shape.

**What good looks like.** GitHub, Obsidian and Linear keep a task item as typed: one space after the box, lower-case x.

**Fix shape.** Normalise in the one place weave reads markdown out of the editor before a save: `^(\s*[-*+] )\[([ xX])\] {2}` becomes `$1[x] ` or `$1[ ] `, outside fenced code. Pin it with exact-string asserts: /task then "Buy milk" stores "- [ ] Buy milk", and an unrelated edit leaves a stored "- [x] " line byte for byte.

issues.name: Error: the tests workflow checks out at depth 1, so the architecture-map pin test fails on every main landing
issues.description:
## Observed
Both matrix legs of the `tests` workflow fail on every main SHA on GitHub Actions. The run on `e51ade8` (id 36702179722) fails all four legs, and so does every main run back through `5091c23` on 2026-09-29. The Gerrit gate is green throughout, so main lands red on GitHub and nothing watches it.

The failing assertion is one test:

```
not ok 78 - the map is pinned to a commit in this repository
  location: 'test/architecture-map.test.mjs:27:1'
  error: Got unwanted exception: pinned revision b83f6573dacee5b8df261a86d5f58899b88a2725 is not an ancestor of HEAD
  Actual message: "Command failed: git -C .../weave merge-base --is-ancestor b83f657... HEAD"
```

## Cause
`.github/workflows/test.yml:26` uses `actions/checkout` with no `fetch-depth`, which defaults to a depth-1 clone. `merge-base --is-ancestor` cannot answer under a shallow clone, so it exits non-zero and the test reads that as a dangling pin. The pin is fine: `git merge-base --is-ancestor b83f657 HEAD` returns 0 in a full checkout of the same SHA.

`.github/workflows/security.yml:38` already carries `fetch-depth: 0` with the comment "gitleaks reads the whole history", so the two workflows disagree about checkout depth.

## Fix shape
Add `fetch-depth: 0` to the checkout step in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. One line. Do not re-pin the map.

---

issues.name: Error: the vendored dompurify 3.4.12 carries an open XSS advisory, so the security workflow fails on every main landing
issues.description:
## Observed
The `security` workflow fails on every main SHA. Every other scanner passes and one line fails:

```
gitleaks: pass · semgrep: pass (19 results, all in baseline) · zizmor: pass · actionlint: pass · hadolint: pass
vendor: fail
  dompurify   3.4.12   GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7
```

## The advisory
`GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7`, severity medium: "DOMPurify: IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS". Vulnerable range `<= 3.4.12`, first patched in `3.4.13`. `security/vendor.lock.json` pins `dompurify` at `3.4.12`, so weave ships the vulnerable build under `public/vendor/`.

weave runs dompurify on user-authored document and cell content, which is exactly the sanitize path an XSS advisory lands on.

## Fix shape
Upgrade the vendored file to dompurify 3.4.13 or later, then rehash with `node scripts/vendor-lock.mjs` and re-run `node scripts/vendor-advisories.mjs`. Issue #532 built this scanner; this is its first real catch, so the finding is the dependency, not the tool.

issues.name: Slow: per-request CPU grows about 3.5x when the workspace doubles, because entityCount scans every entity on each schema read
issues.description:
## Measured
Benchmark of v0.4.52 (e51ade8) in Docker at the Railway Free plan limits (--cpus=1 --memory=512m), CPU read from the container's cgroup cpu.stat over batches, 2026-09-30.

- At 4,389 entities: table view query 14.5 CPU ms, p95 26 ms; schema read under 5 ms; blended mix 135 req/s at 16 concurrent (p95 273 ms).
- At 8.4k entities: table query 51 to 118 CPU ms and 100 KB; schema read 45 to 67 ms; blended throughput fell to about 70 req/s.
- Doubling the workspace cost roughly 3.5x the CPU per request. One cause: `describeSchema` counts every table's rows by scanning all entities (`entityCount` in `src/engine.js`) on every page load. Not profiled further.
- Memory: about 10 KB of RAM per entity held (63 MB idle at 219 entities, 150 MB at 8.4k).

Related, not the same defect: "Slow: home boot holds the loader 6 to 9 s behind a serial /api/schema call" (34254215) covers the serial boot shape; this row covers the per-request cost growing faster than the workspace.

## Good looks like
Per-request CPU grows no faster than the rows a request returns. Row counts for the schema come from an index or a maintained counter, as Airtable and Fibery show counts without a table scan.

## Fix shape
Keep a per-table row count updated on create/delete (or a `SELECT count(*) ... GROUP BY table` over an indexed column) and stop scanning entities in `entityCount`. Then profile the table query at 8k and 16k rows to find the rest of the superlinear cost. Hosting impact: on Railway Free, RAM per held row is already the binding cost; CPU growth decides when 1 vCPU runs out.

Filed by the harness weave-stack-guide session, 2026-09-30, weave v0.4.52, commit e51ade8. Bench scripts and raw results: harness session scratchpad bench/ (res-*.json, ops.tbl, ceil.tbl).



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-06T12:26:16.377Z · session 0402-de57 · from #266, #397

**Repro:** Not reproduced as a user-visible slowness, and the mechanism is confirmed by reading. On :4400 at sha d75e88e, 2026-10-06, with 6,094 entities and a 142 MB store, GET /w/weave/api/schema returns in 30 to 50 ms warm (three runs: 50, 30, 30 ms), against the 45 to 67 ms the row measured at 8.4k inside a 1-vCPU container. So the shape the row describes is there, and this host is simply faster than the Railway Free box the benchmark used; nothing new is needed to confirm the cause, which is visible in the source.

**Code:**
- src/engine.js:7041 describeSchema, and src/engine.js:7065 inside it: entityCount: this.listEntities(db.id).length, evaluated once per table
- src/engine.js:4831 listEntities walks Object.values(this.state.entities) and filters on dbId, so describeSchema costs tables times entities on every call: about 50 tables by 6,078 rows on the weave workspace today
- src/engine.js:6810 scores a table for search with the same listEntities(db.id).length, so the nav and search paths pay it too
- src/engine.js:7220 #fileLedger is a second whole-entity walk, run on a different path, for reference on what a single pass over the entity map looks like

**Fix shape:** The row proposes a per-table counter maintained on create and delete. One pass is the smaller first step and carries no invalidation risk: walk Object.values(this.state.entities) once inside describeSchema, bucket live rows by dbId into a Map, and read each table's count from it. That turns tables-times-entities into entities, needs no new state, and cannot drift from the rows the way a maintained counter can when a row is restored from trash, purged, or moved between tables. A maintained counter or an indexed SELECT count(*) ... GROUP BY is the next step if one pass is still too much, and it should be measured rather than assumed, because the row's own benchmark names the table-view query (51 to 118 CPU ms at 8.4k) as the larger cost and leaves it unprofiled.

**Test to write first:**

issues.name: Error: test/update-check.test.mjs is red on both node 22.16 legs and green on node 24, so main still lands red on GitHub
issues.description:
## Observed
`test/update-check.test.mjs` is red on both node 22.16 legs of the `tests` workflow and green on both node 24 legs. Run 36832802958 on main `f2d1a7f` (2026-10-01): node 24 on ubuntu-latest and node 24 on macos-latest pass, node 22.16 on ubuntu-latest and node 22.16 on macos-latest fail. `scripts/test.mjs` gave the file its second chance and it lost again, so this is a real regression and not Issue #44 flake: the leg prints `# RETRYING 1 file(s) that failed: .../test/update-check.test.mjs` and then `# RETRIED and still red`.

Five cases abort together, all `failureType: cancelledByParent`, the first at `test/update-check.test.mjs:142`:

```
not ok 10 - a hung request times out in seconds and never blocks a status call
  ---
  duration_ms: 9.634496
  type: 'test'
  location: '/home/runner/work/weave/weave/test/update-check.test.mjs:142:1'
  failureType: 'cancelledByParent'
  error: 'Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved'
  code: 'ERR_TEST_FAILURE'
  stack: |-
    process.emit (node:events:518:28)
  ...
# Subtest: an unreadable cache is ignored, not fatal
not ok 11 - an unreadable cache is ignored, not fatal
  ---
```

The surrounding tallies are `# pass 2263 / # fail 0` on the first run and `# pass 9 / # fail 0` on the retry, so the nine cases before line 142 pass and the file's own exit code, not an assertion, is what reddens the leg. `Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved` is node:test reporting that something in the file left work outstanding when the loop drained: a timer, a socket or an un-awaited promise that node 24 happens to settle in time and node 22.16 does not.

## Why it was invisible until now
The whole `tests` workflow failed on every main SHA for two days under Issue #558 (checkout at depth 1 broke the architecture-map pin test), so a second, unrelated red in the same run had nothing to stand out against. With #558 fixed in `f2d1a7f`, two legs went green and these five cases are the only thing left holding the run red. The Gerrit gate does not see it: it runs one node, the local one (node 24), where the file passes.

## What good looks like
All four matrix legs green on a main landing. `package.json` declares node >= 22.16 and the Dockerfile pins a 22.x tag, so 22.16 is a supported runtime and the file has to hold there, not only on 24.

## Fix shape
Reproduce under node 22.16 (`node --test test/update-check.test.mjs`, nvm or a 22.16 container), then find the handle the file leaves open past the point the loop drains. The first cancelled case, "a hung request times out in seconds and never blocks a status call" at line 142, deliberately hangs a request, so the likely culprits are that test's own pending fetch or timer and the server it starts. Awaiting the abort and closing the server (or giving the timer `unref()`) is the shape. Keep the five assertions.

---
Filed 2026-10-01 by the overnight weave fixer while verifying Issue #558 live on GitHub Actions. Read off run 36832802958 on `grunion-ai/weave` main at `f2d1a7f`; the failing-job log is attached as a copy.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-03T07:12:18.551Z · started · session gs-623a34

---

Fixed 2026-10-03 by the overnight weave fixer, attempt 1. Landed as `5eef2fa` (merge `d2ec8be`), Gerrit change 556, Code-Review +2 and Verified +1 on patchset 1.

Root cause. `createReleaseCheck` cut a hung request off with `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`, whose timer is unref'd, so the abort landed only while something else held the event loop open. A real socket does hold it, which is why the hosted check was never affected. `test/update-check.test.mjs` injects a fetch that just hangs and holds nothing, so on node 22.16 the loop drained at about 7 ms against a 50 ms cut-off, the awaited `refresh()` never settled, and node:test reported `Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved` and cancelled the case at line 142 along with the four after it. Node 24's test runner happens to hold a handle for long enough, which is the whole of the version split: the same case ran 52 ms and passed there. Neither version keeps that timer alive on its own, measured directly: a two-line script that arms `AbortSignal.timeout(50)` and waits for the abort prints `aborted? false` on 24 and on 22.16 alike.

Reproduced before any change. `nvm install 22.16.0`, then `node --test test/update-check.test.mjs` on `gerrit/main` at `8d5ce63`, three consecutive runs, each exit 1 with `# pass 9`, `# fail 0`, `# cancelled 5` and the first `not ok 10` at `test/update-check.test.mjs:142` carrying the same error string as the CI log. Deterministic, not a flake.

Fix. The cut-off is now a ref'd `setTimeout` over an `AbortController`, cleared in the `finally` that already saved the cache and dropped the inflight promise, so it clears on the success path, on both early returns and in the catch. Nine lines in `src/update-check.js`. `AbortSignal.timeout` stays at its other call sites (`src/supervisor.js`, `src/service.js`, `src/oidc.js`): those await real sockets, and the whole suite is green on 22.16, so none of them was swept into this change.

Tests. Two cases run the check in a bare child process, which holds no ambient handle, so they pin this on any node version instead of only on 22.16. `the timeout fires with nothing else holding the event loop open` was red on node 24 before the change, exit 13 with `Detected unsettled top-level await`. `the cut-off is cleared when the answer lands, so the process still exits at once` guards the risk this change introduces, since the new timer is ref'd: against a copy of the module with the `clearTimeout` line removed, the process sat 3.08 s on a 3 s cut-off, so the case is red without the clear. The original five assertions are untouched.

Verified. The file is 16 of 16 on node 22.16 and on node 24, before the merge and again against the merged tree at `d2ec8be`. Whole suite on node 22.16 in the worktree: exit 0, main lane 2397 pass, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, browser lane 979 with `test/system-tables-nav-browser.test.mjs` green on its second chance (Issue #44). Whole suite on node 24: exit 0, 2396 and 979 pass, fail 0, skipped 0, no `# RETRYING` line. Gerrit gate on patchset 1: 2398 and 979 pass, fail 0, skipped 0.

GitHub Actions is the answer this Issue asked for. Run 37108829410 on main `d2ec8be`: node 22.16 on ubuntu-latest, node 22.16 on macos-latest, node 24 on ubuntu-latest and node 24 on macos-latest all success, where the two preceding main runs (`5602c56`, `80f342a`) both failed on the two node 22.16 legs. On node 22.16 on ubuntu-latest the three cases read `ok 2240 - a hung request times out in seconds and never blocks a status call`, `ok 2241 - the timeout fires with nothing else holding the event loop open` and `ok 2242 - the cut-off is cleared when the answer lands, so the process still exits at once`, with `# fail 0` and `# cancelled 0` on the lane and no `# RETRYING` line anywhere in the run.

This Issue's repro lives in the test suite, not in the running app, so the post-merge check was `:4400` serving the merged sha and then the file re-run under 22.16 against the merged tree. `/api/health` reports `sha d2ec8be` and `startedAt 2026-10-03T08:10:50Z`, later than the submit, and the file is 16 of 16 on 22.16 twice from a checkout of `d2ec8be`. Nothing in the UI changed, so no scratch server was started and no both-theme screenshots were taken.

Records. `changelog.d/update-check-timeout-563.md` written per the fragment convention; CHANGELOG.md untouched. No `Development/Feature` covers this and none needed a state change. No `Handbook/Guide` or `Wiki/Article` documents the update check, searched on update check, WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK, latestRelease, release and node version, so none was edited. The Quality mirror regenerates from the test files. `Fixed in` is left empty: no release carries this yet, and the release that does will link it.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-03T08:17:01.727Z · fixed · Gerrit 556 → d2ec8be

**Tests added:**
- test/update-check.test.mjs: the timeout fires with nothing else holding the event loop open
- test/update-check.test.mjs: the cut-off is cleared when the answer lands, so the process still exits at once

**Live verification:** GET /api/health on :4400 reports sha d2ec8be, startedAt 2026-10-03T08:10:50Z. The repro lives in the suite rather than the app, so the live check was to re-run test/update-check.test.mjs under node 22.16 against a checkout of the merged tree: 16 of 16, twice. The Gerrit gate runs node 24 only and does not prove this one; GitHub Actions run 37108829410 on main d2ec8be does, with all four matrix legs green where the two preceding main runs failed on both 22.16 legs.

**Root cause:** `createReleaseCheck` in `src/update-check.js` cut a hung request off with `AbortSignal.timeout`, whose timer is unref'd, so the abort landed only while something else held the event loop open. A real socket holds it, which is why the hosted check never suffered; the injected hanging fetch in the test holds nothing, so on node 22.16 the loop drained at about 7 ms against a 50 ms cut-off and node:test cancelled the case at line 142 and the four after it. Node 24's runner happens to hold a handle long enough, which is the whole version split.

**Fix:** a ref'd `setTimeout` over an `AbortController`, cleared in the `finally` that already saved the cache, so the cut-off no longer depends on what else the process is doing. `AbortSignal.timeout` stays at its other call sites (`src/supervisor.js`, `src/service.js`, `src/oidc.js`), which await real sockets and are green on 22.16.

**Changelog:** `changelog.d/update-check-timeout-563.md`, the fragment mechanism this repo now uses. `Fixed in` is empty: no release carries it yet.

issues.name: Looks broken: a rollup or lookup that draws rating icons still clips them
issues.description:
## What was measured

On :4490 (a scratch server on the Issue #404 fix, weave v0.4.52, Chromium 1500x900) Showcase > Field Types, first row, measured with `td.getBoundingClientRect().width` against the cell's `.wv-rating` `scrollWidth`:

| Field | Type | Max | Column | Content box | Icons need | Clipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Peer skill | rollup (avg over a rating) | 5 | 88px | 80px | 119px | yes |

Issue #404 gave the `rating` field type a column width that fits its icons. A rollup that reads a rating draws the same icons, and a lookup of a rating does too, but both keep the plain rollup (88px) and lookup (136px) type defaults, so their icons still cut at the cell edge.

Two things make this its own fix rather than a line in #404. The computed cell wraps the icons in the `Σ` / `ƒ` chip, which takes width of its own inside the cell. And the icons inside that chip render at 23px each, not the 18px a plain rating cell paints, so the geometry constants in `public/column-resize.js` (`RATING_METRICS`) do not describe this cell.

## What good looks like

A rollup or a lookup that draws rating icons opens wide enough for all of them, the same way a rating column does since Issue #404.

## Fix shape

`defaultWidth` in `public/column-resize.js` reads `f.rating.max` for a `rollup` or a `lookup` (the engine already hands the client `rating: { max, icon }` for both, `src/engine.js` `#ratingOf`), and adds the computed chip's own width to the icon run. Measure the chip and the chip's icon box the way `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` holds the rating cell's three numbers, rather than adding a fourth guessed constant. Feature #235 plans to move the `Σ` and `ƒ` marks out of the cell into the column header, which would change that measurement, so check where that Feature stands first.

Test in `test/rating-browser.test.mjs`: a rollup column over a max-5 rating, and a lookup over one, open with every icon inside the cell's content box.

- test/rating-browser.test.mjs: a rollup that draws rating icons opens wide enough for them (light and dark, Issue #564)
- test/rating-browser.test.mjs: a lookup that draws rating icons opens wide enough for them (Issue #564)

Measured on a scratch server at 4490 on a copy of the live db with a max-12 rating rolled up onto Showcase > Field Types, both data-bs-theme values: the column went from 93px holding 179px of icons and carrying the grid clipped class, to 187px with all twelve icons inside a 179px content box and overhang 0. issues.name: Wrong data: the v0.4.46 release notes claim a rating-column compact form and a fitted width that never shipped
issues.description:
Found while cutting v0.4.53 on 2026-10-01.

The published v0.4.46 notes (Release row v0.4.46, Sep 26 2026, and the matching GitHub Release) say, under Feature #235 and Issue #404:

> A rich column opens at the width its graphic needs (a rating's icons, a bar's track plus its widest figure, a ring or a heat tint plus its widest figure, a sparkline's 80px), never under a plain number's 88px; a width a person drags wins. A 10-icon rating opens unclipped (Issue #404), and a rating column dragged narrower than its icons, or past the fit cap, draws a compact `★ 7/10` instead of cutting icons off.

Two claims in that passage do not match the code that shipped:

1. "A 10-icon rating opens unclipped (Issue #404)" did not hold. The fragment that landed in v0.4.53 (`changelog.d/rating-column-fits-its-icons-404.md`, Gerrit change 523, commit aadc9a4) opens with "every rating column opened at the type default of 104px whatever its `max`", and that is what change 523 fixed in `defaultWidth` in `public/column-resize.js`. So between v0.4.46 and v0.4.53 the published notes asserted a fitted rating width that the code did not produce.

2. The compact `★ 7/10` form for a column narrowed past its icons was never landed at all. It is the deliberately unlanded half of Issue #404: it needs a design decision from Kyle. The v0.4.53 notes say so explicitly ("The compact `n / max` form for a column narrowed by hand waits on a design decision and is not in this release").

Why it matters: v0.4.46's notes are published on GitHub and exported to the public repo in `docs/development.json`, so the public record describes two behaviours that do not exist. A reader who narrows a rating column looking for `★ 7/10` finds nothing.

What to decide: either correct the v0.4.46 CHANGELOG section and its Release row Description to describe only what shipped, or land the compact form and close the gap forward. The second half still needs Kyle's design call, so correcting the record is the smaller move.

Filed by the overnight weave release session that cut v0.4.53 (merged ed4ed26).

2026-10-03: Fixed by Gerrit change 585, commit 89a7217 (merged into main as 4b501c7), Claude Opus 5.5 release-truth session. Fixed in: the next release, whose Release row links this under Fixes; no release was cut here. v0.4.46 never shipped (package.json went from 0.4.45 to 0.4.50; no tag, GitHub Release or CHANGELOG.md section), so there is no GitHub Release to amend. The v0.4.46 Release row carries a dated correction and no longer links Issue #404 or Feature #235. Both claimed behaviours shipped later (the 10-icon width in v0.4.53, the compact form in v0.4.62; since v0.4.63 a drag stops at the last icon), so no open Issue is needed. changelog.d/release-truth-629.md carries the correction into the next release notes.

issues.name: Looks broken: changelog-fold.mjs writes an em dash into every CHANGELOG version heading
issues.description:
Found while cutting v0.4.53 on 2026-10-01.

`node scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` writes the version heading as:

    ## v0.4.53 — 2026-10-01

The separator is a unicode em dash (U+2014). The house prose rule bans the em dash in anything a reader other than Kyle sees, and CHANGELOG.md is published in the repository.

Scope and real impact: small. The harness watcher (`scripts/weave-release-tags.mjs`) strips the heading when it builds the GitHub Release body, so the em dash does not reach the published release page; the body starts at the first bullet. Verified on v0.4.53: the published body is 24362 chars and 34 bullets with no heading line. So this is the file in the repo, not the release page.

Also note every prior section in CHANGELOG.md carries the same em dash, because they all came from the same generator. A fix should change the template in `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` and decide whether to rewrite the existing headings in one pass, so the file stays internally consistent rather than splitting at the version where the template changed.

Suggested separator: a comma, a colon, or parentheses around the date.

issues.name: Looks broken: a changelog fragment's internal aside reaches the public GitHub Release body
issues.description:
Found while cutting v0.4.53 on 2026-10-01.

The GitHub Release body is the folded `## v<version>` section of CHANGELOG.md, which is the changelog fragments copied verbatim. A fragment written in the internal register therefore publishes in that register.

The v0.4.53 body carries, in the Issue #410 bullet:

> Kyle called it extra padding to clean up.

That line addresses the team, not a reader deciding whether to update. The same bullet also keeps internal implementation asides that read oddly on a release page.

Two things worth separating here:

1. Fragment authoring. A fragment is published prose the moment it folds, so it should be written for the release-page reader. Nothing in the repo says that today, and `test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs` checks structure rather than register.

2. The published body has no lead and no grouping. v0.4.53 folded 33 fragments into 34 bullets ordered alphabetically by fragment filename, so the first thing a reader sees is the health-check `behind` chip (Issue #459) and the thirteen security fixes are scattered through the list. The grouped notes written for the release do exist, on the `Development/Release` row and in `docs/development.json`, but the watcher does not use them for the release body.

Options for 2: have `weave-release-tags.mjs` prefer the Release row's Description for the body, or have `changelog-fold.mjs` group the fold and carry a lead paragraph. The first reuses notes that are already written and reviewed.

issues.name: Looks broken: signing in from weave.grunion.ai takes five screens, and a new person dead-ends at a 403
issues.description:
## What was measured

Traced live against https://weave.grunion.ai on 2026-10-01 (Railway runs v0.4.52).

**Returning person (account already linked), five hops:**
1. `GET /` answers **401** with a bare HTML page: "This workspace requires authentication" and one link, "Sign in with a passkey or Clerk".
2. `/auth?next=/` offers two buttons, "Sign in with passkey" and "Sign in with Clerk", plus invite text.
3. "Sign in with Clerk" goes to `/api/auth/oidc/start`, 302 to `alive-cat-8639.clerk.accounts.dev/oauth/authorize`.
4. Clerk 302s to its hosted page `alive-cat-8639.accounts.dev/sign-in` (development instance, so the dev banner shows).
5. Callback `/api/auth/oidc/callback` mints a session, then the workspace opens.

**New person (Dylan), dead end:**
1-4 as above, then Clerk sign-up (public) with an email code. The callback answers **403** "No account for this identity ... Ask an operator to link one (weave account link <name> --email <address>)" (`src/routes.js:512`). The operator then needs `railway ssh` (Kyle's own Railway login; the project token has no shell) or the admin-token REST call `POST /api/accounts/<name>/identities`. Nothing in the web UI invites a person by email. The person repeats steps 1-5 afterwards.

## What good looks like

Linear, Attio and Notion: the root URL sends a signed-out visitor straight to the sign-in screen; an admin invites by email from Settings; the invited person clicks the email link, signs up once, and lands in the workspace. One provider screen, no interstitial, no operator CLI.

## Fix shape

* Signed-out `GET /` on a browser request redirects 302 to the sign-in route instead of serving the 401 page; with one door configured, redirect straight to the provider. API requests keep the 401.
* Drop the passkey door on this instance (change 514) so `/auth` has one button, or skip `/auth` entirely when only OIDC is on.
* Invite by email from the web UI: an admin adds an email, weave stores a pending identity, and the first OIDC sign-in with that verified email provisions and links the account. Optional allowlisted domain (for example `grunion.ai`) auto-provisions.
* Send the invite email (Resend, see the planned send-email feature).
* Move Clerk to a production instance on a grunion.ai subdomain so the dev banner and the `accounts.dev` hostname go away.

Related: #547 (passkey offered on a hostname where it cannot work), #478 (no deploy on push), Feature #212 (doors), change 514 (remove passkey door).

issues.name: Looks broken: an unlinked Clerk identity loops between the 403 page and Clerk with no way to switch accounts
issues.description:
## Reproduced

Live on https://weave.grunion.ai at v0.4.53, main df8ded6 (change 514, Feature #243), 2026-10-01.

Since 514, a signed-out visit to `/auth` answers 302 to `/api/auth/oidc/start`, and on to Clerk. An identity that is not linked to a weave account ends at the callback's 403 "No account for this identity". That page's "Back to sign in" link goes to `/auth`. `/auth` sends the person to Clerk again. Clerk still holds their session, signs them straight back in as the same identity, and the callback answers the same 403. The person cannot switch to another identity from inside weave; they have to find Clerk's sign-out on their own.

Checked: `GET /auth` (no cookie) 302 to `/api/auth/oidc/start`; `/auth?signed-out=1` serves the page without redirecting (0 "passkey" matches). Signed-out `GET /` still answers 401 with one link, "Sign in with Clerk", to `/auth?next=%2F`, one hop more than it needs.

## What good looks like

Linear, Notion and Vercel send an unrecognized identity to a page that names the email it signed in as and offers "Use a different account", which signs out at the provider and starts again. The page never links back into an automatic redirect.

## Fix shape

- The 403 page links to `/auth?signed-out=1` (no auto-redirect), and offers "Use a different account" pointing at the provider's end-session endpoint from discovery (`end_session_endpoint`), with `post_logout_redirect_uri` back to `/auth?signed-out=1`. Register that URI on the Clerk OAuth application `oa_3K6ajZDiOLdqHfSeCXqwo0njgdf`.
- The 403 page names the email the provider vouched for, so the person can see which account they used.
- Optional: signed-out `GET /` on a browser request answers 302 to `/auth?next=/` instead of the bare 401 page.

Related: #569 (five screens and the new-person 403 dead end; this row is the loop that 514's redirect adds to that dead end). #547 (passkey on the second hostname) no longer applies once 514 is live: the passkey door is gone.

Filed by the Clerk production cutover session, 2026-10-01, weave v0.4.53, commit df8ded6.

## Fixed 2026-10-02

Gerrit change 543 (patch set 2), commit 6075a3e, landed as merge 1d9bc89 on gerrit/main, stacked on 536 (Feature #252). Every refusal on the sign-in trip is now one page, `noindex` and `no-store`, whose way back is `/auth?signed-out=1`, never bare `/auth`. The no-account `403` reads "No access to <workspace>", points to an invite link and offers "Use a different account". It names no email: since 536, weave asks the provider for `openid` alone and holds none, which supersedes the fix shape's "name the email". Clerk's discovery has no `end_session_endpoint`, so the button starts a new trip with `prompt=login` (`/api/auth/oidc/start?fresh=1`) and no Clerk URI needed registering. The 409 invite-conflict page gets the same button, carrying the unspent invite. The rate-limit answer on those routes is a page, not JSON.

Gate: 2328 + 962 pass (one browser file retried green). GitHub main and `:4400` at 1d9bc89. Railway deployment aa77314f-ca8e-4edc-9d70-51ad5cfab325 SUCCESS. Live on weave.grunion.ai: `/auth?signed-out=1` 200 with no redirect; signed-out `/` 302 to `/auth?next=%2F`; `start?fresh=1` 302 to Clerk authorize with `prompt=login` (plain start carries none), and Clerk goes on to its sign-in page; a callback with a made-up state answers 400 with the new page linking only `/auth?signed-out=1`. The 403 page itself is proven by `test/auth-oidc.test.mjs`, not by a live unlinked identity. Not checked live: whether Clerk asks for credentials when its own session is open (Clerk documents `prompt=login` support since 2025-02-13).

issues.name: Looks broken: the weave mark shows notches at the center crossing in large exports
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** Kyle opened `~/Downloads/weave-logo-512-transparent.png` (exported 2026-10-01 11:35) and saw crescent notches in the blue strand on both sides of the center crossing. The notches also sit in `brand/assets/weave-mark-light.svg` and every other mark built by `markParts` in `src/mark.js`. At 512 px they are about 12 px deep; at favicon and header size they shrink under a pixel, so the platform logo and the loader hide them.

**Cause.** `rope()` in `src/mark.js` draws the center over-segment as a short quadratic, `M22.7,26.3 Q24,24 25.3,21.7` (t of roughly 0.33 to 0.67 of the middle segment). Mask A cuts strand A wherever strand B runs, with a halo of `sw + 2.5` = 6 units. The strands cross at about 53 degrees, so on the outer edge of strand A the cut runs about 5.1 units from the crossing along the strand. The over-segment reaches 2.6 units plus a 1.75 round cap, and a round cap adds nothing at the stroke edge. The gap between the two shows the background through. The quadratic also departs from the true cubic, which leaves a small step where the over-segment meets the strand.

**Good looks like.** In any over-under knot mark the over strand reads as one continuous stroke at any export size; only the under strand shows a gap.

**Fix shape.** Make each over-segment the exact cubic of strand A's odd segment, `M x,yB C x+p/2,yB x+p/2,yT x+p,yT` (for the mark: `M20,28 C24,28 24,20 28,20`). It lies on strand A, so no step, and its ends sit at the wave extremes, 8 units from strand B, so mask B still cuts strand B only at the crossing. A headless Chrome render at 480 px confirmed the notches gone (attached `cmp-crop.png`, left current, right fixed). Check the morph loaders: the over cutter in mask B is not tapered, so a longer over-segment may cut more of strand B at low amplitude; taper or fade it with the amplitude like `maskB`. Then rebuild `brand/assets` (SVG and PNG) with `node brand/build-logos.mjs`, add a geometry test that the over-segment covers the halo cut, and re-export the Downloads PNGs.

Filed by harness session 2026-10-01 (Opus 5.5), weave 0.4.53 at df8ded6.

**Fixed 2026-10-01 in c9cf4d1** (Gerrit change 525, Change-Id I5b5fe2adbb1f54b961f3e6152cbbd993fe3fd139, on weave 0.4.53). `rope()` in `src/mark.js` draws each over-segment as strand A's whole odd segment, the exact cubic `M20,28 C24,28 24,20 28,20` for the mark. The morph loaders (twist, spin) now fade the over cut in mask B with `stroke-opacity` as well as narrowing it; with the longer over-segment, narrowing alone left a hard slot along strand B on near-flat frames. Rebuilt every SVG, PNG and GIF in `brand/assets` and `public/brand`, `favicon.ico`, the two rail marks inlined in `public/index.html`, and the round 6 loader sheet.

Tests in `brand/build-logos.test.mjs`: the over-segment covers every point of strand A the halo cuts around an over crossing (mark, favicon, app icon, travel rope; 0.45 units bare before the fix), each over lies on strand A at amplitudes 4 to -4, the inline rail marks match `rope(3,8)`, and the morph over cut fades to 0 at the flat frame. Local npm test 2264 + 954 pass, 0 fail; gate Verified +1 on patch set 1.

Renders on #9a9a9a at 480 px in Chromium, before and after, are attached: `i571-before-after-512.png` (Kyle's 512 px transparent export, old left, new right) and `i571-spin-frames-before-width-fade-hybrid.png` (spin frames: old, width taper only, opacity only, shipped width plus opacity). The weave-on loader's center notch is gone as well.

issues.name: Wrong data: PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc answers 200 and blanks the document when the body does not use the `doc` key
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** On the live instance, weave main 6480f82, `test` workspace, `Marketing/Leads`.

```
POST /w/test/api/tables/Leads/entities  {"name":"doc route probe"}
PUT  /w/test/api/entities/<id>/doc      {"content":"alpha\n\nbeta","field":"Description"}
  -> 200 {"ok": true}
GET  /w/test/api/entities/<id>/doc?field=Description
  -> {"field":"Description","doc":""}
```

The write answers 200 and reports success. The document is empty.

**Where.** `src/routes.js:1078`:

```js
if (rx.method === 'PUT') { weave.setDoc(m[1], body.doc ?? body.markdown ?? '', fieldRef); return out(200, { ok: true }); }
```

The route reads `doc`, then `markdown`, then falls back to the empty string. A body carrying neither key is not refused: the fallback is written, so a PUT whose text sits under any other key erases the document and says it worked. The GET on the same path answers `{field, doc}`, so `doc` is the spelling the API itself hands back, but nothing in the response to a bad PUT says the body was not understood.

The POST on the same path (line 1079, `appendDoc`) takes the same fallback. Appending an empty string is harmless, which is why only the PUT destroys anything.

**What it cost.** An overnight fixer writing its note onto Issue #550 sent `{content, field}`, read 200 {"ok": true}, and blanked that Issue's 1,932-character Description. It was recovered in full from revision 1119, so nothing was lost, but the agent had no signal at all until it read the document back. Revision history is what makes this recoverable rather than fatal: `GET /api/entities/<id>/doc/revisions` and `POST /api/entities/<id>/doc/revisions/<seq>/restore`.

**Fix shape.** A PUT whose body carries neither `doc` nor `markdown` is a 400 naming the keys the route takes. Clearing a document stays possible with an explicit `{"doc": ""}`. The same check belongs on the POST, which otherwise reports a successful append of nothing. Test: `PUT` with an unknown key is a 400 and leaves the stored document exactly as it was; `PUT {"doc": ""}` still clears it; `POST` with an unknown key is a 400.

issues.name: Error: a change can land with no changelog fragment and nothing refuses it
issues.description:
**Reproduced tonight, by accident.** Gerrit change 527 fixed Issue #551 and merged as `e85ada8` carrying nine files, none of them under `changelog.d/`. The gate voted `Verified +1` and the change submitted. The fix would have been absent from the v0.4.54 release notes if the release step had not been given the missing bullet by hand.

**Where.** `test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs` guards one direction only: a commit that adds lines to `CHANGELOG.md` must also change the `package.json` version (`changelogGuard` in `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs`). Nothing asserts the other direction, that a commit touching `src/`, `public/` or `bin/` and naming an Issue or Feature in its subject also adds a `changelog.d/<slug>-<number>.md`. The routine that lands overnight fixes requires the fragment in the same commit as the fix, so the requirement exists and is simply unenforced.

**Why it matters.** The release notes are the one public record of what a version changed, and `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` can only fold what is on disk. A fix with no fragment ships silently, and the gap is invisible until someone compares the merged commits against the folded section, which is what caught this one.

**What good looks like.** towncrier and changesets both fail a check when a change carrying a user-visible edit has no fragment, and both let a commit opt out with an explicit marker for a refactor or a docs-only change.

**Fix shape.** Extend `changelogGuard` with the second direction: for each non-merge commit under test, if its diff touches `src/`, `public/`, `bin/` or `scripts/` and its subject names `(Issue #N)` or `(Feature #N)`, require a `changelog.d/` file added in the same commit, and allow an explicit `No-changelog: <reason>` trailer to opt out. A release commit, which deletes fragments and bumps the version, is already distinguishable and stays exempt. Tests: a fix commit with no fragment fails, the same commit with a fragment passes, the trailer passes, and a release commit passes.

Filed by the overnight weave fixer, session kind-hopper-b5bb3d, 2026-10-02, weave main `e85ada8`.



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-04T07:06:08.266Z · started · session dazzling-volhard-9cae91



🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · fixed · session dazzling-volhard-9cae91

**Fixed.** Gerrit change 595, merged as `0812e35`. `fragmentGuard` in `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` now reads the commits the other way round: a non-merge commit that changes `src/`, `public/`, `bin/` or `scripts/` and names `(Issue #N)` or `(Feature #N)` in its subject must add a `changelog.d/` file in that same commit. A refactor or a docs-only change opts out with a `No-changelog: <reason>` trailer, and a reasonless trailer does not; a release commit bumps the version and deletes the fragments it folded, so the bump exempts it. The expand and close arrows sit in their own row above the breadcrumb, and that row scrolls away with the content. **Cause.** `drawDock` (public/app.js:754) renders a separate `.dock-head` row (back, spacer, expand, close) as a sibling of `.dock-entity`. Only `.dock-entity .view-header` is sticky (style.css:2006, Issue #411), so `.dock-head` is in normal flow and leaves the screen on scroll. The full-page pose already puts its pose controls inside the crumb row (`poseControls`, app.js:11022, `crumb-actions` at 11049).

**Good looks like.** Notion, Linear and Fibery side peeks: one header row holding breadcrumb on the left and every control on the right, pinned to the top of the pane while the body scrolls.

**Fix shape.** Delete `.dock-head`. When `inPeek`, pass back/expand/close into `renderEntityView` and render them in the same `crumb-actions wv-toolbar` span as eye and kebab (back sits left of the crumb path, as on the full page's nav button). A browser test reads the rendered toggle and asserts the column cannot go below it, for the default words and for a long custom word.
