issues.name: Document history panel header slides under the sticky section head after a scroll
issues.description:
## Measured
weave v0.4.43 (227f778), Chromium 1280x640. Open History on an Issue's Description, scroll the entity 200px: the sticky section head from Issue #411 covers the panel's top border and part of the "N REVISIONS" row. Not clipped at rest at 390-1280px widths.

## Where
public/style.css .wv-doc-history (no top offset under the sticky head); the panel is prepended inside the section body (public/app.js openHistory).

Found during the #429 design review: https://claude.ai/artifact/JQHiv3fCeWP6rU2L2QvJHi



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-08T12:20:33.017Z · session fix-0402-88ee · from #708, #709

**Repro:** Not reproduced on :4400 at 56ed806, Chromium 1280x640, against Issue #708's row. The panel this row describes is gone: `.wv-doc-history` does not exist in public/style.css any more and nothing is prepended inside the section body. History now opens `.wv-activity`, a `position: fixed` rail at top 8px, right 8px, bottom 8px, width 328px, z-index 900, appended to document.body, with `body.wv-activity-open #main` giving it 344px of margin. Measured at scroll 0, 200, 400, 800 and 1287: the rail stays at [8, 632] throughout, so the sticky section head (z-index 5, inside the scroller) cannot reach it. The "N REVISIONS" row this row names is now the rail's own `.wv-act-head` plus its filter chips, which never enter the scrolling pane.

**Code:**
- public/style.css:1013 `.wv-activity { position: fixed; top: 8px; right: 8px; bottom: 8px; z-index: 900 }` — the rail that replaced the inline panel.
- public/style.css:1012 `body.wv-activity-open #main { margin-right: 344px }` — the pane yields the width instead of hosting the panel.
- public/app.js:10223-10240 renderView: a revision now hides `.doc-section-body` and inserts `.wv-act-view` after it inside the section; a field or comment prepends `.wv-act-view.top` into `.entity-body`.
- public/style.css:997-998 `.doc-section-head { position: sticky; top: calc(var(--wv-view-h, 0px) - var(--wv-pane-pad, 0px)); z-index: 5; background: var(--tblr-bg-surface) }` — the head this row blamed, unchanged.

**Fix shape:** Close this row as overtaken, or restate it. What remains of the shape it describes is ordinary sticky behaviour rather than the clipping it reports: the opaque section head still passes over `.wv-act-view` as the diff scrolls under it, the same way it passes over body text, which is what Issue #411 asked for. Nothing is clipped at rest at any scroll position measured. If the diff's `.wv-act-bar` stamps row should never go under the head, that is a new decision about the diff view, not a missing top offset on a panel that no longer exists, and it wants its own row with the scroll position named.

**Test to write first:**
- Only if the residual is wanted: test/doc-history-browser.test.mjs, at 1280x640 with a revision selected, scroll the pane until `.doc-section-head` is stuck and assert `.wv-act-bar` is not covered by it, which means `bar.top >= head.bottom` while the bar is on screen. Written against today's build it is red, since the bar passes under the head like any other content.
- A guard worth keeping either way: assert `.wv-activity` reports `position: fixed` and keeps its rect across a 1200px scroll, so a future move back into the scroller cannot reintroduce the clipping this row filed.

issues.name: Error: a date grain sent as a string fails with "A grain with no date parts must keep a time of day"
issues.description:
Source: canned disclosure eval, 2026-10-02. 32 runs of stock Claude Code agents (Sonnet and Opus, no weave skills) driving the real v0.4.54 engine over MCP, two tasks (household budget, sales pipeline), four context arms. Call logs and scores: ~/Documents/queue/weave-disclosure-eval/.

Measured: 23 failed weave_add_field calls across all four arms and both models. Agents send config {"grain":"month","format":"month"} or {"grain":"day","format":"iso"}. normalizeGrain (public/date-grain.js:42) accepts an array or {year,month,day} flags only, so a string collapses to no parts and the engine answers with the time-of-day error, which names the wrong problem. Agents then retry two or three shapes before landing on ["year","month"].

Good: the first write succeeds, or the error says what shape a grain takes.

Fix shape: either accept a single-part string as a one-element list, or refuse it with "grain is a list of parts, e.g. [\"year\",\"month\"]". Pick one; the refusal is the smaller change. Unit test in test/date-grain.test.mjs for a string grain.

Filed by the disclosure-eval session, 2026-10-02, v0.4.54, serving commit cc3b8d9.

Fixed 2026-10-02 by Gerrit change 538, commit 9545ef1 (merge 3e067ee) on main: normalizeGrain refuses a grain that is not a list or flags object with: grain is a list of parts, e.g. ["year","month"] for a month or ["year"] for a year; parts are year, month, day. No string alias. Test: test/date-grain.test.mjs.

1. On workspace creation, generate an adjective-animal name from two curated lists: neutral or positive adjectives only, no pair that reads as an insult; animals limited to those with a Lucide icon (bird, cat, dog, fish, rabbit, snail, squirrel, turtle and the rest Lucide ships), so the workspace icon can match the animal.
2. Display name capitalizes both words ("Quiet Otter"), slug kebab case (quiet-otter). The slug obeys the current rule at src/engine.js:2831, so this lands without waiting on #592; when #592 splits display name from slug, the display name moves to its own field.
3. On a slug collision within the instance, append a number (quiet-otter-2).
4. Replace every 'Weave Workspace' and bare 'workspace' fallback (engine.js:962, server.js, worker.js, bin/weave.js:233, routes.js:337) with the generated name; keep existing workspaces as they are.
5. Out of scope here, open with Kyle: the names of a seeded first space and table (proposal: Projects / Inbox) and the New table dialog's 'General' default.

Related: #592 (display name vs slug), #578 (agents name the workspace after the task).

The display name is Title Case ("Quiet Turtle", per Kyle 2026-10-02) and the slug is kebab case. A taken slug gets -2, -3. A file someone named (--data ./other.db) keeps its name, the Worker keeps its route name, and existing workspaces ("Weave Workspace", "workspace") are not renamed. issues.name: Wrong data: deleting a row by Table#N ref errors after a soft delete and leaves the row on a hard delete
issues.description:
Reproduced on gerrit/main cc3b8d9 (v0.4.54) through the MCP dispatcher, table S/T with rows a (#1) and b (#2):

- weave_delete_entity {entity: "T#1"} answers `Error: Entity 'T#1' not found`, yet row #1 IS moved to the trash (deletedAt set). The agent sees a failure for a write that landed.
- weave_delete_entity {entity: "T#2", hard: true} answers `{"id":"T#2","purged":true}` while row #2 is still in the table: query with includeDeleted returns 2 rows and readEntity("T#2") still returns b.

Cause: src/engine.js deleteEntity(id, ...) resolves the row with getEntity(id) but then uses the raw ref: the soft path returns this.readEntity(id), and readEntity does not resolve a trashed row by Table#N; the hard path runs `delete this.state.entities[id]` with the ref as the key, which deletes nothing, and returns {id, purged: true} with the ref as the id. Every MCP tool description says entity takes an id or "Table#publicId", so agents do pass refs. The CLI passes e.id (bin/weave.js:794) and is not affected; REST passes the path segment (src/routes.js:1011).

Good: every entity verb accepts the same ref forms; a delete answers success exactly when it deleted, and names the row's real id.

Fix shape: use e.id after the getEntity resolve throughout deleteEntity (soft return, hard purge, the purged reply, undo and activity), with a test for both paths by Table#N ref on MCP and REST.

Filed by the MCP token-efficiency session (Issues #595/#596), 2026-10-02, v0.4.54, commit cc3b8d9. Not fixed in that change; out of its scope.

Fixed by Gerrit change 582 (commit 89a3d0f, merged to gerrit/main as 313c26d), 2026-10-03, session reverent-cray-353456: deleteEntity binds the row's id once getEntity resolves the ref, so the soft reply, the hard purge, deleteDocRevisions, the save mark and the reply use it; getEntity also resolves a trashed row by Table#N, so a second delete, a read and a restore by ref find it. Gate: test/delete-by-ref.test.mjs (engine soft, hard, undo, restore; MCP; REST). Fixed in: the next release (unreleased at filing).

issues.name: Wrong data: a lookup of a select field shows the option id, not the option name

issues.description:
**Measured.** `hub.create(name)` in `src/server.js` validates with `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]*$/i` and checks for a duplicate through `instances.get(name)`, which is case-sensitive. The file is `<name>.db` in the data dir. On a case-sensitive filesystem (the Railway Linux volume) `Acme` and `acme` both pass and become two workspaces, two files and two URLs (`/w/Acme/`, `/w/acme/`). On macOS (case-insensitive APFS) the second create would open the first file under a new name. Found while designing per-workspace MCP routes for Feature #254, where `/w/<name>/mcp` is the address an agent stores.

**Good looks like.** Slack, Notion and GitHub treat workspace and org slugs as case-insensitive: one slug, any casing resolves to it, and creation refuses a case variant.

**Fix shape.** Lowercase the name at create and at lookup (or refuse uppercase in the regex), and have `get` resolve case-insensitively so existing mixed-case workspaces keep working. Test: create `acme`, then `Acme` answers 409.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-02 (weave v0.4.54 on main, v0.4.53 live).

Fixed by Gerrit change 583 (commit f581770, merged to gerrit/main as c18a52e), 2026-10-03, session beautiful-mclaren-f542cc: new slugs are lowercase, hub.get resolves any casing (an exact match first, so two legacy files that differ only by case both still resolve), and create or rename to a case variant of a held slug answers 409 over REST and MCP. Reproduced on 388c77c before the fix: create('Acme') after create('acme') succeeded on APFS and opened acme.db under the new name; get('ACME') was null. No existing workspace file is renamed. Gate: test/workspace-slug.test.mjs (create acme, then Acme answers 409; a mixed-case Acme.db keeps resolving at Acme and acme). Fixed in: the next release (unreleased at filing).

issues.name: Slow: Verified gate serves the newest approved change first, so older ones wait for hours
issues.description:
**Measured** on 2026-10-02. Change 530 (Issue #583) got Code-Review +2 and then sat unverified for about 83 minutes while the gate ran newer changes. The poller's policy line at that point read `targets 539/1, 538/1, 537/1, 536/1, 535/1, 534/1, 533/1, 529/2, 531/1, 530/1`: ten +2 tips, with 530 last. Change 532, pushed after 530, was verified first; 539 started next. Each full suite runs roughly 15 to 60 minutes (cap 3600s), so 530 had several hours of queue ahead of it, and every new push by another session would land ahead of it again.

**Cause.** `weave-review-poll.mjs` lists open changes with `/a/changes/?q=is:open+project:weave` (line 74), which Gerrit returns most recently updated first. `nextGateTarget` (line 44) takes the first unrun target from that fresh listing, and `selectGateTargets` (line 28) keeps the listing's order. The gate is therefore last in, first out: on a busy day the oldest approved change can wait indefinitely. Fresh listings each run were the right fix for stale queues; they made ordering depend on Gerrit's sort instead.

**Good looks like.** Zuul and Gerrit's own submit queues serve approved changes first in, first out by the time the approval landed, so a change's wait is bounded by the queue length when it was approved.

**Fix shape.** Sort `selectGateTargets` output by the timestamp of the Code-Review +2 vote (from `labels['Code-Review'].all[].date`), oldest first, falling back to `created`. Test in `weave-review-poll.test.mjs`: three +2 tips with approval dates out of listing order come back oldest approval first; a new +2 arriving later never jumps an older one. Workaround until then: `scripts/weave-review.sh <n>` runs one change by hand (used for 530 on 2026-10-02).

Filed by harness session 2026-10-02 (Claude Opus 5.5), gate poller at ~/.harness-serve a753b72.

issues.name: Slow: the gate verifies the newest +2 first, so an older change waits behind every later push
issues.description:
## Measured

2026-10-02, harness `scripts/weave-review-poll.mjs` (served from `~/.harness-serve`), log `/tmp/weave-review-poll.log`.

- Change 531 (Feature #248) took Code-Review +2 at 01:39 UTC. The poll that ran next listed `targets 532/1, 531/1, 530/1` and verified 532.
- The following poll listed `targets 539/1, 538/1, 537/1, 536/1, 535/1, 534/1, 533/1, 529/2, 531/1, 530/1` and verified 539.
- About an hour later it listed `targets 546/1, 544/1, 543/1, 542/1, 541/3, 540/1, 534/2, 538/1, 537/1, 536/1, 535/1, 533/1, 529/2, 531/1, 530/1` and verified 546. 531 and 530 had moved from second and third to the last two places.
- One gate took about 40 minutes at load average 47 on 10 cores (a single browser case ran 75 s in the 539 log). With 14 targets ahead, 531 had no expected start.

Cause: `LIST` is Gerrit's default `is:open` order, most recently updated first, and `nextGateTarget` takes the first eligible change from it. A change pushed later always sorts ahead of one already waiting, so under a fleet of agents the oldest +2 can wait indefinitely.

## What good looks like

Zuul's gate pipeline and Gerrit's own submit queue serve changes in the order they became ready. An older approved change runs before a newer one.

## Fix shape

In `selectGateTargets` / `nextGateTarget`, order targets by the time of their Code-Review +2 (oldest first), falling back to the change number. Add a test in `scripts/weave-review-poll.test.mjs` with three +2 tips approved in order and listed newest first, asserting the oldest is gated first.

Workaround used: running `weave-review.sh 531` by hand queues it on the machine-wide gate lock.

Filed by the Feature #248 onboarding session, 2026-10-02, weave v0.4.54, gerrit/main cc3b8d9.

issues.name: Slow: an orphaned wall-clock cap timer from a dead gate holds the gate lock for up to an hour
issues.description:
## Measured
2026-10-02 21:25-22:05 PDT. `~/.gerrit/weave/gate.lock/change` read 548 for over 30 minutes while the load average sat near 3. `lsof ~/.gerrit/weave/gate.lock.flock` showed the flock held by pid 60799 (`bash scripts/weave-review.sh 548 --submit`, ppid 1) and its child `sleep 3600` (60800). The pid recorded in `gate.lock/pid` (81743) no longer existed, and change 548 was ABANDONED; its log ends `RETRIED and still red: the run failed without naming a file`. Pid 60799 was the wall-clock cap subshell, `( sleep "$CAP"; kill -TERM -- -"$SUITE" )` at harness `scripts/weave-review.sh` line 234: it inherits descriptor 9, so when the gate's main process died without killing it, it kept the gate lock until its hour-long sleep ran out. Eight other gate runs were queued behind it. Killing process group 60799 released the lock at once and 538 took it.

## Good looks like
A dead gate frees the lock within seconds. The cap timer never holds the lock descriptor.

## Fix shape
Close descriptor 9 in the cap subshell (`( exec 9>&-; sleep "$CAP"; ... )`), and have the gate's EXIT trap kill the cap subshell's process group. Optionally: gate_lock_acquire reports a holder whose recorded pid is dead.

Filed by the Feature #252 harness session, 2026-10-02, while gating Gerrit 536.



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-08T08:33:14.085Z · session fix-0002-62d0 · from #609, #594, #700, #566, #615

**Repro:** Not reproduced, and this routine cannot close it: the fix is in the harness repository. Measured at 08:33Z, after three gate runs this fire. The real lock is an fcntl flock on ~/.gerrit/weave/gate.lock.flock, and it is free: a LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB take succeeded immediately, and lsof reports no process holding that file. No weave-review.sh is running and no sleeping cap subshell is alive. The gate.lock directory beside it still reads pid 15802, change 740, started 1791447586 (08:19:46Z), and pid 15802 is gone, because gate_lock_release closes the descriptor and never clears those three files. A reader who checks gate.lock/pid sees a dead pid and concludes the lock is stuck; the lock it names is not the lock. All three gates this fire released cleanly: their logs read "gate lock: waited 0s" and "gate lock: held 428s", 429s and 429s.

**Code:**
- The fix surface is ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-review.sh line 247, the cap subshell (sleep "$CAP"; kill -TERM -- -"$SUITE") &, and its lock helper ~/.harness-serve/scripts/weave-gate-lock.sh. Both are in the harness repository, not the weave tree, so no Gerrit change against weave can close this row and the fix cannot be served by :4400 or verified there.
- gate_lock_acquire opens descriptor 9 on gate.lock.flock and flocks it; its comment says a child that inherits the descriptor holds the slot until it exits. The cap subshell at 247 is such a child, and it sleeps for WEAVE_SUITE_CAP_SECS, 3600 by default.
- Line 250 already does kill -- -"$WATCHDOG" after the suite returns, so the orphan is cleaned on the normal path. What the row describes is the path where the gate dies before line 250 runs: the EXIT trap at line 93 calls cleanup, which calls gate_lock_release, which closes descriptor 9 in the parent only.
- Only the stale metadata is observable after the fact, and it is observable after every clean run too, so it is not evidence of the defect.

**Fix shape:** A harness change, as the row says: close descriptor 9 inside the cap subshell (9>&- in the subshell) so it never holds the slot, and have the EXIT trap kill the watchdog process group as well as release the descriptor. Worth adding beside it: clear gate.lock/pid, change and started on release, so the directory stops reading as held once the lock is free. A fixer run can measure this and write it down, which is what this note is, but it cannot land it.

**Test to write first:**
- None in weave. A harness-side case would start a gate, kill it between the suite and line 250, and assert that the next gate takes the lock without waiting out the cap.

issues.name: Wrong data: after an upgrade /api/health reports a latest release older than the running version for up to a day
issues.description:
## Measured
2026-10-03 06:16Z, https://weave.grunion.ai/api/health right after Railway deployment afb54d54 (dc1a47f) started the container at 06:14:48Z:

```
"version": "0.4.56", "startedAt": "2026-10-03T06:14:48.088Z",
"latestRelease": "0.4.54", "releaseCheckedAt": "2026-10-03T00:49:48.082Z", "releaseBehind": false
```

GitHub's Latest release at that moment was v0.4.56 (published 06:08:29Z). The instance reported a latest release two versions older than the build it was running.

Cause: `createReleaseCheck` (src/update-check.js) loads `update-check.json` beside `WEAVE_DATA`, which sits on the volume and survives a redeploy. `refresh()` skips while `now - attemptedAt < interval` (one day), and nothing compares the cache with the version that is starting, so a new build inherits the old build's answer for up to 24 hours. Noticed by the parent harness session during the Feature #250 bootstrap.

## What good looks like
A running version never reports a latest release older than itself. The check re-asks at boot when the cached answer is older than the running version (or was written by a different version); within one version, the once-a-day cache keeps working as documented.

## Fix shape
1. In `createReleaseCheck`, ignore (or re-fetch over) a cached `latest` when `newerVersion(version, cached.latest)`, and record the writing version in the cache file.
2. Test in test/update-check.test.mjs: a cache holding 0.4.54 read by a 0.4.56 build makes one request at boot; a cache holding 0.4.56 read by 0.4.56 makes none.

## Not affected
Feature #250's supervisor keeps its own check in memory (no cache file, ten-minute interval, one check right after it starts listening) and compares against the version it serves, so this stale field does not delay a swap.

---
Filed 2026-10-02 by the Feature #250 harness session (Claude Opus 5.5), weave v0.4.56, commit dc1a47f.

2026-10-03: Fixed by Gerrit change 585, commit 89a7217 (merged into main as 4b501c7), Claude Opus 5.5 release-truth session. Fixed in: the next release, whose Release row links this under Fixes; no release was cut here. update-check.json records the version that wrote it; another version, or a cache from before this fix, asks GitHub again at boot; status() never reports a latest release older than the running version. Tests in test/update-check.test.mjs.

issues.name: Slow: the first live self-update stalled every request for about ten seconds after the switch
Looks broken: Entity card's top edge scrolls away; only the crumb row and title stay
issues.description:
**Reproduced** from Kyle's screenshots on live :4400 (v0.4.54, 4c0c0fc), Issue #601 open full page. At rest the entity card shows its rounded top edge, its top padding, the crumb row (breadcrumb, eye, kebab, collapse, close) and the title. After a scroll the crumb row and title stay pinned, but the card's top edge, rounded corners and padding above the crumb row scroll away, so the header floats against the window edge with no frame around it.

**Cause.** `#main` (style.css:373) is `min-height: calc(100vh - 16px)` inside a document that scrolls; the whole page moves and only `#main > .view-header` sticks at `top: 0` (style.css:303). The docked pane does the same inside `#dock` with `top: -14px` (style.css:2006). Sticky can pin the header; it cannot pin the card's own edge and padding, which belong to the element that is scrolling.

**Good looks like.** Linear, Notion and Fibery entity pages: the card or pane is fixed to the window, its frame never moves, and only the body below the title scrolls inside it.

**Fix shape.** Make each panel a fixed-height frame: `#main` and `#dock` get `height: calc(100vh - 16px)` and `overflow: hidden`, with the crumb row and title in a non-scrolling head and everything below the title in one inner scroller (`overflow-y: auto`). Move sticky offsets that read the page scroll (grid thead `top: var(--wv-view-h)`, doc rail, section heads, `view-header-loose` on html and #dock) onto the inner scroller. Browser test, both themes, full page and dock: scroll the body to the bottom; the card's top border, crumb row and title keep the same `getBoundingClientRect().top` as at rest. Lands with or after the shell row filed alongside (independent pane scrolling).

Filed by harness session 2026-10-03 (Claude Opus 5.5), weave v0.4.54, commit 4c0c0fc, from Kyle's screenshots. Follows Issue #583 (change 530).

**Fixed 2026-10-03** in Gerrit change 570, stacked on change 569 (Issue #609), landed as decb13c (merge 2311534) after weave v0.4.60; it ships with the next release through changelog.d/entity-frame-holds-608.md. issues.name: Error: a release that crashes after the swap takes the hosted instance down, with no rollback to the release before it
issues.description:
## Measured
Read from `src/supervisor.js` at `4c0c0fc` (Feature #250, live on https://weave.grunion.ai since 2026-10-03).

- Before the switch, failure is covered: `swapTo` (about line 226) kills a new worker that is not healthy within `healthTimeoutMs` (60 s) and the old worker keeps serving.
- After the switch there is no cover. The old worker gets `SIGTERM` once it drains (line 252, `drainTimeoutMs` 30 s). If the new worker exits later, the exit handler (line 121) calls `onWorkerDied`, which defaults to `process.exit(1)` (line 84). Railway restarts the container: an outage of a container boot plus health check.
- On that restart `bootRelease` (line 70) picks the newest release with the OK mark that is not in `failed`. The crashed release has its OK mark and is not in `failed`, so it boots again. A release that passes `/api/health` and crashes on the first real request loops: boot, serve, crash, restart.
- Only a failure at boot marks the release failed, and the fallback then is `image` (the bootstrap build, currently 0.4.56), not the previous release. The comment at line 268 says the previous release is kept on disk because "a rollback needs nothing more", but no code path boots it directly.
- Health only proves the server answers. A release that serves wrong data or 500s on real routes is never rolled back.

## What good looks like
Blue/green with a probation window, as in Kubernetes rolling updates with `progressDeadlineSeconds` or Fly's canary health checks: the old worker stays warm after the switch, and the supervisor switches straight back, inside the same container, when the new one crashes or its error rate rises during probation. Nothing restarts and no request is lost.

## Fix shape
1. After the switch, keep the old worker running (not listening for new connections) for a probation window, for example 5 minutes, instead of `SIGTERM` after the drain.
2. During probation, a new-worker exit or a 5xx share above a threshold switches traffic back to the old worker, marks the new release `failed` with the reason, and records `lastSwap.ok = false, rolledBack: true`.
3. After probation, stop the old worker as today.
4. On a crash after probation: mark the serving release failed before exiting, so `bootRelease` boots the previous release on restart, not the same one and not `image`.
5. Migrations: a release that has already run a schema migration cannot hand back to a worker that cannot read the new schema. Either keep probation before deferred migrations settle, or record in the release which schema it needs and refuse a rollback across one.
6. Tests: a new worker that crashes 10 s after the switch hands traffic back with zero failed requests under a request loop; a crash after probation boots the previous release on restart.

Decision pending: Kyle asked for the row only, no build (2026-10-03). The overnight fixer must not pick this up until he says build.

Filed by the harness session 2026-10-03 (Claude Opus 5.5), live instance v0.4.60, weave-serve at 4c0c0fc. Related: Feature #250, Issue #606, Issue #607.

issues.name: Slow: a change the gate verified goes stale before it lands, because the gate merges main before it waits for the lock and submits after main has moved
issues.description:
## Measured
Gerrit change 537 (Feature #250) took 4 h 15 min from upload (01:57Z, 2026-10-03) to merge (06:12Z). About 2 h of that went to two conflicts with main, not to defects:

| Patch set | Gate result | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PS1 | Verified -1, 03:30Z | real: two registry contracts |
| PS2 | Verified -1, 04:02Z | merge gate: does not merge cleanly with main `d163594` (`bin/weave.js` HELP block) |
| PS3 | Verified +1, 05:33Z | submit then failed: path conflict after Issue #594 (`openDefaultWorkspace`) and v0.4.55 landed while PS3 sat in the queue |
| PS4 | Verified +1, merged 06:12Z | rebased by hand, full gate run again |

The cause is in harness `scripts/weave-review.sh` at `d32bfcd`:
- Lines 162-176 fetch `gerrit/main` and merge it into the change, then line 179 calls `gate_lock_acquire`. The comment above it says the fetch and merge gate still overlap across concurrent runs. A run can wait hours for the lock (Issues #601, #602, #604), so the merge it tests is against a main that is hours old by the time the tests start.
- Lines 240-249 submit after the tests, against whatever main is then. A change that was green on a stale merge either conflicts at submit (PS3) or lands an untested combination.
- On any conflict the gate votes -1 and exits. Nothing rebases, so every textual conflict costs a full queue wait plus a full run (about 90 min under tonight's load of 15 open changes).

## What good looks like
A merge queue: GitHub merge queue, Zuul's dependent pipeline, bors-ng. The change is merged with main at the moment its test run starts, inside the queue's lock, and lands before the lock is released, so the tested tree is the tree that lands. A trivial rebase is done by the queue, not the author.

## Fix shape
1. Keep the pre-lock merge as a cheap fast-fail, then after `gate_lock_acquire` fetch `gerrit/main` again and re-merge. Test that merge.
2. Submit before `gate_lock_release`, while main cannot have moved through the gate. Record the main SHA tested in the Verified message and refuse the submit if `gerrit/main` moved anyway (a hand submit).
3. When the in-lock merge conflicts only because main moved, call Gerrit `POST /changes/<n>/rebase` once; if Gerrit rebases cleanly, run on the rebased patch set inside the same lock hold instead of voting -1 and requeuing.
4. A true conflict still votes -1, with the conflicting paths named.
5. Tests in `scripts/weave-review*.test.mjs`: main moves while a run waits for the lock; the run tests the fresh merge and lands it with no second queue wait.

Related: Issues #601, #602 (gate ordering), #604 (orphaned lock timer).

## Where the fix lands
This fix is in the HARNESS repo (`grunion-ai/harness`), not in weave, so it does not go through Gerrit. Work in your own harness worktree from `origin/main` (`git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<slug>-<suffix> -b claude/<slug>-<suffix> origin/main`), never in the shared checkout. Land it as a harness PR with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u grunion-ai)`, self-review and squash-merge per the harness Ship Mandate, then confirm the change is live: launchd `ai.grunion.weave-review` runs `scripts/weave-review-serve.mjs`, which fast-forwards `~/.harness-serve` to `origin/main` each cycle, so check `git -C ~/.harness-serve log -1` carries the merge and the next gate run logs the in-lock merge. Never `pkill` by pattern (see memory pkill-pattern-kills-other-sessions-gates); never run the gate by hand while the poller owns the lock.

Kyle cleared this for the overnight fixer on 2026-10-03.

Filed by the harness session 2026-10-03 (Claude Opus 5.5), from the change 537 landing; harness main `d32bfcd` for `scripts/weave-review.sh`.

issues.name: Error: End does not move the caret in a code block on the phone dock
issues.description:
**Reproduced** in Chromium (Playwright) at 390x844 on weave v0.4.60 (gerrit/main 4c0c0fc): dock an entity whose document holds a fenced code block (`#/table/<id>?e=<entity>`), click the code, press End. The caret stays at the CODE element's offset 0 (`getSelection()` reads `{node: "CODE", off: 0}`), so typed text lands at the start of the line. At 1300x900 on the full page the same press moves the caret to offset 12, the line's end.

**Cause.** The phone dock is `position: fixed; inset: 0` with `overscroll-behavior: contain` (public/style.css, the `@media (max-width: 600px)` `#dock` rule, from Issue #549). In Chromium, `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the scroll container stops End from moving the caret in a contenteditable code block. Adding the stylesheet override `#dock { overscroll-behavior: auto !important }` makes the same press land at offset 12. Found while landing Issue #609, where `overscroll-behavior: contain` on `#main` broke `test/code-raw-toggle-browser.test.mjs` (two cases, End then type: `"```js\n // hiconst x = 1;\n```"` and `"```jxs"`); #609 left it off #main and the desktop dock for that reason.

**Good looks like.** End moves to the end of the line in every pose, as it does on the full page and in any native text field.

**Fix shape.** Drop `overscroll-behavior: contain` from the phone `#dock` rule; the document no longer scrolls since #609, so nothing is left for the sheet's scroll to chain into. Browser test at 390x844: dock a code document, click the code, press End, type, and the saved markdown has the text at the line's end.

The stylesheet's own comment from Issue #609 already said `#main` and the dock must leave the property alone for this exact reason; the phone sheet was the last place still setting it. Nothing is lost: since #609 the document no longer scrolls, so a scroll that runs out at the sheet's edge has nowhere to chain.

**Tests added:**

It docks the record (`#/table/<id>?e=<entity>`), clicks the code, presses End, types ` // hi`, and asserts the saved markdown reads ```` ```js\nconst x = 1; // hi\n``` ````; it then asserts the sheet computes `overscroll-behavior: auto`. issues.name: Looks broken: Opening another record in the dock lands at the old record's scroll position
issues.description:
**Reproduced** in Chromium at 1440x900 on weave v0.4.60, both before and after Issue #609 (old code at 4c0c0fc and the stack at 2311534 give the same numbers). Dock a record with a long document (`#/table/<id>?e=<a>`), scroll the dock to its end (scrollTop 4,356), then open another long record from the table's `#id` link. The new record opens at scrollTop 1,778 of 2,662 (clientHeight 884), its title and the top of its document off screen above the reader. On live :4400 the same happens from the Guide dock (CLI reference scrolled to 1,255) into the Issue table's #609 row, which opened at its own end, scrollTop 807 of 1,691. A full-page hop resets: `#/entity/<a>` scrolled to 4,364, then `#/entity/<b>` lands at 0.

**Cause.** `drawDock()` (public/app.js) keeps the one `#dock` element across records: `panel.replaceChildren(host)` and an awaited `renderEntityView` fill it again, and nothing resets `scrollTop`, so the browser only clamps the old offset to the new content's height.

**Good looks like.** Linear, Notion and Fibery side peeks open each record at its top. A back step (Esc or the back arrow, Issue #276) could return to the offset the reader left, which is a separate choice.

**Fix shape.** When the dock's top frame changes to a different entity, set `#dock.scrollTop = 0` before the render paints; keep the offset for a redraw of the same entity (an edit, a `keepScroll` refresh). Browser test: dock record A, scroll to the end, open record B from the table, assert `#dock.scrollTop` is 0 and B's title is on screen; then redraw B by editing a field and assert its scroll held.

Filed by harness agent session 2026-10-03 (Claude Opus 5.5) while verifying Issues #608 and #609 on :4400, weave v0.4.60, commit 2311534.

issues.name: Gap: ws-rail-inset-browser skips itself on macOS, so a clean suite never reports skipped 0
issues.description:
## Measured

`test/ws-rail-inset-browser.test.mjs:57` ends its measurement with `if (!seen.Issue.gutter) return t.skip(\`overlay scrollbars here: no gutter to measure (${all})\`)`. The case only asserts anything on a platform that reserves a classic scrollbar gutter, so on macOS, which draws overlay scrollbars by default, it skips every run. A full suite in a worktree off `gerrit/main` on 2026-10-04 reported 3,674 tests, `fail 0`, and exactly one skip: this case. The browser lane itself ran in full, 1,076 tests, so the Playwright `node_modules` symlink was present and this is not the missing-symlink case.

## Effect

Two things follow. The rail-inset behaviour the case was written to pin is never checked on the machine that gates every change, so a regression in it lands green. And `# skipped 0`, which the overnight fixer routine requires of a full suite as its signal that the browser lane really ran, is unreachable here: every clean run reports one skip, so the rule cannot be read literally and a session that honours it either aborts a good fix or learns to ignore the count.

## What good looks like

A clean full suite on this machine reports `skipped 0`, so a non-zero skip count again means something went wrong. The rail-inset behaviour is checked on every run rather than only on platforms with classic scrollbars.

## Fix shape

Give the case a gutter to measure instead of skipping: Playwright can force classic scrollbars for the context, and the assertion block already handles a real gutter. Where a measurement genuinely cannot exist on this platform, split the case so the part that does not need a gutter (the rail at left 0, the sidebar at 52, `scrollLeft` 0) still asserts, and only the short-table comparison is conditional. Either way the suite ends with no skips.

issues.name: Error: system-tables-nav browser case loses a repaint between waitForSelector and $eval, costing unrelated changes a Verified -1
issues.description:
## Measured

The gate's browser lane fails `test/system-tables-nav-browser.test.mjs` on changes that cannot touch it, with:

```
not ok - browser: three fixed rows under the spaces; Trash opens the workspace trash
  error: 'page.$eval: Failed to find element matching selector "#main input.view-title"'
  system-tables-nav-browser.test.mjs:41
```

Two gate logs in `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs` carry it, both on test-only or unrelated changes:

| Log | Change | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `598-1.log` | 598 | red on the first run, green on the retry, so the gate let it stand |
| `600-1.log` | 600 (a test-only case added to `test/pane-scroll-shell-browser.test.mjs` for Issue #451) | red twice, so the change took a Verified -1 it had not earned |

Green locally on change 600's commit in three runs, including `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE=4` (1 of 1 each time). The gate ran it at half the cores alongside the rest of the browser lane.

## Root cause

Lines 40 and 41 of `test/system-tables-nav-browser.test.mjs` are two separate round trips to the same selector:

```js
await page.waitForSelector('#main input.view-title');
assert.equal(await page.$eval('#main input.view-title', (i) => i.readOnly), true, ...);
```

`waitForSelector` resolves on the node the first paint put there. `drawDatabase` opens with `main.replaceChildren()`, and the view header settles on a ResizeObserver after that, so the header repaints and the node `waitForSelector` saw is detached. `$eval` resolves the selector again from scratch and throws when it lands in the gap. On an idle machine the gap is sub-frame; under the lane's load it is wide enough to lose. Nothing about the assertion is wrong, only the way it reads.

Row #290 collects flaking cases but names different ones, and row #619's pair miss wall-clock budgets rather than a detached node, so the fix shape there does not apply here.

## Good looks like

The read retries with the selector, so a repaint between finding the node and reading it costs nothing.

## Fix shape

Read through a locator, which re-resolves on each attempt, instead of a handle taken once:

```js
assert.equal(await page.locator('#main input.view-title').evaluate((i) => i.readOnly), true, ...);
```

Then audit the rest of the browser suites for the same two-step shape: a `waitForSelector` followed by `$eval` or `$$eval` on a selector the view repaints.

**Code:**
- The box is the view popover, not the grid. Frames are the 1400x900 journey viewport scaled to the 640px cap in recordFrames (0.457), so the popover's measured left 659px top 69px lands at frame 301,31 and its box at 144x162. The grid's own re-render happens 6 ms AFTER the flash frame.

This flash sits 19 ms after the journey's click and 16 ms after its Escape, inside that same window, in the one rule the gate never reached. The popover is on screen for about two frames only because the journey opens it and dismisses it 36 ms later; a reader holds it open for as long as they are reading it.

issues.name: Error: applying a schema that creates related tables fails with 'Use addRelation() to create relation fields'
issues.description:
## Reproduced

Two tables in one space, `Deal.Company` a relation to `Company` (inverse `Deals`), a lookup over it on Deal and a rollup over `Deals` on Company. `fresh.applySchema(w.describeSchema().filter((s) => !s.system))` into an empty workspace threw `Use addRelation() to create relation fields` after making the first table, leaving `CRM/Company` with Name and Description only.

Cause: the create-table branch of `applySchema` (`src/engine.js:2629-2641` at a438721) passed every descriptor to `addField`, relations included, and created each table's fields in the table's own pass. A relation can name a table the document lists later, a rollup crosses an inverse that relation mints, and a formula may read either, so no single per-table order works.

## Good looks like

Airtable's base duplication and Fibery's space templates both recreate linked records and their lookups and rollups in one step: the schema arrives whole or not at all.

## Fix shape

A table the apply creates gets its plain fields at once. Its relations (through `addRelation`, with the cardinality read from both ends of the document), then its lookups, rollups and formulas (in passes until none is left, so a rollup may read a formula and a formula a lookup), then the view fields' config and the table costume, come after every table in the document exists.

Found while building Feature #261 (Use Template), whose fidelity test copies a space wearing every costume into a fresh workspace through applySchema. Fixed in the same Gerrit change (topic use-template-261); this row records it.

Filed by the use-template session, 2026-10-05, weave v0.4.65, commit a438721.

issues.name: Wrong data: applying a schema drops select and multiselect option icons
issues.description:
## Reproduced

A select with options `{name: 'Lead', hue: 'blue', icon: 'lucide:sparkles'}`. `describeSchema()` carries the icon in `optionsFull`; applying that document onto a fresh workspace made the option with no icon, and applying an edited `options` list onto the same workspace cleared every option's icon.

Cause: `configFromDescriptor` in `applySchema` (`src/engine.js:2531-2542` at a438721) rebuilt each option from its name and colour alone, and `fieldChanged` compared colours only, so an icon edit was not even seen as a change.

## Good looks like

Notion and Fibery keep an option's emoji or icon through a template copy and through every option-list edit.

## Fix shape

Carry `icon` from `optionsFull` into the rebuilt option; an option the document does not give an icon keeps the one it had; `fieldChanged` counts an icon difference.

Found while building Feature #261 (Use Template), whose fidelity test copies a space wearing every costume into a fresh workspace through applySchema. Fixed in the same Gerrit change (topic use-template-261); this row records it.

Filed by the use-template session, 2026-10-05, weave v0.4.65, commit a438721.

issues.name: Wrong data: applying a schema makes a many-to-many relation one-to-many
issues.description:
## Reproduced

A document describing a many-to-many relation (both ends `many: true`) applied to a workspace whose tables exist but lack the relation created it as `one-to-many`, so the inverse end held one row.

Cause: `applySchema` (`src/engine.js:2696-2700` at a438721) chose the cardinality from the descriptor's own `many` alone: `fDoc.many ? 'one-to-many' : 'many-to-one'`. The inverse end's `many` sits on the target table's descriptor and was never read; one-to-one could not be expressed either.

## Good looks like

Airtable and Fibery recreate a link field with the same cardinality on both sides.

## Fix shape

Find the inverse descriptor in the same document (`targetDb` + `inverseField`) and map the two `many` flags to one of the four cardinalities; without the inverse, the older reading stands.

Found while building Feature #261 (Use Template), whose fidelity test copies a space wearing every costume into a fresh workspace through applySchema. Fixed in the same Gerrit change (topic use-template-261); this row records it.

Filed by the use-template session, 2026-10-05, weave v0.4.65, commit a438721.

issues.name: Wrong data: a lookup of a relation field shows the target row's uuid, not its name
issues.description:
Reproduced on the CRM template space (weave workspace, :4400, v0.4.65 at 52acab9): CRM/Activities has `Company`, a lookup over the `Contact` relation (many-to-one to CRM/Contacts) reading the contact's `Company` field, itself a many-to-one relation to CRM/Companies.

The grid cell prints `73ec5913-99de-407e-93e8-af823f3e662b` where it should print `Northwind Traders` as a chip. `POST /api/tables/<Activities>/query` returns the same: `fields.Company = ["73ec5913-…"]` and `raw.Company` identical, so every reader (grid, entity page, MCP, CSV) sees the id. weave_build's dry-run `computed` sample shows the same uuids, so the build preview cannot catch it either.

Where: src/engine.js, the `case 'lookup'` dressing at ~6973 to 6981 (gerrit/main 52acab9): a looked-up select, multiselect or workflow is dressed through `#displayValue` (Issue #598), and "other types keep their value as read", which for a relation is the id list. The sibling grid renderer has no relation branch for a lookup column either.

Good looks like: Fibery and Airtable both render a lookup of a link field as the linked record's chip (name, link to the row); a to-many relation gives a chip list. Fix shape: in the lookup case, when `target.type === 'relation'`, resolve each id through the far table's entity name (the same path the relation column itself paints) and emit the chip shape the relation column emits, so `fields.Company` carries `{id, publicId, name, db}` and the grid draws a chip. Add the case to the describeSchema/applySchema fidelity test (test/use-template.test.mjs) so a copied template keeps it, and a regression in the lookup suite.

Found while building the CRM template (Feature #261). Filed by the use-template session, 2026-10-05, weave v0.4.65, commit 52acab9.

## Fix (2026-10-05)

Change 604 (http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/604), landed as commit 048ef0a on gerrit/main.

A lookup whose target field is a relation now answers the far row's summary `{id, publicId, name, db}` with its chip in `fields`, and a list of them when either hop is to-many, each far row once. `raw` keeps the ids, as it does for the relation column. `relations: 'chip'` sends the summary once in `chips`, and the grid grafts it back. The grid and the entity page draw the relation column's `.k-rel` chip, linked to the row. `select`, `where`, formulas, CSV and MCP (`weave_query`, `weave_get_entity`) read the name. The Handbook lookup page describes this, and its outdated line saying a to-many lookup takes the first match now says it reads a list.

Files: src/engine.js (`#lookupRelation`, used by `#readEntityIn` and the `#displayValue` lookup case), public/app.js (`lookupTargetOf`, lookup chips in `editorFor`, `graftChips`), src/handbook.js, test/lookup-relation-chip.test.mjs (new, 6 cases), test/lookup-relation-chip-browser.test.mjs (new, 3 cases: grid in light and dark, entity page), test/use-template.test.mjs (the template fixture carries a lookup over a relation, and the copy reads the chip), changelog.d/lookup-relation-chip-643.md.

Gate (Verified +1 on patchset 1, log 604-1.2): lifecycle pack 13/13; unit lane 2635 tests, 2635 pass; browser lane 1093 tests, 1092 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (overlay scrollbars). The first gate run voted -1 on the environment because chromium-headless-shell 1234 was missing; the coordinator repaired the cache and the run was repeated.

Live check: :4400 /api/health reports sha 048ef0a (started 16:24:57Z). POST /w/weave/api/tables/a6b62fc2-71e3-48d8-b10a-8eac7510ed62/query answers Company as a chip on all 5 CRM/Activities rows: Northwind Traders on #1, #2 and #4, Contoso on #3, Fabrikam on #5, each with db CRM/Companies.

issues.name: Error: template exercise rerun in the same minute is refused, the copy's name is in the trash
issues.description:
## What was reproduced

A second run of the live template exercise in the same minute fails on the copy step. From `~/.weave-serve` at 30e40cc:

```
node scripts/template-exercise.mjs --base http://127.0.0.1:4400 --from weave --into test
```

The four source tables pass, then:

```
FAIL CRM: Use template into test failed: POST /api/spaces/fd99fd5a-.../use answered 409: Space 'CRM check 20261005-1055' is in the trash — restore or purge it first
```

Two causes, both in the script:

- `scripts/template-exercise.mjs:19` `stampOf()` stamps the copy's name to the minute (`yyyymmdd-hhmm`), and `scripts/template-exercise.mjs:40` names the copy `<space> check <stamp>`, so two runs in one minute pick the same name.
- `scripts/template-exercise.mjs:59` soft-deletes the copy (`DELETE /api/spaces/:id` without `?hard=1`), so the trashed copy keeps holding its name. The engine refuses a new space under a trashed one's name by design (`src/engine.js:1722`).

Each run also leaves its copy in `test`'s trash: `CRM check 20261005-1033` and `CRM check 20261005-1055` are there from today's runs.

## What good looks like

A test run leaves nothing behind and can run back to back. A CI fixture in a peer tool (a throwaway database or schema per run) is named uniquely per run and dropped at the end.

## Fix shape

Name the copy to the second plus a short random suffix; purge the copy (`DELETE /api/spaces/:id?hard=1`) at the end of a run and on failure, with a `--keep` flag to leave it for a look; purge the two trashed copies; add a suite case that runs the live function twice against the in-process server in the same second and both runs pass.

Filed by template-exercise-rerun session, 2026-10-05 (Claude Opus, weave 0.4.65 at 30e40cc).

## Fix

2026-10-05, change 606, cd5179e (Gerrit MERGED; :4400 restarted on cd5179e at 18:17:07Z).

- `scripts/template-exercise.mjs` names the copy `<space> check <yyyymmdd-hhmmss> <4 hex>`: to the second, plus a random suffix, so two runs stamped alike differ.
- The copy is purged (`DELETE /api/spaces/:id?hard=1`) at the end of a run and on failure, so a run leaves nothing in `test`, not even trash. `--keep` leaves it live for a look.
- `test/template-exercise.test.mjs`: two runs stamped the same second both pass and leave no copy, live or trashed. The case is red on 30e40cc with the 409 above.
- The two trashed copies from today, `CRM check 20261005-1033` and `CRM check 20261005-1055`, were purged through `DELETE /w/test/api/spaces/:id?hard=1`; the older `CRM` space in `test` is untouched.

Two live runs back to back against :4400 at cd5179e both passed (copies `CRM check 20261005-111734 8144` and `CRM check 20261005-111736 361e`, each purged); `test` holds Marketing, Chip floor 614 and CRM, and no copy sits in the trash.

Fixed by template-exercise-rerun session, 2026-10-05 (Claude Opus, weave cd5179e).

- src/handbook.js:5-768 FIELD_DOCS, :770-2237 GUIDES, :2239-2459 FORMATTING_SAMPLES — the three template-literal blocks, about 2,450 lines of markdown.

issues.name: Wrong data: a row an automation changed names the person as Modified By, not the automation
issues.description:
Reproduced on Net (weave.grunion.ai) 2026-10-06. Request #3 in Workflow Demo was moved to Done over MCP; the "Close out on Done" automation then ticked Resolved and appended to Description. The grid shows Modified By "kyle via VMH4hSRpVOhCwUno" for the automation's write, and the activity log records the field-updated entry for Resolved with actor "kyle via VMH4hSRpVOhCwUno" (seq 2449), the same actor as the state change that triggered it. Good looks like: Airtable and Fibery both credit the automation as the author of the change it made. Kyle, 2026-10-06: "modified by should not be the user, it should be the automation chip."

Fix shape: writes made inside an automation run carry the automation as actor (its Workflows row id and name), keep the triggering person on the automation-ran entry, and Modified By / activity render that actor as the Workflows row's chip, linking to the row.

Writes made inside an automation run carry the actor `workflow:<Workflows row id>` in their activity entries and the changed row's Modified By; the automation-ran entry keeps the triggering person and gains detail.workflow = the row id. issues.name: Looks broken: a document reference chip is cut to the width of its [[…]] source
issues.description:
## What the user sees
In the document editor a `[[Table#n]]` reference is drawn as a chip laid over its literal, and the chip can only be as wide as that literal. A bare `[[Issue#64]]` therefore cuts the record's name off after a few characters, and an aliased `[[Table#n|Name]]` whose literal is longer than the name leaves a blank gap.

## Measured
2026-09-28 on :4400, Issue #65's page, Chromium and WebKit: the hand-typed `[[Issue#64]]` and `[[Issue#165]]` chips are held to 81 px and 90 px, and each name ellipsizes. Cause: `refreshRefChips` in `public/app.js` sizes each overlay to the literal's client rect (`width:${r.width}px`), because Vditor owns the IR DOM and Lute cannot be taught chips. Split out of Issue #97, whose costume half (the reference is the pointer chip, outline and ↗, no tint) lands as its own change on 2026-10-05.

## What good looks like
Notion's mention reads as one whole chip with the record's full name and flows with the text; it never ellipsizes inside the width of its source.

## Fix shape (decision needed from Kyle)
(a) a rendered reading state that swaps to the live editor on the first click or focus, with no button, so chips flow inline (size L; must not bring back a visible edit toggle, per the document-editor-is-the-renderer ruling);
(b) keep the overlay, and have the `#` picker and a save-time pass write every reference as `[[Table#n|Name]]`, so the literal is about as wide as the name (size S);
(c) accept the limit.
The 09-28 enrichment on #97 recommended (b) first. Test first: in `test/doc-ref-chips-browser.test.mjs` or `test/entity-hierarchy-browser.test.mjs`, a bare `[[Task#1]]` whose name is longer than its literal reads whole (label scrollWidth equals clientWidth), light and dark.

Filed by fork session 2026-10-05 (orphans-hopper), weave main f50d224, while landing the 09-26 orphan d7a012c for Issue #97.



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-07T12:28:37Z · session fix-1102-1oyz · from #556, #680, #686

**Repro:** Still there on :4400 at 3ca61e2, with the same numbers the row measured on 09-28. Issue #65's page, Chromium 1280x900: the overlay must be scrolled into view first, because refreshRefChips skips any paragraph outside the viewport (public/app.js:9386), which is why a page-load probe finds no chips at all. Once the line is centred, the two hand-typed bare references draw as anchors 81 px and 90 px wide holding names of 79 and 107 characters. Screenshot in external/weave-worktrees/evidence-679/chips-4400.png.

**Code:**
- public/app.js:9357 refreshRefChips, the whole overlay pass; the sizing is the one template literal at :9416, `width:${r.width}px`, taken from the literal's single client rect at :9405-9407 (a reference that wraps across lines is left literal)
- public/style.css:1166-1180: the clip is on the anchor (`.doc-ref-chip { overflow: hidden }`), NOT on the label. The label computes `text-overflow: clip` and `overflow: visible`
- public/app.js:8671 entityReference already writes `[[${db}#${publicId}|${name}]]`, reached from referenceFor (:8677) and pickReference (:9640). So the picker half of the row's option (b) is already shipped: every reference the # picker inserts is aliased

**Fix shape:** Option (b) is half done. The gap is a save-time pass over hand-typed bare references, not the picker. The row's own estimate of (b) as size S holds for what is left: walk the spans lib.findRefSpans already finds (public/editor-lib.js:21, which reports `label` as null for a bare reference), resolve each, and rewrite `[[Issue#64]]` to `[[Issue#64|<name>]]` on the way to storage. Decision still Kyle's, and (a) and (c) are untouched by this.

**Test to write first:**
- The assertion the row proposes, `label scrollWidth equals clientWidth`, PASSES on the broken build and would catch nothing: measured 79/79 and 88/88, because the label does not overflow, the anchor clips it
- What does separate the two: the label's own laid-out text width against the anchor's box. `range.selectNodeContents(label); range.getBoundingClientRect().width` reads 474 px and 673 px against `anchor.clientWidth` of 81 px and 90 px. A probe span carrying the label's font and text reads 501 px and 713 px, so either measure works as the width the chip should have
- Put it in test/doc-ref-chips-browser.test.mjs, and scroll the reference into view before measuring, or refreshRefChips never draws it

issues.name: Wrong data: a document edit by another person folds into the previous author's Activity entry and is credited to them
issues.description:
**Reproduced.** Scratch server on weave gerrit/main 2b46e4a (v0.4.66), port 4471. One record, three document writes inside a minute by three actors: `PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc` as alice ("First draft of the plan."), then bob (adds a risks section), then agent (trims it), each with its own `X-Weave-Actor`. `doc_revisions` holds three revisions with actors alice, bob and agent, as it should. The record's activity holds ONE `doc-updated` entry, actor **alice**, detail `{field: "Description", length: 59, prevLength: 0, delta: 59, preview: "First draft of the plan."}`: bob's and the agent's edits are folded into alice's entry and credited to her, and the delta and preview describe neither of their edits.

**Where.** src/engine.js `#logActivity`: a `doc-updated` landing within 10 minutes of the last entry for the same field folds into it (Issue #32's one-session-one-entry rule), and the condition never compares `last.actor` with `this.actor`. The revision log's coalescing in `#recordDocRevision` does check the actor (`latest.actor === this.actor`), so the two logs disagree about who wrote what. Issue #588 (Gerrit 647) stops a restore folding either way; a plain edit by another person still folds.

**What good looks like.** Google Docs and Notion group edits into sessions per author: a second person's edit is its own entry with its own name, even seconds later. weave's own revision log already does this.

**Fix shape.** Add `&& last.actor === this.actor` to the fold condition in `#logActivity`, and an engine test in test/activity-seq.test.mjs (or doc-revisions) that two actors writing the same field inside the window leave two `doc-updated` entries, each with its own actor and delta.

Filed by fork session activity-restore (harness b879c5e0) on 2026-10-05, weave gerrit/main 2b46e4a, found while reproducing Issue #588.

issues.name: Looks broken: hiding the last column changes the width of the column that becomes last
issues.description:
## Symptom
Hiding the last column of a table changes the width of the column that becomes last. Kyle's rule is that a hide or a show never changes another field's width.

## Measured
On `:4400`, `uno` workspace, `Agent/Sessions` (1,791 rows, 18 columns, Chromium 1470×900, the grid in `wv-overflow-x`), hiding the last column `Last Modified` (203 px) widens `Created` from **192 px to 203 px**. Showing it again puts `Created` back to 192 px. Every other column holds its width to the pixel through both. Reproduced on gerrit/main `0a23ea9` on a scratch server over a copy of uno, and on `:4400` serving `ec3e83e`, so it predates the Issue #328 fix and is not caused by it.

## Where
`public/app.js`, `renderTable`: `widthOf` composes each column's width from `override`, `storedWidth`, `cellPads`, `floors` and `widest` (`public/app.js:4254-4268`), and `layoutCss` writes one fixed width per column index. The drift is in the last position only, which points at the pad or floor measured for the trailing column rather than at the stored width: neither column carries a stored width in the view, and 203 px is exactly the width the hidden column had.

## What good looks like
Airtable and Notion leave every remaining column at its own width when a column is hidden; the table just gets narrower.

## Fix shape
Find what the last drawn column gets that the others do not (the trailing pad in `cellPads`, or the `floors` measurement taken against the add-field cell), and make a column's width independent of its position. Gate it with the width assertion already in `test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs` ("kept its width through the hide"), extended to a table wide enough to overflow, where the hidden field is the last column.

---
Found while verifying the Issue #328 fix live on `:4400` (harness session 1502-7811, overnight fixer run 2026-10-06), and measured against unchanged main as well.

🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt 1 · 2026-10-07T04:47:27.939Z · fixed · Gerrit 683 → 54287fc

**Tests added:**
- test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs: hiding the last column of an overflowing table whose last two columns are dates leaves every other column at its width, and showing it again puts them back
- test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs: the last cell in a row carries the same right padding as the cell before it

**Live verification:** GET /api/health sha 54287fc startedAt 2026-10-07T04:46:36Z. Repro re-run on :4400, uno Agent/Sessions, Chromium 1470x900: hiding Last Modified leaves Created at 192px and moves no column at all, in both data-bs-theme values; showing it again moves none. Before the fix the same script read Created 192 to 203. Last Modified now opens at 187px, its own measurement with no position bonus. Root cause: Tabler .card-table tr td:last-child pads the last cell 20px where .table-sm pads every other 4px, and settle() measures a date column floor from that cell box, so the column drawn last measured 16px wider than itself. The grid restates its own padding on the last cell now. The uno view was left as it was found (no hidden fields).

issues.name: Looks broken: a signed-out link preview opens on the row UUID alone
issues.description:
Reproduced by reading src/routes.js at f688239. With linkPreview on and no session, linkPreview() (src/routes.js:189) answers /e/<uuid>, /s/<uuid> and /t/<uuid> with a page whose meta tags carry the table and space names, the row title and every preview field value (src/routes.js:215-220, 258). Line 192 refuses non-UUID refs for signed-out callers, so the UUID is the only gate: knowing it is the credential. The flag is off today on every local workspace in ~/.weave and on the three cloud paths probed at weave.grunion.ai (signed-out logo route answers 401).

Peer tools split the address from the secret. Notion and Linear unfurl only through an installed app or a share token. weave already does this for views: shareView mints a separate wvv_ token with 144 random bits (src/engine.js:1744).

Fix shape: give a row its own share token, the way views have one, and serve signed-out previews only for a shared row. Required before any switch to time-ordered IDs (UUIDv7 publishes the creation millisecond; RFC 9562 advises against using it as a secret).

Filed by the ID-format review session, 2026-10-06, weave checkout f688239.

**Repro:** Not reproduced live, and the reason is worth recording: the preview page only ever stands in for the auth wall. src/routes.js:361 reaches it inside requireAuth && !openDoor, so a signed-out preview needs BOTH requireAuth and linkPreview on. On :4400 at efdebea the weave and uno workspaces both answer requireAuth false and linkPreview false, so a signed-out GET of /e/<uuid> returns the ordinary app (200), not the preview page, and turning the flag on to probe would change a workspace Kyle reads. The row's reading of the code holds at efdebea: for a signed-out caller the UUID is the only gate.

**Code:**
- src/routes.js:361-365 the only caller of the signed-out preview, inside the requireAuth branch; :364 serves it with Cache-Control no-store
- src/routes.js:200-203 linkPreview; :202 matches /e/, /s/ and /t/ with one path segment; :203 is the whole gate for a signed-out caller, if (signedOut && m && !UUID_RE.test(m[2])) return null

- src/routes.js:278 previewLogo serves the workspace logo on the same flag with no session
- src/engine.js:1773-1775 shareView, the precedent: a separate wvv_ token of 18 random bytes, 144 bits, minted per view

**Fix shape:** Unchanged: a per-row share token minted the way shareView mints one, with the signed-out preview served only for a shared row. One detail this run adds: the token has to reach linkPreview, which today takes only the path, so either the match at :202 grows a token segment (/e/<uuid>/<token>) or the check moves to the query string; a path segment keeps it out of referers the way the view token already is. issues.name: Gap: an automation's append to a document records no revision, so the document's history skips it
issues.description:
**Found while fixing Issue #686** (Gerrit 695, weave 3ca61e2), which gave the automation path the `doc-appended` activity entry it was missing.

**What happens.** `#runAction`'s append-doc branch in `src/engine.js` writes `e.docs[docField.id]` itself, records undo and (since 3ca61e2) logs activity. It never calls `#recordDocRevision`. A rule that appends to a document leaves no row in `doc_revisions`, so the document's own history skips what the rule wrote: the clock-arrow in the section head and `GET /api/entities/<id>/doc/revisions` do not list it, and nobody can compare with or restore to the text as the rule left it. A person's append through `appendDoc` records one.

**Measured** on :4400 2026-10-07 (weave 3ca61e2) in /w/test > Issue 686 > Request #1. After the rule "Close out on Done" appended "Closed Oct 7, 2026." the activity feed holds seq 666 `doc-appended` with actor `workflow:b4c18464…`, and the Description revision list holds nothing from that write.

**Good looks like.** Notion and Google Docs keep a version for an automated edit the same as for a person's, named by whatever made it. weave's own person path already does.

**Fix shape.** The branch duplicates the append arithmetic `appendDoc` already has. Call `this.appendDoc(e.id, this.#template(action.text, e, db), docField.id)` and the revision, the undo and the activity entry all come from one place. Two things wanted deciding first, which is why #686 did not take it: `appendDoc` calls `this.save()` inside the run where `#runWorkflows` saves once at the end, and the revision window in `#recordDocRevision` compares actors, so two fires of the same rule inside ten minutes would coalesce into one revision rather than two. A test in test/doc-revisions.test.mjs: a rule's append leaves a revision whose actor is `workflow:<row id>` and whose text is the document after the append.

Filed by the weave fixer, session fix-1102-1oyz, 2026-10-07, weave 3ca61e2.



🔎 overnight-fixer · enriched · 2026-10-07T13:00:46.157Z · session fix-1102-1oyz · from #471

**Repro:** Read against gerrit/main 90dbb1f (v0.4.74). The two questions the row left open are both answered in src/engine.js, and one of them makes the fix smaller than the row assumed.

**Code:**
- `workflowActor` (src/engine.js:256) is `workflow:${rowId}` on the Workflows registry row, so it is the same string on every fire of one rule.
- `#recordDocRevision` (src/engine.js:6115) replaces the latest revision in place when `latest.actor === this.actor` and it is inside `revisionWindowMs` (6123-6127). With a constant actor per rule, two fires of the same rule inside that window do coalesce into one revision. The row guessed right. A person editing twice inside the window coalesces the same way, so this is the designed window, not a second defect.
- `updateDoc` (6087) and `appendDoc` (6107) both call `#recordDocRevision(e, f, before, after, { prior })` on their own, after the activity log and the undo record. `save()` is a separate call beside it (6088, 6108), not something `#recordDocRevision` does.
- 3ca61e2 already hoisted `before` and `after` into the append-doc branch of `#runAction` for the activity entry, so both values the revision needs are in scope there.

**Fix shape:** The branch does not have to reuse `appendDoc` to get the revision. One line beside the activity log — `this.#recordDocRevision(e, docField, before, after, { prior: { at: e.updatedAt, by: e.modifiedBy } })` read before the write — gives the revision row without pulling `save()` into the run and without touching the duplicated append arithmetic, which stays its own question. The `appendDoc` reuse the row describes is still the fuller answer; this is the one that fits inside the run loop as it stands.

**Test to write first:**
- test/doc-revisions.test.mjs: a rule that appends to a document leaves a revision whose actor is `workflow:<Workflows row id>` and whose text is the document after the append, with the pre-append text kept as the revision below it.
- test/doc-revisions.test.mjs: two fires of the same rule inside `revisionWindowMs` leave one revision holding the later text, which is the window behaving as designed and must not read as a regression.

issues.name: Gap: the flicker gate cannot ratchet a frame finding, so a frame fingerprint in flicker-fixed.json is never checked
issues.description:
## Measured
`test/flicker-gate-browser.test.mjs` is the ratchet that keeps a fixed flicker fixed: it walks every journey and fails when a fingerprint listed in `test/flicker-fixed.json` comes back. It cannot see a `frame` finding.

- `regressed()` (`test/lib/flicker.mjs:240`) counts an event only when `GATED.includes(e.kind)`, and `GATED` is `['transient', 'blank', 'revert', 'shift']`. The sweep's fifth kind, `frame`, is not in it.
- The gate walks each journey with the DOM probe alone (`walk(browser, j, ctx, { probe })`, no `record`), so no frames are captured and no `frame` event is ever produced there in the first place.

So a `frame` row's fix shape, which tells the fixer to add the fingerprint to `test/flicker-fixed.json` so the gate fails if it returns, buys nothing for that kind: the entry is inert. `scripts/flicker-sweep.mjs` is the only thing that reads frames, and it runs nightly outside the gate.

Found on 2026-10-07 while enriching Issue #638 (`switch-view|frame|box 320,40 160x160`), the first `frame` row to reach the overnight fixer.

## What good looks like
A fixed flicker stays fixed whatever its kind. Either the gate records frames for the journeys that have a `frame` fingerprint listed and compares them, or a `frame` fingerprint is refused by the gate as unsupported and the kind's rows say in their own fix shape where their regression test goes instead. Silently accepting an entry that is never checked is the one outcome to avoid.

## Fix shape
1. Decide which of the two it is. Recording frames in the gate costs a CDP screencast per journey and makes the gate's own paint timing part of the result, which is why the sweep owns frames today.
2. If the gate takes frames: record them only for journeys with a listed `frame` fingerprint, and extend `regressed()` to take frame findings alongside the DOM events.
3. If it does not: make a `frame` key in `test/flicker-fixed.json` fail the suite loudly (a case in `test/flicker-core.test.mjs` reading the real file), and fix the `frame` wording in `routines/weave-flicker-routine.md` so a filed row names the test that will hold it.

issues.name: Looks broken: linking a relation opens a name-only list instead of workspace search
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-10-07: "adding relations by link button then search is wrong. should be able to get a similar to workspace search and be able to select anything based on the relation definition."

Reproduced on v0.4.75 (cb0b29f):
- `+ Link existing` on an entity's related section (public/app.js:9757-9778) POSTs `/tables/<target>/query` with `select:['Name']`, loads every row of the target table, and hands them to `searchPicker` (public/app.js:1459) as plain labels with a `#pid` hint. Filtering is a client-side substring match on Name only.
- No icon, no field context, no match highlighting, no recents, no ranking. A row whose Name is blank shows as `(unnamed)`. The whole target table loads before the first keystroke, so a large table is slow to open.
- The ⌘K palette (`openCommandK`, public/app.js:10262) already has the right shape: server-side `universalSearch`, grouped results with icon, name, excerpt and location, recents, keyboard nav, and an `onPick`/`kinds` hook. `/api/search` (src/routes.js:1159) takes no table scope, so the palette cannot be pointed at a relation's target today.

Good looks like (Fibery, Notion, Linear): the link button opens the same search surface as global search, scoped to what the relation definition allows. Typing matches any text on the target rows, not just Name. Already-linked rows show as checked. A to-one relation replaces on pick; a to-many relation toggles and stays open for more picks. `+ New <term>` sits in the same palette as the last option.

Fix shape:
1. `/api/search` gains a `tables=<id,...>` scope (and `kinds=entity`) so `universalSearch` returns only rows of the relation's target table(s).
2. `openCommandK` gains `scope`, `selected` and `multi` options; picking in multi mode toggles a check and keeps the palette open, Esc or Enter-on-empty commits.
3. Every relation-linking surface routes through it: `+ Link existing` on the related section, the relation cell editor in the grid, the bulk `Link N to…` action (public/app.js:4159), and the entity page relation field.
4. Cardinality comes from the field definition: many-to-one and one-to-one replace, one-to-many and many-to-many add and remove.
5. Retire the Name-only `/query` preload for these surfaces.

Filed by the harness session 2026-10-07, weave v0.4.75 (cb0b29f).

2026-10-07 landed: Gerrit change 703, commit 9bea0b1 on gerrit/main (base v0.4.75 cb0b29f). GET /api/search takes tables=<id,...>; openCommandK gains scope, selected, multi, onCommit and create; linkSearch(f) reads cardinality from the field (to-one replaces and closes, to-many toggles and commits on Esc or Enter on an empty box) and ends with + New <term>. + Link existing, the relation editor in the grid and on the record, and the bulk Link to… route through it; the Name-only /query preloads are gone. Also fixed: + Link existing referenced an undefined `item` in its commit, so linking there threw. Tests: test/scoped-search.test.mjs (3 pass), test/link-search-browser.test.mjs (4 pass), row-selection-browser Link to… updated; gate 2,759/2,759 green, Verified +1 on the first run. Filed by the harness link-search-703 session.

issues.name: Looks broken: on iPhone the docked formatting bar slides off the keyboard when Safari pans the page
issues.description:
## Reproduced
`placeToolbarBubble` (`public/app.js:8087-8093`) sets the docked bar's `bottom` to `innerHeight - visualViewport.height - visualViewport.offsetTop`, which is right. It only re-runs on `visualViewport` **resize** (`public/app.js:8109`) and on `selectionchange`. iOS Safari keeps the layout viewport tall while the keyboard is up and pans the visual viewport as the caret moves; that pan changes `offsetTop` and fires `visualViewport` **scroll**, not resize.

Measured in WebKit with `visualViewport` stubbed to a 400px keyboard-up viewport: after the resize event the bar's bottom is 412px (correct). After a scroll event that moves `offsetTop` to 120 the bar's bottom stays at 412px; the correct value is 292px. On a phone that leaves the bar 120px above the keyboard, floating over the text, until the next selection change.

Not yet seen on a real iPhone (no Xcode on this Mac); the defect is confirmed in code and in the stubbed run.

## What good looks like
Apple Notes and Notion keep their format bar flush on top of the keyboard while the page scrolls.

## Fix shape

issues.name: Looks broken: on a phone there is no Undo without a hardware keyboard
issues.description:
## Reproduced
1. Open a document on a 375px screen, tap into the text, type a word.
2. Look for Undo. The Undo and Redo buttons live only in the formatting bar (`public/app.js:8010`), and that bar shows only while text is selected (`placeToolbarBubble`, `public/app.js:8082-8084`). With a caret and no selection there is no Undo on screen.
3. iOS's own Undo (shake, three-finger swipe left, or the Undo key on the iPad keyboard bar) runs the browser's native undo. Measured in WebKit: after typing " UNDOME", `document.execCommand('undo')` returns true and the word stays. Vditor keeps its own undo stack and rebuilds the DOM on every input, so the native stack has nothing to undo.

So a phone user who deletes a paragraph by mistake has no way back except the document history panel.

## What good looks like
Apple Notes answers shake and three-finger swipe, and shows Undo in the keyboard bar. Notion's iPhone editor keeps Undo and Redo in its toolbar above the keyboard whenever the caret is in the text.

## Fix shape
Two parts, either one helps on its own:
1. Route `beforeinput` with `inputType` `historyUndo` / `historyRedo` to `vditor.undo.undo` / `redo` (preventDefault the native one), so iOS gestures reach Vditor's stack.
2. On a phone, show Undo and Redo whenever the caret is in the document, not only with a selection. This is part of the keyboard bar mockup; it waits on Kyle's pick.

issues.name: Looks broken: on a phone the pinned header takes 132 to 178px of an 812px screen while writing
issues.description:
## Reproduced
Open a row with a long description on a 375x812 screen and scroll the document. Two things stay pinned:
- `.view-header` (crumbs row, then a second row with History, Preview, More, Collapse, Close, then the 30px row title): y 8 to 150.
- `.doc-section-head` (DESCRIPTION, history, copy, more): y 150 to 178.

The first line of text sits at y 179. That is **178px, 22% of the screen**. With the iOS keyboard up (about 336px on an iPhone 13 in portrait, plus the 44px bar), the visible writing area is about 430px and the pinned header takes about 40% of it.

Issue #411 made these headers sticky on purpose, and that is right on a desktop. On a phone the cost is different.

## What good looks like
Apple Notes shows only a slim nav bar (back, share, more) and scrolls the title away with the text. Notion's iPhone page scrolls the title and properties away and leaves a 44pt bar with back and more.

## Fix shape
Design call first (mockup on the weave mobile flow canvas). Candidate: at 600px and below, while the document has focus or is scrolled, collapse the header to one 44px glass row (back crumb, title cut to one line, more) and let the section head scroll with the text. Keep #411's sticky headers on desktop.

## Both phone paths, measured
- Row opened from a table (the dock, the usual path): `.view-header` y 0 to 104 (crumbs, then History, Preview, More, Collapse, Close), `.doc-section-head` y 104 to 132. First text at y 133: **132px, 16% of the screen**, about 31% of the area left above the keyboard.
