`docs/ONTOLOGY.md` gains the "Every level is a table" section; the ontology gate checks the section exists and that every config field it names is a real field of the Tables registry. meta-model 10 → 14 tests; 649 green in the main tree.

features.name: Space and workspace views are the registry grids; opening a row opens the structure
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 62f5e4a)

Kyle: *"this should be reflected not just in the document but in the view of tables within a space and view of spaces within a workspace, these should be tables with all relevant fields; opening them opens the space or table which is the entity of the workspace."*

Follows Feature #126 (table configuration as fields on the registry row) — this lands the same truth in the UI.

### What landed

- **The space page IS the Tables registry grid**, scoped to the space by the `Space` relation: Name, Description, Space, Fields, Field Order, Hidden Fields — every column editable in place, through the same engine sync (renaming the row renames the table; editing Field Order reorders it, with the full-permutation validation).
- **The workspace page IS the Spaces registry grid**, above the system card: Name, Description, Tables.
- **Opening a registry row opens its structure.** Row clicks and the `#N ↗` open link both route through `registryHref()` / `openRegistryRow()`, navigating by the row's `sysId` — which `readEntity`/query now expose for system-registry rows (plain rows carry none).
- The hand-rolled `space-table-row` list and the home page's flat table list are gone. Both themes verified in the live browser; row-click → space → table → row loop verified end to end.

### Notes

- Cells still behave as cells: clicking Field Order edits it; the row surface and the `#N ↗` link are the navigation affordances.
- ui-contract's row-click routing contract now allows the registry hop (still exactly 3 routed surfaces).

features.name: Workflows system table: workspace-level workflow registry with script, state, health, diagram
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 16e9dad)

Kyle: *"Lets create a new system table like activity at the workspace level called Workflows"* — each row is a workflow: related tables it touches, related spaces it touches, the executable automation script itself as a field, version, state (Draft, Active, Deactivated), health (Healthy, Warning, Failed), last run datetime, and a document field holding a mermaid diagram of the workflow. A Type field ships with **no types yet** — types get designed and rolled out later.

### Shape (all system fields)

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tables | relation m:m → `Workspace/Tables` | inverse `Workflows` on the registry |
| Spaces | relation m:m → `Workspace/Spaces` | inverse `Workflows` |
| Script | document, kind `code` | the executable itself |
| Version | number, 0 decimals | |
| State | workflow | Draft (default, not-started) / Active (in-progress) / Deactivated (canceled) |
| Health | select | Healthy (green) / Warning (yellow) / Failed (red) |
| Last Run | date, time on | |
| Diagram | document, markdown | mermaid renders natively |
| Type | select, **zero options** | the socket future workflow types plug into |

### Engineering notes

- Unlike the registries, **Workflows rows are ordinary data**. The meta-model interceptors now own exactly `spaces`/`tables`/`fields` and pass any other system table through to normal row CRUD — previously a row update on a non-registry system table fell into the structural branch and threw.
- Legacy workspaces grow the table on first open via `#ensureMetaTables`; this workspace did.
- New suite `test/workflows-table.test.mjs` (5 tests); engine's count test expects the sixth system table. 694 green; verified rendering live (filter strip shows the three states, Docs (2) carries Script + Diagram).

### Open for the types rollout

Type options, per-type Script contracts, what flips Health, and what runs Last Run — all deliberately unbuilt.

features.name: One relation map, drawn at the workspace and at a space
features.description:
**Raised by Kyle, 2026-08-24**: "the relation map directly accessible from the left nav is much better design than the one under weave but the content of the mmd native is better — can we get the best of both worlds and define one relation map view which lives in the workspace and space level?" and, separately, "we also don't need a map button in each space".

Weave carried two maps:

| | content | design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mermaid card on the workspace home (Feature #51) | **right** — user tables only, grouped into their space, one labelled arrow per relation | wrong — mermaid's own palette, theme-blind, a dark box on a light page |
| SVG behind `#/map` (the left-nav entry) | wrong — the registry drawn alongside user tables, a circle layout that hid structure, most edges unlabelled | **right** — weave's own cards, chips and type, clickable nodes, automations drawn in |

**Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit f4bbf56, Gerrit change 43, Verified +1).** They are one view.

`public/relmap-layout.js` is the pure half — a column per space in schema order, the registry left out, one edge per relation pair carrying both ends' cardinality (crow's-foot order: `Owner ∗–1` reads "many Tasks to one Person"), endpoints landing on the card border so an arrowhead has somewhere to sit, and room reserved ahead of time for a self-relation's loop and for each automation pill. Passing a `spaceId` narrows it to that space plus whatever it actually touches, the guests drawn dashed and named by their own space.

`relationMapView()` in app.js draws it in three places from one renderer:

1. the `#/map` page (the left-nav entry, unchanged as an entry point),
2. a card on the workspace home — the mermaid card and `/api/relation-map.mmd` fetch are gone,
3. a card on every space page — which is why the per-space **Map** button goes too. A space shows its own map instead of linking to the workspace's.

Gate: `test/relmap-layout.test.mjs` (12 tests) covers the content rules, the space altitude, the reserved room, and the wiring — including that the mermaid map and the Map button stay gone.

features.name: Agent-complete configuration: the remaining schema and view verbs over MCP
features.description:
**Every schema and view choice an agent can make in the UI, reachable without a browser.**

Audit 2026-08-24 across engine / REST / CLI / MCP / registry rows. Most of the surface is already agent-reachable through registry-row CRUD (rename, reconfigure, reorder, hide, delete) — the gate is awareness, not capability, and that half is answered by the new Handbook guide.

Genuinely unreachable from MCP today, REST-only:

| Capability | REST | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table `icon` | `PATCH /api/tables/{id}` | the nav and every crumb read it |
| Table `noun` | same | names the create action |
| `systemFields` | same | Created/Modified/By columns |
| Space `icon` | `PATCH /api/spaces/{id}` | nav grouping |
| Saved views + share links | `POST /api/views`, `/share` | the multi-table read an agent would hand to a human |
| Automations: list, describe, update, delete | `/api/automations` | `weave_create_automation` can write one and never read it back |
| Workspace name, description, logo | `PATCH /api/workspace` | |
| Declarative apply | `PUT /api/schema` | blocked behind [[Issue#56]] until the round trip is lossless |
| Activity feed / audit | `/api/activity`, `/api/audit` | reading what changed |
| Table and space delete | `DELETE /api/tables|spaces/{id}` | (registry rows cover this with `hard: true`) |

Also stale: `weave_add_field`'s description names 13 of the 18 field types (`document`, `field`, `key`, `attachments` and `relation` are missing) and none of the costume config keys; `weave_create_table` takes no `icon`.

Proposed: `weave_update_table`, `weave_update_space`, `weave_create_view` / `weave_list_views` / `weave_share_view`, `weave_automations` (list/describe/update/delete), `weave_apply_schema` (after #56), `weave_activity`. Each lands with its tool-description vocabulary — colors, icons, formats — so the tool list itself teaches the visual meaning.

features.name: Universal reference rule: every entity answers to its unique id and id-based permalink
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit ae6b203)

Kyle: *"lets go for a more universal and durable fix ... all entities where names are referenced via the unique ID that each entity has and its permalink. This will help make sure everything is more extensible later. all entities should behave this way."*

The one-off interceptor fix (Feature #128's note) becomes a rule: **every entity — workspace, space, table, row — is referenced by its unique id and carries an id-based permalink; names are display labels.**

### What landed

| Level | Identity | Permalink | Rename-proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | `meta.id`, minted once in `#migrate` | `/w/<id>/` (name URL = alias) | ✅ verified live |
| Space | uuid (existing) | `#/space/<id>` stamped in schema | ✅ |
| Table | uuid (existing) | `#/table/<id>` stamped in schema | ✅ |
| Row | uuid (existing) | `/e/<id>` now on every `readEntity` | ✅ |

- **Mentions**: `[[<uuid>]]` resolves by id and renders the *current* name — a rename never breaks a document. `[[Task#12]]` stays as the human spelling.
- **Surfaces stop joining on names**: space page scopes its registry grid by `sysId` (was Space-name match); the workspace rail links chips by id URL and resolves the active workspace from a name-or-id segment; workspace rename navigates to the id permalink; the home permalink chip copies the id URL.
- API: `GET /api/workspace` and `GET /api/workspaces` expose `{ id, url }`.

### Contract

`test/permalinks.test.mjs` (7 tests): identity minted once and kept through export/import/rename; every level resolves by id after renames; `/w/<id>/` routes before and after a rename; the list carries ids; id mentions render current names. ui-contract gains the no-name-join gates. 710 green.

### Why extensible

A new entity kind follows the rule and gets durable identity for free — no per-surface name-joins to invent, no rename hazards to discover later.

features.name: Table row selection with a floating action bar (puck)
features.description:
**Row selection in the table view, with a floating action bar.**

Checking rows in a table opens a bar that floats over the bottom of the grid and acts on the whole selection at once. Prompted by Kyle, 2026-08-24, against the Fibery reference bar (`2 selected · Edit Fields · Convert to · Duplicate · Merge into… · Download all files · Copy as Markdown · 🗑`).

### Selection mechanics

- The checkbox is **its own column, to the left of the row's `#` link** — the link never disappears, so a row stays openable while a selection is live.
- The column holds its width at rest and reveals the box on row hover, or once any selection exists. An idle grid stays clean.
- The header box is select-all, with an indeterminate state for a partial selection.
- Clicking anywhere in a row toggles it, except on the `#` link. `Esc` clears.
- Selected rows take a soft accent tint and a 2px accent rule on the leading edge.

### The bar — five designs explored, **Puck chosen** (Kyle, 2026-08-24)

| # | Design | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Pill — Fibery-faithful, every action labelled | Readable, but 940px wide and it grows with every action |
| 2 | **Puck** — icon-only, hover labels, overflow `⋯` | **Chosen.** Fixed width, survives a narrow panel |
| 3 | Dock — selection summary segment + actions segment | Scales, at one extra click for demoted actions |
| 4 | Inked — solid ink instead of glass | Best contrast, loudest thing on a cream page |
| 5 | Command — the selection as a ⌘K scope | Never needs to grow; costs a keystroke |

Glass shell: `blur(22px) saturate(180%)`, hairline border, inset top highlight, three-layer shadow. Rises 14px with a fade on appear. The grid gains bottom padding while a selection is live so the bar never covers the last row.

### Commands (revised with Kyle, 2026-08-24)

Fibery's set was cut down — **Convert to**, **Download all files**, **Copy as Markdown** and **Merge into…** are all out. What replaces them is weave-shaped:

**On the bar** — Set state (opens the workflow chips), Set a field… (pick a field, one value across the selection), Link to… (pick a relation and a target, connect every selected row), Duplicate, and Move to trash past a hairline.

**Under `⋯`** — Move to table…, Roll up into a new entity… (create one parent and link the selection to it), Show these in the map, Select all with the same… (grows the selection instead of acting on it), Copy links.

The bar is contextual: no *Set state* on a table without a workflow field, no *Link to* without relations.

### Cut, and why

- **Convert to…** — changing a row's type is a schema decision; it belongs in the field/table dialog where you can see what breaks.
- **Download all files** — a zip across a selection is a rare ask and a slow, failure-prone job.
- **Copy as Markdown** — every weave page is already markdown, and ⌘C can carry this without a slot on the bar.
- **Merge into…** — reconciling every field and relinking every edge is a wizard, not a puck button.

### Artifact

Interactive mockup with all five bars, both themes, working popovers and select-all: `docs/mockups/table-bulk-select.html`.


---

### Revision — Kyle, 2026-08-24 (second pass)

**Set state is cut.** A table can carry more than one workflow field, so a single *Set state* button is a lie about the schema. State is a field like any other and lives inside **Set a field…**, which now opens a two-step picker: field list → value editor (state chips, select options, a text/number input, or a checked/unchecked pair). The demo table carries two workflow fields (`Status` and `Stage`) precisely to show this. The alternative Kyle named — generating one bar command per workflow field — trades the puck's fixed width for a bar that changes shape per table, and is recorded but not taken.

**Link to… no longer wears a chain-link icon.** A chain reads as a hyperlink; the glyph is now two rows joined by an edge with a junction dot, which reads as a table relation. The picker is two-step and search-first (per Feature #100's one selection dialect): relation → search the target table → pick the row.

**Show these in the map** and **Select all with the same…** are cut. The map is a place you go, not somewhere a selection pushes you; growing a selection is the filter strip's job.

**Selected rows** carry the accent tint alone — the leading accent stripe is removed.

**Checkbox alignment.** Header and body checkboxes now share one padding rule at equal specificity and sit inside an identical 34×30 label hit target, so the select-all box lands on the same vertical line as every row's box. `.grid thead th` had been out-specifying a plain `th.cb`.

Final set — **on the bar**: Set a field…, Link to…, Duplicate, and Move to trash past the hairline. **Under `⋯`**: Move to table…, Roll up into a new entity…, Copy links.


---

### Slice 1 shipped — 2026-08-26 (`b8f0a39`)

Selection state and the checkbox column are live. `public/selection-core.js` is
the pure half (toggle, range, prune, headState, selectAll, barCommands); the
DOM half is `renderTable` in `public/app.js`.

**One departure from the spec above, forced by Ledger.** This record says
"clicking anywhere in a row toggles it, except on the `#` link". Ledger landed
the same evening (`a2cca58`) with the opposite rule: a bare row click raises
THAT CELL's editor. Two meanings for one gesture is one too many, so the
checkbox owns selection outright and **shift-click extends the span from the
last box hit**. Clicking a cell leaves the selection alone; checking a row
opens no editor. Both halves are pinned by tests.

Selection is a set of entity ids, never row indices — a sort re-orders every
row and the same records stay chosen; a row that leaves the page is pruned.
Painting is not a redraw, so an open cell editor survives a click in the
column. Escape clears unless a dialog or popover owns the keystroke first.
Trashed rows get no box.

Tests: 13 pure cases (`test/row-selection.test.mjs`) + 9 browser cases
(`test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs`). `ui-contract`'s colCount pin moved to
`+ 4`; what the add-row span must EQUAL is now proved against a live header.

**Still to build:** slice 2, the puck itself, and slice 3, the commands
(Set a field…, Link to…, Duplicate, Move to trash, and the `⋯` set).

### Slice 2 shipped — 2026-08-26 (`dcddcf4`)

The puck is live. Icon only, hover labels, the count in an accent pill, trash
past a hairline, glass shell, rises 14px on appear. The grid grows a floor
while one is up so the bar never covers the last row it acts on.

**The bar carries only commands that can run.** `barCommands` takes a `built`
list; a designed-but-unbuilt button reads as broken rather than forthcoming.
Today that is **Duplicate** and **Move to trash**. `moreCommands` answers to
the same rule, so there is no `...` overflow yet.

Duplicate copies every writable field; computed fields and documents are not
copied, because a computed field is a read and recomputes on the copy. A bulk
command that half works and reports success is how a row goes missing quietly,
so the toast names what did NOT land.

Handbook gained "Working on many rows at once" under the grid section.

Tests: 16 pure + 14 browser. Full suite 901/901 on a tree carrying only this
work.

**Slice 3 remains:** Set a field... (two-step picker, field then value, state
included), Link to... (relation then search the target), and the overflow set
(Move to table..., Roll up into a new entity..., Copy links). Each wants a
batch write at the engine or route layer rather than the current per-row loop.

### Slice 3 shipped — 2026-09-05 (`2d9eef9`)

The commands are live. **On the bar:** Set a field… (field → value: state
chips, options, checked/unchecked, or a typed box; state is a field like any
other), Link to… (relation → search the far table → one target), Duplicate,
⋯, Move to trash. **Under ⋯:** Move to table…, Roll up into a new …, Copy
links. The overflow is contextual like the bar: no Move to table… when this
is the only table, no Roll up… without a relation, and an empty overflow
takes the ⋯ off the bar.

**One write per command.** `bulk(ids, op, params)` is the engine verb —
`POST /api/bulk`, `weave bulk`, `weave_bulk` (agent-surface gate entry
`entity.bulk`). It runs the single-row verbs underneath, so each row keeps
its own undo step and activity entry, and reports per row: `done` and
`failed[{id, error}]`. The toast names what did NOT land (`bulkToast` in
selection-core). Move re-creates each row in the far table by field name AND
type — option and state values travel by name — trashes the original, and
lists what stayed behind (unmatched fields, files, comments) under
`moved[].skipped` and in a `moved` activity entry on the copy. Rollup
creates the parent in the relation's target table, then links.

**Two things found on the way.** A picker placed itself before its list was
drawn, so one that flips above its trigger (every puck picker) measured a
title-only height and landed on top of the bar; `anchorPop` now runs after
the draw. And the Escape that closed a picker kept bubbling to the grid's
listener, which by then saw no popover and emptied the selection — the
picker spends the keystroke now. Both pinned.

Issue #161 fixed in the same change: the bar is `position: fixed` at the
viewport's bottom centre; the grid keeps its 62px floor.

Handbook "Working on many rows at once" carries the two command tables.

Tests: 20 pure + 24 browser (`row-selection*`), 9 engine/door
(`test/bulk.test.mjs`). Full suite 1683/1683, skipped 0.

features.name: The grid is a record: the Ledger table view
features.description:
**Chosen by Kyle 2026-08-24** from the grid study (three directions, then two): Records was cut, Sheet was kept in reserve, Ledger was built.

The grid read as a form. Every cell wore a control, hovering drew a box around each one — so a row looked ruled between its fields — and a row click fought the cell it landed on.

**Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 289fa64, Gerrit change 49, Verified +1).**

## The rule

**The `#id` link navigates, every cell edits.** A bare row click no longer opens the entity; it raises that field type's own editor and places the cursor. `WeaveEditorLib.cellActivation()` is the pure half:

| Field type | A click on the cell |
| --- | --- |
| text · number · url · email · key · date | focus the input, caret at the end |
| select · multiselect · workflow | open its picker |
| relation · attachments | open the record search / file chooser |
| checkbox | toggle it |
| formula · rollup · lookup · document · field | nothing — not edited from the grid |

⌘-click opens the row in the **side peek**, so the table keeps its place.

## The skin

- Chips stay chips — a value from a set of options still wears one (Kyle) — they lose the border and the box, not the tint.
- The × and + link are chrome about the row: hidden until it is hovered or holds focus.
- Computed cells drop the tinted ground and keep their glyph.
- **No cell draws itself a border on hover** (Kyle's correction). The row's tint is the feedback; the focused control is the only thing wearing one.
- The leading column is set heavier — it carries the row's identity.

## Density

Comfortable (46px rows) or Compact (32px), a segmented control in the toolbar, remembered per table per person in `localStorage` — a way of reading the table, not a property of it. Rows came down from 68px on the way: an input at rest is text, so it is sized like text (`min-height: 0`), and a relation's chips stopped wrapping onto a second line.

## Overflow

A capped column says what it is hiding. Clipped is **measured after layout**, never assumed, so the marker always means there is more. A clipped cell wears a ⤢ and opens the whole value on hover — as a **copy** in a layer over the grid (`.cell-pop-layer` off `.table-wrap`). The cell itself is never touched, so no column can move; verified live, `gridMoved: false`.

## Gates

`test/ledger-grid.test.mjs` (14 tests) pins all four of Kyle's corrections plus the skin and density. `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` rewrote the two assertions the old row-click contract owned — the board and embedded related rows still route the old way. `test/column-fit.test.mjs` now starts from a deliberately squeezed column: its "the width must move" wait measured against whatever auto-layout handed out, which stopped meaning anything once the name column got heavier, and failed on a fit that was correct (312 → 317, covering a 297px value).

Verified live at :4400 — row heights 46/32, density persisted, all five field types raising the right editor with the caret placed, read-only cells inert, peek 920px carrying the right entity.

features.name: Grid interaction: arrows navigate, cells rest, selection comes free
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-24 (Kyle), over four rounds. The last one decides the shape.

1. "mock up at least 5 UX interact pattern sets that include row select, cell edit, tab/arrow/return to navigate, shift-enter to create new item" → seven sets, A–G.
2. "click to select, click again to edit… what do we lose with this?" → G, two-click, and its seven costs.
3. "check boxes should not need double click. what if on hover you can always single click into the edit, command click and shift click always de/select multiple. rebuild the mock ups with only 3" → selection moved onto the modifiers; G retired.
4. **"I want to nav with L and R and tab"**

## Why round 4 is structural, not a tweak

`←` and `→` cannot navigate while a cell is a live text input — the caret is already using them. The round-3 direction claimed both and could only have one. Wanting the horizontal arrows for navigation means cells **rest as values** and open on purpose.

Two things fall out that Kyle did not ask for, and both are wins:

- **Keyboard row selection comes free.** `Space` is unclaimed at rest, so it picks a row up, `⇧↑`/`⇧↓` extend and `⌘A` takes the table. Round 3 needed a whole extra direction (K, a nav mode behind `Esc`) to buy exactly this. The H-versus-K question dissolves.
- **Hover finally has a job** — showing the control a click would open, rather than every cell wearing one at once.

## The three

| | | ← → at rest | ← → in an open cell | Row select | Build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NOW** | What ships (#133 Ledger) | the caret, always | the caret | none | — |
| **REST** | Resting cursor; the caret takes them back | **navigate** | the caret, until Tab/Return/Esc | keyboard + pointer | S |
| **EDGE** | Edge-through; they never stop navigating | **navigate** | caret, then **out at the text edge** | keyboard + pointer | S+ |

Both give Kyle what he asked for at rest. They differ on one axis only: whether `←`/`→` ever stop navigating.

## Still true from earlier rounds

One click edits whatever the type and a **checkbox flips on that one click**; `⌘`-click toggles a row and `⇧`-click takes the run; `Return` commits down the column; `⇧Return` makes the next item; `⌘Return` opens the record **as a page** — the side peek is not carried forward (verdict below).

## The peek

Counted, not argued. #39 built the side peek as every row's click target; #117 replaced that with the entity page and kept `peekEntity` only "for callers that want a slide-over on top of a page". No such caller was ever written. The one call site left is the `⌘`-click row target added by #133 — the exact case #117 had ruled out. Dropping it frees `⌘`-click outright and removes `peekEntity` (~56 lines), 17 CSS rules and 5 `inPeek` branches threaded through `renderEntityView`. The one honest argument for keeping it — the table holds its scroll position — is the trade #117 already made.

## Recommendation

**Build REST. Ship EDGE behind a setting if the corridor proves worth it.**

REST never surprises anyone: the caret owns the horizontal arrows inside an open cell exactly as it does in every text field on the machine. EDGE is the stricter reading and its appeal is real — a row of short values walks end to end on one key — but the keypress that leaves the cell is indistinguishable from the one before it, and an **empty cell is at both edges at once**, so a run of blanks becomes a corridor you fall through. That is worth having deliberately, which is what a setting is for. It is one branch in the open-cell keymap.

1. Cells rest as values; hover arms them. The click path is unchanged, so `activateCell` is already correct — it just runs on an armed cell rather than a permanently live one.
2. One keymap. At rest: arrows and `Tab` move, `Space` selects, `Return` or any character opens. Open: `Return` commits down, `Tab` commits across, `Esc` reverts.
3. Selection from both hands — `⌘`/`⇧`-click and `Space`/`⇧↑↓`.
4. Drop the peek in the same change; that is what makes `⌘`-click free.
5. Then the puck bar of #132, which now has a selection to act on.
6. EDGE as a per-table or per-user setting once REST is in.

## Still open

- **Do `←`/`→` step out of an open cell?** The only thing separating REST from EDGE, and a setting rather than a verdict.
- Does `⇧`-click take a run of rows or a rectangle of cells? Rows is smaller and matches #132; cells opens fill-down and paste later and cannot be retrofitted cheaply.
- Where does the docs-chips column sit in the arrow and Tab order? Documents are not cells.
- Does a resting grid still read as editable on a table of mostly-empty fields?

## Artifact

`docs/mockups/table-grid-keymaps.html` (beside `table-bulk-select.html` from #132) — three live grids with real checkbox, select-picker and date-calendar columns. **An open text cell is a real `<input>`**, so EDGE's "step out at the end of the text" is measured from `selectionStart` rather than mimed, and a caret readout above the grid shows which edge the keymap is seeing.

## Test coverage

`test/grid-patterns.test.mjs` — 20 cases, Quality suite #42. The mockup carries ONE pure keymap core in `<script id="pattern-core">`; the test extracts and presses it, so the page and the asserted behaviour cannot drift. Asserts all four arrows plus `Tab` navigate at rest in both challengers; that neither can be `always-live`, because that is what would take `←`/`→` back; that the resting state hands over `Space`/`⇧↑↓`/`⌘A` for free while `Space` inside an open cell is still a space; that REST gives the horizontal arrows to the caret even at the text edge; that EDGE steps out only at an edge, passes straight through an empty cell (at both edges at once), and keeps `⇧←`/`⇧→` selecting text; and that the demo reads a real `selectionStart` rather than faking the edge.

### Slice shipped — 2026-09-05 (`b5e9054`, merged as `16c1b8e`)

REST is live: cells rest as values, the arrows and Tab navigate, Space selects, Return opens. `public/grid-keymap.js` is the study's REST core ported into the app (the pure half — `keymap`, `keyOf`, `step`, `extend`); the DOM half is one `keydown` listener in `renderTable` in `public/app.js`. The open-cell branch names where EDGE would go and does not build it.

**The cell is the focus stop.** Every field `<td>` carries `tabindex=0` and every control inside a row `-1`, so Tab lands on select, multi-select, checkbox and date cells (Issue #84) and the last cell of the last row is the end of the grid, never the browser chrome. Hover arms the one cell under the pointer; the resting cursor is an inset ring on the cell, in tokens, both themes.

**The open questions, decided:**

- *Where does the docs-chips column sit in the arrow and Tab order?* **Not a stop.** A document chip opens the record and holds no value the grid edits, so the cursor passes over it (`cell-nostop`). The description preview is the row's own prose and **is** a stop; Return opens it in the dock.
- *Rows or a rectangle for ⇧-click?* Rows, as #132 — and from the keyboard, ⇧↑/⇧↓ extend a run of rows keyed on entity ids with the same anchor rule as the checkbox column.
- *Do ← → step out of an open cell?* Not built (EDGE); one comment marks the branch.
- *Does a resting grid still read as editable on empty fields?* The hover arming is the cue; not re-studied here.

**Two departures from the text above, both forced by rulings that landed after it:** ⌘-click and ⇧-click on a cell stay the browser's (`023b777`, "the clicks the browser owns": ⌘ opens a tab, ⇧ a window), so pointer selection remains the checkbox column from slice 1 of #132 rather than moving onto the modifiers; and ⌘Return opens the record in the **dock**, the one entity panel since the peek was excised (`9d19e14`) — "as a page" predates that. Nothing of `peekEntity` remained to remove; two stale comments and one Handbook line went with this change.

Also fixed on the way: the inline-add path focused `td:nth-child(2) input`, the `#id` cell since the checkbox column landed, so a new row never opened on its name. ⇧Return (and the + New line) now open the first field cell.

Handbook: "The grid from the keyboard" under the grid guide, with the at-rest and open-cell tables.

Tests: `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs` (17 pure) + `test/grid-keymap-browser.test.mjs` (15 browser); `test/grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs` moved to the resting-cursor contract. Gate: 1625 pass, 0 skipped. Gerrit change 215.

**Still to build:** EDGE behind a per-table setting, if the corridor proves worth it (item 6 of the recommendation).

features.name: Agent surface coverage is a test, not a promise
Attachments chip uses paperclip emoji, not flat icon
features.description:
## Pain Point

The attachments chip (`.k-attach`, built in `public/app.js`) leads with a paperclip EMOJI (📎), which renders in colour and sits inconsistently beside the monochrome glyphs used by every other chip since the tiered chip/pill design system (value / pointer / computed) landed on 2026-08-24.

## Problem Statement

weave already vendors a flat icon set at `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js`, surfaced via the `iconEl('iconly:paper', 'wv-icon')` helper in `public/app.js` — that helper is the intended replacement for emoji glyphs, but the attachments chip wasn't switched over when the design system shipped.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Swap the 📎 emoji for the vendored flat paper-clip icon via `iconEl(...)` in the `.k-attach` chip build in `public/app.js`, matching how other chip tiers already render their leading glyph.



_Shipped 2026-08-31. The attachments chip draws `iconly:paper`; the paperclip emoji is gone._



---
**v0.5 triage (2026-09-02):** Verified shipped: 1a75472 — .k-attach chip draws iconly:paper; zero paperclip emoji left.

features.name: Expand STATE_ICONS glyph vocabulary (14 entries, now shared by select/multiselect)
features.description:
## Pain Point

`STATE_ICONS` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` has only 14 entries (`''  ○ ◔ ◑ ◕ ● ✓ ✕ ⏸ ⚑ ★ ! ? →`), surfaced via the `.opt-icon` button on each option row in the field tray — and since the 2026-08-24 chip/pill design system landed, that same picker is now offered to select and multiselect field options, not just workflow states.

## Problem Statement

14 glyphs is thin coverage for the union of workflow states plus every select/multiselect option across every field in the app. Authors will run out of distinct, meaningful icons and start reusing glyphs for unrelated options, undermining the point of the picker.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Expand `STATE_ICONS` with additional monochrome glyphs. Do NOT remove or reorder any of the existing 14 entries — authors may already have chosen them for existing options/states — only append.



_Shipped 2026-08-31. STATE_ICONS went from 14 entries to 19 drawn marks — blocked, running, link, automation and target joined — and the same catalogue is offered at every gate, not only the option row._



---
**v0.5 triage (2026-09-02):** Verified shipped: STATE_ICONS now 19 entries (field-dialog-core.js:130); 382d2f6 + 82f8e10.

features.name: files/url field types use emoji icons, not flat icons
features.description:
## Pain Point

In `FIELD_TYPES` (`public/field-dialog-core.js`), the `files` field type icon is 🗂 and the `url` field type icon is 🔗 — both colour emoji sitting among the otherwise-monochrome tiles in the field tray's type grid.

## Problem Statement

Same inconsistency as the attachments-chip emoji: the tiered chip/pill design system (2026-08-24) established a monochrome flat-icon vocabulary via `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js` and the `iconEl(...)` helper in `public/app.js`, but these two `FIELD_TYPES` entries were never migrated off emoji.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Replace both the `files` and `url` icons in `FIELD_TYPES` with flat icons from `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js` via the existing `iconEl(...)` helper, matching the treatment used elsewhere in the type grid.



_Shipped 2026-08-31 (ed47705). `url` takes the drawn link mark, `files` takes `iconly:folder`, and the tile renders through iconEl. A test fails any FIELD_TYPES tile carrying an Emoji_Presentation character._



---
**v0.5 triage (2026-09-02):** Verified shipped: 03b46e6 — no emoji left in the field-type grid; resolution inverted the title (flat marks won).

features.name: Define a first-class person field type with a real avatar
features.description:
## Pain Point

The weave chip system landed 2026-08-24 as Gerrit change 61 (repo grunion-ai/weave, files public/chip-core.js, public/style.css, public/app.js). It has three tiers — value (filled tint, no border), pointer (1px outline plus ↗), computed (glyph then value). Kyle's requirement during the design review was: "person field type should have an avatar no matter the chip style." That shipped, but on a heuristic, because weave has no person concept to hang it on.

## Problem Statement

* weave has no `person` field type. `VALUE_TYPES` in src/engine.js is text, number, date, daterange, checkbox, url, email, select, multiselect, workflow, relation, field, key, attachments. A colleague is just a `relation` to whatever table happens to hold people.
* weave also has no users/members concept at all — the only system table kind in src/engine.js is `workspace` (spaces and tables as rows). There is no identity to attach a photo, a display name, or a handle to.
* So `personAvatar()` in public/app.js decides person-ness by matching the RELATION'S TARGET TABLE NAME against a regex, `PERSON_TABLE = /^(people|persons?|members?|users?|contacts?|owners?|team|staff|employees?)$/i` in `relationIsPerson()`.
* That is wrong in both directions: a table called "Reviewers" or "Assignees" or anything in another language gets no avatar, and a table called "Team" that holds squads rather than humans gets avatars it should not have. It also silently changes behaviour when someone renames a table.
* The avatar today is initials on a hue hashed from the display name (`hueForName` and `initialsFor` in public/chip-core.js, hashing into the 9-entry RAMP_ORDER). There is no photo path at all — `.av img` exists in the CSS and nothing ever populates it.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Direction, not a spec to follow blindly:

* Add `person` to the field types as a first-class type, so person-ness is declared rather than guessed. `relationIsPerson()` in public/app.js is the single function that changes — it was written to be that seam, and the comment in the source says so.
* Decide what a person IS in weave: probably a designated people table per workspace, or a built-in system table alongside the existing `workspace` one. This is the real design question and should be settled before any code.
* Give a person a photo. `.av img` styling already exists in public/style.css and the files API (`/api/files/:id`) and the `attachments` field already handle uploads, so the plumbing is largely there; the missing piece is where the photo lives on the person record.
* Keep initials-on-a-hashed-hue as the fallback when there is no photo — that behaviour is already tested and Kyle liked it.
* Add the type to the tray's `FIELD_TYPES` grid in public/field-dialog-core.js so it is selectable, with a flat icon (see sibling ticket #1875 about emoji-vs-flat icons in that same grid).

Known limitations to carry forward:

* Nine ramp hues plus a name hash means two colleagues sometimes get the same avatar colour. Initials still separate them and a photo removes the question, but it is worth deciding whether the hash should widen when the person type lands.
* Contract tests for the current behaviour live in test/chip-system.test.mjs (the avatar, initials and hash tests). Those pin the fallback and should survive; the test asserting the target-table heuristic is the one that changes.

Sibling of the other weave chip-system follow-ups filed the same day: Task Name #1873 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-42e3-7d42-8d5d-28b2587e1b03]], Task Name #1874 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-4b0e-77e2-a8a0-dcbc4ace5fd1]], Task Name #1875 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-5364-723c-a6f6-01ca84af0e43]].

features.name: The picker is a token box: chips live with the cursor
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-25 (Kyle) — *"selected chips should be in the cursor box so user can navigate around with arrows to quckly delete and type to add with the top fit autoselected on search and added with enter up down arros to navigate options enter to select. pressing enter with none selected updates the select field. true for multi select and linked fileds, single select and states are slickly different since selection overwrites"*

## What changed

The chosen values moved **inside** the search field. One box now carries both halves of the edit — the chips already chosen, then the caret — instead of a chosen-list stacked above a separate search bar. Everything that picks from a list opens it: multiselect, linked records, select, workflow states, field types, formats.

## The grammar

| Key | multi (multiselect, linked records) | single (select, workflow state) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| typing | filters the list with the **top fit armed** | same |
| `Enter` | adds the armed option (a second `Enter` takes it back out), clears the search, stays open | picks it — a selection **overwrites**, so it commits and closes |
| `Enter` on an empty search | saves the set | closes; the field already carries what is in the box |
| `↑` `↓` | move the arming through the visible list | same |
| `←` `→` | walk the chips in the box, from the caret leftward | walks its one chip |
| `Backspace` | takes the last chip, or the one the cursor sits on | picks the field's empty value (`—`); a workflow state has none, so it is refused |
| `Delete` | takes the chip under the cursor, cursor stays put | same |
| `Esc` | closes without saving | closes |
| outside click | saves (unchanged) | closes |

**Top fit** is a ranking, not "first one containing the letters": exact label, then prefix, then word-prefix, then anywhere in the label, then a hint-only match (a record's `#id` on a link picker). Typing `do` against Backlog / To do / Doing / Done arms **Doing**.

## Where it lives

| Layer | File |
| --- | --- |
| The grammar, pure | `public/picker-core.js` — `keyDown` returns `{state, effect}`; effects are `pick` / `commit` / `close` |
| The DOM | `searchPicker` in `public/app.js` — feeds it keys plus whether the text caret sits at position 0 |
| The box | `.picker-box` / `.picker-chips` (`display:contents`) / `.picker-chip.sel` in `public/style.css` |
| Tests | `test/picker-core.test.mjs` (16 cases) + two contract cases in `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` |

Chips redraw as their own element so a redraw never detaches the focused input; `display:contents` keeps them flowing in the box's own row, so a full box wraps with the caret rather than clipping.

## Verified live (127.0.0.1:4400, Product/Task, both themes)

| Field | Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Tags` multiselect | `ch` → Enter, `bu` → Enter, `←` `←` Backspace, Enter | `['design','feature','bug']` persisted |
| `Priority` select | `p2` → Enter | `P2` written and closed |
| `Priority` select | Backspace on its chip | cleared to empty |
| `State` workflow | `rev` → Enter | `Review`; the chip carries no `×` and Backspace is refused |
| `Project` linked | `←` Backspace then `Esc` | edit discarded, link intact |


## Amended 2026-08-26 (change 67, commit 7a1cfe8) — three rows of the grammar above are now wrong

Kyle used the shipped box and filed [[Issue#63]], [[Issue#64]] and
[[Issue#65]]. The first two were one defect: chosen options stayed in the list
wearing a ✓, so `↓` from a fresh box usually armed something already chosen and
Enter took it back out. Read these rows in place of the ones in the table:

| Key | multi (multiselect, linked records) | single (select, workflow state) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the list | holds only what is **not** already a chip in the box | unchanged — the current value stays listed and ticked |
| `Enter` | adds the armed option and disarms the list; it can no longer take one back out | unchanged |
| `Enter` after a pick | nothing is armed, so it saves — pick-then-Enter is the whole edit | n/a |
| `Enter` on a search matching only what is chosen | nothing (it used to fall through and save) | nothing |
| `⌥1`–`⌥9` | takes the row that number names | same |
| un-picking | `⌫` on the chip, or its × | unchanged |

The `✓` on a multi row is gone with the row itself. An emptied list says
"Everything is chosen" rather than "No matches". Every visible row carries its
number; Option is the modifier because the box is a search field and a bare
digit has to keep typing.

New gate: `test/picker-browser.test.mjs` drives the box through real key
presses in Chromium. The "Verified live" table below was a hand check, and a
hand check is what let [[Issue#63]] ship.

features.name: Users: identity, auth, permissions, sharing (design-only spec)
features.description:
# Users — complete spec (outline; details intentionally blank)

Design-only feature request. Nothing here is scheduled for implementation. Each section below gets filled in one at a time, in review with Kyle; a section is done when its **Decisions** block replaces its **Open questions** block. The spec is complete when no section still says TBD.

**Existing substrate (v0.4, Feature #14):** `wv_` bearer tokens (sha256 stored, minted once), roles admin/writer/reader, `requireAuth` workspace switch, structural audit log with actor, `createdBy`/`modifiedBy` strings on entities. Deliberately deferred then: account rows as a registry table, per-space permissions. This spec is the full build-out that deferral pointed at.

---

## 1. Identity model — who a "user" is

Scope: the User as a first-class record; the relationship between User (person or agent), Account (credential holder), and Actor (audit attribution). Whether agents are users with a flag or a separate kind.

Open questions: user vs account — one thing or two? Are agents users? Is identity server-wide or per-workspace? Canonical identifier (handle, email, id)?

Details: TBD.

## 2. System table of users

Scope: Users as a registry/system table visible in the UI like Spaces/Tables/Fields — queryable, relatable, but lifecycle-managed by the system, not row CRUD.

Open questions: which space does it live in? What is user-editable vs system-owned? Does it depend on a key/sensitive field type so tokens can never render? Export behavior?

Details: TBD.

## 3. Authentication

Scope: how a human signs in to the web app and how an agent authenticates to the API/MCP. Sessions vs bearer tokens. The `requireAuth` switch's final semantics.

Open questions: password, magic link, OAuth/OIDC, or token-only? Session storage and expiry? Local single-user mode — does auth stay optional forever on localhost? Interplay with hosting (Fly.io SaaS vs BYOC), where auth is the known blocker.

Details: TBD.

## 4. Keys: CLI + MCP keygen and association

Scope: full `wv_` token lifecycle — mint, list, rotate, revoke, expire, scope — via CLI, MCP, and UI; every key bound to a user; per-agent keys.

Open questions: scoped keys (read-only, one space, one table)? Expiry defaults? Rotation UX? How does an MCP session name its user? Key display safety (needs the key field type)?

Details: TBD.

## 5. User levels (roles)

Scope: the role ladder. Today admin/writer/reader; decide the final set and what each rung means globally.

Open questions: add owner? guest/viewer distinct from reader? Are roles global, per-workspace, or both? Can a user hold different roles in different workspaces?

Details: TBD.

## 6. Permissions & access control

Scope: the enforcement model — what a role can see and do at workspace, space, table, and entity level. Schema-vs-data split (registry-row writes already count as schema).

Open questions: per-space permissions (the deferred half of #14)? Entity-level or field-level ACLs, or explicitly out of scope? Default-open or default-closed? Inheritance and override rules? Read visibility vs write rights?

Details: TBD.

## 7. Workspace assignment & membership

Scope: one server, many workspace `.db` files — who belongs to which workspace, membership records, default workspace on login.

Open questions: where does membership live (per-workspace db vs server-level)? Can a workspace be personal vs shared? What does removing a member do to their attributions?

Details: TBD.

## 8. Invites

Scope: getting a new user in — invite creation, delivery, acceptance, expiry, and the role granted on join.

Open questions: invite = link token? email delivery or copy-paste link only (zero-dep constraint)? Who may invite? Re-invite/revoke? What happens pre-acceptance in people fields?

Details: TBD.

## 9. Sharing

Scope: granting access narrower than membership — share an entity, view, or document with a user, or via link; public/anonymous links.

Decisions (2026-09-07, with Kyle — build-out designed as [[Feature#194]]):

* **Sharing is v1.** One grant object in `state.meta.shares` replaces every bespoke public surface: `{ id, token 'wvs_…', scope {kind: entity|table|space|view|workspace, id}, mode, visibility, label, createdBy, createdAt, expiresAt?, revokedAt? }`. A document is its entity's doc surface, so there is no `document` scope kind.
* **Powers are a ladder, not a flag:** read / comment / edit / manage (add-delete). `comment` ships in the enum and the dialog but answers 403 until §12 lands. `edit` updates in-scope entities only; `manage` adds create and delete; neither ever touches schema or registry rows, keeping [[Feature#14]]'s schema rule intact.
* **A share composes with permissions rather than bypassing them.** One containment function, `withinScope(grant, target)`, gates the page surface, the API read and the API write alike; it can only ever narrow, never widen.
* **Two visibilities.** `public` resolves for anyone holding the link; `private` resolves only for a signed-in account — the middle rung between a public URL and full membership.
* **Tokens are stored in plaintext** so the dialog can re-show a link, and are redacted from export. Revocation is the control, not secrecy at rest. This pass also fixes the export leak of account `tokenHash` and view `shareToken`.
* **Shares are audited** on mint and revoke through [[Feature#14]]'s existing actor plumbing.
* **[[Feature#17]] is absorbed:** existing view `shareToken`s lift into grants on load and `/view/:token` becomes a redirect, so links already handed out keep working. The passcode applet keeps its own door for now.
* Deferred: per-user sharing (needs §1 identity), editable web pages under `/s/`, remote chips into another instance, passcodes on shares.

## 10. People field type

Scope: a real field type holding user references on any entity — assignee, owner, reviewer. Single and multi. `createdBy`/`modifiedBy` graduate from strings to user refs.

Open questions: is it a relation to the Users table or a distinct primitive? Filtering/grouping semantics ("me" filter)? @-mentions in documents? Watchers as a people field?

Details: TBD.

## 11. Avatars

Scope: avatar image per user — storage in `files/`, upload paths (UI/CLI/API), rendering in chips, people fields, activity, comments; deterministic initials/color fallback; agent avatars distinguishable from humans.

Open questions: size/format limits? Generated identicon vs initials? Where do avatars render first?

Details: TBD.

## 12. Attribution, activity & audit

Scope: every write attributed to a user everywhere — entity activity feeds, comments, document edits, and the existing structural audit log — with one actor model across all of them.

Open questions: backfill of historical string actors ("web", "cli")? Does the audit log become user-queryable per user? Retention?

Details: TBD.

## 13. Notifications

Scope (not in the original list — proposed): telling a user something happened — mention, assignment, state change on a watched entity.

Open questions: in-app only, or email/webhook? Digest vs realtime? Is this deferred to its own feature once people fields exist?

Details: TBD.

## 14. Presence & concurrent editing

Scope (not in the original list — proposed): who is here now — presence dots, and how user identity interacts with concurrent edits/conflicts.

Open questions: in scope at all, or explicitly deferred? Minimum viable presence without websockets?

Details: TBD.

## 15. Admin surface

Scope: managing users — UI page, CLI (`account …` grows into `user …`), MCP tools; deactivate vs delete; what admin-only means once users exist.

Open questions: soft-deactivate semantics (keys die, attributions persist)? Last-admin protection? Impersonation for debugging — allowed or banned?

Details: TBD.

## 16. API / CLI / MCP surface

Scope: the complete external contract — REST endpoints, CLI commands, MCP tools — for everything above, named and versioned in one place.

Open questions: naming (`account` vs `user`)? Back-compat for existing `wv_` tokens and `account` CLI? What do anonymous requests see when `requireAuth` is off?

Details: TBD.

## 17. Data model & migration

Scope: sqlite tables (users, memberships, invites, shares, sessions, keys), what `exportJSON`/`importJSON` carry (never key material), migration from v0.4 accounts, JSON-workspace behavior.

Open questions: users in the workspace db or a server-level db beside it? Export portability of identity across servers? Downgrade story?

Details: TBD.

## 18. Security model

Scope: threat model and hard rules — hashing, one-time key display, rate limiting, session fixation, CSRF for the web app, injection-safe rendering of user-supplied names/avatars, secrets never in exports or logs.

Open questions: which of these are v1 gates vs hosted-only concerns? Brute-force lockout policy?

Details: TBD.

## 19. Rollout & testing

Scope: TDD gates per section, phase ordering (what unlocks what), milestone assignment, and the definition of done for the whole feature.

Open questions: likely spine — users table → people field → permissions → invites → sharing? Which milestone (v0.5 hosting wants auth early)?

Details: TBD.

---

**Walkthrough state:** none of the 19 sections reviewed yet. Next action: go through them one by one with Kyle, replacing Open questions with Decisions.



## Kyle's direction, 2026-10-02 (Slack model, no hub root)

Kyle, verbatim: "I'm not sure if I want a hub root. I want the workspace behaviour to be more like slack where I can use different logins to different workspaces but still see it all within my one environment. I own what spaces are in my environment provided I have access. But other than that my privileges in each workspace are determined by my role and perms based on whoever invited me to that workspace."

This answers several open questions above:

- **Identity is per workspace.** An account lives in its workspace and links to one login (provider email plus pinned subject). The same person may use different logins in different workspaces. This is the model weave already has; the hub root is the exception.
- **Roles are per workspace**, granted by whoever invited the person (Feature #255 roles: Observer, Editor, Architect).
- **The environment belongs to the person.** It is the set of workspaces any of their logins can open, shown in one rail. The person adds or removes workspaces from it; adding needs access.
- **No hub root.** No account administers every workspace. Workspace creation, the keystore and the workspace list stop depending on the default workspace's admins.

Open questions this raises:

1. Where the environment lives: client-held sessions, one per workspace (Slack's model; no workspace learns about the others), or a server-side person record that links several logins (syncs across devices, but the instance then knows which logins belong together).
2. Who may create a workspace once the root is gone: any signed-in login (creator becomes Architect), or an operator switch.
3. Where the hub root's remaining jobs go: the keystore per workspace, the docs workspace as an ordinary workspace, operator verbs (backup, restore, rescue) on the CLI only.
4. MCP: `/w/<name>/mcp` already fits (Feature #254). `/mcp` would become "the workspaces this login can open", with a workspace argument on each tool, rather than the default workspace.
5. Migration of today's root admin and the `deploy-check` admin tokens.

Recorded by the harness session of 2026-10-02 (weave v0.4.54 on main).



## Kyle's rulings, 2026-10-02 (second pass)

Kyle accepted the three recommendations above: **client-held sessions** with a "find my workspaces" step per login (no server-side person record), **any signed-in login may create a workspace** and becomes its Architect (operator switch to turn it off), and the **root's leftover jobs** move to each workspace (keystore) or to the CLI on the box (backup, restore, rescue).

One exception, verbatim: "keep weave docs (self named workspace) as unremovable workspace for which everyone is an observer (and a submitted via bug submission) which will be a type of form".

- **The `weave` docs workspace is built in.** It cannot be deleted, renamed or left. It appears in every environment.
- **Everyone is an Observer there.** No invite needed; nobody's role there comes from an inviter.
- **Everyone may submit a bug.** Submission goes through a form, a new kind of thing that lets a role with no write access create one row in one table (Feature #257). Today's `POST /api/bug-report` route (Feature #142) becomes the first form.
- Open: does "everyone" include signed-out visitors (a public Handbook), or only signed-in logins on the instance?

features.name: In-app bug reporter: four symptoms + a replayable action trace
features.description:
## What shipped

A bug glyph sits in the bottom-right corner of every page. Clicking it floats a small panel beside the button — no backdrop, so the broken page stays visible while the report is written.

The panel is note-first: the caret lands in the text box, so the fastest report is to start typing. Under it, four symptoms toggle as a **multi-select** — `Slow`, `Looks broken`, `Wrong data`, `Error` — because one bug is often slow *and* wrong. Either half is enough to send: a sentence alone is the "other" nobody needs a fifth button for. The Send button becomes **Sent** in place rather than relying on a toast.

## Why it is worth more than a bug form

Every session runs a ring-buffer recorder (`public/bug-core.js`). It keeps routes entered, controls clicked, requests that failed or were slow, and anything that threw. Submitting turns that into a **Replay** section: numbered steps, each stamped with how many seconds before the click on Send it happened, plus the raw trace as JSON so an agent parses instead of scraping prose.

Two rules the buffer never breaks:

- **Values are not actions.** A control is remembered by its name — a grid cell by its column and its row's entity id — never by what was typed into it. Secrets are stripped before the report leaves the page.
- **An error outranks recency.** At capacity the buffer drops an ordinary event, never the throw.

Quiet successful reads are not recorded at all. A page load fires a dozen 200-in-3ms GETs; recorded, they filled the buffer with the app working correctly and pushed the actual actions off the end (measured live: 17 requests to 5 actions). Only failures, slow calls, and real writes are evidence — and weave posts its reads, so the rule classifies by path, not by verb.

## Where it lands

`POST /api/bug-report` files into **this** workspace's `Development/Issue` whichever workspace the reporter was in — a bug in weave is not a row in somebody's data. Symptoms go into the `Symptom` multiselect so a week of reports is filterable; severity is the worst symptom picked, Medium when none is. The server stamps its own version, start time and uptime rather than trusting the page's copy — a stale build reporting its own version is how this project's most common false bug starts.

A workspace whose `Symptom` options were renamed, or that predates the field, still keeps the report: the symptom survives in the Description and the field is left alone. A label edit costs the field, not the bug.

## Tests

`test/bug-report.test.mjs` — 55 cases across the recorder, redaction, the rendered report, the route, and the UI's own source-level promises (including a parse gate, after a traced SVG path arrived with potrace's line wraps still inside a string literal and blanked the page).

features.name: Credential field: generalize key (design-only spec)
features.description:
# Credential field — generalizing `key` (design-only spec)

Design-only feature request, sibling to Feature #141 (Users). Nothing here is scheduled for implementation. It answers the one question #141 §6 left open — "field-level ACLs, or explicitly out of scope?" — with: **out of scope, permanently.** Permission moves to the credential, not the field.

**Existing substrate (v0.4, Feature #64):** the `key` field type stores the NAME of a secret; the value lives in `~/.weave/keystore.json` (chmod 600), never enters the workspace `.db`, and is deliberately unreadable over HTTP. `resolveKey` exists only for the engine's own consumers (automations, integrations). MCP promises "no tool returns a secret value."

---

## 1. The thesis: permission belongs to the secret, not the field

The two motivating use cases — a team-shared password and a stored SSN — both require that a human can get the value back out, which breaks the current never-read-back contract on purpose. The design keeps the deeper invariant instead: **the secret value never enters the table.** The field stores metadata (ordinary table data, visible to anyone with table access — no exception to "table access = see the table"). The value lives in a credential object with **its own access list**, and reveal is a separate, authorized, audited act against that object.

This is how every mature secret manager already works: 1Password gates by vault, AWS Secrets Manager by resource policy — per-secret, never per-field. It also avoids weave's first per-field read rule, which would otherwise have to be consulted by every view, formula, lookup, export, deck render, and MCP read path, and would invite row-level ACLs next.

## 2. Grain (what the field stores)

```
{
  kind: 'apikey' | 'token' | 'id' | 'password' | 'pair',
  keystore: 'local' | '1password' | 'aws-sm' | 'google-sm' | 'cloudflare' | 'apple-passwords',
  ref: string,            // keystore entry name / external ref
  parts?: [{name, secret: bool}],   // pairs: client_id (visible) + client_secret (masked)
  redacted?: bool,        // overrides the kind default
  rotatedAt?, rotatedBy?  // metadata only
}
```

* `pair` is ONE credential with named parts, only the secret part masked. Two fields pointing at two entries loses the pairing and doubles ACL bookkeeping.
* Kind sets the default posture, it does not decide masking alone: an AWS account ID is an `id` fine in the open; an SSN is an `id` that is not. `redacted` is per-credential.

## 3. Costume (how it renders)

Masked chip: kind glyph + keystore badge + label + `●●●●` in mono. Click → reveal (if permitted) with auto-rehide; copy-without-display button; inline audit note ("revealed 3× this week"). The value never renders in a normal cell path.

## 4. Access model

* **No field-level permissions.** Table access governs the metadata only.
* Per-credential ACL on the keystore entry: v1 = `owner (creator) + shared-with account list`, built on the existing v0.4 accounts (`wv_` tokens, admin/writer/reader), upgradeable when #141 lands real users.
* Kind defaults: `password`/`apikey`/`token`/`pair` → open to keystore holders (availability to the team); `id` with `redacted` → owner-only (confinement). One mechanism, opposite defaults.
* **Copy counts as reveal.** Copy-to-clipboard-without-display is the primary UX (value never hits the screen) but is identical in the access model and the audit log.
* Every reveal/copy lands in the existing `audit_log` (who, which credential, when) and is surfaced in the UI. The visible trail is what makes team sharing tolerable.

## 5. External keystores delegate

For 1Password / AWS SM / Google SM / Cloudflare refs, weave stores `{keystore, ref}` and never holds the value. Reveal = deep link into the manager, or resolution through the integration's own auth — the external manager's access model gates the value. Weave's own ACL question exists **only for the local keystore**. Apple Passwords has no server API: ref-only, "open in Passwords" affordance, full stop. This tiering is also the scope fence: weave's local keystore serves automation creds and low/mid-stakes team secrets; anything deserving a real vault gets a pointer to one. Weave never becomes 1Password.

## 6. Local keystore prerequisites

* **Encrypt at rest before widening what goes in.** Plaintext JSON at 0600 is fine for API keys on a single-user local instance; not fine once SSNs and hosted (v0.5) exist. This is a gate, not a nice-to-have.
* One new surface: `POST /api/keys/:name/reveal` (or per-credential id), ACL-checked, always audited. Admin token alone is not sufficient — the ACL is.

## 7. The exclusion invariant (kept, made explicit)

No formula, lookup, or rollup may ever reference a secret value — a formula concatenating a secret into a text field is a one-step exfiltration bypassing every reveal control. Automations receive values only as injected headers/env at execution time, never as readable intermediate state. Values never enter search index, exports, decks, or MCP reads; if a reveal MCP tool ever exists it is a deliberate, separately-scoped tool, not a widening of `weave_query`. Today all of this is free because the value is not in the db — the spec makes it a stated contract so it survives the generalization.

## 8. Migration

Existing `key` fields become `kind: 'apikey', keystore: 'local'` with **no reveal grant** — the current never-read-back promise holds for everything already stored. Reveal-ability is opt-in per credential, by its owner.

## 9. Sequencing

1. **Grain + costume.** Kind/keystore/ref/parts/redacted config, masked chip rendering. No access change — everything still non-revealable. Ships independently, pure win.
2. **Encrypt the local keystore.**
3. **Per-credential ACL + audited reveal/copy** for the local keystore, on v0.4 accounts.
4. **External keystore refs** — Cloudflare/AWS/Google first (they have APIs); Apple link-only.

## 10. Open questions

* Encryption key management for the local keystore (server key beside the db? passphrase? OS keychain?).
* Does `resolveKey` for automations need per-credential ACL too, or does "automation = workspace-level actor" hold until #141 lands?
* Reveal session shape: per-click grants vs short-lived reveal tokens.
* Whether `id`-kind non-secret values (visible account IDs) should ever store the value in-table instead of the keystore — or whether uniformity wins.

**Walkthrough state:** thesis and access model discussed with Kyle 2026-08-26 (chat); sections 2–9 drafted, not yet reviewed one-by-one.

features.name: Column ⋮ menu redesign: drawn icons, one row metric, an advertised hold
features.description:
**Asked for by Kyle, 2026-08-27**, with a screenshot of the open menu: *"redesign this dialog to match weave design language. I like the hold to delete and animation."*

The column header's ⋮ menu was the last surface still assembling itself out of characters. Five rows in one small panel and no two of them agreed.

## What the screenshot showed

| Row | What it was | Why it read wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `✎ Edit field…` | a pencil **character** inside the label string | the font gives ✎ its own advance width and optical size |
| `+ Insert field…` | a plus character, same trick | a different advance width, so a different label left-edge |
| `↑ Sort ascending` | arrow character, plus a `'✓ '` prefix when the sort was live | the check shunted the whole row right whenever it was on |
| `↓ Sort descending` | ditto | — |
| `Delete field` | a Tabler `.dropdown-item`, red, no icon | another design system's padding and radius among weave's, and its label started somewhere none of the others did |

Four different left edges in a five-row menu, and four optical sizes among the glyphs. This is the exact defect **Issue #87** names — *"a unicode mark carries its own advance width and its own optical size"* — on the one surface that issue had not reached.

## What it is now

1. **Every mark is drawn.** `iconEl()` at `--wv-icon-md`, on the same `0 0 24 24` canvas as the rest of the app. `FIELD_MENU_ICONS` names them in one place. Picked by eye off a contact sheet of every candidate in both vocabularies, not by name: `iconly:arrow-up` is a solid teardrop that reads as a **map pin** at 16px, so sort uses the drawn `↑` / `↓` marks. `edit` and `delete` stay on iconly because that is what the entity command bar already draws for the same two verbs.
2. **A bare `+` joined the mark set.** Iconly's only plus is a filled rounded square, which came out the darkest thing on the panel beside a hairline pencil. `'+': line('M12 5.4v13.2M5.4 12h13.2')` — stroke 2.6, the same move Issue #87 made for the five marks it drew. Not offered in the icon picker; `STATE_ICONS` is unchanged.
3. **One row for every row.** The destructive row is a `.chip-pop-row` now, tinted, not a `.dropdown-item`. `holdToConfirm` takes a `rowClass` so the other four call sites keep theirs.
4. **Sort state is the popover's own check**, in the trailing `.chip-pop-check` slot the picker already uses — so the label never moves, and `showPopover` opens focus on the live sort for free.
5. **The panel names its column.** `Priority · SELECT` above a rule. The ⋮ paints millimetres from the *next* column's label (live check, 2026-08-16) and the hovered tint was the only thing tying panel to column.
6. **The hold is kept and advertised.** Kyle likes the gesture; a hold nobody knows about is a button that does nothing. The row carries a quiet `HOLD` chip at rest that clears once the press starts, where the swapped `Hold to delete…` label takes over. The sweep is now a `linear-gradient` off `--tblr-danger` rather than a literal `rgba(214,57,57,.25)`, darkening toward the leading edge so it reads as a front travelling across the row instead of a block growing out of the left. Still `scaleX` on a transform, still untransitioned on collapse — the Feature #75 contract is untouched.
7. **Popovers arrive rather than appear** — `wv-pop-in`, 120ms, opacity + transform only, with a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out. Shared by every `.chip-pop`.

## A bug found on the way

The delete row being a `.dropdown-item` was not only a look. `showPopover` walks `.chip-pop-row` for ↑↓, so **the one row that most deserves deliberate aim was the only one the keyboard could not reach.** Logged as its own Issue.

## Evidence

`after-light.png`, `after-dark.png`, `after-sorted.png`, `after-holding.png` (attached) — the panel in both themes, with a live sort, and mid-sweep at ~430ms. Captured with Playwright at 1200×760 @2x against a throwaway workspace.

## Gates

- `test/field-menu-browser.test.mjs` — **7 new cases, real browser.** All seven fail against the pre-change `public/` and pass after; verified by running the suite against `git show HEAD:public/{app.js,style.css}` in a scratch tree.
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` — 7 new source/CSS contracts (131 → 138). Same before/after check.
- `node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'` → **1108 pass, 0 fail.**

features.name: The description is a role, and it previews its first lines
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-08-27: "description should be a default field in all entities. it can be renamed or deleted but it should always show a preview of the properly formatted first few lines, not an md document chip."

Three claims, and only the first was true.

## The role

`createTable` already minted a `Description` document field on every table, but the role lived in the literal string and in the accident of sorting first. A table now carries **`descriptionFieldId`**, beside `nameFieldId` — an id, so a rename costs nothing to maintain, and `null` on delete, which is the tombstone that lets `#ensureDescriptionField` tell "the owner removed it" from "this table predates the role" (`undefined`, which adopts the first document field rather than minting a second).

Unlike `nameFieldId`, nothing is defended: renaming and deleting are the point. Every reader of "the default document" — `#resolveDocField`, `readEntity`, the append-doc automation and its label — goes through one `descriptionField(db)`, so reordering columns no longer silently reassigns which document is the description. Registry tables have no description role: their `Description` is the TEXT column mirroring the real space/table description, and Workflows' `Script`/`Diagram` are structure, not prose.

`describeSchema` emits `role: "description"` on the one field that holds it, and `applySchema` renames the minted field to match instead of skipping any descriptor literally called `Description`.

## The preview

The description leaves the `Docs (n)` cell for a **column of its own**, which reconciles the two rulings rather than reversing either. What Kyle rejected on 2026-08-24 was a flattened 90-character slice of ONE document standing in for the row ([[Issue#58]]); Spec, Model and test keep exactly the chips that ruling won. The description gets a column because it says something.

`WeaveEditorLib.docPreview(md, { lines })` is the block pass and the only one: hashes off headings, bullets off list items, quote carets dropped, tables, rules and fenced code skipped whole. Each line is then dressed through `inlineTokens`, so there is still one inline grammar in the browser, shared with `dressedText` via a new `dressTokens`. A document that is not prose is NAMED, never flattened — `HTML app` (its `<title>` when it has one), `JSON model · 2 keys`, `graph diagram` — because a doctype makes a terrible summary. Classification is `docKind`'s, so a preview and a chip can never disagree.

**Where the design could not take Kyle literally.** A row holds ONE line. `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` requires every docs-carrying row to be the same height and at most 48px comfortable / 34px compact — caps Kyle himself drove a comfortable row down to on 2026-08-26. Two lines is ~43px of content and blows both. So the cell shows the first line and carries the rest hidden in the same DOM, and `showCellPop`'s `cloneNode` copy reveals all three on hover at 380px, wrapped. `markClippedCells` gained an OR for "carries more than one preview line", or a cell whose first line fits would never be markable and the rest would be unreachable. Empty is a dashed invitation — never opacity, never Tabler's global `.empty`.

## Bugs found and fixed on the way

[[Issue#104]] a deleted description came back on the next open. [[Issue#105]] a renamed Issue description threw the whole bug report away. [[Issue#106]] describeSchema→applySchema duplicated a renamed description and re-minted a deleted one.

## Gates

New: `test/description-field.test.mjs` (9), `test/doc-preview.test.mjs` (11). Extended: `test/schema-roundtrip.test.mjs` (+4), `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` (+3, live Chrome — marks not syntax, hover reveals the rest, empty is dashed), `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (+1), `test/doc-chips.test.mjs` (+1 and the ruling narrowed in its header rather than deleted), `test/bug-report.test.mjs` (+1), `test/applet.test.mjs` (+1), `test/handbook.test.mjs` (+1 — the page said "Documents never take a column of their own" and NOTHING pinned the sentence, so it could have rotted silently; that hole is closed).

Suite: **1142 pass, 0 fail.**

features.name: The task applet: one table, one screen, one thumb
features.description:
# The task applet

`/w/<ws>/t` — a passcode-gated single page over one table, built for mobile Safari and nothing else. No workspace rail, no table switcher: a view onto a table, not the web app. Kyle, 2026-08-27: *"its more like a view to a weave table than a weave web app"*.

## Where it sits

Generated by `src/applet.js`, mounted in `src/routes.js` in the block that already existed for share links — **ahead of the auth wall**, because like a share link it carries its own authorization. Not dropped in `public/`: on the Cloudflare adapter the assets binding serves `public/` before the Worker runs, so a file there would be ungated forever.

## The gate

`WEAVE_APPLET_PASSCODE`, compared in constant time, answered with a server-set `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1y` cookie. WebKit caps *script-written* cookies at seven days; one the page never touches it leaves alone. With no passcode configured there is no applet at all — not even a gate to guess at. The passcode lives in the environment, never in the workspace, so it cannot leave through `/api/export`.

Eight wrong tries in ten minutes and the door stops answering, per workspace rather than per process.

## Field-driven

The applet bakes in no field names. The workflow field is whichever field has that type, its states are its own, and *active* is a question about categories — not about the word "Open". Every other field draws itself from its type through weave's own hue ramp (`public/chip-core.js`), so a field added to the table appears on the phone with no code change. `WEAVE_APPLET_TABLE` points it somewhere else and the page follows.

## What it does

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Create | Return creates and keeps the caret; the next task is one keystroke away |
| State | The glyph cycles not-started → in-progress → done, by category |
| Swipe | Right marks it done, left marks it in progress — absolute, not relative, and armed only past 24px so Safari's back gesture survives |
| Fields | One chip rail on the task page, 58pt where labelled rows took 370; every chip opens its editor as a sheet on the same page |
| Blanks | An empty deadline or tag set still holds a dashed chip on the row — triage happens in the list |
| Dates | Today / Tomorrow / the day after by name / Next week as chips, `parseNaturalDate` for what you type, the native picker underneath |
| Files | From the compose paperclip or the task page |
| Prose | `PUT /t/entity/:id/doc`, written in a full-height sheet |
| Defaults | `WEAVE_APPLET_DEFAULTS` applies field values to everything it creates |
| Bugs | The weave FAB, filing real `Development/Issue` rows and answering with the number |

## The keyboard

Safari grants `focus()` only inside a user gesture, and an `await` spends it. So the focus call happens first, synchronously, in the tap that enters the eighth digit — which is why the gate is an overlay on this page rather than a page of its own. A navigation would have thrown the gesture away.

Focusing *without* a gesture is actively harmful: the caret lands but no keyboard comes, and the user's first real tap is then a tap on an already-focused input, which raises nothing. A coarse pointer is left alone on open; the first tap that is not aimed at a row raises the keyboard via blur-then-focus.

One tap remains the floor. iOS grants no gesture to a page opened from a Shortcut or a Home Screen icon, and nothing in the page can conjure one.

## Hosted

Deployed to the grunion Cloudflare account as `weave-uno`, one SQLite-backed Durable Object, seeded from `uno.db` on 2026-08-28. **The hosted copy and the local file are separate copies and do not sync** — a decision still open.

## Tests

`test/applet.test.mjs`, 32 cases: the gate, the forged cookie, the rate limit, the scope of the data, the promise that the applet can only ever reach its own table, and the field-driven contract against a table whose workflow is called Stage.

features.name: Nav stats strip: workspace entity count + on-disk size
features.description:
The sidebar foot carries a quiet stats strip under "+ New space": the workspace's live entity total and what it weighs on disk, in GB (TB past 1000 GB).

## How it works

- `engine.storageStats()` — live entity count (trashed rows excluded) + size: the store's `.db` with WAL/SHM sidecars plus attachment bytes summed from each entity's own file ledger. `files/` is shared by every sibling workspace, so the directory itself is never the measure.
- `GET /api/health` ships `entities` + `sizeBytes` with the existing payload — workspace-scoped, one fetch shared with the instance chip (`state.healthP`).
- `renderNav` sums the same per-table `entityCount` figures the nav rows already show; `fmtSize` speaks GB/TB only (a small workspace reads "0.01 GB", never switches down to MB).
