- `.nav-stats` in style.css: 11px monospace secondary, same register as the version chip. Verified in both themes.

Shipped in commit a87f8dc; suite `test/nav-stats.test.mjs` (5 cases) covers engine, store, health route, formatter and markup.

features.name: Fast in-app navigation: rope reserved for workspace loads, skeleton carries hash routes, 304 statics, custom 404 page
features.description:
Space/table/entity switches felt slow. Measured: the API answers in milliseconds (schema 2.6ms, table query 0.7ms) — the wait was the loader itself. withPageLoader wrapped every hash route; the rope appeared at 200ms and then always finished a full 2s cycle, and its 94%-opaque wash covered the Feature #49 skeleton it painted over.

Shipped:
- The rope is reserved for full page loads (boot — which is also every workspace switch, since those navigate to /w/<id>/). Hash routes ride the skeleton alone.
- The table skeleton draws the destination table's real column count via visibleCols(db) — the schema is already client-side, so the real shape is free.
- Statics carry Last-Modified and answer If-Modified-Since with 304: a workspace switch revalidates ~1.1MB of vendor JS/CSS instead of re-downloading it (Cache-Control stays no-cache).
- Branded 404 page (public/404.html, standalone, both themes): unknown page paths and unknown workspaces get it on GET; API callers keep the JSON error.

Verified live on :4400: hash navs never show the rope (MutationObserver count 0 across table switches), skeleton head draws 9 lines for a 9-column table, /no/such/page renders the 404 page in both themes, app.js answers 304.

Tests: test/nav-speed.test.mjs (5 cases) + reworked page-loader contracts incl. a new Function parse gate. Full suite green: 1162 pass.

Follow-up (Kyle, 2026-08-28, change 116): the rope covers ANY load expected to exceed 500ms — every route goes back through withPageLoader with LOADER_SHOW_AFTER_MS raised 200 -> 500. Routine navs still finish on the skeleton; a genuinely slow route or boot weaves the rope. Verified live: fast nav rope-free, a fetch delayed to 900ms shows the rope.

features.name: Table view config as fields: Filter and Sort on the Tables row
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-28
Option F: a table's view configuration is field values on its Workspace/Tables registry row, extending the Field Order / Hidden Fields precedent (2026-08-24).

- `updateTable {filters}` — `{ workflowFieldName: [stateNames] }`, validated (field must exist and be workflow, states must exist); empty clears. Replaces the per-browser localStorage filters from Feature #38: filters are table truth now, shared across browsers.
- `updateTable {sort}` — `[{ field, dir: asc|desc }]`, validated; empty clears. Replaces the ephemeral client sort that was lost on every navigation.
- The Tables row mirrors both as text — `Filter: State: Open, Doing` / `Sort: Due desc, Name asc` — and editing the row text writes back through the same verb with the same validation (#interceptUpdate → updateTable).
- describeSchema emits `filters`/`sort`; applySchema applies them (update + create paths).
- Client: filter chips and the ⋮ sort menu PATCH the table; the grid initialises sort from the schema.
- No new field types: validated text on the registry row is the established pattern. `ponytail:` a spec-valued `query` field type is the upgrade path when filters outgrow workflow states.
- Density stays per-person by design (a way of reading, not schema).

Tests: test/table-config-fields.test.mjs (6). Suite green 1168/1168.

features.name: Target-set (polymorphic) relations: one field, several legal target tables
features.description:
## What shipped

A relation field may now carry a **target set** — `targetDbs`, a list of member tables — instead of the single `targetDb`. Values may point at rows of any member. The registry's `Workspace/Spaces` and `Workspace/Tables` are legal members, so a row can point at a **space** or a **table** as easily as at another row.

## Design rulings (2026-08-28 design review)

- **One-way by design.** No inverse field is minted for a multi-target field — the alternative sprays a field across every member table. The reverse direction is a read.
- **Singleton sets collapse to the classic paired relation, bit-for-bit.** Existing fields and data are untouched; rollback is a plain revert.
- **Lookups and rollups keep the single-target contract** and refuse a target set — no one far table exists to read a field from.
- **Query traversal resolves each hop per-row** (`t.dbId`), so `Scope.Name` matches whichever member table the target lives in.
- **Chips carry their home table**; the picker searches every member; the relation map draws one edge per member.
- **Deleting a member table prunes it from every target set**; an emptied set takes its field with it.

## Evidence

- Suite: `test/polymorphic-relation.test.mjs` — 15 tests. Full run 1183/1183 green.
- Commit `c2b25b3` (v0.4.3), Gerrit change 121 (Verified +1).
- Live smoke on this server: one `Scope` field held a Note row, the `Smoke` space row, and the `Note` table row in a single value.
- Rollback: `git revert c2b25b3`; delete any multi-target fields first (or restore the pre-deploy db backup `backups/weave-pre-polymorphic-20260828-080733.db`) so old code never reads a `targetDbs` config it does not know.

See the Wiki article "Target-set relations: pointing at structure" for the full use-case walkthrough.

features.name: Editor toolbar + click-to-open outline panel
features.description:
Kyle (2026-08-29): "weave md editor needs some improvement, add tool bar and update the left side outline to only show on click not hover and float in at the midpoint fo the viewport"

**Toolbar.** The embedded editor's toolbar was deliberately empty (`toolbar: []`, the slash menu was the only chrome). Reversed: a compact strip — headings, bold, italic, strike, inline code, link · bullet/numbered/task lists · quote, code block, table, divider · undo, redo — styled as a quiet border-bottom strip on the page ground (`.doc-editor .vditor-toolbar`), `toolbarConfig: {hide:false, pin:true}`. The slash menu keeps the full catalogue (references, mermaid, raw HTML, math). Gotcha: the toolbar's headings dropdown reuses Vditor's `vditor-hint` class, so every slash-menu test selector is now scoped `.vditor-hint:not(.vditor-panel--arrow)`.

**Outline rail.** Hover-reveal removed. The resting rail stays a minimap; the first click anywhere on it (capture phase, so a closed-rail dash click opens rather than jumping blind) adds `.open`: the track goes `position:fixed; top:50%; translateY(-50%)` — vertically centred on the viewport — with its x pinned to the rail's own left, re-measured on every refresh and on window resize (a click can beat layout). A heading click jumps and closes; Escape or a click away closes.

Shipped in commit 74c9769 (1188 tests green). Suites updated: Embedded editor (renamed toolbar case), Phase 4 editor browser (16→17, click/midpoint/Escape coverage), new suite Outline dash rail (test/doc-rail.test.mjs, 15 cases). Handbook: Document formatting grew "The toolbar"; "The dash rail" rewritten for click-to-open. Verified live in both themes on :4400.

features.name: Development sync: every build ships and applies its issue list
features.description: **What ships.** Every build carries `docs/development.json` — the canonical Development space (Issues + Features, with status, severity/milestone, symptom, and description) exported at release time by `scripts/export-development.mjs`. On `weave serve` boot, `syncDevelopment()` (src/weaver-seed.js) applies the manifest to the local weave docs workspace: rows matched by name take the shipped status, unmatched manifest rows are created, and locally filed rows are never touched. A stamp on workspace meta makes the pass one write per build. Gate: test/development-sync.test.mjs pins the manifest to the package version, so a release without a fresh export fails the suite.

features.name: Icon picker is a category grid, not a list of names
features.description:
## Pain Point

The icon picker was a list: every icon on its own line with its name beside it, numbered ⌥1–9. At 119 icons that is a very long column to read down when the thing you are choosing is a shape.

## Problem Statement

A name beside every icon is a column you read instead of a set you scan, and it costs a line each. The name still has work to do — it is what a search matches — but it does not need to be on screen to do it.

## Solution Shape

A grid per category. Icons rest in the chrome's grey and come up to full ink under the cursor; nothing is labelled; the name is the tooltip and the search key. `ICON_CATEGORIES` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` sorts the drawn marks and the vendored names into eleven groups — there is no marks-versus-flat-set split, because that was never a distinction a person picking an icon cares about. The category rides on each choice as `hint`, which pickerCore already ranks against, so 'money' finds the whole group without a second search path and the grid groups on the same field. `No icon` is the first cell, wearing the ghost ring the unset button already wears.

Both gates open it: the space and table icon button, and the option and state icon in the field dialog.

Guarded by four browser cases in `test/icon-vocabulary-browser.test.mjs` and four pure cases in `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`.

_Shipped 2026-08-31 — 82f8e10, 83cf448._

features.name: Selection-bubble toolbar with the full control set
features.description:
Kyle picked this configuration in the Toolbar Lab artifact (2026-08-30 session): bar style = bubble, full item set, dividers on, icons legible, labels on hover — with the instruction "ensure that every toolbar feature is thoroughly tested including dropdowns for headings, file upload for all supported file types. For this icon size numbered list and checkbox are hard to see. Text labels on icons should show on hover."

**What shipped (commit ec2b11a, supersedes the fixed strip half of Feature #151):**

- **Selection bubble.** The Vditor toolbar leaves the flow: `.doc-editor .vditor-toolbar` is absolute + hidden, and `placeToolbarBubble` (app.js) floats it over the selection on `selectionchange` (microtask, not rAF — throttled pages). Above the selection, below when the selection touches the host top; clamped to the host; stays while the pointer/focus is inside the bar so the headings dropdown and link input survive their own clicks.
- **Full item set.** headings · bold · italic · strike · inline-code · link | list · ordered-list · check · outdent · indent | quote · code · table · line | undo · redo · upload. `toolbarConfig {hide:false, pin:false}` — visibility belongs to the bubble layer.
- **Uploads for every file type.** Custom `upload.handler` → base64 → `POST /api/entities/:id/files` (any mime), link inserted into the doc — images embed (`![]()`), everything else links. `mountDocEditor` now takes `entityId`.
- **Legibility.** All toolbar icons draw at 16px minimum (the ordered-list and check glyphs were the complaint).
- **Hover labels.** Vditor's aria-label tooltips (name + shortcut) ride every button; z-index cleared above the bubble border.

**Tests:** new suite test/toolbar-browser.test.mjs (16 cases — geometry, every control, headings dropdown, png/pdf/txt uploads verified end-to-end incl. served mime + entity.files), updated Embedded editor + Phase 4 static/browser contracts. Full suite 1244/1244 green. Two Vditor quirks documented in-test: toolbar-applied formats never arm the undo stack, and background-tab timer throttling starves its 800ms undo debounce.

Handbook: Document formatting › "The toolbar" rewritten for the bubble.

features.name: Structure trash: table and space delete is recoverable
features.description: Deleting a table or a space tombstones it (deletedAt) instead of purging, matching the entity soft-delete contract: rows stay where they are, hidden by the parent; restoreTable/restoreSpace bring the subtree back with relations intact; hard remains the explicit cascading purge. Registry rows mirror the trash both ways, a trashed name is held until restore or purge, and a table cannot be restored into a trashed space. Surfaced on REST (DELETE ?hard=1 + /restore), MCP (weave_restore_space, weave_restore_table, hard flags) and CLI (space/table restore, --hard). Re-rules the old meta-model ruling that a registry-row delete is always final. Tests: test/structure-trash.test.mjs (10). Gerrit change 129.

features.name: Workspace trash: delete and restore a workspace
features.description: DELETE /api/workspaces/<name> writes a deletedAt tombstone into the workspace's own meta - it drops out of the hub list and switcher, survives restarts and rescans, and its URL keeps answering. ?deleted=1 lists the trash; POST /api/workspaces/<name>/restore brings it back. The default workspace refuses deletion, a trashed name cannot be re-created, and there is deliberately no hard delete: removing a .db file is a human filesystem act. Tests: test/workspace-trash.test.mjs (5). Gerrit change 130.

features.name: Lifecycle regression gate: 12-op pack, auto-verify, breadcrumb rejects, service promote
features.description: test/regression/lifecycle.test.mjs runs workspace/space/table/entity x create/delete/restore as 12 named tests (+1 persistence check). weave-review.sh runs the pack FIRST and on red votes Verified -1 with a breadcrumb naming the exact failed lifecycle tests, persisting the full log to ~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/<change>-<ps>.log before voting; the full suite gates after. weave-review-poll.mjs (launchd ai.grunion.weave-review, 120s) auto-verifies every unjudged patchset, so builds that break the lifecycle are rejected automatically. `weave service promote` fetches gerrit/main into a clean serve checkout (~/.weave-serve), reruns the pack, kickstarts the service and probes /api/health for the promoted version, rolling back to the previous SHA on any red - production is a SHA that passed the pack twice. Proven live: probe change 133 was auto-rejected with named breadcrumbs and abandoned. Gerrit changes 132 + 134.

features.name: Document fields are first-class columns with declared-kind viewers
features.description:
One document field holds one document of a declared kind, rendered natively (Kyle, 2026-08-31).

## What changes

**Grid**: the shared `Docs (n)` cell is retired. Every document field is a column of its own — it hides behind the eye, reorders and resizes like any field. The description keeps its first-lines preview; every other document cell is the named chip with its kind badge (Kyle chose the chip over a preview, 2026-08-31).

**Entity page**: the field's declared `kind` (markdown / html / code) rules the viewer — an html field runs in its frame with the `</>` source toggle, a code field edits directly in the monospace code box, markdown mounts the rendering editor. Content sniffing survives only as the fallback for fields that declare nothing. Declared kind rules rendering; it never rejects content (no migration).

## Where

- `public/editor-lib.js`: `docViewMode(declared, text)`, `docChipKind(declared, text)`
- `public/app.js`: visibleCols admits documents; `docChipCell`; docSection routes on docViewMode; eye popover lists documents; Docs th/td + `docChips` + `chipDocumentFields` removed
- `src/vocabulary.js` + `src/handbook.js`: renders text updated
- Gates: `test/doc-columns.test.mjs`; doc-chips + ui-contract updated

## Shipped 2026-08-31 (commit fd44648)

Grid verified live: Script and Diagram are columns on Workspace/Workflows; Showcase Brief renders named empty chips; no Docs (n) header anywhere. Entity page verified on a probe entity: kind=code mounted the monospace code box directly (SQL content, no frame, no toggle), kind=html framed markdown content with the </> toggle (declared kind outvoted the sniff), an undeclared Description mounted Vditor. Suite 1243/1244 (the one red is the toolbar-bubble WIP's browser test, pre-existing). Quality: Suite "Doc columns" (test/doc-columns.test.mjs, 10 cases) added.

features.name: Lifecycle pack ring 2: edge cases and real-sqlite grain
features.description:
The 12-op lifecycle pack (test/regression/lifecycle.test.mjs) covers the happy path, mostly in-memory. Ring 2 adds the corners where restore actually fails in practice:

- The same 12 ops run through a real .db save/close/reopen cycle (today only entity soft-delete has that; table/space/workspace trash have never been tested across a sqlite reopen).
- Purge from the trash at every level (soft delete then hard).
- Restore-vs-name-conflict: restore a trashed table/space/workspace whose name a live one has since taken.
- Undo interacting with structure trash (undo stack must stay clean of structural ops).
- FTS delisting for live rows whose CONTAINER is trashed (search index vs engine-state filter).
- Concurrent CLI + server writes around delete/restore (maybeRefresh path).

Gate wiring: the ring-2 file joins the pack stage in weave-review.sh so its names enter the breadcrumb vocabulary. Context: gap 4 of the 2026-09-01 gate-gaps report; the risk is the gate saying "restore works" while restore fails on a real .db after a restart.

features.name: Trash and restore in the app UI (tables, spaces, workspaces)
features.description:
Restore now exists on REST, MCP and CLI, but the app itself has delete controls and no way back: no trash view and no restore button for tables, spaces or workspaces. Hold-to-delete in the UI is soft (recoverable by design) yet unrecoverable in practice without a terminal.

Scope:
- Trash section reachable from the sidebar and from table/space menus, listing trashed structures with deletion time (data already flows: registry trash + /api/workspaces?deleted=1).
- One-click Restore per row; hold-to-confirm Purge (hard) mirroring the existing entity-trash pattern.
- Workspace switcher gains a trashed-workspaces affordance (restore via POST /api/workspaces/<name>/restore).
- Browser tests pin the contract (ui-contract style + a browser test per surface), so the UI joins the lifecycle regression gate.

Context: gap 5 of the 2026-09-01 gate-gaps report. Both themes must be checked (data-bs-theme).

features.name: Inline file viewers: centered, medium, resizable, demotable to links
features.description:
Kyle (2026-08-31): "add test cases for upload image and pdf with viewer inside .md, same with html. add resize anchors and default size to scale to medium. on hover above files show a toolbar that allows show the file as a link. Defaults all files to centered inline formatting" + "confirm files survive .md export — and html and pdf".

**Shipped (commit 4a22aa5):**
- Uploaded **images** embed as markdown images; **PDF and HTML** files embed as `<iframe class="wv-file">` raw-HTML blocks — the IR editor previews them live (`.vditor-ir__preview`) and every export passes them through.
- **Defaults:** centered block, medium width (max 60% of the column), `resize: both` native grip, PDFs/HTML at 4:3. Same styling in the editor (style.css) and the rendered `.html` export (src/markdown.js page CSS).
- **Hover toolbar** (`attachFileTools`, app.js): hovering any viewer floats a one-action toolbar — **Show as link** rewrites the markdown (`![name](url)` / iframe block → `[name](url)`), so the demotion persists. `ponytail:` the reverse action and persisting a resized width into the markdown are deliberate omissions until asked for.
- **Exports:** `.md` keeps the markup verbatim; `.html` renders viewers with the centered-medium CSS; `.pdf` still builds (viewers degrade — pdf.js strips inline HTML).

**Tests:** four new cases in Toolbar bubble (browser) — viewer defaults (display/resize/centered/medium), live iframe previews for uploaded pdf+html, hover demotion for both viewer kinds, and the three-export survival check. Full suite 1269/1269. Handbook Document formatting updated.

features.name: Gate hardening: merge gate, main watcher, promote rehearsal on real data
features.description: Three gate gaps closed (2026-09-01 gate-gaps report, items 1-3). MERGE GATE: weave-review.sh merges every patchset with the freshest gerrit/main inside the throwaway worktree before testing; a conflict is itself Verified -1 with breadcrumb, so a change is verified as it will land, not as it was written. MAIN WATCHER: weave-review-poll.mjs watches gerrit/main and origin/main; every advance (Gerrit submit or direct GitHub push) gets the lifecycle pack run on the new tip, and a red files a High-severity Issue naming the failed tests - the ungated GitHub door now trips an alarm. PROMOTE REHEARSAL: service promote copies ~/.weave/weave.db (the built-in weave workspace, the most data anywhere), runs the named mutation battery (src/rehearse.js) against the copy AND against a fresh workspace built from nothing, and rejects before restart on any red; `weave rehearse --data <copy>` runs it by hand and refuses without an explicit target. The rehearsal found a real bug on its first run (orphaned inverse-field registry row - see the linked Issue). Gerrit change 135; harness commit 6980e8d.

features.name: Reference index + collapsible preview chips: a chip is a reference, not a relation
features.description:
A chip in a document is tracked as a reference, never a stored relation: nothing is configured, nothing is unlinked; the reference exists exactly as long as the text does.

**Reference index.** `referencesTo(entityRef)` scans every live document on demand for all accepted spellings: `[[Table#pid]]` (qualified or not, with |label), `[[uuid]]`, and permalink links ending in `/e/<uuid>`. Returns entity summaries sorted by table then public id. Served at `GET /api/entities/:ref/references`. The entity page grows a **References · N** card of linked chips, fetched on its own and absent when nothing points here.

**Collapsible preview chips.** `previewFields(entityRef)` picks the workflow state first, then non-empty simple values in schema order, three at most. Zero configuration by design (Kyle, 2026-09-01): arranging the table field order IS the curation. Mentions resolved with fields render collapsed to the name with a caret; the caret opens the field segments; the whole chip stays a link to the entity. Doc pages carry the toggle script; chips without fields render exactly as before.

Shipped in e30a65d (2026-09-02). Tests: test/backlinks.test.mjs, 7 cases (preview order/cap/skip-empties, all four spellings match, deleted referrers drop out, self-reference excluded, REST route, chip HTML collapsed and capped, no-fields regression). Full suite 1280 tests green apart from the known flaky slash-commands case, which passes in isolation. Deployed to the :4400 server from ~/.weave-serve; /references verified live (200).

features.name: References go both ways: outbound doc-chip mirror (referencesFrom)
features.description:
A document's chips ARE its outbound references — computed from the text on read, never stored, so the list is 1:1 with what the documents say (the 2026-09-01 references-are-not-relations ruling, other direction).

- Engine `referencesFrom(ref)`: shares `referencesTo` spellings — `[[Table#pid]]` (qualified or not, with |label), `[[uuid]]`, and URL spellings, which now widen for BOTH directions: a markdown permalink, an HTML chip's `href`, and a mermaid `click` target all reduce to `/e/<uuid>`.
- Dead pids stay text; self-mentions and deleted targets never count; deduped; sorted db then publicId.
- `GET /api/entities/:ref/references-from` serves it.
- Entity page: **References** card (outbound) beside **Referenced by** (inbound, renamed from References).
- Tests: 5 new cases in test/backlinks.test.mjs; full suite green.

Gerrit change 146, Verified +1, awaiting +2.


**2026-09-02 follow-up (Gerrit 150, Verified +1):** both reference cards are now native `<details>`, closed by default; chips are the shared `k k-rel` relation chips with `k-home` table badges (no × — nothing to unlink). Source-gated in test/backlinks.test.mjs.

features.name: Date grain & costume: partial dates (year·month, day-of-month, month·day, time-only), nine styles, 12h/24h clock, floating/fixed/instant zones, elapsed ranges; number compact + accounting
features.description:
# Grain and costume for date fields

**Shipped 2026-09-02** — Gerrit changes 144 and 145, commits `427b317` and `46a3f46` on `main`.

A date field now declares two things separately:

- **grain** — which parts it CAPTURES and stores: any contiguous run of year · month · day, plus a time of day. A card expires in a month, never on a day; rent falls on the 15th of no particular month. Storing the missing part would store a lie, so the grain leaves it out.
- **costume** — how the stored parts PRINT: a style (`iso us eu long short month quarter ordinal relative`), a clock (`24h` | `12h`), what a clock time means (`floating` | `fixed` zone | `instant`), zero-padding (`pad`). A range adds `elapsed`.

The rule between them: **a costume that needs a part the grain never stored is refused at definition time** — `month`/`quarter` need a month, `ordinal` a day, `relative` a year — with the missing part named. The tray offers only the styles the grain can wear.

## Storage
ISO 8601 truncated forms (XSD gYear / gYearMonth / gMonthDay / gDay), which sort as text within a grain:

| Grain | Stores | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| year · month · day | `2026-08-15`, `2026-08-15T09:15` | a due date, a meeting |
| year · month | `2026-08` | card expiry, a monthly target |
| year | `2026` | a fiscal year |
| month · day | `--08-15` | a birthday |
| month | `--08` | a seasonal window |
| day | `---15` | rent day |
| none + time | `09:15` | an opening time |

A fuller value is cut to the grain; a thinner one is refused. Every existing date field is the full grain with a floating clock — exactly what its values already are — so nothing migrates.

## Zones
`floating` is what weave always did, now named. `fixed` carries an IANA `zoneName` on the field. `instant` stores UTC (`2026-08-15T16:15Z`) and renders in the reader's zone: the browser sends `X-Weave-Zone` on every request; the engine renders reads and queries inside it; the CLI and MCP read in UTC.

## Numbers
`format: compact` (1.2M, $1.2M) and `accounting: true` (parenthesised negatives, needs currency).

## One rule, one file
`public/date-grain.js` is imported by the engine and read by the browser, so the server and the cell cannot disagree. `public/date-core.js` delegates to it.

## Surfaces
Engine normaliser + validation + defaults, `describeSchema`/`applySchema` round trip, vocabulary (`dateGrains`, `dateStyleNeeds`, `clocks`, `zones`), Handbook pages for `date`, `daterange`, `number` (the eu/long examples were wrong and are fixed), the field tray (Stores → Format → Clock → Zone → Elapsed), the cell control and popover (calendar / month grid / year grid / 1–31 grid / clock), typed input (`the 3rd`, `08/2026`, `2026`, `dec 25`, `5:40 pm`).

## Tests
`test/date-grain.test.mjs` (13 cases: grain normalisation, truncation and refusal per grain, defaults per grain, formulas on partial values, legality, all nine styles on every grain, clocks, zones incl. DST, ranges + elapsed, schema round trip); `number-format` +2 (compact, accounting); `field-dialog-core` +5; ui-contract updated. Full suite: 1306 pass. Browser-verified on a scratch workspace in both themes.

## Origin
Kyle's ruling over the Field Costumes explorer (2026-08-26 → 09-02): formatting is a field property, never a user setting; the parts a field stores are a decision separate from how they print.

features.name: Regression coverage v2: every user action, gated merge/promote, live retest with autorollback
features.description:
One plan to finish what the lifecycle gate started: regression coverage for EVERY user action, gates on merge and promote, and a live retest with automatic rollback after each landing. Ordered phases, each independently shippable.

## Where the pipeline stands (2026-09-02)

Working today: per-patchset gate (lifecycle pack first, full suite after, named breadcrumbs, persisted logs) - merge gate (change tested merged with live main; conflict = Verified -1) - auto-verify poller every 120s - main watcher (pack on every gerrit/origin main advance; red files a High Issue) - service promote (pack + rehearsal on a copy of weave.db + a fresh workspace, health/version probe, rollback to previous SHA) - generated Quality mirror (src/quality-mirror.js, re-synced on every landing).

## Phase 1 - The full user-action pack (grows the 12-op pack to every capability)

The canonical list of user actions already exists: the SURFACE table in test/agent-surface.test.mjs (~50 capabilities, each mapped to engine methods, an MCP tool and a CLI command). The regression pack extends to one named op per capability: fields (add/update/delete/retype), relations incl. polymorphic target sets, links/unlinks, workflow state moves, documents (get/set/append/export), comments, files (attach/read/delete), views + share tokens, automations (create/fire/update/delete), undo, search + universal search, CSV import/export, JSON import/export, schema apply, accounts, keys, registry rebuild, workspace record + logo.

Anti-drift, same discipline as the Quality mirror: a gate test derives the required op list FROM the SURFACE table, so adding a capability without a regression op fails the suite. Target: pack stays under ~10s (it runs first on every patchset).

## Phase 2 - Gate the gates

The pipeline itself gets a test suite (the false-rejection on a missing PATH and the check-mode mutation bug both shipped untested):
- Unit: parseTap/promoteVerdict (done), plus merge-gate decision logic and the watcher's advance/record state machine extracted into testable functions.
- Script-level: run weave-review.sh against a throwaway Gerrit change fixture in CI-less mode (dry flag) asserting: conflict -> merge-gate breadcrumb; pack red -> named lifecycle breadcrumb, suite skipped; pack green + suite red -> full-suite breadcrumb; log persisted before vote.
- A scheduled live drill (monthly): push a seeded-bug probe change (the 133 pattern), assert auto-rejection with named breadcrumb, abandon. The drill IS the test that the gate still fires.

## Phase 3 - Live retest + autorollback after every landing

Today the watcher tests the SOURCE of the new tip; nothing retests the RUNNING server after promote. Add:
- Post-promote live probe: after kickstart, run the pack's HTTP-level ops against the live server in a scratch workspace (create/delete/restore via REST on :4400, then purge). Red -> automatic rollback to the previous SHA (mechanism exists in promote) + High Issue.
- Post-merge auto-promote (opt-in flag on the poller): a green watcher run on gerrit/main triggers service promote, making landing -> live retest -> rollback one automatic chain. Until enabled, promote stays manual but the live probe still runs on whatever is serving.
- Stale-production alarm: buildStatus already detects the served version lagging main; the watcher surfaces it (Issue after N cycles stale) instead of nobody acting on it.

## Phase 4 - Pack ring 2: edges and real-sqlite grain (= Feature #159)

The 12 ops through a real .db save/close/reopen at every level; purge-from-trash; restore-vs-name-conflict; undo x structure trash; FTS delisting for rows whose container is trashed; concurrent CLI + server writes (maybeRefresh). Ring-2 names join the breadcrumb vocabulary.

## Phase 5 - Trash/restore in the app UI, browser-tested (= Feature #160)

Trash views + one-click restore + hold-to-confirm purge for tables, spaces and workspaces; browser tests pin the contract so the UI joins the gate. Both themes.

## Order and effort

1 then 3 give the most protection per hour (full action surface, then live retest closes the loop Kyle named: "once merged the live version should be tested again with autorollback"). 2 hardens trust in the machinery, 4-5 deepen and surface it. Effort: P1 large (a day+), P2 medium, P3 medium, P4 medium, P5 medium-large.

## Acceptance

- Every SURFACE capability has a named regression op, enforced by a derivation gate.
- A seeded bug in any user action is auto-rejected pre-merge with a breadcrumb naming the op.
- A landing that breaks the live server is rolled back automatically within one poll cycle, with an Issue naming what failed.
- Features #159 and #160 close and fold their tests into the pack.

features.name: Lucide icons with movingicons.dev motion replace Iconly flat
features.description:
## Pain Point

The icon set was Iconly free: 101 flat glyphs drawn to uneven boxes, so weave carried a per-icon scale table (bug ×1.42, the `-2` arrows ×1.5), a hidden-name list and eight money glyphs of its own to fill the gaps. The set was closed, filled, and still.

## Problem Statement

One vocabulary needs one grid and one weight, and it should grow without hand-drawing. Motion, where it exists, has to fire once and rest — never loop (Kyle, 2026-09-02).

## Solution Shape

Lucide shapes (ISC) carrying the motion movingicons.dev adds (MIT, github.com/jis3r/icons): 595 names, 537 moving, generated by `scripts/build-lucide-moving.mjs` into `public/vendor/lucide-moving.{js,css}` and `public/icon-registry.js`.

- Value form `lucide:<name>`. Every `iconly:<name>` stored before resolves through the registry's aliases to its Lucide twin — nothing migrates, a legacy value rings the cell its twin sits in.
- Fourteen state marks draw as Lucide twins; the six progress rings stay hand-drawn, re-inked to 2.0.
- Motion: once per hover and once per press on the icon itself — nothing on load or as a picker opens (the load wave shipped 2026-09-02 and was ruled out 2026-09-05, Issue #192, Gerrit 213); `infinite` becomes a single run at build time; reduced-motion switches it off.
- The picker keeps the eleven curated groups in Lucide names plus the recommended additions, then Lucide's own categories.
- Vocabulary, MCP and CLI descriptions, the Handbook guide, AGENTS.md and the bug reporter speak the new form.

Landed as Gerrit 153/154 (f688ca4). Gate: `test/icon-registry.test.mjs`; full suite 1312/1312. Canonical description: the Showcase entity **Icon library**.

features.name: Configurable Name field: rename it, make it a formula, never delete it
features.description:
## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-02)

> "name can also be a formula" · "why can't the name field be renamed or retyped? doesn't make sense"

Make the Name field configurable: **renameable** (Title, Subject, Invoice #…), **retypeable between text and formula** (a computed name, Fibery-style — `Company + " · " + Stage`), and still **undeletable** (a row needs an identity). Follows Feature #40's re-home (Gerrit 155): the row term already lives on the Name field's config, so the Name field is the one place a table says what a row is and how it is named.

## Why the guards exist today

Three engine guards in `updateField` / `#migrateFieldType` / `deleteField` refuse rename, retype and delete of `db.nameFieldId`:

```js
if (field.id === db.nameFieldId) throw new WeaveError('Cannot rename the Name field', 'invalid');
if (field.id === db.nameFieldId) throw new WeaveError('Cannot change the type of the Name field', 'invalid');
if (field.id === db.nameFieldId) throw new WeaveError('Cannot delete the Name field', 'invalid');
```

The reason is coupling, not principle. The role already exists (`db.nameFieldId`, the same pattern `descriptionFieldId` uses), but consumers key on the literal `'Name'` and on the value being a stored string:

| Where | Count | What keys on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public/app.js` | 17 | `f.name === 'Name'` (dialog disable, term section, field-menu delete guard, ⋮ shortcut, grid column filter, fields-table delete), `values: { Name }` on the entity page rename and the related-rows add button, `select: ['Name']` on relation pickers, two cross-table headers |
| `src/engine.js` | 6 | `createEntity` maps `input.name` → `values.Name`; `applySchema`'s create branch skips the field literally named `Name`; the registry Fields table routes a `Name` patch to `updateField` |
| `src/store.js` | 1 | `#ftsText` indexes `String(e.values[nameFieldId])` — a stored string, never a computed one |
| `entityName()` + `listEntities` summary | 2 | `String(e.values[db.nameFieldId] ?? '')` |
| `TYPE_MIGRATIONS` | — | no field can become a formula after creation; the dialog's ƒ toggle is `disabled` on edit |

## Design

**1. Rename** — lift the guard. `describeSchema` marks the field `role: 'name'` (as it marks `role: 'description'`); every app.js check switches from the literal to the role. `findField(db, 'Name')` falls back to the name-role field when no field is literally called Name, so `values: { Name }`, `select: ['Name']`, CSV import and every MCP/CLI caller (`weave_create_entity {name}`, `--name`) keep working unchanged — agents never break. `applySchema` renames the minted Name field to the descriptor that claims the role, exactly as it does for the description.

**2. Retype text ⇄ formula** — `TYPE_MIGRATIONS.text` gains `formula`, `formula` gains `text`; the migration keeps `config.term` (today `#migrateFieldType` replaces config wholesale and would drop the row term). text → formula requires an expression and clears stored values; formula → text **freezes** the computed value into each row (the natural "stop computing" gesture). `entityName()` evaluates the formula live; the entity's own writes materialise the computed name into `values[nameFieldId]` so FTS search, sort and the store see a string (cross-row dependencies re-materialise on that row's next write — a known, documented staleness for search only). `createEntity` ignores `name` when the name field is computed instead of throwing. Other types (number, date, select) as a name stay blocked — they read as identifiers, not names.

**3. Delete stays blocked.**

**UI** — the Name field's dialog enables the name input and the ƒ toggle (text ⇄ formula only); the entity page title and the grid's identity column render read-only when the name is computed; quick-create ("+ New deal") skips the name prompt for a computed name and just creates the row.

**Docs** — Handbook "Data model" / Fields guide: the Name field can be renamed and can be a formula; it cannot be deleted.

## Verification

| Gate | Method |
| --- | --- |
| Rename | engine test: rename → `entityName`, `values: { Name }` alias, `select: ['Name']`, `describeSchema role: 'name'`, applySchema round-trip to a fresh workspace with the renamed field |
| Formula name | engine test: text → formula computes, term survives, `createEntity({name})` tolerated, FTS finds the computed name after the row's write, formula → text freezes |
| UI contract | `ui-contract`: no `=== 'Name'` literals left in app.js (role-keyed), read-only title when computed, ƒ toggle enabled on edit for text/formula |
| Suite | full `node --test` green + lifecycle pack + Gerrit merge gate; promote to :4400 and verify a renamed + computed Name live |

## Provenance

Row term (Feature #40, re-homed Gerrit 155 / a58fb13) established the Name field as the home of "what a row is". This feature makes the field itself configurable. Built in the isolated worktree `.wt/name-field` off `30a7ba5`.

## Shipped 2026-09-02 (Gerrit 166, commit 84f10ba, v0.5)

Built in the isolated worktree `.wt/name-field` off `30a7ba5`; landed through the Gerrit gate (pack + merge gate + full suite green, 1439/1439); the main watcher mirrors to GitHub and deploys `:4400`.

**What landed**
- Rename: guard lifted; `describeSchema` marks `role: 'name'`; every app.js read is role-keyed (`nameFieldOf(db)`); `findField(db, 'Name')` falls back to the name-role field so `values: { Name }`, `select: ['Name']`, CSV import, `weave_create_entity {name}` and the CLI keep working after a rename. `applySchema` renames the minted Name field to the descriptor that claims the role (create and update paths).
- Text ⇄ formula: `TYPE_MIGRATIONS.text` gains `formula`, `formula` gains `text` (client mirror too; formula stays the ƒ toggle, never a grid tile). text → formula requires an expression and clears stored values; formula → text freezes each row's computed value. The Name field may only be text or a formula. `config.term` survives the migration. `entityName()` evaluates live; `#mark` materialises the computed name into `values[nameFieldId]` on the row's own writes so FTS search indexes a string (cross-row inputs refresh on that row's next write — search may lag, the displayed name never does). `createEntity` tolerates `name` when the name is computed; a direct write is still refused.
- Delete stays blocked.
- UI: the Name field's dialog enables the name input, draws ƒ on edit for text/formula fields, offers text as the only tile ("a name is text, or a formula (ƒ below)"); the entity page title is read-only and italic when computed (tooltip shows the expression) and patches by the field's label when not; quick-create skips the name prompt for a computed name.
- Handbook Fields page: the Name field can be renamed and can become a formula; it cannot be deleted.

**Tests** `test/name-field.test.mjs` (5), `ui-contract` (+1 gate: one literal `'Name'` read allowed, the pre-role fallback inside `nameFieldOf`), `field-dialog-core` mirror pinned.

**Verified in the browser** (`:4492`, worktree code): Name → Title renamed the column; ƒ with `concat(Company, " · ", Amount)` computed "Acme · 1200" in the grid (ƒ glyph on the header) and as the read-only italic title on the entity page; relation map still counts "3 deals".

features.name: Inline icons: `:name:` draws an icon inside a document
features.description:
## Pain Point

A document could name an icon but never show one: the icon library page listed `lucide:check` beside a font-sized `✓`, tables of icons were tables of names, and the only inline pictures a writer had were emoji.

## Problem Statement

Kyle, 2026-09-02: "show fully formatted real icons in the .md — these can replace emojis." Then, of the first attempt (an overlay painted over the literal): "these are still broken, like they are sitting on top of other icons — rebuild from scratch."

## Solution Shape

`:bell:` is Lute's own shortcode node. The inventory REPLACES the GitHub emoji table on every editor (Vditor only merges its hint map into it), each name pointing at a static svg under `public/vendor/icons`, so the token draws inline as a node of the surface — in a table cell as much as in prose — serialises back to `:bell:`, and `:smile:` stays text. The `:` completion popup is therefore the inventory, every entry drawn. A progress ring goes by an ascii alias (`:ring-quarter:`), a state mark by its Lucide twin (`:check:`). The server renderer (exports) and the dressed text cells speak the same grammar; the dark theme recolours the images with a filter.

Landed as Gerrit 160 (the first form) and 181 (the rebuild, 84f3e62). Tests: `test/inline-icons.test.mjs`, `test/inline-icons-browser.test.mjs` (drawn in prose and cells, no emoji, round-trips to the token).

features.name: One entity surface: split dock unifies peek + entity page
features.description:
One entity surface: the split dock replaces the side peek and unifies with the entity page.

**Shipped in four Gerrit changes (2026-09-02):**
- **138** — `public/entity-surface-core.js`: pure pane state machine (poses closed/split/expanded, drill chain, crumb model with home tags, wrap-around selection rule, re-anchor + view-as-table transitions, Esc-as-pop, linear history). DOM-free, fully unit-tested.
- **140** — the entity dock: `#dock` panel beside `#main`; the grid's #id link docks the entity (no navigation), ⌘-click opens a new browser tab, the docked row stays lit, Esc closes, route changes tear down with the peek's scoped-editor discipline.
- **161** — two poses, one renderer: expanded IS the classic entity page at `#/entity/id` (same geometry: doc rails, drag reorder, icon scale); Tabler `arrows-diagonal` on the dock expands, `arrows-diagonal-minimize-2` on the page re-docks, ✕ closes to the table, ⌘⇧E flips either way; the page crumb's table link means re-dock, not leave.
- **164** — geometry review round (Kyle): even 50/50 split of the room beside the nav by default, dock side padding matches #main's 28px, and a draggable divider on the dock's left edge (pins a per-browser width, `wv-dock-width`; double-click restores the even split; clamped so the table keeps 320px).

**Design source:** five-option exploration (tray / center modal / split dock / zoom-in-place / card stack) iterated over four artifact rounds; split dock with crumbs-only return won. Remaining design ideas not yet built: in-pane relation drilling with a crumb trail, pane history ‹ ›, home-tag re-anchor, view-as-table filtered anchor, doc full-screen as a crumb level, side-peek retirement.

**Suites:** test/entity-surface-core.test.mjs, entity-dock-browser, entity-pose-browser, entity-dock-resize-browser; ledger-grid + ui-contract gates updated to the new contract.

**Review rounds (2026-09-02, Kyle):**
- **168** — divider tooltip removed; the hover hairline is the affordance.
- **172** — pose flips replaceState instead of pushing history: Back no longer walks look-alike #/table / #/entity twins.
- **174** — one hidden set, both halves: an eye flip redraws the grid AND the docked pane, whichever side it came from.
- **176** — the eye popover rebuilds its rows in place (same node, same position, same scroll) — the close-and-reopen jump is gone.
- **179** — the side peek is fully excised: doc chips and description previews dock their entity; peekEntity + overlay + CSS deleted.

features.name: A stale instance says so: health carries the build, the UI toasts
features.description:
Kyle (2026-09-02): "my local should always be on the latest and should show a toast when it is not."

**Shipped (Gerrit change 170):** the node adapter reads its own checkout — HEAD at boot, the first remote's main lazily (never blocking a request, at most every 5 minutes, 4s timeout so an offline instance stays silent) — and `/api/health` carries `{sha, latestSha, behind}`. The health chip (bottom-right) wears the warning tint with both shas; a toast names the condition and the way out (`weave service promote`), once per load. Build info is **opt-in** (`startServer({build})`, passed by `bin/weave.js serve`): an embedded or test server must not read git or toast about a checkout it does not represent — learned the hard way when the dev checkout's genuine behind-ness toasted into the toast-stacking browser test.

Proved live on its first deploy: the serve checkout at the staleness merge reported behind:true against main's very next merge (change 169), then cleared on redeploy.

Tests: server health contract (spins its own build-carrying server), ui-contract toast/chip contract, applet host pin extended.

features.name: The chrome draws only the inventory, and an emoji is not an icon
features.description:
## Pain Point

The inventory drew the sidebar and the picker, but the chrome kept its own vocabulary: a hand-drawn nav chevron, `⋮` `×` `+` `⠿` `▾` typed into buttons, `◐ ● ○` on the theme toggle, Vditor's toolbar sprite, an Iconly `fill` rule turning stroke icons into blobs, and an emoji could still be stored as an icon.

## Problem Statement

Kyle, 2026-09-02: "confirm the new icon inventory is used and enforced across weave, including system fields and system UX like chevrons" and "I'm still finding emojis, this should not be possible."

## Solution Shape

- Every system control draws the inventory through `iconEl`: the nav chevron (`chevron()` is `lucide:chevron-right`), the row kebab, chip removes and adds, drag grips, sort marks, the term caret, the source toggle, the reference chip's caret in exports, the workspace-rail plus, the theme toggle (sun-moon / moon / sun), the field-type tiles that were symbols, the computed-field marks, the credential chip kinds, the slash menu rows, and Vditor's toolbar bubble (`WV_TB_ICONS` built from `LUCIDE_MOVING`, dense glyphs at 1.4). Letters stay letters: Aa # @ ✱ Σ ƒ and B I S ` H.
- The chrome marks ⧉ ⟳ ⛶ ↑ ↓ ‹ gain Lucide twins, so the chrome moves too.
- The engine refuses any icon value outside the inventory, a legacy alias that resolves, or a drawn mark — `Icon '🎉' is not in the inventory` — on spaces, tables, select options and workflow states; the renderer draws nothing for a bare string.
- The inventory grows by what the chrome draws: 163 curated names, 175 vendored.

Landed as Gerrit 181 (84f3e62). Tests: `test/icon-values.test.mjs`, the pinned chrome tests moved to the inventory.

features.name: Field-dialog core owns the fold-back and the patch body
features.description:
defFromFieldView and editPatchConfig were the last two pure functions of the unified field dialog still private to public/app.js, covered only by regex scans over the app source. Both moved into public/field-dialog-core.js — renamed definitionFromFieldView, and editPatchConfig now reads DEFAULTABLE directly — and gained behavior tests in test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs: the fold-back per type (including the SSN/vault credential regression: a key column must reopen as itself, never the apikey/local defaults), the PATCH body per type, and the explicit-null clears for costume keys, the default, and the row term. The old source-scan assertions in ui-contract and credential-chip now pin only the dialog delegation. No behavior change. Landed as Gerrit change 190 (6c2d837), gate 1506 pass / 0 skipped.

## Release window

Landed 2026-09-04 as Gerrit change 190 (`6c2d837`) at package version 0.4.4. Development/Release rows became mandatory later in the same window (`fa0dcf3`), so no Release row names this commit; [[Release#5]] (v0.4.5) is the first written under the "Landed as <sha>" convention.

## Deploy trail

The landing tripped two watcher Issues, both since fixed in the harness watcher rather than in weave: [[Issue#172]] (GitHub mirror 403, credential still outstanding) and [[Issue#173]] (a false "not deployed" verdict from an lsof probe that matched a client socket).

features.name: Table activity as a nav panel: recent changes in the table, toggled by its Activity system field
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04: "activity for table entity should also be a left nav panel that shows when toggled and lists changes in that table, recent in preview."

**Shape.** With `Activity` on in a table's System toggles, a panel beside the left nav lists that table's recent changes — who changed which row, what, when — newest first, a short preview per event, and a link into the full Activity table filtered to the table. Off means no panel. The toggle is the table's existing `systemFields` entry, so the grid's ⚡ column, the entity page's side column, and this panel all follow one switch.

**Open questions.** How many events the preview holds; whether the panel is pinned across navigation within the table or only on the table page.

features.name: Chip and Card: two system view fields say how every row appears elsewhere
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-04: "each weave entity needs a new field which represents its in line chip and card view. these should be new system fields hidden by default." Then: the config says what the chip and the card contain — the entity id link, the state, the name, a description preview at small/medium/large, and two or three other fields by default; it is the same for every row of the table; the entity page renders both as they will appear elsewhere; and the config editor shows the preview too.

**What shipped**

- A `view` field type, computed, in two shapes. Every table mints **Chip** and **Card** (`#ensureViewFields`, on create and on first open of a legacy workspace), `system: true`, held by role — `chipFieldId` / `cardFieldId` — so a rename costs nothing; never deletable (every row has one by existing), never retyped, never created by hand. Hidden from the grid by default through the existing `hiddenFields` list; the eye unhides them. Registry tables carry none.
- Config per table: `{ shape, link, state, description: none|small|medium|large, fields: [names] | null }`. Defaults — chip: state on, no link, no description, first two fields; card: link on, state on, small description, first three fields. `fields` is stored by id (a rename keeps the segment, a delete drops it), validated in the engine's words; documents, files, keys, definitions and the views themselves cannot ride along.
- `renderView(ref, shape, { limit, config })` is the one renderer: `{ shape, id, publicId, url, name, link, state: {name, category}, description, fields: [{label, value}] }`. The description is the plain first lines of the description document through editor-lib's `docPreview` (a page, a model or a diagram is named, never flattened). `readEntity` ships both under their field names — the one-line form in `fields`, the object in `raw`; every relation summary carries `chip`; `previewFields` (doc mentions, Feature #163) is now the chip's segments, so a doc mention follows the config.
- `GET /api/entities/:ref/view?shape=&config=` draws one row under a candidate config without saving — the dialog's live preview.
- UI (`public/view-core.js` + app.js): one `relationChipEl` for every relation cell and reference card — the far row's chip, segments behind the doc-mention caret inside the link, so the ↗ stays the last pixel; `viewCardEl` tile; an unhidden view is a read-only grid column; the entity page's **Appears as** strip shows both, hidden or not, each with a gear into the field dialog; the dialog's view pane has the link/state switches, the description size control, the field checklist (or "the first few"), and the live preview.
- Schema: `describeSchema` emits `role: chip|card` with the config by name; `applySchema` matches by role, configures the minted pair, never adds a `view`; export/import and `duplicateTable` map the ids; CSV leaves the views out; a partial `fieldOrder` may leave them out (they close the order, and a new column lands before them).
- Fixed in passing: a hidden column used to un-hide on rename (`hiddenFields` is by name).

**Tests.** `test/view-fields.test.mjs` (21: minting, legacy adoption, roles through rename/reload, guards, config validation, id storage, render chip/card, explicit fields, description sizes, readEntity shape, previewFields parity, relation summaries, export/import/clone, applySchema by role, CSV, candidate config, the route) and `test/view-fields-ui.test.mjs` (12: dialog core round trip + engine-verbatim messages, view-core segments/title/eligible, app.js and style.css source gates, parse gate). Handbook `view` page, vocabulary entry, ONTOLOGY.md, agent-surface listing. Full suite 1539/1539.

**Verified live** on a scratch server over a copy of this workspace: the entity page strip, caret open/close, the gear → dialog → save round trip on Chip (link on) and Card (state off) landing on the right field, the live preview reacting to every control, the eye unhiding Chip and Card into real grid columns, dark theme.



## Shipped 2026-09-04
Gerrit change 202, merged as 52f7dea; gate 1541/1541 (13 browser cases included). Deployed to :4400 at 21:13Z; the live weave workspace minted Chip and Card on first open (hidden). Handbook: the `view` page under Field types.

## What came next, 2026-09-07

This feature built the mechanism. Kyle's design review then settled what the two shapes look like and how they behave: [[Feature#191]] rules the Ledger chip, the Tile card and the state mark as the only state control. [[Feature#193]] adds the nine config keys those shapes need — chip placement and fold, cover framing, a second workflow field, property columns and labels.



## State as of 2026-09-07 — v0.4.8 released, main at 2a033a4

**One sentence above is now wrong.** The Appears-as strip does not show both views "hidden or not". It draws only the views the eye leaves on, and a fresh table hides both, so the strip is empty until Chip or Card is switched on there. Kyle's ruling, [[Issue#212]]: "chip and card visibility toggled off but are still showing. this should fail a test." One hidden set rules the grid, the field rows and the strip alike. Everything else in this record still holds.

### The lineage

| Record | What it did | Where it landed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[Feature#175]] | the two view fields, one `renderView`, the strip, the dialog preview | Shipped, v0.4.5 (52f7dea) |
| [[Feature#180]] | Handbook page: chip and card anatomy — every element, its hitbox, how to use it | Shipped, v0.4.6 |
| [[Feature#181]] | card-view mockups A–E: a field value inside a card is the cell's own chip | Shipped, v0.4.6 |
| [[Issue#193]] | the retract caret pointed down at nothing; open is now a half turn, facing the label | Fixed, v0.4.6 |
| [[Issue#194]] | the default chip rendered too small | Fixed, v0.4.6 |
| [[Issue#200]] | an embedded relation table drew Chip/Card as `[object Object]` and ignored the eye | Fixed, v0.4.6 |
| [[Issue#212]] | the strip ignored the eye | Fixed on main, f97f0da |
| [[Issue#208]] | Kyle's own report of the same thing, filed from uno | Fixed on main, 2a033a4 |

The last two are unreleased: the v0.4.8 row names commit 136c07c, which predates both. They join the next Release row.

### What the shipped surfaces say now

- The Handbook `view` page and the **Chip and card anatomy** page ([[Feature#180]]) both carry the corrected rule: minted hidden, unhide one in the eye to see it in the strip and the grid.
- `appearsAsPanel` reads `db.hiddenFields`, the same set the grid and the field rows read. `test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs` drives the page's own eye — toggle, PATCH, redraw — and asserts the strip's two slots.
- An embedded relation grid filters through `visibleCols(target)`, so Chip and Card stay out of it until someone unhides them, and the generic cell fallback refuses an object rather than printing `[object Object]`.

### Still open — the successors

The mechanism shipped without saying what a chip and a card should LOOK like; that is the whole of the work below.

- [[Feature#191]] — **the Ledger chip and the Tile card**. Kyle scored ten treatments of one row on 2026-09-07 (Linear, Notion, Trello, Jira, GitHub, Airtable, Asana, Dribbble, Apple Mail, Slack) and picked two shapes plus one ruling: the state mark is the only state control, and it opens a picker grouped by category. Planned, v0.5.
- [[Feature#193]] — **the config those two shapes need**: nine keys read by the same `renderView` — chip `qa`, `avatar`, `place`, `fold`, `thumb`; card `cover` with `aspect` and `fit`, `stateName`, `props.cols`, `props.labels`. Planned, v0.5.
- [[Feature#184]] and [[Feature#185]] — second rounds of the card and chip mockups.
- [[Issue#216]] — the appears-hidden browser suite times out under the full gate on roughly half the runs. It passes 3 of 3 alone.

### Gate today

1802 tests, 1801 pass, `# skipped 0`. The single failure is [[Issue#216]]'s flake, green in isolation.

features.name: Reuse pass wave 1: one test harness (browser lifecycle, source readers, signals not sleeps)
features.description:
# One test harness: the browser lifecycle, the source readers, and signals instead of sleeps

Wave 1 of the 2026-09-04 reusability survey (the pass that followed the icon-inventory work). Landed as Gerrit 204, 205 and 206, on top of the wave-0 fixes (194–200).

## What changed

- **`test/lib/browser.mjs`** — `launch(name, seed, options)` seeds a Weave, starts a server on a free port, launches Chromium, and closes both after the suite; it returns `null` after registering a skip when playwright is absent. All 24 browser suites use it; each kept its own seed and its test bodies untouched. `test/browser-harness.test.mjs` pins the shape: a suite that drives a page imports the harness and never imports playwright or starts its own server. (−684 / +308 lines.)
- **`test/lib/source.mjs`** — `APP`, `CSS` (comments stripped), `HTML`, `read()`, `rulesFor()`, `fnBody()` (to the closing brace), `fnBodyOf()` (to the next top-level function), `liftFunction()`. Four copies of the CSS reader, three of the body slicer, four hand-rolled `new Function()` lifts and five "app.js still parses" tests became one each; `test/source-helpers.test.mjs` holds the single parse gate and the readers' own tests.
- **Signals instead of sleeps** — the icon-motion hover waits for the motion parts to arm and rest; the eye toggle waits for the flipped `aria-checked`; the inline-icons autosave polls the engine for the typed text and retries the first click once; `bug-report`'s `post()` retries once on a socket-level TypeError. These were the two flakes that voted -1 on the wave-0 chain.

## Left out on purpose

- **Fixture factories** (`taskFixture` / `devFixture` over the ~40 two-line `createSpace` + `createTable` seeds). The survey itself graded it medium risk (a shared factory can change field ids and order under tests that assert on column position) and asked for file-by-file rollout; the two-line seed reads better in place than a call into a factory. Skipped.
- **Retrofitting the ten ad-hoc CSS regexes onto `rulesFor`**. Each regex targets a specific rule; converting them changes what is asserted, one file at a time, for ~80 lines. Left for whoever next edits those files.
- **Sleeps that assert an absence** (a hold released early must not delete; a two-heading document must not grow a rail) stay as sleeps. There is no event for something not happening.

features.name: Reuse pass wave 2: app chrome helpers (Escape, decoration registry, anchor math, buttons, chips, CSS tokens)
features.description:
# Wave 2 of the reuse pass: app chrome helpers

One of four waves from the 2026-09-04 reusability survey of weave (the pass that followed the icon-inventory work). Wave 0 (six zero-risk fixes) and wave 1 (the shared test harness) landed as Gerrit 194–206. This record holds wave 2 for a future session: the app.js and style.css mechanisms that exist several times and should exist once. No engine or API change belongs here.

## Boundary

features.name: Reuse pass wave 4: one command registry and one error contract across CLI, MCP and HTTP (Kyle's go)
features.description:
# Wave 4 of the reuse pass: one command registry and one error contract across CLI, MCP and HTTP

The last wave of the 2026-09-04 reusability survey, and the only one that adds a mechanism. It waits for Kyle's go: it rewrites every agent surface at once. Waves 0 and 1 landed as Gerrit 194–206; waves 2 and 3 are the app-chrome and engine records.

## Boundary

Decklet HTML decks stay self-contained micro-applications that weave only views (Kyle, 2026-09-04); the deck routes (`/e/:id/deck.html|json`) stay hand-written HTTP and are out of the registry's scope.

## The problem

Every operation is written three times: a `case` in `bin/weave.js` (35 commands, ~310 lines of switch plus a 178-line HELP string), a `TOOLS` entry and a `dispatchTool` case in `src/mcp.js` (50 tools, ~540 lines), and a route in `src/routes.js` (33 routes). The sub-action lists are hand-typed 20 times (CLI ×13, MCP ×7) and had drifted (the key list; wave 0 pinned the one sanctioned difference, no `reveal` on MCP, Feature #143). Each surface also answers "what is a value" its own way on create (engine flattens the body, MCP picks by hand, CLI wants pre-formed JSON), and the HTTP role gate re-derives the capability list a third way, as regexes (`routes.js` ~149–161). Errors: HTTP maps `WeaveError.code` to a status (`statusFor`, now with `forbidden → 403`), MCP drops the code (`Error: message`, `isError`), the CLI exits 1 for everything.

Wave 0 added the HTTP column to `test/agent-surface.test.mjs`, so all three doors are now gated for presence. Parity of arguments and results is still by hand.

## The proposal

One table, one entry per operation:

```
{ name: 'field.delete', args: { db: 'table ref', field: 'field ref' },
  run: (weave, a) => weave.deleteField(a.db, a.field),
  http: { method: 'DELETE', path: '/api/tables/:db/fields/:field' },
  cli: { command: 'field', sub: 'delete' }, writes: 'schema' }
```

From it:

- **CLI**: the switch collapses to one generic dispatcher (~60–80 lines); HELP is generated from `{ name, args, description }`.
- **MCP**: `TOOLS` and the dispatch switch both derive from the registry; only the prose descriptions stay hand-written per entry.
- **HTTP**: the plain-CRUD ~60% of routes.js (spaces, tables, fields, entities, views, automations, accounts, keys) generalises; doc rendering, deck routes, bug-report, share links, the applet, MCP-over-HTTP and the workspace hub stay hand-written because they have real per-route concerns (path params, binary bodies, status codes, viewerZone).
- **Role gate**: `writes: 'schema' | 'entity' | 'none'` on each entry replaces the regex list.
- **Error contract**: `{ code → { http, mcp, exit } }` per `WeaveError.code`, e.g. not-found → 404 / -32001 / 44, conflict → 409 / -32002 / 45, forbidden → 403 / -32003 / 46; MCP keeps the code on the wire instead of dropping it. Wave 0's rule that a mutation with no natural return answers `{ id, deleted }` becomes a registry invariant.
- `agent-surface.test.mjs` becomes a well-formedness check over the registry (every entry has all three doors or a documented reason) plus the existing engine-method coverage.

Net: ~250–350 lines out of the three files against ~200–250 in the shared registry; the 51st operation is written once.

## Small items that fold into this wave

- `pick()` / `pickFlags()` exist twice (mcp.js ~22, bin/weave.js ~50).
- The workspace-name regex `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]*$/i` is typed in engine.js (`updateWorkspace`) and server.js (`hub.create`); export one `isValidWorkspaceName`.
- The 20 sub-action dispatch lists become `dispatchSub(table, sub)` over the registry's action map.

## Risk and the gate

High: it touches every live surface at once. Mitigation: `test/agent-surface.test.mjs`, `test/cli.test.mjs`, `test/mcp.test.mjs`, `test/mcp-http.test.mjs`, `test/server.test.mjs`, `test/accounts-audit.test.mjs`, `test/mutation-results.test.mjs` and `test/credential-reveal.test.mjs` already exercise the affected behaviour end to end. Go only after waves 2 and 3 are green, and after Kyle says so.

features.name: Relation map: layouts that show polymorphic junctions as hubs — mockups, then the chosen one
features.description:
Requested by Kyle 2026-09-05 after Feature #182 shipped, looking at the Showcase space's relation map: "relation map visualization for polymorphic junctions is not sufficient. I like the table style but the layout does not communicate the interconnected nature."

**Problem.** The relation map (Feature #129, table-shaped nodes grouped by space, edges per relation) draws a target-set relation as N separate edges fanning out of one table. With five polymorphic tables in Showcase (Comments.On, Activity.Subject, Notes.Related, Approvals.Of, Tags.Applied to) the picture is a hairball: you cannot see that `Activity` is a hub reaching everything, that `Comments` and `Tags` share three targets, or that `Notes.Related` points at structure (Workspace/Tables, Spaces) as well as rows. Plain pairs (Task→Project, Line Items→Expense) and target sets look identical.

**Keep.** The table-style node card (name, row count, icon, space band). Kyle likes it.

**Deliverable 1 — mockups (this row).** ONE self-contained HTML page (docs/mockups/relation-map-polymorphic.html) with 3–4 layout options drawn on the real Showcase schema (pull it from `GET /w/weave/api/schema`), both themes side by side, one line per option on what it communicates and what it costs:
- A. **Junction node.** A target-set relation becomes its own small diamond/pill node labelled with the field name; one edge from the source, one to each member; members of the same set share an edge colour. Hubs read as hubs.
- B. **Bundled edges.** Keep tables only; edges of one target set leave the source as one thick stroke and split near the targets (edge bundling), with the field name on the trunk.
- C. **Concentric / hub-and-spoke.** Polymorphic sources ring the centre, plain tables outside, structure tables (Workspace/*) in a distinct outer band; edge weight = member count.
- D. **Matrix companion.** Under the map, a sources × targets grid (dot = member of set, filled = many) as the exact record; the map stays for shape, the grid for truth.
Each option must show plain vs polymorphic distinctly (stroke style or glyph) and a hover/selection state that lights one set at a time.

**Deliverable 2 — implementation (follow-on Feature after Kyle picks).** Cytoscape layout + style in `public/app.js` (~line 1034), same map at workspace and space level (#129), Handbook Data model guide updated.

**Execution rule.** Mockups built by a background agent in an isolated worktree, landed through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`) as docs/mockups; HTML attached to this row and copied to the parent session's scratchpad.



**2026-09-05 — Deliverable 1 landed.** Gerrit change 229 (commit c069e8b, merged as 93695d6): `docs/mockups/relation-map-polymorphic.html` + `test/relmap-mockup.test.mjs`. The page (attached) draws options A Junction node, B Bundled edges, C Concentric hub-and-spoke, D Matrix companion on the live Showcase schema, light and dark side by side, today's node card verbatim, plain relations grey vs target sets in colour with the ◆ glyph, hover/click lights one set at a time in both panes, one Communicates/Costs line per option. No network, SVG drawn inline. Status left at Planned: Kyle picks an option, then Deliverable 2 gets its own Feature.

**State 2026-09-07.** Deliverable 1 (the mockup page) is in release [[Release#6]] v0.4.6 (2e60c20). Deliverable 2 has no code: it waits on Kyle picking A, B, C or D. Until then this Feature stays Planned and the shipped relation map is unchanged.

Kyle 2026-09-05 after reviewing Feature #181's five options (A header line, B footer row +N, C labelled grid, D compact, E reading card): "I want more variations of card view options."

**Deliverable.** Extend docs/mockups/card-view-options.html (same generator, scripts/export-card-view-options.mjs, same live chip CSS, both themes side by side, one line per option on what it optimises for) with at least eight further options that vary axes A–E did not touch:
- **F Cover card** — a leading colour/state band or attachment thumbnail across the top; fields below.
- **G Two-column split** — name + description left, a vertical stack of labelled field chips right.
- **H Kanban tile** — the card as it would sit in a board column: state implied by the column, so no state chip; assignee/person avatar and due date as the only chips.
- **I Sidebar accent** — a 3px left accent in the state colour, single-line fields row, id in the corner.
- **J Table-row card** — a card that keeps the table's column order as inline cells (a row you can lift out of the grid).
- **K Icon-led** — table icon large at left, name and one key field only (the chip-picker/search-result costume).
- **L Dense list item** — 32px tall, name + two chips + relation count, for long relation lists in the entity side column.
- **M Person/relation-forward** — the relation targets drawn as a chip cluster first (who/what this connects to), name second.
- **N Timeline card** — date range as a bar with the fields hanging from it (for daterange-carrying tables).
- **O Editable card** — same as B but every chip is in its edit costume (picker open on one) to show in-card editing.
Also a **matrix** at the top: options × axes (field placement, density, labels, overflow, state treatment, description size) so the options can be compared in one glance, and a note on which options collapse into the same renderer with different `Card` config vs which need a new `shape`.

**Constraints.** Same as #181: field values are the live chips (k-state, k-select/k-multi, k-rel pointer with ↗ and no fill, k-computed date, k-more), 4px radius, Card contract (`shape`, `link`, `state`, `description`, `fields`). Extend `test/card-view-mockup.test.mjs` to name every option.

**Execution rule.** Built by a background agent in an isolated worktree, landed through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`); HTML attached to this row and copied to the parent session's scratchpad.



## Round 2 built 2026-09-05
Landed in ceeca34 (Gerrit change 233, merged; gerrit/main 26b7a90). docs/mockups/card-view-options.html now carries fifteen options: A–E verbatim from #181, plus **F** cover card · **G** two-column split · **H** kanban tile (no state chip; owner + due) · **I** sidebar accent · **J** table-row card · **K** icon-led · **L** dense 32px list item · **M** relation-forward · **N** timeline bar · **O** editable card (every chip in its picker box, Severity open). Matrix at the top compares all fifteen on field placement, density, labels, overflow, state, description and renderer. Closing note: A–E, H, M, O are renderView('card') under a different Card config; F, G, I, J, K, L, N need a new shape or a layout key. Option O's picker rules are lifted from public/style.css (pickerCss) like the chip rules. Gate: test/card-view-mockup.test.mjs (7); full suite 1693/1693, skipped 0. The HTML is attached to this row (card-view-options-r2.html). Status stays Planned — Kyle picks next.

**State 2026-09-07.** Rounds 1 and 2 are both in release [[Release#6]] v0.4.6 (2e60c20) as one page, options A–O. No card renderer change has landed. Waits on Kyle picking an option; A–E, H, M and O need only a Card config, the other seven need a layout key. Related: [[Feature#181]] (round 1), [[Feature#185]] (the chip inside these cards).

features.name: Chip anatomy, round 2: alternatives that drop the avatar, ↗ and ×, and make in-chip segments live chips
features.description:
Kyle 2026-09-05, reviewing the Chip and card anatomy guide (Feature #180, elements 1–8 of the chip):

> "Let's propose some alternatives. I like 5 (caret), I like 4 (home badge). 1 (avatar) rarely makes sense since we don't often have avatars. 7 (open mark ↗) doesn't make sense if the whole thing is a link. Chips in 6 (segments) should be represented the same size and way they are elsewhere so they can be interacted with — a state can be changed, a multiselect can be changed. 8 (×) may not be necessary since we use this chip inline and it can be deleted with backspace."

**Rulings to carry.** Keep 4 home badge and 5 caret. Drop 1 avatar as a default element (a person table may still opt in through its Chip view config). Drop 7 ↗: the chip IS the link, so no separate promise glyph. Segments (6) are the real state / select / multiselect / relation chips at the shared chip size (`--wv-chip-font`, `--wv-chip-line`) and stay **interactive**: click a state segment → the state picker, change it on the row; a multiselect segment → its picker. That means the chip is no longer one undivided link: the name (and id) navigates, segments edit. Drop 8 × in inline/document contexts where Backspace removes the chip; decide whether a relation cell keeps × or also relies on Backspace/Delete on a focused chip.

**Deliverable.** ONE self-contained HTML page (docs/mockups/chip-anatomy-alternatives.html) with 4–5 chip alternatives, each drawn in the real markup at the live chip size, both themes side by side, in the three surfaces (relation cell, [[…]] mention in a document, References list), with hitboxes outlined as in #180 and a one-line note on what each trades:
- **P Name-link + live segments.** Name/id is the link; segments are live chips; caret; home badge; no ↗, no avatar, no ×.
- **Q Whole-chip link, segments pop on caret.** Collapsed chip is one link; caret expands a strip of live segments below/beside; editing happens in the strip.
- **R Split chip.** Two visual halves: pointer half (name, id, home badge) and value half (live segments), one 4px outline around both.
- **S Minimal.** Name + state chip only, everything else on hover.
- **T Cell-only ×.** Same as P but the relation cell keeps a × on hover/focus; inline drops it.
Include keyboard behaviour per option (focus chip → Backspace removes / Enter opens / Space on a segment opens its picker) and which option collapses into today's renderer with config only.

**Follow-on.** Kyle picks; a Feature lands the chip change and updates the anatomy guide (#180) and chip system (#175).

**Execution rule.** Built by a background agent in an isolated worktree, landed through Gerrit (`refs/for/main`); HTML attached here and copied to the parent session's scratchpad.



**2026-09-05 — mockup landed.** `docs/mockups/chip-anatomy-alternatives.html` (Gerrit change 234, commit 9059bb6, merged as abd9446): options P–T in the real chip markup at the live size, three surfaces × both themes, hitboxes outlined, keyboard table and distance-from-today per option. Generator `scripts/export-chip-anatomy-alternatives.mjs`; gates `test/chip-alternatives-mockup.test.mjs` + `test/chip-alternatives-browser.test.mjs`. The HTML is attached to this Feature. Status stays Planned until Kyle picks.

**State 2026-09-07.** The mockup page is in release [[Release#6]] v0.4.6 (2e60c20). The shipped chip is unchanged: it still carries the avatar, the ↗ and the ×, and its segments are still shrunk by the `.wv-seg-state` `.82em` rule that every option here overrides. Whichever option lands should delete that rule rather than override it, and update [[Feature#180]] (the anatomy guide) and [[Feature#175]] (the chip and card contract) in the same change. Waits on Kyle picking P, Q, R, S or T.

decklet: 16px grid + layout guides + snap (branch feat/grid-snap)
features.description:
# decklet: 16px grid + layout guides + snap, hand-off (2026-09-07)

The work, the decisions, and the open items, so the next session can pick up from here, the weave Feature row, or the branch history.

## Where

| Thing | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Branch | `feat/grid-snap` on github.com/grunion-ai/decklet (pushed; three commits ahead of `main` at a858920) |
| Worktree | `~/Documents/decklet-wt/grid-snap` (node_modules symlinked to `~/Documents/decklet/node_modules`) |
| Commits | 6958eaf guides + snap · 7246430 the magnetic feel · eb2d012 the 16px grid + library re-cut |
| Suite | `npm test` in the worktree: 119 pass, 0 skipped (Playwright live proofs run) |
| Demo deck | `~/Documents/decklet-grid-demo.html` (also `grid-demo.html` untracked in the worktree; model in the session scratchpad `grid-demo.json`) |
| Feel mockup | https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7724e90c-a1a8-4425-84f4-4dcd3d39701c |
| Gridlines mockup | https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1c05e5b0-de3f-40e5-983a-fd7b137d387a |
| Memory | `decklet-guides-snap-branch.md` in the harness auto-memory |

## What shipped on the branch

- **HUD toggle `#snap`** (Lucide magnet, after spellcheck). OFF by default. Browser state under `NS+':snap'`, never a model key. `fileHtml()` resets it, so a saved copy opens with it off. Hidden from the present-mode peek pill (one more button put the pill on a 4:5 deck's page counter).
- **16px grid overlay** (`GP=16`): one `.gg` repeating-gradient node, opacity .11, painted by `render()` whenever the toggle is on. Never in present, the contact sheet, print, the ⤓ PDF, or the file: all four draw through `drawEls`, which paints neither grid nor guides; CSS also hides `.gl,.gg` under `body.present` and `@media print`.
- **Layout guides** (`guides(s)`): every slot edge of the slide's layout (x, x+w, y, y+h), the content margin, and the canvas mid-lines, each rounded onto the 16px lattice. Hidden at rest; shown while a drag is in flight (`#canvas.dragging`); the held line brightens (`.gl.on`). A slide with no layout gets margin + mid-lines.
