- **Snap** (`snapTo`): guides first with a 10px reach and a 4px hold on a line already held (`SNAPO={px:10,centers:true,mid:true,hyst:4}`, Kyle's pick from the mockup), box centre snaps too; when no guide is in reach the nearest grid line takes the axis. Applies to drag, the resize nib (far edges), and connector point nibs. Arrow-key nudge never snaps.
- **Library re-cut on the lattice** (`lib/layouts.mjs`, `GRID=16` exported): margin 64 / 896, content width 832; supertitle y 48, title y 80; kpi tiles 256 wide on a 288 pitch (four-up: 192 on 208, right edge 880); agenda rows on a 64 pitch; timeline rule on 240 with 16px dots at 224 standing on it; every slot edge of all nineteen layouts is a multiple of 16, and `libraryFor()` re-seats scaled geometry (1600×900) on the lattice. Default `styles.margin` in the template is now 64.
- **Gates**: `test/gate.test.mjs` section 2l (pure contract + one live proof covering paint, drag, hold, resize, nib, off, print, sheet, PDF byte-identical, save, reload); `test/layouts.test.mjs` asserts every library edge `% 16 === 0` before and after scaling; HUD manifest in SKILL.md updated; `deck.html` rebuilt.

## Decisions Kyle made

1. Feel: magnetic (10px, +4 hold), box centre snaps, canvas mid-lines, lines only while dragging, held line brightens.
2. A universal 16px grid overlays the editor; every layout line must sit on it; the grid shows only in the editor view.
3. Every slide has layout lines (hidden until drag) usable as snap targets.

## Open before merge

- [ ] Kyle tries the demo deck and sends back what felt wrong (reach, hold, grid weight on screen, which lines win).
- [ ] `templates/candidates.*` and `templates/shots|thumbs` still show the old geometry: regenerate via `templates/build-*.mjs`.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry for 0.6.0 and the `package.json` bump. Say plainly that the library re-cut moves every deck that uses library layouts by a few px on re-create; the explainer keeps its own 60px margin, so its guides round to 64 and sit 4px off its slots.
- [ ] SKILL.md still names the toggle "Layout guides + snap" in the button title (tests pin that string); consider renaming to "Grid + guides + snap" with the tests.
- [ ] Merge to `main` (squash or keep the three commits), push with the grunion-ai credential, then `git -C ~/Documents/decklet pull --ff-only` and remove the worktree.

## Gotchas found

- `window.snap` inside a deck is the undo-snapshot function; the button is `$('snap')`. Tests must not touch `snap.*` bare.
- Selection boxes must come from the model, not `getBoundingClientRect()`: under a fractional canvas scale the DOM rect lands half a pixel off and the snap misses by one.
- A held line beats a fresh search, so a Playwright drag that passes through a nearer line on an intermediate step lands there; use `steps: 1` when the test wants the far line.
- Playwright runs that are killed mid-way leave Chromium processes behind: `pkill -f ms-playwright`.

features.name: decklet: five candidate layouts from the open-source sets (intro, image-full, feature-grid, table, people)
features.description:
## Why
The decklet library (19 layouts, `lib/layouts.mjs`, 0.4.0) mirrors Slidev's built-in layout set. Kyle asked (2026-09-07) for five more drawn from the open-source sets the OSS landscape report identified (Slidev built-ins; Presenton's HTML/Tailwind template layouts). These are the five that earn a place; `iframe*` (network) and `none`/`default` (free rows already cover them) were rejected.

## The five
| # | Layout | Source | Slots | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `intro` | Slidev `intro` | title (Title) · subtitle (H2) · author (Body) · meta (Caption) · optional image right | A cover with a person on it: who is talking, to whom, when. `cover` carries the deck name only. |
| 2 | `image-full` | Slidev `image` / `full` | image (full-bleed media) · band (tinted box, bottom 120px) · title (H1 on the band) · caption | Full-bleed photo or diagram with a caption band; the two image layouts give the picture 400×320, a thumbnail. |
| 3 | `feature-grid` | Presenton icon-bullets / Slidev `default` cards | supertitle · title · 3–4 cards: icon (svg) · head (H2) · body (Body) | The "three things" slide. Not `process-steps` (no order), not `kpi-grid` (no number). |
| 4 | `table` | Presenton table | supertitle · title · header row (Label ×4) · rows (Body 4×4, alternating tint) · source (Caption) | Tabular content is hand-placed rows today; the most-requested missing shape in the sample decks. |
| 5 | `people` | Presenton team grid | supertitle · title · 3–4 cards: avatar (round media) · name (H2) · role (Label) · note (Caption) | Team, panel, logos, contacts. Same tile geometry as feature-grid with a round media slot. |

## Shape
Each is a `LIBRARY` entry in `lib/layouts.mjs` (group: openers for intro, visuals for image-full, text for feature-grid, numbers for table, visuals for people), with `use`, `density` and slots in the existing shape; `validate --layouts` lists them; SKILL.md's LAYOUT LIBRARY table and pick-by-content rules gain a row each; `test/layouts.test.mjs` gates slot names and geometry inside the canvas. Rebuild `decks/layout-catalogue` (harness) so the catalogue shows 24 slides.

## Depends on
Land after the dead-space recut (Issue: "decklet: six library layouts leave the bottom third dead") so the new layouts are cut to the same height rules (takeaway/source where reading-density).

## Not in the decklet ROADMAP.md yet
The engine's ROADMAP.md (in progress in another session, lanes: Platform & release · Notes & presenting · Mobile & touch · Documents & formats · Export) has no layouts lane; this feature and the recut issue are the candidates for one.

features.name: Releases are rows: Development/Release, and its notes are mandatory
features.description:
**Shipped 2026-09-04 in v0.4.5** (Gerrit 203 → `8f8258d`). Requested by Kyle: "need a release notes table under weave's Development where notes for each release are mandated and stored."

## The shape

`Development/Release` holds one row per release. Name is the version (`v0.4.5`), `Date` and `Commit` record when and what landed, `Fixes` points at the Issues the release closes and `Ships` at the Features it delivers, and the release notes live in the Description. Both relations carry an inverse, so an Issue row now says `Fixed in → v0.4.8` and a Feature says `Shipped in`.

## The notes cannot be skipped

Three gates refuse an unwritten release, so a version bump that forgot its notes never reaches main:

| Gate | Refuses |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/export-development.mjs` | a row with an empty Description, and a missing row for the current `package.json` version |
| `syncDevelopment` in `src/weaver-seed.js` | a manifest release without notes |
| `test/development-sync.test.mjs` | a build whose package version has no notes-bearing row |

`ensureReleaseTable` creates the table on demand, so a workspace seeded before this existed grows it on the next sync rather than needing a migration. The manifest ships releases alongside issues and features, so every instance inherits the history.

## Order of operations for a release

Write the Release row on `:4400` first, then bump `package.json`, then run the export, then move the `## Unreleased` bullets under the version heading in `CHANGELOG.md`, and land it as one change. Reversing the first two steps makes the export refuse, which is the point.

## Evidence

v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.4.3 and v0.4.4 were backfilled from `CHANGELOG.md` when the table was created. Four releases have been cut through the gate since: v0.4.5, v0.4.6, v0.4.7 and v0.4.8. Tests added in `test/development-sync.test.mjs`: the fresh-seed shape including the Issue-side inverse, table-created-on-demand followed by rows and both relations, a notes-less release refused, and the shipped manifest carrying notes for the package version. Docs: `CLAUDE.md` rule 5, `DEVELOPMENT.md` under "Releasing".

The same change dropped a `node_modules` symlink that had been committed by accident and added the bare name to `.gitignore`, so the Gerrit gate's Playwright link can never land in a patchset again.

features.name: The Ledger chip and the Tile card: what a row looks like everywhere else
features.description:
[[Feature#175]] gave every table a Chip and a Card and put one `renderView` behind both, so a row looks the same wherever it turns up. It never said what those two should look like. The shapes came from the grid by default, and the state segment on a rendered chip is read-only text.

Kyle reviewed ten treatments of one row on 2026-09-07 — the same Feature row drawn the way Linear, Notion, Trello, Jira, GitHub, Airtable, Asana, Dribbble, Apple Mail and Slack each draw one — scored them across ten criteria, and picked two shapes plus one interaction ruling.

## The Ledger, drawn as the Chip

A single line: the state mark, the `#id` in mono, the title, then the configured chips, an optional thumbnail, the owner avatar and the action tray. The mark leads because the category reads before the words do. The tray never hides, so a row in a list is one click from its permalink.

Densest of the ten. Home: tables, search results, the ⌘K palette, relation cells, doc mentions.

## The Tile, drawn as the Card

Cover on top when the table has one, then the `#id` and title, the description preview, a state row that is also the control, and the configured properties two-up with their labels. Nothing on it needs a tooltip.

Home: boards, galleries, the Appears-as strip, reference cards.

## The mark is the only way state changes

Every treatment that offered a one-click state control used a checkbox, and a checkbox lies about a table with six states in four categories. The ruling:

- The state **mark** is a button. Clicking it opens a picker grouped by category — Not started, In progress, Done, Canceled — with the named states under each. A two-state Note and a six-state Issue wear the same glyph and the same gesture.
- The tray carries **copy link** and **open** only. An "advance state" arrow was drafted and cut: with two terminal categories, "next" is a guess.
- The caret rule from #175 still holds. The chip is a link, and the mark is the one pixel inside it that does not navigate.

## A row with two workflow fields

A table may carry `State` and `QA` at once. Three treatments were drawn and all three are supported by config rather than by picking one:

| Treatment | Reads as |
| --- | --- |
| Primary mark leads, second trails as a chip with its own mark | the default; the second state is clearly secondary |
| Two marks stacked in the leading slot | a long list scanned by category alone |
| Both spelled out as labelled controls | widest, never needs a tooltip |

## Scoring, for the record

Ten criteria across the seven shortlisted styles. The Ledger and the Tile came from the two ends of that table: highest density, and the shape that loses nothing.

| Style | Total of 20 |
| --- | --- |
| Notion gallery | 13 |
| Linear row · GitHub item · Airtable record · Asana task | 12 |
| Jira card | 11 |
| Trello card | 10 |

## Evidence

The five screenshots attached here are the mockup as reviewed: the three options with their full and compact forms, the twelve Ledger configurations, the two config panels, the scoring matrix, and the original ten-style gallery. `weave-card-styles.html` is the whole interactive mockup — open it in a browser, the pickers and the config panels work.

The config keys this design needs are [[Feature#193]].

features.name: Overnight fixer: a nightly run that lands one to three Issue fixes or leaves a note
features.description:
**Running since 2026-09-05.** Kyle asked for a routine that picks one to three open Issues a night, fixes them, verifies the fix, completes the merge and post-merge verification, updates the documentation, and ships nothing it could not finish — leaving a note on the Issue instead, so the next run avoids it and the session that picks it up knows what already failed.

The machinery lives in the harness repo, not in weave: `routines/weave-fixer-routine.md` is the spec, `scripts/weave-fixer.mjs` is the tested core (16 tests), and the durable scheduled task `weave-overnight-fix` fires at 03:00 local. It is a development-process row of the same kind as the lifecycle regression gate and the gate hardening work.

## The attempt line is the contract

Every attempt appends one parsable line to the Issue's Description:

```
🌙 overnight-fixer · attempt N · <ISO> · started | abandoned | fixed · <detail>
```

Selection skips any Issue whose last line is not `fixed`, so a failure is never retried blind. An abort line states that nothing shipped, the hypothesis, what was tried, an excerpt of the evidence, whether a Gerrit change was abandoned, and the name of the attached patch. A claim left at `started` for more than twelve hours belongs to a session that died, so the next run reopens it with an abandoned line.

One consequence to know: an abandoned Issue stays out of selection until a person clears the line or the Issue is closed. That is deliberate. Nobody wants the same failing approach attempted four nights running.

## What counts as shipped

A fix is shipped only when the Gerrit change is MERGED, `:4400` serves that SHA with a start time later than the submit, and the original repro is re-run against the live app. Each Issue gets its own subagent and its own worktree, writes the failing test first, and needs the full suite green with zero skips — a skipped browser suite means the Playwright symlink is missing, which the gate treats as red. The shipping agent reads its own diff, extends the tests, votes +2 and submits. Budget: no new Issue after 05:00, hard stop at 06:30, and a budget stop is an abort rather than a reason to rush a gate.

## Three nights in

| Night | Fixed | Release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-05 | #134, #83, #133 | v0.4.5 |
| 2026-09-06 | #142, #157 (#129 abandoned as a duplicate that no longer reproduces) | v0.4.7 |
| 2026-09-07 | #69, #110, #114 | v0.4.8 |

Every fix landed with new tests and screenshots attached to its Issue. The 09-05 run also found that Issue #150 had been fixed in Gerrit 196 and never closed, and that fifteen watcher-filed operations rows were sitting open; both were cleared by hand afterwards. Run logs live at `reports/weave-fixer/<date>.md` in the harness repo, and no email is sent — the Issue rows and the logs are the record.

## What it declines

The core drops rows the main watcher files about its own mirror and deploy loop, and anything whose text asks for a decision. Judgment then declines Issues whose repro cannot be stated in two sentences, and anything resting on taste Kyle has not settled. Those skips carry a reason in the run log and leave no line on the Issue, because a decision that was never attempted is not an attempt.

features.name: Chip and Card config: placement, fold, cover framing, a second workflow
features.description:
The view section of the field dialog carries four knobs today: show the `#id`, show the state, the description size, and which fields ride along. That is enough to draw a chip. It is not enough to draw the Ledger and the Tile of [[Feature#191]], which need to know where chips sit, when they fold, how a cover is framed, and what a second workflow field does.

Nine new keys on the `view` config, read by the one `renderView`, so every chip and card surface picks them up together.

## Chip

| Key | Values | Default | Draws |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qa` | `none` · `mark` · `chip` | `none` | a second workflow field as a stacked mark or a trailing chip |
| `avatar` | `none` · a person field | `none` | the avatar at the right end, before the tray |
| `place` | `trail` · `under` | `trail` | chips after the title, or on their own line beneath it |
| `fold` | 1–6 | 3 | how many chips draw before the rest fold into `+N` |
| `thumb` | `none` · an attachments field | `none` | a 64×42 thumbnail inside the row height |

## Card

| Key | Values | Default | Draws |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cover` | `none` · an attachments field | `none` | the image above the title |
| `cover.aspect` | `16:9` · `4:3` · `1:1` | `16:9` | the cover's box |
| `cover.fit` | `fill` · `fit inside` | `fill` | whether a tall image crops or letterboxes |
| `stateName` | on · off | on | the state name beside its mark, or the mark alone |
| `props.cols` | 1 · 2 | 2 | the property grid |
| `props.labels` | `above` · `inline` | `above` | label over the value, or beside it |

`qa` and `avatar` are shared with the chip and read the same way.

## Rules the keys inherit

- **Fold, never clip.** `+N` opens the row. A cell that runs out of room already says `+N` in the grid; the chip now does the same.
- **One meaning per channel.** A select chip spends a hue from the ten-hue ramp, a relation stays outlined with no fill, a label-and-value pair stays neutral. Adding a knob never adds a colour.
- **Auto stays the default.** "The first few non-empty fields, in column order" is still what an unconfigured table gets, and arranging the columns is still the curation.
- **The mark is the control.** Wherever `state` draws, its mark opens the picker. See [[Feature#191]].

## Panels

Both panels are drawn in the attached mockup: the preview sits at the top of each and redraws as the form changes, exactly as the view section does today. `weave-card-styles.html` on [[Feature#191]] is the interactive copy — the controls work.

features.name: Shares: one grant primitive for public and cross-network access
features.description:
# Shares: one grant primitive for public and cross-network access

Design landed 2026-09-07 with Kyle. Not yet built. This is the concrete build-out of [[Feature#141]] §9 (Sharing), and it touches §4 (scoped keys) and §6 (permissions). It absorbs [[Feature#17]]'s view share links and stands beside the passcode task applet, which keeps its own door for now.

## Pain Point

Two one-off public surfaces exist and neither generalizes. [[Feature#17]] share links publish exactly one saved view through a `wvv_` token and a bespoke HTML renderer that derives its columns from row 0. The task applet publishes exactly one table behind a passcode. Nothing publishes an entity, a document, a table or a space — and there is no scoped door an outside agent or another weave instance can read through.

## Problem Statement

Three gaps, one shape:

1. **No general grant.** Sharing an entity, a document, a table or a space needs a new bespoke surface each time, as [[Feature#17]] and the applet each proved.
2. **The page surfaces are already anonymous.** Role caps and `requireAuth` are both `path.startsWith('/api/')`-only (`src/routes.js:142,145`), so `/e/:ref/doc.html`, `entity.pdf` and `deck.html` are readable without a token today. Any sharing design has to either formalise that or close it — leaving it undecided is the actual hole.
3. **No cross-network read.** An agent or a second instance has no scoped credential; the only key that reads anything reads everything.

Two adjacent leaks found while surveying, fixed in the same pass: `GET /api/export` returns `state.meta` wholesale including account `tokenHash` and view `shareToken` values (`src/engine.js:4486`), readable by a reader token; and `POST /api/import` is not in `schemaWrite`, so a writer token can replace the whole workspace.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

One grant object in `state.meta.shares`, exported and imported with the workspace, secrets redacted:

```
{ id, token: 'wvs_…',
  scope: { kind: 'entity'|'table'|'space'|'view'|'workspace', id },
  mode: 'read'|'comment'|'edit'|'manage',
  visibility: 'public'|'private',
  label, createdBy, createdAt, expiresAt?, revokedAt? }
```

A document is its entity's doc surface — there is no separate `document` scope kind, because an entity grant already covers `doc.html`.

**Mode ladder**, enforced server-side and always inside scope:

| Mode | Powers |
| --- | --- |
| read | GET subset, POST query, markdown render — the list [[Feature#14]] already grants readers |
| comment | read + comment endpoints; reserved, 403 until comments ship (§12) |
| edit | read + field updates on in-scope entities; never create, delete or schema |
| manage | edit + create/delete entities in scope; never schema, never registry rows |

**Engine.** `mintShare` / `listShares` / `revokeShare` / `shareByToken`, and one containment function `withinScope(grant, {spaceId, tableId, entityId, viewId})` used by the page gate, the API read gate and the API write gate alike. It is modelled on the applet's `mine()` (`src/applet.js:162-167`), which is the existing precedent for scope filtering.

**Routes.** The pipeline order becomes `share resolver → applet → Bearer wall → role caps`. The resolver strips the `/s/:token` prefix and re-enters the existing dispatch under a scoped context, so there is no parallel route tree:

* `/s/:token` — landing redirect for the scope kind
* `/s/:token/e/:ref[/doc.html|deck.html|entity.pdf]` — the existing renderers, containment checked first
* `/s/:token/table/:id`, `/s/:token/space/:id` — server-rendered read pages through `renderDocumentPage` (`src/markdown.js:357`), built from schema rather than row-0 keys; this retires [[Feature#17]]'s inline renderer
* `Bearer wvs_…` on `/api/*` — the enumerated subset for the grant's mode, filtered through `withinScope`; MCP takes the same token under the same caps, and no custom header is introduced
* `visibility: private` — the resolver additionally requires a signed-in account before honouring the grant
* `requireAuth` extends to page surfaces and exports; `/s/` and `/t` become the only anonymous doors

**Client.** One share dialog, reused from the entity page header, the table header control and the space page: mode picker (read / comment, disabled until comments exist / edit / add-delete), public–private toggle, mint and copy, then the existing grants with revoke beside each. It follows the unified field dialog's pattern.

**Migration.** Existing `views[].shareToken` values lift into `meta.shares` as `{kind:'view', mode:'read', visibility:'public'}` on load; `/view/:token` becomes a 302 to `/s/`, so links already handed out keep working.

## Decisions taken (Kyle, 2026-09-07)

* **Mode ladder over a read-only flag.** The dialog offers read, comment, edit and add-delete. Comment ships in the enum and the dialog but stays 403 until comments exist.
* **Public and private links.** Private means the link resolves only for a signed-in account — the middle ground between a public URL and full membership.
* **Cross-network v1 is the scoped JSON API plus MCP.** Remote `[[…]]` chips pointing at another instance build on that stable JSON later, not now.
* **Tokens are stored in plaintext** in workspace meta so the dialog can always re-show a link, and are redacted from export. Revocation, not secrecy at rest, is the control.
* **Web pages under `/s/` render read-only in v1** regardless of mode; the write modes serve the API and MCP surface. An editable scoped web surface is the recorded upgrade path, and the applet covers the phone task list meanwhile.

## Verification plan

* `test/share-grants.test.mjs`: mint, verify, expiry, revoke; the containment matrix including denials; mode enforcement at each rung; visibility (anonymous 401 vs signed-in 200); `requireAuth` × share interplay; export redaction; [[Feature#17]] migration and the `/view/` redirect; the three `/s/` page kinds rendering. The accounts-audit test grows share mint and revoke rows.
* Live on :4400 — mint an entity share, open it logged out, confirm `/e/<ref>` closes with `requireAuth` on, curl the scoped API from another machine, revoke and confirm 404.
* A Handbook page for shares, which the regression gate requires for any new surface.

## Out of scope, deliberately

Comment endpoints (the mode is reserved, not built); an editable scoped web surface; per-user sharing, which needs §1 identity; remote chips; passcodes on shares; migrating the applet onto shares.

features.name: Formula check: validate and preview an expression before it is saved, from MCP, REST, the CLI and the dialog
features.description:
A formula is the one field type where an agent could not tell, before writing to the schema, whether what it was about to save would compute. The engine had no way to answer "is this expression valid for this table?" short of creating the field and reading a cell back — and until v0.4.5 it would happily create the field either way.

## The check

`check(expression, fieldNames)` in `src/formula.js` parses an expression and resolves every name against a list, with stub values: it catches syntax errors, unknown functions and unknown fields, and needs no row to do it. `addField` and `updateField` run it and refuse what fails, so an invalid formula can no longer reach storage from any door. A formula naming its own field fails as an unknown field — it never converges.

`checkFormula(db, expression)` wraps it with a preview: when the table has rows, the expression is evaluated against one and the computed value comes back with the row it came from.

## One verdict, four surfaces

| Surface | Call |
| --- | --- |
| MCP | `weave_check_formula` — `{db, expression, entity?, excludeField?}` |
| REST | `POST /api/tables/:id/formula-check` |
| CLI | `weave formula check <table> '<expression>'` |
| Dialog | the live line under the script editor |

The loop is the same for a person and for an agent: **check until `ok: true`, save, read a cell back.** A bad expression returns `{ok: false, error}` rather than throwing, so a checking agent never has to catch. Saving an invalid one is refused with the same message the check gives, which makes checking first free rather than merely advisable.

## In the dialog

The verdict line under the script editor prints the parse error in red while you type, or `= value` with the row it computed on. Function chips insert `name()` and land the caret between the parens. The field being edited no longer offers its own chip.

## Evidence

`test/formula-check.test.mjs`, 19 tests: static checking (brackets, keywords, function-name collisions, bad date-unit literals), engine refusal at add and update, self-reference, `excludeField` by name and by id, named-entity preview, and the REST surface including a 200-with-error for an invalid expression and a 400 for an invalid save. Full suite green at 1480 with no skips; `test/agent-surface.test.mjs` carries the `formula.check` row, so the tool, the command and the AGENTS.md entry cannot drift apart.

Landed as Gerrit 167.

features.name: Grid: the “+ New” row floats at the bottom of the viewport on long tables
features.description:
## Request (Kyle, 2026-09-07)

> new row in weave should float at the bottom of the page for long tables so you dont have to scroll to the end

## Today

The `+ New <term>` control is the last `<tr class="add-entity-row">` of the grid (`public/app.js`, `buildGrid`, right after the row loop). On a table with hundreds of rows it sits below the fold; adding a row means scrolling to the end first. The header is already sticky (`.wv-grid thead th { position: sticky; top: 0 }`), so the foot is the only edge that scrolls away.

## Expected

- The `+ New` row is `position: sticky; bottom: 0` inside the grid's scroll container (`#dock` scrolls, `overflow-y: auto`), so it stays visible at the bottom edge while the reader is anywhere in the table, and rests in its natural place once the reader reaches the end.
- Short tables look unchanged: the row still reads as the last row of one surface that grows from the bottom.
- Clicking it still creates the row and hands the caret to the new Name cell (Issues #125, #195); the new row is scrolled into view above the floating foot, not hidden behind it.
- Background matches the surface (the sticky header pattern) so rows scrolling underneath do not bleed through.
- Entity-page related sections (`.related-section .add-entity-row`) keep their inline placement.

## Where

`public/app.js` (the `add-entity-row` append in the grid builder), `public/style.css` lines ~454-457, Handbook page for the grid if it documents the foot button.

## Verify

Playwright: seed a table with 200 rows, open the grid at scroll top, assert the `+ New` button's bounding box is inside the viewport; scroll to the end, assert it is still visible once; click it and assert the new row's Name input is focused and fully visible (not occluded by the foot). Related-section foot stays non-sticky.

features.name: Toggle field type: two named states, renameable in config, default on or off
features.description:
## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-07)

A `toggle` field type: a weave-language switch with two named states, rendered as a proper toggle (not the checkbox's box), configurable and defaultable.

## Shape

- **Type** `toggle`, value `true`/`false` (same storage as `checkbox`; `checkbox ⇄ toggle` migration in both directions, lossless).
- **Config** `{ on: "On", off: "Off", default: false }` — both labels renameable (e.g. `Active/Paused`, `Enabled/Disabled`, `Public/Private`), `default` picks the state a new row starts in. Labels are shown next to the switch; the value stays boolean so formulas, filters, CSV, MCP and the API read `true`/`false`.
- **Render** everywhere a value draws: grid cell, entity page, chip/card (renderView), filter bar, field dialog config editor (two label inputs + default switch), Handbook page. Tabler tokens, both themes, soft-squared like the chip system (`--tblr-*`; wv- prefixed classes). Keyboard: Space flips it in the grid (grid rests on values).
- **Vocabulary** `fieldTypes` gains `toggle` with the config example; `weave_add_field` / `field add` accept it; `TYPE_MIGRATIONS`, `DEFAULTABLE_TYPES`, quality mirror, agent-surface gate all updated.

## Verify

- engine tests: create, default on/off, rename labels, migrate checkbox→toggle→checkbox, formula reads boolean, filter `=` true.
- browser suite: cell renders the switch with the on/off label, click + Space flip it, dialog config round-trips, dark theme screenshot.
- Handbook page exists (suite gate).

features.name: Universal permalink: /w/ws/e/uuid emitted by API, MCP, CLI, chips and search, and accepted as input everywhere
features.description:
Kyle's ruling, 2026-09-07: the link shape `http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/‹ws›/e/‹uuid›` stays. The requirement is that it is universal: every surface emits the same string, the same string is searchable, and every surface accepts it as input. The five shortening proposals (public ids in the path, base58, no hash, extension-as-renderer, no `/w/`) were trashed the same day.

## Where the surfaces disagree today

| Surface | Emits | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Row crumb `#N ⧉` | `origin + /w/ws/e/uuid` | correct, the reference |
| Chip / card `url` (engine.js `#chipOf`, `#summary`) | `/e/uuid` | no workspace prefix, so it 404s outside the default workspace |
| ⌘K and `GET /api/search` entities | `/w/ws/e/uuid` | correct; tables and spaces still emit `/#/table/`, `/#/space/` |
| `GET /api/entities/:id`, `POST …/entities` | no `url` at all | callers rebuild it by hand |
| MCP `weave_get_entity`, `weave_create_entity`, `weave_update_entity` | `readEntity` shape, no `url` | same gap; only `weave_search` carries one |
| CLI `bin/weave.js` | nothing | no permalink output on any command |
| Bug reporter (routes.js `docs.createEntity`) | `/w/ws/#/entity/uuid` | hash form, not the `/e/` form |
| Document / mention resolver (routes.js `resolveMention`) | `/w/ws/e/uuid/doc.html` | fine |
| Search input | `#143`, `Table#143`, text | a pasted permalink or bare uuid returns `[]` |

## Shape

One function `permalink(kind, id)` on the engine, fed the workspace prefix once at construction (the server already computes `wsPrefix` per request in routes.js; MCP and CLI pass the workspace they were started against). It returns `/w/‹ws›/e/‹uuid›` for rows, `/w/‹ws›/#/table/‹id›` and `/w/‹ws›/#/space/‹id›` until those routes change. Origin is prepended only at the edge that knows it (the browser uses `location.origin`; MCP and CLI take `--origin`, default `http://127.0.0.1:4400`).

Emit it everywhere a row leaves the engine: `readEntity`, `createEntity` responses, chips and cards, search hits, the bug reporter, and a `--json` `url` on CLI commands that touch a row.

## Accept it everywhere

`#resolve` (the `Table#12` / `Space/Table#12` resolver) also accepts a full permalink, a path (`/w/ws/e/uuid`), a bare uuid, and `/e/uuid`. Every API, MCP and CLI parameter that takes an entity id goes through it, so a pasted link works as an argument.

`search()` treats a uuid or a permalink as an exact-id hit that outranks text, the way `#143` does now. Pasting a link into ⌘K opens the row.

## Verification

- one test iterates every emitter above and asserts the string equals `permalink('entity', id)`; adding an emitter without going through `permalink()` fails the agent-surface gate
- `GET /api/entities/:id.url`, MCP `weave_get_entity.url`, and `weave --json get ‹id›` return the identical string
- `GET /api/search?q=‹full permalink›` and `?q=‹uuid›` return that row first
- `weave_get_entity {entity: "http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/weave/e/‹uuid›"}` resolves
- chip `url` inside `/w/uno/` carries `/w/uno/`
- lifecycle pack green

features.name: Formula chips that teach: grouped function chips, a signature card on hover/focus/tap, excluded fields greyed with the reason, the catalog served by the vocabulary
features.description:
The formula builder's chips are the only place the vocabulary is discoverable, and until now they were twenty-two flat function names with the signature hidden in a title attribute — invisible on touch, and to an agent reading the DOM. Fields a formula cannot read (documents, attachments) were silently missing, which reads as a bug rather than a rule.

## What shipped

- **Groups.** The function chips sit in the four groups the grammar has — logic (`if`, `empty`, `contains`), text, number, date — one labelled row each, in `public/field-dialog-core.js` `formulaFunctionGroups()`.
- **The card.** Hover, focus or tap a chip and a `.fx-sigcard` under the chips shows the signature, one sentence of doc and an example. It is an element in the DOM, so it works on touch and an agent can read it; the title attribute is gone. A click still inserts the call with the caret between the parens.
- **Greyed, not gone.** `formulaFieldChoices(fields, selfName)` lists every field but the one being edited; a document or attachments field comes back with an `excluded` reason, drawn disabled with a strike-through and the reason on its aria-label and card.
- **One catalog, every surface.** Each `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` entry carries `group`, `doc` and `example`; `src/vocabulary.js` serves the list verbatim as `formulaFunctions` (+ `formulaGroups`) through `weave_vocabulary`, `weave vocabulary formulaFunctions` and `GET /api/vocabulary`. The Handbook formula page and AGENTS.md name it.

## Gates

- `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`: every function names a group, a doc and an example that passes `check()`; groups list every function exactly once; excluded fields carry their reason.
- `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`: the served catalog is `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` and its names are `FUNCS` in `src/formula.js`.
- `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`: four labelled rows; hover and focus show the card, leaving hides it; a tap inserts; document/attachments chips are disabled with the reason and insert nothing.

Design review: formulabuilder.html, direction A. Follows Feature #195 (the check step).

features.name: The formula dialog prints its own API: an "As an agent would do it" footer with the CLI lines and MCP sequence for what is being built
features.description:
Agent-first means the browser is never the only place a thing can be done, and the fastest way to keep that true is to print the equivalent calls where the human is standing. The formula dialog now documents itself: what was just built by clicking is one command away from a script.

## What shipped

- **The footer.** Under the script's chips, a `<details>` titled **As an agent would do it**, closed on load. Its `<pre>` holds three numbered CLI lines with a comment each — `weave formula check <table> '<expression>'` (with `--exclude-field` when editing), `weave field add <table> <name> formula --config '{"expression":…}'` (or `weave field update` for an existing field), `weave get <table>#1` — and the MCP sequence `weave_check_formula → weave_add_field → weave_get_entity` (`weave_update_field` when editing).
- **Live.** The text follows the expression and the name box as they are typed, and every chip insertion.
- **Pure.** `agentRecipe({table, field, expression, edit})` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` returns `{cli: [{note, cmd}], mcp, text}`. Shell quoting is single quotes with `'\''` for an embedded quote; a name with a space is quoted; `<name>` and `<expression>` stand in for what is not typed yet and stay bare.

Same pattern later for selects, workflows, relations: the field dialog grows one shared "as an agent" footer.

## Gates

- `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`: add vs edit recipes, the MCP sequence, shell and JSON quoting, placeholders.
- `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`: the footer is on the page closed, opens, carries the three lines and the MCP line, and follows a renamed field.

Design review: formulabuilder.html, direction C. Follows Feature #204 (chips that teach) and #195 (the check step).

features.name: Formula scan preview: a typed verdict, scan over up to 200 rows for null and error counts, a row cycler in the dialog, the number costume only for a numeric result
features.description:
One preview row is proof the formula parses; it is not proof it is right. A formula valid on row 1 and null on a third of the table is exactly the bug one preview row cannot show.

## What shipped

- **`type` on every verdict.** `checkFormula` names what the preview computed to: `number`, `text`, `boolean`, `list`, `null`, `error`.
- **`scan: true`.** One extra engine pass over up to 200 rows returns `scan: {rows, capped, nulls, errors, sampleByOutcome: {ok, null, error}}` — each sample names its row (`entity`, `id`; `error` carries the message), and `type` then comes from the rows that computed, not the first row alone. The numbers an agent asserts against before saving.
- **Every door.** `weave_check_formula {scan: true}`, `POST /api/tables/:id/formula-check {scan: true}`, `weave formula check <table> '<expr>' --scan`. The agent-surface gate now reads `checkFormula`'s signature and fails when an option is missing from the MCP schema, the CLI flags or the route.
- **The dialog.** The verdict line wears a typed badge; under it a row cycler (`‹ row n of N — "name" ›`) steps the preview through the first 200 rows, and `⚠ 2 rows → null · 1 → #ERR` reports the scan. The **Result format** (number costume) section renders only when the result type is a number — and stays for a table with no rows to type it on.
- **Found on the way:** `dateadd()` on an empty date returned the epoch shifted (Issue #237) — fixed, null in, null out.

## Gates

- `test/formula-check.test.mjs`: type per verdict; scan counts, samples and dominant type; the 200-row cap and `capped`; no scan block on an invalid expression or without the option; REST accepts `scan`.
- `test/agent-surface.test.mjs`: every `checkFormula` option reaches every door, and AGENTS.md says what scan returns.
- `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`: the badge and the costume following the type; the cycler stepping and wrapping; the scan note staying while stepping.
- `test/formula.test.mjs`: Issue #237.

Design review: formulabuilder.html, direction B. Follows Features #204, #205, #195.

features.name: Formula autocomplete: [ offers fields and two letters offer functions in a popover at the caret, keyboard-driven, no editor dependency
features.description:
Chips are discovery; typing is speed. Once the vocabulary is known, `[` should offer fields and two letters should offer functions, drawn from the same two lists the chips draw from, ranked by prefix. Misspelled field names die at the keystroke instead of at the check; the verdict line stays live underneath — the two mechanisms answer different moments.

## What shipped

- **`formulaSuggest(text, caret, fields, selfName)`** in `public/field-dialog-core.js`: an unclosed `[` before the caret offers every readable field (documents, attachments and the field being edited left out) whose name starts with what follows the bracket; otherwise a word of two or more letters under the caret offers the functions that start with it, alphabetically, each with its signature. A closed bracket, an opened call, one letter or no match offer nothing.
- **`formulaApply(text, suggestion, item)`**: rewrites the word under the caret with the pick and says where the caret lands — inside a call's parens.
- **The popover** (`.fx-ac` in `app.js`): positioned at the caret from a hidden mirror div wearing the textarea's font, padding and width — no contenteditable, no editor dependency. ↑ ↓ move the selection, Return (or Tab) picks, Escape closes the popover and stops there (the tray stays open). A mouse pick runs on mousedown so the textarea keeps focus and its caret; blur closes it.

## Gates

- `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`: bracket mode (prefix, bare, closed, excluded and self left out), function mode (two letters, one letter, opened call, no match, the word under a mid-text caret), and the rewrite + caret landing.
- `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`: the popover opens on `[` with readable fields only, narrows as letters follow, ↓ + Return picks and closes, the popover sits at the caret; two letters list functions with their signatures, ↑ ↓ move, Escape keeps the text and the tray, Return lands the caret inside the parens.

Design review: formulabuilder.html, direction D. Reuses the catalog from Feature #204; follows #205, #206, #195.

features.name: Auth ladder: passkey sign-in first, scoped API tokens second
features.description:
## Pain Point

Weave has one door for people and agents alike: a `wv_` bearer token minted once by `grantKey` (src/engine.js ~2041–2104), stored as a sha256, switched on per workspace by `requireAuth`. A person opening weave in a browser has no way to sign in that does not involve pasting a secret. The task applet grew its own numeric passcode for the same reason. Kyle's phone note names the order he wants: passkeys for humans, then API tokens as a typed, scoped credential.

## Problem Statement

* No human-grade sign-in exists. Every browser session is either open (`requireAuth` off) or needs a pasted token.
* Tokens are one kind. There is no distinction between a person's session, an agent's long-lived key, and a one-off share grant ([[Feature#194]] is designing the third).
* [[Feature#141]] §3 (Auth) is still an Open-questions block. This request is the concrete answer Kyle wants recorded for it.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Passkeys (WebAuthn) as the human sign-in.** Registration on first visit when `requireAuth` is on; the credential public key lands on the account row that [[Feature#141]] §2 introduces. No passwords, ever. The Browser pane in the harness cannot do passkeys (known), so the agent-browser named-session path stays the automation door.
* **API tokens become a typed credential with a scope.** Keep `wv_` as the prefix; add `type` (person-session, agent-key, share-grant) and `scope` (workspace, space, table, entity; read or write) at mint time. `resolveKey` returns the scope so routes can refuse out-of-scope calls.
* **Order of work:** passkey registration + sign-in on the existing account rows → token typing → scope enforcement in src/routes.js. The task applet passcode retires once passkeys work on iOS Safari (they do, from the Home-Screen icon too).
* Design belongs in [[Feature#141]]; this row tracks the build.

## Source

* uno Task #57 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Weave passkey auth then api token type"

## Verify

* With `requireAuth` on, a fresh browser registers a passkey and lands on the workspace without typing a token.
* A minted agent key carries `type` and `scope`; a call outside its scope returns 403 with the one error contract from [[Feature#179]].
* Existing `wv_` keys keep working (typed as agent-key, scope = workspace) — no re-mint.

features.name: Cloud backup of weave: scheduled off-machine copies, restorable in one command
features.description:
## Pain Point

Everything weave holds lives in `~/.weave/` on one MacBook: one `.db` per workspace (WAL mode), `files/` for attachments, `keystore.json` + `keystore.key` for credentials. The only backups are ad-hoc (`weave.db.seed-backup-2026-08-28` sitting beside the live file) and the JSON export in `weave export`, which the Handbook itself warns drops attachments when taken alone. A lost or wiped laptop loses the whole self-referential record: Issues, Features, Handbook, uno tasks.

## Problem Statement

* No scheduled backup exists. Nothing leaves the machine.
* A correct backup is three things together: a WAL-checkpointed `.db` per workspace, the `files/` tree, and the keystore pair. Copying the `.db` mid-write without a checkpoint yields a torn file.
* Restore is undocumented. There is no `weave backup` / `weave restore` verb in bin/weave.js (verbs today: account, activity, audit, … workspace).

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **`weave backup` verb** in bin/weave.js: `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` per workspace, then tar the `.db` files, `files/`, and the keystore pair into one timestamped archive. Encrypt with the keystore key or an age recipient before it leaves the machine, because `keystore.json` is in it.
* **Destination:** an R2 bucket or a Cloudflare-hosted instance's storage ([[Feature#84]] already reserves the hosting decision). Ponytail ladder: `rclone` to R2 is a one-liner once the archive exists; write no upload code.
* **Schedule:** a launchd job, nightly, keeping 7 daily + 4 weekly. The harness already runs `ai.grunion.weave` and `ai.grunion.weave-uno-pull` under launchd; a third plist is the established pattern.
* **`weave restore <archive>`**: stops nothing, writes into an empty data dir, refuses a non-empty one. The hub adopts dropped `.db` files on the first `/w/<name>/` hit, so no restart.
* Report the last successful backup on `/api/health` so a stale backup is visible where staleness is already checked.

## Source

* uno Task #61 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Cloud backup of weave"

## Verify

* `weave backup` produces an archive; `sqlite3 <db> 'PRAGMA integrity_check'` on the extracted files returns `ok`.
* `weave restore` into an empty dir brings up every workspace with entity counts equal to the source's `/api/health` entities map.
* `/api/health` carries `lastBackupAt`; a nightly run older than 36 h shows as stale.

features.name: Notifications: unread vs delivered, focus modes, batch delivery, OS push to iPhone and Mac
features.description:
## Pain Point

Weave has no notifications. A change to a row Kyle cares about (a comment, a state move, an assignment on uno Task) is invisible until he opens the page. Three phone notes on the night of 2026-09-06/07 circle the same gap from three sides: the difference between "unread" and "delivered", focus modes with batched delivery, and getting a team message to surface as a real OS notification on the iPhone or the laptop.

## Problem Statement

* No notification primitive exists in src/engine.js. The word appears only in the MCP JSON-RPC handler and the icon alias table.
* The activity log (Feature #14 audit, [[Feature#174]] table activity panel) records events but nobody is subscribed to them.
* "Unread" (state on the reader's side) and "delivered" (a transport fact) are different things and a single boolean conflates them, which is how every inbox ends up with 400 unread items nobody will act on.
* Focus modes are a per-person preference, and weave keeps preferences on fields, not users (settled rule). The design has to say where a focus mode lives once [[Feature#141]] gives weave a person.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Two facts per notification, not one:** `deliveredAt` (transport) and `readAt` (the reader). A digest batch sets `deliveredAt` on many rows at once; opening the entity sets `readAt`.
* **Subscriptions as rows.** A system `Subscription` table: who, what (entity, table, space, or a saved view's filter), which events (comment, state change, assignment, mention via `[[…]]` / `#` references from [[Feature#164]]).
* **Focus modes = a delivery schedule on the subscription**, not a user setting: immediate, batched at fixed times (a "work focus" window), or muted. This keeps the preferences-on-fields rule intact.
* **Transports, in ladder order:** in-app bell with the unread count first; then email (reuse whatever [[Feature#216]] lands); then OS push. For OS push, the cheapest working path is an Apple Shortcut or ntfy.sh topic the phone already subscribes to — one HTTP POST per delivery, no APNs certificate. Native APNs only if ntfy proves insufficient.
* Batch delivery renders one message per batch listing the rows, each a permalink ([[Feature#203]]).

## Source

* uno Task #52 (2026-09-06, phone capture, verbatim): "Unreng ntotifqctions vs delicered in batch"
* uno Task #63 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Worl ficus modes and notifivation batches"
* uno Task #62 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "How to make sure i get trams messages iwth apply sustem notifcatjon iphone of laptop"

## Verify

* A comment on a uno Task Kyle is subscribed to appears in the bell within one page load, unread; opening the task clears it; `deliveredAt` and `readAt` are distinct columns in the API read.
* A subscription set to a batch window delivers nothing before the window and one digest at it.
* One ntfy (or Shortcut) push lands on the iPhone and the Mac from a single event, with a permalink that opens the row.

features.name: Integrations as agents: one prompt-defined agent per external system, on the cheapest capable model
features.description:
## Pain Point

Every integration weave has today is hand-written middleware: `scripts/weave-uno-pull.mjs` (worker → local), `scripts/uno-fibery-sync-run.mjs` (uno → Fibery), the underchat→Fibery webhook worker. Each one is a bespoke diff-and-push loop that breaks when either side's schema moves. Kyle's note proposes the alternative: each integration is an agent, defined by a prompt, that reads this workspace and the external system through their APIs and keeps them aligned. The prompt names the cheapest model that can do the job. He also names the meta-need: a Context7-style alternative that builds *maintainable* middleware rather than a pile of one-off scripts.

## Problem Statement

* Integration code is duplicated per pair (uno↔Fibery, worker↔local, …) and none of it is a weave concept; weave cannot list its own integrations.
* Field mapping lives in JS id maps (the Workstream id table in uno-fibery-sync.mjs). Adding a select option means editing code.
* Weave already speaks MCP (src/mcp.js) and has a full HTTP API, so the workspace side of every integration is solved. The external side and the reconciliation loop are what vary.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **An `Integration` table (system space, like Automations).** Columns: external system, prompt (document), model (select: haiku / sonnet / opus / local), schedule, scope (which tables), last run, last verdict, credential (the [[Feature#143]] credential field, so keys never sit in the prompt).
* **Run = one agent invocation** with two toolsets: weave's own MCP server for this workspace, and the external system's MCP or CLI (Fibery has a CLI; GitHub has `gh`; Front and Slack have MCPs). The prompt is the mapping, written in words, versioned like any document.
* **Cheapest-model routing is a column, not a default.** A field-mapping sync runs on Haiku; conflict resolution escalates to Sonnet by the prompt's own instruction.
* **Maintainability rule:** the agent never writes code into the repo. It writes a run log row and, when the mapping drifts, a proposed prompt edit for Kyle to accept. This is the "Context7 alternative": the maintained artifact is the prompt plus the run history, not middleware.
* **Migration:** rewrite uno→Fibery sync as the first Integration row; keep the script until three consecutive agent runs match its output.

## Source

* uno Task #54 (2026-09-06, phone capture, verbatim): "Each ontegratjoj is, agent. Build an intergration vetween fhis worjspace and X. Superion learning agentis spellcheck wiroaac and X. Per integration prompt fore cheapest agent. Conteft 7 alrernative the builds maintainable kiddleware"

## Verify

* An Integration row with a prompt and a schedule runs on time, and its run log row records model, token cost, and a diff summary.
* The uno→Fibery Integration reproduces the launchd script's next push byte-for-byte on Fibery (same rows touched, same field values) for three days.
* Changing a Workstream option in uno needs no code change; the next run maps it or files a proposed prompt edit.

features.name: Doors into weave: sign in with GitHub, Slack, Claude or email; publish pages; iMessage and Apple Shortcuts as capture inlets
features.description:
## Pain Point

Kyle's note is a list of doors, written as one line: "Auth claude github slack email share publish pages imessage? Apple shortcuts built in business imessage". Read as a menu: which identity providers weave should accept, which surfaces it should publish to, and which inlets should feed it. Today the only inlet from the phone is the task applet behind a passcode, and the only publish surface is one saved-view share link ([[Feature#17]]).

## Problem Statement

* Identity: no provider sign-in. Passkeys ([[Feature#208]]) cover a device; a GitHub or Slack identity covers a person across devices and is what a collaborator will already have.
* Publishing: a document, an entity page, or a table cannot be handed to someone as a page. [[Feature#194]] designs the grant; this row asks for the rendered public page as a product surface.
* Capture: the fastest thought-to-row path on iOS is a Shortcut (one Open URLs action today). iMessage has a Business Chat / Messages for Business inlet that could accept a line of text with no app open at all.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Providers via OIDC, behind [[Feature#141]]'s account row:** GitHub first (Kyle and every collaborator have one), Slack second, email magic-link third. "Claude" as a provider means accepting an Anthropic-issued identity if one exists; until then, Claude reaches weave as an agent key, not a person.
* **Publish pages:** a `Publish` action on entity, document, and table that mints a [[Feature#194]] grant and serves a read-only render at a stable URL. Same renderer as the entity page with editing chrome removed; no bespoke HTML like the view share link.
* **Apple Shortcuts inlet:** a documented `POST /w/<ws>/api/tables/<table>/entities` recipe with a scoped token ([[Feature#208]] scopes) so a Shortcut can create a row with Share Sheet text; the applet's passcode door stays until then.
* **iMessage inlet:** Messages for Business needs an Apple registration and a CSP; park it as a design note unless a BlueBubbles-style bridge (already planned for ChatAdvance's funding wizard) can forward a text to the same POST. Ship the Shortcut inlet first; it covers the same gesture.

## Source

* uno Task #60 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Auth claude github slack email share publish pages imessage? Apple shortvuts built in business imessage"

## Verify

* Sign in with GitHub lands on an account row; the audit log names the GitHub login as actor.
* A published document renders at its public URL for a logged-out browser, and unpublishing returns 404 within one request.
* A Share Sheet Shortcut creates a uno Task from selected text with no app switch.

features.name: Native key store: credential values live in the OS keychain, not keystore.json
features.description:
## Pain Point

Credentials weave holds ([[Feature#143]]'s credential field, the `key` type before it) are written to `~/.weave/keystore.json`, encrypted with the sibling `keystore.key`. Both files sit in the same directory, so anyone who can read the data dir can read every secret. The harness rule for everything else on this machine is "secrets go to Keychain, never into a vendored file", and `portable-sync.mjs` refuses to vendor a file that matches a secret pattern. Weave is the one exception, by accident.

## Problem Statement

* Key + ciphertext side by side is obfuscation, not protection.
* A cloud backup ([[Feature#209]]) has to carry `keystore.json` to be restorable, which means the archive is as sensitive as the secrets.
* The engine's key API (`setKey`, `hasKey`, `resolveKey`, `revealKey`, `grantKey`, `revokeKey`, `deleteKey` in src/engine.js) is already a narrow seam, so the storage behind it can change without touching callers.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **A store interface with two implementations:** `file` (today's pair, kept for Linux servers and CI) and `keychain` (macOS `security` CLI via `child_process`, one item per key named `weave:<workspace>:<key>`). Pick by platform, override with `WEAVE_KEYSTORE=file|keychain`.
* **Migration verb** `weave key migrate --to keychain`: moves every item, verifies a round-trip read, then deletes the file pair. Reverse direction supported for moving off the Mac.
* **Backups stop carrying secrets.** With keychain storage the archive holds only key *names*; restore prompts for values, matching the harness's MANIFEST "keychain" row convention.
* Zero new dependencies: `security add-generic-password` / `find-generic-password -w` are the whole integration. A Linux `secret-tool` implementation is a later row if a server ever needs it.

## Source

* uno Task #65 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Native weave integration to key store"

## Verify

* After migration, `ls ~/.weave/` shows no `keystore.*`; `security find-generic-password -s weave:<ws>:<key> -w` returns the value; `weave key reveal` returns the same.
* The engine key test suite passes against both implementations (parameterised, same cases).
* A backup archive taken after migration contains no secret material (grep for the known test value returns nothing).

features.name: Subtable filters: the eye on a relation subtable filters its referenced rows in place
features.description:
## Pain Point

An entity page shows each relation as a subtable of the referenced rows. A Project with sixty Tasks shows all sixty; there is no way to narrow it to open ones without leaving the page for the Task table and building a filter there. The table-level eye (Feature #114) shows and hides fields and deleted rows, and table filters became fields on the Tables row ([[Feature#149]]), so both halves of the mechanism exist. Neither reaches the subtable.

## Problem Statement

* Subtables render the relation's full target set. No filter, no sort, no field choice, and no eye button on the subtable header.
* The reader's intent is almost always a slice: open tasks, this month's activities, unshipped features.
* Where the filter is stored has to follow the preferences-on-fields rule: the subtable's slice is a property of the *relation field*, so every Project's Task subtable shares one configuration, and one edit fixes all of them.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Reuse the eye.** The subtable header gains the same `eye-btn` (public/app.js ~2840) opening the same field-visibility popover, plus a filter section reusing the Filter editor from the Tables row.
* **Storage on the relation field's config**, next to the existing target and cardinality: `{ subtable: { fields, filter, sort } }`. The engine's field-config table ([[Feature#178]] reuse wave 3) is where that shape belongs.
* **Filter grammar** is the one `query` already accepts (`where` triples), so the subtable is a query over the target table with an implicit `[relationField, "=", thisRow]` clause and the stored filter appended.
* A subtable count in the header shows `shown / total` when a filter is active, so a hidden slice is never mistaken for an empty relation.

## Source

* uno Task #66 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Subtable referenced filter implementstion eve icon"

## Verify

* Set "State != Done" on Project→Tasks through the subtable eye; every Project page shows only open tasks and the header reads e.g. `12 / 60`.
* The filter survives reload and is visible in the relation field's config JSON in the field dialog.
* The uno applet and the API are unaffected: `GET /api/entities/<project>` still returns the full relation.

features.name: External references allowed, external relations gated: no permission loops across workspaces
features.description:
## Pain Point

Weave is heading toward cross-workspace and cross-instance access ([[Feature#194]] shares, [[Feature#141]] users). Kyle's note draws the line before the first cross-workspace link exists: a *reference* to something outside the workspace is fine; a *relation* to it is not, unless the outside side has granted permission, because an unchecked relation lets read access on one side pull open write access on the other and loop back through the relation's inverse.

## Problem Statement

* Relations are symmetric in weave: creating A→B writes the inverse on B. Across a workspace boundary that means workspace A can mutate workspace B's rows by linking to them.
* Today relations are confined to one `.db` so the problem cannot happen. The moment [[Feature#194]] lets an instance read another's entities, a relation field targeting a remote table would be the first request, and it is the wrong first request.
* Permission loops: A grants B read, B links to A's rows, A's inverse field now carries B's identifiers, A's readers see B's rows, B's readers see A's readers' view. No single grant authorised that.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Two link kinds, named in the engine.** `reference`: a one-way pointer (a permalink from [[Feature#203]] plus a cached chip render) that writes nothing on the target; allowed to any URL the reader can fetch, including other workspaces and instances. `relation`: the existing symmetric field; its target must be in the same workspace, or in a workspace whose grant explicitly includes `relate` as a verb.
* **Grant verbs** in [[Feature#194]] become: read, write, relate. `relate` is never implied by write.
* **Chips already know the difference.** The pointer tier (outline + ↗) renders a reference; the value tier renders a relation. No new chip style.
* **Engine check** in `createRelation` / `updateField`: a target outside the workspace without a `relate` grant is refused with the one error contract ([[Feature#179]]). Document the rule in the Handbook relations page so the agent surface gate sees it.

## Source

* uno Task #67 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "External references okay but not external relatikns without permisjsons to avoid looped open permission cirsuit"

## Verify

* A document in workspace A can hold a chip pointing at an entity in workspace B; B's row shows no inbound change and B's audit log is empty.
* Creating a relation field in A targeting a table in B fails with a named error until B's grant includes `relate`; with it, the inverse appears in B and B's audit log records A as actor.
* A read-only grant from A to B cannot be escalated to writes on A by any sequence of links from B (test: attempt the loop, assert A's rows unchanged).

features.name: Email out of weave: native send with delivery management, or a Front integration
features.description:
## Pain Point

Weave can store an email address (the `email` type renders a `mailto:` link) and automations can fire outgoing webhooks, but nothing sends mail. Every notification, share, or digest that ends in an inbox has to go through a harness script and `gws`. Kyle's two notes, twenty minutes apart, name both shapes: native email send with management of what was sent, or an integration with Front so a team inbox is the send-and-track surface.

## Problem Statement

* No transport. src/ has no SMTP, no sendmail, no provider client.
* No record. Even if a script sends on weave's behalf, the sent message is not a row, so nothing links it to the entity it was about.
* Two real consumers are queued behind this: notifications ([[Feature#210]]) and published-page sharing ([[Feature#212]]).
* Front is a paid team inbox with an API and a webhook feed; if the team runs on it, sending from weave without it splits the conversation record.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **A `Message` system table** either way: to, from, subject, body (document), related entity, status (queued / sent / delivered / bounced / opened), provider id. Sending is an automation action (`send email`) beside the existing webhook action, so rules can send.
* **Transport, ladder order.** Cloudflare Email Routing is already live for grunion.ai and it can send via Workers; a Resend/Postmark API key in the credential field is the second rung. Both are one HTTPS call, no SMTP library. Delivery events come back through the existing automation webhook inlet and update the Message row.
* **Front as an alternative transport**, not a second feature: a Front API key makes `send email` post a message to a Front conversation, and Front's webhook updates the same Message row. Choosing Front is a select on the workspace's mail settings row.
* Keep provider names out of the engine: one `MailTransport` interface, provider modules under src/mail/.

## Source

* uno Task #68 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Native email send managemeny"
* uno Task #64 (2026-09-07, phone capture, verbatim): "Front integration"

## Verify

* An automation "on state → Review, send email to Assignee" produces a Message row, a real email in the inbox, and a `delivered` status within a minute.
* Switching the transport select to Front sends the same rule's mail through Front and the Message row carries the Front conversation id.
* A bounce arrives as a webhook and flips the row to `bounced`; the entity page shows it in the Activity panel.

**2026-10-03, invite emails landed (mail-216 session).** Gerrit 572 `941fa77`: `src/mail.js` holds the two approved emails (`inviteEmail`, `inviteAcceptedEmail`: subject, preheader, html, text, copy word for word from the design review), the weave lockup as PNG at `/brand/email-lockup-{light,dark}.png` (Gmail strips SVG), light styles inline and a dark block under `prefers-color-scheme`, and the Architect-only preview `GET /api/mail/preview/invite|accepted` (`?role=`, `?theme=`). Gerrit 573 `7585a77`: `src/mail-send.js`, one `fetch` POST to `api.resend.com/emails`, off unless `WEAVE_MAIL_KEY` and `WEAVE_MAIL_FROM` are both set; `POST /api/invites` emails the typed address and answers `mailed: true|false` (`mailError` on a failed send, the invite is made either way); Members says Emailed or shows the link. Shipped in **v0.4.62** (release change 579, merge `93979c5`, tag v0.4.62 Latest). :4400 runs 0.4.62; weave.grunion.ai swapped to v0.4.62 at 20:12:48Z with signed-out `/` 302, `/api/tables` 401, preview 401 signed out and 200 HTML with the `deploy-check` token. Gates: change 573 patch set 4 2464/0 node and 1008 browser (one flake, green on retry); release 2479/0 node, 1027/0 browser. Screenshots (600 and 375 px, light and dark): `~/Documents/queue/weave-invite-emails/`. Still open: a Resend account, the sending domain and its SPF/DKIM DNS, the API key into Railway (`WEAVE_MAIL_KEY`, `WEAVE_MAIL_FROM`; mail is off in production until then), and Kyle's decision on the accepted notice (drop it, keep the inviter's address on the invite until it is used, or show it in-app), since weave keeps no account email (Feature #252). The Message table, delivery status and Front transport in this Feature's shape are not started.

features.name: Autosave everywhere: a pending-save glyph, tap to flush, no Save buttons
features.description:
## Pain Point

Field edits in weave save on blur or Enter through `editorFor` (public/app.js ~2268: PATCH, then a "Saved" toast). Documents save on their own cadence in the Vditor editor. Some surfaces still have explicit commit gestures, and the toast is the only signal, appearing after the fact. Kyle's note asks for the opposite contract on every surface: autosave is the rule, a small clock glyph shows a save is pending, and a tap on it (or Escape) forces the flush. Nothing has a Save button.

## Problem Statement

* Save behaviour differs by surface: grid cells, entity page fields, the document editor, the field dialog, the applet. A user has to learn each one.
* The "Saved" toast fires per field and stacks; during a burst of edits it is noise, and it never says what is *not yet* saved.
* On the phone the blur that triggers a save may never come (iOS keeps the field focused across a background), so an edit can sit unsaved until the tab dies.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **One save queue** in public/app.js: every editor pushes `{ entityId, field, value }`; the queue debounces 600 ms per key, PATCHes in order, retries once on failure, and exposes `pending` count.
* **One glyph, top right of the header:** hidden when idle, a Lucide `clock` while pending, a tick for two seconds after a flush, red `alert` if a PATCH failed. Tapping it flushes immediately. `visibilitychange → hidden` also flushes, which closes the iOS gap.
* **Toasts retire** for successful saves; they remain for errors.
* The field dialog and the document editor join the queue rather than owning their own save path; the applet keeps its own because it has one field.

## Source

* uno Task #51 (2026-09-06, phone capture, verbatim): "Clock or tap off autosave everywhere"

## Verify

* Edit four cells quickly; exactly one glyph shows, no toasts, four PATCHes land in order (network panel), then the tick.
* Kill the server, edit a cell: red glyph, tap it after restart, the edit lands.
* Background Safari on iOS mid-edit; `GET /api/entities/<id>` shows the new value within one second.

features.name: Editor toolbar parity study: compare peer markdown editors and Fibery, mock the target toolbar
features.description:
## Pain Point

The document editor is Vditor in instant-render mode (Feature #45), with a toolbar and outline panel ([[Feature#151]]) and a selection bubble ([[Feature#154]]). Kyle's phone note asks for the comparison that never happened: put the weave toolbar beside Fibery's and the comparable markdown editors, and mock the version weave should have. The toolbar shipped from the Vditor default set, not from a decision.

## Problem Statement

* The current toolbar is Vditor's, trimmed. Which controls earn a slot was never argued; Fibery's toolbar is the reference Kyle uses daily and its control set is different (blocks, mentions, tables, embeds first; marks in the bubble).
* Two toolbars exist (header + bubble) and their division of labour is inherited, not designed.
* No mockup artifact exists for the editor the way chip-card-anatomy.html exists for chips.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

* **Survey, five editors:** Fibery, Notion, Obsidian, Milkdown, TipTap's default. One table: control, where it lives (top bar, bubble, slash menu), keyboard shortcut. Output as a Wiki article in the weave workspace.
* **Mockup page** `docs/editor-toolbar.html` in the style of chip-card-anatomy.html: three variants (A minimal top bar + rich bubble; B Fibery-style block menu + bubble; C slash-only, no top bar) rendered over the same sample document, both themes.
* **Decision with Kyle**, then the build is a follow-on Feature; this row ends at the chosen variant.
* Constraint carried from [[Feature#151]]: no editor dependency beyond vendored Vditor; the toolbar is weave's own DOM over Vditor's commands.

## Source

* uno Task #35 (2026-08-30, phone capture, verbatim): "Compravle md editors ovisitsn fibery tool bar mock io"

## Verify

* Wiki article exists with the five-editor control table.
* `docs/editor-toolbar.html` renders A/B/C in light and dark; screenshots attached to this row.
* Row Description carries the chosen variant and the follow-on Feature link.

features.name: Registry lives at the weave root, not as a 'Workspace' space inside every workspace
features.description:
## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-08)

The system registry — Spaces, Tables, Fields, Workflows as rows — should exist once, under the weave root (the hub that lists workspaces), not as a system space called **Workspace** inside each workspace (uno, test, weave…). Today `#ensureMetaTables` (src/engine.js ~L2378) mints that space per workspace file; `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` L42 already records that the Workspace level is the one level with no registry row.

## Shape

- Root hub gets the registry: `Workspaces` (one row per workspace file, the missing level-1 row), `Spaces`, `Tables`, `Fields`, `Workflows` — each row carrying a **Workspace** relation so rows from uno and test sit side by side. Opening a row deep-links into that workspace (`/w/<id>/#/space/…`).
- User workspaces stop growing a `Workspace` system space. Their sidebar shows only their own spaces. Registry-row writes (rename/reorder/filter as fields, Issues #126 #212 #233) keep working through the root rows, routed to the owning workspace's engine.
- Per-workspace API surface stays (`/w/<id>/api/spaces` etc.); the entity-door interception (`#interceptUpdate`/`#interceptDelete`) moves to the hub.
- Migration: existing workspaces drop the system space on next load (tombstone, not purge, until the root registry has synced); Handbook page updated (the Handbook gate).

## Not

Not a rename of the `Workspace` space. Not per-workspace registry with a root mirror.

## Open questions for the design pass

- Where does the root registry persist — `hub` state file vs derived on the fly from each workspace's `state`? (derived = no second source of truth; Kyle's earlier ruling: referencesFrom is computed, never stored.)
- Cloudflare worker (`src/worker.js`, store-cf) has one workspace per deployment — root == that workspace; keep it working.
- MCP tools that read the registry (`src/mcp.js`).

## Verify

1. `/` root shows the registry tables with a Workspace column; `uno` sidebar has no `Workspace` space.
2. Rename a table from a root Tables row → the uno table renames.
3. All suites green, `# skipped 0`; Handbook has the page; ONTOLOGY.md L42 updated.



## Design (session-builder, 2026-09-08)

**Where the registry lives.** In the hub root's engine — the default workspace (`weave` at `/` on :4400; the DO's one engine on the CF worker; a bare `new Weave()`). The root keeps its `Workspace` system space and grows a **Workspaces** table (system `workspaces`, one row per workspace file, `sysId = meta.id`, the root's own row included). Spaces, Tables, Fields and Workflows each gain a system **Workspace** relation (many-to-one → Workspaces), so rows from uno and test sit side by side under one column.

**Persisted as a projection, derived from structure — not a second source of truth.** The rows are real entities in the root engine, because every behaviour riding on them (#126 config-as-fields, #175/#212 view fields, #233 rollup footers, relations that target registry rows, entity views, the grid) reads entities; a virtual table would need a second read path through query, grid, entity view and rollups. The truth is each workspace's `state.spaces / state.tables / table.fields`. The root rows are re-asserted by the owning engine's structural verbs (the intra-engine sync pattern, lifted one level), `registryReport` names drift and `rebuildRegistry` rebuilds from structure. A hub state file was rejected: it would be a third store. Per-workspace registry rows no longer exist.

**Membership.** `member.joinRegistry(root)`, called by `createWorkspaceHub` on every adopted or created workspace. The member persists `meta.registry = 'hub'`, mints nothing, tombstones a legacy local `Workspace` space (`deletedAt` on the space and its four tables — rows kept, never purged), re-creates its space rollups on the root Spaces table (a name clash gets ` (<workspace>)`), then syncs its Workspaces row and Spaces/Tables/Fields rows into the root. A `maybeRefresh` that actually reloads (CLI writing beside the server) re-syncs. `root.hostRegistry()` is the inverse for the engine the hub stands on. Every `#sysTable/#sysRow/#sysField` helper reads `this.registryHost ?? this`.

**Write routing.** The entity-door intercepts (`#interceptCreate/Update/Delete`, restore) run only in the root, the one engine with system tables. The owner of a row is the engine whose `meta.id` equals the sysId of the row's Workspace row (`root.members`); the intercept calls that engine's structural verb and the verb's own sync writes the row back. A Spaces create names its Workspace (default: the root); Tables and Fields creates inherit the parent row's workspace.

**Cross-workspace `via`.** Table ids are uuids, so `#tableAnywhere(id)` resolves a table across root + members; a space rollup on the root Spaces row reads the owner engine's rows and still answers only on the row of the space that holds the table. Deleting a member table drops its via-rollups on the root.

**Surfaces.** Registry rows carry `sysWorkspaceId`; `registryHref` deep-links `/w/<id>/#/table|space/<sysId>` when the row belongs elsewhere. A member's `describeSchema` has no Workspace space, so its sidebar is clean; the app loads the root registry schema (`GET /api/schema`, unprefixed) for the Σ footer, the space tiles and the space-page grid, and writes registry rows through the root API. `/w/<id>/api/registry` reports the member's slice. MCP `weave_registry` on a member delegates the same way. CF worker: a single-member hub whose root is the engine — unchanged.
