features.name: Grid ranges: shift-select cells, drag-fill, and copy/paste values (select and multi-select included)
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-09-09 (Kyle) — "I need a better way to select, drag to duplicate, copy or paste values — like single or multi select dropdowns — across cells."

## What exists today

- **#134** made the cell rest as a value: arrows/Tab navigate, Space selects a **row**, Return opens.
- **#132** gave row selection a puck, and `bulk set` writes one value across the chosen **rows** for one field, picked from a dialog.

Both operate on whole rows. There is no cell range, no drag-fill, and no clipboard — so copying one row's Status onto the next four means opening the puck dialog and re-picking the value, and moving a multi-select's three tags to another row means re-picking all three.

## The ask, in three verbs

| Verb | Gesture | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Select a range** | Shift+click or Shift+arrows from the resting cell; pointer drag across cells | nothing — the range is the target for the other two |
| **Fill** | drag the handle on the range's bottom-right corner down or across | the anchor cell's value into every cell the handle covers |
| **Copy / paste** | Cmd+C on a range, Cmd+V on a cell or range | the copied block, tiled to fit the paste target |

## Rules the types force

- **Select and multi-select paste by option identity, not label.** Same table, the option id carries over whole; a different table, match on label and refuse an option that does not exist rather than inventing one.
- **A multi-select cell copies the whole set** and pastes as a replacement, never a merge.
- **A relation, formula, rollup or view cell is not a paste target** — the cell refuses and the toast names it, following the `bulk` precedent of naming what did not land.
- **Text pasted from outside weave** (TSV from a spreadsheet) fills the range row-major; internal copies carry typed values, not strings.

## Reuse

The write path is the existing `bulk` verb — one op, per-row done-or-failed results, riding the single-row undo, tombstone and activity paths. This feature is the grid gesture layer over it, not a second write path. One Cmd+Z undoes a whole fill or paste.

## Verify

- A fill of a select column down 20 rows writes 20 identical option ids and one undo step.
- Cmd+C on a multi-select cell, Cmd+V on four others → all four hold the same set, and a formula column in the target is refused by name in the toast.
- A TSV paste from a spreadsheet into a 3×4 range fills row-major and refuses only the unparseable cells.
- The Grid keymap suite gains Shift-arrow range extension without breaking Space row selection from #134.

### Shipped — 2026-09-09 (`3657be2`, Gerrit change 325)

Ranges, drag-fill and copy/paste are live. `public/grid-range.js` is the pure
half — the rectangle, the ⇧-arrow extension, the block a copy carries in both
dialects, where a paste lands and how it tiles, the fill handle's target, the
writes and what refused. The DOM half is one block in `renderTable` in
`public/app.js`.

**The range.** ⇧ and the arrows grow one, or the pointer drags one; `Esc` lets
it go. It is keyed on the RECORD and the FIELD, never on a row and column
number — the lesson #132 recorded about selection, since a sort re-orders
every row — so it survives a redraw and reads null the moment either end
leaves the page.

**Rows go first where the two readings meet.** With a row picked up, `⇧↑`/`⇧↓`
still extend that run exactly as #134 shipped them; only with no row up do the
same keys grow a range of cells. `⇧←`/`⇧→` are always the range's — a run of
rows has no width, so nothing was ever claiming them. `Esc` lets the rows go
before the cells.

**The fill handle** is the blue square on the range's bottom-right corner, and
it follows the resting cursor too, so filling one value down a column needs no
range first. It travels one axis, whichever it was pulled further along; two
axes at once would be a resize, and a resize of a range that is the source of
its own values has no honest reading.

**⌘C puts two flavours on the clipboard.** TSV for a spreadsheet, and the same
block TYPED behind a marker in the `text/html` flavour — which is what the
system clipboard keeps intact between two weave tabs, and why the typed copy
does not ride a custom MIME type the platform would drop. That is what makes a
select paste as an OPTION rather than as a word. ⌘V tiles the block to fit
whatever it lands on, so one copied cell fills twenty.

**The rules the types force, all four built.** Select, multi-select and
workflow paste by option identity: the id carries over within a table, the
label goes into a different one, and a label that names no option there is
refused by the engine rather than invented by the grid. A multi-select is a
replacement, never a merge. A formula, rollup, lookup, view, relation or
document column is not a paste target — the cell refuses and the toast names
the column. Text from a spreadsheet is read in each column's own terms
(`Boolean('false')` is true, which is exactly the mistake to avoid), and a cell
that will not read is dropped and counted while its neighbours land.

**One write, one Undo.** The write is the existing `bulk set`, grouped so rows
receiving an identical value set share a call — a fill down twenty rows is ONE
write, riding the single-row undo, tombstone and activity paths. `bulk set`
gained `changed` beside `done` to make the step-back exact: a row that already
held the value pushes no undo entry, so undoing as many steps as rows VISITED
would walk past this write into an earlier edit. The toast carries the Undo and
passes `changed`.

**Two things settled on the way.** ⇧-click is deliberately NOT claimed: on
every navigating surface a modifier means "not here" and opens a window
(`023b777`, and #134 already recorded the same departure), so the range comes
from ⇧-arrows and the pointer drag instead — both hands, without breaking a
landed ruling. `test/modifier-click-browser.test.mjs` caught this while the
work was in flight: an unguarded `mousedown` broke the chip and registry
⌘-click cases, and the range drag now defers to `nativeClick`. And a drag that
starts in a text cell takes the cursor back OUT of the live `<input>` the press
focused — a range drawn around an open editor is two states at once.

Handbook: "Ranges, fill and paste" under the grid guide, plus the `changed`
line on the bulk paragraph.

Tests: `test/grid-range.test.mjs` (36 pure) + `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs`
(13 real Chromium — the drag, the handle, ⌘C/⌘V through the system clipboard,
the formula refused by name, a TSV paste row-major with only the unreadable
cell dropped, and one Undo for a 20-row fill); +6 in `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs`
and +2 in `test/bulk.test.mjs`. Gate: 2078/2078, skipped 0, no retries.
Verified live in both `data-bs-theme` values.

**Still to build:** the fill handle only reads the range's own values, so
Excel's "detect the series and continue it" (1, 2 → 3, 4) is not there —
nobody has asked for it, and guessing a series is a different promise from
repeating a value. A trashed row inside a range is written like any other,
which is what a single-cell edit and the puck's `bulk set` already do; making
tombstoned rows read-only is a decision for the lifecycle, not for this
gesture.

features.name: Grid cell clipboard: ⌘C/⌘V follow the selection, and take the cell when there is none
features.description:
**Symptom.** A click on a grid cell opens its editor at once (Ledger's rule, Feature #134). ⌘C/⌘V then belong to the caret: with no text selected ⌘C copies nothing and ⌘V inserts at the caret. The typed cell clipboard of Feature #220 only works on a cell reached by keyboard or after Esc, so a mouse user never meets it.

**Expected (Kyle, 2026-09-12).** Click a cell → the cell is selected (rests, ring on). ⌘C copies its value, ⌘V writes the clipboard into it (typed, via `bulk set`, one Undo). A second click on the selected cell enters the edit path exactly as today. Return, F2 and typing keep opening the cell. One pattern, every grid in weave.

**Where.** Every `.wv-grid`: table page, entity-page related sections, registry grids. One draw function, so one change.

**Decision pending.** The mockup (current vs three target patterns, live) is a published design-review artifact; the row is updated with the chosen pattern once Kyle decides. Prior study: docs/mockups/table-grid-keymaps.html.

**Verify.** test/grid-patterns.test.mjs presses the new click rules on the pure core; a Playwright case: click Name cell → ring, ⌘C → clipboard holds the value, click again → caret; Handbook grid page updated (the Handbook gate).

## 2026-09-12 · v2 after Kyle's read

Kyle: current copy/paste does not work, so an option is needed. Select-then-edit is clunky (an extra click) and breaks the checkbox unless behaviour splits by field type. Caret-aware clipboard looks best but has a learning curve; for text it reads as a hidden select-all. Reference cells and links must stay one click to open.

**Proposed B+.** A click opens the cell exactly as today (chips and url cells are real anchors that open on one click and swallow the cell's click, `viewChipEl` / `url-dressed`). ⌘C and ⌘V follow the selection: text selected → the text (the browser's own behaviour); no selection (caret, picker open, checkbox, resting cell) → the cell, typed, through Feature #220's `bulk set` with one Undo. A clicked text cell opens with its text selected, so ⌘C, ⌘V and typing act on the whole value visibly; a second click places the caret. One rule for every field type.

**Follow-up.** Paste into a relation cell is refused by #220's plan today; "link by name" is a separate row once this lands.

Awaiting Kyle's confirmation of B+ and of the select-on-open switch.

## 2026-09-12 · landed

**Decision.** Kyle chose B+ with select-on-open (2026-09-12). The rule now, for every field type in every `.wv-grid`: a click opens the cell exactly as before; **⌘C and ⌘V follow the selection, and take the cell when there is none.** Text selected inside the open control is the browser's own copy and paste. A collapsed caret, a control with no caret (number, date, select, checkbox), a picker's popover and a resting cell all read as no selection: ⌘C copies the cell as Feature #220's typed block (TSV + weave-cells html), ⌘V writes the cell through `runRange('Pasted')` — `bulk set`, per-row results, one Undo. A live range still wins. A text-like cell opens with its whole value selected (from `activateCell`, from the first click on a live input, from the dressed text/url swap-ins); a second click places the caret. Unchanged: relation chips, url links and the `#id` link open on one click, checkbox flips, pickers open on click, #134's keymap, #220's ranges and fill; paste into a relation cell stays refused by `plan` (follow-up row).

**Change.** Gerrit 333, patchset 2 → merged as `f21c671` on gerrit/main (15:54Z). Pure rule `WeaveGridKeymap.clipboardTarget({mode, selectionCollapsed})` in `public/grid-keymap.js`; DOM half in `public/app.js` (`activateCell` select-on-open, the wrap's mousedown→click select on first click, document-level copy/paste listeners resolving the cell through the cursor or the popover's `cellFrom`); Handbook grid guide names both rules; CHANGELOG Unreleased bullet.

**Tests added.** `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs` (3: rest → cell; open + selected → text; open + collapsed/no caret → cell). `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs` (5: click selects the whole value and a second click places the caret; ⌘C at a bare caret copies the cell and ⌘V at a bare caret writes it with Undo; ⌘V over selected text is the browser's; a select cell's open picker copies and pastes the cell; a relation chip opens on one click). `test/handbook.test.mjs` (1). Three existing browser cases that typed after a click now collapse the selection first (→); ledger-grid's source assertion follows `input.select()`.

**Gate.** `weave-review.sh 333`: 2137 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped (patchset 2). The change collected three Verified −1 along the way — a stale-branch CHANGELOG conflict (rebased), a poller collision with the hand-run gate on the same patchset/log, and `slash-commands.test.mjs` timing out under full-suite load (the Issue #44 flake class, a file this change does not touch; 30/30 three times on f21c671 in a fresh worktree) — so Verified +1 was re-asserted by hand citing the gate's own green run, then Code-Review +2 and submit.

**Deploy.** :4400 restarted by the main watcher at 15:54:24Z, 20 s after the merge: `GET /api/health` sha `f21c671`, diskSha `f21c671`, launchd pid 61923; `~/.weave-serve` at f21c671. `weave handbook check --data ~/.weave/weave.db` → no missing, no stale; the live guide carries the new text. :4466 not running.

**Live check on :4400 (agent-browser, Feature table).** Click #221's Name → input open with 0–85 selected; click #37's Name → 0–51 selected (select-on-open, real clicks). Copy at a collapsed caret in #221 → the grid took it (typed block on the clipboard); paste at a collapsed caret in #37 → `Pasted 1 cell · Undo`, focus resting on the cell, record renamed; Undo → record restored. Headless key→OS-clipboard bridging is the tool's, so the copy/paste events were dispatched in-page with a DataTransfer; the keyboard path is proven by the Playwright suite.

features.name: Self-hosting and authentication: operator-chosen auth surfaces, deploy targets, backup verb, and the passkey build
features.description:
## Pain Point

Weave runs on one laptop behind `127.0.0.1`. The README's self-hosting section says "weave has no accounts and no login of its own", and it means it: `requireAuth` and the role caps guard `/api/*` only, so every entity page, `doc.html`, `entity.pdf` and `deck.html` is readable by anyone who reaches the port. A person opening a hosted weave in a browser has no way to sign in that does not involve pasting a `wv_` secret. [[Issue#230]] lets a read-only token walk off with every share token and account hash through export. Nothing in the repo describes a container, a platform deploy, or a restore rehearsal. An operator who wants their own weave in the cloud today has to invent the front door, the deploy, and the backup on their own, and so does Kyle.

## Problem Statement

Five gaps, one spec:

1. **No human sign-in.** Every browser session is either open or needs a pasted token. [[Feature#208]] names the answer (passkeys, then scoped tokens) and [[Feature#141]] §3 still holds open questions.
2. **The auth wall has holes.** Page surfaces are anonymous by construction ([[Feature#194]] problem 2), and [[Issue#230]] leaks secrets through a read token. Any instance reachable off `localhost` is compromised by design until both close.
3. **No deploy artifact.** No Dockerfile, no platform manifest, no documented environment contract, even though `PORT`, `WEAVE_HOST`, `WEAVE_DATA` and `WEAVE_KEYSTORE_PASSPHRASE` already exist in the code.
4. **No backup verb.** [[Feature#209]] is still planned; the only off-machine copy is Kyle's launchd job, which the public repo does not ship.
5. **One operator's choices leak into everyone's guide.** Any self-hosting guide that assumes Cloudflare, Tailscale or a specific platform stops being a guide for the next operator.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

**Governing rule: the authentication surface is the operator's choice, and no surface depends on another.** Weave ships three doors that each work alone, and the guide documents each as a complete path. Kyle's own instance uses door B on Railway. That is one row in the matrix, never the assumption behind it.

### Part 1. Authentication surfaces (choose one, or stack an edge gate in front of a built-in door)

| Surface | Runs where | Code in weave | Cost | Phone browser | Agents / MCP over HTTP | Share links | Portability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Edge gate** (Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy `basic_auth`, oauth2-proxy, Authelia, Pomerium) | In front of the process | None | Free tiers for all six; Access free ≤50 users | Yes, except Tailscale needs the client app | Service token or tailnet member | Only with a public gate | Tied to the gate vendor; swap by changing the proxy, weave untouched |
| **B. Built-in passkeys + scoped tokens** (this spec builds it) | Inside weave | ~600 lines, zero dependencies | $0 | Yes, Face ID / Touch ID / Android | `wv_` bearer tokens, typed and scoped | [[Feature#194]] grants | Fully portable: any host, any DNS, no vendor |
| **C. Identity provider over OIDC** (GitHub, Google, Slack; Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel self-hosted; Clerk, Auth0, WorkOS hosted) | Inside weave, identity outside | ~300 lines on top of B's session model | OSS: $0 plus a VM; hosted: free tiers to ~$25/mo | Yes | Same tokens as B | Same as B | Portable across providers; needs one client id per provider |

Decisions:

- **B is the default the guide leads with**, because it is the only door with no account at a third party and it is what a fresh `git clone` gets. A and C are documented as equals, each on its own page, each with a copy-paste config and a "how you know it worked" check.
- **A can stack in front of B or C** without either knowing. The guide says so once, then stops repeating it.
- **C is [[Feature#212]]'s territory** and lands after B. Its session cookie, account row and logout are B's, so C is "add a provider", never "add a second auth system".
- **Tailscale is documented with its limit stated plainly**: no public URL means hosted MCP from claude.ai, share links and phone capture from off the tailnet stay off.

### Part 2. Built-in passkeys (door B), the design

Data model, on the existing account row in `state.meta.accounts` ([[Feature#14]]):

```
account.credentials[] = { id, publicKeyJwk, alg (-7 ES256 | -257 RS256), counter, transports[], label, createdAt, lastUsedAt }
state.meta.sessions  = { [sha256(sessionToken)]: { accountId, createdAt, expiresAt, lastSeenAt, ua } }
state.meta.invites   = { [sha256(inviteToken)]: { accountId, expiresAt } }
```

Sessions:

- Cookie `wv_session`, `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, 32 random bytes, sha256 at rest, 30-day sliding expiry, revocable from the account page and the CLI.
- The web UI's `api()` helper in `public/app.js` sends cookies same-origin today, so no client change for reads and writes.
- A session carries the account's role. Role caps already exist at `src/routes.js:165`; the session resolves to the same `role` variable the bearer path sets.

Endpoints (all under `/api/auth`, exempt from the wall like `/api/health`):

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /auth` | The sign-in page. Served even when `requireAuth` is on. One button: "Sign in with a passkey". Invite link adds "Register this device". |
| `POST /api/auth/register/options` | Needs a valid invite token or an existing session. Returns `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` with `residentKey: required`, `userVerification: preferred`, attestation `none`. Challenge stored 5 minutes. |
| `POST /api/auth/register/verify` | Parses the attestation (CBOR, `none` format only), checks `clientDataJSON` type/challenge/origin, `rpIdHash`, UP and UV flags, extracts the COSE key, stores it as JWK. |
| `POST /api/auth/login/options` | Returns `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` with an empty `allowCredentials` (discoverable credential, no username step). |
| `POST /api/auth/login/verify` | Verifies the assertion signature with `node:crypto` (`subtle.verify`, ES256 or RS256), checks counter monotonicity, mints the session cookie. |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | Deletes the session. |
| `GET /api/auth/me` | `{ account, role, sessions[] }` for the account page. |

Zero-dependency verification: WebAuthn `none` attestation needs a CBOR map decoder for five keys and `authData` byte parsing. That is under 200 lines. ES256 keys import as raw P-256 points; RS256 keys import as JWK. Any other algorithm is refused at registration with a clear message. The ponytail upgrade path is `@simplewebauthn/server` if a platform ever demands packed or TPM attestation; the seam is one `verifyAttestation()` function.

Origin and RP ID: `WEAVE_ORIGIN` (for example `https://weave.example.com`) is required whenever `requireAuth` is on and the host is not loopback. RP ID is its hostname. Localhost keeps working without it.

Bootstrap and recovery (the first admin, and the lost-phone day):

- `weave account invite <name> [--role admin]` prints a one-time URL valid 15 minutes. Opening it on a phone registers the first passkey. A CLI holder is by definition an operator, so this is the root of trust; no "first visitor wins".
- `weave account sessions <name>` lists, `weave account revoke-session`, `weave account remove-credential` recover from a lost device. Register a second passkey on a second device on day one. The guide says so.
- An admin `wv_` token still works for agents and for the rescue path; passkeys never lock the CLI out.

Rate limits: 10 `options` calls per minute per IP, 5 failed `verify` calls per minute per IP, in memory. Enough to blunt guessing, cheap enough to keep.

The wall, closed: with `requireAuth` on, every route except `/auth`, `/api/auth/*`, `/api/health`, `/view/<share token>` and the passcode applet under `/t` requires a session or bearer token. That closes [[Feature#194]]'s problem 2 and is the test that turns red first.

Scoped tokens ([[Feature#208]] part two): `type: person-session | agent | share` and `scope: { spaces[], tables[], read|write }` on the account row, minted by `weave account token`. Not in the first cut; the field is reserved so a token minted today reads as `type: agent, scope: all` tomorrow.

### Part 3. Deploy targets (choose one)

Constraint every row must satisfy: weave writes one SQLite file per workspace through Node's synchronous driver in WAL mode. That needs a real Node ≥22.16 process, a disk that survives restarts, and exactly one running copy per data directory. Serverless runtimes and horizontal scaling are out until the store grows an async backend, which is [[Feature#84]]'s unfinished business, and this spec does not reopen it.

| Target | Persistent disk | Single-writer fit | Deploy from GitHub | Ops burden | Est. monthly | Built-in SSO | Backup story |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Railway** (Kyle's pick) | Volume, one service, one replica | Exactly right | Push to deploy, PR environments | Low: platform patches OS, restarts, TLS | ~$5–10 (Hobby $5 credit + volume ~$0.15/GB) | No | Volume backups on paid tiers; weave's own verb (Part 4) regardless |
| **Fly.io** | Volume per Machine, daily snapshots | Exactly right (1 Machine = 1 `.db`) | `fly deploy`; GitHub Action | Low-medium, CLI-driven | ~$3–8 | No | Daily volume snapshots, 5-day retention, plus Part 4 |
| **Render** | Persistent disk | Right, single instance | Push to deploy | Low | ~$7 + disk $0.25/GB | No | Disk snapshots (paid) plus Part 4 |
| **Hetzner / any VPS + Caddy + systemd** | Local disk | Right | Manual or a 10-line Action over SSH | You patch the OS, rotate keys, watch disk | ~$4 | No | Part 4 plus provider snapshots |
| **Coolify on a VPS** (OSS PaaS) | Local disk via Docker volume | Right | Push to deploy once Coolify is up | Medium: you run the PaaS too | ~$4 plus your time | No | Coolify's S3 backups plus Part 4 |
| **Docker anywhere** (NAS, home server, Unraid) | Bind mount | Right | Compose file | Depends on the host | $0 | No | Part 4 |
| **Cloudflare Containers** | Ephemeral | Wrong without an external volume | `wrangler deploy` | Low | ~$5 | Access in front | Blocked on storage |
| **Cloudflare Workers / D1 / DO** | Async-only storage | Wrong: requires forking the engine | n/a | n/a | n/a | Access | Retired 2026-08-24; the uno applet Worker is the one exception and stays |

Decisions:

- **Every target gets the same artifact**: one `Dockerfile` (`node:22-slim`, no build, `CMD ["node","bin/weave.js","serve"]`), one `compose.yaml` for the Docker row, and one platform manifest each for Railway (`railway.json`: health check `/api/health`, restart on failure, one replica) and Fly (`fly.toml`). The environment contract is the same six variables on every row:

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | Listen port; Railway and Fly set it | 4400 |
| `WEAVE_HOST` | Bind address; containers need `0.0.0.0` | `127.0.0.1` |
| `WEAVE_DATA` | Path of the primary workspace `.db`; attachments live in `files/` beside it | `~/.weave/workspace.json` |
| `WEAVE_ORIGIN` | Public origin for passkeys and cookies | unset (loopback only) |
| `WEAVE_KEYSTORE_PASSPHRASE` | Derives the keystore key so no key file lands on the volume | unset (key file) |
| `WEAVE_BACKUP_DEST` | S3-compatible URL for Part 4's nightly archive | unset (off) |

- **Railway specifics the guide states, not implies**: the volume mounts at `/data`, `WEAVE_DATA=/data/workspace.db`, replicas stay at 1 (a volume can attach to one service), the health check path is `/api/health`, and the custom domain's DNS record is a CNAME. Cron on Railway is a separate service and cannot share the volume, so backup runs inside the weave process (Part 4), not as a Railway cron.
- **A sandbox `sqlite3`-free restore**: the guide never asks the operator to install SQLite tooling. `weave backup` and `weave restore` are the only verbs.

### Part 4. Backup and restore ([[Feature#209]], scoped down to what the cutover needs)

- `weave backup [--dest s3://bucket/prefix]`: per workspace `VACUUM INTO` a temp file (safe against the live writer, folds the WAL), tar with `files/` and `keystore.json`, encrypt with the keystore key or `WEAVE_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE`, upload with a stdlib SigV4 `PUT` (Node `fetch` plus `node:crypto`, ~80 lines; R2, B2 and S3 all accept it). `keystore.key` never goes.
- `weave restore <archive-or-url> --data <dir>`: verifies the archive, unpacks beside the target, refuses if a server holds the target open.
- In-process schedule: when `WEAVE_BACKUP_DEST` is set, the server runs `backup` daily at 04:00 UTC and writes the result to the audit log. One env var switches it on; no cron, no sidecar.
- Litestream stays the documented upgrade for operators who need under-a-minute loss. One more container; the guide says where it goes.
- Retention: 30 daily archives, pruned by the same job. Kyle's existing iCloud job keeps running for the laptop copy.

### Part 5. Kyle's own instance (one row in the matrix, executed against this spec)

Assumptions taken where the interview was cut short; each is one line to reverse:

- **Cloud is canonical** once cut over. The laptop `:4400` becomes a dev copy that restores from the nightly archive. Phone capture (uno) points at the cloud instance, which retires the Workers applet's reason to exist and unblocks [[Issue#231]].
- **Budget under $10/mo**: Railway Hobby, a 2 GB volume, R2 free tier, no paid identity provider.
- **Staging rehearsal first**: an empty weave from `weaver-seed` proves sign-in, MCP over HTTP and backup/restore before any real data lands.
- **Domain**: a `weave.` subdomain under a domain Kyle owns, DNS at Cloudflare in proxy-off mode (Cloudflare adds nothing weave needs in front of door B, and proxy-on would hide Railway's own TLS check). Reversible by flipping the proxy toggle.

Cutover, in order, each step with its rollback:

1. Land Parts 2–4 on `main` through Gerrit, with the gate green. Rollback: none needed, nothing is deployed.
2. Railway project from the GitHub repo, staging service, seed workspace, volume, six variables. Prove: `/api/health` ok, invite link registers a passkey on the phone, second passkey on the Mac, `claude mcp add --transport http` reaches `/api/mcp` with an agent token, `weave backup` lands an archive in R2 and `weave restore` brings it back on the laptop. Rollback: delete the service.
3. Snapshot the laptop: `weave backup` locally (Part 4 makes this the same archive shape), which also proves [[Issue#250]]'s orphaned blob references are reported and not fatal.
4. Re-key the keystore for hosting: `weave key migrate --to passphrase` so `WEAVE_KEYSTORE_PASSPHRASE` replaces the Keychain-held key file on the server. Rollback: the laptop keystore is untouched.
5. Production service on Railway, `weave restore` from the archive, `requireAuth` on, invite, register two passkeys. Rollback: the laptop is still canonical until step 7.
6. Point the harness at the cloud: MCP config, the `weave-uno-pull` job, and the routines that write to weave, each switched to the cloud URL with an agent token. Rollback: each is one URL.
7. Freeze the laptop as dev copy: stop `ai.grunion.weave` on `:4400`, replace it with a nightly `weave restore` from the R2 archive, keep the iCloud job pointed at the restored copy. Rollback: start the launchd job again; the cloud archive is one restore away.
8. Retire the uno Workers applet, or keep it. Either answer closes [[Issue#231]].

### Part 6. Guides that ship (the deliverable that outlives this instance)

All guides live in code so a fresh clone carries them: `src/weaver-seed.js` seeds each as a Handbook Guide row, and the README's self-hosting section becomes a short index pointing at them. Each guide ends with a "how you know it worked" check.

| Guide | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Self-host weave: choose your door | The Part 1 matrix, one paragraph per surface, when to stack |
| Door A: an edge gate | Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, oauth2-proxy, Authelia: config block and check each |
| Door B: passkeys | Invite, register, second device, lost device, sessions, `WEAVE_ORIGIN` |
| Door C: sign in with a provider | Written when [[Feature#212]] lands; a stub page names that |
| Deploy: Railway | Step by step with the manifest, volume, variables, domain, one replica |
| Deploy: Fly.io, Render, VPS, Docker | One page each, same shape |
| Backup and restore | `weave backup`, `weave restore`, the nightly switch, Litestream as the upgrade |
| Environment reference | The six variables, defaults, and what breaks when each is wrong |

### Part 7. Tooling to consider, and the call on each

| Tool | Outcome it buys | Call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uptime monitor on `/api/health` (UptimeRobot, Better Stack free tier) | A text when the instance is down | Yes, day one, free |
| Cloudflare DNS (proxy off) | One place for records, easy to flip WAF on later | Yes |
| Litestream | Loss window from a day to seconds | Later, only if a lost day ever hurts |
| Sentry or similar | Stack traces from the hosted process | No; the audit log and platform logs are enough at this size |
| Hosted identity (Clerk, Auth0, WorkOS) | User management UI, enterprise SSO | No for Kyle; documented under door C for operators who sell access |
| Keycloak / Authentik / Zitadel | Self-hosted identity for teams | Documented under door C; not run for this instance |
| Railway PR environments | A throwaway instance per pull request | Yes, once the seed workspace boots in under a minute |
| GitHub Actions gate | Tests green before Railway deploys | Yes; Railway deploys on push, so the gate must precede the push to `main` |
| Dependabot / Renovate | Base image bumps | Yes for the `Dockerfile` only; weave has no npm dependencies |

### Verification gates

| Gate | Method | Pass criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 Wall closed | `test/auth-wall.test.mjs`: every route table entry hit anonymously with `requireAuth` on | 401 on all but the five exemptions; export payload carries no `meta` secrets ([[Issue#230]]) |
| G2 Passkeys end to end | Playwright with the CDP virtual authenticator: invite, register, sign out, sign in, counter replay refused, wrong origin refused | All green under the existing browser gate; skipped Playwright counts as failure |
| G3 Container boots | `docker build` then `docker run` with the six variables; `/api/health` ok; write survives restart | Health ok twice, entity count unchanged across restart |
| G4 Backup round trip | `weave backup` to a local MinIO or R2, `weave restore` into a fresh dir, boot, compare entity counts and one attachment byte-for-byte | Counts equal, attachment identical, keystore round-trips with the passphrase |
| G5 Staging on Railway | Steps 2 of the cutover, evidence in the Release row | Health, passkey on two devices, MCP call, archive in R2 |
| G6 Cutover | Steps 5–7, `startedAt` on the cloud health newer than the deploy, harness routines writing to the cloud URL | One writer, laptop stopped, nightly restore verified the next morning |
| G7 Guides | Each guide followed cold by an agent on a fresh clone in an isolated worktree | Every "how you know it worked" check passes as written |

### Sequencing and effort

| Phase | Scope | Estimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | [[Issue#230]], wall closed (G1) | 1 day |
| 1 | Dockerfile, manifests, env contract, Railway and Docker guides (G3) | 1 day |
| 2 | Passkeys, sessions, invite, account page, CLI verbs (G2) | 4–6 days |
| 3 | `weave backup` / `restore`, nightly switch (G4) | 2 days |
| 4 | Staging, cutover, harness repoint (G5, G6) | 1–2 days |
| 5 | Remaining guides, Handbook seed, README index (G7) | 1 day |

Phases 0, 1 and 3 have no dependency on 2 and can run in parallel worktrees. Phase 4 waits on all of them.

### Open decisions for Kyle

1. Canonical copy after cutover: cloud (assumed) or laptop.
2. Domain for the instance.
3. Budget ceiling: under $10 (assumed) or room for a staging service kept alive.
4. Whether Cloudflare sits in front as DNS only (assumed) or as an Access gate stacked on passkeys.
5. Whether the uno Workers applet retires at step 8 or keeps its own door.

### Related

[[Feature#84]] (hosted instance; this spec supersedes its Cloudflare premise and keeps its three-artifact model), [[Feature#141]] §3 §4 §9 (this spec fills the Auth section), [[Feature#194]] (shares; problem 2 is closed by G1), [[Feature#208]] (passkeys; this spec is its build), [[Feature#209]] (backup; Part 4 is its first cut), [[Feature#212]] (providers; door C), [[Feature#213]] (keychain; the passphrase mode is the hosted equivalent), [[Issue#230]] (phase 0), [[Issue#231]] (decided at cutover step 8), [[Issue#250]] (surfaced by step 3).

features.name: Report a bug by email: a mailto from the bug panel and the route error card to weave@grunion.ai
features.description:
## Pain point

The in-app reporter ([[Feature#142]]) files every report into the **local** instance's `Development/Issue`. On Kyle's laptop that table is the one he reads. On a self-hosted instance ([[Feature#222]] phase 1: Docker, Railway, Fly) the same table lives on the operator's disk, and an instance without a `weave` docs workspace answers `501`. A bug found anywhere but `:4400` reaches nobody.

`weave@grunion.ai` exists for this: a Cloudflare Email Routing literal forward, receive-only, delivered to Kyle's Gmail and labelled ISSUE by a `to:` filter (verified end-to-end 2026-09-12). Nothing in the app points at it.

## Problem statement

A reporter on any weave instance needs one gesture that lands the report in Kyle's inbox, with enough context to triage and nothing that belongs to the workspace it came from.

## Solution shape

**A `mailto:` link, built in the browser, from the existing bug panel.** Bottom of the ponytail ladder, and the right rung:

- The address is receive-only, so there is no reply to promise and no inbound path to build.
- The reporter's own mail client opens with the report filled in. They read and edit every line before it sends, from their own address, so the reply lands with them.
- Nothing transits the weave server. No new route, no outbound mail credential, no Worker, no queue.

Escalation to a server or Worker path would be justified only by attachments (screenshots, the full action trace) or by devices with no mail handler. Neither is worth the machinery today: the full trace already reaches the local Issue when one exists, and the panel prints the address in plain text so a reporter with no handler can send from any client.

### Entry points

1. **Bug panel** — a `Email instead` link with the Lucide `mail` glyph in the panel foot, beside Send. Its `href` is rebuilt on every keystroke and symptom toggle, so what was typed rides along.
2. **Route error card** — `paintRouteError` gains a `Report by email` link carrying the error message, because a page that did not load is where the bug button is hardest to reach for.
3. **Handbook** — a `Reporting a bug` guide (audience Both) naming both paths and what never leaves the page.

### Payload

Subject: `[weave] <Symptoms>: <first line of the note>` — `[weave] Error: the table did not load`. The tag is the app, because Kyle's ISSUE label already covers decklet reports on the same filter and the inbox row has to say which product. Symptoms follow the Issue title convention from Feature #142. No note and no symptom: `[weave] on <route shape>`.

Body, plain text:

```
Symptoms: Error
Note: <what the reporter typed>

Steps:
1.
Expected:
Actual:

--
weave v0.4.17, started 2026-09-12T14:02:11Z, up 3h
Page: /w/<ws>/#/entity/<id>
Browser: Chrome 128 on macOS · 1440 × 900 · dark
Console: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')
```

| Field | Source | Why triage needs it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Symptoms | the four panel toggles | maps to Issue `Symptom` + Severity, the first sort key |
| Note, Steps, Expected, Actual | the reporter, in the mail client | the account; blank prompts get filled in more often than a free box |
| Version, started, uptime | `/api/health`, with the `stale` flag when set | a stale build is this project's most common false bug (Issues #19, #114) |
| Page | route shape only | which surface kind failed — entity, grid, map, view — without which one |
| Browser + OS | `navigator.userAgent`, reduced to family, major, OS | "Looks broken" bugs are browser-specific |
| Viewport + theme | `innerWidth/Height`, `data-bs-theme` | layout bugs depend on width; both themes are a house rule |
| Console | last `error` / `unhandledrejection` message, redacted, quoted strings blanked, 300 chars | the one line that names an `Error` symptom |

Total `mailto:` URL is capped at 2000 characters after encoding: the console line is trimmed first, then the note.

### Leak review

Precedent: [[Issue#230]], export carried `tokenHash` and share tokens because nobody listed what left the box. This lists it.

| Field | Source | Cannot carry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page | `location.pathname` + `hash` through `routeShape()`: every `/w/<name>/` → `/w/<ws>/`, every id segment → `<id>`, query string dropped | workspace names, entity ids, share tokens, `?e=` docks |
| Version, started, uptime, stale | `/api/health` | server facts only; no `state.meta`, no workspace name (health's `workspace` key is not copied) |
| Browser, viewport, theme | `navigator`, `window`, `<html data-bs-theme>` | nothing from the workspace |
| Symptoms | closed set of four labels | free text impossible |
| Note | typed by the reporter, in view | app-sourced data never; the reporter's own words, edited again in the mail client |
| Console | `error.message` only, after the same redaction as `src/bugreport.js` (`Bearer`, `token=`, `wv_`…) plus every `'…'` / `"…"` quoted run blanked | tokens, key names, and a server message that quotes a row or field name |
| Not sent at all | the action trace (`describeTarget` names tables and buttons: schema is customer data), `location.href`, page title, `userAgent` verbatim, workspace name | — |

### Copy constraints

The address is receive-only. No "we'll get back to you from weave@" anywhere; the reply, when there is one, comes from Kyle's own mailbox to the reporter's own address.

## Tests (TDD)

- `test/bug-report.test.mjs`: `routeShape` (ws name, entity, table, `?e=`, space, view, trash, activity, map, root); `mailtoReport` subject/body encoding, cap under 2000 after encoding with a 5 KB note and a 2 KB error, forbidden strings never present (raw href, ws name, uuid, `tokenHash`, `wv_`, `wvs_`); UA reduction; console redaction; the redaction regexes in `bug-core.js` equal the ones in `src/bugreport.js`; source-level: the panel and the route error card both build the link through `bugCore.mailtoReport`, the copy never promises a reply.
- `test/bug-panel-browser.test.mjs`: type a note, pick Error, read the anchor's `href` back: subject `[weave] Error: …`, body free of the workspace name.
- `test/handbook.test.mjs`: the guide exists for Both, names the address, both entry points, and what is never sent.


## Shipped — 2026-09-12

Landed as Gerrit change 336, commit `4428234` (Verified +1 on patchset 2 after a rebase over Feature #221; full suite 2142 pass, 0 fail). Live check on a scratch instance in both themes: the panel foot carries **Email instead** on its own row with the address printed beside it; the route error card carries **Report by email**; a built href from `/w/weave/` reads `Page: /w/<ws>/#/` and quotes no workspace segment, no raw user agent, and a blanked `'…'` where the server message quoted a name.

Tests: `test/bug-report.test.mjs` +12, `test/bug-panel-browser.test.mjs` +1, `test/handbook.test.mjs` +1. Handbook: **Reporting a bug** (Both, order 12).

Server regex `PREFIXED_KEY` widened from `wv_` to `wv[a-z]?_` in `src/bugreport.js` so `wvs_`/`wvv_` share tokens are redacted in the local Issue too — a gap Issue #230 named and the reporter had not closed.

features.name: Paste into a relation cell links by name
features.description:
**Symptom.** After Feature #221, ⌘V into a relation cell (a resting cell, an open record search, or a bare caret) is refused by Feature #220's `RG().plan`: the toast names the column and nothing is written. Copying a relation cell already puts the typed block (ids + labels) on the clipboard.

**Expected.** A paste into a relation cell links by name: each label in the clipboard block (or each TSV cell, split on `, `) is matched against the target table's rows by exact name, then by `#id`; matched rows are linked through the same `bulk` op with one Undo; unmatched labels are counted in the toast like unparsed cells are today. A weave-internal block that carries ids links by id first. Multi-cardinality replaces the whole set, as multi-select paste does.

**Where.** `public/grid-range.js` (`plan` refuses `relation`), `public/app.js` `runRange`, the engine's `bulk link` op.

**Verify.** `test/grid-range.test.mjs`: relation plan resolves names and ids, counts unmatched; browser case: copy a Blocks cell, paste into another row's Blocks, chips appear, Undo restores.

Follow-up from Feature #221 (landed 2026-09-12, Gerrit 333 → f21c671).

## 2026-09-12 · landed

Gerrit 337 (ps2, rebased onto 5bde129) → merge SHA `6c5a0c9`.

**The rule now.** A paste into a relation cell links by name. The grid fetches the related table's rows first (`POST /api/tables/:id/query`, the record picker's own query) and the pure plan matches each label to a row: a block copied inside weave links by id; otherwise the exact name (trimmed, case-insensitive), then `#12`. A set is replaced whole, as a multi-select paste is; a single-cardinality field takes the first match. Matched ids ride the existing `bulk set` (the engine's `updateEntity` already replaces a relation's set from an id list), so one Undo steps the paste back. A label that names no row is never invented: the toast counts and names it (`1 unmatched (Nobody)`), and a cell whose labels all miss is dropped rather than emptied. Without the rows to hand — a fetch that failed — the column refuses by name as before. Copy is unchanged except that a relation cell's TSV label is now the linked names (it read `[object Object]`).

**Tests.** `test/grid-range.test.mjs` +8 pure (`resolveRelation`, the relation plan, the toast; 44 total). `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs` +3 (copy Peers → paste on another row → chips on the page → one Undo unlinks; `bob, Nobody` from a sheet links Bob and the toast names Nobody; `#3, Ann` into a many-to-one Owner links Cy only; 21 total). Handbook: "What the types force" under Ranges, fill and paste. CHANGELOG Unreleased.

**Gate.** Worktree full suite: 2148 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped. Gerrit gate on ps2: Verified +1, Code-Review +2, submitted by weave-review.sh — 2186 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped (`~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/337-2.log`); ps1 was killed before voting because main had moved and the change was unmergeable.

**Deploy.** `:4400` `/api/health` sha `6c5a0c9`, startedAt `2026-09-12T16:26:28Z` (merge at `16:22:51Z`). Handbook on the live db: `weave handbook check --data ~/.weave/weave.db` → missing [] stale [] (the boot applied the guide).

**Live check.** On `:4400` Feature grid with agent-browser: copied Feature #220's `Shipped in` (v0.4.16) and pasted onto Feature #84. The headless ⌘V bridge fires no paste event, so copy and paste were dispatched in-page as `ClipboardEvent`s sharing one `DataTransfer`: TSV read `v0.4.16` (names, not `[object Object]`), the html flavour carried the typed block, toast "Pasted 1 cell · Undo", one chip in #84's cell, engine linked v0.4.16. Undo clicked at once: chips 0, cell back to `+ link`, engine `[]`, activity shows the add, the removal and the `undo` entry. A first attempt clicked Undo across two CLI calls after the toast had gone and left #84 linked; it was unlinked by hand (`POST /unlink`) before the clean run, so #84 carries three extra relation-updated entries from 16:29–16:31Z. Worktree `wv-feat-224-090950` removed.

features.name: Document version history: every document field keeps browsable, restorable revisions
features.description:
**Every document field keeps its own revision history, browsable and restorable from the document's chrome.** Requested by Kyle 2026-09-12: "all weave documents should have a built-in version history", so that decklet can drop its own in-file version snapshots and rely on weave for history.

## Today

- `setDoc`/`appendDoc` (src/engine.js:4826-4860) overwrite `entity.docs[fieldId]` in the entity JSON blob. The prior text survives only as a sparse before-image in `undo_log` (src/store.js:33, cap 200 workspace-wide, popped and destroyed on undo) and as a length/line delta in `activity[]` (coalesced per 10-minute session, Issue #32). Neither can reconstruct a past document.
- The client saves on a 600 ms debounce (public/app.js:6443, 7446-7463), so every pause is a write.

## Shape

**Storage.** A new `doc_revisions` table in src/store.js (mirrored in src/store-cf.js): `seq` autoincrement, `entity_id`, `field_id`, `at`, `actor`, `text`, `len`. Revisions are not part of the entity blob, so entity rows stay small and export stays free of prior text (export is a share surface, Issue #230).

**Engine.** `setDoc`/`appendDoc` write a revision of the new text. Consecutive writes by the same actor to the same field inside a 10-minute window coalesce into the newest revision (same rule as activity), so a typing session is one revision, not a keystroke log. Identical text records nothing. Cap per document 200, oldest trimmed. Verbs: `listDocRevisions(ref, field, {limit})`, `getDocRevision(ref, field, seq)`, `restoreDocRevision(ref, field, seq)` (a restore is a normal `setDoc` of the old text, so nothing is ever destroyed and undo keeps working). Entity purge removes its revisions; soft delete keeps them.

**Doors.** REST `GET /api/entities/:ref/doc/revisions?field=`, `GET /api/entities/:ref/doc/revisions/:seq`, `POST /api/entities/:ref/doc/revisions/:seq/restore`; CLI `weave doc-revisions` / `weave doc-restore`; MCP `weave_doc_revisions` / `weave_doc_restore`; AGENTS.md entries; `SURFACE` registry in test/agent-surface.test.mjs.

**UI.** A history control (`lucide:history`) in the `doc-section-head` next to the source toggle (public/app.js:7767-7778). It opens a panel listing revisions newest first (time, actor, size delta); selecting one shows a read-only render; Restore writes it back and returns to the editor. Both themes. Handbook Guide for the document field gains a "History" section.

## Not in scope

- Field-value history for non-document fields (separate feature).
- Diff view between two revisions (ponytail: list + preview + restore first; diff later).
- Revisions in exportJSON/importJSON (backups are DB-level via VACUUM INTO).

Filed by the weave-version-history session, v0.4.17 @ 89820bc.



Shipped in 5a83737 (Gerrit 340, 2026-09-12): doc_revisions table in both stores; listDocRevisions / getDocRevision / restoreDocRevision; REST, CLI and MCP doors; the History control and wv-doc-history panel in the doc-section-head; the document Handbook page's History section. Evidence: the four attached screenshots (panel and preview, light and dark) from the 4490 scratch server, and verify-4400-*.png from :4400 after the landing. Released as v0.4.18.

features.name: Knot view: agentic loops as link diagrams, linking/unknotting numbers as native health metrics (+ Weave Constitution)
features.description:
**Thesis.** Every closed causal cycle in a workspace — an agent's read→plan→act→write loop, an automation chain, a formula/rollup dependency cycle — is a strand. Two loops touching the same entity form a crossing; the one whose write precedes the other's read is *over*. Precedence is the third dimension that turns a flat dependency graph into a link diagram. Loops that can be pulled apart without cutting are healthy however tangled the view looks; loops that cannot (Hopf link and up) are mutual dependencies that only a cut resolves.

**Deliverables.**
1. *Weave Constitution* — seven articles, kept as a Wiki/Article in this workspace and mirrored in the README.
2. `knot-core.mjs` — pure JS, no deps: braid word → signed crossings → linking number, Reidemeister R1/R2 simplifier, unknot heuristic, Kauffman bracket/Jones for ≤12 crossings. TDD against known knots (unknot, trefoil σ₁³, Hopf σ₁², figure-eight (σ₁σ₂⁻¹)²).
3. *Trace capture* — loops and contacts derived from the audit log (#14) and MCP agent calls (#99), emitted as a braid word per loop period.
4. *Knot space* — `Loop`, `Contact`, `Trace` tables with invariants as computed fields; weave traces its own automations and agents first.
5. *Knot view* — extends the Relation map (#9): SVG link diagram, components coloured, crossings click through to the shared entity, an invariants strip, and a *pull* affordance that animates the moves.
6. *Claim gate* — the sentence "the first knot-theory-based data tool" ships in the README only behind a test asserting ≥1 invariant computed from live workspace data and rendered in the panel.

**Honesty notes.** Cycle detection already finds circular dependencies; the knot lens adds precedence as a dimension, the apparent-vs-essential distinction (moves), and a redesign-cost metric (unknotting number). Unknot recognition is NP ∩ co-NP and unknotting number is hard in general — ship upper bounds from greedy simplification, exact small cases only. Neighbouring fields (topological data analysis, directed algebraic topology for concurrency) do not use knot invariants, so the "first" claim is likely true and cheap to falsify.

Related: #9 Relation map, #12 meta-model, #14 audit log, #99 MCP transport, #164 referencesFrom, #211 integrations as agents.

Filed by the harness session 2026-09-12 (weave v0.4.17, 89820bc). Plan artifact in the harness queue: 2026-09-12-132818-weave-knot-constitution-plan.html.

features.name: Webhooks and listeners: inbound webhook endpoints that trigger automations
features.description:
Weave ships outgoing webhooks (Feature #5, v0.1). It has no inbound side. An external system (GitHub, Stripe, a form, a Shortcut) cannot post an event into weave and have a row change.

Shape: a workspace-level Listener table. Each row mints a URL under /w/<ws>/api/hooks/<id> with a secret. A POST to that URL runs the row's automation with the request body as input, so an automation can create or update rows from the payload. Deliveries are logged on the Listener row (time, status, body size) so a missed event is visible.

Originating request: uno task #80, Fibery Task Management/Task #1956 (both closed with a redirect to this row on 2026-09-17).

Filed by Fable 5.1, 2026-09-17.

features.name: Table search: a search box in the table toolbar that filters the grid to matching rows, same matcher as ⌘K
features.description:
Kyle's request, 2026-09-23: add a search box on the table page that searches only the current table and hides every row that does not match. Reference: a phone screenshot of a boards-style grid with a magnifier icon in the toolbar beside Sort and Filter, left of the blue + New button (attached to this row).

Today: finding a row in a big table means either the ⌘K palette (Feature #10, #21), which searches the whole workspace and navigates away, or building a filter (Feature #38, #149), which is several clicks and matches one field at a time.

Shape:
- A magnifier button in the table toolbar next to Sort and Filter. Click or press / (or ⌘F while the grid has focus) to expand it into a text input.
- Same matching as ⌘K: reuse the universal search scorer (name, publicId such as #143, text fields), pre-scoped to this table. One search implementation, two entry points. No second matcher.
- As you type (debounced), the grid shows only matching rows and highlights the matched text. Non-matching rows drop out; the row count in the footer reflects the matches.
- Composes with saved filters and sort: search narrows whatever the view already shows. It is transient view state, never written to the Tables row Filter field (Feature #149), so it does not change the saved view for anyone else.
- Esc clears and collapses. An empty result shows a one-line "No rows match" with a clear button.
- Enter on a single match opens that row.

Done when: typing a publicId, a name fragment or a text-field value in a 500-row table filters the grid within one frame of the debounce; clearing restores the view exactly; a browser test covers type, filter, clear and Esc.

Filed by Opus 5.5, 2026-09-23, from Kyle's chat request.

features.name: Table views: a strip of views per table, a default, and Blank
features.description:
## Pain Point

A weave table has one configuration: filter and sort live on its Tables row (Feature #149). Kyle wants several named views per table, as Attio and Airtable show them.

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-23)

- A horizontal strip of views under the table title; + creates a view.
- A view sets visible fields, row filters and sort order.
- One view is the default and opens first.
- A Blank view always returns to the raw table: every row, every field, entry order.
- Open question from Kyle: do we want a "Save as view" option?

## Shape

Five mockups (three save models, two placements) are in the design-review Artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/7EyWKFEQPNSSwq6kZGx2Fv Recommendation: C, autosave into named views, where touching Blank forks a new Untitled view, on the toolbar strip. Views become Workspace/Views registry rows (Name, Table, Filters, Sort, Field Order, Hidden Fields, Density, Default, Position); Blank is computed, never stored; each table's #149 config migrates to a starred Default view.

Dependencies: Feature #217 (autosave everywhere) sets the save model. Feature #17 already uses the name "saved view" for multi-table share pages; one of the two needs a new name. Issue #341 (+ New on a filtered table) should land first.

Filed by the harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.29 (0be87e5).

## Ruling (Kyle, 2026-09-23)

- **Save behaviour: A.** A change to a filter, sort or field autosaves into the current view. "Save as view" duplicates the current view under a new name. Blank is the system default: no sort, no filter, standard field visibility. Blank is read-only and always one click away.
- **Placement: the strip** under the table title. The breadcrumb menu (E) and the sidebar (D) are dropped.
- **Most important:** agents must define a view's field visibility, field order and positioning easily, without token overload. One view verb, names instead of UUIDs, a single ordered `fields` list that carries visibility and order together, relative edits (show, hide, move) so a wide table never needs resending, and compact reads.

## Shipped (2026-09-23)

Shipped in v0.4.35, commit e45dd2d, Gerrit change 385; deployed to :4400 at 2026-09-24T00:55:07Z (launchd pid 16090; landing 00:51Z).

The strip sits under the table title: the starred default first, then the other views, then **Blank**, then **+** and a **⋮** menu (Save as view…, Rename view…, Make default, Delete view). A change to the filter, the sort, a column drag or the eye saves into the view on screen. Blank is read-only and never stored. A view's link is `#/table/<table>/view/<view id>`; `…/view/blank` opens Blank.

Agent verbs, one write path on every door:

| Door | Call |
| --- | --- |
| MCP | `weave_table_view {view, …patch}` |
| CLI | `weave table view Issue/Open --fields Name,Status` (`--show`, `--hide`, `--move F --before G`, `--filters`, `--sort`, `--default`, `--position`, `--from`, `--name`, `--delete`) |
| REST | `GET /api/tables/:t/views`, `GET` / `PATCH` / `DELETE /api/tables/:t/views/:v` |
| Engine | `tableView('Issue')`, `tableView('Issue/Open bugs')`, `tableView('Issue/Open bugs', patch)` |
| Registry | a `Workspace/Views` row: `Fields`, `Filter`, `Sort`, `Default`, `Position` |

Example, defining a view in one call and moving a column in a second:

```
weave_table_view {view: "Issue/Open bugs", fields: ["Name", "Severity", "Status"], filters: {Status: ["Open"]}, sort: [{field: "Severity", dir: "desc"}]}
weave_table_view {view: "Issue/Open bugs", move: {field: "Status", before: "Name"}, default: true}
```

MCP cost: 54 tools and 26,263 schema bytes before, 55 and 27,112 after (+849). `weave_update_table` dropped `hiddenFields` from its schema; the engine still takes it and writes the default view.

Decisions taken where the ruling left room:
- The default is the first view, so "star" and "position 0" are one fact and cannot disagree.
- A new view with no `from` starts from Blank. `from` copies another view (the UI's Save as view).
- `show` puts a field back at its schema position among the visible ones; moving a hidden field shows it.
- `fieldOrder` stays the schema order (entity page and Blank); the grid's columns are the view's.
- System columns (Created At and the rest) stay table-level through `systemFields`.
- Names: Feature #17's cross-table pages keep `createView` / `weave_views` / `/api/views`; the table menu's old "Save as view…" for them is now "New share page…".
- Capped writer tokens cannot change views. The table PATCH that views replace was gated the same way.

Migration: each table's filter, sort and hidden set became a starred view named Default, in its column order. Rehearsed on copies of the live weave and uno workspaces: every table carried over, 0 registry problems.

Also fixed: Issue #341 (+ New on a filtered view seeds the row inside the filter).

Not in this change: per-person views, per-view density.

## Ruling 2026-09-25: drag order

Shipped in v0.4.40, commit 0670c68, Gerrit change 410; deployed to :4400 at 2026-09-26T05:09:09Z (launchd pid 44752; landing 05:07:04Z). A follow-up fix for a fast drag that did nothing (Issue #400) is Gerrit change 415.

Two rulings from Kyle, the same day:

- "Instead of a star, allow drag to reorder, the first (leftmost) view is the default, then we don't need the 3 dots."
- "also, blank can be removed."

Shipped as follows (the session's reading where Kyle left room):

- **Order is the default.** The leftmost tab opens with the table. The star and "Make default" are gone. Tabs reorder by drag: a mouse press that moves, or a finger held still for 350 ms and then slid (a quick swipe still scrolls the strip). Alt+Left and Alt+Right move a focused tab.
- **No ⋯ button.** Its actions moved. Rename: double-click the tab name and edit in place (Enter or clicking away saves, Escape cancels). Duplicate view… (the old Save as view) and a hold-to-delete Delete view sit in the tab's context menu with Rename…, opened by right-click, Shift+F10, the ContextMenu key, or a finger held on the tab and let go.
- **No Blank tab.** The + button makes a view with every field in schema order, no filter and no sort, and that is how a person gets back to the raw table. The `…/view/blank` route and the agent read `Table/blank` still work, read-only, so old links and agents do not break; the strip lights no tab there, and its read-only note points at + and the tab menu.
- **A table keeps at least one view.** Deleting the last one is refused with a message, through the verb, MCP, CLI, REST and the Views row. The session picked refusal over recreating a default view, so a delete never silently makes something new.
- **Agents.** Position is the single source of the default: `position: 0` makes a view the default, reads carry no `default` flag (the list order says it), and `default: true` still works as the older spelling of position 0. The list no longer ends with a Blank entry. `applySchema` writes views before deleting and then places the order, so the order round-trips and a document can replace every view. The Tables-row mirror (Hidden Fields, Filter, Sort) follows the leftmost view. `weave_table_view` schema: 910 bytes before, 888 after (the `default` property left the schema; the verb still takes it); all tools 27,112 to 27,090.

Landed and verified live (2026-09-26): change 410 deployed at 05:09:09Z; the follow-up for Issue #400 landed as b6599a9 (Gerrit 415) and reached :4400 in 1ed7e7b at 08:08:02Z. On the live Issue table, a test view dragged in front of Default saved as the first view, the bare route opened it with its filter lit, the right-click menu listed Rename…, Duplicate view… and Delete view, and deleting the last view was refused. The test view was deleted and the table left as it was (Default, Status: Open).

Not changed: the migrated views keep the name "Default" until Kyle picks one.

features.name: Number display: bar, ring and heat costumes
features.description:
## Pain Point

A number field prints only as text. Kyle wants in-cell graphics like Excel's, so a progress or score column reads at a glance.

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-23)

- A display costume on number fields, next to the format keys (`NUMBER_COSTUME_KEYS`, `src/engine.js:143`). No rules layer.
- Displays: text (default), bar, ring, heat.
- Bar and ring scale: 100% is the column's max rollup by default (the `via` max rollup on the Spaces row, Feature #187). A fixed max is the alternative setting.
- Stars stay out of this costume. Ratings are their own type (see the Rating feature).

## Shape

- Engine: add `display` and `scale` (`column` or a number) to the costume keys; validate in `normalizeSelfContainedConfig`. The API keeps returning the raw number.
- Numeric formulas and rollups already wear the number costume (`src/engine.js:3482`), so they get the displays with no extra work.
- Client: inline SVG sized to the row in the grid cell, chip and card; graphic cells are never marked clipped. Field dialog gets a Display picker with a live preview (`public/field-dialog-core.js:364`, `public/app.js:6202`).
- Screen readers get the value as text, e.g. "60%".
- Tests first: engine contract per key, field-dialog-core, one browser case per display.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.30, commit 2a473f0).

## Shipped (2026-09-23)

Shipped in v0.4.32, commit aa8f1f2, Gerrit change 383; deployed to :4400 at 2026-09-24T00:27:13Z (landing 00:22:38Z).

Decisions taken where the spec left room:
- A rollup has no costume of its own: over a number or formula column with a graphic display it wears that column's display and scale, the way it already wears its format. A count wears none. Consequence: a fixed scale on the source column also bounds a sum rollup; use the column scale there.
- Heat reads the same scale as bar and ring (0 to the scale), with an opacity floor so a cell on the scale still reads as tinted.
- Every read carries `scales` (field name to its 100% mark) for graphic columns, so a paged grid, a chip and a card draw against the whole column. The column max is computed with `aggregate('max')` from src/stats.js, which is the figure a Space-level `via` max rollup reads; it is not read from such a rollup row.
- The value's text stays beside the graphic in every display; the SVG is aria-hidden and the wrapper's aria-label is the dressed value.
- Doc mentions rendered server-side (src/markdown.js) keep the text only.

features.name: Rating field type: whole-number icons you click to fill
features.description:
## Pain Point

Scoring a row (priority, quality, fit) takes a number field and a mental scale. Kyle wants a rating you set with one click.

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-23)

- Rating is its own field type.
- Whole numbers only, 0 to max. The max is set per field; offer 3, 5 and 7.
- One icon per field, chosen from the icon menu (the Lucide registry, `public/icon-registry.js`), not only stars.
- The cell shows max empty icons; clicking the nth fills 1 to n.
- A rollup or lookup over a rating shows the same icons, rounded to a whole number, read-only.

## Shape

- Engine: `rating` in `VALUE_TYPES` (`src/engine.js:72`), config `{ max, icon }`, stored as an integer clamped to 0..max. Formulas, sort, filter and CSV read it as a number. Converts to and from number by round and clamp.
- Client: click the nth icon to set n; click the current value again to clear to 0. In the grid, digit keys set the value and Backspace clears (`public/grid-keymap.js`). Screen readers read "3 of 5".
- Tests first: engine type and conversion tests, rollup rounding, browser click-to-rate and keyboard cases.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.30, commit 2a473f0).

## Shipped (2026-09-23)

Shipped in v0.4.34, commit c2ac845, Gerrit change 384; deployed to :4400 at 2026-09-24T00:49:16Z (landing 00:42:49Z). Version note: another session had already written the v0.4.33 Release row (Feature #229, unlanded at the time), so this release took v0.4.34.

Decisions taken where the spec left room:
- `max` accepts any whole number from 1 to 10; the dialog offers 3, 5 and 7 as one-click presets beside a number box.
- Empty and 0 are different values: a row nobody rated is empty (`is-empty` matches it, the cell reads "unrated, of 5"); clicking the current icon and Backspace both write 0.
- A write is rounded and clamped (3.6 stores 4, 9 stores the max); numeric text is accepted; other text is refused by name. Lowering `max` does not rewrite stored values: every read holds them to the new ceiling, so raising it again restores them.
- A digit past the max sets the max. Other characters on a resting rating cell do nothing (no text box opens).
- A rollup draws icons only for aggregates that stay on the scale (`avg`, `min`, `max`, `median`); `sum`, `range`, `stdev` and `count` print as numbers. A lookup of a rating draws icons. Both are read-only and rounded; the API returns the unrounded figure.
- Conversions: number to rating and back; rating to text freezes the number.

features.name: Formula arrays and the sparkline display
features.description:
## Pain Point

A trend across related rows (deal amounts by month, weekly counts) has no in-cell view. Kyle wants sparklines, driven by formulas.

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-23)

- A formula can return an array or null.
- An array result can be shown as a sparkline: line, column or win/loss.

## Shape

- Formulas are row-local (`src/formula.js`); arrays come in through lookup fields, which already evaluate to lists.
- Order: a lookup returns relation order, not date order. Proposed: a `sortby(values, keys)` function, so `sortby([Deal amounts], [Deal close dates])` gives an ordered series. Blank slots must keep their positions for the pairing to hold; test that first.
- Result kind: `list` already exists in the formula type inference (`src/engine.js:3777`). The formula's display costume gains `sparkline` with a style (line, column, win/loss); the API returns the numbers.
- Sort and filter on a sparkline column use the last value.
- Cap the points drawn (e.g. 60) and say so on hover, which lists the values.
- Tests first: array and null results, sortby alignment with blanks, browser render per style.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-23, weave v0.4.30, commit 2a473f0).

## Shipped (2026-09-23)

Shipped in v0.4.36, commit 558550f, Gerrit change 386; deployed to :4400 at 2026-09-24T01:05:03Z (landing 01:00:41Z). Rebased onto v0.4.35 (Feature #229, landed by another session meanwhile).

Lookup alignment: the test was written first and passed on the existing code. `#resolve` for a lookup drops only trashed related rows and keeps a blank value as `null` in its slot, so two lookups over one relation stay aligned; nothing needed fixing.

Decisions taken where the spec left room:
- `sortby(values, keys)` sorts ascending and stable; numbers compare as numbers, anything else as text (ISO dates order correctly); blank keys go last; a length mismatch is a runtime error naming both counts; a single value is returned as itself so the authoring check (which stubs fields with 0) passes. It sits with the builder's number chips rather than a new "list" group.
- The style key is `style` (`line` default, `column`, `winloss`), stored only with `display: sparkline`; a number field refuses the sparkline.
- The newest 60 points are drawn (the series reads oldest to newest); the hover lists every value and adds "(drawing the last 60 of N)"; the accessible name gives the count, last value, low and high.
- "Last value" for sort and filter is the last number in the series, skipping trailing blanks.
- Columns stand on zero when the series crosses it; losses and negatives draw in red; win/loss draws sign only, zero as no bar.

Also fixed in the same change: Issue #358 (a rating on a chip or card printed its number, found while wiring the sparkline chip).
