features.name: Field resize, reorder and freeze: labels never clip, widths stay put, drop across the seam to freeze
features.description:
## Pain point

Kyle reviewed an inline mockup of the table grid (show_widget `weave_grid_resize_reorder_freeze_v2`, 2026-09-25) and approved its behaviour for build: "If implemented to match the mock up behaviour then this result will be very good." Today the grid has resize (Feature #42), fit-on-double-click (Feature #112) and a frozen `#` column (Issue #252), but a header can still clip, and the grid does not state what happens to the other fields when one changes.

## Rules (Kyle, 2026-09-25, non-negotiable)

1. **A header label never truncates.** No drag, keyboard nudge, frozen-zone cap or autofit takes a field below its full rendered header: icon, full label, any badge or lock, padding, and resize-grip clearance. Measure it from the rendered header, never a fixed px floor. No ellipsis on header labels.
2. **Adding, removing, showing or hiding a field never changes another field's width.** Neighbours slide over. Nothing is squeezed or redistributed to fill the view. A hidden field keeps its width and its place for when it returns.
3. **Every field type has a default width.** Mockup values: Name 220, Text 180, Long text 280, Select 124, Person 136, Date 112, Number 88, Currency 104, Checkbox 56, URL 180. Map the remaining weave types to the nearest of these. A longer header label raises that field's own default, never a neighbour's.
4. **A click that ends a drag or resize never opens the field menu.** (Extends the Safari pointer-capture fix from Issue #98 to reorder drags and freeze drops.)

## Behaviour (from the approved mockup)

* **Resize** moves only the dragged field. Fields to its right slide by the delta, widths unchanged. Header and cells paint through one function during the drag (Issue #160). A small readout shows `<Field> <px> +/-delta` while dragging. Double-click on the grip fits to the longest value, between the label floor and a per-type maximum.
* **Reorder** by dragging the header. A ghost follows the pointer, the grabbed column dims, and a single vertical insertion line marks the drop point. Never highlight or swap the displaced field ([[weave-open-ledger-and-column-major-reorder]]). No-op positions hide the line. On drop, every moved column slides into place (FLIP, about 180 ms). The wrap auto-scrolls near its edges during a drag.
* **Frozen zone.** Only the ID (`#`) field is locked and frozen by default. It never drags and nothing drops before it. There is **no draggable divider**. Dropping a field across the frozen seam freezes it; dropping a frozen field back across unfreezes it. The insertion line carries a small "Freeze here" or "Unfreeze" tag when the drop changes membership. Cap the frozen zone at 60% of the visible grid width; past the cap the drop lands on the scrolling side. The seam keeps its Issue #252 behaviour (hairline strengthens only while scrolled).
* **Keyboard.** On a focused header, Alt+Shift+Left/Right moves the field one place (crossing the seam freezes or unfreezes in place); Alt+Left/Right resizes by 8 px, stopping at the label floor.
* **Header row** stays sticky while the body scrolls vertically, and frozen header cells stay pinned in both axes.

## Persistence

Widths, field order and frozen count are view configuration: store them on the current view per Feature #229 (autosave into the current view) and the Tables registry row precedent ([[weave-table-config-lives-on-the-tables-row]]). Expose frozen count through the same agent view verb as field order.

## Verification

Browser suite assertions must read **every other column's width before and after** each action (resize, reorder, hide, show, add, remove, freeze drop), and assert the header label's `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` at the floor. Assert which column landed where, not that a drag event fired (Kyle, 2026-09-02). A click after a drag must not open the field menu.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-09-25 (mockup review), against weave v0.4.40.

features.name: Rating: default max of 5, any quantity, and a clickable default
features.description:
## Pain Point

The rating field dialog (Feature #231, v0.4.34) caps the max at 1 to 10 behind presets of 3, 5 and 7, and asks for the default rating in a text box. A rating is a row of icons, so typing a number to set its default reads wrong.

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-25)

- The max defaults to 5.
- The user can set any quantity, not only 3, 5 or 7.
- The default rating is chosen on an interactive preview drawn with the selected icon, not in a text box.

## Shape

- Engine: a new rating field gets `max: 5` when none is given. Lift the 1 to 10 cap to any whole number from 1 up; keep an upper guard only if the grid needs one to stay usable, and say what it is on this row.
- Field dialog: the max is a whole-number input prefilled with 5 (presets may stay as shortcuts beside it). The default is a live row of `max` icons in the chosen icon: click the nth to set the default to n, click it again to clear. The preview redraws when the icon or the max changes, and a default above a lowered max clamps down.
- Keyboard: the preview takes focus; arrow keys move the value, digits set it, Backspace clears. Screen readers read "Default: 3 of 5".
- Tests first: engine default and cap, field-dialog-core, and a browser case that sets a default by clicking the preview and sees a new row start at it.

Follows Feature #231.

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-25, weave v0.4.39, commit 6a2ced2).

## Shipped

Landed in v0.4.43 as commit 689c2b1 (Gerrit change 413), 2026-09-26; live on :4400 from 09:03 UTC.

- The max is any whole number from 1 to 100; 5 when none is given, on the engine, `POST /api/tables/:id/fields`, `weave_add_field` and `weave field add`.
- **Upper guard: 100.** Every icon is a button in every visible grid cell, so a max in the thousands would put tens of thousands of nodes in one screen of rows and stall the paint, and a row past 100 icons is wider than any screen. The reason sits beside `RATING_MAX` in `src/engine.js`; the dialog mirrors it (`public/field-dialog-core.js`, contract-tested).
- Field dialog: a whole-number Max box prefilled with 5, with 3, 5 and 7 as shortcut chips. The default is a live row of `max` icons in the chosen icon (`ratingEl`, the grid cell's control): click the nth to set n, click it again to clear; focused, the arrows move it, a digit sets it, End sets the max, Home, Backspace or Delete clear it. A screen reader hears "Default: 3 of 5". It redraws on an icon or max change, and a default above a lowered max comes down with it.
- Also fixed: Issue #396 (a default sent with a new max was clamped to the old max).
- Showcase › Field Types gains Brightness, 12 suns with a default of 6.
- Verified on :4400 in both themes: the preview followed an icon change (sun to heart) and a max of 20, a click on the 15th set "Default: 15 of 20", the 7 chip clamped it to 7 of 7, ArrowLeft gave 6 of 7, Cancel left the field untouched, and a row made with + New started at 6 of 12. The scratch rows were deleted.
- Found while verifying: Issue #404 (a rating column narrower than its icons clips the last ones; Love and Brightness open clipped).

## Screenshots

![Brightness settings: the max box, the chips and the default row of 12 suns at 6](/w/weave/api/files/d2f2331a-850e-4af0-912a-4c316c336021)

![Icon changed to a heart, max typed as 20, the 15th clicked: Default 15 of 20](/w/weave/api/files/3a3590d7-92fa-429e-a6f5-ddde6a1746a7)

![Dark theme: the 7 chip clamped the default to 7, ArrowLeft set 6 of 7, the row focused](/w/weave/api/files/5a6f910b-9726-4c93-8385-7a4ce7801cd5)

![A new row, #8, starts at 6 of 12 suns in the Brightness column, light theme](/w/weave/api/files/d53a8757-5cae-447e-b783-ef834cd13350)

![The same in the dark theme](/w/weave/api/files/9308e4e1-9616-4411-986f-000600250ae7)

features.name: Rich cells: a color setting (Quiet ink default), redrawn cells, fitted column widths
features.description:
## Pain Point

Kyle, 2026-09-25, on the rich cells from Features #230, #231 and #232: "I don't like the design of the columns or the colors." Bars are 10 px slabs, rings are heavy, heat is a filled orange box, every rating icon is orange, win/loss uses saturated red and blue, the Σ and ƒ marks repeat in every cell, and rating columns clip icons past about five (Issue #404).

## Ask (Kyle, 2026-09-26)

* Color is a setting on the field, with three choices from the mockups. The default is Quiet ink.
* Redraw the cells to match the mockups.
* Better column widths.

## The three color settings (key `color`)

| Value | Label | Bars, rings | Heat | Rating icons | Sparkline | Win / loss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ink` (default) | Quiet ink | text color on a hairline track | gray tint behind the number, stronger with the value | filled in text color, empty as a hairline outline | secondary text color | text color / muted |
| `icon` | Color by icon | teal | cool to warm tint behind the number | the icon's own hue: star amber, heart rose, bolt violet, flame orange; other icons fall back to the accent | blue | green / red |
| `accent` | One accent hue | workspace accent | accent tint, stronger with the value | accent | accent | accent dark / accent light |

All colors come from theme tokens or ramps that hold in both themes; no raw hex in a cell without its dark twin.

## Cell shape (all three settings)

* Bar: 6 px tall, round ends, fixed 80 px track, the dressed number to its right in tabular figures.
* Ring: 16 px, 2.5 px stroke, round cap, percent to its right.
* Heat: the dressed number on a rounded tint, no filled chip.
* Rating: 14 px icons, 1 px gap; empty icons as outlines.
* Sparkline: 1.5 px line with a dot on the newest point; column style with 1.5 px radius; win/loss as small blocks above and below a midline.
* The Σ and ƒ marks leave the cell and stay in the column header only.

## Column width

A rich column's default width fits its graphic: rating = max × (icon + gap) + padding; bar = track + widest dressed value; ring and heat = graphic + widest value; sparkline = a fixed 64 to 96 px. A width the user dragged wins. Never clip icons (Issue #404).

## Shape

* Engine: `color` on the rating config, the number costume and the formula display, validated to the three values, default `ink`; the API returns it.
* Settings tray: a Color picker with three swatches, each drawn as a live sample in that setting, beside Display.
* Tests first: engine validation and default, a browser case per setting in both themes, and a width case that fits a 10-icon rating without clipping.
* Showcase: the Rich fields view shows each setting at least once, through the existing Showcase sync.

Mockup: the three-option widget from the 2026-09-25 harness session (A Quiet ink, B Color by icon, C One accent hue).

Filed by Claude (harness session 2026-09-26, weave v0.4.43, commit 9d2f855).

features.name: Row density: Compact, Comfortable and Spacious, held to a declared height and saved with the view
features.description:
Approved by Kyle on 2026-09-27 from the density mockups (design review artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/TtynafGSufewqfUboVtm8P, source ~/Documents/queue/weave-density/2026-09-27-weave-density-design-review.html). Fixes Issue #440.

## Problem

Row height is the tallest cell plus two paddings plus a 1px rule, so content sets the row. Measured on :4400 at weave main 483514a across 31 tables: Comfortable rows run 45, 47, 49 and 70px (Compact 31 to 56). The grid windows its rows from ONE measured height per table and density (Issue #324), so mixed grids drift and the flip anchor (Issue #342, #413) inherits the error.

## The three densities

| Setting | Row | Cell box | Padding | Lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compact | 32px | 24px | 4px | 1 |
| Comfortable (default) | 44px | 28px | 8px | 1 |
| Spacious (new) | 72px | 56px | 8px | 2 |

Density changes row height only. Text stays 13px (--wv-grid-font) and every column keeps its width at all three settings. The row rule is an inset shadow, so it takes no height.

## Row form per field type

| Field type | Compact | Comfortable | Spacious |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name, text | 1 line, ellipsis | 1 line, ellipsis | 2-line clamp |
| Rich text, doc preview | first line, marks kept, no block padding | same | first two lines |
| Select, workflow | chip 18px | chip 20px | chip 20px |
| Multi-select, relation | whole chips on 1 row, then +N | whole chips on 1 row, then +N | whole chips on 2 rows, then +N |
| Computed card | chip, title only | chip, title only | compact card, title + 1 line |
| Person | 16px avatar | 20px avatar | 24px avatar |
| File, image | 16px icon | 22px thumbnail | 48px thumbnail |
| Row checkbox | 14px box, 26px hit area from a pseudo-element (no layout) | same | same |
| Number, date, rating, checkbox | one line | one line | one line |

A chip shows whole or not at all. Chips never get cut at the cell edge; the +N counter carries the hidden ones, and the cell pop shows them all.

## Enforcement

1. Declared track: --wv-row-h, --wv-cell-h, --wv-lines on .wv-grid[data-density]; td height is the token, box-sizing border-box.
2. One clip box: the cell builder wraps every value in a box of height --wv-cell-h with overflow clip. A table cell treats height as a minimum, so the fixed child holds the row. One choke point, not one rule per type.
3. Row forms: each renderer receives the line budget and draws the form above; text uses line-clamp var(--wv-lines).
4. Overflow: the existing clipped marker and cell pop (Issue #157), with the clip test extended to height.
5. Windowing reads the token: rowH() reads --wv-row-h instead of the measured cache from Issue #324. In development one sampled row per paint is compared with the token and a mismatch logs the field type.

## Saved with the view

Density is a property of the saved view (Feature #229), beside filter, sort and field order. A pick in the toolbar density dropdown (Feature #237) autosaves to the live view. A new view starts at Comfortable. The per-browser localStorage key weave-grid-density:<table id> retires: a view with no density reads it once, saves it, and the key is removed.

## Gates (written first)

- Row pitch: grid-density-browser seeds one field of every type with worst-case values (600-character markdown, 12 chips, a computed card, an image); every painted row equals 32, 44, 72 in both themes. Red on main today.
- Only height moves: computed font-size and every column width identical across densities.
- Whole chips: no chip crosses the cell box; hidden count equals the +N value.
- Saved in the view: flip, reload, switch views; density persists and a second view keeps its own.
- grid-chrome caps become exact equality; #324, #342, #413 cases pass, plus a flip into and out of Spacious at row 400 of 600.

Open: Comfortable at 44px or held at 47px. Building 44px.

Filed by the harness session on 2026-09-27 (weave density design), weave main 483514a.

## Landed

Gerrit change 451, weave main 3e5e66b (2026-09-27). Gate: Verified +1, 2868 tests, 1 file retried green (table-views-browser, the Issue #341 case timed out once under load and passes in isolation). Height sweep on a copy of every :4400 workspace with the new code: 741 painted rows, Compact 32px x741, Comfortable 44px x741, Spacious 72px x741. Left open: a plain text value (an input at rest, including most Names) stays one line at Spacious; text that carries marks, the description and the card take two.

features.name: Hairline grid header: labels on the surface and a plus that trails the last field
features.description:
Approved by Kyle in chat on 2026-09-27: hairline header with a trailing plus. The screenshot attached to this row is the problem as Kyle saw it.

## Problem

The grid header (`.wv-grid thead`) is a grey tinted band (`--tblr-bg-surface-secondary`) with rounded top corners. The add-field "+" sits in `th.add-field-head`, the one column with no width of its own, which takes whatever the fields leave of the card (Feature #233, rule 2). On a small table that stretches the grey band past the last field to the card edge: a long empty grey strip, a rounded corner, and a lonely "+". The bottom "+ New" bar (Feature #196) wears the same grey on hover, so the table reads bottom-heavy. Header behaviour (sticky, resize, reorder, freeze) is right and does not change; only the look is wrong.

## Spec

1. The header has no fill band. Labels sit on the card surface over one bottom hairline, one step stronger than the row separators.
2. Labels are sentence case (no uppercase, no tracking), 12 to 13px, weight 500, in the secondary colour.
3. The header background stays opaque (the card surface) so rows never show through while it is sticky. While the header is stuck during a vertical scroll it carries a very faint shadow below it; at rest it has none.
4. Hovering a column header tints that one header cell, the affordance for resize, reorder and the field menu.
5. The "+" trails the last field. On a small table it sits right after the last column, and the empty stretch after it carries no fill and no rounded corner. No field is stretched or squeezed to fill space (Feature #233, rule 2).
6. When the table overflows sideways the "+" stays reachable: the add-field cell is `position: sticky; right: 0` on an opaque surface background, with a short left fade so columns slide under it. The fade shows only while the grid overflows.
7. The bottom "+ New" bar drops its grey so it matches the hairline header.
8. Frozen columns, the column-drag insert line, the resize grip and dark mode still look right, in both themes.

## Acceptance tests

- The header cells' background is the card surface colour, in light and dark, and no header cell has a rounded corner.
- The header row's bottom rule uses the strong border token; the body row rule uses the default one.
- Header labels compute to `text-transform: none`, weight 500, 12 to 13px.
- On a small table the "+" button's left edge sits within 16px of the last field header's right edge, and every cell after the last field is transparent or the surface colour.
- On a wide table the add-field cell computes `position: sticky` and `right: 0px`, and its "+" stays inside the wrap's visible box scrolled to the far left and to the far right.
- The overflow fade shows on the wide table and not on the small one.
- The header carries no shadow at rest and a faint one once the grid has scrolled under it.
- The "+ New" button has no grey fill on hover.
- Existing gates for sticky headers, resize, reorder and freeze stay green.

## Shipped

Landed 2026-09-27 as Gerrit change 463 (http://localhost:8282/c/weave/+/463), commit `01701ab`, merged into gerrit/main at `a80878c` and mirrored to GitHub main at `a80878c`. The release that carries it links this row when it is cut; no version bump rode with the change.

- Gate: `weave-review.sh 463` voted Verified +1 on patchset 1 @ 01701ab: 2891 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (log `~/.gerrit/weave/review-logs/463-1.log`). Self-review Code-Review +2, submitted, MERGED.
- New suite `test/grid-hairline-header-browser.test.mjs`: 14 cases, 7 per theme, red on the parent (14 fail) and green on the change (14 pass).
- Updated: `test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs` and `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` no longer expect the "+" to take the slack; the forced ⋮ click in `test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs` scrolls Stage clear of the sticky "+" first.
- Serve: the deploy watcher restarted launchd's :4400 at 14:50:56 PDT, and `/api/health` reports `sha a80878c`, `stale false`. On :4400, Showcase/Notes paints its header at the surface colour (rgb(250, 250, 248)) with `text-transform: none`, the "+" 0px after the last field and 251px of bare card past it; Showcase/Field Types overflows, and its "+" cell computes `position: sticky; right: 0px`.
- Screenshots: before and after, both themes, attached to this row.

## Follow-up for Kyle

The Σ rollup row (`tr.wv-foot`, shown when a table opts in) still wears `--tblr-bg-surface-secondary`, so a table that shows it keeps a grey band under the hairline. The spec did not cover it, so it was left as it was.

features.name: Repoint a lookup or a rollup in place
features.description:
## Pain Point

A lookup or a rollup cannot be pointed somewhere else once it exists. Issue #387 made the settings tray show the recipe as read-only Relation, Field and Aggregate rows (Showcase › Field Types › Peer skill reads `Peers`, `Skill · rating`, `avg`), with the line "The recipe is set when the rollup is created and cannot be changed here." Changing any of the three still means deleting the column and adding a new one, which loses its name history, its width, its place in every view and any formula that reads it by name.

## Ask

Kyle decided on 2026-09-28 to keep the recipe read-only in Issue #387 and to file the editable recipe as this Feature rather than build it there.

With this Feature you could open a lookup's or a rollup's settings, pick another relation, another field on the far table or another aggregate, and save. The column keeps its name, description, width, views and position, and every cell shows the new result at the next read.

## What the engine needs

* **A repoint lane in `updateField`.** Today `updateField` accepts no `relationField`, `targetField` or `aggregate` for a lookup or a rollup. The lane should run the same validation `addField` runs (one shared recipe check), so an edit can never produce a column a create would refuse. A new relation keeps the old target field only if that field exists on the new far table; otherwise the edit must name one. An aggregate other than count needs a target field. A space rollup (`via`) stays read-only in the tray, since it is set from the grid's Σ row. The CLI (`weave field update`), the route (`PATCH /api/tables/:id/fields/:id`) and MCP (`weave_update_field`) take the same keys.
* **Stored values: none to migrate.** Lookups and rollups are computed on read, so a repoint changes every cell at the next read. The per-save column scale cache (`#scales`) is already cleared on every save.
* **The inherited display follows on its own.** `#ratingOf` and `#numberDisplay` read the new source: an avg of a rating that becomes a sum stops drawing stars, a count carries no display, and a number display or format on the old source no longer applies.
* **Formulas that read the column can break.** Formulas name the field, so they keep parsing, but the value they read can change type: a lookup gives a list, an avg a number, a join text. A repoint that changes the result type can turn a working formula into null or an error on every row. The engine should re-check dependent formulas with the `formula-check` scan and either refuse the repoint or name the formulas that now fail.
* **Filters, sorts and view settings** that name the field keep working by name, but a filter value or sort chosen for numbers stops making sense on text. The tray should warn when the result type changes.
* **Undo and history.** The edit is undoable like any other schema write, and the audit row names the old and the new recipe.

## Starting points

* Client: `throughRelation(fixed)` in `public/app.js` draws the three rows in the same `dsection` slots the create pickers use. Dropping the `fixed` flag and sending the recipe keys from `editPatchConfig` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` is the whole tray change.
* Engine: Gerrit change 443 (not landed, Verified -1 on patchset 4) carries a first repoint lane, `#recipe()` in `src/engine.js` with `test/rollup-recipe.test.mjs`. It does not re-check dependent formulas yet.
* Tests first: an engine contract per key (repoint by relation, field and aggregate; refused exactly where a create is refused; a dependent formula reported), the HTTP route, and a browser case that saves a repoint and sees the cell redraw, in both themes.

Filed by Claude (harness session 1b4685bd, 2026-09-28), following Issue #387.

features.name: Workspace system tables pinned in the nav: Activity, Trash, Workflows
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-09-29: "I want to create weave systems tables which live in the bottom of the left NAV cannot be renamed or reordered or deleted and are workspace-level tables for Activity, Trash, Workflows"

**Shape.** Three fixed rows pinned under the spaces in the left nav, in this order: Activity (the workspace activity feed, #/activity), Trash (every trashed row in the workspace, #/trash), Workflows (Workspace/Workflows, #/table/<id>). Workflows leaves the Workspace space list so it has one place in the nav. The rows carry no kebab and no grip.

**Engine.** updateTable refuses a rename of any system table (Workspace/Spaces, Tables, Fields, Workflows, Workspaces, Views) on every door: REST PATCH, MCP weave_update_table, CLI, and a Name edit on the Tables registry row. Writing the name a system table already has is accepted, so schema apply keeps working. Delete and move were already refused.

**Workspace trash.** New GET /api/trash lists every trashed row in the workspace (MCP weave_trash and CLI weave trash already did when no table is named). The page adds a Table column; a trashed table or space shows as its Workspace/Tables or Workspace/Spaces row, and Restore on that row restores the structure. Views rows are hidden there because they travel with their table.

Covers the sidebar-reachable half of Feature #160 for rows, tables and spaces. Tests: test/system-tables-nav.test.mjs.

features.name: Remove the built-in passkey door once provider sign-in has landed
features.description:
## Request
Kyle, 2026-09-29: "rip out our hard coded passkey handing now we've switched to clerk". Sign-in moves to one OpenID Connect provider (Clerk on his instance, Gerrit change 513, Feature #212). The hand-rolled WebAuthn door (Door B) goes.

## State when filed
- Change 513 is open with no Code-Review and no Verified vote. `gerrit/main` at `b83f657` holds no `WEAVE_OIDC` code.
- Production (https://weave.grunion.ai, main `b83f657`) offers passkeys only. The Railway service already carries `WEAVE_OIDC_ISSUER`, `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` and `WEAVE_OIDC_NAME`; they do nothing until 513 lands.
- Both production workspaces hold one account, `deploy-check`, with no passkey. No invite was ever minted there.

## Order that keeps a person able to sign in
1. Change 513 lands and deploys.
2. A person signs in through the provider on production.
3. This removal lands, stacked on 513 so it cannot land first.

## Scope
- Goes: `src/webauthn.js`, the `/api/auth/register/*` and `/api/auth/login/*` routes, the passkey and register-device parts of `src/auth-page.js`, the engine's credential and invite verbs, the CLI verbs `account invite` and `account remove-credential`, the MCP tools for them, the guide "Door B: passkeys" and every sentence that points at it, and the passkey tests.
- Stays: sessions (`wv_session` cookie, `account sessions`, `account revoke-session`), `wv_` tokens, `requireAuth`, `WEAVE_ORIGIN` and `WEAVE_TRUST_PROXY` where the provider door or the session cookie still reads them, share links and the applet passcode.
- Stored passkeys on existing accounts are left in the data and ignored; no migration deletes them.

## Open decision
This reverses the 2026-09-12 ruling in Feature #222 that every door is the operator's choice and none depends on another. After this, a self-hoster's choices are an edge gate (A) or a provider (C). The change stays parked without Code-Review +2 until Kyle confirms that scope.

features.name: Starter templates: one click builds a working CRM, personal finance, task or notes workspace
features.description:
Source: Kyle's 2026-10-02 walkthrough call with an outside tester, who pointed a stock Claude Code agent (no weave skills) at the public repo and asked it to build a budget and spending tracker.

Raised at 01:00:35 to 01:02:14 and 01:03:50: Kyle called first impressions "make or break" and proposed shipping prebuilt use cases. "Here's CRM. Here's how we've built CRM. You press one button. Give me this template. And it's built." Candidates named: CRM, expense tracking / personal finance, notepad, writing, tasks.

Shape: a Templates gallery on the new-workspace flow and an MCP verb (template.list, template.apply) so an agent can pick one before it improvises. Each template carries its tables, relations, display costumes, sample rows and a short agent note on how it is meant to grow. Personal finance should ship with Accounts, Transactions, Recurring, Income and a Months table rolling up recurring, income and net transactions per month (raised at 13:51 to 17:46).

Filed by the transcript-extraction session, 2026-10-02, v0.4.53, serving commit cc3b8d9.

## Progress 2026-10-03: three templates shipped

Landed in Gerrit change 563, commit e0481bb (weave v0.4.60 line, changelog fragment changelog.d/starter-templates-244.md). Chosen from a review of Kyle's sessions: personal finance came up five times, tasks four, a CRM four, docs twice, so Docs is gone.

**Shipped.** Onboarding step 3 and the first-run empty state offer three cards, in this order. Titles and blurbs are the copywriter's finals, and a card's title is its space's name.

| Card | Blurb | Tables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Money | Transactions and income, totaled by month | Transactions (Date, Amount in USD, Category, Account, Month), Accounts (Kind), Recurring (Amount, linked to its Transactions), Income (Amount, Date, Month), Months (Spent and Earned rollups, Net = Earned - Spent) |
| Work | Tasks with status, due date and priority | Tasks (Status workflow, Due, Priority) |
| People | Companies by stage, linked to their contacts | Companies (Website, Stage), Contacts (Email, Phone, Company) |

- Each template is a weave_build spec (Feature #253): the empty state sends one POST /api/build, POST /api/onboarding runs the same build server side. The old steps() walk is gone, so templates have no builder of their own.
- Sample rows ship: build already takes rows, so each template carries a few, dated to the month it is built in. Money's Months row shows Spent $193.02, Earned $3,200.00, Net $3,006.98 out of the box.
- Transactions has no separate Description column: every table already carries a Description document field.
- Months avoids date-grain formulas (Issues #576, #590). Linking a transaction to its month is by hand.
- Handbook "Making a workspace your own" names the three and how Money totals a month; applied to the live workspace.
- Gate: test/starter-core.test.mjs (each template builds clean; two transactions and one income on one month compute Spent, Earned and Net), test/onboarding.test.mjs, test/onboarding-browser.test.mjs, test/first-run-browser.test.mjs. Patch set 1 gate: non-browser 2423/2423, browser 982/982.
- Screenshots attached: step 3 light, dark and 375 px; Money/Transactions, the Money space page and Money/Months after picking Money.

**Still open here.**
- The MCP verb (template.list, template.apply) so an agent can pick a template before it improvises.
- A Templates gallery beyond the three cards, and the per-template agent note on how it is meant to grow.

features.name: Onboarding: a short welcome that starts by naming the first workspace
features.description:
Source: Kyle in a harness session, 2026-10-02: "need to add an onboarding flow to weave starting from naming the first workspace give defaults, but let the user rename always allow skip design using weave language. friendly welcome low text."

Low text: one heading and at most one short line per step. Built from weave's own parts: the shared dialog (Issue #263), Tabler tokens, soft squared chips, Lucide icons, both themes, phone width. features.name: Workflows table is the automation control panel: one row per automation, an on/off toggle on every row
features.description:
Decision (Kyle, 2026-10-02): each automation is a row in the built-in Workspace/Workflows table, and that table is the control panel for them. This settles open decision 1 on the three-horizon roadmap (a rule is a row, not a bespoke editor).

Today: engine automations live in state.automations (3 triggers, 4 actions, CRUD over REST, MCP and the CLI) and the browser only draws them on the relation map. Workspace/Workflows carries Script, State, Health and Last Run fields, holds 0 rows on :4400, and nothing executes it. The two never meet.

Target shape (mockup shown in session 2026-10-02):
- One Workflows row per automation. Trigger and actions are field values on the row.
- An On toggle field (the existing toggle type, Feature #202) is the first column. Off means the engine skips the row.
- Columns: On, Name, When (table and trigger), Then (actions), Health, Last run. The engine stamps Last run and Health on every fire.
- A workspace-wide switch in the table header pauses every row without changing each row's toggle.
- Migration moves existing state.automations into rows; REST, MCP and CLI keep their verbs and read and write the rows.
- The ontology page moves automations from machinery to rows in the same commit.

Open for Kyle: does the toggle replace the State select (Draft, Active, Deactivated); keep or strike the workspace-wide switch; does a failing row stay on or turn itself off.

Unblocks Feature #227 (inbound webhooks). Related: Feature #242 (system rows in the nav), Issues #561 and #562.

Filed by Claude Code session 2026-10-02, weave v0.4.54, commit cc3b8d9.

2026-10-02: the first slice shipped in weave v0.4.56 (Gerrit 535, commit 11a5dfc). Every row of Workspace/Workflows now carries a system On toggle, worded On / Off, off until switched, first after Name in the field order and the Standard view, minted on existing workspaces at load. The engine does not read it yet, the State select stays, and state.automations is not migrated; those are the next slices and wait on the open questions above.

Ruling (Kyle, 2026-10-03): three separate columns, one owner each.
- On is the user's switch and nothing else. The engine never flips it.
- State is setup: Setup incomplete or Ready. While a row is Setup incomplete and Off, its toggle is greyed and cannot be switched on. A row whose setup breaks while On (for example its trigger field is deleted) keeps On, the engine skips it, and the user can still switch it off.
- Health is runtime: Healthy, Warning, Failed, No runs. "On but broken" lives here, with the reason on hover. A failing row stays On; it never turns itself off.
- This answers two of the three open questions above. The toggle does not replace State; State changes from Draft/Active/Deactivated to Setup incomplete/Ready, since Deactivated duplicates Off. A failing row stays on. Still open: keep or strike the workspace-wide pause switch.
- Mockup: show_widget weave_workflows_toggle_state_health_v2, session 2026-10-03.


2026-10-05: the engine slice shipped in weave v0.4.67 (Gerrit 633, commit 5f6931d; release 047ae4a). Every automation is a Workflows row: the Script holds the rule as JSON {table, trigger, actions} with names; On gates every fire and the engine never writes it; State is Setup incomplete / Ready, computed on every write and structural change, and a Setup incomplete row that is Off refuses On with the reason; Health (Healthy green, Warning amber, Failed red, No runs slate) with a new Health Reason text field, and Last Run, are stamped on every fire; a rule broken while On stays On, is skipped and reads Failed. state.automations migrated onto rows (adopting same-name rows on the same table). REST, MCP and CLI verbs read and write the rows. Verified on Net: rows #4 and #5 were adopted (no duplicates), State Ready, listed by weave_automations; #5 Off left Request #4 unresolved at Done, #5 On ticked Request #5 with Modified By workflow:<#5 id>, Health Healthy and Last Run stamped. Still open: the workspace-wide pause switch, the UI for State/Health/reason (parallel UI change), and Warning, which nothing raises yet.

features.name: Hosted instance updates itself in place: a supervisor swaps workers on a new release with no failed request
features.description:
Decision (Kyle, 2026-10-02): the hosted instance at https://weave.grunion.ai keeps itself on the newest release without a Railway redeploy and without a dark window. Chosen over a Railway GitHub trigger, a holding relay, a web/storage split and a Durable Objects port.

## Measured
- 2026-10-02: `/api/health` answered `version 0.4.53`, `latestRelease 0.4.54`, `releaseBehind true`, uptime 29 h. v0.4.54 (`cc3b8d96`) reached GitHub main 08:57Z and Railway built nothing.
- Railway service `weave` (`6027b050-4307-4386-8d21-296328a92640`) has no repo trigger; every deployment on record was started by hand (Issue #478).
- A volume-backed Railway service cannot run two deployments at once, so every Railway redeploy has a gap. Last deploy: created 19:56:35Z, container up 20:00:03Z, healthy 20:01:04Z.
- weave has zero runtime dependencies (`node:sqlite`) and no WebSocket or event-stream routes, so a new release is a source tarball and nothing else.

## Shape
1. `bin/weave.js supervise` holds the listening port and runs the server as a child worker. Railway's start command becomes `supervise`.
2. The supervisor reuses the existing release check (`src/update-check.js`). On `releaseBehind`, it downloads the tag's tarball from GitHub, accepts it only when the tag's commit is on `grunion-ai/weave` main, and unpacks it to `/data/releases/v<version>/`.
3. It starts a second worker from that directory on a side port against the same SQLite files (WAL), polls its `/api/health`, then routes new connections to it and lets the old worker drain in-flight requests before exit.
4. Migrations: the new worker opens read-compatible, and runs schema migrations only after the old worker has exited.
5. Failure keeps the old worker serving and records the attempt; a release that fails health is not retried until the next release.
6. `/api/health` reports which release directory is serving and when the last swap ran. Railway rebuilds remain only for Node version or Dockerfile changes.
7. Settings: `WEAVE_AUTO_UPDATE=1` opts in, so local installs do not change behaviour.

## Verify
- Test: a load loop of requests across a swap returns zero errors; a release whose health fails leaves the old worker serving; a tag off main is refused.
- Live: on the next release, a 1 s probe of `/api/health` shows the version change with no failed probe, and Railway shows no new deployment.

Closes Issue #478 once live. Deploy guide "Deploy: Railway" states the self-update path.

Filed by the harness session 2026-10-02 (Claude Opus 5.5), live instance v0.4.53.

---

**Shipped 2026-10-03 (Feature #250 harness session, Claude Opus 5.5).**
- Code: Gerrit 537, commit 94202475, merged as dc1a47f (`src/supervisor.js`, `weave supervise`, deferred migrations in the engine, Deploy: Railway step 7). Gate green: 2357 + 973 pass, 0 fail. Released in v0.4.57 (Gerrit 551, a53abd8).
- Fix after the first live swap: Gerrit 555, merged as 80f342a (Issue #607, settle wrote every row). Released in v0.4.60 (Gerrit 557, 5602c56). Docs: Gerrit 553 (no hand Railway deploys).
- Bootstrap: Railway start command `node bin/weave.js supervise`, `WEAVE_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, deployment afb54d54 of dc1a47f, SUCCESS 06:14:56Z; health showed the supervisor block and every walled path answered 401 (admin tokens 200).
- First live swaps: v0.4.57 -> v0.4.58 at 07:02:47Z went through the supervisor with no Railway deployment, but two 1 s probes timed out (Issue #607); v0.4.58 -> v0.4.59 at 07:32:47Z ran unobserved.
- Live proof, v0.4.59 -> v0.4.60, 2026-10-03: the supervisor installed v0.4.60 from its tag at 07:52:47.505Z (`/api/health` → `supervisor: {release: "v0.4.60", dir: "/data/releases/v0.4.60", lastSwap: {from: "v0.4.59", to: "v0.4.60", ok: true}}`). A probe sent `GET /api/health` (expect 200) and `GET /api/workspace` (walled, expect 401) every second from 07:38:26Z to 07:54:29Z: 954 ticks, 1,908 requests, 0 unexpected answers. In the 30 s either side of the swap, 60 ticks (120 requests), 0 non-200 health answers, 0 non-401 wall answers, slowest 1.3 s. A second health-only probe, 994 requests from 07:37:15Z to 07:53:49Z, 0 failed. Railway's newest deployment is still 9364ec65 (06:42:26Z, a hand deploy by another session), so no Railway build ran for v0.4.58, v0.4.59 or v0.4.60.

features.name: Sign-in asks the provider for no personal information
features.description:
## Request
Kyle, 2026-10-02, looking at the Clerk consent screen on his phone: "I dont actually want anyones personal infromation". The screen at accounts.weave.grunion.ai lists three grants: verify your identity, your email address, your basic profile information.

## Measured
- `src/oidc.js:106` requests `scope: 'openid email profile'`.
- `profile` is never read. `oidc.js:128` returns only `{ issuer, subject, email, emailVerified }`.
- `email` has one job: the first sign-in pins a subject to an identity that an admin linked by email (`engine.js:3215-3265`, `accountForIdentity`). After the pin, the subject alone matches.
- The email stays on `account.identities[]` and in the `identity-linked`, `identity-unlinked` and `identity-pinned` audit entries after it has done that job.
- `oidc.js:123` falls back to the userinfo endpoint to fetch an email when the id token has none.

## Good looks like
Tailscale and Fly invite a person with a one-time link; the service records the provider subject at redemption and keeps no email. The consent screen then lists one line, "Verify your identity".

## Fix shape
1. Scope becomes `openid`. Remove the userinfo email fallback.
2. Linking an identity mints a single-use, expiring invite code (stored as a hash) instead of taking an email. Redeeming it after a provider sign-in pins `{ issuer, subject }` to the account. `POST /api/accounts/:name/identities` returns the invite link; `DELETE` unlinks by subject.
3. Migration: identities that already carry a pinned subject drop their email field. Unpinned email-only identities become pending invites. Scrub emails out of existing identity audit entries.
4. Clerk OAuth application `oa_3K6ajZDiOLdqHfSeCXqwo0njgdf`: scopes to `openid` only. Consent screen off is a follow-up that also helps Issue #569.

Clerk still holds the email it needs to run sign-in; weave stops asking for it and stops storing it.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-02 against weave v0.4.54 (cc3b8d9). Related: Feature #212, Feature #243, Issue #569, Issue #570.

features.name: Build verb: one call creates a whole workspace outline, tables, fields, relations and rows
features.description:
Source: canned disclosure eval, 2026-10-02 (32 stock-agent runs over MCP on v0.4.54) plus a one-turn probe of claude -p with and without the weave MCP server. Data: ~/Documents/queue/weave-disclosure-eval/.

Measured: agents spend 50 to 100 turns building a 5-table workspace because every field, relation and row is its own call (16 add_field, 12 create_entity, 3 to 4 add_relation per run). weave_apply_schema exists but was used 0 times in 32 runs: it takes the 22 KB document weave_schema emits, which no agent writes by hand.

Shape: weave_build (MCP), POST /api/build (REST) and weave build <file> (CLI) take one compact spec: optional workspace name; spaces; tables with fields written as short entries ({name, type, plus that type's settings}); relations by table name; optional rows per table with relation values by name. dryRun validates the whole spec and returns every error at once. Apply runs in one transaction in dependency order (tables, fields, relations, rows) and returns a compact summary: counts, created names, ignored keys, errors. The spec format is the same one a starter template ships in (Feature #244).

Filed by the token-efficiency session, 2026-10-02, v0.4.54, commit cc3b8d9.

2026-10-03, build-verb session: landed as Gerrit change 542 (patch set 4), commit 84fbc27, merge 0722ca7 on gerrit/main; ships in the next release after v0.4.60. Spec as built, the same on all three doors: MCP weave_build {spec, dryRun?, skipExistingRows?} (a bare spec without the wrapper is accepted); REST POST /api/build with body {spec, dryRun?, skipExistingRows?} or the bare spec, 200 when ok and 400 when not; CLI weave build <spec.json> [--dry-run] [--skip-existing-rows], exit 1 when not ok. Top-level keys: workspace (string, renames the workspace when it differs), description (workspace description), spaces (list). A space is {name, icon?, description?, tables}; a table is {name, icon?, description?, fields?, rows?}. A field is {name, type, ...config}: the config keys weave_add_field takes for that type, written flat (select: options [{name, color?}]; number: format, currency, decimals; date: grain, format; lookup: relationField, targetField; rollup: relationField, targetField, aggregate; formula: expression). A relation is a field {name, type: "relation", to: <table name, Space/Table or a list for a target set>, cardinality?: many-to-one (default) | one-to-many | many-to-many | one-to-one, inverseName?}; to resolves to a table in the same spec first. A row is {Name, <field>: value, ...}; a relation value is the target row's Name (or a list of names). Order: workspace, spaces, tables, plain fields, relations, lookups and rollups, formulas, rows, then the rows' relation values, so rows link by name to rows made in the same call. Existing spaces, tables and same-typed fields are reused and listed in existing; a field that exists with another type is an error at its path. Rows append; skipExistingRows: true skips a row whose Name the table already holds. A refused icon (space, table, rating, option, state) or option colour is dropped and listed in ignored with a reason; it never blocks the thing that wears it. A step that fails only because an earlier one did is not charged a second error. Validation: the whole spec, rows included, runs first on an in-memory copy of the workspace; dryRun: true stops there and writes nothing, and any error means nothing is written. The real run is not one transaction: a failure after a clean trial (not seen in tests) returns what landed plus the error. Reply, one line of JSON: {ok, dryRun?, created: {spaces, tables, fields, relations, rows}, existing: ["space Budget", "table Budget/Account", "field Budget/Account.Kind", "row Budget/Account: Amex Gold"], ignored: [{path, keys, reason?}], errors: [{path, error}]}, paths like spaces[0].tables[1].fields[2] or spaces[0].tables[1].rows[0]. weave_build is in the default MCP tool list (58 tools, 16 listed). Example: {"workspace":"personal-finance","spaces":[{"name":"Budget","icon":"lucide:wallet","tables":[{"name":"Account","fields":[{"name":"Kind","type":"select","options":[{"name":"Credit card"},{"name":"Checking"}]}],"rows":[{"Name":"Amex Gold","Kind":"Credit card"}]},{"name":"Transaction","fields":[{"name":"Amount","type":"number","format":"currency","currency":"USD"},{"name":"Date","type":"date"},{"name":"Account","type":"relation","to":"Account","cardinality":"many-to-one"}],"rows":[{"Name":"Whole Foods","Amount":142.18,"Date":"2026-08-03","Account":"Amex Gold"}]}]}]} replies {"ok":true,"created":{"spaces":1,"tables":2,"fields":3,"relations":1,"rows":2},"existing":[],"ignored":[],"errors":[]}. Found along the way: Issue #598 (a lookup of a select shows the option id).

Validation 2026-10-03 (disclosure-eval session): 16 stock Claude Code runs under Claude Code defaults (tool search on) against a scratch clone of gerrit/main at 0722ca7, two canned tasks, two runs per cell. R0 = main as landed (16 core tools, no MCP instructions): Opus 0.78 at $1.52 per run, Sonnet 0.72 at $0.42; 15 of 16 runs called weave_build. R1 = main plus a 995-character build-first primer in initialize.instructions: Opus 0.94 at $1.69, Sonnet 0.91 at $0.30 in 13 turns. Today (pre-#253 surface) was Opus 0.75 at $2.32, Sonnet 0.69 at $0.75. The proxy prototype with next[] and hints[] on the build reply scored Opus 1.00 and Sonnet 0.97; the gap is option icons, colour and the month grain, so plan steps F2 (primer) and F4 (hints on the build reply) are what remain. Runs: ~/Documents/queue/weave-disclosure-eval/runs/*-R0ts-* and *-R1ts-*.

Correction 2026-10-03 (disclosure-eval session): the validation above ran on claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5; a CLI update then moved the opus and sonnet aliases to the 5.5 models. Rerun on opus-5-5 and sonnet-5-5 against the same commit 0722ca7: main as landed Opus $0.71 and Sonnet $0.28 per run, main plus primer Opus $0.52 in 9 to 14 calls and Sonnet $0.33. Same models, Airtable Opus $0.80 and Fibery Opus $1.25. Call anatomy and remaining levers: Issues #625 to #628, report https://claude.ai/artifact/KQkSmhRZ1uhxVKobKhmQzh.

features.name: Hosted MCP sign-in: terminal command opens the browser for OAuth (mcp.weave.grunion.ai)
features.description:
**Sign in to the hosted MCP server from a terminal, through the browser.** Kyle asked 2026-10-02 for `mcp.weave.grunion.ai`, where a user runs one command and authenticates with Clerk in the browser. Today an agent needs a `wv_` token minted by an admin and pasted into its config; no person can connect an agent on their own.

## What the user does

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http weave https://mcp.weave.grunion.ai/mcp
```

The first call (or `/mcp`, Authenticate) opens Clerk in the browser. Codex: `codex mcp login weave`. The client stores and refreshes the token.

## Shape

1. **Protected resource (RFC 9728).** `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (and the `/mcp`-suffixed path) names the configured OIDC issuer as the authorization server. `/mcp` without a credential answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`.
2. **Token check, zero dependencies.** A bearer that is not a `wv_` token goes to the issuer's `userinfo_endpoint` (from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, already fetched by `src/oidc.js`). A verified email maps to an account through the Door C identity link. Cache by sha256 of the token with a short TTL; never store the token. Unlinked email: 403. Rejected token: 401.
3. **Routes.** `/mcp` serves the default workspace, `/w/<name>/mcp` the others; both reuse `handleMcpMessage`. `/api/mcp` stays. The wall stays per workspace.
4. **Audit.** Writes record the account and the OAuth client: "kyle via Claude Code".
5. **`wv_` tokens keep working** on every route.
6. **Provider-agnostic.** Clerk is configuration; any OIDC issuer with dynamic client registration works.

## Infra (outside the code)

- Railway custom domain `mcp.weave.grunion.ai` on service `weave`; Cloudflare CNAME (DNS only) plus `_railway-verify.mcp.weave` TXT.
- Clerk production instance (`clerk.weave.grunion.ai`): dynamic client registration on.
- Railway deploys by hand (no trigger, Issue #478).

## Gate

Tests: 401 header, metadata document, userinfo to account mapping, unlinked 403, rejected 401, cache hit, `wv_` path unchanged, per-workspace route. Live: Kyle signs in once from Claude Code and `tools/list` returns the weave tools.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-02 (weave v0.4.54 on main, v0.4.53 live).


## Built 2026-10-02

Gerrit change 544 (`mcp: agents sign in to a hosted instance through the browser (Feature #254)`), patch set 4, commit 28e15e1 on top of gerrit/main c869a17. Code-Review +2 by the building session; not landed when this was written: the Verified gate queue had not reached it, and the session's two gate runs both stopped on a merge conflict with a moving main before any test ran. Whoever lands it: wait for Verified +1 (or run `weave-review.sh 544 --submit`), then submit.

What changed against the plan above:

- **Identity is the subject, not the email.** Feature #252 landed mid-build: Door C now links by an invite that pins the provider subject, asks for `openid` alone and keeps no email. The MCP door follows it. Userinfo is read for `sub` only, `accountForIdentity({issuer, subject})` runs on the URL workspace then the hub root, and the metadata's `scopes_supported` is `["openid"]`. A subject with no account answers 403 telling the person to open their invite (`weave account link <name>`) in a browser once.
- **Roles.** Feature #255 renamed admin to Architect; MCP over HTTP stays Architect-only, so the linked account needs that role.
- **Audit.** Writes record `<account> via <client>`. The client is the access token's `client_id` (or `azp`) when the token is a JWT; Clerk's tokens are opaque, so in practice it reads `kyle via oauth`.
- **Origins.** New env `WEAVE_MCP_ORIGINS` (comma separated, e.g. `https://mcp.weave.grunion.ai`). The resource origin is the configured origin (WEAVE_ORIGIN or this list) whose host the request arrived on, else WEAVE_ORIGIN; the Host header is never echoed, and each listed host is added to the served hosts.
- **Extras.** Five refused tokens a minute per address get 429 (each unknown token costs a provider call); a provider that is down gets 502, not 401, so the client does not loop through sign-in. `GET /mcp` is 405. Token answers are cached 60 s by sha256, capped at 1000 entries.
- **Known limit, documented in the Handbook:** no RFC 8707 audience check, since Clerk does not bind tokens to a resource.

Tests: `test/mcp-oauth.test.mjs`, 13 cases (metadata on three paths, 404 without an issuer, 401 challenge per workspace, origin by Host, userinfo to account, JWT client in audit, unlinked 403, rejected 401 with negative cache, positive cache, wv_ unchanged, per-workspace isolation, 429 and 502, 405). Focused suites 97/97. Full suite on the PS4 tree: 2341 + 963 pass, 0 fail.

Live check after deploy: set `WEAVE_MCP_ORIGINS=https://mcp.weave.grunion.ai` on Railway, add the custom domain, turn on dynamic client registration in Clerk, and make sure Kyle's account is Architect and its identity is pinned (he has signed in once in a browser since v0.4.55).

Filed by the Feature #254 build session, 2026-10-02, change 544 PS4 (28e15e1).



## Shipped in v0.4.59, verified live 2026-10-03

Landed as Gerrit change 544 (merge 8d5ce63, after a rebase onto the invite change), released as v0.4.59 (change 554); the host installed the tag itself at 07:32 UTC (supervisor swap v0.4.58 to v0.4.59, no Railway redeploy). Kyle ran `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http weave https://weave.grunion.ai/mcp`, signed in through Clerk, and `claude mcp list` reports weave Connected. No `mcp.weave.grunion.ai`: Railway's plan allows one custom domain per service, and Kyle chose path routing. The Clerk consent page confused him: Issue #610.

features.name: Roles: Observer, Editor and Architect
features.description:
## Request

Kyle, 2026-10-02, verbatim: "Observer (free) can only view and comment, Editor (paid seat) can view and create/edit entities, Architect (paid) everything including create delete edit workspace spaces tables, field definitions". Asked as part of "fix the 403 dead end for new people" (Issue #569): an invited person needs a role to land in.

## Measured before

- `src/engine.js` `Weave.ROLES = ['admin', 'writer', 'reader']`, default `writer`.
- `src/routes.js` caps: a `reader` could not POST at all (`This token is read-only`), so a reader could not comment; a `writer` was already refused every schema verb (spaces, tables, fields, relations, views, workspace PATCH, `/api/mcp`, registry rows, bulk into system tables) and workspace create/delete (hub-root admin gate).
- Comment author on `POST /api/entities/:id/comments` was whatever the body said (the app sends `me`).

## Shape

- reader -> observer, writer -> editor, admin -> architect. Every open (`#migrate`, so import too) rewrites a stored old name; routes read any old name still on a row through `Weave.roleName`, so a `wv_` token or session minted before keeps opening the account.
- Observer: reads, posts a comment (author forced to the account name) and deletes a comment it made; every other write is 403. Weave has no comment edit verb for any role, so there is nothing to edit.
- Editor: what writer had. Architect: what admin had.
- CLI, REST, MCP and the handbook use the new names; `--role admin|writer|reader` and the REST/MCP `role` field still take the old names for one release and answer with a `note` naming the new one.
- Labels: `Weave.ROLE_LABELS` = Architect, paid / Editor, paid seat / Observer, free. Billing words only; see the seats and billing Feature row.

Filed by the roles-and-invites session, 2026-10-02, weave v0.4.54 at 9f252d7.



Shipped 2026-10-03: Gerrit change 545, commit ba84b1f (merge 2279058), gate 2300/2300 node and 962/962 browser; Railway deployment 18a9bc97-04fa-4e63-8fad-6b3040da69ba, live accounts read architect. The role picker with the billing labels arrived with Issue #569 (change 549, c4d17fe). A role weave does not know is held to observer caps.

features.description:
## Request

## Measured

- A seat count per workspace: Editors plus Architects, Observers free.
- A payment provider and a plan record; the invite form shows the seat it will use.
- A role change verb (none exists today; an account's role is fixed at creation) that asks for a seat on Observer -> Editor.

features.name: Forms: submit one row into a table without write access (the bug reporter becomes the first form)
features.description:
**A form lets someone create one row in one table without write access to it.** Kyle, 2026-10-02: everyone is an Observer in the built-in `weave` docs workspace, and everyone may still submit a bug, through "a type of form" (recorded on Feature #141).

## Today

Bug reports file through a dedicated route, `POST /api/bug-report` (`src/routes.js`, Feature #142), into `Development/Issue` in the docs workspace. It hard-codes the table, the fields (symptoms, note, action trace) and the server-supplied version stamp. Nothing else in weave can take a submission from a reader.

## Shape

- A form is a row (likely a `Workspace/Views` kind or its own registry table) naming a target table, the fields shown, their order, labels and defaults, hidden fields the server fills (version, reporter, time), and who may submit (a role floor such as Observer, or signed-out visitors).
- Submitting creates exactly one row and nothing else: no reads of other rows, no edits, no schema. The submitter is the actor in the audit log.
- Every surface: a page in the web app, `POST /api/forms/<id>/submit`, an MCP tool, a CLI verb (agent-surface gate).
- The bug reporter becomes the first form, keeping its symptoms, trace and server stamp; `/api/bug-report` stays as an alias.

## Gate

Tests: an Observer submits and gets one row; an Observer cannot write the table directly; hidden fields cannot be set by the submitter; a disabled form refuses; the bug reporter's existing tests pass through the form.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-02 (weave v0.4.54 on main).

features.name: Flicker loop: probe, nightly sweep and ratchet
features.description:
Weave finds its own UI flickers every night, files them, and keeps the fixed ones fixed.

What: (1) a page probe, test/lib/flicker.mjs, that reports what the reader saw for less than 150 ms and should not have: a node painted and swapped for different content (transient), an element painted empty and refilled (blank), a class, hidden or style that flipped and flipped back (revert), content that moved with no input (shift), and an A, B, A run in the Chromium screencast (frame). Swaps that answer a keystroke or press within 50 ms, identical redraws, zero-size live regions and same-value attribute writes are not counted. (2) Nine journeys in test/lib/journeys.mjs on a messy 400-row seed: load, open a table, scroll, edit a cell, open a row in the dock, switch view, type in a document, trash and undo, flip the theme. (3) scripts/flicker-sweep.mjs walks them three times and keeps what two runs saw, with the frames around each sighting. (4) test/flicker-gate-browser.test.mjs walks every journey in the Gerrit gate and fails when a journey cannot finish or a fingerprint listed in test/flicker-fixed.json comes back. (5) Harness routine weave-flicker (launchd ai.grunion.weave-flicker, 01:30/02:30/03:30, first quiet fire runs) sweeps gerrit/main and files one Issue row per new defect with flicker-fp: marker lines; the overnight fixer closes a row by adding its fingerprint to flicker-fixed.json.

Why: Kyle, 2026-10-03, asked for a loop that tracks UI flickers and eliminates them, to raise weave's polish. Before this, public/app.js (13,840 lines) carried no flicker or layout-shift telemetry and 1 of 168 open Issues described a flicker. The first baseline sweep on gerrit/main 29f6d99 confirmed a skeleton painted for 12 to 88 ms on fast loads, grid rows swapped while scrolling, and a layout shift of 0.56 on the grid spacer.

Filed by the flicker-loop session, 2026-10-03, on gerrit/main 29f6d99.

features.name: MCP injection measurement harness

`security/mcp-inject/` measures whether an agent working through weave's MCP server carries out an instruction planted in workspace data. features.name: Use Template: a template space copies its schema into another workspace
features.description:
Source: Kyle, 2026-10-05. A CRM template space will live in the weave workspace on the main instance. Any space can be marked as a template; a template space shows a Use Template button that copies the space's schema, never its rows, into a workspace the user picks.

## Shape

- `template` is a space attribute, like `icon`: `updateSpace(id, { template: true })`, a Template checkbox on the space's Workspace/Spaces registry row (the row edit and the verb are two doors onto one write), `template: true` in describeSchema, applied by applySchema.
- The copy is the space's describeSchema() entry, carried whole: tables, fields and their config, option colours and icons, workflow states and icons, column widths, field order, hidden fields, filters, sort, views, body blocks, the term, the space icon and the table icons. Rows never travel.
- A relation whose target table lies outside the space is left out and named in the result as skipped; relations, lookups, rollups and formulas inside the space travel intact. The copy is never itself marked as a template.
- Engine verb `useTemplate(space, target, { name })` where target is another workspace engine; applySchema gains a `partial` option so a one-space document leaves the target's other spaces alone. A target that already holds a live space of that name is refused with a conflict.
- Route `POST /api/spaces/:id/use { workspace, name? }` on the source workspace; the caller needs to read the source and to be an architect on the target (`roleOn`). `GET /api/templates` lists the workspace's template spaces.
- UI: the space page shows Use Template when the space is a template; the dialog offers every other workspace of the hub and a name prefilled with the space's name; success toasts a link to the new space.
- CLI `weave template list` and `weave template use <space> --into <other.db> [--name N]`; MCP `weave_template_list` and `weave_template_use`, the verbs Feature #244 still owed.
- Gate: a fidelity test builds a space wearing every costume, uses it as a template into a fresh workspace, and compares the two describeSchema entries after stripping ids, urls and counts; the outside relation is the one named difference.

Related: Feature #244 (starter templates: a build spec per card). This feature makes any live space a template, so a template is a space someone has already shaped, not a spec in the code.

Filed by the use-template session, 2026-10-05, weave v0.4.65, commit a438721.


## Shipped

Gerrit change 603, commit 52acab9 (on top of v0.4.65; rides the next release). Gate: lifecycle pack + full suite green, 1089 of 1090 browser cases (one skip for overlay scrollbars), patch set 2. Patch set 1 went red on the new browser case: the row-page checkbox locator met the grid boxes still on screen after a hash change; the row page now opens in its own page.

- Engine: `template` space attribute, Workspace/Spaces **Template** checkbox (minted on open), `templateDoc()`, `useTemplate()`, `listTemplates()`, `applySchema(..., { partial })`.
- Doors: `GET /api/templates`, `POST /api/spaces/:id/use`, `weave template list|use`, MCP `weave_template_list`, `weave_template_use` (HTTP).
- UI: Use template on a template space page, dialog with workspace picker and name; conflict and refusal said in the dialog; checked at 375 px in both themes.
- Handbook guide **Templates**.
- applySchema gaps found by the fidelity test and fixed here: Issues #639, #640, #641, #642.
- Tests: test/use-template.test.mjs, test/use-template-routes.test.mjs, test/use-template-browser.test.mjs, test/schema-roundtrip.test.mjs.

features.name: Template exercise: every template's tables, fields and relations are exercised in suite and against live instance
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-10-05: "as part of our testing workflow I want to confirm add remove link works for all templates and template tables and fields as well as use template works to implement template in test workspace."

## Shape

1. **Fixtures.** `test/fixtures/templates/crm.json` holds the live CRM template (the `CRM` space of the weave workspace, `template: true`) as `templateDoc()` output: no ids, urls or counts. `scripts/template-fixture.mjs [--base http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/weave] [--space CRM]` rewrites it from a running instance, so the fixture follows the live template.
2. **One exercise, two adapters.** `scripts/template-exercise-core.mjs` exports `exerciseTable(api, table)`. `api` is `createRow`, `updateRow`, `getRow`, `link`, `unlink`, `deleteRow`, `restoreRow`, `listRows`, backed by an engine or by HTTP. Per table: add a row that sets every writable field by type (text, number with currency and percent formats, date, checkbox, url, email, select, multiselect, workflow by state name, document) and read each value back; for every relation, make a row in the target table, link it, assert the link from both ends (the inverse field on the far row), check every lookup, rollup and formula answers while linked, unlink, assert both ends empty; soft-delete the row, assert it is in the trash and out of the list, restore it, assert it is back; hard-delete everything it made. Returns `{ table, fields, relations, computed, ok, failures }`.
3. **Suite.** `test/template-exercise.test.mjs`: every fixture is applied with `applySchema(partial)` into a fresh engine, marked a template, listed by `listTemplates()`, exercised table by table, then copied with `useTemplate()` into a second engine named `test`; the copy describes equal to `templateDoc()` of the source and passes the same exercise. The three starter templates in `public/starter-core.js` are built with `build()` and exercised too.
4. **Live.** `scripts/template-exercise.mjs --base http://127.0.0.1:4400 --from weave --into test` runs the exercise over HTTP on every template space of `weave`, uses each into `test` under a timestamped name, exercises the copy, deletes the copy, prints a table per template and exits non-zero on any failure. A real defect it finds is filed as a `Development/Issue` row and the suite asserts the gap with the Issue number.
5. **Docs.** The Templates guide in the Handbook names the suite and the live script.

Filed by template-exercise session, 2026-10-05 (Claude Opus, weave gerrit/main 048ef0a).

features.name: Rich link previews: a permalink unfurls as the mark, workspace › space › table, #id and name while the uuid stays the address
features.description:
## Decision

Kyle, 2026-10-05, after the link-surfaces mockups (https://claude.ai/artifact/Mr3A2s2XEJGu6bA4zbg6ns): the uuid routes stay the address for workspaces, spaces, tables and rows, so every link is unique and survives renames. The preview does the reading. A pasted permalink unfurls with the weave mark or the workspace logo, the path (workspace › space › table), the public id and a name snippet. The uuid never needs to appear in a preview, a share sheet or a chat card.

## Today, verified on :4400 at e2621b3 (v0.4.66)

- `GET /w/weave/e/<uuid>` answers 302 to `/w/weave/#/entity/<uuid>`. A fetcher that follows it gets `public/index.html`: `<title>Weave</title>`, no `og:` or `twitter:` meta. Every row previews as "Weave".
- `/e/Issue%23287` resolves the same way; `/e/287` 404s.
- On weave.grunion.ai an anonymous GET 302s to `/w/weave/auth?next=…`, then to accounts.weave.grunion.ai, which answers Slack's fetcher with 403. Nothing unfurls, nothing leaks.
- `engine.previewFields(id)` (state first, then non-empty simple fields in schema order, limit 3) and `resolveMention`'s `Issue#287 — name` label already exist. `/api/workspace/logo` serves the workspace logo typed from its bytes.


## The change

1. **Permalink answers with meta.** `GET /w/<ws>/e/<ref>` (uuid or `Table#n`) answers 200 with the app shell plus a server-rendered head, then jumps to the hash route with `location.replace` so Back behaves as it does today. Head: `<title>Issue #287 · <name> · weave</title>`, `og:title` = `Issue #287 · <name snippet>` (cut around 80 characters), `og:description` = `weave › Development › Issue` on one line and the state plus previewFields on the next (`Status Fixed · Severity Medium · Symptom Wrong data`), `og:site_name` = workspace title, `og:url` = the canonical `/w/<slug>/e/<uuid>`, `og:type` = article, `twitter:card` = summary, `twitter:label1`/`data1` pairs for the state and fields (Slack renders them as a two-column list), and a `<link rel=icon>`.
2. **Image.** `og:image` is the workspace logo when one is set and raster (PNG, JPEG, WebP; Messages and Slack ignore SVG), otherwise a bundled raster weave mark in `public/brand/`. Absolute URL, built from the request origin.
3. **Spaces and tables.** A space and a table get a server-seen permalink of the same shape (`/w/<ws>/s/<uuid>`, `/w/<ws>/t/<uuid>`, 200 plus meta, jump to `#/space/` or `#/table/`), with `og:title` = `Development · space` or `Development / Issue · table`, description carrying the row count. The ⧉ control on a space page and a table header mints these. The workspace root `/w/<ws>/` gets the same head with the logo and the workspace title.
4. **Wall.** A new workspace setting, `Link preview before sign-in`, off by default. Off keeps today's 302 to sign-in for anonymous requests. On lets an anonymous GET of a permalink receive the head only: title, path, id, name, logo, and the state plus preview fields; no entity payload, no API calls, then the sign-in jump. Stored on the workspace row, editable in workspace settings, read by the permalink route before the wall check.
5. **Tab title.** The server-rendered title means the tab reads the row before the client runs; `breadcrumbs.js` docTitle keeps ownership afterwards.

## Tests

- `test/permalinks.test.mjs`: 200 and the exact meta for an entity, a `Table#n` ref, a space, a table and the root; the jump target; a deleted or unknown ref still renders the branded 404; `og:image` falls back to the bundled mark when no logo is set and to the logo when it is raster.
- A browser case next to `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs`: opening a permalink lands on the entity, Back leaves the workspace in one step as today.
- The wall: anonymous GET with the setting off answers 302 and no meta; with it on, the head carries the meta and no entity data; a Bearer-token GET is unchanged.

## Out of scope

features.name: Attachments preview, size and fit: a live viewer for one file, a contact sheet for many
features.description:
## Problem
An attachments field rendered as chips only. The record could not show its files: no thumbnails, no viewer, no cover, and an uploaded HTML page could only be downloaded (Issue #483 serves it inert).

## Solution (Kyle, 2026-10-05, from three mock-ups)
Three config keys on the field, through `normalizeSelfContainedConfig`, the field tray, `describeSchema` and `applySchema`:
- `preview`: `link` (chips) | `inline` (a contact sheet of the files, or the one file in its viewer) | `auto` (pictures in the sheet, the rest as chips) | `cover` (the picture above the record; single-file fields only). Unset follows the field: `auto` for many, `inline` for one.
- `size`: `small` | `medium` (default) | `large`: the sheet's cell and the viewer's height.
- `fit`: `trim` (default; the whole file, the cell trimmed to its shape, rows justified) | `fill` (uniform cells, the file cropped). Nothing is ever stretched.

A sheet cell opens the fullscreen viewer (Feature #47), which gained ← → between a field's files and a sandbox for HTML. A single-file field shows its file in place with no click: an image, a PDF or plain text in a frame, an HTML upload live under the new `GET /api/files/:id?view`, served `text/html` only under `HTML_VIEW_POLICY` (sandbox with scripts and popups, never `allow-same-origin`, `default-src 'none'`); the bare route still downloads it. The tray's strip is labelled Show as (the vditor contract bars the word Preview from app.js).

Deferred (`ponytail:` in code): server-made stills for PDF and HTML cells (glyph tiles today); the cover sits under the sticky title bar rather than between the crumbs and the name.

## Gates
`test/attachments-preview.test.mjs` (normaliser, patch, schema round trip, dialog mirror, fileHeaders, the ?view route), `test/attachments-preview-browser.test.mjs` (sheet with --ar from the image, sandboxed live HTML whose script runs and cannot reach the page, cover, lightbox).

Mock-ups: https://claude.ai/artifact/FBjE3A1679u1XMbCqcm2Zm (config options), https://claude.ai/artifact/TKhw4YE8dmHPHzsgLVFcis (single-file matrix and openers), https://claude.ai/artifact/VRqRedtkwScvJNRbd3LhKi (live viewer). GitHub hand-off: https://github.com/grunion-ai/weave/pull/8.

Filed by the cloud session that built it (session 017sKPzc57GjpzGQ3geKzJow), landed by the local session that ran this task.

## Landed

Local gate on the rebased tree: 289 pass, 0 fail; the Gerrit gate verified patchsets 4 and 5. Showcase record: http://127.0.0.1:4400/w/showcase-attachments/e/b77a58e1-d0b0-4036-8c46-192cbb80455c

features.name: Prefilled create links: open a new-row form with fields set from the URL
features.description:
## Pain Point

Kyle wants the iPhone share sheet to save a link into Net Library/Saves under his own Clerk sign-in, with no token on the phone. Squirrel, the share Shortcut, posts with a pasted `wv_` bearer today, and the install question that asks for it failed on the phone on 2026-10-06.

## Problem

weave has no way to hand someone a pre-filled new row. A link can open a table, never a draft. Signed-out visits also lose the query string: `src/server.js:412` keeps only `url.pathname`, and `src/routes.js:263` builds `/auth?next=` from that path, so any prefill would vanish across the Clerk round trip.

## Solution

Prefilled create links, for any table:

- `<table route>/new?<Field>=<value>&...` opens the standard new-row form with those fields set. The person taps Save; opening the link never creates a row, so a third-party page cannot plant rows.
- Values parse the way the entities API parses them: a select takes the option name, a relation takes the target row's Name. An unknown field name is dropped and named in a notice.
- The table menu gets "Copy create link", built from the fields filled in so far.
- A signed-out visit keeps the query string in `next` through sign-in, and lands on the filled form. Field values are capped so `next` fits the sign-in cookie.

Uses beyond Squirrel: bookmarklets and Raycast, agent hand-offs where a routine sends Kyle a draft Task or Issue to confirm, "file this" links in email and the daily brief.

Narrower slice of Feature #212 (Apple Shortcuts as a capture inlet).

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-06 (Squirrel reinstall), against weave.grunion.ai Net Library/Saves.
