features.name: List layout: grouped, ordered, checkable rows in a table view
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-10-07 (Kyle), from the list vs table design canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/5fgiRKDDcpgXEjH8x2oiVX. Kyle: "a layout same view as a list looks good provided we get the view filter sort right", "should allow multi level grouping", "all saved as part of view", "check box is just a field so is progress bar which is part of a roll up", "lets reuse as much as possible but probably need a new grouping selector".

## Definition
A list holds things to finish, in an order you set; a table holds records to compare, in an order the data sets. A list layout carries five traits: completion, manual order, name first with chips, grouping and nesting, and an add row. The first list view (removed 2026-08-22, Feature #105, b12e9a8) had none of them.

## Scope
List is a **layout of an existing per-table view** (Feature #229), beside Table. Same rows, same filter, sort, fields and density.

**Reused, not rebuilt**
- Row = the table's Chip (`renderView` shape chip, Features #175/#191/#193). Chip placement comes from the Chip config, never a list setting.
- Checkbox = a checkbox field drawn with the standard `.form-check-input`. No bespoke circle.
- Progress = a rollup field with `display: bar`, shown when the linked row's Chip includes it.
- Group heading as Chip = the linked row's Chip via `relationChipEl`, opens the row.
- Dates typed in the add row = `public/nl-date.js`. Pickers = `pickerSelect`. Drag handle = the six-dot handle from the View dropdown.

**New**
1. `layout: table | list` on the view.
2. **Grouping selector**: toolbar button "Group: A › B" beside Filter and Sort. Ordered levels (cap 3); each level = field, heading `label | chip` (chip only for link fields), group order (option order, linked table order, A to Z). Every level collapses. Generalises the Statistics panel's one-level Group by (`columnStatsPanel`, `/tables/:id/stats?by=`). Eligible: category fields, links, checkbox, dates by grain.
3. Saved manual `order` per view, used while the view has no sort.
4. `nest` by a self Parent link: indent, drag right / Tab to nest, left / Shift+Tab to un-nest.
5. Completed rows: `completedBy: <checkbox field>`; checked rows leave their group and sit in a collapsed "Completed · N" group at the bottom.
6. Add row at the end of each innermost group: fills every group level value and every equals-filter; dates parse with nl-date.

**Saved in the view, autosaved:** layout, group levels with headings and group order, collapsed groups, completedBy, nest, order. Reset and New view = system default (no grouping, Table).

## Filter and sort rules
1. No sort = manual order, stored per view.
2. A sort orders rows within each group; handles stop reordering; group-change and nest drags still work; clearing the sort restores the saved order.
3. Filter runs first; matching checked rows go to Completed. A filter that excludes checked rows hides Completed.
4. A matching child keeps its filtered-out parent visible, dimmed and uncounted.
5. Empty groups show only with no filter on.
6. Add row inherits group values and equals-filters.
7. Footer: "3 of 8 <row term> · 1 completed" (Issue #448 form).
8. Switching Table and List loses nothing; Table ignores the list keys.

Drag into another group sets every level that differs.

## Agent surface
One view verb, names not UUIDs (views ruling 2026-09-23): `group: [{field, heading, order}]`, `layout`, `completedBy`, `nest`, `collapsed`, compact reads.

## Out of scope
Lists inside documents (task-list blocks) stay as they are. Cross-table tree views (one view over two tables). Grouping in Table layout (the key is stored; Table ignores it for now). Phone two-line rows stay with #272.

Filed by the list-vs-table design session, 2026-10-07, against weave v0.4.75 (gerrit/main 9bea0b1).

features.name: Ontology outline for agents: weave_ontology with outline, concept and since
features.description:
## What was measured

On the `weave` workspace at v0.4.75 (`cb0b29f`), `weave_schema` returns 113,062 characters (about 28,265 tokens) for 36 tables and 359 fields. A one-line-per-table outline of the same schema measured 5,993 characters (about 1,498 tokens), a 19x cut. Only 95 of 359 fields carry a description.

The `ONTOLOGY` export (`src/engine.js:312`) is read by `test/ontology.test.mjs` and `src/handbook.js` only. No runtime path, MCP tool or primer line reads it, so agents never see the ontology.

## Scope (the minimal first set)

- `weave_ontology {depth:"outline"}`: every table on one line, with its fields, types, option or state names, and relations as `name -> Target*` with the inverse.
- `weave_ontology {concept:"Issue"}`: one table in full, including field descriptions.
- `weave_ontology {since:<etag>}`: only the spaces whose schema changed since that etag.
- A schema version per space, counted from the structural audit log; the workspace etag combines the space versions.
- The MCP primer's first line tells agents to read the outline first, and stays under 2,048 characters.
- No storage change. Extends, shared properties, predicates, shapes, actions, views and import by reference come later, one change each.

## Done when

The outline of the `weave` workspace is under 2,000 tokens. The one-shot build score does not drop. Tests are written first, the change lands through Gerrit, and a real `weave mcp` call on :4400 returns the outline.

## Peer reference

schema.org and Palantir Foundry AIP give agents a compact, scoped view of the model rather than a full dump.

## Decisions recorded with Kyle on 2026-10-07

Shapes warn by default and never refuse a write for now. Schema history lives on the space. Shared properties live at workspace or space scope, and the nearest scope wins. The Space rename is still open: Library is recommended over Package and Book.

Related: #119 (ONTOLOGY export), #215 (cross-workspace references), #244 (starter templates).

Filed by the harness session on 2026-10-07 (weave v0.4.75, `cb0b29f`).



## Landed 2026-10-07

Gerrit change 705 merged as `a238969` (patchset 2; patchset 1 went Verified -1 on webkit browser suites outside the change, filed as Issue #711). Released in v0.4.76, Gerrit 714, release commit `e4f1675`.

Measured on the live `weave` workspace through a real `weave mcp` process started from `~/.weave-serve` at `a238969`:

- `weave_ontology {depth:"outline"}`: 5,250 characters, about 1,313 tokens (chars/4), for 36 tables in 7 spaces. `weave_schema` on the same workspace: 103,226 characters through describeSchema.
- `{concept:"Issue"}`: 1,073 characters.
- `{since:"4f953866"}` with nothing changed: 24 characters, `unchanged; etag 4f953866`.
- The primer is 1,793 characters; its first line reads `weave: read the weave_ontology outline first.` `tools/list` names 17 tools, `weave_ontology` first.

One-shot build eval (queue/weave-disclosure-eval, realproxy R0, Sonnet, budget and pipeline, two reps each): 31/34 checks on gerrit/main `9bea0b1`, 32/34 with this change. Agents read the outline first and used `concept` to check a table after the build.

Tests: `test/ontology-outline.test.mjs` (14), with `test/fixtures/ontology-weave.json` (the live schema, 36 tables); its outline stays under 8,000 characters. Gate on patchset 2: full suite green, browser suites ran.

Doors: MCP `weave_ontology` (default list), `GET /api/ontology?depth=&concept=&since=`, `weave ontology [--concept T] [--since E]`. Space versions come from the audit log: each schema audit entry names the spaces it touched.

Open upgrade paths (also in the commit message): cache the history keyed on the newest audit seq if a workspace grows tens of thousands of schema entries; backfill `spaces` onto entries written before this change.

features.name: Space definition: the unit of meaning, not a container
features.description:
## Decision

Kyle kept the name Space on 2026-10-07, after weighing twenty alternatives (Library, Package, Book, Folder, Section, Solution and others). The name stays and the definition changes. Today a space is defined as "a named container grouping the tables of one area of work" (`src/engine.js` ONTOLOGY, `docs/ONTOLOGY.md`). The new definition frames it as the unit of meaning: the tables of one area, the scope of `Space/Table` names, the unit a template copies, and, from Feature #277, the owner of its own schema version.

## Scope

- The `definition` string for `space` in the ONTOLOGY export
- The Space row of the glossary in `docs/ONTOLOGY.md`, kept in step by `test/ontology.test.mjs`
- The handbook page that defines a space (`src/handbook.js`), applied to the live `weave.db` (see Issue #255)

The docs state only what is true today. Shared properties and import by reference are planned, not shipped, and the docs must not claim them.

## Why not rename

Scored against seven design needs, Space fit 6, Folder 2 and Section 1. Folder suggests nesting and passivity; Section suggests a fragment of a document. A rename would touch about 800 uses, the MCP verbs and the registry.

Related: #119, #277.

Filed by the harness session on 2026-10-07 (weave v0.4.75).

## Landed 2026-10-07

Gerrit change 704, commit f6d8ae9 (merge 4960fa5 on gerrit/main), rebased onto Feature #277 (a238969) before submit. Code-Review +2 and Verified +1 from the gate. Deployed to :4400 at 13:51 on the v0.4.75 build; the handbook was applied to the live weave.db with `weave handbook sync` (Issue #255) and the guide shows the paragraph. Other "container" hits left as they are: `docs/development.json` lines 2016 and 3040 (Issue rows calling workspaces, spaces, tables and views "containers" in search), and `containerHints` in `src/field-hints.js` (the build-hint function for spaces and tables). features.name: Find my workspaces and invite flows: one rail across several logins
features.description:
Kyle asked for this row on 2026-10-07 after reviewing the sign-in storyboard. Filed, not scheduled.

## What the person does
1. Signs in once per login (Clerk). weave asks for openid only (Feature #252), so a login is an issuer and a subject.
2. Find my workspaces: for each signed-in login, weave asks every workspace on the instance whether that subject has an account there, and adds each yes to the rail. No workspace learns which other workspaces answered.
3. Add login: the rail's + menu offers Add login. Clerk opens with an account picker (prompt=select_account), the person picks or adds a second login, and Find my workspaces runs for it.
4. Accept an invite with a second login: an invite link (weave account link, 7-day single use) opened in a browser that already holds login 1 offers "Accept as login 1" or "Use another login". The second choice runs Add login and pins that subject.
5. New device or cleared cookies: the rail starts with the built-in weave docs workspace only; each login signs in once and Find my workspaces rebuilds the rail.

## Rules from Kyle's rulings
- Sessions live in the browser, one per workspace. No server-side person record links logins (rulings, second pass).
- Roles per workspace come from the inviter (Feature #255).
- The weave docs workspace is always in the rail and everyone is an Observer there.

## Depends on
- Per-workspace sessions (filed alongside this row).
- Hub root removal (Feature #141 open question 5) before member workspaces stop accepting a root session.

## Open questions
- Does Find my workspaces run automatically after each sign-in, or only from the + menu?
- Do signed-out visitors see the weave docs workspace (public Handbook)?

## Peer behaviour
Slack's "Find your workspaces" emails a list per address; weave holds no email, so the lookup runs per subject inside the browser session.

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-07 (weave user and workspace sign-in storyboard), weave v0.4.75, commit 9bea0b1. Design source: Feature #141, sections "Kyle's direction, 2026-10-02" and "Kyle's rulings, 2026-10-02 (second pass)".

features.name: Per-workspace sessions: expiry, sign-out and access removal lock one workspace only
features.description:
Second of three rows from the 2026-10-07 storyboard. Kyle said "tackle the rest", so this one is being built.

## Measured today (main 9bea0b1)
- One wv_session cookie per host, Path=/ (src/routes.js:85). A session minted on one workspace, or on the hub root, opens others through the root fallthrough (src/routes.js, session resolution).
- POST /api/auth/logout clears that one cookie, so signing out anywhere signs out everywhere.
- Issue #710: the cookie is written once at sign-in and dies at 30 days even though the server slides expiresAt.

## Behaviour wanted
- The browser holds one session per workspace. A request to /w/<name>/ uses that workspace's session.
- 30 days without use expires that workspace's session only. Use slides it (Issue #710 fixed first).
- Sign out of <workspace> revokes and clears that workspace's session only. Sign out everywhere clears every session this browser holds.
- An Architect removing an account revokes its sessions in that workspace at once; the next request there gets a page that says access was removed, never a sign-in loop.
- Signing in to a second workspace with the same login while Clerk still remembers it mints that workspace's session through the OIDC redirect with no screen.
- The hub-root fallthrough stays until hub root removal lands (Feature #141 question 5), so Kyle keeps access to member workspaces meanwhile.

## Fix shape

features.name: Drag to reorder: lift animation and drop-zone placeholder on every reorder surface, web and mobile
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-10-08: every place in weave where something can be dragged to reorder needs one shared treatment, on web and on phones.

What good looks like:
1. Lift. On pickup the dragged item rises: scale about 1.02 to 1.03, a deeper shadow, slight opacity on the source, a grabbing cursor on web. On touch, a long press (about 250 ms) lifts with the same animation plus a haptic tick where the platform offers one (navigator.vibrate on Android; none on iOS Safari).
2. Drop-zone placeholder. The slot the item will land in opens as a placeholder the size of the item (a dashed or tinted gap), and neighbours slide aside with a short transform transition (about 150 to 200 ms). No insertion line alone, no highlighted row that reads as a swap (see Issue #115).
3. Drop. The item settles from the pointer into the placeholder with a short ease-out; cancel (Escape or drop outside) animates it home.
4. Auto-scroll near the edges of the scroll container while dragging (Issues #3, #450, #432 cover past defects).
5. prefers-reduced-motion: keep the placeholder, drop the scale and slide animations.
6. Keyboard reorder keeps working where it exists.

Peer tools: Linear, Notion and Trello lift the card and open a gap; iOS Reminders and Things lift on long press with a haptic. dnd-kit and SortableJS are the reference behaviour.

Fix shape: one shared reorder module (pointer events, works for mouse and touch) and one set of CSS tokens for lift, placeholder and settle, then move every reorder surface onto it: grid column headers (Feature #41, #233), entity-page field list (Feature #117), Fields popover, view tabs (Issue #400), select option lists (.opt-grip in field-dialog-core.js), board cards, sidebar items, and any other draggable list found in public/app.js. Each surface gets a browser test that asserts the lift class, the placeholder element and the final order, on desktop Chromium and the WebKit iPhone 15 profile.

Current draggable surfaces found by grep: public/app.js, public/column-resize.js, public/field-dialog-core.js, public/style.css (.opt-grip, .dragging, .drop-slot, .drop-target, .wv-col-dragging).

Filed by the harness session of 2026-10-08 against weave v0.4.43, commit 56b0b79.

**2026-10-08, Shipped.** Landed through Gerrit as change 767 (5343686: the shared module public/reorder.js, the CSS tokens and every surface) and change 768 (623b8fd: the Handbook text). Both are merged on gerrit/main and deployed to :4400, which restarted at 12:16 PT on the v0.4.83 build. The version is not bumped; changelog.d/drag-reorder-282.md rides the next release.

Surfaces on the shared module: grid column headers (the Feature #233 frozen seam and its Freeze here / Unfreeze tag kept), the Fields popover, view tabs, group levels, workflow states, select options (a new grip), entity page fields, entity page blocks and list view rows. Weave has no board view and no sidebar reorder, so those two items in the ask had nothing to move. File drops stay native.

Tests: the gate on change 767 was green with no retries (unit lane 2821 of 2821, browser lane 1437 pass and 1 skip). On main 623b8fd, test/drag-reorder-browser.test.mjs passed 15 of 15 on desktop Chromium and test/drag-reorder-phone-browser.test.mjs passed 10 of 10 on the WebKit iPhone 15 profile.

Attached: mid-drag screenshots taken on :4400. live-column-drag.png shows the Feature table with Status lifted before Description. live-field-list-drag.png shows this page with Milestone lifted into the top slot. Both drags ended with Escape and wrote nothing.

## v0.4.4 — 2026-08-31

- **Development sync** (#152): every build ships `docs/development.json` — the canonical Issue + Feature lists exported at release by `scripts/export-development.mjs` — and `weave serve` applies it to the local docs workspace on boot. Updating weave now updates the known/resolved issue list and the roadmap; locally filed rows are never touched (match is by name). `test/development-sync.test.mjs` pins the manifest to the package version.
- **Workspace delete** (Issue #122): `DELETE /api/workspaces/:ref` + a hold-to-confirm action on the workspace page. The `.db` (with WAL/SHM) moves to `<dataDir>/trash/` — recoverable, invisible to the hub's scan. The default and weave docs workspaces refuse.
- **A fresh workspace explains itself** (Issue #123): hub-created workspaces open with a description naming the first steps and what the Workspace registry space is.
- **The registry registers itself** (Issue #126): the system Workspace space and its four tables are rows in Spaces/Tables like everything else — the registry now means its own description. Deleting or repurposing those rows is refused; columns cannot be added to system tables through the Fields registry.
- **Percent means percent** (Issue #127): number fields with the percent costume follow the spreadsheet convention — stored fraction, displayed ×100 (0.325 → "32.5%"), input ÷100. Existing percent values migrate ÷100 once on first open, so every cell reads exactly as it did.
- **Formula chips insert parseable tokens** (Issue #128): a field chip inserts `[Due Date]` when the name needs bracketing (spaces, punctuation, keywords, function-name collisions) and the bare name only when it is a safe identifier.
- **Shift+Enter is save-and-create-another from inside a row** (Issue #125): the cell commits, the new row's Name cell takes focus.
- **Empty-schema banner gone** (Issue #124): "This table has no fields beyond its name." read as breakage, not help.

releases.name: v0.4.3
releases.description:
## v0.4.3 — 2026-08-28

- **Target-set (polymorphic) relations** (#150): one relation field may target SEVERAL tables — `targetDbs` — including the registry's `Workspace/Spaces` and `Workspace/Tables`, so a row can point at a space or a table as easily as at another row (a bug scoped to a whole space, a dependency on an entire workstream, an agenda mixing rows with structure). One-way by design (no inverse spray); lookups/rollups keep the single-target contract; filters traverse per-row; chips carry their home table; the picker searches every member; the relation map draws one edge per member. Rollback-safe: singleton relations are bit-for-bit unchanged, and removing multi-target fields restores the pre-feature shape exactly.

releases.name: v0.4.0
releases.description:
## v0.4.0 — 2026-08-21

### The agent-native meta-model
- **The workspace's structure, as rows** (#12): a `Workspace` system space holds `Spaces`, `Tables` and `Fields` registries — real entities synced both ways by the engine's own verbs. Create a row, get a space/table/column; rename the row, the real thing renames; custom fields (a workspace logo, an owner) ride structure for free.
- **Every field is a row** (#52): the Fields registry is the schema surface, carrying each column's shape as a `field`-type Definition (#85 — entity page as the control surface, `materializeField`).
- **The schema as a document** (#13): `weave schema export/apply` — edit the JSON, the workspace grows to match; deletions need `--allow-destructive`, type changes never apply.

### Identity, audit, and the road to hosting
- **Every change names its actor** (#65): createdBy/modifiedBy + per-table system columns (Created/Modified At/By, Activity #95); server X-Weave-Actor, CLI WEAVE_ACTOR/OS user, MCP client name.
- **Accounts, roles, audit** (#14): admin/writer/reader tokens (sha256 at rest, handed out once), requireAuth for the hosted future (#84, v0.5), a durable audit log of structural change.
- **The key field type** (#64): secrets live in a chmod-600 keystore, never in workspace data; set over HTTP, never readable back.

### Views
- **Filters** (#38, closes the oldest issue #2): workflow-state chips driving the engine's where-language server-side.
- **Side peek** (#39, #48): rows and activity entries open beside the page, not instead of it.
- **Saved views + share links** (#17): named blocks resolved live; sharing mints a revocable capability URL that outlives the auth wall.
- **The workspace page** (#51): its own shape as a read-only mermaid map; **record nouns** (#40).

### Typed values
- **Number costumes** (#97): format/unit/decimals/separator, display-only, formulas keep raw numbers.
- **The date system** (#44): iso/us/eu/long + time costumes, date math in formulas (dateadd, datediff, year/month/day, now), and a type-or-pick cell that reads "next friday".

### The editor, completed
- **Syntax highlighting** (#35): the slash menu seeds a language; rendered pages load vendored highlight.js on demand.
- **Live `[[…]]` chips in the editor** (#86): an overlay decoration over Vditor's IR — Lute owns the text, weave never mutates it; literal under the caret.
- **Outline dash rail** (#87) and **collapsible headings** (#88): a minimap with a place tracker; folds are view state (content byte-identical), persisted per document.
- **The row editor** (#89): one shared Vditor instance mounts into the focused row (2ms warm) — and the icon-sprite leak `destroy()` misses is fixed.
- **Math** (#90): KaTeX 0.16.47 vendored (with mhchem — load-bearing); the heavier diagram engines stay out, documented.

### Operations
- **Service management** (#54): `weave service install|status` (launchd), health with startedAt/uptime, instance status in the nav.
- Hygiene: mermaid 11.17.0 (XSS advisories, #8), MCP version honesty (#19), qualified relation refs (#21), board title ellipsis (#20), activity coalescing (#32), webhook test deflaked (#27).

Slipped to v0.5 (recorded on their tracker rows): #84 hosting, #16 attachments field type, #46, #47, #49, #50, PDF non-WinAnsi glyphs (Issue #4).

## v0.4.5 — 2026-09-05

Landed as 3f944ae. Fixed:

- [[Issue#134]] ⌘-click on an entity link opens a new tab (Gerrit 207)
- [[Issue#83]] Tab carries on from the row you are on (Gerrit 208)
- [[Issue#133]] Doc downloads ⋮ menu stays on the page (Gerrit 209)
- [[Issue#232]] Formula builder saved unparseable expressions with no warning (Gerrit 167)

Shipped:

- [[Feature#195]] Formula check: validate and preview an expression before it is saved

- **The ⋮ panel stays on the page** (Issue #133): the document section's downloads menu opened past the right edge — a 178px panel at `right: 1383` in a 1280px viewport, so the reader saw a sliver of "…ownloa" and could reach none of it. The side was chosen where each menu was written (`align: 'right'`, passed by three callers out of seven), which no constant can get right on both edges. `dotsMenu` now measures on open: `menuSide()` weighs the anchor, the panel width and the bounds it has to live inside, and `menuBounds()` takes those bounds from the nearest ancestor that clips its overflow — the side peek, not the window. The caller's `align` survives as the preference and wins whenever it fits. Same panel now opens at `right: 1238`.
- **Tab carries on from the row you are on** (Issue #83): editing a cell and tabbing out fires the PATCH, and the grid redraw that follows it landed a beat after the browser had already moved focus along the row — tearing out the cell just reached and dropping focus on `<body>`, so the next Tab restarted at the top of the page. Every grid redraw now reads the live focus on the way in and puts it back on the same cell, caret where it was.
- **⌘-click opens a tab, everywhere** (Issue #134): one predicate, `nativeClick`, answers ⌘/Ctrl, Shift and the middle button, and one capture-phase listener acts on it for the surfaces that navigate without being a link — a grid row, the relation panel's rows, an activity row, a ⌘K hit, a node on the relation map. Each declares its destination as `data-href` and nothing else; real anchors are left to the browser, and form controls keep their own modifiers, so shift-click still extends a text selection and the row checkbox still range-selects.
- **Release notes are rows** (2026-09-04): `Development/Release` holds one row per release — version, Date, Commit, the Issues it `Fixes`, the Features it `Ships`, and the notes as its Description. The notes are mandatory: the export refuses a row without them, sync refuses a manifest without them, and the suite refuses a package version with no row. The four releases to date are backfilled from this file; the manifest now ships them, so every instance's docs workspace grows the table on its next boot.
- **Chip and Card: every table says how its rows appear elsewhere** (Kyle, 2026-09-04): two `view` fields minted on every table, hidden from the grid by default, never deletable, held by role (`chipFieldId` / `cardFieldId`) so a rename costs nothing. The config is the table's — the #id link, the workflow state, a description preview at `none`/`small`/`medium`/`large`, and which other fields ride along (or the first few non-empty ones in column order). The chip is what a relation cell, a doc mention and a reference card draw — one builder, segments behind the doc-mention caret; the card is the tile a board or gallery will draw. The entity page shows both under **Appears as**, each with a gear into the field dialog, whose pane previews the view live under the candidate config (`GET /api/entities/:ref/view?shape=&config=`). `readEntity` ships both under their field names (one line in `fields`, the object in `raw`); every relation summary carries `chip`. CSV export leaves them out; a partial `fieldOrder` may too. A hidden column now stays hidden through a rename.
- **Formula authoring gets a check step** ([[Issue#232]], [[Feature#195]]): `check()` validates an expression statically — syntax, function names, field references — and the engine refuses to save one that fails, including a formula that references its own field. `weave formula check`, `POST /api/tables/:id/formula-check` and the `weave_check_formula` MCP tool run the same check and preview the computed value on a real row, so the loop for a human and an agent is identical: check until `ok: true`, save, read a cell back. The script editor shows the verdict live while typing (red parse error, or `= value` from row 1), function chips land the caret inside the parens, and the field being edited no longer offers itself as a chip.
- **Icons move** : the icon set is Lucide (595 names) carrying movingicons.dev motion — an icon plays once when the page loads, once when the picker scrolls it into view, once per hover, never on a loop. The value form is `lucide:<name>`; every `iconly:<name>` stored before 2026-09-02 resolves to its Lucide twin through `public/icon-registry.js`, so nothing migrates. Fourteen state marks (✓ ✕ ★ ! ? ▶ ⏸ ⊘ ⚑ ◎ ⛓ ⌁ → +) draw as their Lucide twins; the six progress rings stay hand-drawn, re-inked to the same stroke. Rebuild the set with `scripts/build-lucide-moving.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.6 — 2026-09-05

Landed as 2e60c20. Shipped: [[Feature#134]] [[Feature#132]] [[Feature#156]] [[Feature#180]] [[Feature#181]] [[Feature#182]]. Fixed: [[Issue#84]] [[Issue#98]] [[Issue#100]] [[Issue#160]] [[Issue#161]] [[Issue#190]] [[Issue#191]] [[Issue#192]] [[Issue#193]] [[Issue#194]] [[Issue#195]] [[Issue#196]] [[Issue#197]] [[Issue#198]] [[Issue#200]] [[Issue#201]] [[Issue#202]] [[Issue#203]] [[Issue#204]].

- **The grid from the keyboard** (Feature #134, Issue #84): cells rest as values and open on purpose. At rest, ←→↑↓ move, Tab and ⇧Tab move and wrap row to row without ever leaving the grid, Return opens the cell (value selected, picker up, checkbox flipped), any character opens it and types over the value, Space toggles the row, ⇧↑/⇧↓ extend the run, ⌘A takes the table, ⇧Return makes the next row open on its name, ⌘Return docks the record. Open, Return commits down, Tab commits across, ↑↓ commit and move, Esc puts the value back. Every field `<td>` is the focus stop, so Tab now lands on select, multi-select, checkbox and date cells the browser's own order skipped, and the last cell of the last row is the end of the grid rather than the start of the browser chrome. The keymap is one pure core, `public/grid-keymap.js`; the Handbook grid section carries both tables.
- **The puck's commands, slice 3** (Feature #132, Issue #161): the selection bar gains **Set a field…** (pick a field, then a value: state chips, options, a checkbox, or a typed box, written across the selection), **Link to…** (pick a relation, search the far table, pick one row), and under ⋯ **Move to table…** (each row re-created in the chosen table by field name and type, the original trashed, unmatched fields, files and comments named as skipped), **Roll up into a new …** (one new parent in the relation's table, every chosen row linked to it) and **Copy links**. The bar is fixed to the bottom of the viewport, so it stays in reach on a grid taller than the screen.
- **One bulk verb, three doors** (Feature #132): `POST /api/bulk`, `weave bulk <set|link|move|rollup> <ref...>` and the `weave_bulk` MCP tool are the same engine call, `bulk(ids, op, params)`. Every row is its own attempt: the reply names `done` and `failed` with the reason, each row keeps its own undo step and activity entry, and the verbs underneath are the single-row ones, so nothing can drift from them. A bulk command that half works and reports success is how a row goes missing quietly; this one reports per row.
- **Column resize tracks the pointer, stops at the label, never opens the field dialog** (Issues #98, #100, #160): a drag that only set `style.width` painted nothing under a stored min/max-width, so the column jumped on release; every move now paints header and cells through the same `paintColumnWidth` the commit uses, with one rounding, so the painted width is the stored width. The floor was the engine's 60px, so a header could hide its own label. Now the floor is the label's measured width plus the header padding, from the pure core in `public/column-resize.js`. Safari resolved the click of a captured drag to the header under the pointer and opened the field tray; the grip now marks the header for the gesture and the header click is inert until the next press.
- **A range is picked in ONE dialog** (Issue #197): a daterange field was two date controls side by side, and the tray's default was a bare text box the engine could only refuse. `rangeControl()` is one box reading the whole span in the field's costume and one calendar; the first pick starts a span, the second closes it (swapped if it came first), the days between are lit, typed Start/End inputs live inside it, and the grain reaches it, so year·month picks two months and a clock range two times. The same control mounts in the grid cell, on the entity page and in the tray's Default.
- **Every opener docks** (Issue #198): only the ledger's #id link and the document chip went through `dockEntity`; a relation chip, a card, a mention, a ⌘K hit, a trash row and a fresh row all set `location.hash` and drew the expanded page. `openEntity()` now travels to the entity's table when you are elsewhere and docks beside it; one capture-phase listener routes every plain click on an entity link through it. `#/entity/<id>` stays the expanded page for a new tab, a permalink and the outward arrows.
- **A new row takes the caret** (Issue #195): + New and Shift+Enter aimed at `td:nth-child(2) input`, which has been the #id link since the selection column landed, so the focus call was a silent no-op. `focusNewRow` scrolls the row into view and opens its Name cell. The foot button calls the grid's own `onAdd`: the space page and the home page create "New table" / "New space" in place, and a relation grid's + New creates, links and focuses.
- **Workspaces from the rail** (Feature #156, Issues #190, #202, #204, #191): right-click any rail chip for **Update logo…**, **Remove logo** while one exists, and **Delete workspace…** where the hub allows it. Delete confirms by typing the workspace's name; the current workspace redirects home, a sibling stays put with an Undo toast. Trashed workspaces restore from a 26px glyph in the bottom-right cluster beside the version tag, present only while the trash has rows. `GET /api/workspaces` rows carry `deletable`, so the UI hides the affordance where the server would refuse it. The + New workspace glyph is centred.
- **Chips: one size, a caret that faces the text, a label that truncates** (Issues #194, #193, #201): the chip size lives in two tokens, `--wv-chip-font` (13px) and `--wv-chip-line` (22px, a 24px hit target), read by every chip surface. The retract caret is a half turn, so expand and retract read as one control folding in and out. A pointer chip's name sits in a `.k-label` span. Inside a constrained column it ellipsizes; the home badge and ↗ stay at the right end, and the full name rides in the title.
- **The embedded relation grid keeps the target table's hidden set** (Issue #200): a Release's Fixes grid drew Chip and Card and every cell read `[object Object]`. `relatedGrid` filters through `visibleCols(target)`, and the generic cell fallback refuses objects: a `wv-unrendered` marker names the type instead of a box holding `String(obj)`.
- **The v0.3.0 schema page is gone** (Issue #196): `addFieldDialog` fell back to `openSchemaEditor()` whenever the add did not start on a table route, which every registry grid is. It now hands you back to wherever you were; the schema editor, the relation dialog only it reached and the `.schema-table` rule are deleted.
- **An icon moves only on its own hover or press** (Issue #192): the load wave and the picker-scroll play are gone; a document-level pointerdown joins the mouseover listener, one run per trigger through the same `playIcon` gate, reduced-motion stills it.
- **Every seeded space and table wears a `lucide:` icon** (Issue #203): Release rocket, Issue bug, Feature star; `ensureReleaseTable` carries the rocket, so workspaces seeded before the table existed pick it up on the next sync.
- **Handbook and mockups** (Features #180, #181, #182): a "Chip and card anatomy" guide draws the real chip and card markup with a dashed outline and a numbered badge on each of 13 elements, and a legend of what each does, how you use it and where its hitbox is; `docs/chip-card-anatomy.html` is the same guide as one self-contained page. `docs/mockups/card-view-options.html` holds fifteen card options (A–O) with a comparison matrix, every field value drawn as the cell's own chip. The polymorphic-relations guide points each use case at its Showcase table. Chip anatomy round 2 (P–T) and the relation-map junction mockups (A–D) are on the same shelf.

**Open after this release.** Three mockup sets landed here with no implementation behind them, each waiting on one decision from Kyle: [[Feature#183]] relation-map layouts A–D, [[Feature#184]] card views A–O, [[Feature#185]] chip anatomy P–T. Two defects were carried open rather than fixed: [[Issue#199]] (a grid-focus browser test flakes about one run in six) and [[Issue#205]] (two export scripts drifted when their parents landed side by side, because the gate runs each patchset against its own parent, not the merged result).

## v0.4.7 — 2026-09-06

Landed as 887d915. Fixed:

- [[Issue#142]] Wrong data: Icon names should show in sear bar on select or hover (Gerrit 237)
- [[Issue#157]] Looks broken + Slow + Error: hover preview not working for name field in this db (Gerrit 238)

- **A name that runs past its column expands on hover again** (Issue #157): the marker that opens the hover expansion was measured on the `<td>`, and a text cell's `<input>` is `width: 100%` — the value overflows inside the control, the cell never reports overflow, and so no Name on any grid was ever marked. Clipping is now read from the control as well as the cell, so every text-backed cell participates. The expansion itself was the second half: it cloned the `<input>`, and a cloned control falls back to its own intrinsic width, so hovering opened a box that cut the value off in the same place. The copy is now the value as text, carrying the control's own font, weight and metrics, and it wraps inside the popover the way a description's lines do.
- **The icon picker names what you are pointing at** (Issue #142): the grid said everything in shapes and kept every name in a native tooltip — slow for a mouse, silent for a keyboard, and no help at all to someone reopening the picker to check which icon is set. The search bar now reads out the name of the cell under the pointer or the focus ring, and rests on the icon already set when neither is on the grid. The grid is unchanged: no name beside any cell, same icons, same groups.

## v0.4.8 — 2026-09-07

Landed as 136c07c. Fixed:

- [[Issue#69]] Programmatic scrolling jumps, and scrolls every ancestor with it (Gerrit 242)
- [[Issue#110]] Import drops a plain number field (Gerrit 243)
- [[Issue#114]] Stale server process serves new app.js against an old engine — creates fail until restart (Gerrit 244)

- **A server older than its own checkout says so** (Issue #114): static assets are read from disk per request and `src/*` is loaded once at boot, so a checkout that moves under a running process serves new client code against an old engine — on 2026-08-28 that made + New and Shift+Enter fail silently for three minutes, with nothing on screen naming the mismatch. `/api/health` now carries `diskSha` beside `sha` and the verdict `stale`, read for real (throttled to 5s) rather than inferred: the existing `behind` cannot stand in for it, since that compares the boot commit to the *remote*, arrives lazily or not at all, and its remedy is a pull rather than a restart. The instance chip in the bottom-right wears the danger tint with both commits, and a toast on load names the running commit, the one that served the page, and the restart. `weave service status` reports the same verdict — its old check compared version strings, and most commits do not bump the version.
- **Import carries every column across** (Issue #110): a table's columns are read from `fieldOrder` everywhere they are listed — the grid, `describeSchema()` and so `GET /api/schema`, the CSV header, the phone applet — while the fields themselves live in `db.fields`. An order that had forgotten a field left that field present and invisible, and `importJSON` copied the order across verbatim, so a plain `number` column arrived on the far side of `GET /api/export` → `POST /api/import` with the same table and entity counts and no column. Opening a workspace and importing one now reconcile the two: an id naming no field goes, a field the order forgot comes back on the end, and the repair is written once rather than re-derived on every open.

- **One scroll moves one box** (Issue #69): `Element.scrollIntoView()` is defined to scroll every scrollable ancestor of its target, so jumping to a heading in a docked document dragged the page behind the dock along with it — the reset Kyle reported against the outline rail. The four programmatic scrolls (the outline rail, the editor's slash menu, the search palette, a new grid row taking the caret) now go through `scrollTargetIntoView()`, which resolves the one box that may move and leaves every other scroller where the reader left it. The rail's jump became a glide, and lands the heading on the same reading line its tracker measures from; a reader who asked for less motion, and a hidden tab that would never run the animation frames, still get the instant landing. `keepScroll()` holds every box the reader had scrolled instead of the grid's alone. The arithmetic — which box, and where its scrollTop lands — is pure, in `public/editor-lib.js`.

## v0.4.9 — 2026-09-07

Landed as 056519e. Fixed:

- [[Issue#216]] appears-hidden browser suite times out under the full gate (Gerrit 291)
- [[Issue#199]] grid-tab-focus-browser: 'a redraw triggered by an edit leaves focus on the row' flakes ~1 in 6 runs (Gerrit 292)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md. The eleven bullets below landed on main from other sessions between v0.4.8 and tonight; every row they name is linked under Fixes and Ships.

- **Autocomplete in the formula itself** (Feature #207): in the script box, `[` offers this table's readable fields and two letters offer the functions that start with them, in a popover positioned at the caret (a mirror div wearing the textarea's metrics, no editor dependency), drawn from the same two lists the chips use and ranked by prefix. ↑ ↓ move, Return picks and lands a call's caret between the parens, Escape closes the list without closing the tray. `formulaSuggest()` / `formulaApply()` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` are the pure half. Gates: `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`, `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A formula preview you can steer** (Feature #206, Issue #237): the check's verdict names the result `type` (number, text, boolean, list, null, error), and `scan: true` — `--scan` on the CLI, `{scan: true}` on `weave_check_formula` and `POST /api/tables/:id/formula-check` — evaluates over up to 200 rows for `{rows, capped, nulls, errors, sampleByOutcome}`, the figures an agent asserts against before saving. The dialog wears the type as a badge, steps the preview through the rows with `‹ row n of N ›`, reports `⚠ n rows → null · m → #ERR`, and shows the **Result format** section only for a numeric result. The agent-surface gate now reads `checkFormula`'s signature so an option missing from any door fails the build. Found on the way: `dateadd()` on an empty date returned the epoch shifted, not null (Issue #237). Gates: `test/formula-check.test.mjs`, `test/agent-surface.test.mjs`, `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`, `test/formula.test.mjs`.
- **The formula dialog prints its own API** (Feature #205): a collapsed **As an agent would do it** footer under the script shows the CLI lines for what is being built — `weave formula check`, `weave field add`/`update` with the expression, `weave get` — and the MCP sequence `weave_check_formula → weave_add_field → weave_get_entity`, following the name box and the expression as they are typed. `agentRecipe()` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` is the string builder (shell-quoted, placeholders for what is not typed yet). Gates: `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`, `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`.
- **Formula chips that teach** (Feature #204): the builder's function chips sit in the four groups the grammar has — logic, text, number, date — and hovering, focusing or tapping a chip shows a card with the signature, one sentence of doc and an example, in the DOM rather than a title tooltip. Document and attachments fields are listed greyed with the reason instead of vanishing. Every `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` entry carries `group`, `doc` and `example`, and `weave_vocabulary` / `weave vocabulary formulaFunctions` / `GET /api/vocabulary` serve the catalog verbatim. Gates: `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`, `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`, `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A text field can be literal** (Issue #86): `{ "literal": true }` on a text field's config — the dialog's **Literal** box, or `--config` from the CLI/MCP — paints the characters as typed instead of dressing inline markdown, so a column of syntax, a regex or a glob reads as written. Gates: `test/text-literal.test.mjs`, `test/text-literal-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A date box is as wide as its date** (Issue #159): the date input was a fixed 120/200px box, and an ordinal costume ("Wednesday 30th September 2026") was cut off inside it. The box now measures its text in its own font and grows to it; the stylesheet width is the floor. Gate: `test/date-box-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The clipped-cell expansion opens for a resting pointer** (Issue #67): crossing a row of clipped cells flashed each one in turn; a cell now expands after the pointer has rested on it for 180ms, and a pointer that leaves first opens nothing. The design questions the Issue left open are answered in its note. Gate in `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs`.
- **The grid-tab-focus suite waits for the cursor, not for two animation frames** (Issue #199): the first assertion failed about once in six runs, reading `{ eid: null, field: null, tag: 'BODY' }` where the tabbed cell belongs. It settled and then read focus in a second round trip, and the redraw lands between the two: replacing the `<tbody>` drops focus on `<body>` until `restoreGridFocus` puts the cursor back a frame later. A per-frame trace of the gesture shows the dip plainly — `TD/Tail` → `BODY` → `TD/Tail`, 16ms apart on an idle machine, and unbounded on a loaded one. The wait now reports the cell it settled on from inside the same evaluate, so no frame separates settling from reading, and the "mark gone plus two animation frames" read is gone with it. Every wait in the suite also carried a 5s cap while the suite itself has taken 52s under the full gate (`review-logs/227-1`) and 27s (`282-1`); the caps are gone, and a case that holds the redraw's query open for 5.5s keeps them gone. Tab out of a resting cell still reads focus without waiting, because it writes nothing and nothing is in flight. Gate: `test/grid-tab-focus-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The appears-as browser suite waits for the eye's round trip, not for a sleep** (Issue #216): `test/appears-hidden-browser.test.mjs` timed out on two of four full-gate runs while passing every time on its own. A flip is a PATCH, then the page's redraw, then the popover teaching its own rows the new state — and the helper waited only for the popover to close plus 400ms, a margin the tail clears by 20ms when the machine is idle and misses under a loaded gate. A rebuild landing inside the next flip's click orphans the mousedown, so no `click` fires and focus falls to `<body>`, where Escape can no longer reach the popover: it stays open and the wait burns its full 30s. The helper now waits for the switch itself to read the new state, which is the last step of that round trip, and the sleep is gone. `test/entity-eye-sync-browser.test.mjs` already waited on that signal but capped it at 5s, and the same round trip took 8.7s on a loaded gate; the cap is gone too.
- **A writer token cannot un-trash a table** (Issue #149): `POST /api/tables/:id/restore` joins move and duplicate in the schema-write gate. Gate in `test/table-move-duplicate.test.mjs`.
- **The outline opens in place** (Issues #131, #144): clicking the dash rail used to float the headings in a fixed panel at the viewport's middle, so the outline "snapped" away from the dashes just clicked. The panel now widens the minimap where it is — same sticky anchor, same left edge — and the inline x-pin that fixed positioning needed is gone. Browser gate: `test/doc-rail-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A sniffed diagram draws, a sniffed model edits as code** (Issues #188, #189): an undeclared document field holding mermaid source or a JSON model went to the markdown editor, which drew the source as paragraphs. `docViewMode` now returns `diagram` for mermaid (drawn by the one `renderMermaidIn` every fenced block uses, with the app's `</>` source toggle) and `code` for JSON (the monospace code box). The mermaid sniff wants a diagram header — `graph LR`, `flowchart TD`, `pie title …`, a kind on its own line — so "graph theory, a primer" stays markdown. Browser gate: `test/doc-kinds-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The slash menu is a list to scroll, not a sheet** (Issue #137): the inline clamp let the menu grow to the whole viewport; it is now capped at 400px with tighter rows, and a wheel over the menu stops at the menu's edge instead of chaining to the page — the window scroll that Vditor answers by closing the menu ("it disappears when trying to scroll"). Browser gate in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`.

releases.name: v0.4.10
fixes: Slow: project page not loading stuck on skeleton'
Nine watcher ops rows claim they were fixed in v0.4.5
Looks broken: double nested scroll bar when trying to scroll past the end int Abel view
The Quality mirror is 28 test files behind
A late eye-popover rebuild swallows the click that is in progress
releases.description:
## v0.4.10 — 2026-09-08

Landed as 69718fd. Fixed:

- [[Issue#118]] A route that fails says so, instead of holding the skeleton (Gerrit 300)
- [[Issue#229]] v0.4.5 no longer claims nine fixes it never made (Gerrit 301)
- [[Issue#136]] One box scrolls on the table page (Gerrit 299)
- [[Issue#95]] One Suite row per test file, enforced (Gerrit 297)
- [[Issue#240]] The eye's rows are taught, not swapped (Gerrit 294)

- **A route that fails says so, instead of holding the skeleton** (Issue #118): opening uno's Project table left the page on its loading skeleton and never took it off. The grid's `POST /tables/<id>/query` answered 500, `showDatabase`'s await rejected, and nothing above it caught — `paintSkeleton` had already replaced `#main`, so the page sat holding the skeleton of a table that was never going to arrive. The hole belonged to every route rather than to the grid: `showEntity` was the only one that caught at all, and it caught by falling home, which says nothing about what broke. `paintRouteError` now names the failure in the server's own words and carries the retry where the skeleton used to wait, and both entry points end in it — `renderRouteSafely` wraps the hashchange render (through `Promise.resolve().then`, since `renderRoute` may return a promise, a value or nothing, and may throw before it returns) and boot's first render gets the same catch. The card is Tabler tokens only, so it reads in both themes. The 500 itself no longer reproduces on main: its cause was a rollup or lookup whose target field had been deleted, which made `#resolve` throw on every read that reached the row, and `ae1f150` fixed that (Issue #206) — uno's Project table still carries the scar in its description, a "Total Estimate" rollup over a Task estimate that no longer exists. Verified on a copy of the live uno workspace: the pre-fix build painted 83 skeleton elements and no error state, this one paints the error card and none. Gates: `test/route-error-browser.test.mjs`, `test/page-loader.test.mjs`.

- **v0.4.5 no longer claims nine fixes it never made** (Issue #229): the main watcher files a `gerrit/main @ <sha> did not reach GitHub` row every time its mirror push is refused, and a closing sweep on 2026-09-05 linked nine of those rows `Fixed in → v0.4.5`. That release merged the same morning and touched none of them — the mirror failures ended when `gh`'s active account went back to `grunion-ai`. The nine are unlinked from the release's `Fixes` and stay closed; v0.4.5 carries Issues #134, #83, #133 and #232 with Features #175, #190 and #195, as it always did. The manifest is gated on it now: no release in `docs/development.json` may name a watcher incident row among its fixes. Gate: `test/development-sync.test.mjs`.

- **One box scrolls on the table page** (Issue #136): a grid wider than its card scrolls in a box of its own (Issue #233), and that box claimed half the screen whatever stood above it. On a short window the chrome, the half-screen box and the gutter under it added up past the viewport, so the page scrolled around a box that already scrolled — the two nested bars Kyle filed, where the inner one runs out and the outer one takes over. The box is cut to the room left below its own top now, and where that room falls under 120px the page takes the whole scroll back: one box moves either way. The cut also follows the box while the chrome above it is still arriving — a description that lands after the grid moves the box down, and the first measurement is then a box too tall for the room. Measured on the Issue table at 1470×500, the page overflowed the window by 74px and now overflows by none. Gate: `test/grid-scroll-region-browser.test.mjs`.

- **One Suite row per test file, enforced** (Issue #95): the Quality mirror is generated from `test/`, and the Suite table says "One row per test file" — but two files had grown a second row each (`applet` alongside `Applet`, and two `Structure trash` rows), and no amount of syncing removed them. `syncQualityMirror` keyed the workspace's existing rows into a `Map` by File, so a second row with the same File overwrote the first and the loser was then invisible to both passes: never renamed, never reconciled, never pruned. The rows are grouped by File now instead of overwritten, the oldest row wins (keeping the id anything already links to), and every twin is pruned by the same pass that clears a suite whose file left the tree. `weave quality check` therefore reports the drift it used to skip — it was returning `removedSuites: 0` against a live mirror carrying 182 rows for 180 files. Gate: `test/quality-mirror.test.mjs`.

- **The eye's rows are taught, not swapped** (Issue #240): flick two switches quickly and the second one did nothing — no movement, no column change, and focus left on `<body>` so Escape stopped closing the popover. A flip's tail is asynchronous (PATCH, schema reload, redraw, then the rows), and under load nothing bounds it, so it could land between a mousedown and its mouseup; `replaceChildren` then detached the row the mousedown had focused, and a down and an up on different nodes fire no `click` at all. `relearnRows` now copies the new switch state onto the rows that are already there, keeping the node, its focus and `showPopover`'s arrow walk — which captures its row list once, at open — and rebuilds only when the row set itself changed, where Issue #223's focus restore still applies. Each row handler reads the table at click time, since a taught row keeps the handler it was built with. The Σ footer picker shares the tail and the fix. Gates: `test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.11 — 2026-09-08

Landed as 343d475. Fixed:

- [[Issue#244]] A manifest correction never reaches an instance that already applied the wrong one (Gerrit 304)

- **A corrected manifest can take back what a wrong one claimed** (Issue #244): fixing v0.4.5's `Fixes` in the canonical workspace and re-exporting `docs/development.json` repaired the canonical record and every instance that had yet to sync. The one instance that synced between the mistake and the correction kept the false claim, and would have kept it forever — `syncDevelopment` applied the manifest additively, so `w.link(id, 'Fixes', …)` added the nine watcher rows and nothing ever removed them, however few targets the next manifest named. A release row is manifest-owned in a way an Issue row is not: no instance links its own rows into an upstream release, so its `Fixes` and `Ships` are reconciled to exactly what the manifest names, added and unlinked both. Issue and Feature rows stay additive, which is what protects a locally filed row through an update. Reproduced on a fresh workspace fed the 2026-09-05 manifest and then the corrected one: the old code held 13 fixes with 9 watcher rows among them, this one lands on the 4 the manifest names. Gate: `test/development-sync.test.mjs`.

fixes: A fresh install applies half its manifest: an unknown Milestone throws and boot swallows it
releases.description:
## v0.4.12 — 2026-09-08

Landed as 3caf058. Fixed:

- [[Issue#245]] A fresh install applies half its manifest: an unknown Milestone throws and boot swallows it (Gerrit 306)
- **A fresh install applies its whole manifest** (Issue #245): the shipped `docs/development.json` carries Feature rows whose `Milestone` the seeded select stops short of — `v0.4`, `v0.5` — and a select validates on write, so `syncDevelopment` threw on the first such row. The throw landed mid-pass: Issues applied, Features applied up to that row, the release block never reached, and the stamp, written last, never set — so every boot repeated the same half-pass behind `bin/weave.js`'s bare `catch { /* no manifest in this build */ }`, a comment naming the one thing that was not happening. `widenSelects` now appends the values the manifest carries to a select or multiselect before any row is applied, append-only, so existing option ids and hues survive along with the rows holding them. Each row's writes are guarded on top of that: a row the workspace still cannot take costs that row rather than the pass or the release block behind it, and is named in the returned `skipped`; only a whole pass writes `meta.developmentSync`, so a skipped row comes back on the next boot. The boot catch prints what it swallowed. A freshly seeded workspace fed the shipped manifest went from a throw, no stamp and 0 Release rows to 430 rows created, 12 updated and 11 releases with their contents. Gate: `test/development-sync.test.mjs`.

## v0.4.13 — 2026-09-08

Landed as fa06db7. Fixed:

- [[Issue#249]] Looks broken: hide summation row by default (Gerrit 314)
- [[Issue#121]] Wrong data: file missing? (Gerrit 277)

Also shipped: [[Feature#219]], the registry at the weave root, which landed earlier today.

- **The registry lives at the weave root** (Feature #219): the system registry — Spaces, Tables, Fields, Workflows as rows — exists once, in the Workspace space of the default workspace, instead of being minted inside every workspace file. The root grows a `Workspaces` table (one row per workspace the hub serves — the level-1 row `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` said was missing) and every registry table gains a system `Workspace` relation, so uno's tables and test's sit side by side under one column. A member workspace joins the root on adoption: its sidebar shows only its own spaces, its structure is projected as root rows its own structural verbs keep true, and a row edit at the root routes to the engine that owns it. A legacy per-workspace `Workspace` space is tombstoned (rows kept) and its space rollups move to the root Spaces table, where `via` now names a table in any workspace — the Σ row and the space tiles keep working in members. Registry rows deep-link into their workspace; a member's `/w/<id>/api` answers for its registry rows. The Worker's single-workspace hub is its own root, unchanged. Handbook: **Registry at the root**. Gates: `test/root-registry.test.mjs`, `test/root-registry-hub.test.mjs`, `test/root-registry-routes.test.mjs`, `test/root-registry-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A grid has no Σ row until someone asks for one** (Issue #249): Kyle filed "hide summation row by default" from a uno table. The Σ row shipped in Issue #233 as on-unless-hidden, and the flag behind it stored only the hiding: `hideRollups: true` meant off and the absence meant on. Flipping the default on that shape would have hidden the rows Kyle had switched on himself, because a table he opted into looked exactly like one he had never opened. So the flag now says both things — `false` is a table that asked for the row, `true` is one switched back off, and the absence means nobody has asked, which reads as off. Nothing stored needed rewriting: `true` was off before and is off now, and every absence was on before and is the new default. The eye's **Σ rollup row** switch is the way in, and it writes both directions; the **Hide Rollups** checkbox on the Tables row reads checked for a table nobody opted in, which is what it now shows. Gates: `test/table-config-fields.test.mjs`, `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.
- **A JSON export carries its attachment bytes, and a lost blob says so** (Issue #121): a file-backed workspace keeps attachment blobs in a sibling `files/` directory, outside `state`, and `exportJSON()` was a deep clone of `state` — so a dump named every file and carried none of them. `weave export --out dump.json` then `weave import --file dump.json` into another data directory left every attachment as metadata pointing at nothing: the row still offered a link, the link answered raw 404 JSON, and the reporter could only ask "file missing?". The export now walks each entity's file ledger and the workspace logo, reads those blobs and carries them as base64; `importJSON` — and opening a `.json` dump as a workspace, which is an import by another name — writes them back into `files/` and drops `fileBlobs` from state, so no base64 rides a save into `weave_meta`. A blob already gone is simply absent: an export must not fail on damage it did not do. `weave export` and `GET /api/export` always carry the bytes; MCP's `weave_export_json` is a reader rather than a backup and omits them unless asked (`blobs: true`). The other half is the loss itself: `readEntity` marks a file whose blob is gone with `missing: true`, the dressed cell reads `c-json-editor.html (missing)`, and the entity page and the grid cell drop the anchor and draw the name dimmed in a dashed chip. No new colour, and the × stays, so a dead pointer can be cleared. Gates: `test/file-blobs.test.mjs`, `test/attachment-missing-browser.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.14 — 2026-09-09

Landed as 749002e. Fixed:

- [[Issue#222]] The field dialog cannot author a space rollup (via) — only the Σ footer picker and the API can (Gerrit 321)

- **The field dialog can write a space rollup** (Issue #222): a rollup over a whole table — the Σ under a grid column — is a field on the `Workspace/Spaces` row of the space that holds the table, and `via` names the table instead of a relation to cross. Three surfaces wrote one: the Σ footer picker with a switch, `weave field add --config`, and `weave_add_field`. The dialog offered only the registry's own relations, so `+ field → rollup` on the Spaces grid could produce a count of `Tables` or `Workflows` and nothing else. Its rollup section now asks **Rolls up** — *Through a relation* or *Over a table* — on the Spaces registry, the one place the engine accepts `via`, and *Over a table* picks the table, the aggregate and the column. Every other grid's rollup section is untouched, because `via` is refused there. Reopening a space rollup also folds back onto its table and keeps its `where`, where before it claimed an empty relation and dropped the filter. Writing a filter stays API-only. Gates: `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`, `test/space-rollup-dialog-browser.test.mjs`.

## v0.4.15 — 2026-09-09

Landed as 253d36c. Fixed:

- [[Issue#44]] Slash-command browser tests flake under the full suite (Gerrit 323)
- [[Issue#239]] Browser suites flake under the full parallel gate (Gerrit 323)

- **A test that fails once gets asked again** (Issues #44 and #239): `npm test` runs through `scripts/test.mjs`, which re-runs the files that failed — only those — and lets the second answer stand. Sixty-eight of the 192 suites drive a real Chromium, and under the full run a wait for a menu to paint can lose to a thirty-second budget: a different browser case failed on roughly every other full run while the same file alone was green eight times out of eight, and each one cost a Verified −1 on a change that was fine plus a re-gate to prove it. A regression is not a coin toss, so a broken file fails both times and the vote stands; the retry can only rescue a failure that did not reproduce. Nothing green pays for it — there is no second run on a passing suite. The flake is not absorbed either: every retried file is named on stdout under `# RETRYING` and `# RETRIED`, inside the `tail` that `weave-review.sh` quotes into its Verified +1, so a suite that keeps needing the second chance says so in the review that passed it. Capping browser concurrency was the other candidate and the measurements refused it: the 68 browser suites take 110 s at `--test-concurrency=4` against 66–70 s at 10, 16 and 24, and were green at every one of those over eight runs. `npm test` is now the one command in the README, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, the PR template and the GitHub matrix. Gates: `test/test-runner.test.mjs`, `test/extras.test.mjs`.

releases.name: v0.4.16

# column should freeze to the left edge and never reorder
ships: Grid ranges: shift-select cells, drag-fill, and copy/paste values (select and multi-select included)
releases.description:
## v0.4.16 — 2026-09-10

Landed as 6ea8aa4. Fixed:

- [[Issue#251]] State field should start with default states (Gerrit 326)
- [[Issue#252]] # column should freeze to the left edge and never reorder (Gerrit 327)

Also ships [[Feature#220]] Grid ranges: shift-select cells, drag-fill, and copy/paste values, which landed as 3657be2 after v0.4.15.

- **The # column freezes to the grid's left edge** (Issue #252): a wide table scrolls sideways inside its wrap, and the whole header used to go with it — scroll right to read a far column and the row lost its identity, with no id to say which record the values belonged to and the `#12 ↗` permalink off screen. The `#` and the selection checkbox beside it are anchored to the wrap's left edge now, and they travel as a pair: the checkbox pinned at the edge, the `#` clearing exactly the width the checkbox column renders at, which the suite reads off the live layout rather than trusting the arithmetic. A frozen cell floats over content that is still moving, so it paints: a token ground in both themes, a chosen row's 9% accent mixed against that surface instead of against `transparent`, and a hairline down its right edge that is reserved at rest and only takes its colour once the wrap is actually scrolled — the frozen column reads as a seam, not as a panel laid over the grid. Five sticky layers now have numbers instead of sharing two, because a tie is broken by document order and that put a body cell over the Σ rollup row it scrolls beneath: frozen body cells, the Σ row, the Σ row's own frozen corner, the header, the header's corner. The other half of the Issue — that no drag can move the `#` or land a field ahead of it — was already locked when Issue #139 landed and needed no change. Gates: `test/frozen-id-column-browser.test.mjs` (11 cases, both themes, including the Σ row, the sticky `+ New` row and a grid with no checkbox column) and the standing `test/table-reorder-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A state field starts with states in it** (Issue #251): adding a **State** column opened the tray on an empty list and then refused the save — "Workflow field needs at least one state" — so a status column cost you a status vocabulary before it could exist, and `weave field add T Status workflow` threw unless `--config` carried a `states` array. The engine already knows four state categories, and those four are the lifecycle almost every column wants: a workflow whose config omits `states` now arrives as **Not started · In progress · Done · Canceled**, one per category, `Not started` the default. The seed sits at the point of blankness rather than in a relaxed validation — `normalizeSelfContainedConfig` fills an absent `states`, the tray's `blankState('workflow')` hands back the same four, and `"states": []` is still refused, because a list someone emptied on purpose is not a lifecycle. An option-less select converting to a workflow lands on the four as well, where it used to hit that refusal. The four are ordinary states once they are there: rename, reorder, recolour, add and delete them in the field config tray. Handbook: the `workflow` page's Config section names the defaults and the empty-array refusal. Gates: `test/workflow-defaults.test.mjs` (8 cases — engine, CLI, REST and MCP parity, dialog round-trip, and the dialog/engine/Handbook parity), `test/workflow-defaults-browser.test.mjs` (4 cases, both themes).
- **Grid ranges: shift-select cells, drag-fill, and copy/paste values** (Feature #220). Kyle: "I need a better way to select, drag to duplicate, copy or paste values — like single or multi select dropdowns — across cells." #134 made the cell rest as a value and #132 gave a run of ROWS one write; both stop at the row, so copying one Status onto the next four meant reopening a dialog and re-picking. A rectangle of cells is now a **range**: `⇧` and the arrows grow one, or the pointer drags one, and `Esc` lets it go — rows first when both are up, so Space and `⇧↑↓` still mean exactly what they meant. The blue square on the range's bottom-right corner is a **fill handle**: drag it down a column or across a row and the range's values are written over everything it covers, one axis at a time. `⌘C` puts TSV on the clipboard for a spreadsheet and the same block typed for another weave tab, which is what makes a select paste as an option rather than as a word; `⌘V` tiles the block to fit whatever it lands on, so one copied cell fills twenty. Select, multi-select and workflow paste by **option identity** — the id carries over within a table, the label goes into a different one, and a label that names no option there is refused rather than invented. A multi-select is a replacement, never a merge. A formula, rollup, lookup, view, relation or document column takes no paste: the cell refuses and the toast names the column, following `bulk`'s precedent of saying what did not land. Text from a spreadsheet is read in each column's own terms (`false` is false, not `Boolean('false')`), and a cell that will not read is dropped and counted while its neighbours land. The write is the existing `bulk set`, one call per distinct set of values — so a fill down twenty rows is one write — and the toast carries an **Undo** that steps the whole thing back. `bulk set` gained `changed` beside `done` for that: a row that already held the value pushes no undo entry, and counting the rows it merely visited would step past this write into somebody else's. Not built: `⇧`-click, which stays the browser's "open a window" on every navigating surface (`023b777`); the range comes from `⇧`-arrows and the pointer drag instead. Handbook: "Ranges, fill and paste" under the grid guide. Tests: `test/grid-range.test.mjs` (36 pure), `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs` (13 browser), plus 6 keymap cases and 2 engine cases.

## v0.4.17 — 2026-09-11

Landed as 7d9886a. Fixed:

- [[Issue#255]] Handbook rows in the live workspace never pick up a landed edit to src/handbook.js (Gerrit 329)

- **The Handbook on a running install follows the build** (Issue #255): `applyHandbook` wrote the `Handbook/Guide` and `Handbook/Fields` pages only from `seedWeaver`, and `serve` seeds only when no `weave.db` exists, so an existing docs workspace kept the pages of whichever build first created it. A landed Handbook edit passed its gate and never reached the reader: on 2026-09-10 the live **Making a workspace your own** guide was missing the whole "Ranges, fill and paste" section. `serve` now stamps a hash of the generated pages on the docs workspace's meta at boot, beside the Development sync, and re-applies them when the hash moves — one pass per build, not one per boot, fail-open and logged. The apply stays name-matched and additive: a guide someone wrote themselves is never touched, and nothing is deleted. `weave handbook sync --data <weave.db>` applies on demand and `weave handbook check` exits 1 on drift, modelled on `quality`. The first boot on `:4400` brought two stale field pages, `workflow` and `rollup`, up to date. Gate: `test/handbook-sync.test.mjs` (10 cases, including a real `serve` boot against a stale `weave.db`).

Paste into a relation cell links by name
Report a bug by email: a mailto from the bug panel and the route error card to weave@grunion.ai
