releases.description:
## v0.4.18 — 2026-09-12

Ships:

- [[Feature#225]] Document version history: every document field keeps browsable, restorable revisions
- [[Feature#224]] Paste into a relation cell links by name
- [[Feature#223]] Report a bug by email: a mailto from the bug panel and the route error card to weave@grunion.ai
- [[Feature#221]] Grid cell clipboard: ⌘C/⌘V follow the selection, and take the cell when there is none
- [[Feature#67]] Self-hosting: positioning as an Airtable/ClickUp/Fibery alternative + deployment guide in README

Fixed:

- [[Issue#276]] Wrong data: opening a relation replaces the left panel with the other table, cutting the breadcrumb trail

- **Every document keeps its history** (Feature #225, Kyle 2026-09-12: "all weave documents should have a built-in version history", so decklet can drop its in-file snapshots): `setDoc`/`appendDoc` overwrote `entity.docs` and the prior text survived only as an undo before-image (popped on undo) and a length delta in the feed — nothing could bring a past document back. A new `doc_revisions` table beside the entity blob (mirrored in the Durable Object store) now takes a snapshot of the new text on every document write — `setDoc`, `appendDoc`, an `updateEntity` naming a document, a create born with one. Writes by one actor to one field inside ten minutes fold into the newest snapshot (the activity feed's own window, Issue #32), so a typing session is one revision and the 600 ms autosave never builds a keystroke log; identical text records nothing; 200 per document, oldest trimmed. A document that predates the log gets its prior text as the baseline on its first write. `listDocRevisions` is metadata only, newest first (`seq`, `at`, `actor`, `len`); `getDocRevision` carries the text; `restoreDocRevision` is an ordinary `setDoc` recorded fresh, so a restore never overwrites the session it steps back from, and undo records fresh too. A purge drops the row's revisions; the trash keeps them; an export carries the current text only. Doors: `GET /api/entities/:ref/doc/revisions?field=`, `GET …/revisions/:seq`, `POST …/revisions/:seq/restore`; `weave doc-revisions` / `weave doc-restore`; `weave_doc_revisions` / `weave_doc_restore`. In the chrome, a `lucide:history` control beside the source toggle shows once a document has more than one revision and opens a panel inside the section — newest first with relative time, actor and size delta; a row renders that revision read-only in place of the editor under a **Viewing revision** bar; **Restore** writes it back and re-renders, **Back** or Escape returns. Both themes. Handbook: the `document` page's **History** section. Gates: `test/doc-revisions.test.mjs` (22 — the store contract on memory, sqlite and the DO shim; coalescing, baseline, cap, restore, undo, purge; the three doors), `test/doc-history-browser.test.mjs` (3, both themes).
- **Paste into a relation cell links by name** (Feature #224): Feature #220's plan refused a `relation` column, so once Feature #221 let ⌘V reach the cell, a paste into `Owner` or `Peers` wrote nothing and the toast named the column. A paste now links: the grid fetches the related table's rows first — the same `POST /api/tables/:id/query` the record picker runs — and the pure plan matches each label to a row, a copied weave block by id, otherwise the exact name (trimmed, case-insensitive), then `#12`. Matched ids ride the existing `bulk set` (the engine's `updateEntity` already replaces a relation's whole set from an id list, and a single-cardinality field takes one), so a paste is one call per distinct value set with one Undo, and copy is untouched. A label that names no row is counted and named in the toast (`1 unmatched (Nobody)`) beside the unreadable count; a cell whose labels all miss is dropped rather than emptied. Without the rows to hand — a fetch that failed — the column refuses by name as before. Handbook: the "What the types force" list under "Ranges, fill and paste". Gates: `test/grid-range.test.mjs` (+8 pure: `resolveRelation`, the relation plan, the toast), `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs` (+3: copy → paste → chips → Undo; a TSV label with one stranger; a single relation from `#id, name`).
- **Passkeys: people sign in without a token** (Feature #222 part 2, door B; Feature #208; Feature #141 §3): with `requireAuth` on, a browser had no way in that did not involve pasting a `wv_` secret. `GET /auth` is now a sign-in page served through the wall — one button, a discoverable passkey, no username step — and `/api/auth/*` carries the two WebAuthn ceremonies, verified with `node:crypto` and a 60-line CBOR decoder, no dependency: `none` attestation, ES256 or RS256, clientDataJSON type/challenge/origin, `rpIdHash`, user presence, the signature over `authData || sha256(clientDataJSON)`, and a counter that must advance once either side counts. A verified sign-in mints a 30-day sliding session in an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` cookie (`Secure` under an https `WEAVE_ORIGIN`), stored as its sha256 beside the account; the wall accepts it as it accepts a Bearer token, and a Bearer token wins when both are present. A dead cookie sends a page to `/auth?next=…` and an API call to a JSON 401. The first passkey starts from the CLI: `weave account invite <name>` prints a one-time URL good for 15 minutes; `account sessions`, `account revoke-session --all`, `account remove-credential` are the lost-device verbs, on the CLI and on `weave_accounts`. `/auth` doubles as the account page — passkeys, sessions, sign out, sign out others, add this device. `WEAVE_ORIGIN` is required when auth is on off loopback (`serve` refuses to start without it); `WEAVE_TRUST_PROXY=1` lets the in-memory rate limits (10 options and 5 failed verifies a minute per address) read `X-Forwarded-For` behind Railway or Fly. Sessions and invites never leave through an export. New Handbook guide **Door B: passkeys**. Gates: `test/webauthn.test.mjs` (fixtures built in-test from a software authenticator, every negative case), `test/auth-session.test.mjs` (engine + routes: invite → register → wall → logout → wall; expiry, revocation, rate limits, Bearer precedence), `test/auth-passkey-browser.test.mjs` (Chromium's virtual authenticator through the real page).
- **`weave backup` and `weave restore`, with a nightly that needs one env var** (Feature #222 phase 3, Feature #209, Issue #250): the only backups were a laptop script into iCloud and the JSON export the Handbook warns drops attachments. `weave backup` now takes the whole data directory — every workspace `.db` through `VACUUM INTO` from a throwaway connection, so a server mid-write neither blocks it nor lands in it; `files/`; `keystore.json` — into one POSIX tar with a `manifest.json` last: entries, a sha256 per entry, entity counts per workspace, the weave version, and the orphan report. `keystore.key` never goes in; its material seals the archive instead (AES-256-GCM under a scrypt key), or `WEAVE_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` / `WEAVE_KEYSTORE_PASSPHRASE` when set, and with none of the three the archive is a plain tar and says so. A reference to a blob that is gone from `files/` (Issue #250 found fifty-six) is counted and listed, never fatal. `--dest s3://bucket/prefix` (or `WEAVE_BACKUP_DEST`) uploads with a SigV4 signer written on `fetch` and `node:crypto` — R2 via `WEAVE_BACKUP_ENDPOINT`, B2, S3 — and prunes past the newest thirty archives; the signer reproduces the three worked examples in the S3 reference. `weave restore <archive|s3://…|https://…> --data <dir>` verifies every sha256 against the manifest, refuses a database a server holds open (a `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar or a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` that cannot take the lock) and an existing target without `--force`, then unpacks; `weave restore <ref>` stays the entity verb. `weave serve` with `WEAVE_BACKUP_DEST` set runs the backup daily at 04:00 UTC on an in-process timer chain (Railway cron services cannot share the volume), writes `backup-completed` / `backup-failed` to the audit log, and `/api/health` carries `backup: {lastAt, lastStatus, nextAt, dest}`. Handbook: **Backup and restore** — the three variables, R2/B2/S3 examples, retention, the rehearsal, `keystore.key`, Litestream as the upgrade. Gate G4: `test/backup.test.mjs` (23 cases — round trip with two workspaces, an attachment byte-for-byte, an orphan and the keystore; live-writer safety; the ustar writer against `tar -tf`; the signer vectors; upload, list and prune against an in-test bucket; the scheduler on a fake clock; health).
- **The dock follows the click; the page stays** (Issue #276, Kyle 2026-09-12): a relation chip pointing at a row in another table used to tear the table down, push `#/table/<other>` and dock the row beside the *other* table, so the crumb restarted there and the reader lost the grid they were reading. `openEntity` now docks the row beside the table under the reader whatever table the row lives in, pushes no history, and only travels when there is no table page at all (home, a space, activity, ⌘K from there). A hop from inside the dock extends the dock's chain across tables — each frame carries its own table, the state carries the anchor — and the dock's crumb is that chain run through `entityCrumbs`, so the table crumb appears where it changes (`Deals › Acme › Contacts › #4`) and a new back arrow (or Esc) walks it one frame back; a frame already on the chain cuts back to it. `?e=<id>` on the current table hash survives a reload for a foreign row, which renders from its own table. The expand arrow still lands on `#/entity/<id>`. Gates: `test/entity-dock-browser.test.mjs` (4 new cases), `test/entity-dock-default-browser.test.mjs` (expectations moved to the page-stays rule, plus the no-table-under-you case), `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` (`dockCrumbs`). Handbook: the grid guide names the rule.
- **The auth wall covers every route, and an export keeps its secrets** (Feature #222 phase 0, Issue #230, Feature #194 problem 2): `requireAuth` and the role caps applied to `/api/*` only, so with auth on every entity page, `doc.html`, `entity.pdf`, `deck.html` and the app shell itself were readable by anyone who reached the port. With `requireAuth` on, every route now needs a Bearer token; a browser gets a small page saying the workspace requires authentication, an API call keeps the JSON 401. The doors that stay open: `/api/health`, a view's share link, the passcode applet under `/t`, and the static CSS/JS/font/image assets a sign-in page will need. A reader token may read any page and write at none. `GET /api/export` — and `weave export`, and the MCP tool — no longer carry account `tokenHash` values or view share tokens: an imported account keeps its name and role but verifies no token until re-created, an imported view arrives unshared until shared again. `POST /api/import` is a schema write and needs an admin token. Gate: `test/auth-wall.test.mjs` (six cases; the route list is derived from `src/routes.js` so a new route cannot hole the wall unnoticed).
- **Grid cell clipboard follows the selection** (Feature #221, Kyle's "B+", 2026-09-12): a click opens a cell exactly as before, and `⌘C`/`⌘V` follow the selection — text selected in the open control is the browser's own copy and paste; with no selection (a bare caret, a picker's popover, a checkbox, a resting cell) they take the **cell**, typed, through Feature #220's `bulk set` with one Undo. A clicked text-like cell opens with its whole value selected, and a second click places the caret. Chips, url links, the `#id` link, checkbox flips and pickers are untouched. Pure rule `WeaveGridKeymap.clipboardTarget` (`test/grid-keymap.test.mjs`); gestures in `test/grid-range-browser.test.mjs`; the Handbook's grid guide names both rules.

releases.name: v0.4.19
fixes: Wrong data: date and number columns sort by their display string, so Sep 9 rows sit above Sep 12
Wrong data: a formula that depends on itself through a cycle resolves to null with no error
Wrong data: the End key is swallowed inside the inline cell editor
releases.description:
## v0.4.19 — 2026-09-13

Landed as 6ccb90b. Fixed:

- [[Issue#279]] Wrong data: date and number columns sort by their display string, so Sep 9 rows sit above Sep 12 (Gerrit 343)
- [[Issue#283]] Wrong data: a formula that depends on itself through a cycle resolves to null with no error (Gerrit 344)
- [[Issue#260]] Wrong data: the End key is swallowed inside the inline cell editor (Gerrit 345)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **The caret keys stay with the caret** (Issue #260): click into a long name, press End, type — and the edit landed in the MIDDLE of the value. A CX audit did exactly that and left Issue #85 named "L zzs broken: …". `End` inside an open cell was the browser's, and Chromium reads a bare End in a single-line field as *scroll to the end of the document*: the windowed grid (Issue #271) scrolled a thousand rows, recycled the row the editor sat in and dropped focus on `<body>`, while the caret never moved. The grid places the caret itself now — `Home` and `End` in an open cell resolve to a `caret` verb and the keystroke is consumed, so nothing scrolls — and only for a single-line `<input>`: a textarea's `End` belongs to the line it is on, and a select, number or date control has no caret to place, so each of those keeps the browser's key. `⇧End`, `⌥←`/`⌥→` and `⌘←`/`⌘→` are real editing commands, were never broken, and stay the browser's; at rest `Home`/`End` are still the first and the last ROW of the table. Handbook: the **In an open cell** table in the grid guide. Gates: `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs` (the open-cell verb, the three modified forms, and the resting rows), `test/grid-window-browser.test.mjs` (End in an open cell of a 1,200-row table: the caret lands at the end of the value, the window holds its scroll, and the next character appends).
- **A loop says so** (Issue #283): a formula that reached its own field the long way round — `Total` reading `Bonus` while `Bonus` read `Total` — hit the depth-8 recursion guard, which returned `null`. The cell then read like a legitimately empty one, and one level up the arithmetic turned that null into a number nobody could explain (a two-row rollup loop computed `6`). Two halves now. **At save**, an expression that closes a cycle through the table's other formulas is refused with the path — `Formula 'Bonus' would close a reference cycle: Bonus → Total → Bonus` — on `addField`, on `updateField`, on a text→formula type change (which validated nothing), and in `checkFormula`, so the dialog says it before the save does; the walk only follows formula→formula edges, every other type being a leaf, and a field that is not in the table yet is matched by the name a live formula still calls it. **At read**, a computed field that re-enters itself for the same row answers with `#CYCLE:` and the path instead of null — fields alone when the loop stays on one row, `Alpha › Double → Alpha › PeerSum → Beta › Double → Beta › PeerSum → Alpha › Double` when it travels between rows, because the rows are what closed it — and the marker travels rather than being consumed: a formula reading a looping field reports the loop, a rollup reports it rather than summing it, a lookup carries it out, and no display costume is painted over it. The loop that no save can see — one that closes through a rollup or a lookup, which needs two rows pointing at each other — is exactly what this half catches. The stack unwinds in a `finally`, so an erroring formula never leaves the next read looking cyclic. Gates: `test/formula-cycle.test.mjs` (11 — the four save doors, the REST 400, the rollup loop through two rows, the row outside the loop, the unwind, and `references()` over both arms of `if`).
- **A sort orders the value, not the costume it wears** (Issue #279): uno's `Agent/Sessions` — 720 rows, sorted Created descending, Created a `date` field wearing the `long` format — put "Sep 9, 2026 9:51 AM" above every row created on Sep 12, so an hourly writer's rows read as missing. Both comparators had been handed the painted string: the engine's `#pathValue` returns display values, and `query`'s sort compared those, while `public/app.js` compared `item.fields[…]` for the grids that hold every row. `"Sep 9"` beats `"Sep 12"` as text, `"15,829,984"` loses to `"900"`, and `"$17.25"` beats `"$9.50"`. Sorting now undresses the two types whose painted form does not order the way the value does — a number stays a number, a date stays its stored instant — and leaves every other type on its display form, because for an option, a state or a joined relation the name *is* the value. It is the rule a formula already read by (`#resolve`) and the one the Handbook's date guide already promised ("comparison, sorting and date math all run on the stored value"). Filters are untouched: `contains "Sep"` still reads the costume. Both halves changed together, so a paged grid (server-side sort, Issue #271) and a whole one land in the same order. Gates: `test/sort-values.test.mjs` (5 — date, number through separators and currency, select by option name, empty cells last, the filter guard), `test/sort-values-browser.test.mjs` (2 — the same table read through the server's sort and through the grid's own).

releases.name: v0.4.20
fixes: Wrong data: a daterange column sorts by its painted range, so Oct 1 sits above Sep 9
Slash-menu wheel test flakes on its own (fails 2 of 3 runs alone on main)
releases.description:
## v0.4.20 — 2026-09-14

Landed as 1dc47fb. Fixed:

- [[Issue#287]] A range sorts by its start, then by its end (Gerrit 347)
- [[Issue#275]] The slash-menu wheel case waits for the page, not for a clock (Gerrit 348)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **The slash-menu wheel case stops racing its own page** (Issue #275): the Issue #137 case in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs` — "a wheel over the slash menu never scrolls the page out from under it" — lost three of Gerrit 334's gate runs on a change that never went near the editor, and took the Verified vote down with it. The flake lived in the keystroke that opens the menu. Vditor hides its hint on any scroll, with a listener on the window and another on the editor's own element; pressing Enter in the case's eighty-paragraph fixture parks the page at the end of the document, and the next keystroke animates it back to the caret over about a second. That keystroke is the `/`: the menu opened, the animation's first scroll event shut it again, and the wait for something visible spent its thirty seconds against twenty-one rows sitting at `display: none` — the signature the gate logged, three times. An 8× CDP CPU throttle standing in for a loaded gate machine reproduced it on four runs in five. The case now lets the page come to rest, puts the caret in the middle of the viewport, and waits for the scrolling to stop before it types, so the `/` has no scrolling left to cause: ten runs in ten under the same throttle, and the file green ten times running unthrottled. Two sleeps became conditions alongside it — the menu is measured once the clamp that caps it has landed, and the page is read after the wheel when scrolling stops rather than 400 ms later — and a new assertion refuses to let a wheel that missed the menu pass for one that hit it. The wheel contract itself is word for word what it was, and no product code changed.
- **A range sorts by its start, then by its end** (Issue #287): Issue #279 undressed the two types whose painted form does not order the way the value does, and left `daterange` dressed — its raw value is an object, and ordering it needed a product call nobody had made. So a `Window` column sorted on `"Oct 1 – Oct 3, 2026"` against `"Sep 9 – Sep 12, 2026"` and put October first, because `O` beats `S`. The rule is the one a calendar keeps: a range sorts by its start, and two spans that open on the same day are broken by their ends, so the shorter one stacks first. `weaveDateGrain.rangeKey` builds that key — the stored ends joined in order, which compare as text within a grain the way a single date already does — and both comparators read it: the engine's `#pathValue` under `undressed` (so `weave query --sort`, `POST /api/tables/:ref/query` and `weave_query` all move together) and `public/app.js` for the grids that hold every row. An open end is refused at the door and only `importJSON` can write one, so `rangeKey` sorts it after a closed range that opens on the same day — an open range extends furthest. Handbook: the `daterange` guide's Gotchas. Gates: `test/sort-values.test.mjs` (+3 — start-then-end with a tie on the start, a range of clock times, the refusal plus the imported open end), `test/sort-values-browser.test.mjs` (+2 — the server's sort and the grid's own, on the same table).

Wrong data: a text→formula type change saves an expression nothing validated

## v0.4.21 — 2026-09-15

Landed as ce0d0c7. Fixed:

- [[Issue#270]] Opening a table no longer reads its trash (Gerrit 350)
- [[Issue#284]] Automation changes land in the audit log (Gerrit 351)
- [[Issue#288]] A type change into a formula checks the expression (Gerrit 352)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **A type change into a formula checks the expression** (Issue #288): `addField` and `updateField` both ran `checkExpression` before storing a formula, but `#migrateFieldType` checked only that an expression was present, so `updateField(t, 'X', { type: 'formula', config: { expression: 'if(upper(' } })` landed and every row read `#ERR: Unexpected end of formula`. The migration branch now runs the same parse and known-field check, with the field's own name off the list, beside the cycle refusal Issue #283 put there; the refusal carries the message `addField` gives and leaves the type alone. `applySchema` used to turn a computed Name into a formula before creating the fields it reads, which the check would now refuse, so both its create-table and existing-table paths apply that type change after the table's other fields. Gates: `test/formula-cycle.test.mjs` (+1: parse error, unknown field, self-reference, then a valid migration), `test/name-field.test.mjs` (+1: a computed Name that reads later fields through the declarative door, fresh and onto an existing table).
- **Automation changes land in the audit log** (Issue #284): `createAutomation`, `updateAutomation` and `deleteAutomation` wrote no audit row, so `weave audit` could not say who added, paused or removed a rule. They now write `automation-created` (table, name, trigger type), `automation-updated` (table, name, the patched keys, the way `field-updated` does) and `automation-deleted` (table, name) through the same audit helper the schema verbs use, with the caller as actor. A delete of an id that does not exist changes nothing and writes nothing; automations on system tables stay out of the log like their fields do. The REST, CLI and MCP surfaces all call these verbs, so every door is covered. No schema change: `audit_log.detail` is free-form JSON. Gate: `test/accounts-audit.test.mjs` (+1).
- **Opening a table no longer reads its trash** (Issue #270): `showDatabase` fetched `GET /api/tables/:id/trash` beside every table query, and for the Case table that list was 1,577 KB, built from a second whole-workspace scan plus a `readEntity` per trashed row, all to print "(N)" beside the eyeball's "Deleted rows" switch. The query now takes `trashCount: true` and answers the table's trash count as a number (the whole table's trash, not the filtered page's), so the open costs one `POST …/query`. The trash list is fetched only when "Deleted rows" puts the trashed rows in the grid. The option reaches `weave_query` on MCP as well as `POST /api/tables/:ref/query`; a query that does not ask keeps its `{ total, items }` shape. Gates: `test/soft-delete.test.mjs` (+2: the count on request, and the REST and MCP opt-in), `test/trash-on-demand-browser.test.mjs` (new: no trash fetch on open, the eye still reads `(1)`, one trash fetch when the deleted rows are shown), `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (the eyeball contract now names the count on the query).

fixes: Slow: every cell commit refetches the whole table and rebuilds the grid
Wrong data: writing a relation logs activity on the near row only, never on the far row
releases.description:
## v0.4.22 — 2026-09-16

Landed as 40872cb. Fixed:

- [[Issue#257]] A cell commit patches its row in place (Gerrit 354)
- [[Issue#286]] A relation write lands in both rows' histories (Gerrit 355)

Also carries the finished half of [[Issue#267]] (tab title + <h1>, Gerrit 356); that Issue stays open on its Back-navigation half, which needs a decision.

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **A cell commit patches its row in place** (Issue #257): committing a cell fired `PATCH /api/entities/:id`, then `GET` of the same row, then `POST …/query` for the whole table, and `drawDatabase` rebuilt the grid with `main.replaceChildren()`, so every commit on the Case table cost the full open again, and even a 30-row table flashed and lost its scroll position. `PATCH /api/entities/:ref` now answers the fresh row plus `affected`: the ids the write marked dirty (a new `Weave#touching` collects them beside `#dirty`, which every save clears) together with the rows the edited one links to, since a lookup or rollup there shows its value. The client's `wvPatchRows` keeps each `<tr>` and its `<td>`s and redraws only the cells whose value moved. The cell is the focus stop (Feature #134), so a cell that is not repainted cannot lose focus, and scroll, selection, range and any open editor all survive. The follow-up `GET` is gone. The client still does a full re-read for a registry row, an edit to the sorted or filtered column, a bulk write or undo, and any response without `affected`. The response body is still `readEntity`, so older clients, the CLI and MCP see no change. On live `:4400`, one Name commit with Tab on Development/Issue (277 rows) fires one `PATCH` and nothing else, in 334 ms, and rows drawn, `scrollTop` and focus all hold. Gates: `test/cell-commit-patch.test.mjs` (new, the server contract), `test/cell-commit-patch-browser.test.mjs` (new, the DOM half); nine cases in `grid-keymap-browser`, `grid-tab-focus-browser` and `toggle-browser` now wait on the write coming back rather than on a replaced `<tbody>`.
- **The tab title names the place, and the table title is an `<h1>`** (Issue #267, part): `document.title` read "Weave" on every page, so tabs, history entries and bookmarks all looked alike. A new `weaveBreadcrumbs.docTitle` builds `<row or table> · <workspace>`: a table or space page reads its name, a docked row or the entity page reads the row, the workspace page reads the workspace name alone, and "Weave" is left only where no workspace has loaded. Closing the dock gives the tab back to the table, and a rename retitles it. The editable title input now sits inside an `<h1 class="view-title-h">` that resets the element's own margin and type, so the header measures the same in both themes (19px/700, identical box). Not in this change: Back walking docked rows. The dock pushes no history entry by the rulings on Issues #198, #226 and #276, and changing that needs a routing decision. Gates: `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` (+1), `test/doc-title-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases).
- **A relation write lands in both rows' histories** (Issue #286): `#setRelationValue` updated both sides of a paired relation but logged `relation-updated` only on the row the caller touched, so a project whose Tasks list gained or lost a row showed nothing in its activity — the field had moved under it with no entry to say so, and the steal case (a single-value inverse moving to a new holder) left the losing row silent too. Each far row now gets its own entry in the same write, naming its own field and the row on the other end, tagged `inverse: true` so a reader can tell the write a row made from the write it received; Fibery shows the link on both feeds the same way. Every door that moves a relation is covered, because they all go through this one path: `link`, `unlink`, `updateEntity`, `createEntity`, a hard delete's unlink, and an undo stepping any of them back. A one-way target-set relation is unchanged — the target has no inverse field to name, so nothing is logged there. Gate: `test/relation-activity.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases).

## v0.4.23 — 2026-09-17

Landed as fdad622. Fixed:

- [[Issue#280]] Search keeps the hierarchy and finds saved views (Gerrit 358)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **Search keeps the hierarchy and finds saved views** (Issue #280): `universalSearch` sorted workspace, space, table and row hits together and then sliced to `limit`, and a row can score up to 20 against 8–9 for a container, so `GET /w/weave/api/search?q=weave&all=1&limit=200` returned 200 rows and no workspace, and `q=issue&limit=40` never returned the Issue table. `limit` now bounds entity rows only: a shared `Weave.capRows` keeps every matching workspace, space, table and view, caps rows, and orders in three tiers: an exact id hit first (Issue #113), then the containers, then text-matched rows. The scoped route, the cross-workspace merge (`all=1`) and `weave_search` on MCP all go through it. Saved views are searched by name (kind `view`, url `#/view/<id>`), and a ⌘K pick on one opens the view. Gates: `test/search-hierarchy.test.mjs` (new, 4 cases: engine, id-hit ranking, scoped and cross-workspace routes), `test/search-view-browser.test.mjs` (new: the palette labels and opens a view).

fixes: Error: about half of fetch failures are swallowed; a failed ⌘K search leaves stale results with no signal
Slow: window resize is undebounced and every filter-chip click refetches the whole table
Wrong data: the entity activity log silently truncates at 500 entries
Wrong data: an open tab keeps a stale schema after a field-config change made elsewhere until a hard reload
Looks broken: the workspace page titles the tab with the workspace name twice
releases.description:
## v0.4.24 — 2026-09-17

Landed as 2fea3bc. Fixed:

- [[Issue#265]] A failed request says so (Gerrit 362)
- [[Issue#269]] A burst of filter-chip clicks is one query; a window drag reschedules the outline once per frame (Gerrit 363)
- [[Issue#281]] A capped activity log says it is capped (Gerrit 364)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **A capped activity log says it is capped** (Issue #281): an entity keeps its newest 500 activity entries, and older ones were dropped with nothing to say so, so a busy entity's history read as complete. The workspace audit log (Feature #14, `audit_log`) never held entity activity: `#audit` records structural actions only (tables, views, keys, accounts, schema applies), so it keeps none of the dropped entries. Each trim now adds the number it dropped to `activityDropped` on the entity (stored in the entity's JSON row, no migration). The entity read carries it through the route, CLI (`weave get`) and MCP (`weave_get_entity`); the activity feed adds `dropped` for its scope (`GET /api/activity`, `weave activity`, `weave_activity`). The entity's Activity pane shows one line, "N older entries not kept", and the Activity table note repeats it. The cap stays 500 (`ACTIVITY_CAP`). Entities trimmed before this change have no recoverable count and read 0: an entity holding exactly 500 entries may never have lost one, so a length-based marker would guess. Not in this change: keeping every entry and paging at read time, which changes stored size and needs a decision. Gates: `test/activity-cap.test.mjs` (new, 4 cases: the count and its accumulation, the feed's scoped sum, legacy entities read 0, route/CLI/MCP parity), `test/activity-cap-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases: the pane line in both themes and absent under the cap, the table note).
- **A burst of filter-chip clicks is one query; a window drag reschedules the outline once per frame** (Issue #269): each filter-chip click PATCHed the table, re-read the schema and re-queried the grid on its own, and read the selection the strip was drawn with, so a second quick click overwrote the first and three clicks cost three round-trips. The strip now keeps its own copy of the selection, a click paints its chip at once, and one PATCH and one re-query run 250 ms after the clicks pause; flushes chain, so a click during a re-read queues one more instead of racing it. A reader who leaves the table inside the pause keeps the saved filter and is not pulled back to the grid. Not in this change: filtering already-loaded rows client-side. The grid reads its rows through the engine's where-language by contract (Feature #38), and a narrowed grid has no copy of the rows a widened filter needs, so that half needs a decision. The window `resize` listener rescheduled every document rail on every event; it now does one pass per animation frame. Gates: `test/filter-strip-browser.test.mjs` (new, 2 cases: four clicks in one task paint at once, land as one PATCH and one query, keep every chip, and show the rows `Weave#query` returns for the selection; a click just before leaving the table is saved without pulling the reader back to the grid), `test/doc-rail-browser.test.mjs` (+1: thirty resize events schedule no rail work inside the burst and one per rail after the frame).
- **A failed request says so** (Issue #265): the ⌘K palette ran its search inside a `setTimeout` with no `try`, so a failed search was an unhandled rejection and the palette kept the previous query's results, and with no cancellation a slow earlier answer could land after a newer one and overwrite it. The palette now paints a "Couldn't search: <reason>" row under its input and aborts the previous keystroke's request (`api()` takes an optional `{ signal }`). The workspace registry no longer empties the rail silently: a failed root-schema fetch or a non-2xx answer toasts, while a 401/403 still reads as "no registry to show". The inline `#` search toasts once per run of failures instead of never, and a record or view that fails to open toasts before falling back to the workspace home. Every other bare `catch` in `public/app.js` now carries a one-line comment naming why silence is right (local parsing, storage, decoration fetches). Gate: `test/fetch-failures-browser.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: a source rule over every bare catch, the registry, # search, showEntity/showView and `api()` signal checks, and two browser cases, one for the failed search row and one for the stale response dropped).
- **An open tab notices a schema change made anywhere else** (Issue #274): `state.schema` was fetched once at boot and refreshed only on the tab's own structural edits or on window refocus (Feature #33), so a Severity field recoloured by the CLI, an agent over MCP, an automation or a second tab kept rendering `hue-slate` through every hash navigation until someone hit reload. Rows refetch on every navigation, so the grid drew fresh values against field definitions the tab had held for hours: a renamed field kept its old header, a new option rendered as an uncoloured chip. The structure now carries a version. `Weave#schemaVersion()` fingerprints the structural rows (meta, spaces, tables, automations) with `publicIdCounter` dropped, since a row insert is not a schema change; it is derived rather than stored, so the CLI and the server compute the same string with nothing to bump or coordinate, and it is memoised behind every save and reload at about 0.4ms on the largest workspace here. Every API response stamps it as `X-Weave-Schema-Version`, and `GET /api/workspace` carries it in the body for callers that read no headers. In the client, a read stamped with a version the tab has not loaded (a GET, or the row query every navigation makes) refetches the schema and redraws, through the same `syncSchema` the focus listener now calls. A write does not: the tab caused it, and the path that made it already refreshes what it needs, so a column resize still commits without a repaint (Issue #160). Four navigations with an unchanged schema cost zero extra round-trips. Route renders are chained while this lands, one at a time in the order they were asked for: the render that discovers the drift is the one making the query, so without an order it can finish last and win the page back for the schema it was drawing from. Gates: `test/schema-version.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases: the fingerprint holds across row writes and moves on a field config, a table rename, a new column and a new space; the header and the workspace body), `test/schema-stale-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases: the repro as filed, a column added elsewhere, and the no-extra-round-trip guard).
- **The workspace page titles the tab once, not twice** (Issue #298): `document.title` on a workspace home read `Weave Workspace · Weave Workspace`, because `showHome` sets the page name to the workspace's own name and `docTitle` then joins it to the workspace name again. Its contract said the opposite since Issue #267 (`public/breadcrumbs.js`: "The workspace page is the workspace name alone"), and `test/doc-title-browser.test.mjs` only ever saw the right title because it polls for five seconds and caught the moment between `syncDocTitle(null)` and the header's repaint. `docTitle` now collapses the pair when the page name is the workspace name, so the assertion lands on a resting state. Found while chaining route renders for Issue #274. Gate: `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` (+1).

releases.name: v0.4.25
fixes: Slow: no gzip or ETag, 23 render-blocking scripts, 2.1 MB cold load, schema fetched 2–3× per route
releases.description:
## v0.4.25 — 2026-09-18

Landed as 2cabe6d. Fixed:

- [[Issue#258]] Statics and JSON go out gzipped, statics carry an ETag, and a route reads the schema once (Gerrit 366)

Everything this release carries, from CHANGELOG.md.

- **Statics and JSON go out gzipped, statics carry an ETag, and a route reads the schema once** (Issue #258): nothing the Node server sent was compressed, whatever the browser said it could inflate, so a cold load of `/` moved 2,187,417 bytes over 46 resources. The Node adapter (`src/server.js`) now gzips text-shaped answers of 1 KB or more (`text/*`, JSON, JavaScript, XML, SVG) when `Accept-Encoding` allows gzip (`acceptsGzip` follows RFC 9110: gzip's own q wins over `*`, q=0 refuses), with `Vary: Accept-Encoding`; images and tiny answers are left alone, a static's gzip is cached by path and validator, and the Worker adapter is untouched because Cloudflare compresses at its edge. Measured against a copy of the live data: `app.js` 533,704 → 170,981 bytes, `/api/schema` 98,125 → 19,234, `tabler.min.css` 536,141 → 68,867, `style.css` 164,576 → 42,096; a cold load of `/` 2,187,417 → 505,208 bytes. Statics also carry a weak `ETag` (size and mtime; weak so one validator covers both encodings) and answer `If-None-Match` with 304, ahead of the existing `If-Modified-Since` (Feature #148). In the client, the home page's relation map, every space page and `#/map` fetched `/api/schema` again although the tab already held it and Issue #274 keeps that copy current; they now read `state.schema` and fetch only `/automations`. `loadSchema` starts its own schema, the root registry (`readRegistry`, member workspaces) and `/workspace` together instead of one after another, and the home page asks for `/workspace` and `/workspaces` together. Schema reads: a cold load of `/` 2 → 1, a space page 1 → 0, `#/map` 1 → 0; a member workspace's cold load 3 → 2 (its own and the root registry's). Not in this change: content-hashed asset URLs with immutable caching, and deferring or concatenating the 23 boot scripts, which change the asset pipeline and load order (split into their own Issue). Gates: `test/compression.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: app.js gzipped and byte-identical once inflated, identity without the header and on q=0, the schema gzipped with its route headers intact, PNG and tiny answers left alone, ETag and If-None-Match 304 in both encodings, the Accept-Encoding parser, the gzip cache keyed by path), `test/schema-fetch-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases: one schema read on boot with the map drawn, none on a space page or `#/map`, a member's three boot reads in flight together), `test/fetch-failures-browser.test.mjs` (the registry case follows the read into `readRegistry`).

releases.name: v0.4.26
fixes: Wrong data: activity entries carry a wall-clock time and no sequence number, so equal timestamps have no order
releases.description:
## v0.4.26 — 2026-09-20

Landed as 38ab0eb. Fixed:

- [[Issue#282]] Wrong data: activity entries carry a wall-clock time and no sequence number, so equal timestamps have no order (Gerrit 370, 371)

- **Activity entries carry a commit counter, and the feed orders by it** (Issue #282): an activity entry recorded only a wall-clock `ts`, so two writes inside one millisecond had no defined order, and a clock that stepped backwards reordered history. The feed's id tie-break was wrong in both directions: across entities it ranked same-millisecond events by entity uuid, which is arbitrary, and within one entity it compared the index as a string, so `:9` read as newer than `:10`. The live weave workspace holds 6,681 entries that share a timestamp with another, and the Documents record's feed rendered 12, 11, 9, 10, 8. Every entry now carries `seq`, a monotonic counter over the workspace kept on `meta.activitySeq` and minted at the single stamping site: `seq` is the order, `ts` stays the display, and the feed, the route, the CLI and MCP all sort on it descending. `deleteEntity` and `restoreEntity` pushed straight onto `e.activity` and bypassed that site; both route through it now, which also gives them an actor they never had and the `ACTIVITY_CAP` trim they skipped. A folded document session keeps the seq it started with, since it is one event. `activitySeq` is excluded from the schema fingerprint for the same reason `publicIdCounter` is: a row write must not cost every open tab a schema refetch (Issue #274). Every open numbers whatever it finds unnumbered and never moves a number already handed out, because a CLI and a server can share one `.db`, and a write from one of them landed unnumbered inside the hour this shipped. Verified on a copy of the live `weave.db`: the numbering pass covered 10,531 entries and exactly two rows moved, the `:9` and `:10` pair the defect predicts. Gates: `test/activity-seq.test.mjs` (new, 9 cases: the counter and its uniqueness, the feed's order against adversarial uuids, `:10` over `:9`, a clock stepping backwards, deleted and restored stamping, the fold keeping its seq, the numbering pass and its idempotence, the schema fingerprint, and route, CLI and MCP parity across a `.db` reopen), `test/activity-seq-browser.test.mjs` (new, 1 case: the Activity table reads newest first in both themes).

releases.name: v0.4.27
fixes: Slow: 24 render-blocking scripts and no immutable asset caching, so every warm load revalidates 32 assets
releases.description:
## v0.4.27 — 2026-09-21

Landed as a893892. Fixed:

- [[Issue#313]] Slow: 24 render-blocking scripts and no immutable asset caching, so every warm load revalidates 32 assets (Gerrit 373)

- **A warm load fetches none of the shell's assets, and no boot script blocks the parser** (Issue #313): every static went out `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so a warm load of `/` on :4400 revalidated 31 static assets over the wire (24 answered 304), behind 24 classic scripts that each blocked parsing in turn. weave has no build step, so the Node adapter (`src/server.js`) now versions the shell when it serves it: `createAssetVersions` rewrites every local `src`, `href` and module `import` in `index.html` that names a file to `?v=<first 12 hex of its sha1>` (cached per file until its mtime or size moves), and an asset asked for at its current version is sent `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. An unversioned or stale-versioned ask keeps `no-cache`. The shell stays `no-cache`, and its ETag is now a hash of the bytes served, with no `Last-Modified`, because an asset can change under an unchanged `index.html` and a 304 on the file's mtime would keep the old URLs. All 24 classic boot scripts carry `defer`; deferred scripts and the inline lean-qr module run in document order once the DOM is parsed, so `window.leanQR` now exists before `app.js` runs instead of after. Not in this change: concatenating the `*-core.js` modules. The Cloudflare Worker (Issue #231) is unchanged and stays correct: its Assets binding serves `public/index.html` as written, with plain URLs and the platform's own revalidation, so `public/index.html` must keep plain URLs (a test pins it). Measured on a scratch server over a copy of the live data, warm load of `/`: static assets on the wire 31 → 0, bytes 9,902 → 0, parser-blocking scripts 24 → 0, page errors 0 in both themes, document editor boots as before. Gates: `test/asset-cache.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases: every served shell asset carries its content hash, immutable only at the current hash, the shell's ETag follows its bytes and ignores If-Modified-Since, versions follow a content change and skip missing files and page links, every classic script deferred with plain URLs on disk), `test/asset-cache-browser.test.mjs` (new, 2 cases: the deferred boot renders with every boot global in place and no page error; a warm load sends only the document to the server), `test/bug-report.test.mjs`, `test/chip-system.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (script-tag pins follow `defer`).

## v0.4.28 — 2026-09-22

Landed as 8f6dd53. Fixed:

- [[Issue#336]] Looks broken: fluttering when hovering over icons maybe with long names, changes popover width for s (Gerrit 376)

- **The icon grid keeps one width while the readout names what the pointer is on** (Issue #336): the picker popover was shrink-to-fit, and its widest content is the name readout Issue #142 put in the search bar. Hovering a long label (`tick · done · complete`) widened the box from 292px to 345px, the `auto-fill` grid reflowed into the new width, the cell slid 12px out from under the pointer, the leave event reset the readout to the shorter resting name, the box snapped back, and the pointer was over the cell again: a flutter that shook the grid for as long as the cursor rested there. `.picker-pop:has(.picker-cells)` now declares `width: 292px` instead of `min-width: 292px`, which also gives the `max-width: 50%` on `.picker-name` a definite box to measure against, so a long name ellipsises inside the row instead of pushing the row wider (a percentage max-width against an indefinite containing block never constrained intrinsic sizing, which is why the existing cap did not hold). The row-term picker carries no readout and opts back out with `width: auto`, so it still sizes to its widest row. Verified on a copy of the live data in both themes: width 292px at rest and 292px under the longest label in the vocabulary, cell movement 0px, against 292px and 345px with a 12px shift before. Gate: `test/icon-vocabulary-browser.test.mjs` (1 new case: popover width and the hovered cell position are identical at rest and while the longest label is read out, and the readout stays inside the box).

Looks broken: clicking new breaks scroll, on clicking new the protected new row should be come an en
releases.description:
## v0.4.29 — 2026-09-23

Landed as 0be87e5. Fixed:

- [[Issue#317]] Looks broken: bouncing scroll when hitting the bottom of a table (Gerrit 378)
- [[Issue#324]] Looks broken: clicking new breaks scroll, on clicking new the protected new row should be come an entry with cursor dropped in name field (Gerrit 379)

- **The last row of a table holds still, and + New lands the caret there** (Issue #324): Kyle filed two complaints about one gesture, clicking "+ New record" at the foot of the Issue grid: "clicking new breaks scroll", and the new row should become an entry with the cursor in its Name field. One mechanism sat under both. A grid draws the rows in view and stands two spacers in for the rest, sized at ONE measured row height, and that height was re-read from whichever row happened to head the window, on every pass. weave's rows are not all the same height (the live Issue grid measures 46.5, 47 and 48), and the spacer above a window 250 rows down stands in for 250 of them, so a pixel of row-to-row variance became hundreds of pixels of page height. At the last row, where the scroll is already at its maximum, the box clamped to the new height, the clamp resized the wrap, and the `ResizeObserver` watching the wrap measured again: a three-position cycle roughly thirty times a second with no hand on the wheel. The report's own replay log carries the other half of that signature, 60 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors in the 1.9 seconds before Kyle hit Report. The + New button under it never held still long enough to be clicked, which is why the row it makes never took the caret. The height is now measured once per table, density and width and then kept (`win.rowHAt` names what was measured), so a density flip or a resize measures again and a scroll never does. Measured on a copy of the live `weave.db` at the reporter's 2187x1359 viewport, in both themes, standing at the last row of the Issue table: self-scrolls over two idle seconds 60 to 0, positions in the cycle 3 to 1, and a + New click that Playwright abandoned after six seconds of an unstable button now lands with the caret in the new row's Name cell. Not in this change: a row born outside the table's active filter is nowhere in the grid's order, so + New on a filtered table still makes a row the reader cannot see, which is Issue #341 and Kyle's call to settle; and a density flip sending the reader back to the top of the table, which is Issue #342. Gates: `test/grid-bottom-bounce-browser.test.mjs` (3 new cases: the last row of a page-scrolled 600-row grid with uneven rows fires no scroll of its own over two idle seconds; + New there lands the caret in the Name cell and leaves the page still; a density flip re-measures, so the spacer stands in at the compact row's own height).

- **The bottom of a table holds still** (Issue #317): Kyle hit the end of the Issue grid in Safari and the box bounced, once per wheel notch, for as long as he kept pushing. A grid's rows are not all the same height (the live Issue grid measures 46.5, 47, 48 and 50px), the spacers that stand in for the rows not drawn are sized at ONE measured height, and the window paints a double buffer behind the direction of travel. At the last row the leading edge is pinned, so a direction flip moves only the trailing edge: a buffer of rows swapped with a spacer that did not weigh the same, the content height moved 189px, the box clamped its own scroll to the new bottom, and that 27px clamp read as backwards travel, which flipped the direction again. The direction now comes from `WeaveGridWindow.travelFor`, which holds the direction and its anchor until the reader has travelled a whole row, so a correction the box makes for itself is not a gesture and a slow scroll still accumulates to a flip. Measured on a copy of the live `weave.db` in both themes, twelve notches at the last row: backwards jumps 12 → 0, content heights 11,377/11,566px → one, scroll positions 10,809/10,782 → one, resting on the last row. Not in this change: sizing the spacers from the real heights of the rows they stand in for, which is a row-height index and its own decision. Gates: `test/grid-bottom-bounce-browser.test.mjs` (new, 1 case: pushing past the last row of an 800-row grid with uneven rows travels backwards zero times and rests on the last row), `test/grid-window.test.mjs` (1 new case: a sub-row correction holds the direction and its anchor, a row of travel either way flips it, an unmeasured row height falls back to the density's own).

releases.description:
## v0.4.30 — 2026-09-23

Landed as 2a473f0. Fixed:

- [[Issue#346]] Looks broken: hovering a clipped cell covers the value, so click-to-edit happens under the popover (Gerrit 381)

- **A clipped cell's expansion opens above it, never over the value** (Issue #346, superseding Kyle's #327): hovering a clipped cell for 180 ms drew a copy of its value in `.cell-pop-layer`, pinned so the copied text sat exactly on the live text (the 2026-08-26 over-the-value rule from Issue #93). The copy is `pointer-events: none`, so a click still reached the cell, but the inline editor, the caret and every typed character then sat under a static copy of the old value. Kyle, 2026-09-23: "it blocks click and edit, should show above the row/cell instead". `showCellPop()` now keeps the copy's content on the cell's content left edge and sets its bottom edge 4 px (`CELL_POP_GAP`) above the cell's top. When the room above inside the wrap's visible area, or the viewport, is shorter than the pop, it flips to 4 px below the row, so the first rows of a table still get an expansion instead of one clipped off the top. A `mousedown` (capture) or `focusin` anywhere in the grid takes the expansion down, and a cell whose own control holds focus opens none, so editing never runs under a copy. Kept from earlier fixes: min-width at the cell's width and the 380 px measure, the cell's typography on the copy (Issues #67, #93), the input-to-text swap that lets a long name wrap (Issue #157), the 180 ms rest delay, no column movement, and Esc through `DOCK_ESC_OWNERS`. Gates: `test/cell-pop-above-browser.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases: a clipped Name six rows down opens above its cell within 8 px, on the value's left edge, between cell width and 380 px, in both themes; the first row's pop opens below the row and inside the grid; a real mousedown takes the pop down and a pointer resting on the cell being edited opens none; focus moving into another cell hides it), `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` (the over-the-value case rewritten: left edge kept, the copy never overlaps its cell).

## v0.4.31 — 2026-09-23

Landed as a8e56cf. Ships:

- [[Feature#228]] Table search: a search box in the table toolbar that filters the grid to matching rows, same matcher as ⌘K

- **Table search in the toolbar** (Feature #228): Kyle, 2026-09-23, asked for a search box on the table page that searches only the current table and hides every row that does not match. A magnifier now sits first in the table's toolbar, left of the eye. Click it, or press `/` or `⌘F` on a resting cell, and it opens into a box that narrows the grid as you type (150 ms pause, the palette's). It runs the ⌘K matcher, scoped to the table: a name fragment, a `#143` id, or the words in a text field, a document or a comment. `Weave#search` gained a `table` scope and the table query a `search` parameter, both over one private matcher, so the palette and the box cannot drift apart; the matcher now also reads text, url and email values (a `key` stays out), which the palette gains too. The search runs on the server, so a paged table narrows across every page, in the table's own sort, inside its saved filter, and the foot reads `3 records found`. It is transient view state: in memory, one table at a time, never written to the Tables row, so nobody else's view moves. `Esc` clears and folds the box; `Return` on a single match opens that row in the dock; a miss reads "No records match" with **Clear search**; `+ New` clears the search first, since an empty new row matches nothing (the search's half of Issue #341). The route, `weave_query` (MCP) and `weave query --search` (CLI) all take the parameter. Not in this change: highlighting the matched text inside the cells. Gates: `test/table-search.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: the scope, text-field matches in both entry points, composition with where, sort and paging totals, `#id` and bare id, empty and missed searches, the trash, route and MCP parity), `test/table-search-browser.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases on a 503-row paged table in Chromium and WebKit: typing narrows every page with no PATCH; a text-field value and a `#id` match; `Return` docks a single match; a miss and its clear; `Esc`; `/` and `⌘F` from a resting cell open the box without opening the cell; the saved filter composes and survives; `+ New` during a search shows the new row).

releases.description:
## v0.4.32 — 2026-09-23

Landed as aa8f1f2 (Gerrit change 383). Ships:

- [[Feature#230]] Number display: bar, ring and heat costumes

- **Number display: bar, ring and heat** (Feature #230): Kyle, 2026-09-23, asked for in-cell graphics on number fields, like Excel's, so a progress or score column reads at a glance. The number costume gains `display` (`text` by default, or `bar`, `ring`, `heat`) and `scale` (`column` by default, or a fixed number above 0). A bar and a ring fill to the value's share of the scale; heat tints the cell by it. The value's text rides beside the graphic and is what a screen reader reads (`aria-label="60%"`); the SVG is aria-hidden. The column scale is the column's max, computed through `src/stats.js`, so it equals a Space-level `via` max rollup over the same column. Every read now carries `scales` (field name to its 100% mark) for its graphic columns, so a paged grid, a chip and a card draw against the whole column rather than the rows they hold; the engine caches each max and drops the cache on every write and reload. The API still returns the raw number in `raw` and the dressed text in `fields`. A numeric formula takes the same keys, and a rollup over a graphic column wears that column's display the way it already wore its format (a count wears none). Grid cells, chip segments and card fields draw the graphic; a graphic cell is never marked `clipped`; a click hands over the raw number, as a dressed number already did. The field dialog gains a Display picker, a Scale control (column max or fixed) and three sample rows that redraw as you choose. Going back to text drops a stored fixed scale: `updateField` now clears any costume key the canonical form no longer carries. Stars stay out of this costume, since a rating is its own type (Feature #231). Not in this change: doc mentions rendered server-side keep the text only. Gates: `test/number-display.test.mjs` (new, 9 cases: keys and validation, raw versus dressed, column and fixed scales, the scale following writes and the trash, formula, rollup, chip meter, parity with the `via` max rollup), `test/cell-graphics.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases: share clamping, bar, ring and heat geometry, hover text, the engine's list, the page loading the module), `test/number-display-browser.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: the three displays against fixed and column scales in both themes, a narrow graphic cell never clipped, click-to-edit and redraw, rollup and chip meters, the dialog's picker and sample rows in both themes), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (4 new cases), `test/vocabulary.test.mjs` (the display list held to the engine and the dialog).

## v0.4.35 — 2026-09-23

Landed as e45dd2d (Gerrit change 385). Ships:

- [[Feature#229]] Table views: a strip of views per table, a default, and Blank

Fixes:

- [[Issue#341]] + New on a filtered table makes a row the grid cannot show

- **Table views** (Feature #229): Kyle, 2026-09-23, asked for several named views per table, as Attio and Airtable show them, and ruled on the shape the same day. A strip of tabs now sits under the table title. Each view keeps its visible columns in order, its state filter and its sort. The starred view is the default: it sits first and opens with the table. **Blank** closes the strip: the raw table, every field in schema order, no filter, no sort, computed and never stored. A change to the filter, the sort, a column drag or the eye saves into the view on screen, with no Save button. **+** makes a view from Blank; **⋮ → Save as view…** copies the view on screen under a new name; **Make default**, **Rename view…** and **Delete view** sit in the same menu. Blank is read-only and says so. A view's link is `#/table/<table>/view/<view id>`. The agent surface came first and is one verb on every door: `tableView` in the engine, `weave_table_view` over MCP, `weave table view` on the CLI, and `GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/tables/:table/views/:view`. Tables and views are addressed by name (`Issue/Open bugs`, `Issue/blank`). One ordered `fields` list carries visibility and order together; `show`, `hide` and `move: {field, before|after}` edit one field at a time, so a wide table is never resent; `default` and `position` place the view in the strip; `from` copies a view; writes return the compact view, never the table. Filters and sort go through `updateTable`'s own validators, now shared. The MCP surface grew by one tool and 849 bytes (54 tools and 26,263 bytes before, 55 and 27,112 after); `weave_update_table` dropped `hiddenFields` from its schema, and the engine still accepts it. Every view is a row in the new **Workspace/Views** registry table (`Fields`, `Filter`, `Sort`, `Default`, `Position`, related to its Tables row), and a row edit runs the same verb. `describeSchema` emits each table's `views` and `applySchema` round-trips them; an omitted view needs `allowDestructive`. Migration: on first open, each table's filter, sort and hidden set become a starred view named **Default**, in the column order it had, so the grid reads as it did. The Tables row's Hidden Fields, Filter and Sort now mirror the default view, and `updateTable`'s `hiddenFields`, `filters` and `sort` write it. `fieldOrder` stays the schema order (the entity page and Blank). Naming: Feature #17's cross-table pages keep `createView`, `weave_views` and `/api/views` in code; their table menu item is now **New share page…**, so "Save as view" means one thing. Not in this change: per-person views and per-view density (density stays a reading preference in the header). Gates: `test/table-views.test.mjs` (new, 24 cases: compact reads, Blank, one-call definition, relative edits, refusals that write nothing, one validator and one message for filters and sort, partial updates, positioning, rename and delete, the legacy verbs, field add, rename and drop, migration, the schema document, duplicate and export, the registry row, MCP, the tool's size, REST, CLI, the capped writer token), `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases: strip placement, autosave into the view on screen with a permalink reload, Blank read-only, Save as view, + and Make default, the eye per view, Issue #341, both themes), and 15 existing suites moved to read the default view.

- **+ New on a filtered view starts the row inside the filter** (Issue #341): a row made on a filtered grid was born in the workflow's default state, outside the filter, so the grid never showed it. Views make filtered grids common, so this lands with them. The new row now takes the filter's first state when the filter does not already hold the default (a toggle takes its on label when the filter holds only that). Gate: `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs` (+ New on a view filtered to Done makes a Done row the grid draws).

## v0.4.34 — 2026-09-23

Landed as c2ac845 (Gerrit change 384). Ships:

- [[Feature#231]] Rating field type: whole-number icons you click to fill

- **Rating field type** (Feature #231): Kyle, 2026-09-23, asked for a score you set with one click instead of a number field and a scale to remember. `rating` is a new value type: a whole number from 0 to the field's `max`, drawn as `max` icons with the first ones filled. The config is `{ max, icon }`: `max` is 1 to 10 (5 unless named; the field dialog offers 3, 5 and 7 and takes any other), and `icon` is one icon from the inventory, a star unless named, picked with the same icon picker a space or a state uses. Click the nth icon to set n; click the filled current one to clear to 0. On a resting grid cell a digit sets the rating (a digit past the max sets the max) and Backspace or Delete clears it; no text box ever opens. A screen reader hears "3 of 5". A write is rounded and held to 0..max, numeric text included, and anything else is refused by name; lowering `max` holds every row to the new ceiling on read. Formulas, sort, filter, stats, CSV, bulk Set, paste and the API all read a number. `number` converts to `rating` by rounding and clamping, and back to the number it held. A lookup of a rating, and a rollup whose answer stays on the scale (`avg`, `min`, `max`, `median`), draw the same icons read-only, rounded to a whole icon, while the API keeps the unrounded figure; a `sum` or a spread prints as a number. The chip and the card draw the icons too. Added everywhere the types are listed: the vocabulary, the dialog's type grid, the MCP tool descriptions, the Handbook (a rating page, the definable types, the keyboard table), ONTOLOGY, README, the showcase seed and the uno applet. Gates: `test/rating-field.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: registration and defaults, max and icon validation, rounding and clamping, the default, formulas, sort, filter, stats and CSV, number to rating and back, lookup, rollup and chip), `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: icons and "n of max" in both themes, click to set and to clear, digit and Backspace on the resting cell, a rounded read-only rollup, the dialog's presets, icon picker and sample in both themes), `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs`, `test/cell-graphics.test.mjs` and `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (new cases for the keys, the icon count and label, and the form round-trip).

## v0.4.36 — 2026-09-23

Landed as 558550f (Gerrit change 386). Ships:

- [[Feature#232]] Formula arrays and the sparkline display

Fixes:

- [[Issue#358]] Looks broken: a rating on a chip or card prints as a number, not icons

- **Formula lists and the sparkline** (Feature #232): Kyle, 2026-09-23, asked for in-cell trends across related rows, driven by formulas. A formula may now return a list or null; a list comes in through a lookup over a to-many relation, in relation order. The new `sortby(values, keys)` orders it by a parallel list, ascending and stable, blank keys last, so `sortby([Deal amounts], [Deal close dates])` is the amounts in date order. A test proves the precondition first: two lookups over one relation keep their blank slots in position (a row with no amount holds a null in the amounts beside its date), and a trashed row leaves both lists together. That held already; nothing needed fixing. The formula's display costume gains `sparkline` with a `style` of `line` (the default), `column` or `winloss`; a number field refuses it, since a stored number is one value. The grid cell, the chip and the card draw the newest 60 points (a line with a dot on the newest point and gaps at blanks, columns standing on zero with losses in red, or win/loss bars about a midline); the hover lists every value and says when it cut; a screen reader hears "5 values, last 70, low -20, high 70". Sort and filter on a sparkline column read the last number in the series; the API returns the whole list. The formula dialog offers Display (text or sparkline), Style and a sample series once the check names the result a list. `sortby` joins the builder's number chips and the vocabulary (`sparklineStyles`). Also fixed (Issue #358): a rating or a meter on a chip or a card lost its drawing in `view-core.js`, which kept only a segment's label and text; a rating now draws its icons there. Gates: `test/formula-arrays.test.mjs` (new, 6 cases: lookup slot alignment, sortby ordering and errors, list and null results with the API returning numbers, the sparkline costume and its validation, last-value sort and filter, the chip's series), `test/sparkline-browser.test.mjs` (new, 6 cases: the three styles in both themes, the 60-point cap and its hover, the chip, the dialog in both themes), `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` (1 new case: the chip draws the rating's icons), `test/cell-graphics.test.mjs` (4 new cases), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (2 new cases), `test/vocabulary.test.mjs` (the style list held to the engine and the dialog).

fixes: A density flip sends the reader back to the top of the table
Error: row-selection browser case "Set a field… on a number" flakes under the full gate and needs the retry
releases.description:
## v0.4.37 — 2026-09-24

Landed as 45a7f9c (Gerrit change 389). Fixed:

- [[Issue#342]] A density flip sends the reader back to the top of the table (Gerrit 387)
- [[Issue#349]] Error: row-selection browser case "Set a field… on a number" flakes under the full gate and needs the retry (Gerrit 388)

- **A density flip keeps the reader's place** (Issue #342): flipping Comfortable to Compact part way down a long grid put the reader back at row 0. Two things sent them there. The row window is placed from a body-relative offset divided by the row height, so the same offset at a shorter row height is a different row: on a 600-row table at scroll 10,800 the flip drew from row 332 instead of row 209. And the segmented control rebuilt its buttons on every pick, so the button the reader had just clicked left the document, focus fell to `<body>`, and the browser scrolled to the top of the page to show it. The grid now owns the flip (`wrap.wvSetDensity`): it reads the row at the top edge off the DOM before the flip, applies the new density, re-measures, and lands that row back under the sticky header inside the one gesture, so nothing is painted in between. Read off the DOM rather than off the row height because weave's rows are not all the same height (Issue #324) and an estimated anchor was twenty rows out. The control keeps its buttons and moves the `on` mark, which holds focus where the reader put it for every segmented control in the app, the field dialog's included. Gates: `test/grid-density-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases: a wide grid scrolling in its own wrap holds the row across Compact and back to Comfortable, a page-scrolling grid holds it too, and the clicked button keeps focus and the mark).
- **The bulk-write browser cases wait for the paint** (Issue #349): `Set a field… on a number` failed its first run and passed on the retry in three Gerrit gate logs. `runBulk()` clears the selection the moment `POST /api/bulk` answers and repaints the written rows only after the re-read behind it lands, so a case that reads the cells between those two moments loses the race under a loaded gate. A new `holdRepaint()` helper stalls that re-read by 600ms, which turns the gap from a coin flip into a certainty, and the six affected cases in `test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs` now wait for the value they assert instead of reading it off the click. The product is unchanged; the reads were early. Gates: `test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs` (6 cases rewritten, then 5 consecutive raw runs, 3 runs under CPU pressure and 3 alongside the full suite, all 24/24).

releases.description:
## v0.4.38 — 2026-09-25

Landed as 4257a73 (Gerrit change 391). Fixed:

- [[Issue#321]] Looks broken: some times table title and description stays visible onsite Coll sometimes not, should (Gerrit 390)

- **The view header holds at the top of the page** (Issue #321): Kyle, reading a table in Safari, "some times table title and description stays visible ... sometimes not, should always stay visible with breadcrumbs and upper right toolbar". The "sometimes" was which box scrolls. A grid wider than its card takes a vertical scroller of its own (Issue #233), so the page never moves and the header only looked pinned; a grid that fits clips, the page is the scroller, and the header left with it — measured on the Issue table at Kyle's 2187x1359, where a 2500px scroll put the header at -2468. `#main > .view-header` is sticky now, so the breadcrumb, title, description and toolbar read the same in both modes. The 16px under it is padding rather than margin, because rows read straight through a transparent band, and z-index 6 clears every sticky layer the grid has (Issue #252 tops out at 5) while tying with the cell expansion and the field menu, which are later in the document and still open over it. The grid's own field headers and the Σ row start where the header ends: `viewHeader` measures it into `--wv-view-h` on the root, and a `.wv-fit` wrap — the one that clips, so the page is its scroller — adds it to their `top`; every other wrap scrolls itself and keeps its own top edge. The same reading is `scroll-padding-top`, so a focused control, a hash anchor or find-in-page stops below the header, and it feeds the grid's window arithmetic, which read the page's top edge as 0 and put a commit mid-table a header's height out. A header that would take half the window does not pin at all: a 200px window, or a description the reader expanded to thirty lines, would hold nothing but header, and the Show less control at its foot would sit off screen with no way to scroll to it. The docked pane keeps its header in the flow, as before. releases.description:
## v0.4.40 (2026-09-25)

Landed as 0670c68 (Gerrit change 410).

Ships:

- [[Feature#229]] Table views: drag order is the default; the star, the ⋯ button and the Blank tab are gone

- **Drag a view tab to choose the default** (Feature #229, Kyle's rulings of 2026-09-25): "Instead of a star, allow drag to reorder, the first (leftmost) view is the default, then we don't need the 3 dots", and "blank can be removed". The leftmost tab opens with the table, and the order of the strip is the only thing that says so. A tab moves by drag with a mouse (press and move), with a finger (hold still for a moment, then slide, so a quick swipe still scrolls the strip), or with Alt+Left and Alt+Right on a focused tab. Double-click renames a tab in place: Enter or clicking away saves, Escape cancels. Right-click, Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key (or a finger held and let go) opens Rename…, Duplicate view… and a hold-to-delete Delete view. Duplicate view… replaces the old Save as view item. The + button makes a view with every field in schema order, no filter and no sort, which is how you get back to the raw table. An old `…/view/blank` link still opens the raw table, read-only, with no tab lit, and its note now points at + and the tab menu. A table keeps at least one view: deleting the last one is refused with a message, on every door. Agents: position is the single source of the default. `weave_table_view` reads carry no `default` flag, `position: 0` makes a view the default, `default: true` still works as the older spelling of the same move, the strip list no longer ends with a Blank entry, and `Table/blank` still reads the raw table. `applySchema` writes views before it deletes and then places the order, so a document can replace every view and the order round-trips. The tool's schema went from 910 to 888 bytes. Kyle did not say where rename, duplicate and delete should go once the ⋯ menu left; the session chose double-click and the tab's context menu. Gates: `test/table-views.test.mjs` (26 cases: the position alias, the last-view refusal through the verb, MCP, CLI, REST and the Views row, the order round-trip and a replace-every-view document) and `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs` (13 cases: no star, dots or Blank tab in the DOM, a mouse drag and a touch drag that persist and change what the bare route opens, a quick swipe that does not reorder, double-click rename with Escape, the tab menu, hold-to-delete and the last-view refusal, keyboard reorder and Shift+F10, + from a filtered view, and the old blank link), green in Chromium and WebKit.

releases.description:
## v0.4.43 — 2026-09-26

Landed as 689c2b1 (Gerrit change 413). Ships:

- [[Feature#234]] Rating: default max of 5, any quantity, and a clickable default

Fixes:

- [[Issue#396]] Wrong data: a rating default sent with a new max is clamped to the old max

- **Rating: any max, five unless named, and a default you click** (Feature #234): Kyle, 2026-09-25: "for ratings default to 5 but allow the user to put any quantity; also the default rating selection should not be a text box but an interactive rating preview using the selected icon." A rating's max is now any whole number from 1 to 100; it was 1 to 10. A rating made with no max is out of five on every door (the engine, `POST /api/tables/:id/fields`, `weave_add_field` and `weave field add`), and one test now holds all four to it. The guard of 100 stays on purpose: every icon is a button in every visible grid cell, so a max in the thousands would put tens of thousands of nodes in one screen of rows, and a row of more than 100 icons is wider than any screen. The reason sits beside `RATING_MAX` in `src/engine.js`, and the dialog mirrors the number. In the field dialog the max is a whole-number box prefilled with 5, with 3, 5 and 7 as shortcut chips beside it; a number past the guard is marked invalid and never saved. The default is no longer a text box. It is a row of `max` icons in the chosen icon, drawn by the same `ratingEl` the grid cell uses: click the nth icon to set the default to n, and click it again to clear it. With the row focused, the arrow keys move it by one, a digit sets it (a digit past the max sets the max, 0 clears), End sets the max, and Home, Backspace or Delete clear it. A screen reader hears "Default: 3 of 5". The row redraws when the icon or the max changes, and a default above a lowered max comes down with it. The Showcase gains Brightness, a 12-point sun rating with a default of 6, through the existing `SHOWCASE_ADDITIONS` sync. Gates: `test/rating-field.test.mjs` (3 new cases: any max up to the guard with a value of 17 stored, out of five on all four doors, a default sent with a new max and clamped by a lowered one), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (4 new cases: the guard mirrored from the engine and the typed box, click and label, the keys, the clamp in the state and the definition), `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` (2 new cases, one per theme: a 12-icon preview, click to set and to clear, the keys with focus held, a clamp on a lowered max, an icon change, then a row made with + New starting at the default and drawn in the grid), `test/seed.test.mjs` (1 new case: Brightness and a new row at its default).
- **A rating default sent with a new max kept the old max** (Issue #396): `updateField` read the `default` lane before the rating's `max` lane, and the field dialog sends both in one save, so raising a 5-point rating to 12 with a default of 11 stored a default of 5. The rating lane now runs first, and lowering the max clamps a standing default in the config as well as on every row. Gate: `test/rating-field.test.mjs` ("a default rides with the max").
