releases.description:
## v0.4.42 (2026-09-26)

Ships:

- [[Feature#233]] Field resize, reorder and freeze: labels never clip, widths stay put, drop across the seam to freeze

Fixes:

- [[Issue#399]] Looks broken: a dragged column snaps back to its old place on the next sort, and rows scrolled in later draw the old cell order

- **Columns keep their widths** (Feature #233, Kyle's mockup review of 2026-09-25). Every field type opens at a default width: Name 220px, text, links and multi-selects 180, long text 280, selects 124, relations 136, dates 112, numbers 88, currency 104, checkboxes 56. A header label never clips: a longer label widens its own column, and no drag, keyboard nudge or fit goes under it. A date column also opens wide enough for its format's longest date. Showing, hiding, adding or removing a field leaves every other width alone; the space at the right of the grid takes up the difference. A hidden field comes back at its own width and in its own place.
- **Resize** moves only the column you drag. The columns to its right slide over, and a readout shows the field, its width and the change. Double-click the edge to fit the longest value, up to the type's maximum. Alt+Left and Alt+Right on a focused header resize by 8px.
- **Reorder** by dragging a header: a ghost follows the pointer, one line marks where the column lands, and the moved columns slide into place. Near the edges of a wide grid it scrolls. Alt+Shift+Left and Alt+Shift+Right move a focused header one place.
- **Freeze** a field by dropping it across the seam beside #, and unfreeze it by dropping it back. The line reads "Freeze here" or "Unfreeze" when a drop changes the frozen zone. Frozen fields stay put while the grid scrolls sideways, up to 60% of its visible width.
- Widths, order and the frozen count belong to the view. Agents set them with `weave_table_view` (`widths`, `frozen`), the CLI with `--widths` and `--frozen`, and the Workspace/Views row carries Frozen and Widths.
- Fixed: a dragged column snapped back to its old place on the next sort, and rows scrolled into view later showed the old cell order (Issue #399).

releases.description:
**Correction, 2026-10-03 (Issue #565).** Version 0.4.46 never shipped. package.json went from 0.4.45 to 0.4.50, and no v0.4.46 tag, GitHub Release or CHANGELOG.md section exists. The notes below describe work that landed later, and two of their claims held on no build until then. The 10-icon rating width shipped in v0.4.53 (Issue #404, commit aadc9a4). The compact `★ 7/10` form shipped in v0.4.62 (Feature #235, commit f244163); since v0.4.63 (Issue #614) a drag stops at the last icon, so only a rating whose icons pass the 320px fit cap draws the compact form. This row no longer lists Issue #404 under Fixes or Feature #235 under Ships: #404 points at v0.4.53 and #235 at v0.4.62.

---

**Rich cells: a colour setting, redrawn cells and fitted column widths** (Feature #235, and Issue #404): Kyle, 2026-09-25, on the bars, rings, heat, ratings and sparklines of Features #230 to #232: "I don't like the design of the columns or the colors." His decision the next day: put colour in the field's config, default to quiet ink, redraw the cells to the A/B/C mockups, and give the columns better widths. A rating, a number's display and a formula's display now take `color`: `ink` (Quiet ink, the default, never written down), `icon` (Color by icon) or `accent` (One accent hue). Quiet ink draws bars and rings in the text colour on a hairline track, heat as a grey tint that deepens with the value, rating icons filled in the text colour with hairline outlines for the empties, and sparklines in the secondary text colour. Color by icon draws bars and rings teal, runs heat from cool to warm with the share, fills a star amber, a heart rose and a bolt violet (any other icon takes the accent), draws the sparkline blue and win/loss green and red. One accent hue draws every graphic in the workspace accent, losses in a lighter accent. Every colour is a token with a dark twin. The engine validates the key on add, update and schema apply, and refuses anything else with the list; the schema says the colour of every field that draws a graphic, ink included; a lookup and a rollup draw in the colour of the column they read, and the chip and the card carry it. The cells are redrawn: a 6px bar with round ends on a fixed 80px track and the figure to its right in tabular figures, a 16px ring with a 2.5px round-capped stroke hugging its percent, heat as a rounded tint behind the figure, 14px rating icons 1px apart, and an 80 by 18 sparkline drawn at its own size with a dot on the newest point, 1.5px column corners and small win/loss blocks either side of a midline. A rich cell no longer repeats the Σ or ƒ its header carries. A rich column opens at the width its graphic needs (a rating's icons, a bar's track plus its widest figure, a ring or a heat tint plus its widest figure, a sparkline's 80px), never under a plain number's 88px; a width a person drags wins. A 10-icon rating opens unclipped (Issue #404), and a rating column dragged narrower than its icons, or past the fit cap, draws a compact `★ 7/10` instead of cutting icons off. The settings tray gains a Color picker beside Display on a rating, a number display and a sparkline: three swatches, each this field's own graphic drawn in that setting, and the Sample and the rating's default row wear the pick. The Showcase's Field Types table gains a column per setting beside the ink ones (Momentum, Reach, Warmth, Stars, Bolts, Hearts, Age line, Delta blocks), through the existing Showcase sync. Gates: `test/cell-color.test.mjs` (new, 9 cases: the list, default and storage, refusal, update and clear, inheritance by a lookup and a rollup, the chip and the card, the schema round trip, the HTTP API, and one list across the engine, the vocabulary, the dialog and the drawing), `test/cell-color-browser.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases: each setting's paints in light and dark, the shapes' sizes, the marks leaving the cells, the 10-icon width and the compact form, the tray's swatches and save in both themes, and the number and sparkline Samples), `test/cell-graphics.test.mjs` (6 new cases), `test/column-layout.test.mjs` (2 new cases), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (4 new cases), `test/seed.test.mjs` (1 new case, colours drawn from `CELL_COLORS`), `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`.

releases.description: **A rollup's settings tray says what it does, and repoints in place** (Issue #387): Kyle, reading Showcase > Field Types > Peer skill, "I don't understand the config for this rollup or formula driven rating; config tray looks wrong." The tray for a rollup held its name, its description and "Computed config is not editable, delete and recreate to repoint it". It never named the relation it crosses, the field it reads, the aggregate it runs, or why the column draws stars. The tray now opens on the **Recipe**, `Peers → Skill → avg`, over three pickers (Relation, Field, Aggregate) that hold it; a **Result** line with the saved result on the first row that has one, drawn the way the cell draws it; and **Shows as**, which names the display the column inherits: "The rating on People › Skill: 5 stars, Quiet ink." with a sample, or "A bar from Deal › Amount, on the column max, One accent hue.", or "A count, in plain figures." A sentence says why the display is not set here (a rollup wears the display and the colour of the field it reads), and a button opens that field's settings. A lookup gets the same Recipe, Result and Shows as, without an aggregate. Saving repoints the column: `updateField` now takes `relationField`, `targetField` and `aggregate` on a lookup and on a relation rollup, through the very validation `addField` runs, so an edit can never make a column a create would refuse; a new relation needs a target field on its own table and says so by name, and an aggregate other than count needs a target field. `weave field update` and `PATCH /api/tables/:id/fields/:id` take the same keys. A space rollup (`via`) shows its recipe read-only and points at the grid's Σ row. A long segment strip in the tray (the twelve aggregates) wraps instead of running off the edge. The Handbook's lookup and rollup pages say all of this. Gates: `test/rollup-recipe.test.mjs` (new, 4 cases: a rollup repointed by aggregate, field and relation with the cell following; a repoint refused exactly where a create would be; a lookup repointed; the HTTP route), `test/rollup-tray-browser.test.mjs` (new, 5 cases: the recipe, the result, the inherited rating and why, in light and dark; the owner button; a save that repoints and redraws the cell; a number rollup's bar and colour, a count, a lookup), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (1 new case: the edit sends the recipe, and none for a space rollup).

- **One checkbox, and a Fields popover that drags and fits** (fixes Issues #441, #384, #445, #446): the grid's row selector, the Fields popover, the Filters popover and the field dialog all draw weave's one checkbox, `input.form-check-input`, so each computes the same 16px box, 4px radius, border and checked fill in both themes; the hand-drawn `.field-visible-check` and its `role="switch"` are gone, and each Fields row, Deleted rows, the Σ rollup row and each filter option is a real, labelled checkbox that Space flips. A field dialog checkbox sits on its label's first line everywhere, not over it, and the Literal hint sets its syntax as code. A Fields row reads `grab` at rest over its name and its grip, never an I-beam; a press that moves drags it (the Views list shares the same drag), the cursor reads `grabbing` wherever the pointer goes until the drop, Escape or a cancelled pointer, no text selects, and one square-ended line marks the gap. The Fields popover grows to the room below its button before its list scrolls, its header stays outside the scroll box, and a scrolled list snaps so no row sits half under the top. Tests: `test/checkbox-parity-browser.test.mjs` and `test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs` (new), `test/table-toolbar-browser.test.mjs`, `test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs`, `test/popover-toggle-browser.test.mjs`, `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs`, `test/table-patch-browser.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.

- **The Views list: handles, row buttons, inline naming, and Standard** (fixes Issue #443): the View dropdown has no right-click, context menu or double-click rename any more. Every view row shows its drag handle; a drag by it, with a mouse or a finger, or Alt+Up / Alt+Down on a focused row reorders the list, with the square-ended insertion line the Fields popover uses. Rename, Duplicate and a hold-to-delete are row buttons that show on hover and on keyboard focus, and Rename edits the name in place. **+ Add view** no longer opens a modal: it appends a row inside the open dropdown with a focused, selected name, the next free `View 2`, `View 3`, …; Enter or a click away creates the view and opens it with the dropdown still open, and Escape drops the row. Duplicate uses the same row under its source, offered as `<name> 2`. The first view's row reads **Opens first**, and the caption moves with whichever view is dragged to the top. The first view is named **Standard**: a new table's is born with the name, and a view still called `Default` is renamed once when its workspace opens (its Workspace/Views row too), unless the table already has a Standard; a view named Default afterwards keeps its name. The View button, the Handbook, AGENTS.md and the `weave_table_view` description say Standard. Tests: `test/view-standard-name.test.mjs` (new), `test/table-views-browser.test.mjs` (rewritten for the list), and the view suites that addressed the first view by name.

- **One system default for Reset view and New view; deleted rows and the Σ row saved per view** (fixes Issue #442): `systemDefault(db)` is the one answer to "a fresh view": every regular field in schema order with the table's default system columns, no filter, sort, search, widths or frozen columns, no deleted rows, no Σ rollup row, Comfortable. Reset view writes it into the view on screen and clears the search; + Add view creates the new view from it, so the two cannot drift. Deleted rows and the Σ row are now the view's, beside filters, fields, sort and density: two view keys, `deleted` (true shows the trashed rows in place) and `rollups` (true draws the Σ row, false hides it, null follows the table's older `hideRollups`, so no grid changes on the upgrade), on `weave_table_view`, `weave table view --deleted on|off --rollups on|off|table`, `/api/tables/:t/views/:v`, the schema document and the Workspace/Views row's new **Show Deleted** and **Rollup Row** columns. The Fields popover's Rows boxes save into the current view, and a switch to another view shows that view's own. Tests: `test/view-rows-state.test.mjs` and `test/view-reset-browser.test.mjs` (new, both themes, Chromium and WebKit), `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs`, `test/sort-values-browser.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.

- **Select filters and an "X of N" count in the Filters popover** (fixes Issues #319, #448): the Filters popover offers single-select and multi-select fields beside workflow and toggle fields, each a group of weave's checkboxes with the option's dot, labelled **Single select** or **Multi select**. Options in one field combine with OR, fields with AND, and a multi-select row matches when it has any chosen option; the choice saves into the current view like any filter, and a new row made on a select-filtered grid starts inside the filter (Issue #341). A view's `filters` now take option names for those fields on every surface (engine, `weave_table_view`, CLI, REST, the Workspace/Views row's Filter text), validated like states. The footer reads "X of N" in the table's plural row term (`7 of 413 bugs`, plural even at 1): X counts the rows left after the filters and the search, N every undeleted row. It is one node, updated in place off the grid's own read and announced with `aria-live="polite"`, dimmed while a change is on its way, with Clear all on its right; the groups scroll under it and the popover grows to the room below its button. The query takes `countAll: true` (`weave_query`, `weave query --count-all`, `POST /api/tables/:t/query`) and answers `all`, the undeleted rows before any where or search. The header's crumb path now ellipsizes before the toolbar drops a row, so a filter badge never moves the grid. Tests: `test/select-filters.test.mjs` and `test/filter-select-browser.test.mjs` (new; both themes, Chromium and WebKit).

- **A hairline grid header, and a "+" that trails the last field** (Feature #240, Kyle 2026-09-27): the header was a grey band with rounded top corners, and the add-field "+" sat in the one column with no width of its own, which took whatever the fields left of the card, so on a small table the grey ran past the last field to the card's edge around a lonely "+". The header now paints the card surface (opaque, so rows never show through it while it is stuck) over one hairline a step stronger than the row rule, and its labels are sentence case, 12px, weight 500, in the secondary ink. A hovered header cell takes the secondary surface, the one sign left that it resizes, reorders and opens a menu. The grid is as wide as its columns, so the "+" sits right after the last field and the slack past it is bare card; no field is stretched to fill it (Feature #233, rule 2). On a grid wider than its card the "+" cell is `position: sticky; right: 0` on the surface, with a 16px fade on its left and a chip border, both only while the wrap overflows (`.wv-overflow-x`, set beside `.wv-fit`). A stuck header casts a faint shadow on the rows under it and none at rest: the grid's one capture-phase scroll listener marks the wrap `.wv-head-stuck` once a frame while the header sits below its table's top, for the page and for a scrolling wrap alike; with the Σ row shown the shadow falls from it. The "+ New" bar drops its grey hover fill. Tests: `test/grid-hairline-header-browser.test.mjs` (new, 14 cases in light and dark: surface and square corners, label type, the stronger rule, the trailing "+" and bare slack, the sticky "+" at both scroll ends with its fade, the stuck shadow on page and wrap scroll, the lone hover tint and the fill-free "+ New"), `test/grid-layout-browser.test.mjs` and `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (the "+" no longer takes the slack), `test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs` (the ⋮ case scrolls Stage clear of the sticky "+" before it clicks).

## v0.4.52 (2026-09-28)

Fixes:

- [[Issue#455]] Looks broken: a slash command on a line with text inserts a placeholder block and leaves the text unformatted
- [[Issue#230]] Export leaks account token hashes and share tokens to a reader; import is not schema-gated
- [[Issue#426]] Slow + Looks broken + Error: very slow change state of 8 records
- [[Issue#387]] Looks broken: a rollup's settings tray shows nothing it does, not even that it draws stars
- [[Issue#428]] Wrong data: field config changes save with no Undo toast and leave no Activity entry to roll back from
- [[Issue#253]] A version bump reaches users only if it is published as a release
- [[Issue#247]] Wrong data + Error + Looks broken + Slow: mobile descriptions not captured on save, need autosave an

- **A slash command converts the line you type it on** (Issue #455). Typing `/task` at the end of `Buy milk` now gives `- [ ] Buy milk`. Text, Heading 1 to 6, the three list types and Quote convert the line and keep its words, their formatting and a nested item's indent. An empty line still gets the new block with its placeholder.

- **Importing an export back into the same workspace keeps its sign-ins and share links** (Issue #230). An export leaves out account tokens, share tokens, sessions and invites. Importing that export into the workspace it came from used to erase all of them, which signed everyone out and broke every token and share link. Import now keeps the stored secrets for the accounts and views the export still names. An export imported into a different workspace keeps none of them.

- **Changing the state of several rows at once is held to a time budget** (Issue #426). The server was busy when the slow bulk change was reported in Safari. On a table like the one in the report, a state change on eight rows settles in under 200 ms. A new browser test fails if that change ever takes more than one write, one re-read or 600 ms.

- **A rollup's or lookup's settings tray shows what it computes** (Issue #387). The tray lists the relation it follows, the field it reads and the aggregate it runs. It shows the result from the first row that has one, and says where the column's look comes from, with a link to that field's settings. The recipe is still set when the rollup is created and cannot be changed in the tray.

- **Field settings changes can be undone** (Issue #428). Saving a change to a field's options, states, colours, formula, format, default, description, name or type now shows a toast with Undo. Each change also gets an entry in Activity, where Roll back restores the previous settings. A type change has no Undo; its toast says so.

- **weave tells you when a newer release is out** (Issue #253). A running weave asks GitHub for the latest release at most once a day. A newer release turns the instance chip in the sidebar amber with its version, and a toast says so once. Set `WEAVE_UPDATE_CHECK=off` to turn the check off. DEVELOPMENT.md now names the checkout the release tagger runs from.

- **A document typed on a phone is saved when you leave it** (Issue #247). Words typed just before you switched apps, locked the phone, went back, closed the panel or reloaded could be lost. The editor now saves a document field the moment you leave it, including when the tab is hidden.

## v0.4.53 (2026-10-01)

Fixes:
- [[Issue#382]] Looks broken: ⌘K shows raw URLs and markdown and runs no commands
- [[Issue#398]] Slow: npm test hangs forever when a serve-boot test times out under load
- [[Issue#404]] Looks broken: a rating column narrower than its icons clips the last ones
- [[Issue#409]] Looks broken: the frozen # column lets scrolled cells show through
- [[Issue#410]] Looks broken: a 20px gap sits between the grid edge and the row checkbox
- [[Issue#412]] Looks broken: opening a long view description makes the held header taller than the screen
- [[Issue#415]] Wrong data: ⌘K lists every table, space and view twice, once as a registry row
- [[Issue#423]] Looks broken: a select chip wider than its column cuts its label mid-letter, with no ellipsis
- [[Issue#432]] Looks broken: a column dragged back across the frozen seam keeps auto-scrolling after the pointer leaves the edge band
- [[Issue#435]] Slow: an empty targeted-test filename starts duplicate full suites
- [[Issue#454]] Slow: five browser cases fail the full-suite gate under load and pass alone
- [[Issue#459]] Health reports behind when the checkout is ahead of main or on another branch
- [[Issue#466]] Error: the + New on a filtered view browser case fails gates for unrelated changes
- [[Issue#467]] Wrong data: a field type change has no Undo, and the values it converts cannot be brought back
- [[Issue#469]] Error: the Railway build refuses the Dockerfile because of its VOLUME line
- [[Issue#479]] Error: an imported file id holding ../ wrote and read files outside the data directory
- [[Issue#480]] Error: any workspace with no accounts listed, revealed, overwrote and deleted every key in the shared keystore
- [[Issue#481]] Error: an open or writer-accessible workspace could create, delete and search every workspace on the hub
- [[Issue#482]] Error: an anonymous POST /api/mcp created admin accounts, set keys and replaced the workspace after accounts existed
- [[Issue#483]] Error: an uploaded HTML or SVG attachment opened as a page and ran its script
- [[Issue#484]] Error: a request with a malformed percent-escape in the path ended the server process
- [[Issue#485]] Error: a ref of __proto__ or constructor changed Object.prototype for every workspace
- [[Issue#486]] Error: a page on any website could create, edit or delete rows with a cross-site POST
- [[Issue#487]] Error: the server answered any Host header, so a DNS-rebound page could reach a loopback instance
- [[Issue#489]] Error: a writer token could change the schema through relations, bulk edits and CSV import
- [[Issue#490]] Error: a javascript: link in a document ran script when clicked
- [[Issue#492]] Error: a workspace logo was stored and served with whatever content type its uploader named
- [[Issue#494]] Error: no response carried a security header, so any site could frame weave
- [[Issue#525]] Error: CI actions could be replaced upstream, and the workflow token was not limited to read
- [[Issue#532]] Error: no record of which vendored library versions ship, and no scanner could see them
- [[Issue#546]] Looks broken: workspace rail padding changes with the selected table or space
- [[Issue#549]] Looks broken: at phone width the entity dock is a 56 px sliver and the record title wraps one letter per line
- [[Issue#558]] Error: the tests workflow checks out at depth 1, so the architecture-map pin test fails on every main landing

Ships:
- [[Feature#212]] Doors into weave: sign in with GitHub, Slack, Claude or email; publish pages; iMessage and Apple Shortcuts as capture inlets
- [[Feature#242]] Workspace system tables pinned in the nav: Activity, Trash, Workflows
- [[Feature#260]] MCP injection measurement harness

Thirty-three changelog fragments landed between v0.4.52 on September 28 and this
release. Thirteen of them are the first phase of the security review of 2026-09-29,
each a server fix with a gate under `test/security/`. Two of the thirty-three landed on
the night of the release: the CI checkout depth that failed every main landing
(Issue #558) and the rating column width (Issue #404).

### Security review, phase one

- **File and logo ids stay inside `files/`** (Issue #479). A file id, logo id or
  `fileBlobs` key in an imported workspace was joined onto the `files/` directory
  unchecked. An id holding `../` wrote the import's bytes outside the data directory and
  read any reachable file back through export, the file routes and `weave_files`.
  `#blobPath` now accepts only the uuid shape the engine mints and checks that the
  resolved path sits inside `files/`, and `importJSON` refuses a dump carrying any other
  id before it changes the workspace.
- **Keys answer to the hub root's accounts, whichever workspace the URL names**
  (Issue #480). One keystore serves every workspace of a process, and `/api/keys` and
  reveal were gated by the accounts of the workspace in the URL, so a member workspace
  with no accounts opened every key. Managing keys now needs an authenticated root admin
  once the hub root holds an account. A root caller on a key's access list may reveal
  it, and a key's owner may rotate or delete it.
- **Workspace lifecycle and cross-workspace reads answer to the hub** (Issue #481).
  Creating, restoring and deleting a workspace need an admin on the hub root once the
  hub root holds an account. `GET /api/workspaces` and `GET /api/search?all=1` carry
  only the workspaces whose own wall the caller would pass.
- **MCP's accounts, keys and import tools take the same admin gate as REST**
  (Issue #482). `POST /api/mcp` reached `weave_accounts`, `weave_keys` and
  `weave_import_json` without the admin check the REST routes apply. Both doors now ask
  one function, `mayAdminister` in `src/mcp.js`, and `POST /api/import` takes the same
  gate, since an import replaces the accounts.
- **Uploaded files are served inert** (Issue #483). `GET /api/files/:id` and the task
  applet's `/t/file/:id` sent a file with the content type its uploader named and
  `Content-Disposition: inline`, so an uploaded HTML or SVG file opened as a page on the
  workspace origin and ran its script in the viewer's session. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF and
  WebP (checked against their leading bytes), PDF and plain text are served in place
  now. Every other file downloads as `application/octet-stream`.
- **A malformed percent-escape in the path answers 400 instead of ending the server**
  (Issue #484). The node listener called `decodeURIComponent` on the path with nothing
  around it, so a request like `GET /%E0%A4%A` was an unhandled rejection and the
  process exited. The listener's whole body is now guarded, and the next request is
  served.
- **`__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` find nothing** (Issue #485). The engine's
  lookups indexed plain objects by the caller's ref, so these three resolved to
  `Object.prototype` or `Object`, and the write verb that followed set properties on
  every object in the process. Every id and name lookup reads own properties only, the
  three names are refused on create and rename, and an import keyed by one is refused.
- **A write from another site is a 403** (Issue #486). Any page could send a
  `text/plain` POST, a request with no preflight, to a weave instance and create, edit
  or delete rows. A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE is now refused when its `Origin` is
  foreign or it carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. A request with no `Origin` (curl,
  the CLI, agents) is served as before.
- **A request whose Host the server does not answer to is a 421** (Issue #487). Any Host
  header used to be served, so a page on an attacker's name that re-resolves to
  127.0.0.1 was same-origin with a loopback instance. Loopback names, the host of
  `WEAVE_ORIGIN` and the names in the new `WEAVE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` answer, and
  `/api/health` answers any Host so platform probes keep working.
- **A writer cannot change structure through relations, bulk or CSV import**
  (Issue #489). `POST /api/tables/:t/relations` adds a field and is now a schema write.
  `POST /api/tables/:t/import.csv` takes the same system-table check as the entity door,
  and `POST /api/bulk` refuses a writer when any row it names, or any table it writes
  into, is a system table.
- **Document links and images keep only safe targets** (Issue #490). `src/markdown.js`
  wrote a link or image target into `href` or `src` without checking its scheme, so
  `[x](javascript:…)` in a document ran script on the workspace origin when clicked. A
  target is now written only when it is relative, an in-page or in-app anchor, or uses
  `http`, `https` or `mailto`. Any other target renders its text with no anchor.
- **The workspace logo's type comes from its bytes** (Issue #492). `PUT
  /api/workspace/logo` stored the content type the writer named and `GET` served it
  back, so a writer could plant an HTML page at the logo URL. Upload now takes PNG,
  JPEG, GIF and WebP (proved by their leading bytes) and SVG, and answers anything else
  with 415.
- **Every response carries security headers** (Issue #494). None were sent. Every answer
  now has `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`. HTML
  answers add `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'`, so another site cannot
  frame weave. A second, report-only `Content-Security-Policy` names the target state of
  no inline script or style, and is reported without being enforced yet.
  `Strict-Transport-Security` goes out only on a request that arrived over https.

### Supply chain, scanning and injection measurement

- **CI actions are pinned and the token is read-only** (Issue #525). Every action in
  `.github/workflows/` is pinned to a full commit SHA, both workflows grant
  `contents: read` only, and a new `security.yml` runs `scripts/security-scan.mjs` on
  push to main, on pull requests and weekly.
- **Vendored libraries are pinned, and the scan that reads them is repeatable**
  (Issue #532). `security/vendor.lock.json` lists every file under `public/vendor/` and
  `src/vendor/` with its library, version and sha256, and
  `test/security/vendor-lock.test.mjs` fails on a changed, unlisted or missing file.
  `node scripts/security-scan.mjs` runs gitleaks over history, semgrep with weave's own
  sink rules against a baseline so only new results fail, zizmor, actionlint, hadolint
  and the vendor advisory lookup, one pass, with a fail or skipped line each.
  `node scripts/vendor-advisories.mjs` asks OSV for advisories on each vendored file.
- **MCP injection measurement harness** (Feature #260). `security/mcp-inject/` seeds a
  scratch workspace with one row carrying a planted instruction, runs a headless agent
  with an ordinary task over weave's MCP server, and judges whether the instruction was
  carried out. It is run by hand, costs model calls, and sits outside `npm test`. The
  harness only measures. Finding S-22 of the 2026-09-29 security review stays open,
  and its row, #499, stays out of the Fixes list above.

### Grid, columns and chrome

- **A rating column opens wide enough for its own icons** (Issue #404). Every rating
  column opened at the type default of 104px whatever its `max`, so the showcase's Love
  (max 7) and Brightness (max 12) drew their last hearts and suns cut at the cell edge:
  a 7 of 7 read like a 5 of 7, and the right-most icon could not be clicked.
  `defaultWidth` in `public/column-resize.js` now opens a rating at `max` icons plus the
  gaps between them plus the cell's own horizontal padding, floored at the 104px type
  default and capped at the 320px fit ceiling. Only the default moves: a width the
  reader dragged still wins. The compact `n / max` form for a column narrowed by hand
  waits on a design decision and is not in this release.
- **The frozen # pair stays opaque on the row open in the dock** (Issue #409). The
  docked row's highlight is `background: var(--tblr-active-bg)` on every cell, and in
  the light theme that token is 4% of the accent over nothing. The rule won over the
  frozen checkbox and # pair's opaque background, so those two cells let the cells
  scrolling under them show through. The docked row's frozen cells now paint that same
  highlight over the surface.
- **The row checkbox sits 4px from the grid edge** (Issue #410). The checkbox column
  carried Tabler's `.card-table` first-child inset, 20px of empty space left of a box
  that only shows on hover, so the frozen checkbox and # pair was 97px wide before any
  field. `--wv-sel-lead` is now 4px, set on both the select-all header and every row's
  checkbox cell so they keep one vertical line.
- **An opened long description scrolls inside the held header** (Issue #412). Opening a
  sixty-paragraph description with Show more made the header 1,340px tall in a 900px
  window, so it let go and the crumb, title and toolbar scrolled off with it. An opened
  description, or its editor, now stops at a fifth of the window and the rest scrolls
  inside it, so the header keeps holding.
- **A value chip longer than its column ends in an ellipsis inside its fill**
  (Issue #423). In a narrow column a select chip ran its text past its own fill and the
  cell cut it mid-letter. Select, state, multi-select and key chips now carry their text
  in a `.k-label` span that truncates with an ellipsis. A cut label marks its cell
  clipped, so the hover expansion still opens, and carries the whole value as its title.
- **The workspace rail and sidebar hold one left edge on every view** (Issue #546).
  Tabler's `:root { margin-left: calc(100vw - 100%) }` pushed the whole page right by
  the width of a classic scrollbar. In Safari with a mouse attached, the rail and
  sidebar sat 16px further in on a table that scrolls the page than on one that does
  not. `style.css` now sets `:root { margin-left: 0 }`.
- **A record opens as a full-screen sheet on a phone** (Issue #549). Below 600px the
  entity dock covers the screen in place of a 56px column beside the table, where the
  name stood one letter per line and WebKit scrolled the page sideways. The sheet's
  close button and Esc return the table where it was.

### Search

- **⌘K shows one line per hit, grouped** (Issue #382). Each hit used to take three
  lines: a kind badge and title, the full permalink in mono, and a raw markdown snippet.
  Each hit is now one 36px line with a kind icon, the name with the match marked, the
  workflow state chip and its public id. Hits are grouped as Records, In documents,
  Tables, then Spaces and views, and an empty group is hidden. ⌘K with no query typed
  lists Recent: the last eight records and tables opened, kept per workspace in this
  browser. ↑ and ↓ move, Tab jumps between groups, ↵ opens and Esc closes.
- **A table, space or view is found once** (Issue #415). `universalSearch` also returned
  the container's own row in the Workspace registry, so ⌘K listed every table name
  twice, once as a record. Registry rows for workspaces, spaces, tables and views are
  dropped before the row limit.

### Fields

- **A field type change has an Undo that brings the values back** (Issue #467). A type
  change converts every stored value, and until now nothing kept the values from before,
  so its toast said it had no Undo and its Activity entry offered no Roll back. The
  write path now keeps each row's value from before the conversion. Undo in the toast
  and Roll back in Activity restore the definition and every row unchanged since the
  change. A field keeps the values of its newest type change only. An export carries no
  snapshot. A credential field's snapshot holds the secret's name at most.

### Navigation and sign-in

- **Workspace system tables in the nav** (Feature #242). Activity, Trash and Workflows
  sit as three fixed rows under the spaces in the left nav. Trash is the workspace-wide
  trash (`#/trash`, new `GET /api/trash`) with a Table column, where a trashed table or
  space restores from its registry row. A system table can no longer be renamed on any
  door.
- **Sign in with an OpenID Connect provider** (Feature #212, door C of Feature #222).
  With `WEAVE_OIDC_ISSUER` and `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` set, the sign-in page at `/auth`
  carries a link to one provider (Clerk, Auth0, Keycloak, Authentik, Google), and a
  person who signs in there comes back with the same `wv_session` cookie a passkey
  mints. The flow is authorization code with PKCE, and the id token's signature, issuer,
  audience, expiry and nonce are verified in `src/oidc.js` with no dependency. Signing
  in creates no account: `weave account link <name> --email <address>` opens an account
  to the identity with that verified email.

### Build, gate and deploy

- **The `tests` workflow checks out the full history** (Issue #558). `actions/checkout`
  ran at its default depth of one commit, so `test/architecture-map.test.mjs` could not
  ask `git merge-base --is-ancestor` whether the map's pinned revision sits behind HEAD.
  All four matrix legs failed on every main landing from `5091c23` on, while the Gerrit
  gate stayed green on the same code. The same shallow checkout left
  `test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs` asserting nothing. The checkout step now carries
  `fetch-depth: 0`, matching `security.yml`.
- **The full-suite gate stops voting Verified -1 on good changes** (Issues #454, #466,
  #432, #435). On 2026-09-28 the full-suite gate voted the same tree red five times and
  then green. The suite had grown to 130 browser files, and node's default ran nine at
  once, each a Node process with a server plus a Chromium of four or five processes,
  which drove the load average to 27 on a ten-core machine. `scripts/test.mjs` now runs
  everything that does not drive a browser first, at node's default, and then the
  browser suites in their own lane at half the cores. The cases that went red read a
  value a fixed sleep after an action; they now wait for the value they assert. A bare
  `node --test` no longer starts a second full suite.
- **A serve-boot test that times out no longer hangs the suite** (Issue #398). The
  Handbook and Showcase boot tests spawn `weave serve` and wait for it to come up.
  Nothing killed the server when the wait timed out, its pipes kept the test file's
  process alive, and `npm test` sat silent for as long as 28 minutes. Both tests now go
  through `test/lib/serve-fixture.mjs`, which stops the server on every outcome.
- **Health reports `behind` only when main has a commit this checkout lacks**
  (Issue #459). `describeBuild` set `behind: latest !== head`, so a dev worktree one
  commit ahead of main, or a feature branch already carrying main's tip, got the amber
  chip and the "behind main" toast. The server now runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
  and `behind` is true only when that fails.
- **Railway builds the Dockerfile again** (Issue #469). Railway refused the image with
  `dockerfile invalid: docker VOLUME at Line 29 is not supported, use Railway Volumes`.
  The `Dockerfile` no longer carries `VOLUME /data`; Railway, Fly and `compose.yaml`
  each mount `/data` themselves.

CHANGELOG.md carries each fragment's note in full.


**Correction, 2026-10-03 (Issue #568).** These notes first cited the MCP injection measurement harness as Issue #499. That row is security finding S-22, which stays Open until its fix lands; the harness only measures it. The harness now has its own row, Feature #260, listed under Ships above, and the entry cites it. CHANGELOG.md and the GitHub Release for v0.4.53 still read "(Issue #499)"; the next release notes carry the correction.

## v0.4.54 — 2026-10-02

Landed as cc3b8d9. Fixed:

- [[Issue#550]] Looks broken: the slash menu opens under the Description header and the record title, hiding its rows (Gerrit 526)
- [[Issue#551]] Wrong data: an option colour sent as "magenta" is saved as slate with no error (Gerrit 527)
- [[Issue#571]] Looks broken: the weave mark shows notches at the center crossing in large exports (Gerrit 525)

Also shipped: [[Feature#243]] Remove the built-in passkey door once provider sign-in has landed (Gerrit 514).

### Notes

- **The weave mark's over strand is continuous at any size** (Issue #571): `rope()` in `src/mark.js` now draws each over-segment as strand A's whole odd segment, the exact cubic from one wave extreme to the next (`M20,28 C24,28 24,20 28,20` for the mark), in place of a short quadratic across the crossing. Mask A's halo cuts strand A about 5 units either side of the crossing, and the short quadratic covered 2.6, so large exports showed crescent notches of background beside the center crossing (about 12 px deep at 512 px). In the morph loaders the over-segment's cut in strand B narrows and fades with the amplitude; narrowing alone left a hard slot along the longer cut on near-flat frames. Every SVG, PNG and GIF in `brand/assets/` and `public/brand/`, the rail marks in `public/index.html` and the loader sheet are rebuilt. Gate: `brand/build-logos.test.mjs` (the over-segment covers every point the halo cuts, lies on strand A, and the inline marks match).
- **The built-in passkey door is removed** (Feature #243): people sign in through the OpenID Connect provider (Feature #212) and agents keep `wv_` tokens. Gone: `src/webauthn.js`, the routes `POST /api/auth/register/options`, `/api/auth/register/verify`, `/api/auth/login/options`, `/api/auth/login/verify` and `DELETE /api/auth/credentials/<id>` (all now answer 404), the passkey and "Register this device" parts of `/auth`, the engine's invite and credential verbs, the CLI verbs `weave account invite` and `weave account remove-credential`, the `weave_accounts` actions `invite` and `remove-credential`, and the Handbook guide "Door B: passkeys". Kept: the `wv_session` cookie, `weave account sessions` and `weave account revoke-session`, sign-out, the rate limits, `WEAVE_ORIGIN` (now the origin the provider redirects back to) and `WEAVE_TRUST_PROXY`, share links and the applet passcode. A passkey already stored on an account row stays in the data and is ignored; `weave account list` and `/api/auth/me` no longer show it. Before upgrading, link each person's account to a provider identity (`weave account link <name> --email <address>`), or they cannot sign in in a browser. Gates: `test/auth-passkey-removed.test.mjs`, `test/auth-session.test.mjs`.
- **`/auth` goes straight to the provider** (Feature #243): with `WEAVE_OIDC_ISSUER` and `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` set, a signed-out visit answers `302` to `/api/auth/oidc/start`, keeping a same-site `?next`, with no page in between. Signed in, `/auth` still shows sessions and sign-out; signing out lands on `/auth?signed-out=1`, which shows the provider link rather than bouncing back through the provider's own session. Gate: `test/auth-passkey-removed.test.mjs`.
- **The slash menu opens over the record header and the section head, not under them** (Issue #550): a menu that flipped upward was painted over by two sticky bands, because Vditor's own rule puts `.vditor-hint` at z-index 4 while the document section head sits at 5 (Issue #411) and the record header at 6. On a Task page at 1280x800 `document.elementFromPoint` over the menu's own box answered `TEXTAREA.name-edit`, `DIV.view-header` and `DIV.doc-section-head`, so the rows in those bands could be neither read nor clicked, and the word DESCRIPTION cut the menu in half. The menu is now z-index 9, clear of both bands and of the selection bubble (7) with its tooltip (8), and `attachHintClamp` clamps an upward menu's top to the record header's bottom edge — the page's header or the dock's — holding the bottom edge Vditor anchored beside the caret, so the menu gives up rows to its own scroll instead of sliding behind the title. The window cap moved to the sheet as `min(400px, calc(100vh - 24px))`, and a closed menu drops the shrink so the next opening is measured at that cap. Gate: `test/slash-menu-stack-browser.test.mjs` (hit-tests every band of an open upward menu, in the gate's browser and in WebKit, both themes).
- **An option colour weave cannot name answers 400** (Issue #551): `src/vocabulary.js` published eight colours and called pink's hex "magenta", while `src/engine.js` knew ten hues, called that hex "pink", read `color` only as a hex, and swapped any name it could not resolve for slate while answering 201. A select field created with the documented name came back as a grey chip and the caller was told nothing. `public/chip-core.js` now owns the ten hues, the two aliases weave had published for them (`magenta` for pink, `neutral` for slate) and `hueName()`, which resolves a ramp name, an alias or a hex and answers undefined for anything else; `src/vocabulary.js` generates `OPTION_COLORS` from that ramp and publishes each hue's aliases, and the field dialog's dead copy of the old eight hexes, which had held the vocabulary at eight, is gone. `addField`, the select and multi-select options patch, a type change carrying its own options, `applySchema` and a `field` definition value now answer 400 quoting the value and naming the ten hues, on the HTTP routes, the MCP tools and the CLI alike. Reads stay forgiving: `importJSON` writes state verbatim, and an option handed back wearing the colour it already had is accepted, which `src/weaver-seed.js` and `src/handbook.js` need because they widen a select by re-sending the options they found. weave's own Automations `Health` field, seeded with `yellow`, `green` and `red` through the hex-only reader, had stored all three as slate and now carries ramp hues. The Handbook's select page and the guide "Making a workspace your own" name the ten hues and the alias rule. Gates: `test/option-colour.test.mjs`, `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.55 — 2026-10-02

Release cut with Feature #252 (Gerrit 536). Fixed:

- [[Issue#589]] Wrong data: the architecture map cites src/auth-page.js line 176, past the end of the file
- [[Issue#583]] Looks broken: Docked entity's expand and close sit in a row above the breadcrumb and scroll away
- [[Issue#596]] Slow: write tools echo the whole object back, about 1.8 KB to create a one-field row
- [[Issue#595]] Slow: the MCP server lists 56 tools, about 12,000 tokens an agent re-reads every turn
- [[Issue#603]] Error: main is red, mcp-tool-profile expects "admin token" after the roles rename (test fix folded into Gerrit 536)

Also landed, Issue left open: [[Issue#569]], a signed-out browser goes straight to sign-in (Gerrit 532).

Shipped:

- [[Feature#251]] Public privacy and terms pages at /privacy and /terms
- [[Feature#255]] Roles: Observer, Editor and Architect
- [[Feature#252]] Sign-in asks the provider for no personal information

Kyle looked at the Clerk consent screen for weave.grunion.ai, which asked for his identity, his email address and his basic profile, and said he does not want anyone's personal information. From this release weave asks the provider for `openid` alone and keeps no email for sign-in.

### Notes

- **The architecture map re-renders again** (Issue #589): the Sign-in node cited `src/auth-page.js` line 176, past the end of the file since Feature #243, and `node scripts/architecture.mjs` refused to re-render. It now cites `renderAuthPage` at line 113.
- **The docked record has one header row, and it stays pinned while the pane scrolls** (Issue #583): back, expand and close sat in a `.dock-head` row of their own above the breadcrumb. Only the record's `.view-header` is sticky in the dock (Issue #411), so that row left the screen with the first scroll and the pane showed two toolbars stacked. `drawDock` now hands its controls to `renderEntityView`, which puts back at the left of the crumb path and expand and close after the eye and the ⋮, the same crumb row the full page uses for its collapse and close. Titles, labels, ⌘⇧E and Esc are unchanged, and the full-screen dock below 600px keeps the same row. Gate: `test/dock-header-one-row-browser.test.mjs` (scrolls the pane to the bottom, light and dark, after a hop and at 390x844, and checks every control is on screen, in the crumb row and reachable by a tap).
- **Public privacy and terms pages** (Feature #251): `/privacy` and `/terms` answer anyone, signed in or not, with a privacy policy and terms of service adapted from the Basecamp open-source policies (CC BY 4.0), so a sign-in provider's consent screen can link them. The sign-in page links both. Placeholders such as `[Entity name]` stay visible for the operator to fill. Gate: `test/legal-pages.test.mjs`.
- **MCP writes answer compact** (Issue #596): the create, update, link, unlink, state, delete, restore, move and duplicate tools answer with `{id, publicId, name}`, a field write adds its `type` and stored `config`, and `weave_add_relation` answers `{field, inverse}` in that shape. `verbose: true` on any of them returns the whole object as before. Tool text is one-line JSON instead of indented. A fixed build of one space, two tables, four fields, one relation and five rows now answers in 1,614 bytes instead of 17,244. REST and the CLI keep the full reply. Gate: `test/mcp-compact-writes.test.mjs`.
- **The MCP server lists fifteen tools by default** (Issue #595): `tools/list` answers the core build set (`weave_schema`, `weave_query`, `weave_get_entity`, `weave_create_entity`, `weave_update_entity`, `weave_create_space`, `weave_create_table`, `weave_add_field`, `weave_update_field`, `weave_add_relation`, `weave_import_csv`, `weave_vocabulary`, `weave_workspace`, `weave_search`) plus the new `weave_call {name, args}`, which runs any other tool with the same admin gate, compact reply and `verbose` switch. Its description lists every other tool in one line, and `weave_call {name: "help", args: {tool}}` returns a tool's full description and input schema. `weave mcp --tools all` or `WEAVE_MCP_TOOLS=all` (stdio and `POST /api/mcp`) lists all 57. The default list is 11,961 bytes instead of 29,251. Gate: `test/mcp-tool-profile.test.mjs`, which also checks the counts README, AGENTS.md and llms.txt give.
- **Sign-in asks the provider for no personal information** (Feature #252): weave requests the `openid` scope alone, so the provider's consent screen lists one line, and it no longer reads the provider's userinfo endpoint. A sign-in yields the provider's issuer and subject and nothing else. Linking an account mints a one-time invite link that lasts 7 days, stored as its hash: `weave account link <name>`, `POST /api/accounts/<name>/identities` (answers with `url`) or `weave_accounts` `link-identity`. The person opens the link, signs in at the provider, and weave pins their subject to the account. A spent or expired link answers `410`; a subject that already opens another account answers `409` and leaves the invite unused. Unlink names the subject: `weave account unlink <name> --subject <sub>`, `DELETE /api/accounts/<name>/identities?subject=<sub>`. `--email` and `?email=` are refused. On the first open, an identity the provider had already pinned keeps its subject and loses its email; an identity linked by email and never pinned is dropped, so mint an invite for anyone who had not signed in yet. The email also leaves the `identity-linked`, `identity-unlinked` and `identity-pinned` audit entries. Gate: `test/auth-oidc.test.mjs`.
- **Roles are Observer, Editor and Architect** (Feature #255): `reader`, `writer` and `admin` are renamed `observer`, `editor` and `architect`, Kyle's three-level model. An observer now comments: it may post a comment, which carries its own account name whatever the body says, and delete a comment it made; every other write is still a 403. An editor creates, edits and deletes rows and comments and never structure, as a writer did; an architect does everything an admin did. Every open rewrites an old name stored on an account, so every `wv_` token and session keeps working, and the routes read an old name still on a row as the new one. `weave account create --role`, `POST /api/accounts` and MCP `weave_accounts create` default to `editor` and still take the old names for one release, answering with a `note` that names the new one. "Free", "paid seat" and "paid" are labels only (Feature #256 records that seats and billing are not built). Gates: `test/roles.test.mjs`.
- **A signed-out browser goes straight to sign-in** (Issue #569): with a provider configured (`WEAVE_OIDC_ISSUER` and `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`), a page behind the wall answers `302` to `/auth?next=<the page>` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, in place of the 401 page "This workspace requires authentication". `/auth` then sends the browser on to the provider, so a visit to `/` lands on the provider's sign-in with `?next` kept. API callers keep the JSON 401. The 401 page stays for an instance with no provider, where a token or a share link is the way in, and for a bad Bearer token on a page, since signing in is no answer to a wrong token. Gates: `test/auth-passkey-removed.test.mjs`, `test/auth-session.test.mjs`, `test/auth-wall.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.56 — 2026-10-02

Landed as f24254a. Fixed:

- [[Issue#584]] Looks broken: hovering a truncated chip shows the field name, never the full value (Gerrit 529)
- [[Issue#570]] Looks broken: an unlinked Clerk identity loops between the 403 page and Clerk with no way to switch accounts (Gerrit 543)
- [[Issue#594]] Looks broken: a new workspace reads "workspace / workspace / General" on first load (Gerrit 541)
- [[Issue#590]] Error: a date grain sent as a string fails with "A grain with no date parts must keep a time of day" (Gerrit 538)
- [[Issue#586]] Looks broken: a toggle column resizes narrower than its switch and word, so the toggle is cut off (Gerrit 533)

Also shipped: [[Feature#248]] Onboarding: a short welcome that starts by naming the first workspace (Gerrit 531), and the first slice of [[Feature#249]], an On toggle on every Workflows row (Gerrit 535; the feature stays open).

### Notes

- **Hovering a truncated grid chip shows its whole value** (Issue #584): since Issue #423 a value too long for its column ends in an ellipsis inside the chip, and the label span carried the value as its title, but the chip itself kept the field name ("Program"), so hovering the chip's padding showed the field name. The title now sits on the chip: a cut chip carries the value, a chip that fits keeps the title it was drawn with (the field name on a select and a state, none on a multi chip). A column resize rechecks it, in a registry grid as well as a view. Gate: `test/chip-ellipsis-browser.test.mjs` (select, state, multi and key chips in both themes, a short select keeping "Program", and a widened column handing the field name back).
- **A date grain sent as a word names the shape it needs** (Issue #590): the 2026-10-02 agent eval sent `{"grain":"month","format":"month"}` or `{"grain":"day","format":"iso"}` to `weave_add_field` 23 times in 32 runs. `normalizeGrain` read only an array or the tray's `{year, month, day}` flags, so a string collapsed to no parts and the engine answered "A grain with no date parts must keep a time of day", which names the wrong problem; agents then tried two or three shapes before landing on `["year","month"]`. A grain that is not a list or a flags object is now refused with `grain is a list of parts, e.g. ["year","month"] for a month or ["year"] for a year; parts are year, month, day`. A word is not accepted as an alias, because a bare "month" could mean month alone or year·month. The vocabulary's `dateGrainForm` says the same. Gate: `test/date-grain.test.mjs` ("a grain sent as a string is refused with the shape a grain takes").
- **A refused sign-in no longer sends you back into the provider** (Issue #570): a provider account with no account here gets a `403` page, **No access to <workspace>**, that says a workspace admin can send an invite link and offers **Use a different account**. That button goes to the provider's `end_session_endpoint` (with `client_id` and `post_logout_redirect_uri` back to `/auth?signed-out=1`) when discovery names one, and otherwise starts a new trip with `prompt=login` (`/api/auth/oidc/start?fresh=1`, `select_account` added where discovery lists it), so the provider asks for credentials again instead of reusing its session. An invite opened as someone the server already knows (`409`) gets the same button, and its new trip carries the unspent invite. Every refusal page on the sign-in trip (expired or replayed trip, provider error, unverifiable token, provider down, spent invite, and the rate limit, which was bare JSON) now links back to `/auth?signed-out=1`; bare `/auth` sent a signed-out browser to the provider, whose own session signed it straight back in to the same refusal. A trip started under `/w/<name>` comes back to that workspace's sign-in page. Gates: `test/auth-oidc.test.mjs`, `test/auth-session.test.mjs`.
- **A short welcome names the first workspace** (Feature #248): a person new to an empty instance gets one held dialog with three steps. Step one welcomes them, step two names the workspace with a default already filled in and focused (the account's first name, else the workspace's current name), and step three offers the Tasks, CRM and Docs starters or an empty workspace. Enter takes the primary button; Skip on every step and Esc keep the defaults and land in a working workspace. A typed name the engine would refuse is folded into one it accepts ("Acme Team" becomes `acme-team`), and a name another workspace holds is refused before anything is built. The welcome runs once per person, finished or skipped: the mark is on the account row (`onboardedAt`), or on the hub root's meta when nobody is signed in, so it does not come back on another device. It asks only when the person may rename the workspace (no role, or architect), this workspace has no tables of its own, and no other workspace they can open has any, the weave docs workspace aside; an existing person with a populated workspace never sees it, and a populated home does not even ask. New: `GET /api/onboarding` (`{show, name}`) and `POST /api/onboarding` (`{name?, template?}`, which builds the starter server side through starter-core's `steps()`, renames, and marks), `Weave#onboardedAt` and `Weave#markOnboarded`, and `WeaveStarters.workspaceName`. Gate: `test/onboarding.test.mjs` (10) and `test/onboarding-browser.test.mjs` (both themes, every skip, 375 px).
- **A toggle column is never narrower than its switch and its word** (Issue #586): a column's floor was its header label alone, so a toggle named "On" dragged to 45px while its cell paints a 28px track, a 7px gap and the word of its state inside 4px of padding each side; the word ellipsized and then the track clipped. `settle()` in `public/app.js` now gives every toggle column a value floor, as a date column has had since Issue #159: the track, the gap and the wider of the field's two words, measured in the cell's own face, plus the cell's measured padding (`toggleWidth` and `TOGGLE_METRICS` in `public/column-resize.js`). The floor binds a drag, the Alt+arrow nudge, a double-click fit and the frozen-zone cap, and raises a default or stored width under it for that column only, so a toggle worded "Synchronising every night" opens at 203px where the type default is 124. Gates: `test/column-resize.test.mjs`, `test/toggle-width-browser.test.mjs` (default On / Off, Running / Paused and a word past the default, in an on row and an off row, with every other column's width held).
- **Every Workflows row has an On switch** (Feature #249): Kyle ruled that each automation is a row of the built-in `Workspace/Workflows` table and that the table is the control panel. The first piece is a system `On` field of type toggle, worded On / Off and off until someone switches it, placed first after Name in the table's field order and in every view. `#ensureMetaTables` in `src/engine.js` mints it on every workspace, new or existing, the first time this engine opens it; a re-sync never mints a second one or moves a column the reader has since moved. The engine does not read the switch yet, and the State select stays: whether the switch replaces State, a workspace-wide pause and an automatic switch-off on failure are open questions on #249. `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` lists the field. Gate: `test/workflows-table.test.mjs`.
- **A new workspace gets a random adjective-animal name** (Issue #594): a fresh install used to read "workspace" in the heading, the sidebar and the breadcrumbs, because the engine seeded `Weave Workspace` and `weave serve` swapped that for the data file's basename. The seed of a fresh workspace with no name to go on now draws one adjective and one animal from two curated lists in `src/workspace-name.js` and stores the slug, so a fresh `weave serve` opens on a workspace named like `quiet-turtle`. `workspaceName()` also returns the Title Case display name, "Quiet Turtle", which the page can show once Issue #592 gives the display name its own field. Adjectives are neutral or positive; every animal is also an upstream Lucide icon name (bird, cat, dog, fish, panda, rabbit, snail, squirrel, turtle) and `ANIMALS` is exported so the workspace icon can follow the animal once those icons are vendored; `public/vendor/icons` ships none of them today. The slug passes the rename rule. A name already on the instance gets `-2`, `-3` and so on: `weave serve` checks the workspace files beside the data file, and `POST /api/workspaces` with no `name` draws a free one instead of creating a workspace called `undefined`. The Worker still names a fresh Durable Object after its route. Existing workspaces keep their names: one still carrying `Weave Workspace` takes its file's basename as before, and one named `workspace` stays `workspace`. A file someone named still names its workspace: `--data ./other.db` makes `other`, and a hub serves it at `/w/other/`; only the default data file, `workspace`, draws at random. Gate: `test/workspace-name.test.mjs`.

releases.name: v0.4.57
fixes: Error: a push to GitHub main does not start a Railway build
ships: Hosted instance updates itself in place: a supervisor swaps workers on a new release with no failed request
releases.description:
## v0.4.57, 2026-10-02

Shipped: [[Feature#250]] Hosted instance updates itself in place: a supervisor swaps workers on a new release with no failed request (Gerrit 537).

### Notes

- **The hosted instance updates itself in place** (Feature #250): `weave supervise` with `WEAVE_AUTO_UPDATE=1` holds the port and runs `weave serve` as a child worker. Every ten minutes it asks GitHub for the latest release; a newer tag whose commit is on `grunion-ai/weave` main is downloaded, unpacked to `releases/v<version>/` beside the workspace, started as a second worker on the same SQLite files and checked on its own `/api/health`. Healthy, it takes new requests, the old worker drains and exits, and only then does the new one write its open-time migrations (the engine's `deferMigrations` holds every save until that point, and the supervisor holds writes for that moment instead of failing them). The supervisor forwards HTTP rather than TCP, so no client keep-alive socket closes mid-swap. A release that is off main, fails its health check or carries the wrong version inside is recorded and not retried; `/api/health` carries `supervisor.release`, `dir`, `lastSwap` and `failed`. Unset, `supervise` is `serve`. The "Deploy: Railway" guide gains step 7 with the start command. Gate: `test/supervisor.test.mjs` (zero failed requests across a swap under a request loop, an unhealthy release leaves the old worker serving, an off-main tag is refused before download, migrations wait for the old worker's exit, opt-in only).

## v0.4.58, 2026-10-02

Fixed:

- [[Issue#569]] Looks broken: signing in from weave.grunion.ai takes five screens, and a new person dead-ends at a 403 (landed as c4d17fe)

### Notes

- **Invite a new person to a workspace** (Issue #569): an architect opens **Members** on the workspace's home page, enters an email, picks a role (Editor, paid seat, by default) and gets a one-time sign-in link to send; the same section lists the pending invites with role, inviter and date, and revokes one. Opening the link and signing in at the provider makes the account at the invited role, named after the email's local part (`-2`, `-3` when taken), pins the provider's subject to it, spends the invite and lands the person where they were going, so a new person no longer dead-ends at "No account for this identity". The invite is the same hashed `wvi_` code as an account link (Feature #252): the provider is still asked for no email, and the invitee's email lives on the pending invite only, never on the account, in the audit log or in an export. A revoked, spent, expired or other-workspace link answers `410`; a sign-in with no invite gets the refusal page as before. weave sends no invite email yet. Also `POST`/`GET /api/invites`, `DELETE /api/invites/:id`, `weave invite <email>`, `weave invite list`, `weave invite revoke <id>` and MCP `weave_accounts` `invite`, `invites`, `revoke-invite`. Gates: `test/invites.test.mjs`, `test/invites-browser.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.59, 2026-10-03

Fixed:

- [[Issue#591]] Error: agents guess Lucide icon names outside the inventory and the refusal suggests none (landed as 84b1912)
- [[Issue#478]] Error: a push to GitHub main does not start a Railway build (docs, landed as f42f445: the release tag is the deploy)

Ships:

- [[Feature#254]] Hosted MCP sign-in: terminal command opens the browser for OAuth (landed as 27e853f, merge 8d5ce63)

### Notes

- **Agents sign in to a hosted instance through the browser** (Feature #254): with a provider configured (`WEAVE_OIDC_ISSUER` and `WEAVE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`), `POST /mcp` (the default workspace) and `POST /w/<name>/mcp` serve MCP as an OAuth 2.1 protected resource, so `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http weave https://<host>/mcp` opens the provider's sign-in and needs no pasted token. `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (and the `/mcp` and `/w/<name>/mcp` suffixed paths) publish RFC 9728 metadata naming the provider as the authorization server; a call without a credential answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...`. A provider access token is checked at the provider's userinfo endpoint (cached a minute by its sha256, never stored), its subject opens the account a `weave account link` invite pinned it to (the metadata asks for the `openid` scope alone, as the browser door does), and writes record `<account> via <client>` (`via oauth` for an opaque token). Unlinked subject: 403. Rejected token: 401. `wv_` tokens work on `/mcp` unchanged and `/api/mcp` keeps its contract. New: `WEAVE_MCP_ORIGINS`, other public origins the door answers on. Known limit: no RFC 8707 audience check, since Clerk does not bind tokens to a resource. Gates: `test/mcp-oauth.test.mjs`.
- **A refused icon names the nearest inventory icons, and the vocabulary searches icons** (Issue #591): the 2026-10-02 agent eval had 17 refused writes for real Lucide names the curated inventory lacks (`lucide:building-2`, `handshake`, `tags`, `repeat`). The refusal said only "use lucide:<name> from the vocabulary", so the agent pulled the 4.4k-token list or dropped the icon. It now reads `Icon 'lucide:building-2' is not in the inventory; nearest: lucide:landmark (money), lucide:house (other). Search it with weave_vocabulary {section:"icons", query:"<word>"} (CLI: weave vocabulary icons <word>), or use a mark character`, and the write answers 400 with code `invalid`. Names rank by stem or substring, then a short synonym list for the words agents reach for first, then edit distance over the name or one of its words; nothing within reach means no suggestion rather than a misleading one. `weave_vocabulary` takes `section` (that section alone, as the CLI's `weave vocabulary <section>` already did) and `query` (with section `icons`, or alone): matches by name, category or synonym as `{name, category}`, or the nearest names marked `fuzzy`. REST: `GET /api/vocabulary?section=icons&query=build`; CLI: `weave vocabulary icons build`; an unknown section answers 400 on REST. The no-argument call is unchanged. Gate: `test/icon-search.test.mjs`.
- **The release tag is the hosted deploy** (Issue #478, Feature #250): CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md rule 7, DEVELOPMENT.md rule 8 and the "Deploy: Railway" guide now say plainly that a host running `weave supervise` with `WEAVE_AUTO_UPDATE=1` is never redeployed to ship a landing. A platform redeploy restarts the container, fails requests for up to a minute and resets the supervisor; it is kept for a Node version, `Dockerfile` or `src/supervisor.js` change. A fix reaches the host with the next release tag, and the guide says to turn off GitHub automatic deploys on the service.

## v0.4.60, 2026-10-03

Fixed:

- [[Issue#607]] Slow: the first live self-update stalled every request for about ten seconds after the switch (Gerrit 555, landed as 80f342a)

### Notes

- **A self-update no longer stalls requests while the new release settles** (Issue #607): the first live swap on weave.grunion.ai (v0.4.57 to v0.4.58, 07:02Z on 2026-10-03) left every request unanswered for about ten seconds after the switch, because settling the new worker's deferred open rewrote every entity row and search entry of each workspace, synchronously, in the worker that had just started serving. Settling now writes only what the open changed: a held save keeps its dirty set and a plain save is exact. `#migrate` marks every entity it changes and no longer forces a full rewrite, so an ordinary open that repairs something writes only that too. Gate: `test/supervisor.test.mjs` (41 rows rewritten before, only the repaired table's registry row after).

## v0.4.61, 2026-10-03

Fixed:

- [[Issue#613]] Looks broken: /terms and /privacy show [Contact email] and [Address] placeholders
- [[Issue#572]] Wrong data: PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc answers 200 and blanks the document
- [[Issue#563]] Error: test/update-check.test.mjs is red on both node 22.16 legs

Shipped:

- [[Feature#253]] Build verb: one call creates a whole workspace outline

### Notes

- **The sign-in "No access" page and two Handbook lines name the architect role** (Feature #255): the 403 page a signed-in stranger lands on still told them "a workspace admin can send you an invite link", and the Handbook said whoever reaches the port with requireAuth off "is an admin" and called an "admin `wv_` token" the rescue path, all after reader, writer and admin became observer, editor and architect on 2026-10-02. All three now say architect, and a code comment on the invite flow follows. The accepted `admin` input alias and its deprecation note are unchanged. Gate: `test/auth-oidc.test.mjs` asserts the page wording and that no Handbook guide line says admin except the rename note.
- **Build a workspace outline in one call** (Feature #253): `weave_build` (MCP), `POST /api/build` and `weave build <spec.json> [--dry-run]` take one short spec of spaces, tables, fields, relations and rows and run it through the existing verbs in dependency order: workspace name, spaces, tables, plain fields, relations, lookups and rollups, formulas, rows, then the rows' relation values, so a row links by name to a row made in the same call. A field is `{name, type}` plus that type's `weave_add_field` config keys, flat; a relation is a field with `type: "relation"` and `to`. Existing spaces, tables and same-typed fields are reused and listed in `existing`, so resending a whole spec after an error is safe; rows append, so a spec of rows alone is a batch create, and `skipExistingRows` skips a row whose Name the table already holds. An icon outside the inventory or an option colour weave cannot name is dropped and reported in `ignored` with its reason instead of blocking the table, field or option that wears it (on a second eval one refused table icon failed 42 fields, 20 relations and 96 rows), and a step that fails only because an earlier one did is not charged a second error. The spec runs first on an in-memory copy of the workspace, so `dryRun` returns every error at once with its path (`spaces[0].tables[1].fields[2]`) and writes nothing, and a spec with any error writes nothing either. The reply is one line: `{ok, created, existing, ignored, errors}`, where `ignored` names the config keys a field's type does not take, which `weave_add_field` drops without a word. On the 2026-10-02 eval a five-table budget workspace took 50 to 100 calls; the tool description carries a full example spec. Gate: `test/build.test.mjs`, plus the tool-count check in `test/agent-surface.test.mjs`.
- **A document write carries its text or it is refused** (Issue #572): `PUT /api/entities/<id>/doc` read `body.doc ?? body.markdown ?? ''`, so a body spelling its text under any other key wrote the empty fallback: the route answered `200 {"ok": true}` and the document was blank. An overnight fixer sent `{content, field}` and erased a 1,932-character Issue description with no signal that anything was wrong (recovered from revision history, which is what kept this recoverable). A write with neither key is now a 400 naming the two keys the route takes, and the stored document is untouched. Clearing stays an explicit write: `{"doc": ""}` and `{"markdown": ""}` still empty a document. The same refusal covers the applet route, the CLI (`weave doc set` with no `--content` and no `--file`), the MCP tool and `Weave#setDoc` / `Weave#appendDoc` themselves, which coerced `undefined` to `''` for every caller above them. The applet's error mapping also stops calling a refused write a 500. Gate: `test/doc-write-keys.test.mjs` plus an applet case in `test/applet.test.mjs`.
- **The legal pages name a contact address** (Issue #613): `/terms` and `/privacy` went out with `[Contact email]` standing in 9 places (7 in the terms, 2 in the privacy policy) and `[Address]` once, and Kyle wants the sign-up terms checkbox to link both pages to every new person. Each `[Contact email]` is now a `mailto:weave@grunion.ai` link. The privacy policy's rights sentence reads "please contact us at weave@grunion.ai." and no longer carries "or at [Entity name], [Address]". `[Entity name]` stays in all 21 places until the operator names the legal entity. Gate: `test/legal-pages.test.mjs` asserts both pages show the mailto link and neither shows `[Contact email]` or `[Address]`, that `[Entity name]` is still present, and that the text carries no em dash.
- **The release check's timeout fires on its own** (Issue #563): `createReleaseCheck` cut a hung request off with `AbortSignal.timeout`, whose timer is unref'd, so the abort landed only while something else held the event loop open. A real socket does hold it, which is why the hosted check was never affected, but `test/update-check.test.mjs` injects a fetch that just hangs, and on node 22.16 the loop drained first: five cases aborted with "Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved", twice through the retry, and both node 22.16 legs of the `tests` workflow went red while both node 24 legs passed. The cut-off is now a ref'd `setTimeout` over an `AbortController`, cleared on every path, so it does not depend on what else the process happens to be doing. Gate: `test/update-check.test.mjs`, which runs the check in a bare child process and asserts the hung request is cut off there.
