## v0.4.62, 2026-10-03

Fixed:

- [[Issue#608]] Looks broken: Entity card's top edge scrolls away; only the crumb row and title stay (Gerrit 570, landed as decb13c)
- [[Issue#609]] Looks broken: The window scrolls instead of the left nav, main panel and dock each scrolling on its own (Gerrit 569, landed as dc57480)
- [[Issue#389]] Looks broken: a formula's Display and Style sit below sixty field and function chips (Gerrit 445, landed as e2bb456)
- [[Issue#388]] Looks broken: the number display sample shows 0.25, 0.6 and 1, not the field's own values (the sparkline half) (Gerrit 444, landed as f9db16a)
- [[Issue#594]] Looks broken: a new workspace reads "workspace / workspace / General" on first load (Gerrit 562, landed as 4f5523a)
- [[Issue#605]] Looks broken: the first-run empty state says "Tables hold records" where weave says row (Gerrit 563, landed as e0481bb)
- [[Issue#435]] Slow: an empty targeted-test filename starts duplicate full suites (Gerrit 436, landed as 9f90b3a)

Shipped:

- [[Feature#216]] Email out of weave: the approved invite emails, an architect preview and a Resend sender, off until WEAVE_MAIL_KEY and WEAVE_MAIL_FROM are set (Gerrit 572 and 573, landed as 941fa77, 7585a77)
- [[Feature#235]] Rich cells: a color setting (Quiet ink default), redrawn cells, fitted column widths (Gerrit 433, landed as f244163)
- [[Feature#244]] Starter templates: Money, Work and People (Gerrit 563, landed as e0481bb)
- [[Feature#236]] Shared test service: one queue per machine and one warm browser (Gerrit 446, landed as 5a65d65)

Mail stays off on weave.grunion.ai: no Resend account, sending domain or key exists yet, and the accepted notice waits on a decision (Feature #252 keeps no account email).

### Notes

- **The entity frame holds while its body scrolls** (Issue #608): on the full page and in the dock, a scroll kept the crumb row and the title, but the card's rounded top edge and the padding above the crumb row scrolled away, and the header floated against the window edge with no frame round it. The header that leads a pane now takes the pane's top and side padding as its own ground (`--wv-pane-pad`, `--wv-pane-pad-x`), so the panel's top edge, the band above the crumb row, the crumb row and the title keep their place, and only what sits below the title scrolls under them. At rest the page lays out as before. Reading the header where it really sits showed the grid's row window two more things: an open now asks for the page past the window's leading edge only after the reader first scrolls, which keeps an open at one page as before, and the foot's "N of M loaded" note follows a page that lands outside the drawn rows instead of waiting for the next repaint. Gate: `test/entity-frame-browser.test.mjs` (full page and dock, both themes, 1440x900 and 390x844: wheel the body to its end and the card edge, header, crumb row and title keep the top they had at rest, and the band under the card's edge is still the header), plus the dock header suite reading the band at the pane's top and the crumb row at its rest position.
- **A formula's Display sits under its result** (Issue #389): Showcase > Field Types > Age trend opened a tray where about sixty chips (every field of the table, then the logic, text, number and date functions) sat between the script and the Display section, so on a 1000px window Display, Style and Sample started below the fold. The result line (`= [41,29] list`) is now followed directly by Display, Color, Style and Sample, and the chips fold behind **Fields and functions**, closed once a formula exists and open on a new one, with a hint that typing `[` offers a field and two letters offer a function. The Formula checkbox says what it does: on a formula column, "untick to freeze each row's result into plain text"; on a new field, "compute this field from the row's other fields instead of typing it". Gate: `test/formula-tray-browser.test.mjs` (new, 4 cases: a sparkline formula's Display, Style, Color and Sample inside an unscrolled 1000px tray, in light and dark, with the chips folded and reachable; a numeric formula's Display on screen and the untick hint; a new formula with the chips open and the tick hint).
- **An invite can go out by email** (Feature #216, Issue #569): with `WEAVE_MAIL_KEY` (a Resend API key) and `WEAVE_MAIL_FROM` both set, `POST /api/invites` and the Members form email the approved invite to the address typed, one `fetch` to `api.resend.com/emails` with no SDK, and answer `mailed: true`; Members then says **Emailed** in place of the link. A failed send still makes the invite: the answer carries `mailed: false` and Resend's reason in `mailError`, the server log names it without the address, and Members shows the link to copy with a toast. With either variable unset nothing is sent and the copy-the-link flow is unchanged. The accepted notice is not sent, since weave keeps no account email (Feature #252). Gate: `test/mail-send.test.mjs` and `test/invites-mail-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The invite emails exist, and an architect can preview them** (Feature #216, Issue #569): `src/mail.js` holds the two emails Kyle approved on 2026-10-03, the invite a new person gets and the notice an inviter gets once it is accepted, each as subject, preheader, html and plain text. The html inlines its light palette on every element so Gmail keeps the card, button and role chips, keeps a dark palette under `prefers-color-scheme` for Apple Mail and iOS, and shows the weave lockup as a PNG weave serves from `/brand/email-lockup-{light,dark}.png`, since Gmail strips SVG. `GET /api/mail/preview/invite` and `/api/mail/preview/accepted` render them with sample values for an architect, with `?role=` and `?theme=`. Nothing sends them yet. Gate: `test/mail.test.mjs` (copy word for word, a chip and line per role, every variable escaped, no SVG, the dark block, the preview's 401, 403 and 200).
- **The window stops scrolling; each pane scrolls on its own** (Issue #609): `#app` was `min-height: 100vh` and `#main` grew to fit its content, so a long table or record scrolled the whole document, and the workspace rail and left nav held still only through `position: sticky; height: 100vh`. The dock was a sticky box with a scroller of its own, so it scrolled alone while the main panel scrolled with the page. The shell is now a fixed frame: the document never scrolls, and the rail, the left nav, the main panel and the dock each own one scroller; a scroll that runs out at a pane's edge stops there, since the only thing it could chain to is the document. Every reader of the window's scroll now reads its pane: the grid's row window and its page fetches, the wide grid's height cut, the grid loader's placement, the doc rail's reading line, and the sticky offsets of the view header, the field headers, the Σ row, the section heads and the rail, which share one `--wv-pane-pad` term. A stuck `+ New` foot hangs a strip of the surface over the panel's bottom padding, so rows no longer show through under it. The 600px phone dock (fixed, full screen) and the nav drawer keep working. Gate: `test/pane-scroll-shell-browser.test.mjs` (a wheel over the nav, the main panel and the dock moves that pane alone in both themes; scroll chaining stops at the dock's edge; a 2,000-row grid paints its last row at the bottom of the panel; the phone panel, sheet and drawer), plus twelve suites moved from the window's scroll to the panel's.
- **Every new workspace is named "Personal Workspace"** (Issue #594): on 2026-10-03 Kyle replaced the random adjective-animal name v0.4.56 gave a fresh workspace. A fresh `weave serve`, a fresh Docker or Railway volume and `POST /api/workspaces` with no `name` now make `personal-workspace`; the next unnamed workspace on the instance is `personal-workspace-2` ("Personal Workspace 2"), then `-3`. `src/workspace-name.js` drops its adjective and animal lists, and `workspaceName()` still returns the display name, "Personal Workspace", which the page can show once Issue #592 gives the display name its own field. Nothing else moves: a file someone named still names its workspace (`--data ./other.db` makes `other`), the Worker still names a fresh Durable Object after its route, and existing workspaces keep their names, whether `workspace`, `Weave Workspace` (which takes its file's basename, as before) or a name drawn at random under v0.4.56. Gate: `test/workspace-name.test.mjs`.
- **Rich cells: a colour setting, redrawn cells and fitted column widths** (Feature #235): Kyle, 2026-09-25, on the bars, rings, heat, ratings and sparklines of Features #230 to #232: "I don't like the design of the columns or the colors." His decision the next day: put colour in the field's config, default to quiet ink, redraw the cells to the A/B/C mockups, and give the columns better widths. A rating, a number's display and a formula's display now take `color`: `ink` (Quiet ink, the default, never written down), `icon` (Color by icon) or `accent` (One accent hue). Quiet ink draws bars and rings in the text colour on a hairline track, heat as a grey tint that deepens with the value, rating icons filled in the text colour with hairline outlines for the empties, and sparklines in the secondary text colour. Color by icon draws bars and rings teal, runs heat from cool to warm with the share, fills a star amber, a heart rose and a bolt violet (any other icon takes the accent), draws the sparkline blue and win/loss green and red. One accent hue draws every graphic in the workspace accent, losses in a lighter accent. Every colour is a token with a dark twin. The engine validates the key on add, update and schema apply, and refuses anything else with the list; the schema says the colour of every field that draws a graphic, ink included; a lookup and a rollup draw in the colour of the column they read, and the chip and the card carry it. The cells are redrawn: a 6px bar with round ends on a fixed 80px track and the figure to its right in tabular figures, a 16px ring with a 2.5px round-capped stroke hugging its percent, heat as a rounded tint behind the figure, 14px rating icons 1px apart, and an 80 by 18 sparkline drawn at its own size with a dot on the newest point, 1.5px column corners and small win/loss blocks either side of a midline. A rich cell no longer repeats the Σ or ƒ its header carries. A bar, ring, heat or sparkline column opens at the width its graphic needs (a bar's track plus its widest figure, a ring or a heat tint plus its widest figure, a sparkline's 80px), never under a plain number's 88px; a width a person drags wins. A rating column keeps the width rule Issue #404 landed, measured on the new 14px icon, and a rating column dragged narrower than its icons, or past the fit cap, draws a compact `★ 7/10` instead of cutting icons off. The settings tray gains a Color picker beside Display on a rating, a number display and a sparkline: three swatches, each this field's own graphic drawn in that setting, and the Sample and the rating's default row wear the pick. The Showcase's Field Types table gains a column per setting beside the ink ones (Momentum, Reach, Warmth, Stars, Bolts, Hearts, Age line, Delta blocks), through the existing Showcase sync. Gates: `test/cell-color.test.mjs` (new, 9 cases: the list, default and storage, refusal, update and clear, inheritance by a lookup and a rollup, the chip and the card, the schema round trip, the HTTP API, and one list across the engine, the vocabulary, the dialog and the drawing), `test/cell-color-browser.test.mjs` (new, 8 cases: each setting's paints in light and dark, the shapes' sizes, the marks leaving the cells, the 10-icon width and the compact form, the tray's swatches and save in both themes, and the number and sparkline Samples), `test/cell-graphics.test.mjs` (6 new cases), `test/column-layout.test.mjs` (2 new cases, and the Issue #404 case re-measured on the 14px icon), `test/rating-browser.test.mjs` (the geometry case reads the icons past the compact form), `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs` (4 new cases), `test/seed.test.mjs` (1 new case, colours drawn from `CELL_COLORS`), `test/vocabulary.test.mjs`.
- **The sparkline Sample draws the column's own series** (Issue #388, the sparkline half): the number Sample took the column's own figures in Gerrit change 419; a formula's sparkline Sample still drew a fixed 3, 5, 4, 7 … 12 whatever the column held, so a style or a colour could not be judged against the field's data. The Sample now draws the list on the first row that holds two numbers or more, in the chosen style and colour, under a line naming that row ("Acme: 4 values, oldest first"), and each Color swatch draws the same series. A column with no list yet, and a field being created, draw an example series under "Example series. No row of this column holds a list yet." Nothing is drawn until the rows answer, so an example never flashes over a real series. With Feature #235 the number Sample wears the chosen colour as well as the format, scale and display. Gate: `test/spark-sample-browser.test.mjs` (new, 3 cases: the column's own series in the Sample and all three swatches with no example note, in light and dark; an empty column labelled as an example).
- **Three starter templates from the use cases people asked for** (Feature #244, Issue #605): onboarding step 3 and the first-run empty state now offer **Money**, **Work** and **People**, in that order, and Docs is gone (weave already has a document kind). Money is personal finance: Transactions (Date, Amount in dollars, Category, linked to an Account and a Month), Accounts, Recurring (linked to the transactions that paid it), Income (linked to a Month) and Months, where each month row rolls up **Spent** from its transactions and **Earned** from its income, and a **Net** formula subtracts one from the other. Work keeps the Tasks table (Status workflow, Due, Priority), and People keeps Companies and Contacts linked by Company. Each template is now a `weave_build` spec (Feature #253), so it builds in one call with a few sample rows dated to the month it is built in: the empty state sends one `POST /api/build`, and `POST /api/onboarding` runs the same build server side. `steps()` and its per-field REST walk are gone. A card's title is its space's name, so the card and the sidebar call it one thing. The empty state's lead line says row where it said record. Linking a transaction to its month is by hand until Feature #245. Gate: `test/starter-core.test.mjs` (each template builds; two transactions and one income linked to a month compute Spent, Earned and Net), `test/onboarding.test.mjs`, `test/onboarding-browser.test.mjs` and `test/first-run-browser.test.mjs`.
- **One test queue per machine, and one warm browser** (Feature #236): `npm test` no longer runs the suite in the calling process. It queues a job with `scripts/test-manager.mjs`, a per-user FIFO shared by every worktree, which runs one job at a time in `scripts/test.mjs`'s existing lanes and admits it only with 10 GB of free disk, 10% of memory available and a one-minute load under twice the cores; a waiting job prints the reason. The manager keeps one Playwright browser server warm, and each browser suite connects to it with its own contexts, so closing one suite cannot close another's. A raw `node --test` browser suite leases the same queue rather than launching Chromium beside it; a suite pinned to another engine (`engine: 'webkit'`) still launches its own. A job is hashed at enqueue, start and finish, and a worktree that changed during the run turns a pass red. New flags: `--targeted <file ...>` refuses an empty selection, `--affected [--base=<ref>] [--plan]` picks the files a diff can reach and says why (shared code, UI and unknown paths mean the whole suite), and `--status`, `--cancel=<id>`, `--stop` and `--timeout=<ms>` reach the manager. An admitted job times out after one hour by default, the gate's cap, and a disconnect or a dead manager reaps the job's process group and temp files. A job never admitted within `WEAVE_TEST_QUEUE_WAIT_MS` (default 30 minutes), or cut off by a manager stop, prints `# TEST MANAGER NOT ADMITTED: <reason>` and exits 75, so a gate can tell a run that never started from a red one. A raw browser suite's lease carries the admission overrides, and one process shares one counted lease across its `launch()` calls. The manager's socket directory is keyed on a hash of its source, so an older manager never serves newer code. Gate: `test/test-manager.test.mjs`, `test/test-manager-admission.test.mjs`, `test/test-selection.test.mjs`, `test/browser-manager.test.mjs`, `test/browser-manager-lease.test.mjs` and `test/test-runner.test.mjs`.
- **Workers run targeted tests; the poller owns the full gate** (Issue #435): CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and DEVELOPMENT.md told every agent to run `npm test` before each commit and to run `weave-review.sh` by hand, so parallel workers launched full suites beside the poller's gate and raced its Verified votes. The guidance now matches the gate: a worker runs the test files its change touches by name (`node scripts/test.mjs test/<name>.test.mjs`), pushes once, self-reviews and casts Code-Review +2, and the poller runs the full suite on the reviewed stack tip. Bare `node --test` is named as the trap it was: it discovers `scripts/test.mjs` as a test entry, and the runner's `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT` guard (landed with Issues #454 and #466) keeps that from starting a second suite. Documentation only; no code changes.

## v0.4.63, 2026-10-03

Fixed:

- [[Issue#614]] Looks broken: a select or state column resizes narrower than its option chip, so the chip box is cut off (Gerrit 564, landed as c8f0cbe)

### Notes

- **No select, multi-select, state or rating column is cut by a resize** (Issue #614): these columns floored at their header label only, so a State column dragged under a "Setup incomplete" chip cut the chip mid-word, and a rating dragged under its icons cut the last ones. Kyle, 2026-10-03: "make sure no part of the toggle or box can be cut off by field resize." A select or state now floors at its widest option's chip, a multi-select at its widest chip plus the +N count beside it (never the sum), and a rating at every icon up to its 320px fit ceiling, the way a date (Issue #159) and a toggle (Issue #586) already did. The chips are drawn by the cell's own renderer inside the column's own cell and measured there, so a CSS change moves the floor with it; they are measured again when an option is added, renamed or given an icon. The floor binds a drag, an Alt+arrow nudge, a double-click fit and the frozen-zone cap, and raises a stored width under it for that column only; a column with a long option now opens at that floor rather than the 124px default. A rating's floor supersedes Feature #235's "a width the reader dragged still wins" for widths under the icons. Free text still truncates with an ellipsis, and a checkbox column at its label floor already holds its whole box. Gate: `test/chip-width-browser.test.mjs` (drag, nudge, fit, an unshown and a later-added option, a stored width, free text, the checkbox, and every other column's width unchanged) and `test/column-resize.test.mjs`.

releases.description:
## v0.4.64 — 2026-10-04

Landed as 7247ca2. Fixed:

- [[Issue#573]] a change can land with no changelog fragment and nothing refuses it (Gerrit 595)
- [[Issue#464]] opening a table in WebKit raises a ResizeObserver loop error that the bug recorder files as an error (Gerrit 597)
- [[Issue#616]] End does not move the caret in a code block on the phone dock (Gerrit 598)

This release also folds every changelog fragment that landed since v0.4.63, from the sessions that landed them:

- **Agent front door** (Feature #258): the MCP server now sends a primer as `initialize.instructions` on stdio and `POST /api/mcp`. It is `src/mcp-primer.md`, under 2,048 characters (Claude Code keeps no more), and its first line says to build with one `weave_build` call, `dryRun` first; on the 2026-10-02/03 evals a primer of this kind lifted the score from 0.72 to 0.91 (Sonnet) and 0.78 to 0.94 (Opus). AGENTS.md now opens with **Using weave**: the primer verbatim, the model, every surface with how to start it, a tool map generated from `src/mcp.js` by `scripts/agent-docs.mjs`, plans with turn budgets (a build needs no `weave_vocabulary` call, at most `optionColors` and an icon query; Issue #625) and error-to-fix pairs, among them the `"Date desc"` Sort form (Issue #626); the repo map and rules moved under **Developing weave**. The README gains a **For agents** block near the top, CLAUDE.md a router line sending tool users to AGENTS.md, and llms.txt lists the quickstart first. Gate: `test/agent-front-door.test.mjs`.

- **One vocabulary call for every list** (Issue #625): `weave_vocabulary` takes `sections: ["icons", "optionColors", "formulaFunctions"]` and answers each section keyed by name; `section` takes the same list or a comma string, so REST (`?section=icons,optionColors`) and the CLI (`weave vocabulary icons,optionColors`) answer alike. A query still searches the icons section, and a comma list of queries (`"wallet, bank"`) answers as `searches`. The single-section form is unchanged. On the 2026-10-03 disclosure eval agents spent 4 to 15 calls a run on one section each.
- **The build reply shows what computed fields computed** (Issue #627): `weave_build` returns `computed`, mapping each lookup, rollup and formula the build made (`"Budget/Category.Spending"`) to the first three values the grid shows for it, dry run included. Agents had run 3 to 10 `weave_query` read-backs per build to check them.
- **Layout rides the build** (Issue #628): a table in the build spec takes `fieldOrder` (the leading columns; the rest keep their order, in the schema and the default view), `hidden` (columns to hide in the default view; the minted Chip and Card stay hidden) and `sort` (`"Amount desc, Name"` or `[{field, dir}]`). A bad name is an error with its path. Agents had set these with one `Workspace/Tables` row write each, up to ten calls. The primer and AGENTS.md say so in a line each. Gate: `test/agent-call-economy.test.mjs`.

- **The core tool list fits its budget again** (Issue #579): the `weave_add_field` description is shorter, so the core `tools/list` reads 14,465 bytes, under the 14,500 the tool-profile gate allows. Two changes that each passed alone (the build and vocabulary call economy, and the schema-write guidance) landed together at 14,536.

- **Docs match the build** (Issue #593): the README states the auth model that ships (three roles per workspace, `wv_` tokens, OpenID Connect sign-in, authentication off until `weave workspace require-auth`) in "What weave is not", the FAQ and Security, in place of "no authentication". `docs/PARITY.md` is re-scored against v0.4.63 (81.5%: the board and list views score ❌, filtering and permissions move up) and the comparison pages, `docs/README.md` and `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` drop the stale 23-tool and 17-function counts. Gate: `test/docs-drift.test.mjs` holds every tool count in the docs to `src/mcp.js`, recomputes the PARITY score from its own table and refuses "no authentication" in any doc.
- **The board view leaves its last surfaces** (Issue #438): `weave_vocabulary` lists `table` as the only view kind, and the `weave_views` description, `weave help`, the Handbook field and saved-view guides and the Fibery comparison stop offering a board. `createView` refuses `view: 'board'` with an error naming the kinds weave draws. Gate: `test/docs-drift.test.mjs` scans the vocabulary, every MCP tool, the Handbook, the MCP primer, `weave help`, AGENTS.md and llms.txt.

- **A screencast flash now carries its own three frames** (Feature #259): `scripts/flicker-sweep.mjs` picked the frames around a `frame` finding by its timestamp, so the file named "after" was the flash itself and "before" and "during" were the same frame. `evidenceFrames()` in `test/lib/flicker.mjs` takes the A, B, A frames by index for a screencast flash and keeps the timestamp window for DOM findings. Gate: `test/flicker-core.test.mjs`.

- **A flicker probe, nine journeys, a nightly sweep and a ratchet** (Feature #259, harness routine `weave-flicker`): `test/lib/flicker.mjs` watches a page for what the reader saw and should not have (a node painted for a beat and gone, a list painted empty and refilled, a class that flipped and flipped back, content that jumped with no input) and reads the screencast for A, B, A frames; swaps that answer a keystroke or a press, identical redraws and zero-size live regions are not counted. `scripts/flicker-sweep.mjs` walks `test/lib/journeys.mjs` three times and keeps what two runs saw, with the frames around each sighting. `test/flicker-gate-browser.test.mjs` walks every journey in the gate and fails when one cannot finish or when a flicker listed in `test/flicker-fixed.json` comes back. Gates: `test/flicker-core.test.mjs`, `test/flicker-probe-browser.test.mjs`.

- **A code change that names its row ships the changelog fragment it owes** (Issue #573): `test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs` guarded one direction, that a commit adding lines to CHANGELOG.md also bumps the version, and nothing asked for the fragment itself. Change 527 fixed Issue #551 and merged as `e85ada8` with nine files and none under `changelog.d/`, on a `Verified +1`, and that fix reached the v0.4.54 notes only because the bullet was written by hand. `fragmentGuard` in `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` now refuses a commit that changes `src/`, `public/`, `bin/` or `scripts/` and names `(Issue #N)` or `(Feature #N)` in its subject while adding no fragment; a refactor or docs-only change opts out with a `No-changelog: <reason>` trailer, and a release commit, which bumps the version and deletes the fragments it folded, stays exempt.

- **The loading rope keeps moving while the page is busy** (Issue #390): the rope animated `stroke-dashoffset` with SMIL, which Chrome and Safari run on the main thread, so it froze for every long task during boot or a slow route and then jumped. The app now shows the rope at rest through windows that move by `transform` only, which the browser runs on the compositor. Each end of the old dash is an anchor with a round cap, riding the dash's end frame by frame on the same 2000 ms cycle and easing, and the unweave still ends on the two end dots, so the rope looks as it did. `test/page-loader-browser.test.mjs` forces a 250 ms long task and requires fresh frames inside it.

- **Attachments in a query select** (Issue #622): `weave_query` with a `select` naming an attachments field returned `(missing)` for every row, even when the file was there, because the select path resolved the value without its row. It now names the file the way the record does, and still marks a file whose bytes are gone as `name (missing)`.
- **Imports name files without bytes** (Issue #462): `importJSON` now returns `{ files, missing }`, listing every attachment that arrived as a name with no bytes, with a `warning` when any did. `weave_import_json`, `POST /api/import` and `weave import` all return it. The MCP `weave_export_json` dump leaves the bytes out by design (Issue #121), so importing it into a fresh data directory used to produce the Issue #250 rows in silence. A dump imported back where its bytes already sit reports nothing missing.

- **Row writes refuse a missing `values` by name** (Issue #600): `weave_update_entity` sent without `values`, or with `fields` where `values` belongs, used to throw a raw `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. It now answers `values is required: a map of field name to value` and names each key the tool does not take (`unknown 'fields', 'db'`). `weave_create_entity` refuses an unknown key the same way, so `{db, fields: {...}}` no longer leaves an empty row behind. Gate: `test/mcp-refusals.test.mjs`.
- **A Sort cell takes `-Date` and JSON** (Issue #626): a `Sort` written on a `Workspace/Views` or `Workspace/Tables` row as `-Date`, `+Date`, `[{"field":"Date","dir":"desc"}]` (as text or a list) or `["-Date"]` now lands, and the row reads back as `Date desc`. A Sort naming a field the table lacks, or JSON that does not parse, is refused with `Sort reads 'Field asc|desc, Field2 asc|desc', e.g. 'Date desc'`. The primer and the AGENTS.md pitfall table say so. Gate: `test/mcp-refusals.test.mjs`, `test/agent-front-door.test.mjs`.

- **A column of amounts ends on one right edge** (Issues #574, #575): a number cell whose costume printed its raw text (44.22 at two decimals) rested as the bare input, which aligned left while 44.20 and 50.00 sat right; the input now aligns right in a number column. Formula and rollup cells holding a number take the same right alignment. A separator alone keeps the figure's own decimals (44.22 read 44). An empty Description, or any document column with nothing in its loaded rows, opens at the 180px text width instead of the 280px long-text width, the widest default on the grid. Gate: `test/number-align-browser.test.mjs`.

- **Onboarding tests walk every path** (Feature #248): the API and browser suites now run the full matrix, keeping or editing the workspace name and then starting empty or taking each starter (Money, Work, People), plus Skip setup and Esc on each of the three steps. Each path checks the final name, exactly the starter's tables, field types, relation inverses and sample rows, the table it opens on, and that the welcome never asks again. Added cases for a cleared or unusable name, a starter whose space already exists, and an unknown starter. Skip or Esc on the last step drops a name confirmed on step 2; the two cases pin that and name Issue #615. Tests only; no code changes.

- **End reaches the end of a code line on the phone dock** (Issue #616): the phone dock sheet no longer sets `overscroll-behavior: contain`. In Chromium that property on the scroll container stops End from moving the caret inside a document's code block, so the caret stayed at the `CODE` element's offset 0 and typed text landed at the start of the line instead of its end (` // hiconst x = 1;` for `const x = 1;`). `#main` and the desktop dock already leave the property off for the same reason (Issue #609), and since #609 the document no longer scrolls, so the sheet's scroll has nothing left to chain into. Gate: a 390x844 dock case in `test/code-raw-toggle-browser.test.mjs`.

- **The release fold refuses an empty changelog fragment** (Issue #629): `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` skipped a fragment whose text trimmed to nothing and deleted the file anyway, so that change would ship with no line in CHANGELOG.md or its GitHub Release. The fold now stops, names the empty file, and writes and deletes nothing. `test/changelog-fragments.test.mjs` fails a commit whose fragment is not a bullet with text.
- **A changelog fragment cannot ship work under an open security finding's number** (Issue #568): `changelog.d/mcp-inject-harness-499.md` shipped the MCP injection measurement harness in v0.4.53 under #499, the row for security finding S-22, which stays Open until its fix lands. The harness now has its own row, Feature #260, and `scripts/export-development.mjs` refuses to export a release while any fragment cites a security finding that is not Fixed. Correction to the v0.4.53 notes: the harness entry is Feature #260, not #499.
- **/api/health never reports a latest release older than the running version** (Issue #606): `update-check.json` sits beside the data on the volume, so after an upgrade the new build read the old build's answer and reported it for up to a day (weave.grunion.ai on 2026-10-03: version 0.4.56, latestRelease 0.4.54). The cache now records the version that wrote it, a different version asks GitHub again at boot, and an answer older than the running version reports the running version.
- **Correction to the v0.4.46 notes** (Issue #565): v0.4.46 was never tagged or published as a GitHub Release, but its Release row claimed that a 10-icon rating opened unclipped and that a rating column dragged narrower than its icons drew a compact `★ 7/10`. The fitted rating width shipped in v0.4.53 (Issue #404) and the compact form in v0.4.62 (Feature #235). Since v0.4.63 (Issue #614) a drag stops at the last icon, so only a rating whose icons pass the 320px fit cap draws the compact form.

- **Opening a table in Safari no longer records an error** (Issue #464): the grid's fit observer toggled `wv-grid-scroll` on the wrap it watches, and that class caps the wrap's height, so the callback resized what it observed and WebKit raised a window `error`, "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.", on every table a Safari reader opened. The in-app recorder listens on `error`, so a report filed from Safari counted an error the reader never caused. The observer's body now runs in the next frame, which also collapses a first draw's repeat callbacks into one pass. Gate: `test/resize-loop-browser.test.mjs` opens a grid wider than its card in WebKit and resizes the window, and reads back the window errors the recorder would file.

- **A schema write says what is still open and what looks wrong** (Issues #579, #581, #578, #582, #574): `weave_add_field`, `weave_update_field`, `weave_create_table` and `weave_create_space` answer, on MCP, REST and the CLI, with `next[]` and `hints[]` from the new `src/field-hints.js`. `next[]` lists the settings the type still takes, one layer at a time: a new number names format (currency, percent, compact), unit and display; choosing currency opens the code and accounting, choosing a display opens the scale and colour. `hints[]` names a likely slip with its fix: a text column named like a table (link it with the text-to-relation conversion), a money-named number with no currency, a text column named like a figure, select options all slate, status options or workflow states with no icons, a config key the type does not take (it was dropped without a word before), a space or table named after its workspace, and a table or space with no icon. Hints never block a write or change what is stored; the compact MCP reply keeps both lists, and the `weave_add_field` description says so and names the number costume.

- **Text becomes a relation** (Issue #582): `weave_update_field {type: "relation", config: {targetDb}}` converts a text column in place, so an agent that typed an account as text beside an Account table can link it without rebuilding. Each value links to the target row of that name (exact, then case-folded; a figure is never read as a public id), a value no row carries is refused by name unless `createMissing: true` makes the row, and a many-to-many conversion splits on commas. The field keeps its id, width and description, the target gains the inverse, and the change rolls back with its values like any other type change. The lane is the API's: the field tray has no target picker, so `TYPE_MIGRATIONS` and its UI mirror are unchanged.

- **A where compares a formatted number by its number** (Issue #617): `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=` and `in` read the stored figure of a number field, a number formula or a number across a relation, whatever its format, so `["Money", ">", 5000]` on a currency column painted `$12,000.00` matches that row in the engine, REST and `weave_query`. `contains`, `is-empty` and `not-empty` still read the painted text. Gate: `test/where-number-format.test.mjs`.
- **Deleting a row by its `Table#N` reference** (Issue #597): `deleteEntity`, `weave_delete_entity` and `DELETE /api/entities/<ref>` resolve the reference once and use the row's id after that. Before, a soft delete by reference trashed the row and then answered `not found`, and a hard delete answered `purged: true` with the row still in the table; both now answer the row they acted on, by id. A trashed row also answers its reference, so a second delete, a read and a restore by reference find it. Gate: `test/delete-by-ref.test.mjs`.

- **Workspace display names and case-blind slugs** (Issues #592, #599): a workspace now carries a title a person reads beside the slug its URL answers at. Renaming to "Personal finance" (REST `PATCH /api/workspace`, `weave_workspace action:update`, the CLI, the onboarding welcome) keeps that text as `title` and moves the workspace to `/w/personal-finance/`, where the old rule refused anything but letters, digits, `-` and `_`. A name with nothing usable left is refused with the rule spelled out. Slugs are case-blind, like Slack, Notion and GitHub: `/w/ACME/` opens `acme`, and creating or renaming to `Acme` while `acme` exists answers 409 instead of making a second workspace file on a case-sensitive volume. Existing workspace files keep their names and their mixed-case slugs still resolve. `weave_workspace` over HTTP now renames through the hub as REST does, so the new slug resolves at once and a held one is refused. Gate: `test/workspace-slug.test.mjs`.

## v0.4.65 — Oct 5, 2026

Landed as a438721. Fixed:

- [[Issue#452]] Looks broken: left nav new space should always flow at the bottom (Gerrit 601)
- [[Issue#451]] Looks broken: main panel very point scrolls when I'm trying to scroll the left nav. (Gerrit 600)

- **+ New space holds the sidebar's bottom edge** (Issue #452): the button sat in the left nav's own scrolling flow, under the space list, so a workspace with enough spaces pushed it out of sight. Kyle filed it from the uno home at 1470x794, where the button's top measured 1028px in a 794px window and only a scroll to the nav's end brought it back. It now leads the pinned strip at the sidebar's foot, above the records line and the instance chip, and the name input it opens is pinned with it. Gate: `test/pane-scroll-shell-browser.test.mjs` fills the nav past a 794px window and reads the button's rect in both themes, with the nav unscrolled and at its end.

- **A wheel past the left nav's end moves nothing** (Issue #451): Kyle reported the main panel scrolling while he scrolled the left nav. The symptom was already gone on main, fixed on its way past by Issue #609 (`dc57480`, v0.4.62), which made the app shell a fixed frame and put `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the sidebar. Nothing pinned it, so this release carries the regression test. Gate: `test/pane-scroll-shell-browser.test.mjs` wheels 800px past the nav's end and requires the document and the main panel to stay where they were, and reads `overscroll-behavior-y` in all three poses the nav takes.

Cut by the overnight weave fixer, fire of 2026-10-05, session 36486699.

## v0.4.66 — Oct 5, 2026

Landed as b9fd045 (Gerrit 607 and 608).

Ships:

- [[Feature#261]] Use Template: a template space copies its schema into another workspace (Gerrit 603)
- [[Feature#262]] Template exercise: every template's tables, fields and relations are exercised in suite and against live instance (Gerrit 605)
- [[Feature#263]] Remove share QR codes (Gerrit 607)

Fixed:

- [[Issue#643]] Wrong data: a lookup of a relation field shows the target row's uuid, not its name (Gerrit 604)
- [[Issue#644]] Error: template exercise rerun in the same minute is refused, the copy's name is in the trash (Gerrit 606)
- [[Issue#598]] Wrong data: a lookup of a select field shows the option id, not the option name (Gerrit 590)
- [[Issue#576]] Wrong data: a date formula field ignores its year, month and day grain (Gerrit 590)
- [[Issue#620]] Wrong data: a sparkline Sample says no row holds a list when the first list sits past row 50 (Gerrit 590)

- **A lookup of a select shows the option's name** (Issue #598): a lookup of a select, a multiselect or a workflow reads `Credit card` where it read the stored id `credit-card`, in `readEntity` fields, query rows, `select`, `where` and `weave_get_entity`; `raw` keeps the ids. Gate: `test/lookup-option-name.test.mjs`.
- **A date formula keeps its grain** (Issue #576): a formula made over the Date tile carries the date's grain and style (`grain`, `format`, `time`, `clock`, `zone`, `pad`), and the column prints it, so Date with Year and Day unticked plus Formula shows `Aug`, where it showed `2026-08-15`. The grain is the opt-in and is written even when it is the full year·month·day; a formula without one keeps its raw ISO. `addField`, `updateField` (which moves a formula between the date and number costumes), type changes, `describeSchema`, `applySchema` and the field tray all carry it, and the tray reopens a date formula on the Date tile with its grain controls under the script. Gates: `test/date-grain.test.mjs`, `test/field-dialog-core.test.mjs`, `test/formula-builder-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The sparkline Sample finds a list past row 50** (Issue #620): the Sample asks for the rows whose value is not empty, where it read the first 50 rows and said no row held a list when the first one sat further down. Gate: `test/spark-sample-browser.test.mjs`.

- **A lookup of a relation shows the far row's chip** (Issue #643): a lookup whose target field is a relation, such as CRM/Activities.Company reading the contact's Company, answered the company's uuid list in `fields`, the grid, the entity page, CSV and MCP. It now carries the relation's shape, `{id, publicId, name, db}` with the row's chip, and a list of them when either hop is to-many, each far row once; `relations: 'chip'` sends the summary once in `chips` and the grid grafts it back. The grid and the entity page draw the same chip the relation column draws, `select`, `where`, formulas and CSV read the name, and `raw` keeps the ids. A template copied with Use Template keeps it. The Handbook's lookup page says so, and no longer says a to-many lookup takes the first match. Gates: `test/lookup-relation-chip.test.mjs`, `test/lookup-relation-chip-browser.test.mjs`, `test/use-template.test.mjs`.

- **The Share dialog drops its QR code** (Feature #263): sharing a view opens a dialog with the link, already copied to the clipboard, and the read-only note. The QR code that Feature #50 drew beside the link is gone, and so is the vendored `lean-qr` module (`public/vendor/lean-qr.mjs`, its module script in `index.html` and its `security/vendor.lock.json` entry), so the shell loads one fewer asset. The server still sends `.mjs` files as JavaScript. Gate: `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.

- **Every template is exercised, in the suite and live** (Feature #262): each table of the CRM template (kept as `test/fixtures/templates/crm.json`, refreshed from a running weave by `scripts/template-fixture.mjs`) and of the three starters gets a row that sets every field and reads it back, links and unlinks every relation from both ends, checks each lookup, rollup and formula, and is trashed and restored; each template is then used into a `test` workspace and its copy passes the same steps. `node scripts/template-exercise.mjs --base http://127.0.0.1:4400 --from weave --into test` runs it over HTTP against a live instance, hard-deletes every row it made, soft-deletes its copy and exits 1 on a failure. Gate: `test/template-exercise.test.mjs`.

- **The live template exercise reruns cleanly** (Issue #644): a second run of `scripts/template-exercise.mjs` in the same minute was refused with a 409, because the copy was named to the minute and soft-deleted, so its name sat in the `test` workspace's trash. The copy is now named to the second plus a four-hex suffix and is purged at the end of a run and on failure, so a run leaves nothing in `test`; `--keep` leaves the copy live for a look. Gate: `test/template-exercise.test.mjs`.

- **Use Template** (Feature #261): any space can be a template, marked by the **Template** box on its Workspace/Spaces row or `template: true` on `weave_update_space`, `weave space update --template true` and `PATCH /api/spaces/:space`. A template space's page shows **Use template**, whose dialog copies the space's schema, never its rows, into another workspace of the hub under a name you choose: tables, fields and their config, option colours and icons, workflow states, views, widths, field order, hidden fields, filters, sorting, the term, the icons and the space rollups over its tables. A relation to a table outside the space stays behind and the answer names it under `skipped`, with every lookup, rollup and formula that reads through it. A name the target already holds is refused (409), and building in a workspace needs an architect there (403). The engine verb is `useTemplate(space, target, { name })` over the pure `templateDoc()`, and `applySchema` takes `partial: true` so a one-space document leaves the target's other spaces and space rollups alone. Doors: `GET /api/templates` and `POST /api/spaces/:space/use {workspace, name?}`, `weave template list` and `weave template use <space> --into <other.db> [--name N]`, and the MCP tools `weave_template_list` and `weave_template_use` (HTTP only; a stdio server holds one workspace), the `template.list` and `template.apply` verbs Feature #244 still owed. Gates: `test/use-template.test.mjs` (a source space wearing every costume, copied into a fresh workspace, describes exactly as its `templateDoc`), `test/use-template-routes.test.mjs`, `test/use-template-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A schema document applies whole into a fresh workspace** (Issues #639, #640, #641, #642): `applySchema` creates a new table's relations, lookups, rollups and formulas after every table in the document exists, where it used to stop at the first relation with "Use addRelation() to create relation fields"; it reads a relation's cardinality from both ends, so many-to-many and one-to-one stay what they were; it keeps select option icons on a create and through an options edit; and it applies `bodyBlocks`, the entity page's block order. Gate: `test/schema-roundtrip.test.mjs`.

Cut by Claude (harness session, Opus 5.5) with Feature #263, 2026-10-05.

## v0.4.67 — Oct 5, 2026

Landed as 2b46e4a (Gerrit 633, 634, 635) on top of the crumb and cleanup changes. Ships:

- [[Feature#249]] Workflows table is the automation control panel: the engine slice (Gerrit 633)

Fixed:

- [[Issue#674]] engine half: an automation's writes carry workflow:<row id> (Gerrit 634); the chip is the UI half
- [[Issue#676]] {{Today}} prints in the workspace date format (Gerrit 635)
- [[Issue#585]]

- **A long crumb folds its middle instead of hiding the row you are on** (Issues #668, #672): on live :4400 the dock's crumb held 743px of text in a 283px box, and the one-line `text-overflow: ellipsis` cut the right end, which is where the current row sits. Ancestor crumbs now cap at about 17 characters with their own ellipsis, and when the trail still overflows, the middle folds into one "…" button (lucide `ellipsis`) whose menu lists the hidden crumbs (icon, `#id`, Name); choosing one goes there. The first crumb and the last two always show, the fold follows the box on every resize, and the current crumb never shrinks below its icon and `#id`. The full page keeps workspace › space › table and the first row in front. `MAX_TRAIL = 4` is gone from `pushTrail`: a fifth hop used to drop the oldest with no sign, and the fold menu now carries a long trail. `foldPlan` in `public/breadcrumbs.js` is the pure choice; tests in `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` and `test/crumb-fold-browser.test.mjs`.
- **Every crumb wears its icon, and the current crumb names the row** (Issues #669, #673): the workspace crumb shows the workspace's mark as the rail draws it, space and table crumbs show the icons the sidebar draws, and a row crumb shows its table's icon, a muted monospace `#id` and the Name, on the table page, the entity page and in the dock. The current crumb used to print only `#54 ⧉`, the ⧉ copy glyph set in the same text run; it is now the row's icon, `#id` and full Name in bold, and copy-link is an icon button (lucide `link`, same title and behaviour) that shows on hover or focus. Row crumbs no longer have table crumbs between them: the icon carries a hop into another table and the tooltip names it. The dock's crumb starts at the row, since the table panel beside it already names the table. One renderer (`crumbPath` in `public/app.js`) draws every crumb row; `entityCrumbs` and `dockCrumbs` in `public/breadcrumbs.js` return the crumb model. Tests: `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` (crumb model), `test/crumb-icons-browser.test.mjs` (icons at every level on three surfaces, the current crumb, the dock head).
- **One trail for the dock and the full page, with Back and Forward** (Issues #670, #671): expanding a docked row rebuilt the full page's crumb from scratch (workspace › space › table › row), dropping the hops the dock had taken, and the dock had a Back arrow with no Forward. One click history (`crumbNav`, rules in `public/breadcrumbs.js`: `navOpen`, `navHop`, `navBack`, `navForward`, `navPath`) now drives both poses: expand and collapse keep the path, and a link followed from the entity page extends it. Back and Forward sit together at the left of the crumb row in the dock and on the entity page; they replay the click order, while the crumb keeps its cut-back on a revisit (crumbs show place, arrows show time). A new hop after Back drops the forward leg, Esc steps back until the first row and then closes the dock, and closing the dock or the page ends the journey. Browser Back still skips rows opened in the dock (Issue #267 stays open). Tests in `test/breadcrumbs.test.mjs` and `test/crumb-nav-browser.test.mjs`.
- **Crumb text and the crumb row's buttons share one vertical centre** (Issue #585): `.crumb-actions` carries `wv-toolbar` for its button styling, and that class's 16px `margin-bottom` made the actions box 28px of buttons plus 16px of margin, so the row centred a 44px box and the buttons sat 8px above the breadcrumb text on the entity page, in the dock and on the table page. The crumb row now resets that margin, and `.view-header .crumb` carries the gap to the title row (12px). `test/crumb-row-centre-browser.test.mjs` checks each button on the path's line is within 2px of the path's centre on all three surfaces.
- **`weave service promote` and `weave rehearse` are gone** (Issue #649): nothing called them once the deploy watcher began updating the `:4400` checkout itself, so `src/rehearse.js`, `parseTap` and `promoteVerdict` go with them. The amber "behind main" toast now says "Run git pull, then restart weave." instead of naming promote, which failed on any clone without a `gerrit` remote (Issue #458).
- **Three shipped design-study mockups leave the repo** (Issue #645): `docs/mockups/table-grid-keymaps.html`, `table-bulk-select.html` and `formula-builder.html` are gone, along with `test/grid-patterns.test.mjs`, which ran the keymap study's unshipped NOW and EDGE branches. The shipped keymap stays pinned by `test/grid-keymap.test.mjs`, and git history keeps the studies. About 1,950 lines.
- **One HTML escaper per character set, one invite URL** (Issue #647): `src/markdown.js` exports the server's `escapeHtml` for `& < > "`, which `src/routes.js` (the sign-in wall and the shared-view page) and `src/auth-page.js` now use instead of their own copies. `src/mail.js` exports the five-character `esc` (adds `'`), which `src/applet.js` uses. The OIDC invite link is built by `inviteUrl(origin, code)` in `src/engine.js` for the route, the MCP `weave_accounts` tool and the CLI. `createAccount` and `verifyToken` hash through the engine's own `#hash`, and the unread `ACTIVE` and `COSTUME_MONTHS` constants are gone. No output changes.
- **Test suite** (Issue #648): helpers copied across thirty suites (route client, small workspaces, the test-manager harness, the door C server) live once in `test/lib/fixtures.mjs` and `test/lib/idp.mjs`; the KaTeX and Vditor version pins and the dock page-shell grep that other suites already hold are gone; and the runner puts a suite in the browser lane only when it imports the harness, so `test/test-selection.test.mjs` and `test/browser-harness.test.mjs` run in the unit lane.
- `{{Today}}` in an automation's text prints in the workspace date format, the costume every date cell wears ("Oct 6, 2026"), instead of 2026-10-06; `{{Today:iso}}` keeps the ISO form for scripts, and date fields in templates keep wearing their own format (Issue #676).
- **Dead UI code is gone** (Issue #646): `public/field-dialog-core.js` drops `serializeDefinition`, `parseDefinition` and `ratingDefaultClick`, which only tests called once the field dialog lost its JSON code pane. `public/style.css` drops 38 rules and 3 selectors for classes no code emits, and six selectors split across two rules each now live in one rule with the same computed style. `public/app.js` reads a file as base64 through one `fileBase64` helper (attachments, document uploads, the workspace logo) and no longer writes the unread `data-theme` attribute. Two `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` cases that repeated `test/asset-cache.test.mjs` and `test/security/vendor-lock.test.mjs` are removed. No behaviour changes.
- A row an automation changed names the automation, not the person (Issue #674): writes made inside a run carry the actor `workflow:<Workflows row id>` in their activity entries and the row's Modified By, and the `automation-ran` entry keeps the person whose write fired the rule and names the row in `detail.workflow`.
- Automations are Workspace/Workflows rows (Feature #249): the row's Script holds the rule as JSON (`{table, trigger, actions}`, with names), On is the user's switch and gates every fire, State is computed setup (`Setup incomplete` / `Ready`, and a Setup incomplete row refuses to be switched On), and Health (`Healthy` / `Warning` / `Failed` / `No runs`, with Health Reason) and Last Run are stamped on every fire. A rule whose setup breaks while On stays On, is skipped and reads Failed with the reason. Existing rules move onto rows on open, adopting a hand-made row with the same Name on the same table. REST, MCP and the CLI keep their automation verbs.

## v0.4.68, Oct 6, 2026

Cut on 1074c48: Gerrit 644 (the actor chips and automation pulses), the Issue #685 fix, and every change that landed beside them since v0.4.67. Ships:

- [[Feature#265]] Automation changes animate in the open grid and row (Gerrit 644)
- [[Feature#264]] Rich link previews (Gerrit 629)
- [[Feature#266]] Attachments preview, size and fit (Gerrit 637)

Fixed:

- [[Issue#675]] Created By and Modified By are person chips; no token id (Gerrit 644)
- [[Issue#674]] page half: workflow:<id> draws as the Workflows row's chip (Gerrit 644)
- [[Issue#685]] the automation chip opens its row at the root from a member workspace

Issue #661 (no inline comments) landed for src/, bin/, scripts/ and test/; public/ follows.

- **An attachments field says how the record shows its files** (Feature #266; Kyle, 2026-10-05): three config keys on the field, through `normalizeSelfContainedConfig`, the field tray, `describeSchema` and `applySchema`. `preview` is `link` (chips), `inline` (a contact sheet of the files, or the one file in its viewer), `auto` (pictures in the sheet, the rest as chips) or `cover` (the picture above the record; single-file fields only); unset follows the field, `auto` for many and `inline` for one. `size` (`small`, `medium`, `large`) is the sheet's cell and the viewer's height; `fit` is `trim` (the whole file, the cell trimmed to its shape) or `fill` (uniform cells, the file cropped). Nothing is stretched. A sheet cell opens the fullscreen viewer, which gained ← → between a field's files and a sandbox for HTML. A single-file field shows its file in place with no click: an image, a PDF or plain text in a frame, an HTML upload live under the new `GET /api/files/:id?view`, served `text/html` only under `HTML_VIEW_POLICY` (sandboxed with scripts, never same-origin, nothing remote) and framed with the same sandbox; the bare route still downloads it (Issue #483 holds). Gates: `test/attachments-preview.test.mjs`, `test/attachments-preview-browser.test.mjs`.
- **Created By and Modified By are chips** (Issue #675): a person shows as their name on an initial, and a write through an MCP client adds a quiet "via MCP". The client's id ("kyle via VMH4hSRpVOhCwUno") no longer reaches the grid, the entity page, the activity pane, the Activity table or a document's history.
- **An automation's write names the automation** (Issue #674, the page half): an actor of `workflow:<id>` draws as that Workflows row's chip, with the workflow icon, and opens the row.
- **Automations animate where you are looking** (Feature #265): when a write you make fires a rule, each cell the rule changed lights up and fades over a second, in the order the rule wrote them, with Modified By last; one toast names the rule and the row ("Close out on Done ran on #3") and opens the Workflows row. Reduced motion keeps the chip and the toast and drops the pulse. Only the tab that made the write animates: weave has no live channel to other tabs yet.
- **Comment authors and Health say who and why**: a comment an automation wrote (author `workflow:<id>`, Issue #684) shows the rule's chip, and an older comment signed "automation" shows a neutral Automation label. A Workflows row's Health cell, in the grid and on the row's page, shows its Health Reason on hover, so a rule that is on but broken says why.
- **The automation chip opens its row from a member workspace** (Issue #685): in a workspace other than the root, the Modified By chip linked to the Workflows row inside that workspace, whose page failed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'systemFields')". It now links to the root, where the Workflows registry lives.
- **Each brand file lives in one folder** (Issue #651): `node brand/build-logos.mjs` writes the files the app serves (`weave-mark-dark.svg`, `weave-mark-light.svg`, `weave-favicon.svg`, `weave-loader-rope.html`) straight into `public/brand/`, and `brand/render-png.mjs` renders `favicon-32.png` there. Their copies in `brand/assets/` are gone, along with `favicon.ico`. `weave-mark-white.svg` and both lockups, which nothing serves, now live only in `brand/assets/`. `test/page-loader.test.mjs` checks the served files against the generator and refuses a file kept in both folders.
- **The crumb's fold menu stays inside the window** (Issue #677): in a dock against the window's right edge, the "…" menu opened at the button's left and its full row Names ran past the screen. It now shifts left by whatever would overflow. `test/crumb-fold-browser.test.mjs` checks the menu's box with a 420px dock in a 1200px window.
- **A field change's Activity page reads as the change, not as JSON** (Issue #554): recolouring one option printed the field's whole definition twice as one 319-character JSON line each, with the one difference (`"hue":"teal"` against `"hue":"green"`) buried in the fourth wrapped line. The page now shows each changed setting in the field's own terms: an option or a workflow state as its chip before and after, marked Added, Removed, Renamed, Recoloured, Icon changed, Category changed or Moved, with the rest counted as "3 unchanged"; a formula as its text with the inserted and deleted words marked; name, type, format, default (a select default by option name) and the other settings as plain before and after values. The two definitions sit folded under **Show definitions**, pretty-printed with a two-space indent, and Roll back stays where it was. The diff is `public/field-diff-core.js`, pure and tested in node (`test/field-diff-core.test.mjs`); `test/field-config-undo-browser.test.mjs` checks a recolour reads as the option's two chips in both themes.
- **One formatter per costume and one tokenization per formula** (Issues #211, #234, #278): three of Kyle's slow reports on uno's Sessions table ("trouble loading this page", "very slow", "extremely slow") time `POST /api/markdown` at 7.7 to 13.7 s and `GET /stats` at 13.1 s. Re-measured on a synthetic uno (Sessions at 2,500 and 8,000 rows, 23 fields with relations, a lookup, formulas, rollups, a currency and an instant date, seven space rollups, a table description with twelve mentions, five sibling workspaces with trashed rows), the description renders in 20 to 130 ms on its own and `GET /api/workspaces?deleted=1` answers in 2 to 5 ms. Neither was slow. Node serves one request at a time and a POST's body arrives a tick after its headers, so the markdown POST waited behind whichever synchronous read got in first: in the second report it ends 12 ms before `/stats` does. The reads ahead of it spent their time dressing values. Every currency value built an `Intl.NumberFormat`, every instant date two `Intl.DateTimeFormat`s (tens of microseconds each, against under one to format with), and every formula read tokenized its expression again. Issue #235 stopped dressing values nobody reads; this keeps what the dressing that remains builds. The engine keeps one `Intl.NumberFormat` per set of options, `public/date-grain.js` one `Intl.DateTimeFormat` per zone for each of its two uses (keyed on the zone Intl resolves the spelling to, so `america/new_york` and `America/New_York` share one, and each cache clears at 128 entries, because the reader's zone comes off the `X-Weave-Zone` header and a client could otherwise grow it one spelling at a time), and `src/formula.js` the tokens of each expression (up to a thousand texts). A bad currency code or zone is never kept and throws every time, as before, and every dressed string and formula answer is unchanged. Engine medians at 2,500 and 8,000 rows, on 812f250, then with Issue #235, then with this: `tableStats` 885 and 2,965 ms, 89 and 326 ms, 58 and 256 ms; one grid page of 200 rows 103 and 139 ms, 112 and 152 ms, 28 and 62 ms. The page open over HTTP (query, workspaces, schema, markdown and stats in flight together, which is the wait the description sees) took 1,112 and 3,660 ms, then 363 and 656 ms, and now 270 and 534 ms. The first two reports' unpaged query and full trash read were already cut by Issues #271 and #270. Gates: `test/formatter-reuse.test.mjs` ("number costumes read exactly as before, whichever order the configs are dressed in", "instant and fixed-zone dates read exactly as before, zone by zone and across a DST edge", "a bad currency or zone still fails the way it did: refused at definition, never cached", "the stats report and a page of rows build a fixed number of formatters, not one per value", which counted 118 and 2,200 `NumberFormat`s and 601 `DateTimeFormat`s before, "a formula read on many rows answers each row from its own values, and a broken one stays broken", and "a zone spelled many ways keeps one formatter, and distinct zones never grow the caches past the cap", which kept 1,024 formatters for one zone spelled 3,000 ways before).
- **The sidebar's fixed rows read Workflows, Activity, Trash** (Issue #561): the three system rows under the spaces now run Workflows first, then Activity, then Trash, instead of Activity, Trash, Workflows. The Handbook's "System rows in the sidebar" guide states the new order. Tests in `test/system-tables-nav.test.mjs` and `test/system-tables-nav-browser.test.mjs`.
- **The corner trash icon is gone; Trash in the sidebar holds trashed workspaces too** (Issue #562): Trash became a row in the left nav, which made the trash glyph in the bottom-right corner redundant. The glyph and its `#hub-foot` row are removed. Deleted workspaces, which only that glyph could restore, now appear on the Trash page under a Workspaces card with a Restore each; the delete dialog says "Trash in the sidebar". The bug button keeps its place. Tests in `test/workspace-delete-browser.test.mjs`, `test/toast-lane-browser.test.mjs` and `test/bug-report.test.mjs`.
- **No inline comments** (Issue #661): weave's own code carries no `//`, `/* */` or `<!-- -->` comments. 5,619 came out of `src/`, `bin/`, `scripts/` and `test/` with no code change (every stripped file parses to the same syntax tree), and `test/no-inline-comments.test.mjs` fails on any new one. The why behind a change lives in its commit message and its Issue or Feature row.
- **A pasted permalink unfurls** (Feature #264): `/w/<ws>/e/<id>` (and `Table#n`) answers 200 with the app shell and a server-rendered head instead of a bare 302. Slack, Messages and email show the workspace logo or the weave mark, `Issue #287 · <name>` as the title, the path `weave › Development › Issue` and the state and first fields (`Status Fixed · Severity Medium · Symptom Wrong data`), with Slack's `twitter:label`/`data` pairs. The tab reads the row before the app loads, the address moves to `#/entity/<id>` in place, and Back leaves in one step as before. Spaces and tables get the same at `/w/<ws>/s/<id>` and `/w/<ws>/t/<id>`, which the ⧉ on a space page and a table header now copy; the workspace root carries the head too. A new per-workspace setting, **Link preview before sign-in** (off by default; Workspace actions menu, `weave workspace link-preview`, `PATCH /api/workspace {"linkPreview": true}`), lets a signed-out fetcher read that head for a uuid permalink on a walled workspace and nothing more (a `Table#n` address stays walled, since public ids can be counted). The bundled raster mark is `public/brand/weave-mark-512.png`.
- **A Σ switch flips on the click** (Issue #235): Kyle filed "visibility toggles are slow to switch" from a uno table, and the trace's clicks were in the Σ row's picker. Each switch waited on its POST, then on `GET /stats` (every column summarised and every rollup of the table resolved, to repaint one cell), then on a schema reload, 1 to 1.5 s a click. A switch now flips when you click it. Its write waits its turn on the eye's write queue (Issue #243) and decides at that turn whether there is anything to create or delete, so a switch flicked on and off before the first write answers ends off, with no duplicate field and no conflict toast. The tab adds or drops the one Spaces field itself, in the shape `describeSchema()` gives it (a rollup over a bar, ring or heat column carries that `display` and a fixed `scale`, one over a rating carries its `rating`), so no schema reload happens, a later refocus finds nothing changed, and the grid is not redrawn. The last flip of a burst reads back only its column (`GET /api/tables/:ref/stats?field=F`, with `field` on `weave_stats` and `--field` on `weave stats`) and repaints that one footer cell. A write that fails toasts and puts its switch back. The read-back was still dominated by dressing: a space rollup dressed every row's value although only `distinct` and `join` read the dressed list, and the stats report did the same for number and date columns, and a currency builds an `Intl.NumberFormat` per row. Measured in the page on a 2,000-row, 18-field table: the switch moved 165 to 375 ms after the click and now moves within 1 ms; the footer figure, which used to land with the switch, lands 18 to 65 ms after the click; the full `/stats` read dropped from 195 to 40 ms, and one column's read-back takes 7 ms. Gates: `test/footer-rollups-browser.test.mjs` gains "a Σ switch flips before its write answers, and only its column is read back" (holds the read-back open, asserts the switch is on, then counts one POST and one narrow stats read, no `/schema`, no row query, the same grid body, and a refocus that finds nothing to redraw), "a Σ switch flicked on and off before its write answers ends off, with one write each", "a Σ write that fails puts the switch back and says why", and "a Σ over a bar column, flipped on, leaves a refocus nothing to redraw" with its rating twin; `test/space-rollups.test.mjs` gains "tableStats narrowed to one field summarises that column and only the rollups under it" and "REST, MCP and CLI carry the stats field narrowing".

## v0.4.69, Oct 6, 2026

Cut on 8b87880: the four workflow-engine defects found building the License Review demo on Net (Gerrit 654-657, landed ec7c0b6). Fixed:

- [[Issue#681]] a built row is one write, relations included, and an empty placeholder reads (no Field) (Gerrit 654)
- [[Issue#682]] a failing webhook marks its Workflows row Failed with the reason (Gerrit 657)
- [[Issue#683]] weave_create_automation honours enabled:false (Gerrit 656)
- [[Issue#684]] an automation's comment is signed workflow:<row id> (Gerrit 655)

- **A built row is one write** (Issue #681): `weave_build` created each row, fired its on-create automations, and only then linked its relation values, so a template reading `{{Font}}` rendered blank. The build now creates rows table by table in relation order (a table's rows after the rows they point at) and writes every relation value that resolves inside the create, so an automation sees the row whole. Only a reference the build cannot resolve yet (a cycle, or a later row of the same table) is still linked after. A `{{Field}}` placeholder that resolves to nothing now reads `(no Field)` rather than leaving a gap. `test/build.test.mjs` builds a Review row before the Font it names.
- **A failing webhook marks its Workflows row Failed** (Issue #682): a webhook action was sent fire-and-forget, so a rule posting to a host that cannot resolve read Healthy forever. The engine now watches the settled request (5 second timeout): a non-2xx answer, a timeout or a network error sets the row's Health to Failed and its Health Reason to, for example, `POST hooks.example.invalid: ENOTFOUND`; the next run that succeeds reads Healthy with the reason cleared. The write that fired the rule never waits on the webhook and never fails because of it. `test/workflows-engine.test.mjs` covers a 500 then a 200, a refused connection and a listener that never answers, all on local listeners.
- **`weave_create_automation` honours `enabled`** (Issue #683): `enabled: false` was dropped by the MCP tool, so the rule came up On and could fire before anyone switched it off. The tool now passes it through as the Workflows row's On, lists it in its schema and description (default true), and names the `webhook` action alongside the others. The CLI (`--enabled false`) and `POST /api/automations` already honoured it. `test/workflows-engine.test.mjs` creates a rule Off over MCP, checks it never fires, and switches it On with `weave_automations update`.
- **A comment an automation adds names its Workflows row** (Issue #684): an `add-comment` action signed its comment "automation" while the same rule's field writes carried `workflow:<row id>` (Issue #674). The comment author is now that same actor string, so it renders as the rule's chip. An action that names its own `author` keeps it. `test/workflow-actor.test.mjs` checks both.
