## v0.4.70 — 2026-10-06

Landed as fc0448e. Fixed:

- [[Issue#266]] Looks broken: UI labels drift (three names for "add field", four for delete) and the filter strip draws two active styles (Gerrit 664)
- [[Issue#397]] Looks broken: the mention caret in a relation chip is an 11px target nested inside the chip link (Gerrit 665)
- [[Issue#289]] Enter in a long document parks the page at its end, and the next keystroke animates back (Gerrit 666)
- [[Issue#456]] Looks broken: a Raw HTML or reference command shows its marker for 800 ms, and the first undo brings the marker back (Gerrit 668)


## Folded fragments

- **One Activity panel for the whole record, with Restore on the revision** (Issue #429): the document history was a cramped list inside the section ("3 REVISIONS Select one to view it · Esc closes", the hint clipped at the right edge) whose rows offered no revert; Restore sat behind a second click, on a preview with no diff. Now the clock-arrow in a record's header opens a panel beside it with every document's revisions, field and state changes, and comments, newest first under Today, Yesterday and a date, and a document's own clock-arrow opens the same panel filtered to that document. Rows are nav rows: what changed on one line, who and when on the next, and the row's action (Restore, Revert, Delete) one click away on hover. A selected row carries one button and, for a revision, a picker to compare it with any other version of that document; the change shows read-only where it lives, a document's diff in place of its editor (blocks, then sentences, then words, unchanged runs folded) and a field change as a card at the top. Every action toasts with Undo in the corner lane, and Undo steps back that action only, refusing if something else was written since. A restore's row reads "Description restored from <time>" (Issue #588). Gates: `test/history-core.test.mjs`, `test/doc-history-browser.test.mjs`.
- **A Raw HTML or reference command lands on the keypress** (Issue #456): `/raw html` used to paint its `raw-html` marker into the document for 821ms before the block appeared, `/entity`, `/link table` and `/space` opened their picker about 800ms after Enter, and the first undo afterwards brought the marker back and reopened the picker. Both rode Vditor's `undoDelay` timer, which records the undo state in the same callback. The MutationObserver Issue #455 added for block markers now watches every command marker and applies it in the task the marker lands in (`watchCommandMarkers` and `applyCommandMarkers` in `public/app.js`), so the marker is never painted and never reaches the undo stack; the editor's `input` handler keeps the same checks as the net under it. Tests in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs` and `test/slash-convert-line.test.mjs`.
- **A reference in a document is the pointer chip** (Issue #97): Kyle, 2026-08-26, on an entity page: "md references could be improved should look more like rich chips". A `[[Table#12]]` wore a costume of its own: a brand-blue wash and blue text in the editor overlay, and in the app's rendered markdown Tabler's global `.mention` class on top of it (a grey pill with a shadow ring at .857em, underlined on hover), while the same row in a relation cell wore the chip system's pointer tier. The repo had already settled which chip a document reference is: the anatomy guide's surface table gives a `[[…]]` mention in a document "the same chip, from the same config", with "no ×, no avatar". `src/markdown.js` now wraps the link in `.k.k-rel` with a new `k-inline` modifier, and moves the caret inside the link ahead of the segments, the order `viewChipEl` draws; the link keeps `a.mention mention-<kind>`, so the overlay's resolver, the kind glyphs and every consumer of the class still find it. In style.css the tier 2 rules paint it whole (1px outline, no fill, the ↗ as the link's last pixel, primary on hover); `k-inline` keeps it an inline box at the text's own font and line, so a line holding a chip is exactly as tall as one without (the grid's 24px inline-flex chip would have pushed a 13px/18px description line apart), and a rule under `.k-rel > a.mention` takes Tabler's pill back off. The live overlay over the IR editor keeps Issue #379's cover: an `a.mention` sized to the literal's rect on the editor's surface, which hides the literal and carries no tint or ring, titled with the reference's label. Inside it the record's name is the same `.k.k-rel` pointer, hugging the name, with the name in `.k-label` so only it ellipsizes and the ↗ stays visible. The standalone document page (`/e/:id/doc.html`) draws the same outline from its own tokens and its caret click no longer follows the link it now sits in. The markdown source is unchanged, a missing or deleted row keeps its existing treatment (the dashed name on the document page, the literal in the editor), copying the text gives the reference's words without the drawn glyph and ↗, and the PDF export keeps its plain words on purpose (`stripInline` in `src/pdf.js`). The three chip pages generated from the stylesheet are regenerated. Handbook: the Document formatting guide says a reference is the pointer chip at the size of its text. Gates: `test/doc-ref-chips-browser.test.mjs` (new, 7 cases: on the document page, the app's rendered description and the editor overlay, each in light and dark, both live references are `.k.k-rel > a.mention` with a 1px solid outline, 4px radius, no fill and the ↗; a paragraph holding a chip, and one holding a chip with its caret, is exactly as tall as a plain paragraph; the description chip's outline and ink equal a grid pointer's; the missing reference is not a chip; copy yields `See Task#N — Plain target for the plain one.`; the caret opens the field without navigating and a click on the chip opens the record's page; in the editor the cover is opaque and the pointer inside it has no fill, the chip sits inside its line, typing `now ` right after it saves `[[Task#N]] now for` with the chip still resolved, and a click docks the record; the stored markdown keeps its reference), `test/backlinks.test.mjs` (the chip markup, caret inside the link), `test/editor-refs.test.mjs` (the overlay's name is the `.k-rel` chip and no tint is left), `test/entity-hierarchy-browser.test.mjs` (the label's width counts the pointer's 1px outline), `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (the overlay's opaque ground), `test/handbook.test.mjs` (the guide names the pointer chip).
- **Enter in a long document leaves the page where it is** (Issue #289): pressing Enter in the first paragraph of an 80-paragraph Description sent the pane to the end of the document (0 to 2,810px on a 1280x700 viewport), and the next keystroke animated it back over about 900ms; a `/` typed into that animation opened the slash menu and the animation's first scroll event shut it again. Enter now pins the pane where the caret already was: a move of more than 120px within a second of the keypress is put back instantly, as long as the caret was in view when Enter was pressed. The slash menu also owns its own close, so a scroll the reader did not start (no key, pointer, wheel or touch since the menu opened) no longer hides it in the first second, while Escape, a pick and a reader's scroll still close it. Issue #137's wheel contract and Issue #455's slash-line conversion keep their cases. Tests in `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`.
- **The caret beside a relation chip is its own 24px target** (Issue #397): it drew 11.3 by 13.8 px and sat inside the chip's link, between the label and the ↗, so WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 could not be met without the invisible hit area swallowing the ↗ beside it. The caret now sits beside the link rather than inside it, in a 24 by 24 box with the bordered glyph drawn inside, in the grid and in a rendered document alike. The chip's link, its ↗ and the caret are three separate targets. Gates: `test/a11y-browser.test.mjs`, `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs`, `test/chip-anatomy-browser.test.mjs`.
- **One name for creating a field** (Issue #266): the plus at the end of the field headers, the row in the Filters popover, the row in the Fields popover and the tray all three open said "Add a field", "Add field" and "New field" for one action. They all say **New field** now, and the Table views guide says the same. `Add` is left to the controls that attach something that already exists. Gate: `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.
- **No inline comments in the web UI** (Issue #661): `public/` (app.js, style.css, the other scripts, index.html and 404.html) carries no comments, and `test/no-inline-comments.test.mjs` now scans it. The first-party scripts and stylesheet a browser downloads shrink from 1.31 MB to 0.86 MB, or from 419 KB to 230 KB gzipped, and the stylesheet computes the same values in light and dark.
- **A restored document revision says it is a restore** (Issue #588): restoring a revision used to read as an ordinary edit ("Current · web · −79", a plain `doc-updated`), and its Activity entry could fold into the edits around it under another person's name. The new revision now stores `restoredFrom` (the seq it brought back; a `restored_from` column added to `doc_revisions` on open), its history row reads "Restored from 5 min ago" with the version's date and author on hover, and its Activity entry is its own row reading "Description restored to the version from 10/5/2026, 9:49 PM by bob" with `restoredFrom`, `restoredAt` and `restoredBy` in its detail. Typing straight after a restore starts a new revision and a new entry, so the restore keeps the text it restored. Tests in `test/doc-revisions.test.mjs` and `test/doc-history-browser.test.mjs`.

releases.name: v0.4.71
fixes: Slow: per-request CPU grows about 3.5x when the workspace doubles, because entityCount scans every entity on each schema read
Slow: visibility toggle show for fields containing data
releases.description:
## v0.4.71 — 2026-10-06

Landed as f157005. Fixed:

- [[Issue#560]] Slow: per-request CPU grows about 3.5x when the workspace doubles, because entityCount scans every entity on each schema read (Gerrit 670)
- [[Issue#328]] Slow: visibility toggle show for fields containing data (Gerrit 671)

- **Hiding a field leaves the grid on the click** (Issue #328): every eye flip waited for its `PATCH`, then a `GET /api/schema`, then a full table query before the switch moved or the column went anywhere. On a loaded host, where each of those calls took seconds, the gesture read as broken. A hide now repaints the rows the grid already holds, one column lighter, before the write goes out: zero reads, and the switch moves on the click in both popovers. The write still queues behind `eyeWrites` in the order the flips were made (Issue #243), and the grid is read back only when the table disagrees with what was painted, which is how a hidden frozen column or a field added elsewhere still settles. A show reads once, as before: it needs the column's values. Measured on a copy of the `uno` workspace, `Agent/Sessions` at 1,791 rows: click to the column leaving the grid drops from 68-153 ms to 19-31 ms, with the PATCH, the schema read and the table query all moved off that path, and a show stays where it was at 61-80 ms. Gates: `test/fields-popover-browser.test.mjs`, `test/eye-live-rows-browser.test.mjs`, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`.
- **A schema read counts rows in one pass** (Issue #560): `describeSchema` put each table's `entityCount` together by calling `listEntities(db.id)`, which walks the whole entity map and filters on `dbId`, so a page load cost tables times rows: about 50 tables by 6,078 rows on the weave workspace. `GET /api/tables/:id` and the search's table hits paid the same. A benchmark of v0.4.52 inside a 1 vCPU container measured a schema read at 45 to 67 ms at 8.4k entities, against under 5 ms at 4,389. The engine now walks `state.entities` once per schema read, buckets live rows by `dbId` into a Map (`#liveRowCounts`), and reads each table's count from it; `universalSearch` reads the same Map for its table hits, and builds it only when a table name matched. At 50 tables by 6,000 rows `describeSchema` drops from 30.4 ms to 0.89 ms a call. The count is still derived from the rows on every read rather than held as a maintained counter, so it cannot drift when a row is trashed, restored, purged or moved between tables. Gate: `test/schema-count-scan.test.mjs`.

## v0.4.73 — 2026-10-06

Landed as 5805cd7. Fixed:

- [[Issue#555]] Wrong data: saving a document rewrites every task item to two spaces after the box and an upper-case [X] (Gerrit 676)
- [[Issue#470]] Error: in WebKit the Formatting showcase page throws an unhandled rejection from Vditor's math render (Gerrit 677)
- [[Issue#553]] Looks broken: the option preview chip in the field settings tray keeps the old name while the option is renamed (Gerrit 678)
- [[Issue#474]] Error: a volume the process cannot write reports "not a SQLite database", and the guide says to look for EACCES (Gerrit 679)


### Folded from changelog.d

- Editing a document no longer rewrites its task items: the box reaches storage as `[ ]` or `[x]` with one space after it, so a string edit by an agent still matches and an unrelated edit leaves every task line unchanged in the revision history. (Issue #555)
- Opening a document that holds math no longer raises an unhandled rejection in WebKit when a math node leaves the page while KaTeX is still loading; the node is skipped and every other formula still typesets. (Issue #470)
- The preview chip in the field settings tray renames as you type, for a select option and for a workflow state, instead of holding the old name until something else redrew the list. (Issue #553)
- A data directory the process cannot write now fails with a message naming the directory, the uid and the fix, instead of reporting that the database file is not a SQLite database. The Railway deploy guide quotes the message the log really shows. (Issue #474)

releases.description:
## v0.4.74 — 2026-10-07

Landed as 90dbb1f. Fixed:

- [[Issue#556]] a slash command's placeholder is not selected, so typing after /task saves "To doShip it" (Gerrit 693)
- [[Issue#680]] a document edit by another person folds into the previous author's Activity entry and is credited to them (Gerrit 694)
- [[Issue#686]] an automation's append-doc writes the document but logs no activity entry (Gerrit 695)

Folded from 14 changelog fragments:

- A document edit by a second person is now its own activity entry, with their name, their delta and their preview. Edits within ten minutes of each other folded into one entry whatever the actor, so a second author's work was credited to the first and the entry's delta described neither edit. The revision log already split by author (Issue #680).
- An automation that appends to a document now logs a `doc-appended` entry naming the document, with the length it wrote and a preview, the way a person's append does. The text landed but the activity feed never said so, so the rule's append was invisible in history and the record page could not pulse the document the rule wrote (Issue #686).
- On a phone the bug button is now a 44px tap target with the same 26px face, set 3px from the screen edge like the phone applet's, and a row's page leaves 72px at its foot so the last line of a document scrolls clear of it. Desktop keeps the 26px corner button 12px in (Issue #695).
- A code block's copy button now sits in its own gutter at the right of the box, so a long line scrolls under the box edge instead of running beneath the button (Issue #694).
- A table that names no row term of its own now speaks `row` / `rows`, not `record` / `records`, so a fresh table's grid reads "Search rows", "+ New row" and "N rows" in the rail, matching the onboarding welcome and the first-run empty state (Issue #618).
- In a document, Cmd+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Shift+Z elsewhere) now redoes what Cmd+Z undid. Vditor only knew Cmd+Y for redo, so the macOS shortcut did nothing (Issue #697).
- On a phone the formatting bar for selected text is now one row of 44px buttons along the bottom of the screen, riding above the on-screen keyboard and scrolling sideways when it runs long, instead of a two-row bubble of 25x35px buttons over the line above the selection. Desktop keeps the floating bubble (Issue #693).
- On a phone, where the row covers the screen, opening a row is now a history step: Back or swipe-back returns to the table, Forward reopens the row, a relation hop inside the row is its own step, and the row's Close button steps back instead of leaving a duplicate table entry. On wider screens the row docked beside the table still adds no history, as ruled in Issues #198, #226 and #276 (Issue #267).
- The record page lists files attached to the row itself in a **Files** card, with the same link and `(missing)` treatment an attachments field gives, so a row in a table with no attachments field still reaches its files (Issue #463).
- Hiding or showing the last column of a table no longer changes the width of the column beside it. Tabler's `card-table` gives the last cell in a row a 20px right inset where every other cell gets 4px, so the column that landed last measured a box 16px wider than its own and grew by that much. The grid now pads its last cell like the rest (Issue #690).
- On a phone the slash menu's rows are now 44px tall with 15px labels, so a thumb hits the command it aims at. Desktop keeps the compact 28px rows (Issue #696).
- A line command run on an empty line now leaves its placeholder selected, so the first thing you type replaces it. `/task` then "Ship it" stores `- [ ] Ship it`; it used to leave the caret after the placeholder and store `- [ ]  To doShip it` (Issue #556).
- Picking Table from the slash menu now puts the caret in the table's first header cell with "Column" selected, so typing names the column. It used to leave the caret on the line above, and the typing landed in a paragraph over an untouched table (Issue #692).
- A workflow state can take a colour of its own. The swatch in the field dialog opens the same ten-hue picker a select option uses, the category colour stays the default, and **Reset to category colour** puts a state back on it. Chips in the grid, the tray preview, view chips, the command palette and the phone applet all read the state's colour (Issue #427).

## v0.4.76 (2026-10-07)

Shipped:

- [[Feature#277]] `weave_ontology` reads the schema in one short call, and the MCP primer's first line sends an agent there first. The outline is one line per table, grouped by space, ending with the workspace etag: 5,250 characters on the weave docs workspace against 103,226 for `weave_schema`. `{concept: "Issue"}` reads one table in full; `{since: "<etag>"}` answers only the spaces whose schema changed. Each space carries a schema version counted from the structural audit log, so a row write moves nothing. Also `GET /api/ontology` and `weave ontology` (a238969).
- [[Feature#278]] A space is defined as the unit of meaning in a workspace: the tables of one area, addressed as `Space/Table`, under one schema version, in the ONTOLOGY export, `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` and the Handbook (f6d8ae9).
- [[Feature#280]] Each workspace keeps its own browser session cookie, `wv_session_<workspace id>`; signing out of one leaves the others signed in, and `POST /api/auth/logout?everywhere=1` ends them all (c42d253).
- [[Feature#281]] The sidebar foot shows the signed-in account with its role and a sign-out menu (ef14ff3).

Fixed:

- [[Issue#703]] Linking a relation opens the scoped workspace search instead of a Name-only list (9bea0b1).
- [[Issue#704]] A code block at rest paints no stray grey dot (74707b1).
- [[Issue#705]] Phone checklist boxes are 44px tap targets (80b3037).
- [[Issue#706]] The phone formatting bar stays on the keyboard when Safari pans the page (f706904).
- [[Issue#707]] iPhone undo and redo gestures step through the document editor's history (69ac3f9).
- [[Issue#710]] An active browser session reissues its cookie with a fresh 30-day lifetime (a8bdd80).
- [[Issue#634]] The docked document editor's boot flicker is on the flicker ratchet (78b16d7).

## v0.4.77 (2026-10-07)

A phone layout: each change below applies at 600px and narrower, where a row already opens as a full-screen page. Wider screens are unchanged.

Shipped:

- [[Feature#269]] On a phone (600px and narrower) the menu button opens a menu that covers the whole screen: the workspace name and a 44px close button on top, every space and table in 44px rows, the record count, size and version at the foot, and the workspaces, theme and help in a bar along the bottom edge. Wider screens keep the side drawer and the desktop sidebar (Gerrit 717, 9888d68).
- [[Feature#270]] On a phone each breadcrumb is a 36px chip with its icon and label, and the current one is bold; the menu button and the row page's back and forward buttons are 44px glass circles. The workspace crumb is left off on a phone, where the menu names the workspace (Gerrit 718, 71e7d61).
- [[Feature#268]] On a phone a glass search capsule floats at the bottom of the screen and opens the ⌘K search; on a table a blue New circle beside it adds a row. The bug button sits just above the bar, and pages and row pages leave room under their last line so nothing ends behind it (Gerrit 719, 8b5c3b0).
- [[Feature#271]] On a phone the table toolbar (search, view, row height, fields, filters and the table menu), which wrapped to three rows, folds into one sliders button beside the breadcrumbs. Its badge counts the active filters, and it opens a glass sheet holding the same controls as 44px rows, each opening the popover it opens on a desktop (Gerrit 720, 0cec60a).
- [[Feature#274]] On a phone a field's picker (workflow state, select, multi-select and icon pickers) opens as a bottom sheet titled with the field's name, with 56px options and a check on the current value. A list of eight options or fewer opens without focusing the search box, so the keyboard stays closed, and a single-choice list that short shows no search box at all (Gerrit 721, fce4221).
- [[Feature#272]] On a phone a table is a list: each row shows its muted #id, its name over up to two lines and its values as chips underneath, at a declared 88px (68px with one-line names at Compact density) that the row window reads, so scrolling and jumping stay exact. A tap anywhere on a row opens the row instead of editing a cell. The column header and the + New row link give way to the bottom bar's New button (Gerrit 722, 1fb2b8a).
- [[Feature#273]] On a phone a row in a table with a workflow field shows a wide blue "Move to <next state>" button pinned to the bottom of its row page. It moves the row to the state after its current one, refreshes the page and the table behind it, and offers Undo; a row already in its last state shows none (Gerrit 723, c43e19a).
- [[Feature#275]] On a phone, swiping a list row left in a table with a workflow field reveals buttons for the states after its current one. A tap moves the row there and the confirmation, with Undo, shows at the top of the screen. A vertical drag leaves the row as it was, and a tap elsewhere closes the buttons (Gerrit 724, 9d834b2).

## v0.4.78 (2026-10-07)

Shipped:

- [[Feature#276]] A table view can show as a **List**: choose it under **Layout** in the View menu. The list keeps the view's rows, filters, sorting and density and draws each row as the table's Chip. In List layout a **Group** button sets up to three levels (select, workflow, toggle, checkbox, link, or a date by day, week, month or year). A link level can head its groups with the linked row's Chip, so a rollup bar on that Chip shows each group's progress. **Completed by** puts a checkbox field on every row and moves ticked rows to a folded **Completed · N** group. **Nest by** indents rows under a Parent link: Tab and Shift+Tab, or drag sideways. With no sort, drag sets a manual order saved in the view; a sort orders rows inside each group. Each group ends in an add row that fills the group's values and any one-value filter, with its own date box. The footer reads "3 of 8 to-dos · 1 completed". Agents set all of it through `weave_table_view` (`layout`, `group`, `completedBy`, `nest`, `collapsed`, `order`), the CLI and REST (Gerrit 716, 9511b67).
- A rollup takes its own number format and display, so `avg` of a Done checkbox with `display: "bar"` is a progress bar (Gerrit 715, 2814a36).

Known limits in this release:

- The Group button shows only in List layout. Table layout keeps the grouping and ignores it.
- The Statistics panel's Group by takes its fields from the same list as the Group button but still groups one level.
- A list draws every row at once with no paging, and a link level reads at most 500 linked rows for its empty groups and table order.

Fixed:

- [[Issue#714]] A sum or avg rollup over a checkbox read 0 or empty, and a rollup could not show a bar (Gerrit 715, 2814a36).
- [[Issue#713]] A table opened with a record in the dock could turn back into the loading skeleton and stay there; it was the cause of the phone-shell WebKit timeouts in the gate (Gerrit 727, 86fab12).

## v0.4.79 — 2026-10-07

Landed as 3bd00fa. Fixed:

- [[Issue#619]] Slow: two browser cases (eight-row State → Done, entity panel close) flake under gate load (Gerrit 730)
- [[Issue#637]] Error: system-tables-nav browser case loses a repaint between waitForSelector and $eval, costing unrelated changes a Verified -1 (Gerrit 731)
- [[Issue#711]] Error: frozen-ground-browser webkit cases time out in the gate, green when run alone (Gerrit 732)

### Folded fragments

- Three browser suites launched their own WebKit or Chromium through `import('playwright')`, outside the shared harness. Those pages never saw `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE`, so the recipe DEVELOPMENT.md gives for a gate-only red could not reproduce one in `frozen-ground-browser`, `phone-shell-browser` or `editor-math-browser`. All three now ask the harness for the extra engine through `engineOf(name)`, which throttles it and closes it with the suite: the same file runs 13 s unthrottled, 16 s at throttle 4 and 36 s at throttle 20, where before the WebKit half ran at full speed whatever the setting. `test/browser-harness.test.mjs` now holds every `*-browser.test.mjs` to the harness, not only the ones its old pattern matched.
- A first-paint wait that misses now says what the page had instead. `painted()` reports the hash, whether the route skeleton is up, what stands in `#main`, how many grid rows the page counts and the toast text, so a 30 s timeout on `.wv-grid tbody tr.entity-row` reads as a diagnosis rather than a bare budget. The cases on `#711` do not reproduce on this main: the cause was the route skeleton painting over a drawn page, fixed under Issue #713 and shipped in v0.4.78 (Issue #711).
- Two browser cases stop losing the Verified gate to machine load. Both waited on a clock instead of the event they assert: `bulk-settle-browser` held the eight-row State change to a 600 ms wall clock, and `doc-autosave-phone-browser` gave the leave-triggered write a 400 ms request window. The bulk case now waits for the eight rows to leave the filtered view, the toast to read `Set 8`, and the grid's animations to finish. It keeps the counts it was written for: one `POST /api/bulk`, one page re-read, nothing else. In the phone cases the 600 ms autosave debounce is cancelled inside the page, so the only write that can reach the server is the one the leave handler sends, and the wait on it is a hang guard at 15 s. Both files pass at `WEAVE_CPU_THROTTLE=40`, where the old waits went red (Issue #619).
- A browser case no longer loses the node it just waited for. `system-tables-nav` waited for `#main input.view-title` and then read it back through `page.$eval`, which resolves the selector a second time; `drawDatabase` opens with `main.replaceChildren()` and the view header settles on a ResizeObserver after that, so the read could land in the gap and throw. Under gate load the gap was wide enough to cost two unrelated changes a Verified vote. Twenty-eight reads across seventeen browser suites had the same shape and now go through `page.locator(selector)`, which re-resolves on each attempt. `test/browser-read-reresolve.test.mjs` fails on any new one, and `system-tables-nav` carries a case that forces the repaint and shows both halves: the single-shot read throws, the locator read waits it out (Issue #637).

Folded from changelog.d:

- A rollup or a lookup that draws rating icons now opens wide enough for all of them, and holds that width as its resize floor, the way a rating column has since Issue #404. A max-7 rollup drew 104px of icons in an 80px cell before. (Issue #564)
- Opening another record in the dock starts it at the top. The dock reuses one scroller across records, so the previous record's offset carried over and the new record's title sat off screen above the reader; an edit or a refresh of the record on screen still holds its place (Issue #623).
- A lookup of a rating over a to-many relation now draws one group of icons per related row instead of printing the numbers, and a related row with no rating keeps its slot as an unrated group. The chip, the card and the field dialog's sample draw it the same way. (Issue #377)
- Checklist items in a document wrap between words. Before, Vditor's `word-break: break-all` let a line end mid-word ("sen / ds"); a URL longer than the line still wraps inside the column (Issue #715).

## v0.4.81 (2026-10-08)

Landed as 423b52b. Fixed:

- [[Issue#700]] Gap: an automation's append to a document records no revision, so the document's history skips it (Gerrit 738)
- [[Issue#566]] Looks broken: changelog-fold.mjs writes an em dash into every CHANGELOG version heading (Gerrit 739)
- [[Issue#615]] Looks broken: Skip setup on the last onboarding step drops the workspace name the person just confirmed (Gerrit 740)

Folding these fragments:

- The CHANGELOG version heading reads `## v0.4.81 (2026-10-08)`. `scripts/changelog-fold.mjs` wrote the version and the date either side of a unicode em dash, which the house prose rule bans in anything published, and every heading in the file came from that one template. The 73 released headings were rewritten in the same change, so the file does not split at the version where the template changed (Issue #566).
- Skip setup and Esc on the last onboarding step keep the workspace name confirmed with Continue one step earlier. Both posted an empty body, so the server fell back to the default and the name was gone; the primary button on the same step kept it. Skip and Esc on the name step itself, before Continue, still drop what was typed (Issue #615).
- A rule that appends to a document now leaves a revision, so the document's history holds what the rule wrote and a reader can compare with it or restore to it. The revision is signed `workflow:<Workflows row id>`, the same name the activity entry carries. Two fires of one rule inside the revision window still coalesce into one revision, as two edits by one person do (Issue #700).

## v0.4.83 (2026-10-08)

Landed as 4a6e0fc (Gerrit 766). Phone layout fixes found on an iPhone, and a phone cell for the flicker sweep. Fixed:

- [[Issue#724]] Looks broken: on an iPhone, focusing the bug note or a picker search zooms the page (Gerrit 750)
- [[Issue#726]] Looks broken: on an iPhone, tapping outside an open menu does not close it (Gerrit 751)
- [[Issue#728]] Looks broken: on an iPhone a table in the menu needs two taps to open (Gerrit 752)
- [[Issue#723]] Looks broken: the table menu sheet on a phone shows a lone three-dot bar whose menu drops below the sheet over the list (Gerrit 753)
- [[Issue#727]] Looks broken: the phone table menu button draws its icon off centre and its sheet opens flush against it (Gerrit 754)
- [[Issue#738]] Looks broken: on a phone, scrolling the list selects the rows under the finger (Gerrit 755)
- [[Issue#729]] Looks broken: on a phone list row, a three-digit #id link runs into the row name (Gerrit 756)
- [[Issue#730]] Looks broken: on a phone list row at Comfortable or Spacious, the chips split across two lines and drop to the row edge (Gerrit 757)
- [[Issue#725]] Looks broken: swiping a list row right to close it snaps instead of following the finger (Gerrit 758)
- [[Issue#720]] Looks broken: on a phone, the tap that closes a swiped row also lands on what lies under it (Gerrit 758)
- [[Issue#731]] Looks broken: closing a swiped row's actions on a phone flickers (Gerrit 758)
- [[Issue#743]] Looks broken: on an iPhone, a swiped row reveals its actions cut short, so the last action button cannot be tapped (Gerrit 758)
- [[Issue#742]] Wrong data: on a table with two state fields, the phone next-state button and swipe silently move only the first (Gerrit 759)
- [[Issue#733]] Looks broken: on a phone, Activity from a row's menu opens a zero-width panel over the row (Gerrit 760)
- [[Issue#734]] Looks broken: a phone row page shows an Expand button and 22 to 34px header buttons (Gerrit 761)
- [[Issue#735]] Slow: opening a row on a phone waits on 6 to 9 requests, including a refetched editor icon script (Gerrit 762, 763)
- [[Issue#739]] Looks broken: the phone New button creates a blank row instead of opening the new-row sheet (Gerrit 764)
- [[Issue#736]] Looks broken: a phone shows keyboard shortcuts it cannot use (⌘K, ⌘-click, ⌘H) (Gerrit 765)
- [[Issue#638]] Looks broken: the screen flashes for 12 ms in box 320,40 160x160 (switch-view)
- [[Issue#712]] The scroll-grid ratchet entry for Issue #631 comes back under load, so the flicker gate flakes
- [[Issue#732]] Gap: the flicker sweep never walks a phone viewport, WebKit or a touch gesture

### Changelog

- The flicker sweep no longer reports a screencast frame that answers the reader's own click, keypress or scroll. The frame rule now shares the input window the DOM rules have had since Issue #631 (Issue #638).
- The flicker probe measures the reader's input window in painted frames rather than 50 milliseconds, so the scroll-grid ratchet entry no longer comes back on a busy host and the flicker gate stops flaking there (Issue #712).
- The flicker sweep and its gate now walk a second cell: the iPhone 15 profile in WebKit (393x659 viewport, touch, iOS Safari agent), next to desktop Chromium at 1400x900. Six phone journeys cover the bottom search bar, the full-screen menu, the table sheet, a picker sheet, tapping a list row open and going Back, and swiping a row open and closed. Phone fingerprints end in `|phone`; desktop fingerprints keep their old form (Issue #732).
- The probe reports a new kind, `cut`: a painted element removed while the rest of its row is still sliding, so the gap shows for the rest of the slide. A see-through layer with nothing in it no longer counts as a transient when it is replaced (Issue #732).
- `test/lib/browser.mjs` gains the shared phone profile: `launch(name, seed, { phone: true })` launches WebKit and `phonePage(browser)` opens a page as `devices['iPhone 15']` (Issue #732).
- On an iPhone, a table in the menu opens on the first tap. Every hover rule that shows, hides or moves content now applies only where the pointer can hover, and on touch screens the table row menu, the add-table button and the unlink button stay visible instead of waiting for a hover (Issue #728).
- On an iPhone, a tap anywhere outside an open menu, popover, picker, table sheet or the bug panel closes it. Every overlay now closes through one shared dismiss that listens for the touch itself instead of a click, which iOS never sends for a tap on empty space (Issue #726).
- On a phone, Activity from a row's menu opens as a full-screen sheet above the row, with 44px close and filter controls, and the phone's Back gesture closes it. It used to open as a zero-width strip over the row (Issue #733).
- On a phone, a list row keeps its chips on one line under the name at every row height. Chips that do not fit fold into a +N counter instead of wrapping onto a second line that the row clipped at Comfortable and Spacious (Issue #730).
- On a phone, the list's #id column is as wide as the table's largest id, set in tabular figures, so "#149 ↗" no longer runs into the row name and every name and chip line starts on one edge 8px after it. The schema now carries each table's `maxPublicId` (Issue #729).
- On a phone, the + button opens a New sheet for the current table instead of writing a blank row. The sheet is titled by the table's row term ("New bug" on Issue, "New row" on a table with no term of its own), switches tables from a chip, takes the name and the table's short choice fields, and writes nothing until Create, which adds the row and opens it. All fields adds it and opens the full row page (Issue #739).
- On an iPhone, focusing a text field no longer zooms the page. At 600px and below and on touch screens every input, text area, select and editable block is at least 16px, and the app pages carry `maximum-scale=1` (Issue #724).
- The phone browser tests now open their pages as an iPhone 15 in WebKit (393x659 viewport, touch, iOS Safari agent) through the shared profile in `test/lib/browser.mjs`, in place of a 390 or 375 px Chromium window. Desktop cases stay on Chromium. `touchScroll` scrolls the pane under a point the way a finger does (Issue #732).
- On a phone, the row page header keeps one line: the crumb chip, the row menu and Close, each a 44px circle. Expand is gone (the row already fills the screen), and Copy link and Show or hide fields moved into the row menu (Issue #734).
- Opening a row asks for the row once and for its references and document history checks at the same moment, instead of fetching the row twice and the rest after it, so a row on a phone opens one round trip sooner (Issue #735).
- On a phone, scrolling the table list no longer selects rows or text under the finger. A list row opens only on a tap (down and up within 10px and 300ms); any longer or wider touch is a scroll, and list rows start no text selection (Issue #738).
- On a touch phone, weave no longer offers keyboard shortcuts it cannot use: the ⌘K pill in menu search and the bug panel's ⌘↵ hint are hidden, and titles drop their shortcut clause ("Open bug beside the table", "Expand", "Send") through one helper. Desktops keep them (Issue #736).
- On a phone, a swiped list row follows the finger both ways, stretches against either end, and settles open or shut on one transition. Closing keeps the actions in place until the row is home instead of flickering them away first, the tap that closes an open row does nothing else, and the revealed actions are exactly as wide as the buttons they hold, so the last one takes a tap in Safari too (Issues #725, #720, #731, #743).
- On a phone, the table sheet lists the table actions (Column stats, Export CSV, New share page, Row term, Delete table) as its own rows under a Table heading, with Delete table last in red. The lone three-dot row whose menu dropped below the sheet is gone, so is the second Search box, and a Sort row picks the field and direction (Issue #723).
- On a phone, the table sliders button draws its icon centred, and its sheet opens 8px below the button with the two right edges lined up (Issue #727).
- On a phone, a row in a table with more than one state field shows one next-step button per field, stacked and named ("Move Status to In Progress", "Move Review to Approved"), and each moves and undoes only its own field. Swipe offers no state actions on such a table, since a swipe cannot say which field it moves; a table with one state field is unchanged (Issue #742).
- Vendored files the document editor loads on its own (its icons, Lute and content themes) are now served with a one-hour cache, so opening a second row on a phone no longer refetches them. First-party files asked for without their version still revalidate every time (Issue #735).

## v0.4.84 — 2026-10-08

Landed as 3c9d777. Fixed:

- [[Issue#737]] Looks broken: most phone controls are smaller than a 44px touch target (Gerrit 769)
- [[Issue#577]] Looks broken: the page layout breaks at a narrow window width, then snaps back (Gerrit 772)
- [[Issue#246]] The grid’s "+ New row" is shorter than a data row (Gerrit 773)


Folded from 5 changelog fragments:

- The grid's + New row is now a row. Its cell takes the density's row height and the button fills it, so the foot measures 32px Compact, 44px Comfortable and 72px Spacious instead of 34px at all three, and the add row no longer reads as a short strip under the last data row. It stays the sticky foot of the grid (Feature #196), and the phone list's add cell keeps its own height (Issue #246).
- Every drag-to-reorder surface shares one treatment, with a mouse and on phones: grid column headers, the Fields popover, view tabs, group levels, workflow states, select options (new), entity page fields and blocks, and list view rows. On pickup the item lifts with a slight scale and a deeper shadow; the item itself waits, dimmed, in a dashed placeholder at the slot it will land in while its neighbours slide aside; the drop settles it into the placeholder, and Escape or a drop outside sends it home. On touch a 250 ms long press lifts it, with a haptic tick where the platform offers one. The list auto-scrolls near its edges and stops once the pointer leaves the edge band. With reduced motion the placeholder stays and the scale and slide go. Keyboard reorder is unchanged (Feature #282).
- Between roughly 1040px and 620px of window the row pane's Fields block kept the desktop two-column form, and the value column shrank to as little as 40px: chips became slivers and the Amount, Vendor, Due and Note values disappeared. The block now sizes its columns from the pane rather than the window, so the 110px label arrives when the pane is under 330px and the value moves under its label when the pane is under 265px. The value column holds at 120px or more at every width from 1440px down to 375px (Issue #577).
- A date value no longer demands 120px inside a column narrower than that, so the day, month and year stay readable in a narrow row pane (Issue #577).
- On a phone, the Show more toggle under a clamped table or workspace description taps as a 44x44 target. It was drawn at 64x17 and kept that hit area; the drawn link is unchanged (Issue #737).
- On a phone and on any coarse pointer, every control the reader can tap carries a 44x44 hit area. Crumb chips, the copy-permalink and actions buttons, the Set icon button, the view title, the workspace Schema and Members disclosures, the sidebar wordmark, the section carets, the Fields rows and their chips, inputs and date button, and the bug panel's category, send and mail controls were between 10x14 and 44x40 and now pad out to 44 without changing what is drawn, except the Fields rows and the inputs inside them, which grow to a 44px line (Issue #737).
- `test/phone-touch-targets-browser.test.mjs` sweeps the workspace home, the table list, the row page, the full-screen menu, a picker sheet and the bug panel in both themes, in Chromium at 390x844 and in WebKit on the iPhone 15 profile, and names every control whose tappable span through its centre falls under 44px (Issue #737).

## v0.4.85 — 2026-10-08

Landed as pending. Fixed:

- [[Issue#744]] phone reorder grips rest visible on a touch screen (Gerrit 775)
- [[Issue#721]] an empty relation no longer leaves a blank in a phone list row (Gerrit 776)
- [[Issue#391]] the loading mark ships in the shell so a fresh load is never bare (Gerrit 777)


Folded from `changelog.d/`:

- The loading mark now ships inside `index.html` and appears on first paint once the 500 ms threshold passes, so a fresh load no longer sits on a bare shell while the app fetches the animated rope (Issue #391).
- A phone list row no longer leaves a blank where an empty relation sits. The cell held only its hidden "+ link" button, so it still took 47px between the chips either side of it; now a relation cell with no linked row is left out of the line, the chips that remain pack left, and the "+N" count reads from what is left (Issue #721).
- `test/phone-list-rows-browser.test.mjs` seeds an empty relation alongside a filled one and asserts the empty cell is not displayed, the filled one still is unless the line overflows, and no two chips in a row sit more than the 6px flex gap apart (Issue #721).
- On a touch screen the reorder grips now rest at .7 opacity instead of 0, so an entity page field row, an entity page block, a document section and a list view row each show the handle that says they can be dragged. A mouse still reveals them on hover and nothing is drawn differently on a desktop (Issue #744).
- `test/phone-grips-browser.test.mjs` reads the resting opacity of all four grips in both themes, in Chromium at 390x844 and in WebKit on the iPhone 15 profile, and holds the desktop hover reveal in place (Issue #744).
